# Machine summary

Generate one current snapshot of repositories, present Tries, worktrees, tasks,
runtimes and recovery risks for a person or another agent.

```bash
dev summary
dev summary --attention
dev summary --detail compact --no-runtime
dev summary --json
```

The default `auto` Markdown expands dirty/live/HOT/WARM projects and keeps quiet
projects in a compact index. `--attention` also selects missing checkouts,
topology errors, no-remote repositories and local-only branches.

Use `dev journal` for a date range and `dev repo context` for one repository.
The command generates context only; it does not launch an agent or store the
rendered summary.
```

   427	func (s *Service) allowedTarget(kind, path string) bool {
   428		switch kind {
   429		case "hygiene_rules":
   430			return path == filepath.Join(s.Dir, "policy.toml")
   431		case "hygiene_setup":
   432			for _, rel := range []string{".pre-commit-config.yaml", ".gitleaks.toml", ".dev-cli/hygiene.toml"} {
   433				if path == filepath.Join(s.Root, filepath.FromSlash(rel)) {
   434					return true
   435				}
   436			}
   437		case "hygiene_repair_encoding":
   438			rel, err := filepath.Rel(s.Root, path)
   439			return err == nil && validRepairPath(filepath.ToSlash(rel))
   440		case "hygiene_redact":
   441			rel, err := filepath.Rel(s.Root, path)
   442			return err == nil && validRelative(filepath.ToSlash(rel))
   443		}
   444		return false
   445	}
   446	func (s *Service) Restore(ctx context.Context, receipt string, apply bool, o ApplyOptions) ([]configedit.Change, error) {
   447		plan, err := configedit.RestorePlan(ctx, filepath.Join(s.Dir, "recovery"), receipt)
   448		if err != nil {
   449			return nil, errors.New("recovery unavailable or source changed")
   450		}
   451		for _, c := range plan.Preview() {
   452			if !s.allowedTarget("hygiene_redact", c.Path) && !s.allowedTarget("hygiene_rules", c.Path) {
   453				return nil, errors.New("recovery path belongs to another checkout")
   454			}
   455		}
   456		if !apply {
   457			return plan.Preview(), nil
   458		}
   459		paths := []string{}
   460		for _, c := range plan.Preview() {
   461			paths = append(paths, c.Path)
   462			rel, _ := filepath.Rel(s.Root, c.Path)
   463			if IsArtifactPath(filepath.ToSlash(rel)) && !o.WriterStopped {
   464				return nil, errors.New("artifact recovery requires explicit post-writer proof")
   465			}
   466		}
   467		err = gitx.WithLifecycleLock(ctx, s.Common, func() error {
   468			if o.Guard != nil {
   469				if e := o.Guard(ctx, s.Root, paths); e != nil {
   470					return e
   471				}
   472			}
   473			_, e := configedit.Apply(ctx, plan, filepath.Join(s.Dir, "recovery"))
   474			return e
   475		})
   476		return plan.Preview(), err
   477	}

   485	func Settle(ctx context.Context) error {
   486		select {

   489		case <-time.After(500 * time.Millisecond):

// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
// were deleted behind git's back.
func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
	_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
	return err
}

// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
	if branch == "" {
		return false
	}
	_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
	return err == nil
}

// RefState reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves while preserving
// observation failures. A normal rev-parse exit 1 with no diagnostic is an
// authoritative missing ref; every other failure remains an error.
func RefState(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) (bool, error) {
	if ref == "" {
		return false, nil
	}
	_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
	if err == nil {
		return true, nil
	}
	var commandErr *Error
	var exitErr *exec.ExitError
	if errors.As(err, &commandErr) && errors.As(commandErr.Err, &exitErr) &&
		exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 && strings.TrimSpace(commandErr.Stderr) == "" {
		return false, nil
	}
	return false, err
}

// RefExists is the compatibility predicate for callers where probe failure is
// intentionally equivalent to absence. Guarded lifecycle code uses RefState.
func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
	exists, _ := RefState(ctx, dir, ref)
	return exists

// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
// a full Discover.
func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
	_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
	return err == nil
}

// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
	if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
		if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
			return b
		}
	}
	for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
		if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
			return cand
		}
	}
	return ""
}

```text
- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.

**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.

For a release:

1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.

If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.

Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.

## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned

`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.

| Change | Required synchronization |
|---|---|
| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |

`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.

English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.

## Hygiene and skill batch operations

`internal/hygiene` owns per-repository setup plans and batch ledgers. REPOS and
`hygiene manage` are adapters; JSON batch management previews only. Keep legacy
artifact finalizers until their independent lifecycle is replaced. Cached machine
privacy imports use only bounded local cache readers and revalidate their source.
`internal/agentskill` owns selected-removal policy: exact native names/agent scopes
or bundled manifests, source/ownership/dependency proof and postconditions under
the provider lease. Never infer complete Windows validation from an advisory
step's success conclusion; inspect logs and require the dedicated native gates.

## Agent history policy

`dev help ai-artifacts` separates source retention, archive location, protection
and distribution. New configuration is opt-in. Sources are SpecStory Markdown or
explicit files; provider IDs name the originating agent. Do not infer writer exit
from byte stability or close agents to finalize evidence. Archive mode verifies
ignored bytes before cleanup; existing tracked intents retain their original lane.
`git-filter-repo` only operates on new verified copies. Ordinary migration never
rewrites source refs or published tags, and raw backups are not secret audits.

73	func resolveStartRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, ref string) (repo.Repo, error) {
74		if ref != "" {
75			r, _, err := repo.Resolve(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), ref)
76			return r, err
77		}
78		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
79		if err != nil {
80			return repo.Repo{}, err
81		}
82		g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, cwd)
83		if err != nil {
84			return repo.Repo{}, fmt.Errorf("no repo argument and %s is not a git repository", config.Contract(cwd))
85		}
86		return repo.Repo{
87			Name: g.Name, Path: g.MainRoot, RealPath: g.MainRoot,
88			MainRoot: g.MainRoot, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
89		}, nil
90	}

92	func buildStartSpec(ctx context.Context, app *App, req startRequest) (*startSpec, error) {
93		r, err := resolveStartRepository(ctx, app, req.RepoRef)
94		if err != nil {
95			return nil, err
96		}
97		return buildStartSpecForRepository(ctx, app, r, req)
98	}

100	func buildStartSpecForRepository(ctx context.Context, app *App, r repo.Repo, req startRequest) (*startSpec, error) {
101		if r.Bare {
102			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s is a bare repository and cannot host a task checkout", r.Display())
103		}
104	
105		name := strings.TrimSpace(req.Name)
106		if name == "" && req.Branch != "" && req.Mode != task.ModeDirect {
107			name = req.Branch
108		}
109		if name == "" {
110			return nil, errors.New("give the work a name: dev start <repo> --task <name>")
111		}
112	
113		branch, base := strings.TrimSpace(req.Branch), strings.TrimSpace(req.Base)
114		mode := req.Mode
115		if mode == "" {
116			mode = task.ModeWorktree
117		}
118		switch mode {
119		case task.ModeDirect:
120			st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
121			if err != nil {
122				return nil, err
123			}
124			if st.Detached || st.Branch == "" {
125				return nil, errors.New("--direct needs a named branch; this checkout has detached HEAD")
126			}
127			if branch != "" && branch != st.Branch {
128				return nil, fmt.Errorf("--direct tracks the branch already checked out (%s), not --branch %s; "+
129					"omit --branch or use --branch-only", st.Branch, branch)
130			}
131			branch, base = st.Branch, st.Branch
132	
133		case task.ModeBranch, task.ModeWorktree:
134			if branch == "" {
135				branch = "feat/" + config.Slug(name)
136			}
137			if base == "" {
138				base = gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, r.Path)
139			}
140			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, r.Path, "check-ref-format", "--branch", branch); err != nil {
141				return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid branch %q: %w", branch, err)
142			}
143			if !gitx.BranchExists(ctx, r.Path, branch) {
144				if base == "" {
145					return nil, errors.New("cannot determine a base ref; enter one explicitly")
146				}
147				if !gitx.RefExists(ctx, r.Path, base) {
148					return nil, fmt.Errorf("base ref %q does not exist in %s", base, r.Path)
149				}
150			}
151	
152		default:
153			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown start mode %q", mode)
154		}
155		if req.Run != "" && mode != task.ModeWorktree {
156			return nil, errors.New("--run requires the default worktree mode; it cannot be used with --direct or --branch-only")
157		}
158	
159		id := task.MakeID(r.Name, branch)
160		existing, err := existingTaskForStart(app.Tasks, id)
161		if err != nil {
162			return nil, err
163		}
164		if existing != nil && existing.State != task.Done {
165			return nil, fmt.Errorf("task %s already exists (state %s) — use `dev resume %s`",
166				existing.ID, existing.State, existing.ID)
167		}
168	
169		spec := &startSpec{
170			Submodules: req.Submodules, DevelopSubmodules: req.DevelopSubmodules, SubmoduleBases: req.SubmoduleBases,
171			RepoPath: r.Path, RepoName: r.Name, Category: r.Category,
172			Name: name, Branch: branch, Base: base, Next: req.Next, Run: req.Run, Mode: mode,
173			NoProvision: req.NoProvision, NoRuntime: req.NoRuntime, Focus: req.Focus,
174		}
175		if mode != task.ModeWorktree && len(req.DevelopSubmodules) > 0 {
176			return nil, errors.New("--submodule requires worktree mode")
177		}
178		if err := (config.Submodules{Init: req.Submodules, Develop: req.DevelopSubmodules}).Validate(); err != nil {
179			return nil, err
180		}
181		if mode == task.ModeWorktree {
182			if existing, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, r.Path, branch); err != nil {
183				return nil, err
184			} else if ok {
185				return nil, &wt.ErrExists{Branch: branch, Path: existing.Path}
186			}
187			path, err := app.Cfg.WorktreePathFor(r.Name, r.Path, branch, r.Category)
188			if err != nil {
189				return nil, err
190			}
191			if err := wt.ValidateTarget(path, r.Path); err != nil {
192				return nil, err
193			}
194			spec.WorktreePath = path
195		}
196		return spec, nil
197	}

199	func existingTaskForStart(store *task.Store, id string) (*task.Task, error) {
200		existing, err := store.Get(id)
201		if err == nil {
202			return existing, nil
203		}
204		if errors.Is(err, task.ErrNotFound) {
205			return nil, nil
206		}
207		if present, presentErr := store.RecordExists(id); presentErr == nil && present {
208			return nil, err
209		} else if presentErr != nil {
210			// Preserve the established late-save failure behavior for a task-store
211			// path whose existing ancestor is itself not a directory. Any usable store
212			// with an occupied corrupt record fails before external side effects.
213			if taskStoreBlockedByNonDirectory(store.Dir) {
214				return nil, nil
215			}
216			return nil, err
217		}
218		return nil, nil
219	}
220	
221	func taskStoreBlockedByNonDirectory(path string) bool {
222		for {
223			info, err := os.Lstat(path)
224			if err == nil {
225				return !info.IsDir()
226			}
227			parent := filepath.Dir(path)
228			if parent == path {
229				return false
230			}
231			path = parent
232		}
233	}
234	
235	func executeStartSpec(ctx context.Context, app *App, spec *startSpec, log io.Writer) (*startResult, error) {
236		r, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, spec.RepoPath)
237		if err != nil {
238			return nil, err
239		}
240		var result *startResult
241		err = gitx.WithLifecycleLock(ctx, r.GitCommonDir, func() error { var err error; result, err = executeStartSpecLocked(ctx, app, spec, log); return err })
242		return result, err
243	}
244	
245	func executeStartSpecLocked(ctx context.Context, app *App, spec *startSpec, log io.Writer) (*startResult, error) {
246		id := task.MakeID(spec.RepoName, spec.Branch)
247		replaceDoneRevision := ""
248		existing, err := existingTaskForStart(app.Tasks, id)
249		if err != nil {
250			return nil, err
251		}
252		if spec.RequireNewTask && existing != nil {
253			return nil, errors.New("new task identity is already occupied")
254		}
255		switch {
256		case existing != nil && existing.State != task.Done:
257			return nil, fmt.Errorf("task %s already exists (state %s) — use `dev resume %s`",
258				existing.ID, existing.State, existing.ID)
259		case existing != nil:
260			replaceDoneRevision = existing.Revision()
261		}
262	
263		t := &task.Task{
264			Name: spec.Name, Repo: spec.RepoName, RepoPath: spec.RepoPath,
265			Branch: spec.Branch, Base: spec.Base, Mode: spec.Mode,
266			State: task.Hot, Owner: config.Hostname(), Next: spec.Next,
267		}
268		var rt runtime.Runtime = runtime.None{}
269		if !spec.NoRuntime {
270			rt = app.Runtime()
271		}
272		label := worktreeRuntimeLabel(spec.RepoName, spec.Branch)
273		if spec.Mode == task.ModeDirect {
274			label = spec.RepoName + "/" + spec.Name
275		}
276		result := &startResult{Task: t, Runtime: rt}
277	
278		switch spec.Mode {
279		case task.ModeDirect:
280			if err := guardSharedCheckout(ctx, app, rt, spec.RepoPath); err != nil {
281				return nil, err
282			}
283			opened, err := rt.Open(ctx, spec.RepoPath, label)
284			if err != nil {
285				app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
286			} else {
287				result.Opened = opened
288			}
289	
290		case task.ModeBranch:
291			if err := guardSharedCheckout(ctx, app, rt, spec.RepoPath); err != nil {
292				return nil, err
293			}
294			if gitx.BranchExists(ctx, spec.RepoPath, spec.Branch) {
295				if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, spec.RepoPath, "switch", spec.Branch); err != nil {
296					return nil, fmt.Errorf("switch to %s: %w", spec.Branch, err)
297				}
298			} else if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, spec.RepoPath, "switch", "-c", spec.Branch, spec.Base); err != nil {
299				return nil, fmt.Errorf("create and switch to %s from %s: %w", spec.Branch, spec.Base, err)
300			}
301			opened, err := rt.Open(ctx, spec.RepoPath, label)
302			if err != nil {
303				app.warnf("could not open a runtime session: %v", err)
304			} else {
305				result.Opened = opened
306			}
307	
308		case task.ModeWorktree:
309			base := spec.Base
310			if spec.BaseOID != "" {
311				base = spec.BaseOID
312			}
313			m := &wt.Manager{Cfg: app.Cfg, Runtime: rt, Log: log}
314			created, err := m.Create(ctx, wt.CreateRequest{
315				LockHeld:   true,
316				Submodules: spec.Submodules, DevelopSubmodules: spec.DevelopSubmodules, SubmoduleBases: spec.SubmoduleBases, TaskStart: true,
317				RepoPath: spec.RepoPath, RepoName: spec.RepoName,
318				Branch: spec.Branch, Base: base, Category: spec.Category,
319				Path: spec.WorktreePath, Label: label,
320				NoProvision: spec.NoProvision, NoRuntime: spec.NoRuntime, Focus: spec.Focus,
321			})
322			if created != nil {
323				t.WorktreePath, result.Opened, result.Worktree = created.Path, created.Runtime, created
324			}
325			if err != nil {
326				return result, err
327			}
328		}
329	
330		setTaskRuntime(t, rt, result.Opened)
331		if spec.RequireNewTask {
332			_, err = app.Tasks.Create(ctx, t)
333		} else if replaceDoneRevision != "" {
334			err = app.Tasks.ReplaceDone(t, replaceDoneRevision)
335		} else {
336			err = app.Tasks.Save(t)
337		}
338		if err != nil {
339			return result, err
340		}
341		result.TaskSaved = true
342		if !spec.NoRuntime {
343			annotate(app, rt, t)
344		}
345		return result, nil
346	}

	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "start [repo]",
		Short: "Track work directly, on a canonical branch, or in an isolated worktree",
		Long: `Start a tracked change stream in one of three explicit modes:

  default        create a branch + linked worktree, provision it, open a
                 runtime session, and record the task. Safest for work that
                 may be interrupted or run in parallel.
  --branch-only  create/switch a branch in the canonical checkout, with no
                 worktree. Lighter, but that checkout cannot host another
                 branch concurrently.
  --direct       track the branch already checked out in the canonical repo —
                 usually main — without creating either a branch or worktree.
                 Best for one-session ad-hoc changes.

For untracked ad-hoc navigation, use "dev repo open" or press Enter in the
TUI's REPOS view; that opens the project without creating any task at all.

In an interactive terminal, omitting the task name opens a context-aware
wizard. Outside a checkout it offers fast local-repository selection; inside
one it keeps the current repository as the immediate default. It then asks for
task, mode, branch, base and next action. Defaults are shown
inline, and the final summary must be confirmed before anything is created.
Pipes and --json never prompt: pass --task for unattended use.

With no repo argument, the repository containing the current directory is used.
Always pass --base for an unattended branch/worktree task.

Herdr-aware direct/branch starts refuse a checkout occupied by another agent.
Use the root --allow-shared-checkout override only after coordinating disjoint
file ownership. --json emits one pure creation object; only a new first-class
Herdr worktree with its exact returned root pane is launchable. Worktree labels
use repo/branch so Herdr can show native nested repository provenance.

--run sends one shell command to that exact newly created Herdr worktree pane.
It is worktree/Herdr-only, cannot be combined with --json, and only confirms
dispatch; it does not wait for the command or report its exit status. Combine
it with --focus to switch or attach after the command is sent.`,
		Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1),
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			ctx := ctxOf()
			bases, baseErr := parseSubmoduleBases(submoduleBases)
			if baseErr != nil {
				return baseErr
			}
			runExplicit := cmd.Flags().Changed("run")
			if runExplicit && strings.TrimSpace(runCommand) == "" {
				return errors.New("--run requires a non-empty shell command")
			}
			if runExplicit && jsonOut {
				return errors.New("--run and --json are separate launch paths and cannot be used together")
			}
			if runExplicit && app.Runtime().Name() != "herdr" {
				return errors.New("--run requires the Herdr runtime; remove --no-runtime or select --runtime herdr")
			}
			if direct && (branchOnly || noWorktree) {
				return errors.New("--direct and --branch-only are different modes; pick one")
			}
			branchOnly = branchOnly || noWorktree
			mode := task.ModeWorktree
			switch {
			case direct:
				mode = task.ModeDirect
			case branchOnly:
				mode = task.ModeBranch
			}
			req := startRequest{
				Submodules: submoduleMode, DevelopSubmodules: submodulePaths, SubmoduleBases: bases,
				Name: name, Branch: branch, Base: base, Next: next, Run: runCommand, Mode: mode,
				ModeExplicit:   direct || branchOnly,
				BranchExplicit: cmd.Flags().Changed("branch"),
				BaseExplicit:   cmd.Flags().Changed("base"),
				NextExplicit:   cmd.Flags().Changed("next"),
				NoProvision:    noProvision, Focus: focus,
			}
			if len(args) == 1 {
				req.RepoRef, req.RepoExplicit = args[0], true
			}
			if req.Name == "" && req.Branch != "" && req.Mode != task.ModeDirect {
				req.Name = req.Branch
			}

			var spec *startSpec
			var err error
			if req.Name == "" {
				if jsonOut || !app.interactive() {
					return errors.New("give the work a name: dev start <repo> --task <name>")
				}
				var confirmed bool
				spec, confirmed, err = runStartWizard(ctx, app, req)
				if errors.Is(err, errPromptCanceled) {
					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Canceled; nothing was created.")
					return nil
				}
				if err != nil {
					return err
				}
				if !confirmed {
					return fmt.Errorf("task %s was created at %s, but --run was not dispatched: %w",
						result.Task.ID, config.Contract(checkoutOf(result.Task)), err)
				}
				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   command   dispatched to %s\n", paneID)
			}
			if result.Runtime.Name() == "none" {
				return app.cdDirective(checkoutOf(result.Task))
			}
			if focus && !jsonOut {
				return activateRuntime(ctx, result.Runtime, result.Task.RuntimeHandle)
			}
			return nil

	}
	f := cmd.Flags()

	f.BoolVar(&jsonOut, "json", false, "emit one machine-readable creation result")
	cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeRepos(app)

    32	// Sanitize removes known identifying forms. Free-text review is still required:
    33	// no regexp can determine whether every arbitrary name in prose is private.
    34	func Sanitize(text string) string {
    35		text = strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
    36			if r == '\n' || r == '\t' {
    37				return r
    38			}
    39			if unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.In(r, unicode.Cf) {
    40				return -1
    41			}
    42			return r
    43		}, text)
    44		for _, rule := range redactions {
    45			text = rule.pattern.ReplaceAllString(text, rule.replacement)
    46		}
    47		return text
    48	}
    49	func safeFacts(f Facts) Facts {
    50		f.Version = Sanitize(f.Version)
    51		if len(f.Version) > 100 {
    52			f.Version = "unknown"
    53		}
    54		if !regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9+._-]+$`).MatchString(f.Version) {
    55			f.Version = "unknown"
    56		}
    57		if !map[string]bool{"darwin": true, "linux": true, "windows": true}[f.OS] {
    58			f.OS = "unknown"
    59		}
    60		if !map[string]bool{"amd64": true, "arm64": true, "386": true, "arm": true}[f.Arch] {
    61			f.Arch = "unknown"
    62		}
    63		if !map[string]bool{"homebrew": true, "scoop": true, "go-install": true, "standalone": true, "unknown": true}[f.Installation] {
    64			f.Installation = "unknown"
    65		}
    66		return f
    67	}
    68	func publicBody(request DraftRequest) (string, error) {
    69		facts := safeFacts(request.Facts)
    70		text := fmt.Sprintf("# %s\n\n%s\n\n## Environment\n\n- dev: %s\n- OS/architecture: %s/%s\n- Installation: %s\n", Sanitize(request.Title), Sanitize(request.Body), facts.Version, facts.OS, facts.Arch, facts.Installation)
    71		if len(request.Diagnostic) > 0 {
    72			public, err := sshhost.ParsePublicDiagnosis(request.Diagnostic)
    73			if err != nil {
    74				return "", err
    75			}
    76			data, _ := json.MarshalIndent(public, "", "  ")
    77			text += "\n## SSH diagnostic evidence\n\n```json\n" + string(data) + "\n```\n"
    78		}
    79		return text, nil
    80	}

func (h *hygieneCLI) apply(ctx context.Context, s *hygiene.Service, id string, yes, writerStopped bool, expectedKind string) error {
	p, err := s.ReadPlan(ctx, id)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if p.Kind != expectedKind {
		return errors.New("plan kind does not match this command")
	}
	if !yes {
		if !h.app.interactive() {
			return errors.New("review the saved plan, then use --apply --plan ID --yes")
		}
		if err = h.output(p, nil); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		ok, e := newPrompter(h.app).confirm("Apply this hygiene plan?", false)
		if e != nil {
			return e
		}
		if !ok {
			return nil
		}
	}
	result, err := s.Apply(ctx, id, hygiene.ApplyOptions{WriterStopped: writerStopped, Guard: h.guard})
	return h.output(result, err)
}

func (b feedbackStartBackend) CreateLocked(ctx context.Context, snapshot feedback.RepairSnapshot) (feedback.RepairBinding, error) {
	binding := feedback.RepairBinding{}
	app, err := b.freshApp()
	if err != nil {
		return binding, err
	}
	if feedbackConfigRevision(app.Cfg) != snapshot.ConfigRevision {
		return binding, feedback.ErrStale
	}
	r, err := resolveStartRepository(ctx, app, snapshot.Source.Path)
	if err != nil {
		return binding, err
	}
	reportID := strings.TrimPrefix(snapshot.Branch, "fix/feedback-")
	spec, err := buildStartSpecForRepository(ctx, app, r, startRequest{Name: "Repair dev feedback " + reportID, Branch: snapshot.Branch, Base: snapshot.BaseRef, Mode: task.ModeWorktree, NoProvision: true, NoRuntime: true, Submodules: "none", Next: "Review feedback " + reportID + "; dev prompt render feedback-fix " + reportID})
	if err != nil {
		return binding, err
	}
	spec.WorktreePath, err = pathx.Canonical(spec.WorktreePath)
	if err != nil {
		return binding, err
	}
	if spec.WorktreePath != snapshot.Checkout {
		return binding, feedback.ErrStale
	}
	spec.BaseOID = snapshot.BaseOID
	spec.RequireNewTask = true
	result, createErr := executeStartSpecLocked(ctx, app, spec, io.Discard)
	if result == nil || result.Worktree == nil || result.Worktree.Path == "" {
		return binding, createErr
	}
	identity, identityErr := gitx.DirectoryIdentity(result.Worktree.Path)
	binding = feedback.RepairBinding{Snapshot: snapshot, CheckoutIdentity: identity, TaskSaved: result.TaskSaved, Partial: createErr != nil || identityErr != nil}

```text
# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and releases use [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.2.38] - 2026-09-15

### Added

- Generated SSH keys can use a custom name and folder under `~/.ssh`: one missing
  folder directly under `~/.ssh` is created with mode `0700` and shown in the plan,
  and blocked paths name their reason. The terminal key picker and the dashboard's
  **+ Generate a new key** now ask for the key path and an optional comment.
- SSH keys held by Bitwarden, 1Password or Secretive agents (or a validated custom socket) can be
  listed with `dev ssh key list --agent` and selected in the setup key pickers or
  with `dev ssh setup --identity-agent`, so no private key file is needed. Dev
  publishes only the public key and writes a v2 managed alias with `IdentityAgent`;
  `dev doctor` warns when a provider is installed but no usable socket is found.
  dev v0.2.37 and older refuse setup/remove on v2 aliases. Explicit named/custom
  agent selection currently fails closed on native Windows and during remote
  fleet-source imports; normal registration to fleet/Herdr remains supported.
- Explicit interactive FIDO SSH key generation adds `ed25519-sk` / `ecdsa-sk`,
  provider, resident, verify-required and application options to CLI/dashboard
  setup. Native touch/PIN interaction retains selected-key and host-key guards;
  preview names the toolchain and uncertainty, and failures report retained or
  unknown hardware effects separately from local files. Known incompatible tools
  block without probing hardware. Automatic Secure Enclave creation, native
  Windows-controller hardware generation and new hardware generation during
  remote fleet-source imports remain unavailable.
- Explicit vault-key creation adds a standalone `dev ssh key create` workflow and
  setup-picker handoffs for 1Password, Bitwarden desktop and experimental
  Bitwarden in-memory/native-context creation. Bitwarden requires separate memory
  and native-profile approvals, freezes its actual execution context, and never
  claims endpoint attestation. Exact public receipts survive missing agent
  visibility or later SSH cancellation; creation and SSH authentication stay
  separate, with no automatic retry, key import or vault-item deletion.

### Fixed

- Bitwarden native-context permission capture no longer rejects an unchanged
  profile solely because unrelated directory entries change a shared directory's
  ctime. Inode, owner, mode and stable ACL observations remain required; regular
  file and symlink change-time checks are unchanged.
- The dashboard FLEET view reloads its host list after SSH setup registers a
  fleet or Herdr host, instead of showing it only after restarting the CLI. A
  partial SSH setup now names the unfinished steps, such as `lab herdr: unknown`.
- SSH key-setup previews label inherited endpoint values as native configuration
  instead of displaying port `0`, and omit empty managed-directory headings.
- SSH agent inventory distinguishes a genuine empty response from an agent query
  failure. Provider command capture also bounds inherited-pipe cleanup after exit
  or cancellation instead of waiting indefinitely for descendants to close output.

## [0.2.37] - 2026-09-14

### Added

- `dev ssh setup <alias>` on a terminal without `--key` or `--generate-key` opens
----

An unselected native-only ProxyCommand session may connect after fresh static and
effective-source checks. It does not expose reconstructed route/proof authority;
opaque route import, cycles and unsupported selected-key flows stay rejected.

## Repository hygiene

`dev hygiene` provides staged/worktree/history scopes, per-repo block/warn/off
policies, private local identity imports and reviewed text replacement/recovery on
macOS, Linux and Windows. CI uses public rules only. See the
[hygiene workflow](../guides/hygiene.md) for schema-v1 coverage and hook contracts.

`hygiene repair-encoding --file PATH [--invalid replace|remove]` previews
working-file UTF-8 repair; `--apply --plan ID --yes` applies the reviewed plan,
with `--writer-stopped` required for artifacts. Index bytes stay unchanged.
Schema 1 retains `unsupported_text_encoding` and adds optional `encoding`
diagnostics and historical `commit` to coverage gaps; repair plan files also
carry encoding diagnostics. Repair does not claim a successful secret scan.

## Hygiene rollout and selected skill removal

Repository hygiene is a developer commit procedure and needs no installed agent
skill. Batch migration retains specialized legacy finalizers and custom settings;
it does not yet replace the full agent-history-hygiene lifecycle. Gitleaks 8.30+
compatible 8.x is required by setup/scan. Cached machine imports never query
remote hosts or credential providers.

Skill removal requires verified native ownership or a bundled install manifest,
explicit agent scopes and dependency checks. Windows npm-shim removal uses system
PowerShell and bounded process-tree cancellation; unsupported shell syntax or
other shim mutation actions fail closed. The dedicated native removal tests are
required; broad advisory Windows test conclusions are not proof that every
legacy suite passed.
----
saved-reference resolver. Remote source-to-target credentials are outside the
controller save flow. See [SSH workflows](../guides/ssh-hosts.md#fleet-source-profiles-and-local-routes).

## Repository hygiene

`dev hygiene` provides staged/worktree/history scopes, per-repo block/warn/off
policies, private local identity imports and reviewed text replacement/recovery on
macOS, Linux and Windows. CI uses public rules only. See the
[hygiene workflow](../guides/hygiene.md) for schema-v1 coverage and hook contracts.

`hygiene repair-encoding --file PATH [--invalid replace|remove]` previews
working-file UTF-8 repair; `--apply --plan ID --yes` applies the reviewed plan,
with `--writer-stopped` required for artifacts. Index bytes stay unchanged.
Schema 1 retains `unsupported_text_encoding` and adds optional `encoding`
diagnostics and historical `commit` to coverage gaps; repair plan files also
carry encoding diagnostics. Repair does not claim a successful secret scan.

`hygiene manage [repo...] [--all]` opens batch repository setup; `--json` is
preview-only. `setup --migrate-hooks` previews narrow known-hook/rule migration.
`rules import --from machines` reads private candidates from existing local
Tailscale/LAN/Fleet caches. `skill manage` also removes selected owned skills with
explicit agent scopes; existing bundled `skill uninstall` keeps its meaning.

func (h *hygieneCLI) service(ctx context.Context) (*hygiene.Service, error) {
	root := h.repo
	if root == "" {
		root = mustGetwd()
	}
	root = config.Expand(root)
	return hygiene.Open(ctx, hygiene.Options{Root: root, CacheDir: sshDiscoveryCacheDir(), StateDir: h.app.Cfg.StateDir(), GlobalPolicy: filepath.Join(config.ConfigHome(), "dev", "hygiene.toml"), Override: hygiene.Policy{Secrets: hygiene.Mode(h.secrets), Known: hygiene.Mode(h.known), Generic: hygiene.Mode(h.generic)}, PublicOnly: h.publicOnly})
}
func (h *hygieneCLI) base(ctx context.Context) (*hygiene.Service, error) {
	copy := *h
	copy.secrets = ""
	copy.known = ""
	copy.generic = ""
	copy.publicOnly = false
	return copy.service(ctx)
}
func (h *hygieneCLI) output(value any, err error) error {
	if h.json {
		data, e := json.Marshal(value)
		if e != nil {
			return e
		}
		var safe any
		if e = json.Unmarshal(data, &safe); e != nil {
			return e
		}
		textFields := map[string]bool{"detail": true, "notices": true, "file": true, "rule": true, "reason": true, "replacement": true, "source": true, "visibility_source": true, "paths": true, "completed": true, "id": true}
		var scrub func(any, string) any
		scrub = func(v any, key string) any {
			switch x := v.(type) {
			case string:
				if textFields[key] {
					return feedback.Sanitize(x)
				}
			case []any:
				for i := range x {
					x[i] = scrub(x[i], key)
				}
			case map[string]any:
				for k := range x {
					x[k] = scrub(x[k], k)
				}
			}
			return v
		}

		enc := json.NewEncoder(h.app.Out)
		enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
		if e = enc.Encode(scrub(safe, "")); e != nil {
			return e
		}
	} else {
		switch v := value.(type) {
		case hygiene.Report:
			fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "Hygiene %s · %s · %d files · %d blocking / %d warning findings\nReport %s\n", v.Scope, v.Status, v.Files, v.Blocked, v.Warnings, v.ID)
			for _, f := range v.Findings {
				fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "  %s  %s:%d  %s ×%d  %s\n", f.Disposition, feedback.Sanitize(f.File), f.Line, feedback.Sanitize(f.Rule), f.Occurrences, f.ID)
			}
			for _, g := range v.Skipped {
				fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "  excluded: %s %s\n", g.Code, feedback.Sanitize(g.File))
			}
			for _, g := range v.Gaps {
				fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "  coverage: %s %s\n", g.Code, feedback.Sanitize(g.File))
				if g.Encoding != nil {
					h.encodingDetail(g.Encoding)
				}
				if g.Commit != "" {
					fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "    commit: %s\n", feedback.Sanitize(g.Commit))
				}
			}
			if len(v.Gaps) > 0 {
				fmt.Fprintln(h.app.Out, "Scan incomplete: coverage gaps must be resolved; warning findings do not block commits.")
				for _, g := range v.Gaps {
					if g.Encoding != nil {
						fmt.Fprintln(h.app.Out, "Inspect dev hygiene repair-encoding --help for selected working-file repair. It preserves the index; review and stage the repair before rescanning staged content. Historical blobs require a separate history assessment.")
						break
					}
				}
			}
		case hygiene.Plan:
			fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "%s · %s\nPlan %s\n", v.Kind, v.Status, v.ID)
			if v.ReviewFile != "" {
				fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "Private full proposal: dev hygiene review-path %s\n", v.ID)
			}
			for _, f := range v.Files {
				fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "  %s · %d replacements · %s → %s\n", feedback.Sanitize(f.File), f.Replacements, f.BeforeDigest, f.AfterDigest)
				if f.Encoding != nil {
					h.encodingDetail(f.Encoding)
				}
			}
			for _, notice := range v.Notices {
				fmt.Fprintln(h.app.Out, feedback.Sanitize(notice))
			}
			if v.HookAction != "" {
				fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "Hook: %s\n", v.HookAction)
			}
			if v.RequiresWriterStopped {
				fmt.Fprintln(h.app.Out, "Artifact writes require the exact writer to stop before --apply --writer-stopped.")
			}
			for _, r := range v.Recovery {
				fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "Recovery receipt: %s\n", r)
			}
		case hygiene.Status:
			fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "Hook: %s (%s) · configured: %t\nPolicy: secrets=%s known=%s generic=%s\nRemote visibility: %s (never changes policy automatically)\n", v.Hook, v.HookScope, v.Configured, v.Policy.Secrets, v.Policy.Known, v.Policy.Generic, v.Visibility)
			for _, name := range []string{"pre-commit", "gitleaks"} {
				fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "%s: %s\n", name, v.Tools[name])
			}
			for _, g := range v.Gaps {
				fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "  gap: %s\n", g)
			}
		case hygiene.Candidates:
			fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "Private candidates · complete: %t\n", v.Complete)
			for _, c := range v.Items {
				fmt.Fprintf(h.app.Out, "  %s  %s · %s:%d · recommend %s\n", c.ID, c.Kind, c.Source, c.Line, c.Recommended)
			}
		default:
			enc := json.NewEncoder(h.app.Out)
			if e := enc.Encode(value); e != nil {
				return e
			}
		}
	}
	if err != nil {
		return errors.New(feedback.Sanitize(err.Error()))
	}
	return nil
}

21	// candidate is something already on the machine that could become a task.
22	type candidate struct {
23		Task   *task.Task
24		Reason string
25	}

27	func newAdoptCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
28		var (
29			apply       bool
30			yes         bool
31			noWorktrees bool
32			noSessions  bool
33			noBranches  bool
34			state       string
35		)
36		cmd := &cobra.Command{
37			Use:   "adopt",
38			Short: "Import existing worktrees, sessions and branches as tasks",
39			Long: `Bring what is already on this machine under dev's inventory.
40	
41	There is nothing to migrate to start using dev — repositories are discovered
42	wherever your scan roots point, and no directory is moved or renamed. What is
43	worth importing is the work already in flight: linked worktrees created by
44	hand or by another tool, runtime sessions sitting in a repo, and local
45	branches that are ahead of their base.
46	
47	Reports by default. Nothing is created without --apply, and nothing on disk is
48	ever moved, renamed or deleted by this command.`,
49			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
50			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
51				ctx := ctxOf()
52	
53				target, err := task.ParseState(state)
54				if err != nil {
55					return err
56				}
57	
58				repos, err := repo.Discover(ctx, app.Cfg.DiscoveryRoots(), repo.DefaultOptions())
59				if err != nil {
60					return err
61				}
62				existing, err := app.Tasks.List()
63				if err != nil {
64					return err
65				}
66				known := map[string]bool{}
67				for _, t := range existing {
68					known[t.ID] = true
69				}
70	
71				rt := app.Runtime()
72				var sessions []runtime.Session
73				if !noSessions {
74					sessions, _ = rt.List(ctx)
75				}
76	
77				var found []candidate
78				for _, r := range repos {
79					if r.Bare {
80						continue
81					}
82					found = append(found, scanRepo(ctx, app, r, sessions, known, target,
83						!noWorktrees, !noSessions, !noBranches)...)
84				}
85	
86				if len(found) == 0 {
87					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to adopt — everything in flight is already tracked.")
88					return nil
89				}
90	
91				sort.Slice(found, func(i, j int) bool {
92					if found[i].Task.Repo != found[j].Task.Repo {
93						return found[i].Task.Repo < found[j].Task.Repo
94					}
95					return found[i].Task.Branch < found[j].Task.Branch
96				})
97	
98				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%d candidate(s):\n\n", len(found))
99				t := app.newTable("REPO", "BRANCH", "STATE", "WHY", "CHECKOUT")
100				style := app.outStyle()
101				for _, c := range found {
102					t.Add(truncate(c.Task.Repo, 24), truncate(c.Task.Branch, 28),
103						style.taskState(c.Task.State.Label()), c.Reason, config.Contract(checkoutOf(c.Task)))
104				}
105				t.Render(app.Out)
106	
107				if !apply {
108					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "\nRe-run with --apply to record these as tasks.")
109					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing on disk is moved or renamed either way.")
110					return nil
111				}
112	
113				in := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
114				adopted := 0
115				stateExplicit := cmd.Flags().Changed("state")
116				for _, c := range found {
117					if !yes && !confirm(app, in, fmt.Sprintf("adopt %s / %s", c.Task.Repo, c.Task.Branch)) {
118						continue
119					}
120					if c.Task.EffectiveMode() == task.ModeWorktree && c.Task.WorktreePath != "" {
121						locator, locateErr := exactUnmanagedWorktreeLocator(ctx, c.Task.RepoPath, c.Task.WorktreePath)
122						if locateErr != nil {
123							app.warnf("%s: %v", c.Task.Branch, locateErr)
124							continue
125						}
126						requestedState := task.State("")
127						if stateExplicit {
128							requestedState = target
129						}
130						_, applyErr := executeNonTaskLifecycle(ctx, app, locator, flow.AdoptOptions{
131							Mode: task.ModeWorktree, State: requestedState,
132							Name: c.Task.Name, Base: c.Task.Base, Owner: c.Task.Owner,
133							Next: c.Task.Next, Note: c.Task.Note, Tags: flow.NewStringList(c.Task.Tags...),
134						}, false)
135						if applyErr != nil {
136							app.warnf("%s: %v", c.Task.Branch, applyErr)
137							continue
138						}
139					} else if _, createErr := app.Tasks.Create(ctx, c.Task); createErr != nil {
140						app.warnf("%s: %v", c.Task.Branch, createErr)
141						continue
142					}
143					adopted++
144				}
145				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "\nadopted %d task(s) — see them with `dev ls`\n", adopted)
146				if adopted > 0 {
147					fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Give each one a next action so parking it stays cheap: dev park <task> --next \"…\"")
148				}
149				return nil
150			},
151		}
152		f := cmd.Flags()
153		f.BoolVar(&apply, "apply", false, "record the candidates as tasks")
154		f.BoolVar(&yes, "yes", false, "with --apply, do not confirm each one")
155		f.BoolVar(&noWorktrees, "no-worktrees", false, "skip existing linked worktrees")
156		f.BoolVar(&noSessions, "no-sessions", false, "skip live runtime sessions")
157		f.BoolVar(&noBranches, "no-branches", false, "skip local branches ahead of their base")
158		f.StringVar(&state, "state", string(task.Warm), "state to record adopted tasks in ("+task.JoinStates(", ")+")")
159		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "state", taskStateCompletions())
160		return cmd
161	}
162	
163	// scanRepo collects everything in one repository that looks like work in
164	// flight but is not yet recorded.
165	func scanRepo(ctx context.Context, app *App, r repo.Repo, sessions []runtime.Session,
166		known map[string]bool, target task.State, doWorktrees, doSessions, doBranches bool) []candidate {
167	
168		var out []candidate
169		seen := map[string]bool{}
170	
171		add := func(branch, worktree, reason string, state task.State) {
172			if branch == "" || seen[branch] {
173				return
174			}
175			id := task.MakeID(r.Name, branch)
176			if known[id] {
177				return
178			}
179			seen[branch] = true
180			mode := task.ModeBranch
181			if worktree != "" {
182				mode = task.ModeWorktree
183			}
184			out = append(out, candidate{
185				Reason: reason,
186				Task: &task.Task{
187					ID:           id,
188					Name:         branch,
189					Repo:         r.Name,
190					RepoPath:     r.Path,
191					Branch:       branch,
192					Base:         gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, r.Path),
193					WorktreePath: worktree,
194					Mode:         mode,
195					State:        state,
196					Owner:        config.Hostname(),
197				},
198			})
199		}
200	
201		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, r.Path)
202		if err != nil {
203			return nil
204		}
205	
206		if doWorktrees {
207			for _, w := range worktrees {
208				if w.Main || w.Branch == "" || w.Prunable {
209					continue
210				}
211				// A harness's turn-scoped worktree is not a change stream a human
212				// tracks; adopting those would fill the inventory with noise that
213				// the harness will delete on its own.
214				if inventory.IsEphemeralWorktree(w.Path, w.Branch) {
215					continue
216				}
217				state := target
218				reason := "existing worktree"
219				if sessionAt(sessions, w.Path) != nil {
220					state, reason = task.Hot, "worktree with a live session"
221				}
222				add(w.Branch, w.Path, reason, state)
223			}
224		}
225	
226		if doSessions {
227			for i := range sessions {
228				for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
229					if d != r.Path {
230						continue
231					}
232					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
233					if err != nil || st.Branch == "" {
234						continue
235					}
236					add(st.Branch, "", "live session in the main checkout", task.Hot)
237				}
238			}
239		}
240	
241		if doBranches {
242			for _, branch := range unmergedBranches(ctx, r.Path) {
243				add(branch, worktreePathFor(worktrees, branch), "branch ahead of the base", target)
244			}
245		}
246		return out
247	}
248	
249	func sessionAt(sessions []runtime.Session, dir string) *runtime.Session {
250		for i := range sessions {
251			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
252				if d == dir {
253					return &sessions[i]
254				}
255			}
256		}
257		return nil
258	}
259	
260	func worktreePathFor(worktrees []gitx.Worktree, branch string) string {
261		for _, w := range worktrees {
262			if w.Branch == branch && !w.Main {
263				return w.Path
264			}
265		}
266		return ""
267	}
268	
269	// unmergedBranches lists local branches carrying commits the default branch
270	// does not — unfinished work that would otherwise be invisible to dev.
271	func unmergedBranches(ctx context.Context, repoPath string) []string {
272		base := gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
273		if base == "" {
274			return nil
275		}
276		out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname:short)", "refs/heads/")
277		if err != nil {
278			return nil
279		}
280		var branches []string
281		for _, b := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
282			b = strings.TrimSpace(b)
283			if b == "" || b == base || inventory.IsEphemeralWorktree("", b) {
284				continue
285			}
286			// Contained in the base means the work has already landed.
287			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", b, base); err == nil {
288				continue
289			}
290			branches = append(branches, b)
291		}
292		return branches
293	}

32	func (s *lifecycleService) adoptHandler() Handler {

39	func validateAdoptLocator(locator Locator) error {
40		switch {
41		case locator.TaskID != "":
42			return fmt.Errorf("%w: unmanaged adoption must not carry a TaskID", ErrInvalidRequest)
43		case locator.TaskRevision != "":
44			return fmt.Errorf("%w: unmanaged adoption must not carry a task revision", ErrInvalidRequest)
45		case locator.RepoPath == "":
46			return fmt.Errorf("%w: exact repository path is required", ErrInvalidRequest)
47		case locator.GitCommonDir == "":
48			return fmt.Errorf("%w: exact Git common directory is required", ErrInvalidRequest)
49		case locator.CheckoutPath == "":
50			return fmt.Errorf("%w: exact checkout path is required", ErrInvalidRequest)
51		case locator.Branch == "":
52			return fmt.Errorf("%w: exact named branch is required", ErrInvalidRequest)
53		case locator.HeadOID == "":
54			return fmt.Errorf("%w: exact checkout HEAD is required", ErrInvalidRequest)
55		case strings.TrimSpace(locator.Branch) != locator.Branch || strings.ContainsRune(locator.Branch, '\x00'):
56			return fmt.Errorf("%w: exact branch is not normalized", ErrInvalidRequest)
57		case locator.Mode != "" && locator.Mode != task.ModeWorktree:
58			return fmt.Errorf("%w: unmanaged linked-checkout mode must be empty or %q", ErrInvalidRequest, task.ModeWorktree)
59		}
60		return nil
61	}

63	func (s *lifecycleService) planAdopt(ctx context.Context, request Request) (PlanSpec, error) {
64		if err := contextError(ctx); err != nil {
65			return PlanSpec{}, err
66		}
67		if err := validateAdoptLocator(request.Locator); err != nil {
68			return PlanSpec{}, err
69		}
70		commonDir, err := s.canonicalPath(request.Locator.GitCommonDir)
71		if err != nil {
72			return PlanSpec{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize requested repository lock identity: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, err)
73		}
74	
75		var spec PlanSpec
76		err = s.repoLock(ctx, commonDir, func() error {
77			return s.tasks.WithLock(ctx, func(tx *task.Tx) error {
78				var observeErr error
79				spec, _, observeErr = s.observeAdopt(ctx, request, tx.ListRecords)
80				return observeErr
81			})
82		})
83		return spec, err
84	}

86	func (s *lifecycleService) observeAdopt(ctx context.Context, request Request, loader taskInventoryLoader) (PlanSpec, adoptObservation, error) {
87		options := request.Options.(AdoptOptions)
88		base := options.Base
89		if base == "" {
90			base = s.gitDefaultBranch(ctx, request.Locator.RepoPath)
91		}
92	
93		rt, rtErr := s.runtimeForUnmanaged()
94		destructive, err := s.inspectDestructive(ctx, destructiveInspectInput{
95			locator: request.Locator,
96			runtime: rt,
97			rtErr:   rtErr,
98	
99			skipCleanup:  true,
100			inspectTasks: true,
101			loadTasks:    loader,
102		})
103		if rtErr == nil && rt != nil {
104			destructive.runtimeAvailable = rt.Available()
105		}
106		observed := adoptObservation{destructiveObservation: destructive, base: base}
107		if err != nil {
108			return PlanSpec{}, observed, err
109		}
110		if destructive.repoPath != "" && base != "" {
111			observed.baseExists, observed.baseOIDErr = s.gitRefState(ctx, destructive.repoPath, base)
112			if observed.baseExists && observed.baseOIDErr == nil {
113				observed.baseOID, observed.baseOIDErr = s.resolveRefOID(ctx, destructive.repoPath, base)
114			}
115		}
116	
117		observed.taskID = task.MakeID(destructive.repo.Name, request.Locator.Branch)
118		appendAdoptIDClaim(&observed.destructiveObservation, observed.taskID)
119		if destructive.worktreeFound && rtErr == nil {
120			observed.occupancy, observed.occupancyErr = s.inspectOccupancy(ctx, rt, destructive.checkout, runtime.OccupancyOptions{
121				Profile:           runtime.OccupancyStrict,
122				CallerWorkspaceID: s.callerWorkspace,
123				CallerPaneID:      s.callerPane,
124			})
125		}
126		observed.derivedState, observed.runtimeName, observed.runtimeHandle, observed.stateEvidence = deriveAdoptState(observed)
127		observed.candidate = task.Task{
128			ID: observed.taskID, Name: options.Name,
129			Repo: destructive.repo.Name, RepoPath: destructive.repoPath,
130			Branch: request.Locator.Branch, Base: base,
131			WorktreePath: destructive.checkout, Mode: task.ModeWorktree,
132			State: observed.derivedState, Owner: s.host,
133			Next: options.Next, Note: options.Note, Tags: options.Tags.Values(),
134			RuntimeName: observed.runtimeName, RuntimeHandle: observed.runtimeHandle,
135		}
136		return s.adoptSpec(request, observed), observed, nil
137	}

139	func appendAdoptIDClaim(observed *destructiveObservation, taskID string) {
140		if observed == nil || taskID == "" {
141			return
142		}
143		for _, record := range observed.taskRecords {
144			if record.Task.ID != taskID {
145				continue
146			}
147			for index := range observed.taskClaims {
148				if observed.taskClaims[index].ID == taskID {
149					if !strings.Contains(observed.taskClaims[index].Reason, "derived task ID") {
150						observed.taskClaims[index].Reason += " and derived task ID"
151					}
152					sortAdoptClaims(observed.taskClaims)
153					return
154				}
155			}
156			observed.taskClaims = append(observed.taskClaims, destructiveTaskClaim{
157				ID: taskID, Revision: record.Revision, Reason: "derived task ID",
158			})
159			sortAdoptClaims(observed.taskClaims)
160			return
161		}
162	}
163	
164	func sortAdoptClaims(claims []destructiveTaskClaim) {
165		sort.Slice(claims, func(i, j int) bool {
166			if claims[i].ID != claims[j].ID {
167				return claims[i].ID < claims[j].ID
168			}
169			return claims[i].Reason < claims[j].Reason
170		})
171	}

173	func deriveAdoptState(observed adoptObservation) (task.State, string, string, string) {
174		rt := observed.runtime
175		switch {
176		case observed.runtimeErr != nil:
177			return task.Warm, "", "", "runtime backend resolution failed; adoption remains WARM"
178		case rt == nil || strings.TrimSpace(rt.Name()) == "":
179			return task.Warm, "", "", "runtime backend is unavailable; adoption remains WARM"
180		case rt.Name() == "none":
181			return task.Warm, "", "", "runtime none leaves session and recognized-agent evidence unobserved; adoption remains WARM"
182		case !observed.runtimeAvailable:
183			return task.Warm, "", "", "runtime backend is unavailable; adoption remains WARM"
184		case !observed.worktreeFound:
185			return task.Warm, "", "", "exact checkout is unavailable; adoption remains WARM"
186		case adoptStrictOccupancyError(observed.occupancy, observed.occupancyErr) != nil:
187			return task.Warm, "", "", "strict runtime occupancy is not ready; adoption remains WARM"
188		case !observed.occupancy.SessionList.Observed():
189			return task.Warm, "", "", "runtime sessions were not freshly observed; adoption remains WARM"
190		case !observed.occupancy.AgentActivityList.Observed():
191			return task.Warm, "", "", "recognized-agent activity was not freshly observed; adoption remains WARM"
192		case len(observed.occupancy.Sessions) != 1:
193			return task.Warm, "", "", fmt.Sprintf("fresh runtime coverage contains %d sessions, not exactly one; adoption remains WARM", len(observed.occupancy.Sessions))
194		case len(observed.occupancy.Agents) != 0:
195			return task.Warm, "", "", "a recognized agent occupies the checkout; adoption remains WARM"
196		}
197	
198		session := observed.occupancy.Sessions[0]
199		handle := session.Runtime.Handle
200		if strings.TrimSpace(handle) == "" || strings.TrimSpace(handle) != handle || strings.ContainsRune(handle, '\x00') {
201			return task.Warm, "", "", "the sole covering runtime session has no stable nonempty handle; adoption remains WARM"
202		}
203		if !adoptSessionShellOnly(session) {
204			return task.Warm, "", "", "the sole covering runtime session is not shell-only; adoption remains WARM"
205		}
206		return task.Hot, rt.Name(), handle, "exactly one freshly observed shell-only runtime session covers the checkout with stable handle " + handle
207	}
208	
209	func adoptStrictOccupancyError(occupancy runtime.Occupancy, err error) error {
210		if occupancyErr := strictOccupancyError(occupancy, err); occupancyErr != nil {
211			return occupancyErr
212		}
213		var blockers []string
214		for _, session := range occupancy.Sessions {
215			// OccupancySession.Panes contains only panes whose live cwd covers the
216			// checkout. A mixed session may also host an unrelated agent elsewhere;
217			// that agent is not a writer claim on this checkout.
218			for _, pane := range session.Panes {
219				if strings.TrimSpace(pane.Agent) == "" && strings.TrimSpace(pane.AgentSession) == "" {
220					continue
221				}
222				if occupancy.CallerPaneID != "" && pane.ID == occupancy.CallerPaneID {
223					continue
224				}
225				status := strings.TrimSpace(pane.AgentStatus)
226				if status == "" {
227					status = "unknown"
228				}
229				blockers = append(blockers, fmt.Sprintf("recognized agent pane %s (%s)", pane.ID, status))
230			}
231		}
232		if len(blockers) > 0 {
233			return fmt.Errorf("checkout is occupied by %s", strings.Join(blockers, ", "))
234		}
235		return nil
236	}
237	
238	func adoptSessionShellOnly(session runtime.OccupancySession) bool {
239		if strings.TrimSpace(session.Runtime.AgentStatus) != "" || len(session.Runtime.AgentSessions) != 0 {
240			return false
241		}
242		panes := session.Runtime.Panes
243		if len(panes) == 0 {
244			panes = session.Panes
245		}
246		for _, pane := range panes {
247			if strings.TrimSpace(pane.Agent) != "" || strings.TrimSpace(pane.AgentStatus) != "" || strings.TrimSpace(pane.AgentSession) != "" {
248				return false
249			}
250		}
251		return true
252	}

254	func (s *lifecycleService) adoptSpec(request Request, observed adoptObservation) PlanSpec {
255		conditions := []Condition{retireRepositoryCondition(observed.destructiveObservation)}
256		conditions = append(conditions, adoptIdentityConditions(observed.destructiveObservation)...)
257		conditions = append(conditions, adoptBaseCondition(observed))
258		conditions = append(conditions, adoptTaskInventoryConditions(observed.destructiveObservation)...)
259		conditions = append(conditions, adoptRuntimeConditions(observed)...)
260		conditions = append(conditions, adoptStateCondition(request.Options.(AdoptOptions), observed))
261		conditions = append(conditions, condition(
262			ConditionOwner, VerdictMet, RequirementAdvisory,
263			"adoption assigns checkout ownership to host "+s.host, "",
264		))
265	
266		details := map[string]string{
267			"id": observed.taskID, "repo": observed.candidate.Repo,
268			"repo-path": observed.candidate.RepoPath, "checkout": observed.candidate.WorktreePath,
269			"branch": observed.candidate.Branch, "head": observed.locator.HeadOID,
270			"base": observed.candidate.Base, "base-oid": observed.baseOID,
271			"mode": string(observed.candidate.Mode), "state": string(observed.candidate.State),
272			"owner": observed.candidate.Owner, "runtime": observed.candidate.RuntimeName,
273			"runtime-handle": observed.candidate.RuntimeHandle,
274		}
275		effect := NewEffect(
276			EffectCreateTask, "create one task record for the exact unmanaged linked checkout",
277			observed.taskID, false, false, details,
278		)
279		retained := []string{
280			"checkout:" + observed.checkout,
281			"branch:" + observed.locator.Branch + "@" + observed.branchOID,
282		}
283		if observed.derivedState == task.Hot {
284			retained = append(retained, "runtime:"+observed.runtimeName+":"+observed.runtimeHandle)
285		}
286		return PlanSpec{
287			Authority:         adoptAuthority(observed),
288			Conditions:        conditions,
289			Effects:           []Effect{effect},
290			RetainedResources: retained,
291			Confirmation: Confirmation{
292				Kind:   ConfirmationApproval,
293				Prompt: "Adopt this exact unmanaged checkout as a " + strings.ToUpper(string(observed.derivedState)) + " worktree task?",
294			},
295			FallbackCommand: "dev adopt --apply --state " + shellQuote(string(observed.derivedState)),
296			Summary:         "Adopt unmanaged checkout " + observed.checkout,
297			DisplayedAt:     s.now(),

553	func (s *lifecycleService) applyAdopt(ctx context.Context, approved Plan) (Result, error) {
554		if err := contextError(ctx); err != nil {
555			return Result{}, err
556		}
557		if approved.Action != Adopt {
558			return Result{}, &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: approved.PlanID, Reason: "adopt handler received " + string(approved.Action)}
559		}
560		if err := validateAdoptLocator(approved.Locator); err != nil {
561			return Result{}, err
562		}
563		commonDir, err := s.canonicalPath(approved.Locator.GitCommonDir)
564		if err != nil {
565			return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize approved repository lock identity: %v", ErrInvalidPlan, err)
566		}
567	
568		var result Result
569		err = s.repoLock(ctx, commonDir, func() error {
570			return s.tasks.WithLock(ctx, func(tx *task.Tx) error {
571				spec, observed, observeErr := s.observeAdopt(ctx, approved.Request, tx.ListRecords)
572				if observeErr != nil {
573					return observeErr
574				}
575				fresh, buildErr := BuildPlan(approved.Request, spec)
576				if buildErr != nil {
577					return buildErr
578				}
579				if fresh.PlanID != approved.PlanID || fresh.AuthorityFingerprint != approved.AuthorityFingerprint {
580					return &StalePlanError{
581						ExpectedPlanID: approved.PlanID, ActualPlanID: fresh.PlanID,
582						ExpectedAuthorityFingerprint: approved.AuthorityFingerprint,
583						ActualAuthorityFingerprint:   fresh.AuthorityFingerprint,
584						Reason:                       "fresh unmanaged Git, worktree, task, base, runtime, agent, or harness authority differs",
585					}
586				}
587				if fresh.Availability != AvailabilityReady {
588					notReady := &PlanNotReadyError{PlanID: fresh.PlanID, Availability: fresh.Availability, conditions: fresh.Conditions()}
589					return &InvalidPlanError{PlanID: fresh.PlanID, Reason: "fresh adoption conditions are not ready", Cause: notReady}
590				}
591				execution := &executionState{service: s, plan: fresh, tx: tx}
592				result, observeErr = execution.executeAdopt(observed)
593				return observeErr
594			})
595		})
596		return result, err
597	}
598	
599	func (e *executionState) executeAdopt(observed adoptObservation) (Result, error) {
600		effects := e.plan.Effects()
601		if len(effects) != 1 || effects[0].Code != EffectCreateTask {
602			return e.fail(&InvalidPlanError{PlanID: e.plan.PlanID, Reason: "Adopt must contain exactly one create-task effect"})
603		}
604		if observed.runtime != nil && observed.runtime.Name() == "none" {
605			e.warnings = append(e.warnings, "runtime none left occupancy unobserved; the adopted task is WARM")
606		}
607	
608		effect := effects[0]
609		expected := observed.candidate
610		expected.Tags = append([]string(nil), observed.candidate.Tags...)
611		err := e.run(effect, func() (string, error) {
612			candidate := expected
613			candidate.Tags = append([]string(nil), expected.Tags...)
614			created, createErr := e.service.taskCreate(e.tx, &candidate)
615			if createErr != nil {
616				return "task create made no authorized non-task change", fmt.Errorf("create adopted task %s: %w", expected.ID, createErr)
617			}
618			if created == nil || created.Revision == "" {
619				return "task create returned no revision", errors.New("create adopted task returned no revision")
620			}
621			if adoptTaskAuthority(created.Task) != adoptTaskAuthority(expected) {
622				return "task create returned different metadata", errors.New("created task does not match the approved adoption metadata")
623			}
624			persisted, verifyErr := e.tx.GetRecord(expected.ID)
625			if verifyErr != nil {
626				return "task create was not verified", fmt.Errorf("verify created adopted task %s: %w", expected.ID, verifyErr)
627			}
628			if persisted.Revision != created.Revision || adoptTaskAuthority(persisted.Task) != adoptTaskAuthority(expected) {
629				return "task create revision or metadata was not verified", errors.New("persisted adopted task differs from the task create result")
630			}
631			e.snapshot = "task:" + persisted.Revision
632			e.milestone = MilestoneAdopted
633			return "created task " + persisted.Task.ID + " at revision " + persisted.Revision, nil
634		})
635		if err != nil {
636			return e.fail(err, "the checkout, branch, runtime, and Git bytes were not changed; repair the task-store failure and refresh adoption")
637		}
638		if e.milestone != MilestoneAdopted || e.snapshot == "" {
639			return e.fail(&InvalidPlanError{PlanID: e.plan.PlanID, Reason: "adoption ended without a created task revision"})
640		}
641		return e.result(), nil
642	}

1	// Package task stores the small amount of state git cannot answer: which
2	// change streams exist, what state each is in, which machine owns it, and what
3	// the next action is. Everything else — branch, dirty, ahead/behind, whether a
4	// worktree exists — is derived live and deliberately not stored here.
5	package task
6	
7	import (
8		"crypto/sha256"
9		"encoding/binary"
10		"encoding/hex"
11		"fmt"
12		"strings"
13		"time"
14	)
15	
16	// State is where a change stream sits in its lifecycle.
17	type State string
18	
19	const (
20		// Hot: worktree and branch exist, a runtime session is open, actively worked on.
21		Hot State = "hot"
22		// Warm: worktree and branch kept, runtime closed. Back within days.
23		Warm State = "warm"
24		// Cold: committed and pushed, worktree removed. Reconstructible anywhere.
25		Cold State = "cold"
26		// Done: merged. Kept only until the entry is reaped.
27		Done State = "done"
28	)
29	
30	// States lists the lifecycle in order, for help text and validation.
31	var States = []State{Hot, Warm, Cold, Done}
32	
33	// ParseState validates a user-supplied state name.
34	func ParseState(s string) (State, error) {
35		got := State(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)))
36		for _, valid := range States {
37			if got == valid {
38				return got, nil
39			}
40		}
41		return "", fmt.Errorf("unknown state %q: want one of %s", s, JoinStates(", "))
42	}
43	
44	// JoinStates renders the valid state names.
45	func JoinStates(sep string) string {
46		parts := make([]string, len(States))
47		for i, s := range States {
48			parts[i] = string(s)
49		}
50		return strings.Join(parts, sep)
51	}
52	
53	// Icon is the glyph shown in the inventory.
54	func (s State) Icon() string {
55		switch s {
56		case Hot:
57			return "🔥"
58		case Warm:
59			return "🌤"
60		case Cold:
61			return "❄️"
62		case Done:
63			return "✅"
64		}
65		return "?"
66	}
67	
68	// Label is the uppercase column form.
69	func (s State) Label() string { return strings.ToUpper(string(s)) }
70	
71	// CheckoutMode is how a task occupies the repository filesystem.
72	type CheckoutMode string
73	
74	const (
75		// ModeWorktree owns a linked worktree and branch.
76		ModeWorktree CheckoutMode = "worktree"
77		// ModeBranch uses a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout.
78		ModeBranch CheckoutMode = "branch"
79		// ModeDirect tracks ad-hoc work on the branch already checked out in the
80		// canonical repo — usually main — without creating a branch or worktree.
81		ModeDirect CheckoutMode = "direct"
82	)
83	
84	// Task is one change stream. Field names are the TOML keys.
85	type Task struct {
86		// ID is derived from repo and branch; it is the filename stem and is not
87		// stored inside the file.
88		ID string `toml:"-"`
89	
90		// Name is the human label ("atp security recovery").
91		Name string `toml:"name"`
92		// Repo is the repository's display name.
93		Repo string `toml:"repo"`
94		// RepoPath is the main checkout, the directory git commands run in.
95		RepoPath string `toml:"repo_path"`
96		// Branch is the change stream's identity — the one durable handle that
97		// survives every machine, worktree and runtime.
98		Branch string `toml:"branch"`
99		// Base is the ref the branch was created from, recorded so `dev done` can
100		// integrate without re-guessing.
101		Base string `toml:"base"`
102		// WorktreePath is the linked checkout, empty when the task works directly
103		// in the main checkout or has gone cold.
104		WorktreePath string `toml:"worktree_path"`
105		// Mode says whether this task uses a worktree, a branch in the canonical
106		// checkout, or the current branch directly. Older entries infer it.
107		Mode CheckoutMode `toml:"mode"`
108	
109		State State `toml:"state"`
110		// Owner is the hostname that last held this task hot. One writer per
111		// branch at a time avoids two machines diverging the same history.
112		Owner string `toml:"owner"`
113		// Next is the single most valuable field in the file: what to do when you
114		// come back. Without it, parking a task still loses the thread.
115		Next string   `toml:"next"`
116		Note string   `toml:"note"`
117		Tags []string `toml:"tags"`
118	
119		// AgentSession reserves a resumable agent context ("claude:<uuid>"). The
120		// production start/park/resume flow does not yet capture or attach it.
121		AgentSession string `toml:"agent_session"`
122		// RuntimeHandle is the last known runtime session id (e.g. a Herdr
123		// workspace id). RuntimeName records which backend owns that opaque handle.
124		// Both are advisory and must be revalidated against live checkout coverage.
125		RuntimeHandle string `toml:"runtime_handle"`
126		RuntimeName   string `toml:"runtime_name"`
127	
128		Created time.Time `toml:"created"`
129		Updated time.Time `toml:"updated"`
130	
131		// storedRevision is populated only by Store after a successful read/write.
132		// It never enters TOML or Revision and lets legacy Save callers participate
133		// in compare-and-swap without adding a persisted field older binaries erase.
134		storedRevision string
135	}
136	
137	// Revision returns a deterministic fingerprint of the task identity and every
138	// field represented by its TOML record. It is deliberately computed rather
139	// than persisted: older dev binaries can continue to read and rewrite task
140	// files without erasing a revision field they do not know about.
141	func (t Task) Revision() string {
142		hash := sha256.New()
143		writeString := func(value string) {
144			var length [8]byte
145			binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(length[:], uint64(len(value)))
146			_, _ = hash.Write(length[:])
147			_, _ = hash.Write([]byte(value))
148		}
149		writeTime := func(value time.Time) {
150			writeString(value.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano))

179	// EffectiveMode returns the explicit mode, or infers a legacy task. Before
180	// modes were recorded, a path meant worktree and no path meant a canonical
181	// branch task; direct mode is never guessed because it changes integration
182	// semantics and must be explicit.
183	func (t Task) EffectiveMode() CheckoutMode {
184		if t.Mode != "" {
185			return t.Mode
186		}
187		if t.WorktreePath != "" {
188			return ModeWorktree
189		}
190		return ModeBranch
191	}
192	
193	// Title is the display name, falling back to the branch when unnamed.
194	func (t Task) Title() string {
195		if t.Name != "" {
196			return t.Name
197		}
198		return t.Branch
199	}
200	
201	// OwnedBy reports whether host is this task's owner. An empty owner means
202	// unclaimed, which counts as owned by anyone.
203	func (t Task) OwnedBy(host string) bool { return t.Owner == "" || t.Owner == host }
204	
205	// Validate rejects a task that could not be acted on later.
206	func (t Task) Validate() error {
207		if t.ID != "" {
208			if err := ValidateID(t.ID); err != nil {
209				return fmt.Errorf("task ID: %w", err)
210			}
211		}
212		switch {
213		case t.Repo == "":
214			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo is required", t.ID)
215		case t.Branch == "":
216			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: branch is required", t.ID)
217		case t.RepoPath == "":
218			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: repo_path is required", t.ID)
219		}
220		if _, err := ParseState(string(t.State)); err != nil {
221			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: %w", t.ID, err)
222		}
223		switch t.Mode {
224		case "", ModeWorktree, ModeBranch, ModeDirect:
225		default:
226			return fmt.Errorf("task %s: unknown mode %q", t.ID, t.Mode)
227		}
228		return nil
229	}

### `dev hygiene scan`

Scan index, working files or frozen local Git history

```
dev hygiene scan [flags]
```

- `--audit` — include findings suppressed by local exceptions, gitleaksignore and inline pragmas
- `--file` — select an in-scope relative file (repeatable; not history)
- `--range` — history only: full FROM..TO commit OIDs (no implicit fetch)
- `--scope` — scan scope: staged, worktree or history
- `--timeout` — maximum scan duration; incomplete scans fail

### `dev hygiene setup`

Preview or apply repository hygiene configuration and hook integration

```
dev hygiene setup [flags]
```

- `--apply` — apply the exact saved setup plan
- `--migrate-hooks` — preview migration of known equivalent scanner hooks and rule updates; retain finalizers and custom settings
- `--migrate-rules` — preview replacement of existing gitleaks config with bundled safe rules
- `--plan` — reviewed plan ID
- `-y, --yes` — confirm the reviewed plan

### `dev hygiene status`

Inspect effective hooks and policy without executing them

```
dev hygiene status [flags]
```

- `--check-remote` — explicitly query GitHub visibility; never change policy automatically
- `--remote` — remote to query with --check-remote

### `dev instructions`

Share AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md with guarded transfers

```
package cli

import (
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"os"
	"strings"
)

const (
	colorAuto   = "auto"
	colorAlways = "always"
	colorNever  = "never"

	ansiReset   = "\x1b[0m"
	ansiBold    = "\x1b[1m"
	ansiDim     = "\x1b[2m"
	ansiRed     = "\x1b[31m"
	ansiGreen   = "\x1b[32m"
	ansiYellow  = "\x1b[33m"
	ansiMagenta = "\x1b[35m"
	ansiCyan    = "\x1b[36m"
)

type cliStyle struct {
	enabled bool
}

func validateColorMode(mode string) error {
	switch mode {
	case "", colorAuto, colorAlways, colorNever:
		return nil
	default:
		return fmt.Errorf("invalid --color value %q: use auto, always, or never", mode)
	}
}

func styleForWriter(w io.Writer, mode string) cliStyle {
	switch mode {
	case colorAlways:
		return cliStyle{enabled: true}
	case colorNever:
		return cliStyle{}
	}
	if os.Getenv("NO_COLOR") != "" || os.Getenv("TERM") == "dumb" {
		return cliStyle{}
	}
	f, ok := w.(*os.File)
	if !ok {
		return cliStyle{}
	}
	info, err := f.Stat()
	return cliStyle{enabled: err == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeCharDevice != 0}
}

func (s cliStyle) paint(code, text string) string {
	if !s.enabled || text == "" {
		return text
	}
	return code + text + ansiReset
}

func (s cliStyle) title(text string) string   { return s.paint(ansiBold+ansiCyan, text) }
func (s cliStyle) header(text string) string  { return s.paint(ansiBold+ansiCyan, text) }
func (s cliStyle) prompt(text string) string  { return s.paint(ansiBold+ansiCyan, text) }
func (s cliStyle) label(text string) string   { return s.paint(ansiDim, text) }
func (s cliStyle) dim(text string) string     { return s.paint(ansiDim, text) }
func (s cliStyle) success(text string) string { return s.paint(ansiGreen, text) }
func (s cliStyle) warning(text string) string { return s.paint(ansiYellow, text) }
func (s cliStyle) danger(text string) string  { return s.paint(ansiBold+ansiRed, text) }
func (s cliStyle) review(text string) string  { return s.paint(ansiMagenta, text) }

// strong and code are the two roles the Markdown renderer needs. They are named
// for what they mark rather than for a colour so the palette stays in one file.
func (s cliStyle) strong(text string) string { return s.paint(ansiBold, text) }
func (s cliStyle) code(text string) string   { return s.paint(ansiCyan, text) }

func (s cliStyle) taskState(text string) string {
	return s.taskStateFor(text, text)
}
