     1	# Agent-safe worktree retirement
     2	
     3	Recursive submodule disposal is an explicit extension: verify child tasks/artifacts/runtime, local data and fresh remote recovery first, then stage children inside-out and remove the outer checkout without force. Preserve canonical/shared Git and the outer branch. A retained journal is recovered with `dev submodule recover`, not deleted using an old remote proof. See `submodules.md`.
     4	
     5	## The rule
     6	
     7	A feature agent may prepare and integrate work, but it must not destroy the
     8	runtime or checkout containing its own process. Completion has three milestones:
     9	
    10	```text
    11	READY     exact final transcript committed after the writer exits
    12	MERGED    branch integrated; runtime/worktree may still exist
    13	RETIRED   runtime absent, worktree removed, optional branch deleted, task reaped
    14	```
    15	
    16	`hot/warm/cold/done` remain the persisted task states. `done` now means MERGED,
    17	not "everything has already been deleted".
    18	
    19	## Normal local flow
    20	
    21	From the feature worktree:
    22	
    23	```bash
    24	# Commit product changes first. Do not stage the moving transcript.
    25	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid> --plan .claude/plans/task.md
    26	# Exit the agent normally so SpecStory can write its final Markdown.
    27	```
    28	
    29	The outer `specstory run` wrapper calls:
    30	
    31	```bash
    32	dev artifact finalize --run-id "$DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID" --if-pending --writer-stopped
    33	```
    34	
    35	Then an external main/integration workspace runs:
    36	
    37	```bash
    38	dev done <task> --ff
    39	dev retire <task> --delete-branch
    40	```
    41	
    42	`done` only integrates and records MERGED. `retire` re-resolves every runtime
    43	pane, closes eligible sessions, waits for them to disappear, revalidates Git,
    44	and removes the worktree without force.
    45	
    46	`dev flow [repo]` offers Retire only for an exact DONE task. Enter first shows a
    47	revision-bound plan with conditions, ordered effects, retained resources, and a
    48	CLI fallback; branch deletion needs the displayed typed token. Apply locks and
    49	reloads task/repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact authority, repeats safety
    50	checks after closure and before removal, and deletes the task last. If a later
    51	effect fails, its ledger reports completed work and recovery without claiming a
    52	rollback.
    53	
    54	For periodic cleanup from the canonical main checkout:
    55	
    56	```bash
    57	dev sweep --merged-worktrees
    58	# Present the exact candidates/blockers to the user and ask for approval.
    59	dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply --yes
    60	```
    61	
    62	This includes unmanaged linked worktrees whose named branches are already
    63	contained in main. It never treats containment alone as permission: dirty Git,
    64	pending artifacts and runtime blockers still stop cleanup. Branches remain by
    65	default; add `--delete-branches` only when the user approved that separately.
    66	
    67	Claude Workflow ephemeral worktrees use a separate, stricter path:
    68	
    69	```bash
    70	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --stale-days 14
    71	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --json
    72	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply
    73	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply --delete-branches --base main
    74	```
    75	
    76	Run it from the canonical non-bare checkout. The schema-v1 report joins one
    77	bounded, fixed-depth `~/.claude/projects` mapping to live Git state without
    78	decoding or emitting prompts, scripts, logs, result bodies, or transcript
    79	content. V1 requires workflow `completed|killed`, matching agent `done`, journal
    80	`started` and `result`, no same-ID resumed transcript, and provider inactivity
    81	older than `--stale-days` (default 14, minimum 1). Killed/no-result, progress,
    82	resume, malformed/mutating metadata, or unknown time stays `unknown`; there is no
    83	operator-attestation bypass.
    84	
    85	Ownership must also bind provider-observed branch, HEAD, common-dir, and an opaque
    86	non-replayable registration generation to the live target. Claude Code 2.1.259
    87	records no such Git identity, so current Claude Workflow claims report
    88	`provider-git-identity: unknown` and remain report-only even with `--apply`.
    89	A path, derived branch name, or reusable GitDir pathname is never a substitute;
    90	otherwise stale terminal metadata could authorize a replacement checkout at the
    91	same path.
    92	
    93	The worktree must remain registered, present, non-main, named, unlocked and
    94	non-prunable, with exact common-dir/branch/registry-HEAD/live-HEAD agreement. It
    95	must have no staged/unstaged/conflicted/untracked/ignored/recursive-submodule
    96	content, no Git operation, task claim, unsafe artifact intent, caller
    97	containment, or covering runtime. Missing, prunable, unregistered, and orphan
    98	paths are report only. Apply rejects `--yes`, `--close-unknown`,
    99	`--assume-no-runtime`, `--no-runtime`, and JSON; it requires a TTY and per-item
   100	confirmation. Under a common-dir cleanup lock it recollects every fact and
   101	compares the stable candidate fingerprint before plain non-force removal. It
   102	never prunes, closes sessions, deletes provider metadata, or rescues/stashes/
   103	commits dirty work.
   104	
   105	A branch is retained by default, so a clean checkout with unique commits may be
   106	removed safely. Optional branch deletion is a separate proof requiring an
   107	explicit base, unchanged branch/base tips, containment, zero unique commits, and
   108	ordinary `git branch -d`; any post-removal failure leaves the branch retained and
   109	reports partial completion.
   110	
   111	## Pull-request flow
   112	
   113	```bash
   114	dev done <task> --pr
   115	# after CI/review and a commit-preserving merge
   116	git fetch origin
   117	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main
   118	dev retire <task> --delete-branch
   119	```
   120	
   121	A squash merge is not ancestry-equivalent. It requires an explicit operator
   122	attestation:
   123	
   124	```bash
   125	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main --confirm-squash <merge-commit>
   126	```
   127	
   128	This proves only that the named squash commit is in the base; the operator is
   129	asserting that it represents the feature.
   130	
   131	## Safety policy
   132	
   133	Retirement always refuses when:
   134	
   135	- the caller cwd is the target or below it;
   136	- the caller Herdr workspace/pane or tmux pane covers the target;
   137	- a workspace contains panes outside the target;
   138	- an agent is `working`, `blocked`, or `waiting`;
   139	- runtime enumeration fails;
   140	- the checkout is dirty, on the wrong branch, or not contained in its base;
   141	- artifact finalization is armed/finalizing/failed.
   142	
   143	`unknown` or empty agent status requires `--close-unknown` from outside the
   144	target. Runtime enumeration failure requires external `--assume-no-runtime`.
   145	Neither flag bypasses caller containment or active-agent states.
   146	
   147	Raw `git worktree remove --force` and configured external tools can bypass dev.
   148	Never run them from an agent that occupies the target. dev's guarantee covers
   149	only dev-mediated paths. Existing CLI expert acknowledgements remain compatible,
   150	but flow intentionally omits them. Task-backed retirement uses taskflow; explicit
   151	unmanaged path retirement and some record-only/salvage `sweep` actions remain
   152	isolated compatibility paths and must not be described as taskflow-managed.
   153	
   154	## What self-deletion looks like
   155	
   156	A real Codex session deleted its own registered worktree and branch from another
   157	checkout. Herdr kept the workspace and terminal alive because Unix processes can
   158	hold an open cwd inode after the path is unlinked. SpecStory then recreated the
   159	same path with only `.specstory/` content.
   160	
   161	The resulting shell looked alive but was no longer a Git checkout:
   162	
   163	```text
   164	failed to reload config: No such file or directory
   165	fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
   166	```
   167	
   168	Config/skill reloads and new subprocesses failed while Herdr still displayed an
   169	idle agent. Treat `runtime alive + Git registration absent + artifact-only path`
   170	as an orphan requiring transcript salvage and external reconciliation, never as
   171	RETIRED.
   172	
   173	## Artifact rules
   174	
   175	- Match SpecStory Markdown by the exact UUID in its fixed preamble, not filename
   176	  or newest mtime.
   177	- Finalize only after SessionEnd was observed or the outer wrapper supplies
   178	  `--writer-stopped`; byte stability remains a second, independent check.
   179	- Stage only that transcript and explicitly named plans.
   180	- Never stage another provider/session implicitly.
   181	- `.specstory/statistics.json` is derived and ignored.
   182	- New untracked transcripts above 2 MiB need `--allow-large`.
   183	- Scanner/redactor failure commits nothing and leaves a retryable intent.
   184	- Artifact commits are on the same feature branch, not necessarily the same
   185	  product commit; they carry `Agent-Artifact-Session` and
   186	  `Dev-Artifact-Intent` trailers.
   187	
   188	## Task worktree scope
   189	
   190	Worktree-mode `dev start --focus -t <name>` creates a linked checkout; `--focus`
   191	only changes focus. Finishing that task preserves its parent/canonical agent
   192	sessions and other tasks' tabs. A recognized parent agent in any state blocks
   193	FF: recheck after handling it independently in Herdr, choose PR, or cancel.
   194	When integration is already proven and only retirement remains, a parent agent
   195	does not prevent cleanup of the separate child worktree.
   196	
   197	The interactive finish plan may select exact idle/done **task-worktree** agent
   198	panes for closure. Nothing closes until final Apply approval. Parent, other
   199	checkout, mixed, or unverified Herdr workspaces are protected even when a pane
   200	has changed into the target directory. If they still cover the worktree,
   201	retirement stops and identifies the preserved panes. Working/blocked/waiting
   202	agents remain blockers. General foreground programs (an editor, server, or
   203	test command) require a separate FF confirmation: files in the displayed
   204	checkout will change while those programs continue running. `--yes` does not
   205	supply that confirmation; non-interactive calls requiring it stop.
   206	
   207	Interactive `dev done` cleanup and standalone `dev retire` share a preview of
   208	the target, retained resources, workspace/tab/pane IDs, agent states, and
   209	foreground program names, PIDs and directories. Closing known non-agent
   210	programs requires typing `CLOSE <workspace-id>` for each affected workspace,
   211	then approving the final retirement. `--close-unknown` does not authorize
   212	known program termination. Only a proven foreground shell is labeled as such;
   213	unavailable process evidence is shown as unknown, never idle. Herdr provides
   214	foreground evidence; other backends keep their existing explicitly qualified
   215	unknown-runtime policy. Background jobs are **not inspected** and may also stop
   216	when their terminal closes. Raw argv and environment values are not displayed.
   217	
   218	Approvals bind exact task/checkout, terminal topology and program fingerprints.
   219	A changed program, new tab or moved pane requires a refreshed preview. The
   220	single-use version-2 coordinator handoff waits for the exact launching dev PID
   221	to exit and verifies the original pane has returned to its foreground shell;
   222	a replacement program is not exempt. Old handoffs must be recreated. Final
   223	cancellation before Apply changes nothing; failures after effects begin list
   224	completed closures and retained resources. Raw Git and Herdr actions remain
   225	outside dev's locks and revalidation guarantees.
   226	
   227	## External archive policy
   228	
   229	`dev artifact setup` can select a separate Git archive. New prepared intents bind
   230	that destination and policy; old intents keep the commit workflow. Off/check
   231	finalization needs no compatibility redactor script. For redact copies, review
   232	`dev artifact archive` and supply `--archive-plan` when finalizing. Commit reviewed
   233	plans with product changes before preparing one exact SpecStory transcript.
   234	Ignored capture bytes participate in lifecycle readiness; a new recorder write or
   235	missing archive receipt blocks cleanup. See [AI artifacts](ai-artifacts.md).
     1	to resume a task owned by another machine without `--force`. Two machines
     2	committing to one branch is the only reliable way to make this workflow produce
     3	a conflict; the ownership check is what prevents it.
     4	
     5	If two machines genuinely need to work the same feature at once, split the
     6	branch — `feat/auth-ui` and `feat/auth-api` — and integrate afterwards. That is
     7	the same rule as for parallel agents: parallel writers get parallel branches.
     8	
     9	The task registry itself (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/`) is one small TOML file
    10	per task, specifically so it can live in a private git repo and merge cleanly
    11	across machines. Point `paths.state_dir` at one if you want a shared view.
    12	
    13	## Sweeping
    14	
    15	```bash
    16	dev sweep            # report only
    17	dev sweep --apply    # act, confirming each change
    18	dev sweep --merged-worktrees  # from main, include untracked contained worktrees
    19	```
    20	
    21	`sweep` reports two kinds of problem:
    22	
    23	- **Drift** — a task marked hot with no live session, a warm task with one, a
    24	  recorded worktree git no longer knows about, or a branch-backed task whose
    25	  branch git no longer has. That last one is dead rather than drifted: `done`,
    26	  `resume` and `retire` all resolve the branch first, so the record is offered
    27	  for reaping instead of repair.
    28	- **Staleness** — a warm task nobody has touched in two weeks, clean and
    29	  pushed, that could go cold.
    30	
    31	It also lists **live sessions no task claims** — the other half of a crowded
    32	sidebar, and usually the larger half.
    33	
    34	From the canonical default-branch checkout, `--merged-worktrees` switches to a
    35	focused audit of tracked and unmanaged linked worktrees whose named branches are
    36	already contained in main. It suppresses unrelated stale-task/session noise so
    37	the result can be presented directly for cleanup approval. Dirty trees, active
    38	Git operations, pending artifact
    39	intents, active/mixed runtimes, detached heads and unmerged branches are
    40	reported as blockers. Safe candidates still require `--apply` and individual
    41	confirmation; `--delete-branches` is a separate opt-in.
    42	
    43	Agent workflow: show the report to the user as a concrete QA prompt, naming the
    44	exact candidate paths and whether branches would be retained. Only after the
    45	user approves that set may the agent add `--apply --yes`.
    46	
    47	`sweep` never deletes uncommitted work, and never acts without `--apply`. DONE
    48	tasks with runtime/worktree resources are reported as cleanup pending and routed
    49	through the same external-only retirement safety service; their records are not
    50	reaped first.
    51	
    52	The dashboard does not silently reconcile these states. A normal COLD worktree
    53	task points to explicit `dev resume`. A task whose recorded worktree is missing
    54	or no longer registered points to `dev sweep`; generic Enter refuses to open
    55	either the canonical checkout or an artifact-only directory. If sweep reports
    56	unique agent artifacts, salvage them before approving a resume/reap action.
    57	
    58	## Integration
    59	
    60	```bash
    61	dev done --ff     # rebase onto the base, then fast-forward it
    62	dev done --pr     # push and open a pull/merge request via the detected forge CLI
    63	dev done          # TTY: inspect commits/dirty content and choose interactively
    64	```
    65	
    66	Which one depends on a single question: **are this branch's commits worth
    67	keeping in the base's history?**
    68	
    69	- Yes → `--ff`. Linear history, no merge commit, `git bisect` and `git blame`
    70	  stay legible.
    71	- No, it is WIP noise → squash at the integration point.
    72	- Someone (or CI) should look first → `--pr`.
    73	
    74	On a TTY, `dev done` reports branch ahead/behind plus which staged, unstaged and
    75	untracked paths are already equivalent to the base. It can commit all changes,
    76	discard all changes, or cancel before choosing FF/PR. Unique content requires
    77	typing `DROP`; scripts use `--dirty=commit --message ...` or the deliberately
    78	destructive `--dirty=discard --yes`. Ignored files are never discarded. If an
    79	active writer changes the checkout during confirmation or immediately after a
    80	commit, integration stops and the command must be rerun after that writer exits.
    81	
    82	After a bare interactive managed-worktree completion reaches MERGED, the
    83	wizard previews covering runtime panes and agents. It can keep everything,
    84	retire while preserving the branch, or retire and delete the contained branch.
    85	Caller-owned Herdr workspaces are handed to a freshly created external
    86	coordinator; unknown status needs explicit approval and active/mixed sessions
    87	remain blockers.
    88	
    89	Before integration, the TTY wizard can select exact idle/done task-worktree
    90	agent panes for closure only under the final guarded Apply. Parent/canonical
    91	agents remain open and block FF; recheck, choose PR, or cancel. Foreground
    92	non-agent programs require separate consent to changing files while they run.
    93	Interactive retirement separately requires `CLOSE <workspace-id>` to terminate
    94	known programs. Background jobs are unobserved. See `agent-retirement.md`. If FF is blocked by dirty
    95	canonical-checkout bytes, it lists the paths and offers PR, typed `DROP`
    96	discard, exact stash+restore, or cancel. Agent artifacts are labeled.
    97	Stash+restore preserves staged, unstaged, and non-ignored untracked state under
    98	an exact OID, restores the index/worktree after fast-forward, and drops only
    99	that matching stash entry. A conflict retains the stash and task with an exact
   100	recovery command. Dirty submodules and nested repositories remain blockers.
   101	The discard is a separate explicit taskflow effect and no unrelated canonical
   102	bytes are committed automatically.
   103	
   104	For branch/worktree tasks, non-interactive `dev done` without an integration
   105	mode remains report-only. Direct tasks still finish without one. Conflicted
   106	checkouts always require manual resolution.
   107	
   108	Explicit `--ff` integrates and records DONE/MERGED while retaining the worktree
   109	and branch for `dev retire`. Any explicitly selected task agent pane closures
   110	are recorded in the result ledger; no parent pane is closed. `--pr` only publishes and
   111	opens review; after a commit-preserving external merge use
   112	`dev done --merged --base-ref <ref>`. Squash requires explicit
   113	`--confirm-squash <commit>` attestation. `--delete-branch` and `--keep-worktree`
   114	are deprecated on `done`: the branch is deleted only by
   115	`dev retire --delete-branch`, and only when git agrees it is fully contained in
   116	the base. "Merged" is not always "finished", so branches survive by default.
   117	
   118	Cleanup is never inferred from agent lifecycle state. A user must select it in
   119	the post-MERGED wizard or run `dev retire` from a different checkout/runtime;
   120	both paths revalidate, close eligible sessions, wait for release, and remove
   121	without force. Read `agent-retirement.md` before retiring an agent-owned checkout.
   122	
   123	Dashboard row actions now invoke these same finish/resume/retire workflows. Missing checkout recovery is scoped with `dev sweep --task <id>`. See [dashboard actions](dashboard-actions.md).

     1	# AI artifacts: what to keep, archive, and ship
     2	
     3	Keep useful decisions, choose where transcripts live, and ship product inputs.
     4	
     5	## Decide by purpose
     6	
     7	| Material | Purpose | Usual treatment |
     8	|---|---|---|
     9	| Code, tests, current specs and docs | Current behavior and contracts | Maintain with the project |
    10	| Reviewed plans, decisions and pitfalls | Requirements, rationale and lessons | Keep concise, with status and context |
    11	| Raw transcripts, draft plans and tool output | Evidence of the development process | Choose per repository: track, archive elsewhere, or keep local |
    12	| Native sessions and tool databases | Resume state, indexes or curation records | Follow each tool's backup contract |
    13	
    14	AI authorship alone does not determine where a file belongs. Promote useful
    15	conclusions into the project's existing docs, decisions, backlog or pitfalls;
    16	old transcripts are historical evidence, not current instructions. Do not ask
    17	future contributors to read every exploratory conversation to understand code.
    18	
    19	## Four independent choices
    20	
    21	1. Does this material belong in the source repository's Git history?
    22	2. Where is the durable copy, and how will another machine obtain it?
    23	3. Should that copy be checked, redacted, or explicitly stored without scanning?
    24	4. Does the material belong in a source distribution or installed product?
    25	
    26	A private experiment can keep raw chats in Git. A public or long-lived project
    27	can keep reviewed decisions in Git and transcripts in a separate private Git
    28	repository. A private destination does not itself change hygiene policy: choose
    29	it explicitly. An unscanned copy is preserved evidence, not a clean scan.
    30	
    31	## SpecStory: capture is separate from publication
    32	
    33	SpecStory is the current transcript integration. The originating agent is the
    34	provider, for example `codex:<uuid>` or `claude:<uuid>`; SpecStory is the recorder.
    35	Its Markdown export is not the native agent session and does not guarantee resume.
    36	
    37	SpecStory can write per-worktree `.specstory/history/` files or use an explicit
    38	`--output-dir`. Preserve project and session identity when combining histories.
    39	A shared flat directory does not by itself retain project attribution. Tools
    40	such as Lore have their own metadata and curation state; do not assume all of
    41	their databases can be discarded and reconstructed from Markdown.
    42	
    43	For the existing tracked-history workflow:
    44	
    45	```bash
    46	dev hygiene status
    47	dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
    48	dev prepare --session codex:<uuid>
    49	# After the exact recorder has stopped, from outside its checkout:
    50	dev artifact finalize --intent <id> --writer-stopped
    51	```
    52	
    53	Preparation does not stop the writer. Never repeatedly redact a file that a
    54	recorder is still rewriting from its native source. `dev hygiene redact` requires
    55	an exact reviewed plan; artifact writes additionally require post-writer proof.
    56	Private recovery and a stable byte snapshot do not prove that a process exited.
    57	
    58	If history is ignored, ordinary code commits need not scan it. An already tracked
    59	file remains tracked after adding `.gitignore`: removing it from the index is a
    60	separate reviewed operation. Keep or archive ignored history before deleting its
    61	worktree; ignored does not mean disposable or backed up.
    62	
    63	## Choose and apply repository policy
    64	
    65	No policy means existing behavior is unchanged. `track` retains the existing
    66	source-commit finalizer, `archive` preserves selected evidence in a separate Git
    67	checkout, and `unmanaged` leaves retention to the user. Sources are `specstory`
    68	(recorder Markdown) or `files` (explicit source-relative exports/plans).
    69	
    70	```bash
    71	# Create the ordinary archive repository separately; configure its Git identity.
    72	git init -b main /path/to/history
    73	# Explicit private raw preservation; choose check or redact when wanted.
    74	dev artifact setup --mode archive --source specstory --archive /path/to/history \
    75	  --protection off --json
    76	dev artifact setup --apply --plan <id> --yes
    77	dev artifact status
    78	# The same planner through repository setup:
    79	dev repo setup --artifacts --mode unmanaged --json
    80	```
    81	
    82	Setup edits only reviewed policy, local binding, ignore and export files; it
    83	never untracks, commits, pushes or installs tools. `repo setup --artifacts` is
    84	separate from a scaffold plan. Apply there with `--artifacts --apply --plan <id>
    85	--yes`. Review and commit shared policy changes yourself.
    86	
    87	The shareable `.dev-cli/artifacts.toml` contains the stable project ID, retention
    88	mode, source and literal paths. The archive path and protection binding stay in
    89	private host state. Bind a cloned project to the desired archive on each host;
    90	do not infer project identity from a folder basename or current branch.
    91	
    92	`--capture project` keeps normal per-worktree recorder output. `--capture external`
    93	sets a checkout-specific local SpecStory output directory outside Git. It requires
    94	untracked native config and enabled local Markdown export; tracked/complex config
    95	requires manual review. Run setup in each new external-capture checkout. Existing
    96	cloud settings and native session stores remain under SpecStory's control.
    97	
    98	## Preserve copies, then find them
    99	
   100	```bash
   101	dev artifact archive --session codex:<uuid> --json
   102	# Inspect the private review directory, then after the recorder exits:
   103	dev artifact archive --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
   104	dev artifact find --session codex:<uuid>
   105	dev artifact find --commit <full-source-commit-id>
   106	dev artifact find 'literal search text' --all
   107	```
   108	
   109	For `--source files`, select exact configured paths with repeated `--file`.
   110	Inventory is bounded to 10,000 files and each operation to 256 selected files;
   111	current snapshots are limited to 128 MiB per file. Oversized or unsafe inputs
   112	fail explicitly. Search reads committed records on the archive's current branch;
   113	`--all` includes its other projects. Results contain locations and line numbers,
   114	not snippets; no network, native history crawl or agent resume occurs.
   115	
   116	Archive commits contain ordinary snapshot files and metadata under `projects/`.
   117	The metadata binds project/session, original and stored content digests and the
   118	source commit. Source files and source index bytes stay untouched. The project
   119	archive gets text/ident exclusions so CRLF and literal bytes survive Git; custom
   120	content filters such as encryption, LFS or encoding transforms require the
   121	archive's native workflow and are never silently bypassed. Existing Git hooks
   122	still run. Archive access controls and off-host backups remain the operator's
   123	responsibility.
   124	
   125	`off` saves raw input without a scanner. `check` uses enabled source-repository
   126	hygiene policy. `redact` proposes replacements on the copy and checks the result
   127	again. Disabled categories remain disabled; skipped is not clean. Blocking
   128	reports contain safe finding IDs for the existing `dev hygiene rules allow`
   129	workflow. Exact fixture exceptions need review and a reason. Snapshot scans
   130	support inline gitleaks rules and useDefault, not external rule-file includes.
   131	
   132	Unchanged bytes reuse signed local scan evidence only when the path, policy,
   133	exceptions, scanner inputs and executables match. Changed bytes or rules rescan.
   134	Partial scans never pass. Review original/copy payloads privately; raw recovery,
   135	reports and receipts stay under `paths.state_dir`, outside Git and cache clearing.
   136	Filenames and metadata can still identify people or systems: review before sharing.
   137	
   138	After committing product/policy changes, `dev prepare` also supports an archive
   139	policy. Off/check finalization creates the exact archive copy after writer exit.
   140	For redact, preview and review `artifact archive` first, then pass its ID to
   141	`artifact finalize --archive-plan <id> --writer-stopped`. Reviewed plans should
   142	be committed with product changes; prepared SpecStory archive handoffs select one
   143	exact transcript. Old intents keep their original destination and requirements.
   144	The tracked-history finalizer still uses the compatibility skill's scripts.
   145	
   146	Retirement checks signed archive receipts and current ignored capture bytes.
   147	New or changed evidence blocks cleanup until preserved. Local archive durability
   148	is distinct from remote sync; ordinary status and readiness never query a remote.
   149	
   150	## Explicit Git synchronization and original backups
   151	
   152	```bash
   153	dev artifact sync --push --json       # preview contacts the configured remote
   154	dev artifact sync --apply --plan <id> --yes
   155	dev artifact sync --pull --json       # separate pull preview; fast-forward only
   156	
   157	dev artifact migrate --mode untrack --path .specstory/history --json
   158	dev artifact migrate --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
   159	
   160	dev artifact migrate --mode split --path .specstory/history --json
   161	dev artifact migrate --apply --plan <id> --yes
   162	# Optional: publish the original named refs to a separate empty destination.
   163	dev artifact backup <completed-migration-id> --remote <git-url> --json
   164	dev artifact backup --apply --plan <backup-plan-id> --yes
   165	```
   166	
   167	Untrack saves original refs and selected working files, edits ignore rules and
   168	removes only selected index entries. Other staged/unstaged work remains intact;
   169	existing prepared handoffs must be resolved first. Untracking does not itself
   170	configure future archive capture.
   171	
   172	Split requires git-filter-repo and complete local history. It produces verified
   173	`original.bundle`, `original.git`, `history.git`, `filtered.git`, both commit maps,
   174	selected working snapshots in `current/`, and a migration manifest. Every mapped
   175	tree is checked against the selected-path projection. Empty commits/merge topology
   176	and message bytes are retained; rewritten signatures cannot remain valid. A
   177	restore clone verifies the original bundle. Neither source refs nor remotes change.
   178	Raw backups are not a hygiene audit. Other worktrees' uncommitted files, reflogs,
   179	unreachable objects, LFS payloads and submodule repositories are outside coverage.
   180	Detached tips need a recovery ref before migration.
   181	
   182	Backup publication sends frozen named refs with empty-ref leases. Selected
   183	uncommitted working snapshots stay in local `current/`; they are not in the Git
   184	remote backup. Archive sync pins the reviewed destination and branch: push proves
   185	ancestry before an exact lease, pull only fast-forwards. Resolve divergence with
   186	native Git; dev does not force-overwrite or synthesize merges.
   187	
   188	Private operation ledgers retain partial effects, output and recovery paths.
   189	After interruption inspect those paths and the remote, then prepare a new plan;
   190	never blindly replay a partial operation. Original-remote cutover, release/tag
   191	migration and force-with-lease publication of filtered history are separate,
   192	operator-coordinated actions.
   193	
   194	## Distribution, untracking and history migration
   195	
   196	| Action | Effect | Earlier commits |
   197	|---|---|---|
   198	| `.gitattributes` `export-ignore` | Exclude selected paths from `git archive` source packages | Unchanged |
   199	| Ignore and untrack | Stop including new versions in source commits; retain working files | Unchanged |
   200	| Filter a separate repository copy | Build replacement history without selected paths | Different commit IDs in that copy |
   201	
   202	For example, this excludes chats from source archives while leaving them in Git:
   203	
   204	```gitattributes
   205	/.specstory export-ignore
   206	/.specstory/** export-ignore
   207	```
   208	
   209	Verify the exported source still builds, including embedded resources. Packaging
   210	systems have separate inclusion rules; an archive exclusion is not a universal
   211	package filter. New rules affect new tagged snapshots, not old immutable tags.
   212	
   213	When an experiment becomes a maintained project, first inventory and verify a
   214	recoverable original. Build and validate filtered history in a separate copy,
   215	retain commit mappings, and separately coordinate remote replacement, tags,
   216	releases and other clones/worktrees. A bundle covers selected Git objects/refs,
   217	not automatically dirty files, LFS objects or submodule repositories.
   218	
   219	Sync, version control and backup are separate. A synchronized deletion is still
   220	a deletion. Restoring a Markdown export is not restoring the native agent state.
   221	Confirmed leaked credentials require revocation or rotation; filtering Git does
   222	not revoke them or remove copies held by other people and services.
   223	
   224	See `dev help hygiene` for scanning and reviewed redaction, `dev help retirement`
   225	for post-writer handoffs, `dev help repositories` for setup, and `dev help storage`
   226	for durable data versus caches.

The prompt intentionally omits `--wait`, so independent work continues in the
background. Report checkout, branch, workspace, exact pane, profile and agent
name. Observe later with `agent get`, `agent read`, and `agent wait`; never focus
or send probe keys.

Treat `working`, `blocked`, `idle`, `done`, and `unknown` as occupied. `blocked`
requires a user decision. `done` means turn-settled, not cleanup-ready.

## Shared-checkout override

`dev` guards writer-claiming `start --direct`, `start --branch-only`, and
`resume` when another recognized Herdr agent resolves to the same canonical Git
worktree. The inherited pane ID is resolved through `herdr pane current
--current` before excluding the exact caller, so pane moves do not create a
false collision.

Pure `dev repo open`, `dev wt open`, and TUI Enter/focus are navigation: they
reuse/focus the live owner's workspace and do not authorize another writer, so
they need no override. Use global `--allow-shared-checkout` only for an explicit
writer claim after agents have coordinated disjoint file ownership; this skill
must never add it automatically. Default worktree creation remains independent.

## Project-local backend state

Do not add `.claude/settings.local.json` to global/default includes. It is
needed only by an explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude profile:

```toml
[worktree]
include = [".env", ".env.local", ".claude/settings.local.json"]
```
| Spawn independent work | `dev start <repo> --task <name> --base <committed-ref> --json`, validate the exact new pane, then launch there |
| Handoff the same task | Settle the old session, checkpoint dirty code, get explicit user agreement, then resume with a new forked session ID |

A new independent task does not need to wait for an unrelated agent. It does
need a committed base: dirty state in another checkout is not inherited.

## Shared-checkout collision guard

Herdr-aware writer claims (`start --direct`, `start --branch-only`, and
`resume`) compare recognized agents by canonical Git worktree root and reject a
checkout occupied by another pane. `idle`, `done`, `blocked`, `working`, and
`unknown` are all occupied states. Herdr resolves the current pane before
excluding it, so an inherited ID made stale by a pane move is not trusted.

Pure `repo open`, `wt open`, and TUI Enter/focus navigate to the live owner and
do not authorize another writer. `--allow-shared-checkout` is an explicit
escape hatch only for coordinated disjoint writer ownership. Default `dev
start` worktree creation remains allowed because it creates a new boundary.

Use `dev status` in a checkout to see recognized activities.

## When agents can share a checkout

They can when file ownership is explicit and disjoint:

| Parallel work | Same checkout? |

     9	# Repository hygiene
    10	
    11	`dev hygiene` 將可選的 gitleaks、pre-commit、repo 政策、本機私密規則與安全文字
    12	交易整合。Scanner 命中是候選，並不直接代表已確認的 credential 洩漏。
    13	
    14	## 檢查與設定
    15	
    16	先安裝 `gitleaks`、`pre-commit`。Setup 會回報缺少的工具，不暗中安裝套件或覆寫
    17	全域 hook。

    27	不保證過去每次 commit 都執行過。Raw Git 或外部工具仍可繞過 hooks。

    30	保留其他 hooks 及 YAML 註解。同名但命令不同的 hook、未知的 hook 鏈需人工整合。
    31	已有的 gitleaks 設定預設保留；`--migrate-hooks` 可精準遷移已辨識規則，
    32	`--migrate-rules` 則提議整份替換，兩者都須先比對自訂規則。`dev repo setup --enable agent-history-hygiene` 共用此服務。
    33

    38	既有 hook（包含全域 hook），不安裝或改寫全域 hook。只有未設定 hooksPath、
    39	且 common Git directory 沒有 pre-commit hook 時才安裝 repository hook。
    40	已設定的 hook 缺少或無法辨識時需人工整合，不會自動用本地設定蓋過。

    75	退出後才對其 checkout commit。目前不完整取代 agent-history-hygiene：
    76	`dev artifact finalize` 的既有 tracked-history handoff 仍依賴其 scripts；外部 archive
    77	使用 native snapshot 檢查。只要仍有 tracked workflow，這些安裝和 wiring 就保留。
    78	
    79	## 政策與私密規則
    80	
    81	優先序：內建預設 → `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/hygiene.toml` → repo 政策 → 本機 repo
    82	覆寫 → 明確 scan/status flags。建議值是 secret 阻擋、已確認的私密值阻擋、通用
    83	隱私候選警告；各類皆可設為 `block`、`warn` 或 `off`。規則可調整已啟用類別的
    84	處置，但類別 `off` 會停用該類所有規則。
    85	
    86	```toml
    87	version = 1
    88	secrets = "block"
    89	known = "block"
    90	generic = "warn"
    91	```
    92	
    93	三類全部設為 `off` 會回傳明確的 `skipped`，不讀 repo 檔案內容、不執行 scanner；
    94	這是停用，不是 clean scan。
    95	
    96	Private 可見性只提供建議，不會自動弱化政策；未知也不當成 private。GitHub
    97	查詢僅在 `status --check-remote` 發生，`--remote` 預設選 origin。
    98	
    99	```bash
   100	dev hygiene rules policy --known warn --generic off --json
   101	dev hygiene rules apply --plan <id> --yes
   102	dev hygiene rules import --from ssh --json
   103	dev hygiene rules import --from ssh --select <candidate-id> --json
   104	dev hygiene rules import --from local --json
   105	dev hygiene rules add --id private-network --kind cidr --value-file network.txt \
   106	  --replacement 192.0.2.1 --json
   107	```
   108	
   109	先明確選候選才匯入。SSH 只讀取 bounded static Include closure 中的 literal
   110	alias、HostName、User 與 key-path reference，不執行 `ssh -G`、`Match exec`、DNS
   111	或連線，也不讀 key material。Include 不完整會阻擋匯入。常見公開名稱與通用帳號
   112	建議警告；local 來源提供 home path、帳號、Git 姓名與 email。
   113	
   114	`rules import --from machines` 只讀已有的 Tailscale／LAN／Fleet inventory cache，
   115	將 IP、hostname、remote username 列為可勾選的私人候選；不讀 credential store、
   116	keys，不執行探索或連線。保留觀測時間及 stale 標記；缺少快取不會建立新資料，
   117	不完整／損壞會阻擋匯入。預覽後來源內容改變，舊 import plan 即失效。
   118	
   119	Source 中加引號的 password literal 仍會被偵測；未加引號的 assignment 限於設定、
   120	script 與文字格式，以避免 Go 布林欄位／變數運算誤判。格式完整的示範／測試 key
   121	仍先阻擋，經確認後才建立精確例外；不要略過整個 tests／docs 或同一行其他 key。
   122	一般示範用 inert placeholder，detector 測試可於執行時組出 fixture。
   123	
   124	
   125	支援 literal、CIDR、Go RE2 及相對路徑 glob；`directory/**` 選取其下內容。
   126	私密值用 `--value-file` 或 stdin 輸入，不放在命令參數。可用同 ID 的規則 plan
   127	調整／停用規則，或編輯本機私人政策。Scan override 不會持久化；建立 redact plan
   128	前需以相同的持久政策重新掃描。
   129	
   130	本機規則、HMAC key、報告、plan 與恢復資料放在 Git 外的
   131	`paths.state_dir/hygiene/repos/<native-repo-id>/`。Linked worktrees 共用本機政策，
   132	但 plan 綁定特定 checkout。Unix 使用私人權限與 ownership；Windows 使用受保護的
   133	目前 user／SYSTEM ACL。不會自動刪除或匯出。
   134	
   135	```bash
   136	dev hygiene rules allow --report <report-id> --finding <finding-id> \
   137	  --reason 'Reviewed synthetic test fixture' --json
   138	```
   139	
   140	本機例外綁定精確 value／rule／path。可分享的 TOML 例外需指定 `rule`、`path`、
   141	有頭尾錨點的 `pattern` 與原因。`.gitleaksignore` 是 fingerprint 清單，不是 path
   142	移除規則。`--audit` 忽略本機 finding 例外、該檔及 inline `gitleaks:allow`；scanner
   143	設定中的 allowlist 仍有效，必須另行檢視。Placeholder 不會自動放行同一行的其他 key。
   144	
   145	## 掃描範圍
   146	
   147	```bash
   148	dev hygiene scan --scope worktree --json
   149	dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
   150	dev hygiene scan --scope history --audit --timeout 40m --json
   151	dev hygiene --public-only --known off --generic off scan --scope history \
   152	  --range <full-from-oid>..<full-to-oid> --json
   153	```
   154	
   155	Worktree 掃已追蹤檔與未被 ignore 的未追蹤檔；後來加入 `.gitignore` 的已追蹤檔仍
   156	會掃。Staged 使用真正的 index bytes，包含 hidden files 與 partial staging。
   157	`--file` 只能選該範圍內的檔案。
   158	
   159	明確的 range 只檢查選定 commits 所變更的檔案版本，未變更的舊檔留給全量稽核。
   160	History 固定本機 refs 或明確的完整 OID range，涵蓋 merge-only、已刪除與後來
   161	被 ignore 的內容，不暗中 fetch。不掃 reflog、unreachable objects、其他 checkout
   162	未提交內容或遠端 submodule repo。非一般檔與已知 binary 格式列為文字掃描的排除項；
   163	不支援的文字編碼、讀取失敗、超過每檔 128 MiB、來源／ref 變動、shallow history、
   164	取消或 scanner 失敗則回報 incomplete，不能當成 clean。
   165	
   166	JSON schema 1 包含狀態、範圍、固定 refs、數量、遮罩後的位置、處置、排除項與缺口，
   167	不含原始 snippet／credential。Finding ID 與公開檔案摘要使用私人 HMAC。
   168	`complete` 只描述宣告的文字範圍；阻擋命中或不完整皆以失敗狀態退出。不代表驗證過
   169	credential 有效性。未被選取規則涵蓋的檔名仍可能辨識個人，分享前須檢視。
   170	
   171	CI 僅使用公開 repo 規則，不具本機 SSH 字典。PR／push 掃變更的 commit range，
   172	人工 workflow dispatch 掃本機已取得的全部歷史。
   173	
   174	## 修復無效 UTF-8
   175	
   176	Warning 本身不會阻擋 commit。`unsupported_text_encoding` 等 coverage gap
   177	代表掃描不完整，即使 blocking findings 為零仍會失敗。編碼 gap 保留原 code，
   178	新增 `encoding` 物件：`reason`、從零起算的 `byte_offset`、從一起算的 `line`、
   179	`invalid_bytes`、`invalid_sequences`（連續壞 bytes 段數）及可選的 `nul_bytes`。
   180	歷史 gap 也附上觀察到的 `commit`。診斷不輸出原文；修復工作檔不會改寫舊 Git objects。
   181	
   182	```bash
   183	dev hygiene repair-encoding --file .specstory/history/session.md --json
   184	# 明確選擇刪除；預設則替換成 �：
   185	dev hygiene repair-encoding --file notes.txt --invalid remove --json
   186	# 檢閱私人提案，且對應 artifact writer 已退出後：
   187	dev hygiene repair-encoding --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
   188	# 審閱並只 stage 所需修補，再檢查實際 index：
   189	dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
   190	```
   191	
   192	預設 `--invalid replace` 將每段連續無效 bytes 替換成一個 `�`；`remove` 刪除該段。
   193	有效 bytes、既有 `�`、UTF-8 BOM 與換行保持原樣。`--file` 可重複指定；每份
   194	輸入與輸出上限 128 MiB，每份 plan 最多 256 檔、192 MiB 提案輸出。合法文字不需改動。
   195	已知二進位副檔名、NUL、UTF-16/32 BOM 需另行檢視，不猜測舊編碼或原始字元。
   196	
   197	修復使用簽署 plan、即時檔案身分檢查及私人原始 bytes 備份，可經
   198	`dev hygiene restore` 還原，不依賴 secret scanner。Artifact 修改仍要求 writer
   199	已停止及 live occupancy 檢查，涵蓋大小寫變體與巢狀 artifact 目錄。編碼修復
   200	拒絕尾端句點／空白與 DOS 短檔名形式，必須使用標準長路徑；hook 不會自動修復。Apply 只修改工作檔、完整保留
   201	index，因此部分 staging 的檔案在重新審閱並 stage 修補前，staged scan 仍可能失敗。
   202	不要順便 stage 新增的整份聊天。編碼修復不等於 secret redaction 或 hygiene 掃描通過。
   203	
   204	## 預覽、套用與恢復
   205	
   206	```bash
   207	dev hygiene redact --report <report-id> --file notes.md --json
   208	dev hygiene redact --report <report-id> --finding <finding-id> --json
   209	dev hygiene review-path <id>  # 私下開啟提案，勿貼回聊天
   210	dev hygiene redact --apply --plan <id> --yes
   211	# 只有在確切 artifact writer 已退出後：
   212	dev hygiene redact --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
   213	dev hygiene restore --receipt <receipt-id> --json
   214	dev hygiene restore --receipt <receipt-id> --apply --yes
   215	```
   216	
   217	所有支援的一般文字檔皆可選。Plan 綁定 checkout、HEAD／branch、政策、scanner
   218	輸入、native identity 與內容，並附私人簽章。來源或 plan 變動需重做預覽。
   219	重疊命中依 secret → known → generic 優先，同類優先較長 span；預覽只顯示位置、
   220	opaque 摘要與替換數，不重新輸出原 secret。`review-path <id>` 可取得私人完整提案
   221	的位置，完整性也綁定 plan；勿將其內容貼回聊天、Git 或 CI logs。
   222	
   223	Apply 先驗證整批，再逐檔交易，保留 metadata 與私人恢復紀錄。中斷保留 partial
   224	ledger，不能盲目重跑。Index、Git 歷史與安裝的 binary 均不由這個流程修改。
   225	Windows 保護僅適用明確 opt-in 的文字交易，其他 configedit 功能維持原平台契約。Windows 保留 owner／group／DACL 語意；
   226	alternate streams、明確 integrity label 或特殊 attributes 需人工保存。
   227	
   228	Restore 拒絕操作後又被修改／替換的檔案；artifact 恢復也需要 `--writer-stopped`。
   229	Runtime 觀察會阻擋可辨識 writer，但停用或不可用的 runtime 無法證明程序不存在。
   230	Post-writer 聲明與 source revalidation 仍不可省略，raw 外部 writer 不受 dev 鎖保護。
   231	
   232	此 repo 的最後清理步驟見[人工 dogfood 檢查表](../reference/hygiene-dogfood.zh-TW.md)。

`dev repo setup --artifacts` uses the same planner. Archive, find, sync, migrate and
backup are separate operations; they never start an agent or replace the source
remote automatically. See the [AI artifact guide](docs/guides/ai-artifacts.md).

## Repository hygiene

Use `dev hygiene manage --all` to preview and deploy commit checks across selected
repositories, independently of agent skills. Use `dev hygiene status` to inspect effective hooks and `dev hygiene setup` to
preview configuration. `scan --scope staged|worktree|history` checks secret/privacy
policy; reviewed `rules` and `redact` plans keep private values and recovery outside
Git. Hooks block rather than auto-stage. Final transcript cleanup requires the
writer to stop first. `dev hygiene repair-encoding --file <path>` previews
invalid UTF-8 repair with private raw-byte recovery; apply preserves the index,
so review and stage the repair before rescanning. Setup writes project policy
and respects an existing effective hook, including a global one.
See the [hygiene guide](docs/guides/hygiene.md).

## Install

dev start                                            # interactive managed-task wizard
dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main     # non-interactive fast path → hot
dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main \
  --run 'specstory run codex -c "codex"' --focus      # dispatch, then switch to the exact new pane
dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip      # → warm; self-runtime stays alive until exit
dev park --cold --push                               # → cold, only from outside the target runtime
dev resume "token refresh"                           # → hot, rebuilt if needed
dev flow api                                          # preview the repository lifecycle, plan first

dev prepare --session claude:<uuid> --plan .claude/plans/task.md
dev artifact finalize --intent <id> --writer-stopped # manual post-wrapper proof
dev done                                             # TTY finish wizard
dev done --ff                                        # → done/MERGED; runtime + worktree kept
dev retire "token refresh" --delete-branch           # external close/wait/remove → RETIRED

dev done --pr                                        # open review; keep task/worktree
dev done --merged --base-ref origin/main             # verify commit-preserving merge
dev sweep                                            # report drift and cleanup-pending work
dev sweep --merged-worktrees                         # from main: audit contained linked worktrees
dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply                 # confirm each safe retirement
```

On a TTY, bare `dev done` reports branch ahead/behind and classifies every
staged, unstaged and untracked path against the base before offering
commit-all, discard-all or cancel. Unique discard requires typing `DROP`;
scripts use `--dirty=commit --message ...` or `--dirty=discard --yes`. After a
managed worktree reaches MERGED, the bare wizard also previews covering
runtime panes and agents, then offers keep, retire while keeping the branch, or
retire and delete the freshly contained branch. A caller-owned Herdr workspace
is closed only by a newly created external coordinator after a second fresh
retirement audit; active agents and mixed workspaces remain blockers.

Parent/canonical agent sessions and other tasks' tabs are preserved. A parent
agent blocks FF; the wizard offers recheck, PR, or cancel. It can select exact
idle/done task-worktree panes for closure under the final guarded plan, with no
closure before final approval. General foreground programs need an independent
confirmation that FF changes checkout files while they keep running. Interactive
`dev done` cleanup and `dev retire` list workspace/tab/pane IDs, program names,
PIDs and directories, and require `CLOSE <workspace-id>` before terminating
known non-agent programs. Background jobs are not inspected; unknown process
observations are not presented as idle shells. Parent and mixed workspaces stay
open. See [retirement scope](docs/guides/agent-safe-retirement.md#task-worktree-scope).
If local
fast-forward is blocked only by dirty canonical-checkout bytes, dev lists the
paths (marking agent artifacts) and offers PR handoff, exact stash+restore,
typed `DROP` discard, or cancel. Stash+restore preserves staged state and
untracked files, drops only its exact stash OID after a successful restore, and
retains that stash with a recovery command if restore conflicts. Dirty
submodules and nested repositories remain blockers. It never silently commits
unrelated canonical bytes, and active or unknown agents are not closeable from
this flow.

### A task does not have to mean a worktree

Choose the lightest mode that preserves the boundary you need:

```bash
# No task, no branch, no worktree: just open the canonical repo for ad-hoc work.
dev repo open api

# Track a quick change directly on the branch already checked out (usually main).
dev start api --task "fix typo" --direct

# Use a short-lived branch in the canonical checkout, but no linked worktree.
dev start api --task "small feature" --branch-only --base main
```

| Value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `auto` | interactive: prompts to commit or discard; non-interactive: fails, same as `fail` |
| `fail` | refuses to finish with a dirty checkout |
| `commit` | commits everything with `--message`/`-m` (prompted interactively if omitted) |
| `discard` | resets tracked changes and removes untracked files; destructive, requires `--yes` outside a TTY |

`--yes`/`-y` confirms the selected finish plan; it is mandatory for a
non-interactive `--dirty discard` and otherwise skips the interactive
confirmation step. `--push` pushes the branch or base selected by the
integration mode. Successful local or externally verified integration records
DONE/MERGED while retaining the worktree and branch for a
separate `dev retire`; `--keep-worktree` remains only as a no-op compatibility
warning, while `--delete-branch` fails with guidance to use
`dev retire --delete-branch`. `--merged` can use
`--confirm-squash <merge-commit>` as explicit operator attestation for a squash
result; provider status never implies that attestation.

For a managed worktree, bare interactive `dev done` adds a post-MERGED cleanup
choice: keep, retire while keeping the branch, or retire and delete the
contained branch. It previews covering runtime panes and agent states first.
Caller-owned Herdr workspaces are handed to a fresh external coordinator;
explicit modes and non-interactive invocations continue to stop at DONE.
Parent agents remain open and block FF with recheck/PR/cancel. Only exact
idle/done task-worktree panes may close under final Apply approval. General
foreground programs require separate FF file-change consent; both interactive
cleanup entrances require `CLOSE <workspace-id>` for known program termination.
Background jobs are not inspected. A dirty canonical target still offers PR,
stash+restore, typed `DROP`, or cancel. See [retirement scope](../guides/agent-safe-retirement.md#task-worktree-scope).

## Configuration

```bash
dev config init
dev config show
dev config path
credential context. `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/ssh-credentials.toml` stores ask/never
policy, provider references and pending/unknown metadata, not secret values.
Explicit fleet password sources retain priority; discovery does not use the
saved-reference resolver. Remote source-to-target credentials are outside the
controller save flow. See [SSH workflows](../guides/ssh-hosts.md#fleet-source-profiles-and-local-routes).

## Repository hygiene

`dev hygiene` provides staged/worktree/history scopes, per-repo block/warn/off
policies, private local identity imports and reviewed text replacement/recovery on
macOS, Linux and Windows. CI uses public rules only. See the
[hygiene workflow](../guides/hygiene.md) for schema-v1 coverage and hook contracts.

`hygiene repair-encoding --file PATH [--invalid replace|remove]` previews
working-file UTF-8 repair; `--apply --plan ID --yes` applies the reviewed plan,
with `--writer-stopped` required for artifacts. Index bytes stay unchanged.
Schema 1 retains `unsupported_text_encoding` and adds optional `encoding`
diagnostics and historical `commit` to coverage gaps; repair plan files also
carry encoding diagnostics. Repair does not claim a successful secret scan.

`hygiene manage [repo...] [--all]` opens batch repository setup; `--json` is
preview-only. `setup --migrate-hooks` previews narrow known-hook/rule migration.
`rules import --from machines` reads private candidates from existing local
Tailscale/LAN/Fleet caches. `skill manage` also removes selected owned skills with
explicit agent scopes; existing bundled `skill uninstall` keeps its meaning.

## Agent history policy

`dev artifact setup` and `dev repo setup --artifacts` share reviewed plans.
`.dev-cli/artifacts.toml` records project ID, track/archive/unmanaged mode,
specstory/files source, capture location policy, literal paths and export rules.
Host-local archive/protection bindings and signed receipts stay under
`paths.state_dir/agent-history/`. They are durable private state, not cache.

Capture/provider identity, source retention, off/check/redact copy protection
and distribution exclusions are independent. See [AI artifacts](../guides/ai-artifacts.md)
for supported limits, exact preview/apply commands and historical migration.

## SSH dashboard settings (v0.2.34)

```toml
[tui.ssh]
background_refresh = true
```

This option controls only automatic Tailscale status in the active SSH view. LAN scans and connection tests remain explicit. `ssh diagnose --ping --network-only ALIAS` observes ICMP/TCP/banner without an SSH authentication attempt; omit `--network-only` for full verification. `--network-only` cannot combine with `--compare-qos`.

- `dev start --focus` activates the runtime after non-JSON creation.

  a newly created first-class Herdr worktree. It is incompatible with `--json`,
  non-worktree modes, and non-Herdr runtimes, and does not wait for command exit.
- TUI navigation refuses to open a missing COLD checkout and directs the user to `dev resume`.
- Preview-labelled `dev flow [repo]` is an independent full-screen TTY model. It resolves canonical/linked cwd to the exact surface, uses a picker outside Git, shows every registered worktree plus task-only records, and makes every mutation Enter-to-plan then approve. Apply revalidates task revision and exact repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact authority and retains partial step results. Local `r` is network-free; `R` explicitly selects fetch/query/both and keeps minimal review evidence run-local.
- `DEV_TUI_TRACE` starts at `cli.Execute`; it cannot include OS process loading. `tui.initial_view_returned` measures model construction, not renderer flush or physical terminal paint. Use it for same-profile comparisons rather than universal hardware/network guarantees.
- Runtime handles now record backend provenance and are revalidated before cleanup.
- `auto` runtime selection includes Zellij between tmux and none.

- Human-readable output now carries semantic color (`--color auto|always|never`), automatically disabled when `NO_COLOR` is set, `TERM=dumb`, or stdout/stderr is not a terminal.

Containment alone is never permission; dirty state, unfinalized artifacts, in-progress Git operations, and runtime refusals all still block it, and branches survive unless `--delete-branches` is passed.
- `dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees` adds a separate schema-v1 Claude Workflow report. The path/branch convention is only discovery; exact bounded provider linkage plus fresh Git/task/artifact/caller/runtime evidence authorizes TTY/per-item apply. Apply locks and re-fingerprints, removes without force, retains branches by default, and allows only explicit-base unchanged/contained/zero-unique `branch -d`.
- `dev sweep` reports a branch-backed task whose branch Git no longer has as dead and offers to reap the record. Such a task cannot be finished, resumed, or retired, because every one of those paths resolves the branch first; the suggestion stays report-only until `--apply`.
- An unknown command is reported instead of discarded. `dev` silences cobra's own error printing and previously also skipped printing anything whose message began with `unknown command`, so a mistyped command produced no output at all on either stream. The message, cobra's "Did you mean this?" suggestions, and a pointer to `--help` are now printed to stderr with exit status 1.
- A stray argument to a command family is an error rather than a silent help render. `dev wt bogus` used to print `dev wt` help and exit 0 because a family has no `Run` of its own; every family node now reports the unknown subcommand and exits 1, while a bare family still prints its help and exits 0.
- Argument-count and flag errors print the failing command's usage block. `--color` still governs whether that block is colorized.
- Each command family's help carries an ASCII orientation diagram and a `See also: dev help <topic>` pointer, and `dev help <command>` resolves a command name or alias to its topic, so `dev help wt` reaches the worktrees page.
- Semantic color covers every human-readable surface, including the interactive dashboard: `dev --color never`, `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` now disable dashboard color too, which they previously did not.
- `dev sweep` reaps a task whose repository directory no longer exists. Such a record was unreachable by every command in the binary: `done`, `resume`, `park` and `retire` all resolve the repository first, the dead-branch rule excludes direct mode, and the stale-worktree rule requires a recorded worktree path. A live runtime session rules the suggestion out, and reaping removes only dev's record of intent.
- `dev sweep` reports a task-recorded checkout that exists but Git does not register and that holds nothing but agent artifact directories. Removal is offered only when every file inside is byte-identical to one already in the repository; anything else is reported as salvage work and is never removed, including under `--apply`.
- `dev sweep` acts on a cold task whose worktree is still on disk. Inventory has always computed that drift for `dev ls` and the dashboard, but sweep never consulted it, so it was displayed and not actionable.
- `dev retire <path>` reaps the matching task record. Only the by-task form set the task identity, so retiring the same checkout by path left the record behind; the DONE-state and identity checks are unchanged.
- `dev version` reports whether the running build is a published release, and `dev doctor` carries the same line plus the install owner, invoked/resolved executable path, and warnings for distinct `dev` copies on `PATH`. Nothing in the tool answered "am I current?" before, and `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so an untagged feature was invisible to anyone installing it.
- A release publishes platform archives and `SHA256SUMS` and takes its notes from `CHANGELOG.md`. Earlier releases published a GitHub release object and nothing else, so their assets are absent by construction.
- A release publishes Windows `.zip` archives alongside the Unix `.tar.gz` set, refreshes an in-repo Scoop manifest attached to the release (and pushed to the bucket when a token is configured), and publishes the matching source formula to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`. Homebrew publication is a required release step and fails visibly when its repository token is missing or rejected. A manual workflow can retry or backfill the formula for an existing stable release without creating or moving a tag.
- `dev upgrade` checks the exact release's asset inventory. A standalone install downloads its platform archive and verifies `SHA256SUMS`; if no asset exists for that platform, it offers a native source build of the exact tag. New releases include a compact `dev-cli_<tag>_source.tar.gz` verified against `SHA256SUMS`, excluding conversation history; older releases use Go's configured module verification and can require a much larger download. This source fallback and compact archive are available starting with v0.2.35. Network errors, missing checksum entries, and checksum mismatches stop the upgrade. Source builds use the installed Go toolchain, two workers and a 20-minute build limit; a successful candidate must report the expected version before replacement. `--check` never compiles and missing tools are reported before confirmation. Homebrew, Scoop and `go install` ownership still delegates to that manager. Replacement uses atomic rename (Windows moves the live `.exe` aside and sweeps it on the next run); a changed target aborts replacement.
- Android/Termux currently has no published binary. Use `pkg install golang clang git` for native build dependencies. Source upgrades set `GOOS=android`, enable CGO with Termux Clang and disable automatic Go toolchain downloads. Linux archives can fail on Android syscalls and are never substituted. Go must meet the selected release's `go.mod` requirement. An older binary without source fallback needs a one-time native build of a pinned, checksummed source archive into a staging directory, version verification and replacement of the standalone executable; see the repository README's Termux recovery example.
contract. REPOS caches supply presentation only; Git/runtime/task authority still
requires fresh observations and operation-time validation.

## Dashboard discovery registration (v0.2.24)

The first REPOS visit selects the startup repository without reordering; clicking
the selected row opens its actions. An outside startup Git repo offers clickable
previews to append its main root to `paths.repo_paths` or its parent to
`paths.scan_roots`. The active file, including `--config`, remains the only config
source. Comments, existing order and inherited defaults are preserved. Prefer exact
entries for isolated repos; parent scans also cover sibling projects and require
explicit confirmation. Guarded writes support macOS/Linux with private recovery
under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/config-recovery`; symlink configs, unsupported TOML layouts
and other platforms offer manual edits and the config editor. Failed scans remain
unknown. Successful saves refresh local inventory; reload failures are reported
separately. CLI flags and existing JSON contracts are unchanged.

## Contextual Help and compact skill entry (v0.2.24)

Dashboard Help starts with Keys for the current view, followed by Guide and
Manual. View scope applies to TUI search; Manual searches all embedded CLI
Ordinary native sessions retain remaining user SSH behavior. Private temporary
password/exact-key configurations preserve supported settings and reject
LocalCommand, port forwarding, SetEnv and `%`-expanded RemoteCommand.

An unselected native-only ProxyCommand session may connect after fresh static and
effective-source checks. It does not expose reconstructed route/proof authority;
opaque route import, cycles and unsupported selected-key flows stay rejected.

## Repository hygiene

`dev hygiene` provides staged/worktree/history scopes, per-repo block/warn/off
policies, private local identity imports and reviewed text replacement/recovery on
macOS, Linux and Windows. CI uses public rules only. See the
[hygiene workflow](../guides/hygiene.md) for schema-v1 coverage and hook contracts.

`hygiene repair-encoding --file PATH [--invalid replace|remove]` previews
working-file UTF-8 repair; `--apply --plan ID --yes` applies the reviewed plan,
with `--writer-stopped` required for artifacts. Index bytes stay unchanged.
Schema 1 retains `unsupported_text_encoding` and adds optional `encoding`
diagnostics and historical `commit` to coverage gaps; repair plan files also
carry encoding diagnostics. Repair does not claim a successful secret scan.

## Hygiene rollout and selected skill removal

Repository hygiene is a developer commit procedure and needs no installed agent
skill. Batch migration retains specialized legacy finalizers and custom settings;
it does not yet replace the full agent-history-hygiene lifecycle. Gitleaks 8.30+
compatible 8.x is required by setup/scan. Cached machine imports never query
remote hosts or credential providers.

Skill removal requires verified native ownership or a bundled install manifest,
explicit agent scopes and dependency checks. Windows npm-shim removal uses system
PowerShell and bounded process-tree cancellation; unsupported shell syntax or
other shim mutation actions fail closed. The dedicated native removal tests are
required; broad advisory Windows test conclusions are not proof that every
legacy suite passed.

## Agent history archives

History policy is opt-in through `artifact setup` or `repo setup --artifacts`.
Only SpecStory Markdown and explicitly selected files are capture sources.
Archive copies require post-writer proof; off stores unscanned input, while
check/redact use enabled source hygiene rules. Native session databases, cloud
resume, automatic knowledge mining, encrypted/LFS archive filters and original
remote history replacement are outside this integration.

Current file snapshots cap at 128 MiB, inventories at 10,000 files and plans at
256 selected files. Split migration requires git-filter-repo (native CI pins
2.47.0) and complete locally recoverable refs. Backup coverage and partial results
remain explicit. Existing commit finalizers and intent fields retain their lane;
older binaries cannot consume new external-archive intent fields.

## SSH dashboard observations (v0.2.34)

The SSH dashboard has a native discovery/setup UI and profile tree. Missing registry state is empty; unsafe registry state is a recoverable issue and never proof of missing bindings. In-memory discovery survives cache failure. Background Tailscale status is enabled by `[tui.ssh].background_refresh`; neither this nor plain refresh scans LAN or authenticates SSH. Private activity records are durable and separate from discovery cache. Ping is optional and never gates SSH; proxy network stages remain unobserved. New diagnostic flags/fields are additive, and existing alias/list JSON contracts remain unchanged.

passwords in `connect --on` remain outside this controller save workflow.

Password-save features do not import SSH private keys into a vault, provision YubiKeys,
or export Apple Passwords. Those are separate future migration workflows.

## SSH connection view

On native Android/Termux, keep SSH configuration and dev state/cache in the
app's private home. Dev verifies the Termux app boundary instead of requiring
read access to `/` or ownership of Android's system-managed `/data` directories.
Inherited SELinux labels and file encryption metadata must remain unchanged;
new files use an atomic no-replace rename because Android forbids hard links.
No root access or Android permission changes are needed. Shared storage and
arbitrary app-data paths do not receive this exception.

The eighth tab keeps one machine row, with Space expanding its SSH profiles.
Configured connections come first, ordered by the most recent local `dev ssh
connect` or dashboard connection attempt; unrecorded profiles follow by alias.
---
`[tui.ssh].background_refresh = true` refreshes missing or expired Tailscale
observations, at most once per five minutes with a five-second query limit.
Failures keep dated observations. Disable it for cache-only viewing. `r` reloads
local state; LAN scanning and SSH tests always require an explicit action.
`Ctrl+O` also opens problems and suggested actions, even on an empty list.

## Native Android / Termux

Keep SSH configuration and dev state/cache under Termux's private home. Native
Android builds verify the app boundary, preserve inherited SELinux labels and
encryption metadata, and publish new files without overwriting existing paths.
Android's system-owned /data directories do not need permission repair.

```text
    15	
    16	## Three milestones, not one
    17	
    18	Completion is three separate milestones, and the persisted task state `done` now means the middle one, not the last:
    19	
    20	```text
    21	READY     exact transcript preserved in its chosen destination after writer exit
    22	MERGED    branch integrated; runtime/worktree may still exist
    23	RETIRED   runtime absent, worktree removed, optional branch deleted, task reaped
    24	```
    25	
    26	`hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done` remain the only persisted task states — `done` means MERGED, with cleanup possibly still pending. It does **not** mean the runtime or worktree has already been deleted.
    27	
    28	## Commands
    29	
    30	| Command | What it does |
    31	|---|---|
    32	| `dev prepare --session <provider:uuid> --plan <path>` | Arms post-writer artifact finalization without closing the running agent. Product changes must already be committed; the transcript itself is deliberately not staged yet. |
    33	| `dev artifact finalize --run-id "$DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID" --if-pending --writer-stopped` | Preserves the exact stable transcript in the intent's source-commit or external-archive destination after its writer stops. `--if-pending` no-ops silently when no armed intent matches the run id; `--writer-stopped` confirms the outer wrapper has returned. |
    34	| `dev done --ff` | Rebases the task branch onto its base and fast-forwards it locally. Records MERGED; never closes the runtime, removes a worktree, or deletes a branch. |
    35	| `dev done --pr` | Pushes the branch and opens a pull/merge request through an available forge CLI. The task stays under review, not MERGED. |
    36	| `dev done --merged --base-ref <ref>` | Verifies an externally merged branch is contained in `<ref>` and records MERGED. |
    37	| `dev done --merged --base-ref <ref> --confirm-squash <merge-commit>` | Same, but for a squash merge: attests that the named commit, already proven contained in `<ref>`, represents the feature branch. This is an operator assertion dev cannot verify on its own. |
    38	| `dev artifact discard <intent> --yes` | Records that an intent can never be finalized — its transcript was never written, or its HEAD is gone after a rebase — so it stops blocking integration and retirement. It commits and recovers nothing, prints exactly what is being abandoned, and refuses an intent that is still `armed`, because finalization is the path that preserves a transcript. |
    39	| `dev retire [task-or-worktree] [--close-unknown] [--assume-no-runtime] [--delete-branch] [--timeout <duration>]` | Re-resolves every covering runtime session, refuses active agents and mixed-purpose workspaces, waits for closure, revalidates Git state, and only then removes the linked worktree without force. Deletes the task record only after every requested step succeeds. |
    40	| `dev flow [repo]` | Preview UI for an exact DONE task: Enter builds a revision-bound Retire plan, then approval applies it. Branch deletion requires the displayed typed token. |
    41	| `dev sweep --merged-worktrees [--base <ref>] [--apply] [--yes] [--close-unknown] [--assume-no-runtime] [--delete-branches]` | From the canonical checkout, reports (and, with `--apply`, retires) both task-tracked and unmanaged linked worktrees whose branches are already contained in the base. |
    42	| `dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees [--stale-days <n>] [--json]` | From a canonical non-bare checkout, emits a strict Claude Workflow V1 report; JSON schema 1 is report-only. |
    43	| `dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply [--delete-branches --base <ref>]` | Requires a TTY and per-item confirmation, then revalidates each approved fingerprint under the common-dir cleanup lock before plain non-force removal. |
    44	
    45	A dirty checkout does not fail here: `dev done` classifies it against the base
    46	first, offering commit or discard interactively, or taking an explicit
    47	`--dirty` policy from a script. See
    48	[Change-stream workflow](change-stream-workflow.md) for that wizard. The
    49	`--keep-worktree` and `--delete-branch` flags remain accepted on `dev done`
    50	only to fail loudly and point at `dev retire`.
    51	
    52	If fast-forward is blocked by unrelated dirty bytes in the canonical checkout,
    53	the interactive wizard can preserve them with an exact stash+restore
    54	transaction. It restores staged state and untracked files after integration;
    55	dirty submodules and nested repositories still require independent handling.
    56	
    57	After a bare interactive `dev done` reaches MERGED, its cleanup step performs
    58	a read-only retirement preview and asks whether to keep, retire, or retire and
    59	delete the contained branch. Covering Herdr panes and recognized agent states
    60	are shown before approval. Caller-owned Herdr workspaces use a fresh exact-pane
    61	external coordinator; working/blocked/waiting agents and mixed workspaces are
    62	never overridden.
    63	
    64	For a read-only explanation before acting, render or open the generic
    65	`workspace-closeout` recipe from the exact checkout:
    66	
    67	```bash
    68	dev prompt render workspace-closeout .
    69	dev prompt open workspace-closeout . --agent my-agent
    70	```
    71	
    72	The recipe includes the full retirement audit, but its result is advisory.
    73	`eligible` and a merged PR never authorize cleanup; an external `dev retire`
    74	still recollects and revalidates every gate. If `dev done --ff` or
    75	`dev git pull-rebase` stops at a conflict, use `prompt open` only to discuss the
    76	semantic resolution, then explicitly continue/abort Git and rerun the lifecycle
    77	command. See [Prompt handoffs](prompt-handoffs.md).
    78	
    79	## Normal local flow
    80	
    81	From the feature worktree:
    82	
    83	```bash
    84	# Commit product changes first. Do not stage the moving transcript.
    85	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid> --plan .claude/plans/task.md
    86	# Exit the agent normally so SpecStory can write its final Markdown.
    87	```
    88	
    89	The outer `specstory run` wrapper then calls:
    90	
    91	```bash
    92	dev artifact finalize --run-id "$DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID" --if-pending --writer-stopped
    93	```
    94	
    95	An external main/integration workspace finishes the job:
    96	
    97	```bash
    98	dev done <task> --ff
    99	dev retire <task> --delete-branch
   100	```
   101	
   102	`dev done` only integrates and records MERGED. `dev retire` re-resolves every runtime pane, closes eligible sessions, waits for them to disappear, revalidates Git, and removes the worktree without force.
   103	
   104	In `dev flow`, Retire shows conditions, effects, retained resources, and the CLI
   105	fallback before approval. Apply locks and reloads the task revision plus exact
   106	repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact authority, repeats safety checks after
   107	runtime closure and before removal, and deletes the task record last. A later
   108	failure preserves a step ledger and recovery; completed effects are not called
   109	rolled back.
   110	
   111	## Pull-request flow
   112	
   113	```bash
   114	dev done <task> --pr
   115	# after CI/review and a commit-preserving merge
   116	git fetch origin
   117	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main
   118	dev retire <task> --delete-branch
   119	```
   120	
   121	A squash merge is not ancestry-equivalent, so it needs an explicit operator attestation:
   122	
   123	```bash
   124	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main --confirm-squash <merge-commit>
   125	```
   126	
   127	This proves only that the named squash commit is contained in the base; the operator is asserting that it actually represents the feature branch.
   128	
   129	## Refusal conditions
   130	
   131	`retire.Inspect` refuses to proceed whenever any of the following hold, and it re-checks after closing sessions rather than trusting a stale view:
   132	
   133	- the caller's current directory is the target checkout or below it;
   134	- the caller's `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, or `TMUX_PANE` identifies a runtime session that covers the target;
   135	- a covering runtime workspace also contains panes outside the target (mixed-purpose workspace);
   136	- any covering agent status is `working`, `running`, `busy`, `blocked`, or `waiting` — **never overridable, by any flag**;
   137	- agent status is empty or `unknown`, **unless** the caller passes `--close-unknown` from outside the target;
   138	- agent status is unrecognized (anything outside the known set) — always blocks;
   139	- runtime enumeration itself fails, **unless** the caller passes `--assume-no-runtime`.
   140	
   141	`--close-unknown` and `--assume-no-runtime` only relax fail-closed *observations* (an unreadable status, a runtime list that could not be enumerated). Neither flag ever bypasses caller containment or an active-agent state. `retirement.Service.Retire` also revalidates the target's identity, Git ancestry, in-progress Git operations (`gitx.InProgress`, checking `MERGE_HEAD`, `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, `REVERT_HEAD`, `BISECT_LOG`, `rebase-merge`, `rebase-apply`, `sequencer` — not `REBASE_HEAD`, which Git leaves behind after a rebase completes), and worktree cleanliness after runtime sessions close — reality may have changed while a runtime was draining, so no earlier proof carries across that boundary.
   142	
   143	## Periodic cleanup with sweep
   144	
   145	```bash
   146	dev sweep --merged-worktrees
   147	# Present the exact candidates/blockers to the user and ask for approval.
   148	dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply --yes
   149	```
   150	
   151	This surfaces both task-tracked DONE worktrees and unmanaged linked worktrees whose named branches are already contained in the base — run it from the canonical checkout. It reports before applying: containment alone is never permission. Dirty Git state, a pending or unreachable artifact, a locked or prunable worktree registration, an in-progress Git operation, and the same runtime refusal conditions as `dev retire` all still block cleanup. Branches remain after retirement by default; pass `--delete-branches` only when the user separately approved deleting them.
   152	
   153	### Verified Claude Workflow ephemeral cleanup
   154	
   155	Claude Workflow turn-scoped worktrees have a separate strict V1 path:
   156	
   157	```bash
   158	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --stale-days 14
   159	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --json
   160	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply
```

   171	metadata, source mutation, bound exhaustion, and future/conflicting/unparseable

   174	V1 terminal liveness requires workflow `completed|killed`, matching agent `done`,
   175	one journal `started` and `result`, and no same-ID resumed transcript. A killed
