80	func pruneLatest(index *latestIndex) {
81		if len(index.Checkouts) <= maxLatestCheckouts {
82			return
83		}
84		keys := make([]string, 0, len(index.Checkouts))
85		for key := range index.Checkouts {
86			keys = append(keys, key)
87		}
88		sort.Slice(keys, func(i, j int) bool {
89			return index.Checkouts[keys[i]][latestAnyScope].Created.After(index.Checkouts[keys[j]][latestAnyScope].Created)
90		})
91		for _, key := range keys[maxLatestCheckouts:] {
92			delete(index.Checkouts, key)
93		}
94	}

97		path := filepath.Join(s.Dir, latestFile)
98		data, err := safefile.ReadStablePath(ctx, path, 1<<20)
99		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
100			return latestIndex{}, nil
101		}
102		if err != nil {
103			return latestIndex{}, err
104		}
105		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
106		if err != nil {
107			return latestIndex{}, err
108		}
109		if err := privatefile.Check(path, info, false); err != nil {
110			return latestIndex{}, err
111		}
112		var index latestIndex
113		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &index); err != nil || index.Version != 1 {
114			return latestIndex{}, errors.New("invalid hygiene latest-scan index")
115		}
116		return index, nil
117	}

122		if err := s.prepare(ctx); err != nil {
123			return "", err
124		}
125		if scope == "" {
126			scope = latestAnyScope
127		}
128		index, err := s.readLatest(ctx)
129		if err != nil {
130			return "", err
131		}
132		ref, ok := index.Checkouts[s.checkoutKey()][scope]
133		if !ok || ref.ID == "" {
134			return "", ErrNoStoredScan
135		}
136		return ref.ID, nil
137	}

You are reviewing for **recall** at extra-high effort: catch every real bug. At
this level, catching real bugs matters more than avoiding false positives — a
missed bug ships. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (5 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 8 each)

Run **10 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 8 candidate findings**. Do NOT let one angle's conclusions
suppress another's — if two angles flag the same line for different reasons,
record both.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Angle D — language-pitfall specialist

Scan for the classic pitfalls of the diff's language/framework — for example:
JS falsy-zero, `==` coercion, closure-captured loop var; Python mutable default
args, late-binding closures; Go nil-map write, range-var capture; SQL injection;
timezone/DST drift; float equality. Flag any instance the diff introduces.

### Angle E — wrapper/proxy correctness

When the PR adds or modifies a type that wraps another (cache, proxy, decorator,
adapter): check that every method routes to the wrapped instance and not back
through a registry/session/global — e.g. a caching provider holding a
`delegate` field that resolves IDs via `session.get(...)` instead of
`delegate.get(...)` will re-enter the cache or recurse. Also check that the
wrapper forwards all the methods the callers actually use.

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or

that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"

report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

16	func (h *hygieneCLI) reportCmd() *cobra.Command {
17		var (
18			reportID, scope, historyRange, by   string
19			dispositions, rules, categories     []string
20			paths, scanFiles                    []string
21			top                                 int
22			timeout                             time.Duration
23			rescan, audit, findings, showValues bool
24		)
25		cmd := &cobra.Command{
26			Use:   "report",
27			Short: "Summarize a scan by severity, rule and file",
28			Long: `Summarize one hygiene scan without printing every finding.
29	
30	By default the newest stored scan for this checkout is summarized without
31	scanning again; the pre-commit hook's staged scan is therefore available right
32	after a blocked commit. --scope selects the newest scan of that scope,
33	--report an exact report, and --rescan runs a fresh scan first (accepting
34	--range, --file, --timeout and --audit like dev hygiene scan).
35	
36	Groups are ordered by severity (block, warn, accepted), then occurrences and
37	findings. --top limits each group (0 shows all). Filters narrow the findings
38	before aggregation. --findings lists individual findings; --json emits the
39	hygiene_summary schema-v1 document for automation.
40	
41	--values shows masked distinct values per rule and implies --rescan unless
42	--report names a scan captured with values. Raw values and their context are
43	written only to a private review file; print its location with
44	dev hygiene review-path <report-id> and never paste it into chat, Git or CI.`,
45			Example: `  dev hygiene report
46	  dev hygiene report --scope staged --by rule --top 5 --findings
47	  dev hygiene report --rule privacy-email --values
48	  dev hygiene --json report --disposition block,warn`,
49			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
50			RunE: func(c *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
51				ctx := c.Context()
52				if showValues && reportID == "" {
53					rescan = true
54				}
55				if reportID != "" && rescan {
56					return errors.New("--report summarizes a stored scan; it cannot be combined with --rescan")
57				}
58				if !rescan {
59					for _, name := range []string{"range", "file", "timeout", "audit"} {
60						if c.Flags().Changed(name) {
61							return fmt.Errorf("--%s requires --rescan", name)
62						}
63					}
64				}
65				s, err := h.service(ctx)
66				if err != nil {
67					return err
68				}
69				request := hygiene.SummaryRequest{
70					ReportID: reportID, Scope: scope, By: splitFlagList([]string{by}), Top: top,
71					Dispositions: splitFlagList(dispositions), Rules: splitFlagList(rules),
72					Categories: splitFlagList(categories), Paths: splitFlagList(paths),
73					Findings: findings, Values: showValues,
74				}
75				if err := request.Validate(); err != nil {
76					return err
77				}
78				var scanErr error
79				if rescan {
80					report, e := s.Scan(ctx, hygiene.ScanOptions{Scope: scope, Range: historyRange, Timeout: timeout, Files: scanFiles, Audit: audit, CaptureValues: showValues})
81					if report.ID == "" {
82						return h.output(report, e)
83					}
84					scanErr = e
85					request.ReportID, request.Rescanned = report.ID, true
86				}
87				summary, err := s.Summarize(ctx, request)
88				if err != nil {
89					return errors.New(feedback.Sanitize(err.Error()))
90				}
91				return h.output(summary, scanErr)
92			},
93		}

96		f.StringVar(&scope, "scope", "", "newest stored scan of this scope, or the --rescan scope: staged, worktree or history")

113	func splitFlagList(values []string) []string {
114		var out []string
115		for _, value := range values {
116			for _, part := range strings.Split(value, ",") {
117				if part = strings.TrimSpace(part); part != "" {
118					out = append(out, part)
119				}
120			}
121		}
122		return out
123	}
124	
125	func pluralNoun(n int, noun string) string {
126		if n == 1 {
127			return noun
128		}
129		if strings.HasSuffix(noun, "y") {
130			return strings.TrimSuffix(noun, "y") + "ies"
131		}
132		return noun + "s"
133	}
134	
135	func groupDigits(n int) string {
136		text := strconv.Itoa(n)
137		sign := ""
138		if strings.HasPrefix(text, "-") {
139			sign, text = "-", text[1:]
140		}
141		for i := len(text) - 3; i > 0; i -= 3 {
142			text = text[:i] + "," + text[i:]
143		}
144		return sign + text
145	}

147	func (h *hygieneCLI) dispositionCell(disposition string) string {
148		style := h.app.outStyle()
149		switch disposition {
150		case "block":
151			return style.danger(disposition)
152		case "warn":
153			return style.warning(disposition)
154		case "accepted":
155			return style.dim(disposition)
156		default:
157			return disposition
158		}
159	}

161	func (h *hygieneCLI) renderSummary(v hygiene.Summary) {
162		out, style := h.app.Out, h.app.outStyle()
163		shortID := v.ReportID
164		if len(shortID) > 8 {
165			shortID = shortID[:8] + "…"
166		}
167		fmt.Fprintf(out, "Hygiene %s · %s · report %s\n", v.Scope, v.Status, shortID)
168		fmt.Fprintf(out, "  findings %s (occ %s) · block %s · warn %s · accepted %s · gaps %s\n",
169			groupDigits(v.Totals.Findings), groupDigits(v.Totals.Occurrences), groupDigits(v.Totals.Blocked),
170			groupDigits(v.Totals.Warnings), groupDigits(v.Totals.Accepted), groupDigits(v.Totals.Gaps))
171		var filters []string
172		for label, values := range map[string][]string{"disposition": v.Filters.Dispositions, "rule": v.Filters.Rules, "category": v.Filters.Categories, "path": v.Filters.Paths} {
173			if len(values) > 0 {
174				filters = append(filters, label+" "+feedback.Sanitize(strings.Join(values, ",")))
175			}
176		}
177		if len(filters) > 0 {
178			sort.Strings(filters)
179			fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s\n", style.dim("filters: "+strings.Join(filters, " · ")))
180		}
181		if !v.PolicyCurrent {
182			fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s\n", style.warning("policy changed since this scan; rescan before relying on dispositions"))
183		}
184		if !v.CheckoutCurrent {
185			fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s\n", style.warning("this report was scanned from another checkout"))
186		}
187		more := func(omitted int, noun string) {
188			if omitted > 0 {
189				fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s\n", style.dim(fmt.Sprintf("… %s more %s (--top 0 shows all)", groupDigits(omitted), pluralNoun(omitted, noun))))
190			}
191		}
192		heading := func(title string, ordered bool) {
193			if ordered && v.Top > 0 {
194				title = "TOP " + title
195			}
196			if ordered {
197				title += " (occurrences desc)"
198			}
199			fmt.Fprintf(out, "\n%s\n", style.header(title))
200		}
201	
202		if len(v.Severities) > 0 {
203			heading("BY SEVERITY", false)
204			for _, severity := range v.Severities {
205				detail := "0"
206				if severity.Findings > 0 {
207					detail = fmt.Sprintf("%s %s · %s occ", groupDigits(severity.Findings), pluralNoun(severity.Findings, "finding"), groupDigits(severity.Occurrences))
208				}
209				fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s%s%s\n", h.dispositionCell(severity.Disposition), strings.Repeat(" ", max(1, 10-len(severity.Disposition))), detail)
210			}
211		}
212		if len(v.Rules) > 0 {
213			heading("RULES", true)
214			table := h.app.newTable("  DISP", "RULE", "CAT", "FIND", "OCC", "FILES", "VALUES")
215			for _, rule := range v.Rules {
216				values := "—"
217				if rule.DistinctValues != nil {
218					values = groupDigits(*rule.DistinctValues)
219				}
220				table.Add("  "+h.dispositionCell(rule.Disposition), feedback.Sanitize(rule.Rule), rule.Category,
221					groupDigits(rule.Findings), groupDigits(rule.Occurrences), groupDigits(rule.Files), values)
222			}
223			table.Render(out)
224			more(v.Omitted.Rules, "rule")
225		}
226		if len(v.Files) > 0 {
227			heading("FILES", true)
228			table := h.app.newTable("  DISP", "FILE", "FIND", "OCC", "RULES")
229			for _, file := range v.Files {
230				table.Add("  "+h.dispositionCell(file.Disposition), feedback.Sanitize(file.File),
231					groupDigits(file.Findings), groupDigits(file.Occurrences), truncate(feedback.Sanitize(strings.Join(file.Rules, ",")), 60))
232			}
233			table.Render(out)
234			more(v.Omitted.Files, "file")
235		}
236		if len(v.Categories) > 0 {
237			heading("CATEGORIES", true)
238			table := h.app.newTable("  DISP", "CATEGORY", "FIND", "OCC", "RULES")
239			for _, category := range v.Categories {
240				table.Add("  "+h.dispositionCell(category.Disposition), category.Category,
241					groupDigits(category.Findings), groupDigits(category.Occurrences), groupDigits(category.Rules))
242			}
243			table.Render(out)
244			more(v.Omitted.Categories, "category")
245		}
246		if len(v.Findings) > 0 {
247			heading("FINDINGS", true)
248			table := h.app.newTable("  DISP", "LOCATION", "RULE", "OCC", "FINDING")
249			for _, finding := range v.Findings {
250				location := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", feedback.Sanitize(finding.File), finding.Line)
251				if finding.Commit != "" {
252					location += " @" + feedback.Sanitize(finding.Commit)
253				}
254				table.Add("  "+h.dispositionCell(finding.Disposition), location, feedback.Sanitize(finding.Rule), groupDigits(finding.Occurrences), finding.ID)
255			}
256			table.Render(out)
257			more(v.Omitted.Findings, "finding")
258		}
259		if v.ValuesShown {
260			for _, rule := range v.Rules {
261				if len(rule.Values) == 0 {
262					continue
263				}
264				fmt.Fprintf(out, "\n%s\n", style.header("VALUES · "+feedback.Sanitize(rule.Rule)+" (masked)"))
265				table := h.app.newTable("  VALUE", "OCC", "FILES")
266				for _, value := range rule.Values {
267					table.Add("  "+feedback.Sanitize(value.Masked), groupDigits(value.Occurrences), groupDigits(value.Files))
268				}
269				table.Render(out)
270				more(rule.OmittedValues, "value")
271			}
272			if v.ValuesTruncated {
273				fmt.Fprintf(out, "  %s\n", style.warning("value capture reached its limit; counts above cover captured values only"))
274			}
275			fmt.Fprintf(out, "\nPrivate full values: dev hygiene review-path %s\n", v.ReportID)
276			fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s\n", style.dim("(never paste that file into chat, Git or CI logs)"))
277		}
278	
279		fmt.Fprintf(out, "\n%s\n", style.dim("Report "+v.ReportID))
280		for _, gap := range v.Skipped {
281			fmt.Fprintf(out, "  excluded: %s %s\n", gap.Code, feedback.Sanitize(gap.File))
282		}
283		for _, gap := range v.Gaps {
284			fmt.Fprintf(out, "  coverage: %s %s\n", gap.Code, feedback.Sanitize(gap.File))
285			if gap.Encoding != nil {
286				h.encodingDetail(gap.Encoding)
287			}
288			if gap.Commit != "" {
289				fmt.Fprintf(out, "    commit: %s\n", feedback.Sanitize(gap.Commit))
290			}
291		}
292		if len(v.Gaps) > 0 {
293			fmt.Fprintln(out, style.warning("Scan incomplete: coverage gaps must be resolved; a partial report is never clean."))
294		}
295	}

40	func gitBytes(ctx context.Context, root string, input []byte, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
41		return runGitBytes(ctx, root, input, false, args...)
42	}
43	func snapshotGitBytes(ctx context.Context, root string, input []byte, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
44		return runGitBytes(ctx, root, input, true, args...)
45	}
46	func runGitBytes(ctx context.Context, root string, input []byte, isolated bool, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
47		base := []string{"-c", "core.fsmonitor=false", "-c", "core.longpaths=true", "-C", root}
48		if len(args) == 0 || args[0] != "config" {
49			base = append(base, "-c", "core.hooksPath="+os.DevNull)
50		}
51		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", append(base, args...)...)
52		if isolated {
53			cmd.Env = isolatedGitEnvironment()
54		}
55		cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(input)
56		var stderr bytes.Buffer
57		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
58		out, err := cmd.Output()
59		if err != nil {
60			command := "read"
61			if len(args) > 0 {
62				switch args[0] {
63				case "hash-object", "update-index", "ls-files", "diff", "cat-file", "show", "ls-tree", "rev-list", "rev-parse", "symbolic-ref", "for-each-ref", "config":
64					command = args[0]
65				}
66			}
67			return nil, fmt.Errorf("Git observation failed (%s: %s)", command, gitFailureReason(stderr.String()))
68		}
69		return out, nil
70	}

72	// Emit only fixed classifications. Git diagnostics can contain private paths,
73	// source values or input fragments and must never be forwarded to public output.
74	func gitFailureReason(stderr string) string {
75		text := strings.ToLower(stderr)
76		switch {
77		case strings.Contains(text, "filename too long") || strings.Contains(text, "file name too long"):
78			return "path length"
79		case strings.Contains(text, "dubious ownership") || strings.Contains(text, "not owned"):
80			return "ownership"
81		case strings.Contains(text, "permission denied") || strings.Contains(text, "access is denied"):
82			return "permissions"
83		case strings.Contains(text, "index.lock"):
84			return "index lock"
85		case strings.Contains(text, "not a git repository") || strings.Contains(text, "cannot change to") || strings.Contains(text, "no such file"):
86			return "repository path unavailable"
87		default:
88			return "command failed"
89		}
90	}
91	func validRelative(p string) bool {
92		return p != "" && p != "." && !filepath.IsAbs(p) && filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Clean(p)) == p && !strings.HasPrefix(p, "../") && !strings.Contains(p, "\x00") && p != ".git" && !strings.HasPrefix(p, ".git/")

94	func (s *Service) Scan(ctx context.Context, o ScanOptions) (Report, error) {
95		if o.Scope == "" {
96			o.Scope = "worktree"
97		}
98		if o.Range != "" && o.Scope != "history" {
99			return Report{}, errors.New("--range requires history scope")
100		}
101		if o.Scope != "worktree" && o.Scope != "staged" && o.Scope != "history" {
102			return Report{}, errors.New("scope must be staged, worktree or history")
103		}
104		if o.Timeout == 0 {
105			o.Timeout = 20 * time.Minute
106		}
107		if o.Timeout < 0 {
108			return Report{}, errors.New("timeout must be positive")
109		}
110		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, o.Timeout)
111		defer cancel()
112		if err := s.prepare(ctx); err != nil {
113			return Report{}, err
114		}
115		b := &scanBuilder{s: s, findings: map[string]int{}, gapSet: map[string]bool{}}
116		if o.CaptureValues {
117			b.values = newValueCollector()
118		}
119		b.record = scanRecord{Root: s.Root, Report: Report{SchemaVersion: 1, Kind: "hygiene_scan", ID: newID(), RepoID: s.RepoID, Scope: o.Scope, Status: "complete", Created: time.Now().UTC(), PolicyDigest: keyedID(s.key, policyDigest(s.Policy)), Findings: []Finding{}, PrivateRules: len(s.Policy.Rules), PublicOnly: s.PublicOnly, Audit: o.Audit}}
120		if s.Policy.Secrets == Off && s.Policy.Known == Off && s.Policy.Generic == Off {
121			b.record.Report.Status = "skipped"
122			b.record.Report.PolicyDisabled = true
123			if err := s.save(ctx, b.record.Report.ID, b.record); err != nil {
124				return b.record.Report, err
125			}
126			s.recordLatest(ctx, b.record.Report)
127			return b.record.Report, nil
128		}
129		for _, r := range s.Policy.Rules {
130			c, e := compileRule(r)
131			if e != nil {
132				return b.record.Report, e
133			}
134			b.compiled = append(b.compiled, c)
135		}
136		// Keep native Git's temporary path short: nesting it below the repository's
137		// 64-character identity and record ID can exceed Windows Git path limits.
138		// This sibling remains inside the already validated private state hierarchy.
139		scanRoot := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(s.Dir)), "scans")
140		if err := privatefile.EnsureDir(scanRoot); err != nil {
141			return b.record.Report, err
142		}
143		privateDir := filepath.Join(scanRoot, newID())
144		if err := privatefile.MakeDir(privateDir); err != nil {
145			return b.record.Report, err
146		}
147		defer os.RemoveAll(privateDir)
148		config, ignore, inputErr := s.scannerInputs(ctx, o.Audit)
149		if inputErr != nil {
150			b.gap("", "scanner_config_unreadable")
151		}
152		b.record.ScannerDigest = scannerDigest(config, ignore)
153		var err error
154		if inputErr != nil {
155			err = inputErr
156		} else if o.Scope == "history" {
157			err = b.history(ctx, o, privateDir, config, ignore)
158		} else {
159			err = b.current(ctx, o, privateDir, config, ignore)
160		}
161		if err != nil {
162			b.gap("", "observation_failed")
163		}
164		if ctx.Err() != nil {
165			b.gap("", "canceled_or_timed_out")
166		}
167		if e := s.checkInputs(ctx); e != nil {
168			b.gap("", "policy_changed")
169		}
170		if cfg, ig, e := s.scannerInputs(ctx, o.Audit); e != nil || scannerDigest(cfg, ig) != b.record.ScannerDigest {
171			b.gap("", "scanner_config_changed")
172		}
173	
174		r := &b.record.Report
175		for _, f := range r.Findings {
176			if f.Disposition == string(Block) {
177				r.Blocked++
178			}
179			if f.Disposition == string(Warn) {
180				r.Warnings++
181			}
182		}
183		if len(r.Gaps) > 0 {
184			r.Status = "partial"
185		}
186		sort.Slice(r.Findings, func(i, j int) bool {
187			a, c := r.Findings[i], r.Findings[j]
188			if a.File != c.File {
189				return a.File < c.File
190			}
191			if a.Line != c.Line {
192				return a.Line < c.Line
193			}
194			return a.Rule < c.Rule

196		// A timeout still produces a private partial receipt and a failing exit.
197		saveCtx, done := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)

201				return *r, errors.New("cannot save private hygiene values review")

204		if e := s.save(saveCtx, r.ID, b.record); e != nil {
205			return *r, errors.New("cannot save hygiene scan receipt")
206		}
207		s.recordLatest(saveCtx, *r)
208		if err != nil {
209			return *r, err
210		}
211		if r.Status != "complete" {
212			return *r, errors.New("hygiene scan incomplete; inspect coverage gaps")
213		}
214		return *r, nil
215	}
216	func (b *scanBuilder) gap(file, code string) {
217		key := file + "\x00" + code
218		if !b.gapSet[key] {
219			b.record.Report.Gaps = append(b.record.Report.Gaps, Gap{File: b.s.displayPath(file), Code: code})
220			b.gapSet[key] = true
221		}
222	}
223	func (b *scanBuilder) add(rule, category, file, commit string, line int, value string, mode Mode, can bool) string {
224		if mode == Off {
225			return ""
226		}
227		id := keyedID(b.s.key, category, rule, file, commit, value)
228		disposition := string(mode)
229		for _, e := range b.s.Policy.Exceptions {
230			if b.record.Report.Audit {
231				break

286				id := b.add(c.rule.ID, category, file, commit, line, string(data[m[0]:m[1]]), mode, can)
287				b.captureValue(id, c.rule.ID, category, file, commit, line, string(data[m[0]:m[1]]), lineContext(data, m[0], m[1]))
288				if id != "" && can {
289					replacement := c.rule.Replacement
290					if replacement == "" {
291						replacement = "[REDACTED:" + c.rule.ID + "]"
292					}
293					b.record.Edits = append(b.record.Edits, edit{id, file, m[0], m[1], replacement})
294				}
295			}
296		}

298	func (b *scanBuilder) current(ctx context.Context, o ScanOptions, privateDir string, config, ignore []byte) error {
299		var paths []string
300		var selectionBefore []byte
301		if o.Scope == "staged" {
302			raw, err := gitBytes(ctx, b.s.Root, nil, "diff", "--cached", "--no-ext-diff", "--no-textconv", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=ACMR", "-z")
303			if err != nil {
304				return err
305			}
306			paths = strings.Split(string(raw), "\x00")
307			selectionBefore, err = gitBytes(ctx, b.s.Root, nil, "ls-files", "--stage", "-z")
308			if err != nil {
309				return err
310			}
311		} else {
312			raw, err := gitBytes(ctx, b.s.Root, nil, "ls-files", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "-z")
313			if err != nil {
314				return err
315			}
316			paths = strings.Split(string(raw), "\x00")
317			selectionBefore = raw
318		}
319		if len(o.Files) > 0 {
320			selected := map[string]bool{}
321			for _, p := range paths {
322				selected[p] = true
323			}
324			paths = nil
325			for _, p := range o.Files {
326				if !selected[p] {
327					return errors.New("selected file is outside scan scope")
328				}
329				paths = append(paths, p)
330			}
331		}
332		snapshot := filepath.Join(privateDir, "snapshot")
333		if err := privatefile.MakeDir(snapshot); err != nil {
334			return err
335		}
336		init := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "-c", "core.longpaths=true", "-c", "init.templateDir=", "init", "--quiet", snapshot)
337		init.Env = isolatedGitEnvironment()
338		if init.Run() != nil {
339			return errors.New("cannot prepare scanner snapshot")
340		}
341		seen := map[string]bool{}
342		var index bytes.Buffer
343		dataMap := map[string][]byte{}
344		for _, file := range paths {
345			if file == "" || seen[file] {
346				continue
347			}
348			seen[file] = true
349			if !validRelative(file) {
350				b.gap("", "unsafe_path")
351				continue
352			}
353			var data []byte
354			var err error
355			token := ""
356			if o.Scope == "staged" {
357				mode, e := gitBytes(ctx, b.s.Root, nil, "ls-files", "--stage", "--", file)
358				if e != nil {
359					return e
360				}
361				if !bytes.HasPrefix(mode, []byte("100")) {
362					b.skip(file, "nonregular_index_entry")
363					continue
364				}
365				size, e := gitBytes(ctx, b.s.Root, nil, "cat-file", "-s", ":"+file)
366				if e != nil {
367					b.gap(file, "index_unreadable")
368					continue
369				}
370				n, e := strconv.ParseInt(strings.TrimSpace(string(size)), 10, 64)
371				if e != nil || n > MaxFileBytes {
372					b.gap(file, "file_limit")
373					continue
374				}
375				data, err = gitBytes(ctx, b.s.Root, nil, "show", ":"+file)
376			} else {
377				p := filepath.Join(b.s.Root, filepath.FromSlash(file))
378				info, e := os.Lstat(p)
379				if e == nil && (info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || info.IsDir()) {
380					b.skip(file, "nonregular_worktree_entry")
381					continue
382				}
383				data, err = safefile.ReadStablePath(ctx, p, MaxFileBytes)
384				if err == nil {
385					token = b.s.token(ctx, file)
386				}
387			}
388			if err != nil {
389				b.gap(file, "unreadable_or_changed")
390				continue
391			}
392			if issue := inspectEncoding(data); issue != nil {
393				b.binary(file, "", issue)
394				continue
395			}
396			b.record.Report.Files++
397			b.record.Report.Bytes += int64(len(data))
398			can := o.Scope == "worktree" && token != ""
399			b.record.Sources = append(b.record.Sources, source{file, digest(data), token})
400			b.native(file, "", data, can)
401			if b.s.Policy.Secrets != Off {
402				oid, e := snapshotGitBytes(ctx, snapshot, data, "hash-object", "-w", "--stdin")
403				if e != nil {
404					return e
405				}
406				fmt.Fprintf(&index, "100644 %s\t%s%c", strings.TrimSpace(string(oid)), file, 0)
407				dataMap[file] = data
408			}
409		}
410		if b.s.Policy.Secrets != Off && len(dataMap) > 0 {
411			if _, err := snapshotGitBytes(ctx, snapshot, index.Bytes(), "update-index", "-z", "--index-info"); err != nil {
412				return err
413			}
414			findings, err := b.s.Engine.Scan(ctx, EngineRequest{Root: snapshot, PrivateDir: privateDir, Config: config, Ignore: ignore, Audit: o.Audit})
415			if err != nil {
416				b.gap("", "secret_engine_failed")
417				return err
418			}
419			tokens := map[string]bool{}
420			for _, s := range b.record.Sources {
421				tokens[s.Path] = s.Token != ""
422			}
423			for _, d := range findings {
424				file := filepath.ToSlash(d.File)
425				data, ok := dataMap[file]
426				if !ok {
427					return errors.New("scanner returned a file outside its snapshot")
428				}
429				spans := secretSpans(data, d)
430				can := o.Scope == "worktree" && tokens[file] && len(spans) > 0
431				id := b.add(d.RuleID, "secret", file, "", d.StartLine, d.Secret, b.s.Policy.Secrets, can)
432				context := ""
433				if len(spans) > 0 {
434					context = lineContext(data, spans[0][0], spans[0][1])
435				}
436				b.captureValue(id, d.RuleID, "secret", file, "", d.StartLine, d.Secret, context)
437				if id != "" && can {
438					for _, m := range spans {
439						b.record.Edits = append(b.record.Edits, edit{id, file, m[0], m[1], "[REDACTED:" + d.RuleID + "]"})
440					}
441				}
442			}
443		}
444		if o.Scope == "staged" {
445			now, err := gitBytes(ctx, b.s.Root, nil, "ls-files", "--stage", "-z")
446			if err != nil || !bytes.Equal(now, selectionBefore) {
447				b.gap("", "index_changed")
448			}
449		}
450		for _, s := range b.record.Sources {
451			if o.Scope == "worktree" {
452				now, e := safefile.ReadStablePath(ctx, filepath.Join(b.s.Root, filepath.FromSlash(s.Path)), MaxFileBytes)
453				if e != nil || digest(now) != s.Digest {
454					b.gap(s.Path, "source_changed")
455				}
456			}
457		}
458		return nil
459	}
460	func secretSpans(data []byte, d Detection) [][2]int {
461		endLine := d.EndLine
462		if endLine < d.StartLine {
463			endLine = d.StartLine
464		}
465		start, end, line := 0, len(data), 1
466		for i, c := range data {
467			if c == '\n' {
468				line++
469				if line == d.StartLine {
470					start = i + 1
471				}
472				if line > endLine {
473					end = i
474					break
475				}
476			}
477		}
478		if d.StartLine > line || start > end {
479			return nil
480		}
481		part := data[start:end]
482		needle := []byte(d.Secret)
483		var out [][2]int
484		for offset := 0; offset < len(part); {
485			i := bytes.Index(part[offset:], needle)
486			if i < 0 {
487				break
488			}
489			a := start + offset + i
490			out = append(out, [2]int{a, a + len(needle)})
491			offset += i + len(needle)
492		}
493		return out
494	}

base_en="""## Choose the containment base

`dev retire --base <ref>` overrides the containment target for a DONE task or
linked worktree without changing recorded task intent. Resolution checks a local
branch (`refs/heads/X`), then a remote-tracking branch (`refs/remotes/X`, such as
`origin/main`), then a commit. Fully qualified branch refs keep their named kind.
Apply re-resolves the same input and requires the same kind, ref and commit OID;
a moved base or a newly created same-name branch makes the reviewed plan stale.
Remote-tracking refs are local observations, not an implicit fetch.

Without an override, task retirement keeps its recorded base. A recorded
fork-point commit is never silently replaced by the default branch: if it cannot
prove integration, retirement stays blocked with `pass --base <branch>` guidance.
After `dev done --merged --base-ref X`, cleanup hints, the cleanup wizard and the
external coordinator carry X forward as `dev retire --base X <task>`. If a shell
handoff cannot carry the override, dev prints the external command instead.

Optional `--delete-branch` still runs ordinary `git branch -d`, whose own merged
check uses the branch's upstream or HEAD, not `--base`. Against a non-HEAD base,
branch deletion can therefore fail after the worktree was removed; the branch
and DONE task remain, and the result reports partial completion.

"""
base_zh="""## 選擇 containment base

`dev retire --base <ref>` 可覆寫 DONE task 或 linked worktree 的整合驗證目標，不會
改寫 task 記錄的意圖。解析依序檢查本機分支（`refs/heads/X`）、remote-tracking
分支（`refs/remotes/X`，例如 `origin/main`），最後才是 commit。完整分支 ref
維持指名的類型。Apply 重新解析同一輸入，要求類型、ref 與 commit OID 完全一致；
base 移動或新增同名分支都會使已審閱 plan 過期。Remote-tracking ref 是本機觀測，
不會暗中 fetch。

未指定 override 時，task retirement 沿用記錄的 base。記錄為 fork-point commit
時，絕不暗中改用預設分支；若無法證明整合，仍會阻擋並提示 `pass --base <branch>`。
`dev done --merged --base-ref X` 會將 X 帶入 cleanup 提示、wizard 與外部
coordinator，對應命令是 `dev retire --base X <task>`。若 shell handoff 無法攜帶
該 override，dev 會改為列出從外部執行的命令。

可選的 `--delete-branch` 仍執行一般 `git branch -d`；Git 自己的 merged 檢查使用
分支的 upstream 或 HEAD，不是 `--base`。因此對非 HEAD base 清理時，可能已移除
worktree 卻無法刪除分支；分支與 DONE task 會保留，結果回報部分完成。

"""

sweep_en="""`dev sweep --base <ref>` also forwards the selected base to DONE task retirement;
`--merged-worktrees` uses its verified base for managed tasks as well as unmanaged
checkouts. Reviewed retire/remove plans bind worktree-list authority only to the
same branch or paths equal to, containing, or nested under the target. Removing
an unrelated sibling no longer invalidates the rest of an approved
`--apply --yes` batch. A same-branch checkout or target lock/HEAD change still
makes the plan stale; containment and all other guards remain required.

"""
sweep_zh="""`dev sweep --base <ref>` 也會把選定 base 傳入 DONE task retirement；
`--merged-worktrees` 對 managed task 與 unmanaged checkout 都使用已驗證的 base。
已審閱 retire／remove plan 的 worktree-list authority 只涵蓋同分支，或路徑與
目標相同、包含目標、位於目標之下的 worktree。先移除無關的 sibling 不再使
`--apply --yes` 批次剩餘項目過期；同分支新增 checkout 或目標 lock／HEAD 改變
仍會使 plan 過期。Containment 與其他安全檢查仍不可省略。

"""

150				}
151			} else if err != nil {
152				return err
153			}
154			info, err := os.Lstat(p)
155			if err != nil || len(b) != 32 {

159				return err
160			}
161			s.key = b
162			return nil
163		})

174		b, err := json.Marshal(v)

182	}

186		}

198		}
199		if err = json.Unmarshal(b, v); err != nil {

204	func (s *Service) displayPath(p string) string {
205		out := filepath.ToSlash(p)
206		for _, r := range s.Policy.Rules {
207			if r.Kind == "literal" && r.Value != "" {
208				out = strings.ReplaceAll(out, r.Value, "[private]")
209			}
210		}
211		for _, r := range s.Policy.Rules {
212			if r.Kind == "cidr" {
213				c, e := compileRule(r)
214				if e == nil {
215					ranges := c.indices(filepath.ToSlash(p), []byte(out))
216					for i := len(ranges) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
217						m := ranges[i]
218						out = out[:m[0]] + "[private]" + out[m[1]:]
219					}
220				}
221			}
222		}
223		out = strings.ReplaceAll(out, "\n", "[newline]")
224		out = strings.ReplaceAll(out, "\r", "[return]")
225		out = strings.ReplaceAll(out, "\x1b", "[escape]")
226		return feedback.Sanitize(out)
227	}

145	
146	var ipToken = regexp.MustCompile(`[0-9A-Fa-f:.]+(?:%[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)?`)
147	
148	func compileRule(r Rule) (compiledRule, error) {
149		c := compiledRule{rule: r}
150		if !identifier.MatchString(r.ID) || r.Value == "" || len(r.Value) > 8192 || len(r.Replacement) > 4096 {
151			return c, errors.New("invalid hygiene rule ID or size")
152		}
153		if r.Action != "" && !validMode(r.Action) {
154			return c, errors.New("invalid hygiene rule action")
155		}
156		for _, p := range r.Paths {
157			if _, err := path.Match(p, ""); err != nil {
158				return c, errors.New("invalid rule path glob")
159			}
160		}
161		var err error
162		switch r.Kind {
163		case "literal":
164			// Match the exact string or JSON-escaped representation, without exposing it.
165			encoded, _ := json.Marshal(r.Value)
166			escaped := string(encoded[1 : len(encoded)-1])
167			pattern := regexp.QuoteMeta(r.Value)
168			if escaped != r.Value {
169				pattern += "|" + regexp.QuoteMeta(escaped)
170			}
171			c.re, err = regexp.Compile(pattern)
172		case "regex":
173			c.re, err = regexp.Compile(r.Value)
174		case "cidr":
175			c.cidr, err = netip.ParsePrefix(r.Value)
176		default:
177			err = errors.New("unsupported rule kind")
178		}
179		if err != nil {
180			return c, errors.New("invalid hygiene rule expression")
181		}
182		return c, nil
183	}
184	func pathMatches(pattern, file string) bool {
185		ok, _ := path.Match(pattern, file)
186		return ok || strings.HasSuffix(pattern, "/**") && strings.HasPrefix(file, strings.TrimSuffix(pattern, "**"))
187	}
188	func (c compiledRule) indices(file string, b []byte) [][2]int {
189		if len(c.rule.Paths) > 0 {
190			ok := false
191			for _, p := range c.rule.Paths {
192				ok = ok || pathMatches(p, file)
193			}
194			if !ok {
195				return nil
196			}
197		}
198		var result [][2]int
199		if c.re != nil {
200			for _, m := range c.re.FindAllIndex(b, -1) {
201				if m[0] == m[1] {
202					continue
203				}
204				if c.rule.Kind == "literal" && (!literalBoundary(b, m[0], true) || !literalBoundary(b, m[1], false)) {
205					continue
206				}
207				result = append(result, [2]int{m[0], m[1]})
208			}
209			return result
210		}
211		for _, m := range ipToken.FindAllIndex(b, -1) {
212			raw := strings.Trim(string(b[m[0]:m[1]]), ".")
213			addr, err := netip.ParseAddr(raw)
214			if err == nil && c.cidr.Contains(addr.WithZone("")) {
215				start := m[0] + strings.Index(string(b[m[0]:m[1]]), raw)
216				result = append(result, [2]int{start, start + len(raw)})
217			}
218		}
219		return result

14	func refSnapshot(ctx context.Context, root string) (map[string]string, []byte, error) {
15		raw, err := gitBytes(ctx, root, nil, "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname)%00%(objectname)")
16		if err != nil {
17			return nil, nil, err
18		}
19		refs := map[string]string{}
20		for _, line := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(string(raw)), "\n") {
21			parts := strings.SplitN(line, "\x00", 2)
22			if len(parts) == 2 {
23				refs[parts[0]] = parts[1]
24			}
25		}
26		head, err := gitBytes(ctx, root, nil, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
27		if err != nil {
28			return nil, nil, err
29		}
30		refs["HEAD"] = strings.TrimSpace(string(head))
31		return refs, append(raw, head...), nil
32	}
33	func (b *scanBuilder) history(ctx context.Context, o ScanOptions, privateDir string, config, ignore []byte) error {
34		if len(o.Files) > 0 {
35			return errors.New("history scan does not accept file selections")
36		}
37		refs, before, err := refSnapshot(ctx, b.s.Root)
38		if err != nil {
39			return err
40		}
41		b.record.Report.Refs = map[string]string{}
42		tips := []string{}
43		unique := map[string]bool{}
44		for name, oid := range refs {
45			b.record.Report.Refs[b.s.displayPath(name)] = oid
46			if !unique[oid] {
47				tips = append(tips, oid)
48				unique[oid] = true
49			}
50		}
51		sort.Strings(tips)
52		if o.Range != "" {
53			parts := regexp.MustCompile(`^([a-f0-9]{40}|[a-f0-9]{64})\.\.([a-f0-9]{40}|[a-f0-9]{64})$`).FindStringSubmatch(o.Range)
54			if parts == nil {
55				return errors.New("history range must be two full commit OIDs separated by ..")
56			}
57			for _, oid := range parts[1:] {
58				if _, e := gitBytes(ctx, b.s.Root, nil, "cat-file", "-e", oid+"^{commit}"); e != nil {
59					return errors.New("range commit is unavailable locally")
60				}
61			}
62			tips = []string{o.Range}
63			b.record.Report.Refs = map[string]string{"range_from": parts[1], "range_to": parts[2]}
64		}
65		shallow, err := gitBytes(ctx, b.s.Root, nil, "rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository")
66		if err != nil {
67			return err
68		}
69		if strings.TrimSpace(string(shallow)) == "true" {
70			b.gap("", "shallow_history")
71		}
72		if b.s.Policy.Secrets != Off {
73			rows, err := b.s.Engine.Scan(ctx, EngineRequest{Root: b.s.Root, PrivateDir: privateDir, Config: config, History: true, Refs: tips, Ignore: ignore, Audit: o.Audit})
74			if err != nil {
75				b.gap("", "secret_engine_failed")
76				return err
77			}
78			for _, d := range rows {
79				file := filepath.ToSlash(d.File)
80				if !validRelative(file) {
81					b.gap("", "invalid_engine_path")
82					continue
83				}
84				id := b.add(d.RuleID, "secret", file, d.Commit, d.StartLine, d.Secret, b.s.Policy.Secrets, false)
85				b.captureValue(id, d.RuleID, "secret", file, d.Commit, d.StartLine, d.Secret, "")
86			}
87		}
88		commits, err := gitBytes(ctx, b.s.Root, []byte(strings.Join(tips, "\n")+"\n"), "rev-list", "--stdin")
89		if err != nil {
90			return err
91		}
92		// Enumerating trees also covers merge-only blobs, removed files and paths
93		// now ignored. Each blob/path pair is read once across the frozen history.
94		seen := map[string]bool{}
95		for _, commit := range strings.Fields(string(commits)) {
96			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
97				return err
98			}
99			changed := map[string]bool{}
100			if o.Range != "" {
101				paths, e := gitBytes(ctx, b.s.Root, nil, "diff-tree", "--root", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "--no-renames", "--diff-merges=first-parent", "-r", "-z", commit)
102				if e != nil {
103					return e
104				}
105				for _, p := range bytes.Split(paths, []byte{0}) {
106					if len(p) > 0 {
107						changed[string(p)] = true
108					}
109				}
110			}
111			tree, err := gitBytes(ctx, b.s.Root, nil, "ls-tree", "-r", "-l", "-z", commit)
112			if err != nil {
113				b.gap("", "history_tree_unreadable")
114				return err
115			}
116			for _, entry := range bytes.Split(tree, []byte{0}) {
117				pieces := bytes.SplitN(entry, []byte{'\t'}, 2)
118				if len(pieces) != 2 {
119					continue
120				}
121				fields := strings.Fields(string(pieces[0]))
122				file := string(pieces[1])
123				if o.Range != "" && !changed[file] {
124					continue
125				}
126				if len(fields) != 4 || !validRelative(file) {
127					b.gap("", "history_entry_invalid")
128					continue
129				}
130				oid := fields[2]
131				key := oid + "\x00" + file
132				if seen[key] {
133					continue
134				}
135				seen[key] = true
136				if fields[0] != "100644" && fields[0] != "100755" {
137					b.skip(file, "nonregular_history_entry")
138					continue
139				}
140				size, err := strconv.ParseInt(fields[3], 10, 64)
141				if err != nil || size > MaxFileBytes {
142					b.gap(file, "history_file_limit")
143					continue
144				}
145				data, err := gitBytes(ctx, b.s.Root, nil, "cat-file", "blob", oid)
146				if err != nil {
147					b.gap(file, "history_blob_unreadable")
148					return err
149				}
150				if issue := inspectEncoding(data); issue != nil {
151					b.binary(file, commit, issue)
152					continue
153				}
154				b.record.Report.Files++
155				b.record.Report.Bytes += int64(len(data))
156				b.native(file, commit, data, false)
157			}
158		}
159		_, after, err := refSnapshot(ctx, b.s.Root)
160		if o.Range == "" && (err != nil || !bytes.Equal(before, after)) {
161			b.gap("", "refs_changed")
162		}
163		return nil
164	}

1	package taskflow
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"fmt"
6		"strings"
7	)
8	
9	// BaseKind names how a containment base resolved.
10	type BaseKind string
11	
12	const (
13		BaseLocalBranch    BaseKind = "local-branch"
14		BaseRemoteTracking BaseKind = "remote-tracking"
15		BaseCommit         BaseKind = "commit"
16	)
17	
18	// baseResolution is the exact containment base observed for a destructive
19	// plan. Apply re-resolves the same input and requires the same kind, ref and
20	// commit, so a branch created with the name of a recorded commit makes the
21	// plan stale instead of silently changing the proof.
22	type baseResolution struct {
23		input  string
24		ref    string
25		kind   BaseKind
26		exists bool
27		oid    string
28		err    error
29	}
30	
31	// resolveBaseRef resolves a recorded or explicitly selected base in a fixed
32	// order: exact local branch, remote-tracking branch, then any commit-ish such
33	// as a recorded fork-point OID. A probe failure stops resolution rather than
34	// falling through to a weaker kind.
35	func (s *lifecycleService) resolveBaseRef(ctx context.Context, repoPath, input string) baseResolution {
36		resolved := baseResolution{input: input}
37		if input == "" || repoPath == "" {
38			return resolved
39		}
40		if input != strings.TrimSpace(input) || strings.ContainsRune(input, '\x00') || strings.HasPrefix(input, "-") {
41			resolved.err = fmt.Errorf("base %q is not a normalized ref or commit", input)
42			return resolved
43		}
44		type candidate struct {
45			ref  string
46			kind BaseKind
47		}
48		var candidates []candidate
49		switch {
50		case strings.HasPrefix(input, "refs/heads/"):
51			candidates = []candidate{{input, BaseLocalBranch}}
52		case strings.HasPrefix(input, "refs/remotes/"):
53			candidates = []candidate{{input, BaseRemoteTracking}}
54		default:
55			candidates = []candidate{
56				{"refs/heads/" + input, BaseLocalBranch},
57				{"refs/remotes/" + input, BaseRemoteTracking},
58				{input, BaseCommit},
59			}
60		}
61		for _, next := range candidates {
62			exists, err := s.gitRefState(ctx, repoPath, next.ref)
63			if err != nil {
64				resolved.err = err
65				return resolved
66			}
67			if !exists {
68				continue
69			}
70			resolved.ref, resolved.kind, resolved.exists = next.ref, next.kind, true
71			resolved.oid, resolved.err = s.resolveRefOID(ctx, repoPath, next.ref)
72			return resolved
73		}
74		return resolved
75	}
76	
77	func (b baseResolution) authority() string {
78		return authorityHash("taskflow-base-resolution-v1",
79			b.input, b.ref, string(b.kind), boolString(b.exists), b.oid, errorString(b.err))
80	}
81	
82	// describe renders the resolved base for condition evidence.
83	func (b baseResolution) describe() string {
84		switch b.kind {
85		case BaseLocalBranch:
86			return fmt.Sprintf("local branch %s at %s", b.ref, b.oid)
87		case BaseRemoteTracking:
88			return fmt.Sprintf("remote-tracking branch %s at %s", b.ref, b.oid)
89		case BaseCommit:
90			return fmt.Sprintf("commit %s", b.oid)
91		default:
92			return "an unresolved ref"
93		}
94	}
95	
96	// aliasesBranch reports whether the base names the task branch itself, so
97	// branch deletion never removes the base it is proved against.
98	func (b baseResolution) aliasesBranch(branch string) bool {
99		if branch == "" {
100			return false
101		}
102		local := "refs/heads/" + branch
103		return b.input == branch || b.input == "heads/"+branch || b.input == local ||
104			(b.kind == BaseLocalBranch && b.ref == local)
105	}

1	package hygiene
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"strings"
6	)
7	
8	// WriterAgent is one recognized live agent whose working directory covers the
9	// checkout a hygiene or artifact transaction will change.
10	type WriterAgent struct {
11		Caller   bool
12		Blocking bool
13		// Session is the runtime-reported "provider:id" identity, when known.
14		Session string
15	}
16	
17	// WriterTarget is one file the transaction will replace.
18	type WriterTarget struct {
19		Artifact bool
20		// Session is the anchored SpecStory preamble session id, when proven.
21		Session string
22	}
23	
24	const writerOccupied = "a recognized agent still occupies the checkout"
25	
26	// CheckWriters applies the artifact writer policy. Other agents always block
27	// artifact edits. The calling agent may edit artifacts only when every target
28	// is provably another session's transcript, or when the caller explicitly
29	// asserts disjoint ownership; its own transcript is never editable while live.
30	func CheckWriters(agents []WriterAgent, targets []WriterTarget, allowCallerShared bool) error {
31		artifact := false
32		for _, target := range targets {
33			artifact = artifact || target.Artifact
34		}
35		for _, agent := range agents {
36			if !agent.Caller {
37				if agent.Blocking || artifact {
38					return errors.New(writerOccupied + "; stop the writer before applying")
39				}
40				continue
41			}
42			if agent.Blocking {
43				return errors.New(writerOccupied + "; stop the writer before applying")
44			}
45			if !artifact {
46				continue
47			}
48			caller := sessionID(agent.Session)
49			proven := caller != ""
50			for _, target := range targets {
51				if !target.Artifact {
52					continue
53				}
54				if caller != "" && strings.EqualFold(target.Session, caller) {
55					return errors.New(writerOccupied + "; a target is the calling agent's own live transcript")
56				}
57				proven = proven && target.Session != ""
58			}
59			if !proven && !allowCallerShared {
60				return errors.New(writerOccupied + "; the calling agent cannot prove the artifacts belong to another session (stop it, or pass --allow-shared-checkout after confirming the writer exited)")
61			}
62		}
63		return nil
64	}
65	
66	func sessionID(session string) string {
67		if _, id, ok := strings.Cut(session, ":"); ok {
68			return strings.TrimSpace(id)
69		}
70		return strings.TrimSpace(session)
71	}
72

+// scopeDestructiveWorktrees keeps registered worktrees on the target branch or

+func (s *lifecycleService) scopeDestructiveWorktrees(worktrees []gitx.Worktree, branch, checkout string) []gitx.Worktree {

+	return filepath.Clean(path)

+	return err == nil && !filepath.IsAbs(rel) && rel != ".." && !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))

+func writeGuardTranscript(t *testing.T, root, name, provider, session string) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	path := filepath.Join(root, ".specstory", "history", name)
+	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	body := "<!-- Generated by SpecStory, Markdown v2.1.0 -->\n\n# now\n\n<!-- " + provider + " Session " + session + " (now) -->\n\nbody\n"
+	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(body), 0o600); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	return path
+}

+		t.Fatalf("caller could not repair another session's transcript: %v", err)
+	}
+}

33	// FindTranscript selects exactly one SpecStory transcript by its anchored
34	// preamble session UUID. UUID mentions later in a transcript are never used.
35	func FindTranscript(worktree, provider, sessionID string) (Transcript, error) {
36		history := filepath.Join(worktree, ".specstory", "history")
37		entries, err := os.ReadDir(history)
38		if err != nil {
39			return Transcript{}, err
40		}
41		var matches []Transcript
42		for _, entry := range entries {
43			if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".md") {
44				continue
45			}
46			path := filepath.Join(history, entry.Name())
47			inside, err := pathx.Contains(history, path)
48			if err != nil || !inside {
49				continue
50			}
51			gotProvider, gotSession, err := transcriptPreamble(path)
52			if err != nil || gotSession != sessionID || (provider != "" && gotProvider != provider) {
53				continue
54			}
55			matches = append(matches, Transcript{Path: path, Provider: gotProvider, SessionID: gotSession})
56		}
57		switch len(matches) {
58		case 1:
59			return matches[0], nil
60		case 0:
61			return Transcript{}, fmt.Errorf("no SpecStory transcript with preamble session %s:%s", provider, sessionID)
62		default:
63			return Transcript{}, fmt.Errorf("multiple SpecStory transcripts have preamble session %s:%s", provider, sessionID)
64		}
65	}
66	
67	// ReadTranscriptSession returns the anchored SpecStory preamble identity of one
68	// regular transcript file. Symlinks and later UUID mentions are never used.
69	func ReadTranscriptSession(path string) (provider, sessionID string, err error) {
70		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
71		if err != nil {
72			return "", "", err
73		}
74		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
75			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("SpecStory transcript is not a regular file")
76		}
77		return transcriptPreamble(path)
78	}

80	func transcriptPreamble(path string) (provider, sessionID string, err error) {
81		file, err := os.Open(path)
82		if err != nil {
83			return "", "", err
84		}
85		defer file.Close()
86		scanner := bufio.NewScanner(io.LimitReader(file, 16<<10))
87		for line := 0; scanner.Scan() && line < 12; line++ {
88			match := transcriptSessionLine.FindStringSubmatch(scanner.Text())
89			if len(match) != 3 {
90				continue
91			}
92			return normalizeProvider(match[1]), match[2], nil
93		}
94		if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
95			return "", "", err
96		}
97		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("SpecStory session preamble not found")
98	}

105			}
106		}
107		if first, _, ok := strings.Cut(label, " "); ok {
108			return first
109		}
110		return label
111	}
112	
113	// StableSnapshot requires the transcript bytes and metadata to remain unchanged
114	// across a settle interval.
115	func StableSnapshot(ctx context.Context, path string, settle time.Duration) (Snapshot, error) {
116		if settle <= 0 {
117			settle = 250 * time.Millisecond
118		}
119		first, err := snapshot(path)
120		if err != nil {
121			return Snapshot{}, err
122		}
123		select {
124		case <-ctx.Done():
125			return Snapshot{}, ctx.Err()
126		case <-time.After(settle):
127		}
128		second, err := snapshot(path)
129		if err != nil {
130			return Snapshot{}, err
131		}
132		if first.Size != second.Size || !first.ModTime.Equal(second.ModTime) || first.SHA256 != second.SHA256 {
133			return Snapshot{}, fmt.Errorf("transcript is still changing")
134		}
135		return second, nil
136	}
137	
138	func snapshot(path string) (Snapshot, error) {
139		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
140		if err != nil {
141			return Snapshot{}, err
142		}
143		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
144			return Snapshot{}, fmt.Errorf("transcript is not a regular file")
145		}
146		file, err := os.Open(path)
147		if err != nil {
148			return Snapshot{}, err
149		}
150		defer file.Close()
151		hash := sha256.New()
152		if _, err := io.Copy(hash, file); err != nil {
153			return Snapshot{}, err
154		}
155		return Snapshot{Size: info.Size(), ModTime: info.ModTime(), SHA256: hex.EncodeToString(hash.Sum(nil))}, nil
156	}

92	// InspectOccupancy collects independent runtime, recognized-agent, and caller
93	// evidence for target. Initial target canonicalization errors are returned;
94	// observation failures are retained in their corresponding fields so each
95	// action can apply its own fail-closed acknowledgement policy.
96	func InspectOccupancy(ctx context.Context, rt Runtime, target string, opts OccupancyOptions) (Occupancy, error) {
97		checkout, err := inspectCheckoutIdentity(ctx, target)
98		if err != nil {
99			return Occupancy{}, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize occupancy target: %w", err)
100		}
101		result := Occupancy{
102			Target:               checkout.path,
103			Backend:              "none",
104			Profile:              opts.Profile,
105			CallerWorkspaceID:    opts.CallerWorkspaceID,
106			ReportedCallerPaneID: opts.CallerPaneID,
107			CallerPaneID:         opts.CallerPaneID,
108		}
109		if rt == nil {
110			return result, nil
111		}
112		result.Backend = rt.Name()
113		if result.Backend == "none" {
114			return result, nil
115		}
116	
117		result.SessionList.Supported = true
118		resolver, resolvesCurrentPane := rt.(CurrentPaneResolver)
119		result.CurrentPane.Supported = resolvesCurrentPane
120		if resolvesCurrentPane && opts.CallerPaneID != "" {
121			result.CurrentPane.Attempted = true
122			result.CallerPaneID = ""
123			paneID, resolveErr := resolver.CurrentPaneID(ctx)
124			if resolveErr != nil {
125				result.CurrentPane.Err = resolveErr
126			} else if paneID == "" {
127				result.CurrentPane.Err = fmt.Errorf("current pane resolver returned an empty pane id")
128			} else {
129				result.CallerPaneID = paneID
130			}
131		}
132	
133		result.SessionList.Attempted = true
134		sessions, listErr := rt.List(ctx)
135		if listErr != nil {
136			result.SessionList.Err = listErr
137		} else {
138			for _, observed := range sessions {
139				if opts.InspectProcesses {
140					observed.Panes = append([]Pane(nil), observed.Panes...)
141					// Probe only sessions covering the target; unrelated programs are
142					// outside this action's scope.
143					covering, _, _ := classifyOccupancySession(ctx, checkout, observed, opts.Profile)
144					if len(covering) > 0 {
145						for i, pane := range observed.Panes {
146							observed.Panes[i] = observePaneProcess(ctx, rt, pane, result.CallerPaneID, opts.CallerPID)
147						}
148					}
149				}
150				covering, mixed, classifyErr := classifyOccupancySession(ctx, checkout, observed, opts.Profile)
151				if classifyErr != nil {
152					result.SessionCoverageErr = classifyErr
153					result.Sessions = nil
154					break
155				}
156				if len(covering) == 0 {
157					continue
158				}
159				result.Sessions = append(result.Sessions, OccupancySession{
160					Runtime: observed,
161					Panes:   covering,
162					Mixed:   mixed,
163					IsCaller: observed.Handle == opts.CallerWorkspaceID ||
164						occupancyPanePresent(observed.Panes, result.CallerPaneID),
165				})

167		}

169		lister, listsAgents := rt.(AgentActivityLister)
170		result.AgentActivityList.Supported = listsAgents

173			// richer recognized-agent inventory. Preserve that live evidence as the
174			// strict-profile fallback rather than treating an unsupported lister as an
175			// observed empty list.
176			for _, session := range result.Sessions {
177				for _, pane := range session.Panes {
178					if pane.Agent == "" && pane.AgentSession == "" {
179						continue
180					}
181					cwd := pane.CWD
182					if cwd == "" {
183						cwd = pane.ShellCWD
184					}
185					activity := AgentActivity{
186						PaneID: pane.ID, WorkspaceID: session.Runtime.Handle,
187						Agent: pane.Agent, Status: pane.AgentStatus, CWD: cwd, Session: pane.AgentSession,
188					}
189					if coverageErr := appendOccupancyAgent(ctx, &result, checkout, opts, activity); coverageErr != nil {
190						result.SessionCoverageErr = coverageErr

193					}
194				}
195			}
196			return result, nil
197		}
198		result.AgentActivityList.Attempted = true
199		activities, activityErr := lister.AgentActivities(ctx)

202			return result, nil
203		}
204		for _, activity := range activities {

206				result.AgentActivityList.Err = coverageErr
207				result.Agents = nil
208				return result, nil
209			}
210		}
211		return result, nil

214	func appendOccupancyAgent(ctx context.Context, result *Occupancy, checkout checkoutIdentity, opts OccupancyOptions, activity AgentActivity) error {
215		covered, err := activityCoversCheckout(ctx, checkout, activity.CWD, opts.Profile)
216		if err != nil {
217			return fmt.Errorf("classify recognized agent pane %s: %w", activity.PaneID, err)
218		}
219		if !covered {
220			return nil
221		}
222		status := normalizeOccupancyStatus(activity.Status)
223		caller := result.CallerPaneID != "" && activity.PaneID == result.CallerPaneID
224		handle := correlatedSession(result.Sessions, activity)
225		result.Agents = append(result.Agents, OccupancyAgent{
226			Activity:      activity,
227			Status:        status,
228			SessionHandle: handle,
229			IsCaller:      caller,
230			Blocking:      occupancyAgentBlocks(opts, status, caller, handle != ""),
231		})
232		return nil
233	}

237		git    bool

241	func inspectCheckoutIdentity(ctx context.Context, dir string) (checkoutIdentity, error) {
242		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(dir)
243		if err != nil {
244			return checkoutIdentity{}, err
245		}
246		repo, discoverErr := gitx.Discover(ctx, canonical)
247		if discoverErr == nil && repo.Root != "" {
248			root, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(repo.Root)
249			if canonicalErr != nil {
250				return checkoutIdentity{}, canonicalErr
251			}
252			return checkoutIdentity{path: root, git: true, linked: repo.IsLinkedWorktree}, nil
253		}
254		if discoverErr != nil && !errors.Is(discoverErr, gitx.ErrNotARepo) {
255			return checkoutIdentity{}, discoverErr
256		}
257		return checkoutIdentity{path: canonical}, nil
258	}
259	
260	func activityCoversCheckout(ctx context.Context, target checkoutIdentity, cwd string, profile OccupancyProfile) (bool, error) {
261		if cwd == "" {
262			return false, fmt.Errorf("recognized agent has no cwd")
263		}
264		activity, err := inspectCheckoutIdentity(ctx, cwd)
265		if err != nil {
266			return false, err
267		}
268		if target.git && activity.git {
269			if target.path == activity.path {
270				return true, nil
271			}
272			if profile == OccupancyCleanup && target.linked {
273				return pathx.Contains(target.path, activity.path)
274			}
275			pairs := [][2]string{{target.path, activity.path}}
276			if profile == OccupancyStrict {
277				pairs = append(pairs, [2]string{activity.path, target.path})
278			}
279			for _, pair := range pairs {
280				inside, err := pathx.Contains(pair[0], pair[1])
281				if err != nil {
282					return false, err
283				}
284				if !inside {
285					continue
286				}
287				graph, err := gitx.SubmodulesOf(ctx, pair[0])
288				if err != nil {
289					return false, err
290				}
291				for _, node := range graph.Nodes {
292					if node.Initialized {
293						root, err := pathx.Canonical(filepath.Join(pair[0], filepath.FromSlash(node.Path)))
294						if err != nil {
295							return false, err
296						}
297						if root == pair[1] {
298							return true, nil
299						}
300					}
301				}
302			}
303			return false, nil
304		}
305		return pathx.Contains(target.path, activity.path)
306	}
307	
308	func classifyOccupancySession(ctx context.Context, target checkoutIdentity, session Session, profile OccupancyProfile) ([]Pane, []Pane, error) {
309		panes := session.Panes
310		if len(panes) == 0 {
311			for i, dir := range session.Dirs {
312				panes = append(panes, Pane{ID: fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", session.Handle, i), CWD: dir})
313			}
314		}
315		var covering, mixed []Pane
316		for _, pane := range panes {
317			paths := []string{pane.CWD}
318			if pane.Process != nil {
319				for _, process := range pane.Process.Processes {
320					if process.CWD != "" {
321						paths = append(paths, process.CWD)
322					}
323				}
324			}
325			if pane.ShellCWD != "" && pane.ShellCWD != pane.CWD {
326				paths = append(paths, pane.ShellCWD)
327			}
328			paneCovers, paneOutside, observed := false, false, false
329			for _, path := range paths {
330				if path == "" {
331					continue
332				}
333				observed = true
334				inside, err := activityCoversCheckout(ctx, target, path, profile)
335				if err != nil {
336					return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("compare runtime pane %s path: %w", pane.ID, err)
337				}
338				if inside {
339					paneCovers = true
340				} else {
341					paneOutside = true
342				}
343			}
344			if paneCovers {
345				covering = append(covering, pane)
346			}
347			if paneOutside || !observed {
348				mixed = append(mixed, pane)
349			}
350		}
351		return covering, mixed, nil
352	}
353	
354	func occupancyPanePresent(panes []Pane, id string) bool {
355		if id == "" {
356			return false
357		}
358		for _, pane := range panes {
359			if pane.ID == id {
360				return true
361			}
362		}
363		return false
364	}
365	
366	func correlatedSession(sessions []OccupancySession, activity AgentActivity) string {
367		for _, session := range sessions {
368			if activity.WorkspaceID != "" && session.Runtime.Handle == activity.WorkspaceID {
369				return session.Runtime.Handle
370			}
371			if occupancyPanePresent(session.Runtime.Panes, activity.PaneID) {
372				return session.Runtime.Handle
373			}
374		}
375		return ""
376	}
377	
378	func normalizeOccupancyStatus(status string) string {
379		status = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(status))
380		if status == "" {
381			return "unknown"
382		}
383		return status
384	}
385	
386	func occupancyAgentBlocks(opts OccupancyOptions, status string, caller, correlated bool) bool {
387		if opts.Profile != OccupancyCleanup {
388			return !caller
389		}
390		// Cleanup can never close the caller or an activity that does not correlate
391		// with a freshly listed covering session.
392		if caller || !correlated {
393			return true
394		}
395		switch status {
396		case "idle", "done":
397			return false
398		case "unknown":
399			return !opts.CloseUnknown
400		default:
401			return true
402		}
403	}

102	func (s *lifecycleService) inspectDestructive(ctx context.Context, input destructiveInspectInput) (destructiveObservation, error) {
103		observed := destructiveObservation{locator: input.locator, runtime: input.runtime, runtimeErr: input.rtErr}
104		if err := contextError(ctx); err != nil {
105			return observed, err
106		}
107	
108		repository, err := s.gitDiscover(ctx, input.locator.RepoPath)
109		if err != nil {
110			observed.repoErr = err
111			return observed, nil

114		observed.repoPath, err = s.canonicalPath(repository.MainRoot)
115		if err != nil {
116			observed.repoErr = fmt.Errorf("canonicalize Git main checkout: %w", err)
117			return observed, nil
118		}
119		observed.gitCommonDir, err = s.canonicalPath(repository.GitCommonDir)

123		}
124		requestedRepo, err := s.canonicalPath(input.locator.RepoPath)
125		if err != nil {
126			return observed, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize requested repository: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, err)
127		}
128		requestedCommon, err := s.canonicalPath(input.locator.GitCommonDir)
129		if err != nil {
130			return observed, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize requested Git common directory: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, err)
131		}
132		if requestedRepo != observed.repoPath || requestedCommon != observed.gitCommonDir {
133			return observed, &StalePlanError{Reason: fmt.Sprintf(
134				"selected repository identity changed: main %q -> %q, common directory %q -> %q",
135				requestedRepo, observed.repoPath, requestedCommon, observed.gitCommonDir,
136			)}
137		}
138		if filepath.IsAbs(input.locator.RepoKey) {
139			key, keyErr := s.canonicalPath(input.locator.RepoKey)
140			if keyErr != nil {
141				return observed, fmt.Errorf("%w: canonicalize repository key: %v", ErrInvalidRequest, keyErr)
142			}
143			if key != observed.gitCommonDir {
144				return observed, &StalePlanError{Reason: "selected repository key no longer names the Git common directory"}
145			}

147	
148		observed.worktrees, observed.worktreesErr = s.gitWorktrees(ctx, observed.repoPath)

151			if err != nil {
152				observed.worktreeErr = fmt.Errorf("canonicalize selected checkout: %w", err)
153			} else {
154				observed.worktree, observed.worktreeErr = s.resolveWorktree(ctx, observed.repoPath, observed.checkout)

160						observed.contentFingerprint = analysis.Fingerprint
161						observed.contentErr = contentErr
162					}

164				}

166		}
167

169		observed.observeRefs(ctx, s, input.locator.Branch, input.base)
170		if input.inspectArtifacts && observed.worktreeFound {
171			observed.artifact, observed.artifactErr = s.inspectArtifacts(ctx, s.artifacts, observed.checkout)
172		}
173		if !input.noCheckout && !input.skipCleanup {
174			if observed.runtimeErr == nil {
175				if observed.runtime == nil || strings.TrimSpace(observed.runtime.Name()) == "" {
176					observed.runtimeErr = errors.New("destructive inspection has no runtime backend")

196	func (o *destructiveObservation) observeCheckoutFacts(ctx context.Context, s *lifecycleService) {
197		o.status, o.statusErr = s.gitStatus(ctx, o.checkout)
198		o.head, o.headErr = s.gitRun(ctx, o.checkout, "rev-parse", "--verify", "HEAD^{commit}")
199		o.head = strings.TrimSpace(o.head)
200		o.operation, o.inProgress, o.operationErr = s.gitInProgress(ctx, o.checkout)
201	}

203	func (o *destructiveObservation) observeRefs(ctx context.Context, s *lifecycleService, branch, base string) {
204		o.branchRef = localBranchRef(branch)
205		if o.repoPath != "" && o.branchRef != "" {
206			o.branchExists, o.branchOIDErr = s.gitRefState(ctx, o.repoPath, o.branchRef)
207			if o.branchExists && o.branchOIDErr == nil {
208				o.branchOID, o.branchOIDErr = s.resolveRefOID(ctx, o.repoPath, o.branchRef)
209			}
210		}
211		resolved := s.resolveBaseRef(ctx, o.repoPath, base)
212		o.baseInput, o.baseKind, o.baseRef = resolved.input, resolved.kind, resolved.ref
213		o.baseExists, o.baseOID, o.baseOIDErr = resolved.exists, resolved.oid, resolved.err
214		if o.branchExists && o.branchOIDErr == nil && o.branchOID != "" &&
215			o.baseExists && o.baseOIDErr == nil && o.baseOID != "" {
216			o.contained, o.containedErr = s.isAncestor(ctx, o.repoPath, o.branchOID, o.baseOID)
217		}
218	}

220	func localBranchRef(branch string) string {
221		if branch == "" {
222			return ""
223		}
224		return "refs/heads/" + branch
225	}

227	func (s *lifecycleService) inspectDestructiveTaskClaims(ctx context.Context, observed *destructiveObservation) {
228		for _, diagnostic := range observed.taskDiagnostics {
229			observed.taskIncomplete = append(observed.taskIncomplete, diagnostic.Error())
230		}
231		for _, record := range observed.taskRecords {
232			candidate := record.Task
233			if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
234				observed.taskIncomplete = append(observed.taskIncomplete,
235					fmt.Sprintf("task %s is invalid: %v", candidate.ID, err))
236				continue
237			}
238	
239			pathClaim := false
240			if candidate.WorktreePath != "" {
241				path, err := s.canonicalPath(candidate.WorktreePath)
242				if err != nil {
243					observed.taskIncomplete = append(observed.taskIncomplete,
244						fmt.Sprintf("task %s checkout identity is unavailable: %v", candidate.ID, err))
245				} else {
246					pathClaim = path == observed.checkout
247				}
248			}
249	
250			branchClaim := false
251			if candidate.Branch == observed.locator.Branch {
252				repoMatches, complete, detail := s.taskRepositoryMatches(ctx, candidate, *observed)
253				if !complete {
254					observed.taskIncomplete = append(observed.taskIncomplete,
255						fmt.Sprintf("task %s repository identity is unavailable: %s", candidate.ID, detail))
256				} else {
257					branchClaim = repoMatches
258				}
259			}
260	
261			if pathClaim {
262				observed.taskClaims = append(observed.taskClaims, destructiveTaskClaim{
263					ID: candidate.ID, Revision: record.Revision, Reason: "exact checkout path",
264				})
265			}
266			if branchClaim {
267				reason := "exact branch in selected repository"
268				if pathClaim {
269					reason = "exact checkout path and branch in selected repository"
270					observed.taskClaims[len(observed.taskClaims)-1].Reason = reason
271					continue
272				}
273				observed.taskClaims = append(observed.taskClaims, destructiveTaskClaim{
274					ID: candidate.ID, Revision: record.Revision, Reason: reason,
275				})
276			}
277		}
278		sort.Slice(observed.taskClaims, func(i, j int) bool {
279			if observed.taskClaims[i].ID != observed.taskClaims[j].ID {
280				return observed.taskClaims[i].ID < observed.taskClaims[j].ID
281			}
282			return observed.taskClaims[i].Reason < observed.taskClaims[j].Reason
283		})
284		sort.Strings(observed.taskIncomplete)
285	}

287	func (s *lifecycleService) taskRepositoryMatches(ctx context.Context, candidate task.Task, observed destructiveObservation) (bool, bool, string) {
288		candidatePath, err := s.canonicalPath(candidate.RepoPath)
289		if err != nil {
290			return false, false, err.Error()
291		}
292		if candidatePath == observed.repoPath {
293			return true, true, ""
294		}
295		repository, err := s.gitDiscover(ctx, candidate.RepoPath)
296		if err != nil {
297			return false, false, err.Error()
298		}
299		commonDir, err := s.canonicalPath(repository.GitCommonDir)
300		if err != nil {
301			return false, false, err.Error()
302		}
303		return commonDir == observed.gitCommonDir, true, ""
304	}

306	func (o destructiveObservation) branchCheckoutPaths(excludeTarget bool) ([]string, error) {
307		if o.worktreesErr != nil {
308			return nil, o.worktreesErr
309		}
310		var paths []string
311		for _, worktree := range o.worktrees {
312			if worktree.Bare || worktree.Branch != o.locator.Branch {
313				continue
314			}
315			path := worktree.Path
316			if canonical, err := filepath.Abs(path); err == nil {
317				path = filepath.Clean(canonical)
318			}
319			if excludeTarget && o.checkout != "" {
320				candidate, err := filepath.Abs(o.checkout)
321				if err == nil && filepath.Clean(candidate) == path {
322					continue
323				}
324			}
325			paths = append(paths, path)
326		}
327		sort.Strings(paths)
328		return paths, nil
329	}

352			"destructive.worktree-list-error":     errorString(o.worktreesErr),

404	// scopeDestructiveWorktrees keeps registered worktrees on the target branch or
405	// whose path equals, contains or is nested in the selected checkout. Removing
406	// an unrelated sibling between plan and apply cannot change this target, so it
407	// must not invalidate a reviewed plan (for example during a sweep batch).
408	func (s *lifecycleService) scopeDestructiveWorktrees(worktrees []gitx.Worktree, branch, checkout string) []gitx.Worktree {
409		var scoped []gitx.Worktree
410		for _, worktree := range worktrees {
411			related := branch != "" && worktree.Branch == branch
412			if !related && checkout != "" {
413				path, err := s.canonicalPath(worktree.Path)
414				if err != nil {
415					path = lexicalAbsolute(worktree.Path)
416				}
417				related = pathEqualOrBelow(checkout, path) || pathEqualOrBelow(path, checkout)
418			}
419			if related {
420				scoped = append(scoped, worktree)
421			}
422		}
423		sort.SliceStable(scoped, func(i, j int) bool { return scoped[i].Path < scoped[j].Path })
424		return scoped
425	}
426	
427	func lexicalAbsolute(path string) string {
428		if absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path); err == nil {
429			return filepath.Clean(absolute)
430		}
431		return filepath.Clean(path)
432	}
433	
434	func pathEqualOrBelow(root, path string) bool {
435		if root == "" || path == "" {
436			return false
437		}
438		rel, err := filepath.Rel(root, path)
439		return err == nil && !filepath.IsAbs(rel) && rel != ".." && !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator))
440	}
441	
442	func (o destructiveObservation) worktreeListAuthority() string {
443		values := []string{errorString(o.worktreesErr), strconv.Itoa(len(o.scopedWorktrees))}
444		for _, worktree := range o.scopedWorktrees {
445			values = append(values,
446				worktree.Path, worktree.Head, worktree.Branch,
447				boolString(worktree.Detached), boolString(worktree.Bare), boolString(worktree.Main),
448				boolString(worktree.Locked), worktree.LockedReason,
449				boolString(worktree.Prunable), worktree.PrunableReason,
450			)
451		}
452		return authorityHash("taskflow-destructive-worktrees-v2", values...)
453	}
454	
455	func artifactEvidenceFromInspection(inspection artifact.ReadinessInspection) string {
456		if h := inspection.History; h != nil && !h.Ready {
457			return fmt.Sprintf("%d configured history files need a verified archive", len(h.Pending))
458		}
459		if inspection.KnownEmpty {
460			return "no artifact intents match the exact checkout"
461		}
462		states := make([]string, 0, len(inspection.Intents))
463		for _, intent := range inspection.Intents {
464			states = append(states, intent.Intent.ID+"="+string(intent.State))
465		}
466		if len(states) == 0 {
467			return "artifact readiness is incomplete"
468		}
469		return strings.Join(states, ", ")
470	}
471	
472	func mergeAuthority(base, additional map[string]string) map[string]string {
473		out := make(map[string]string, len(base)+len(additional))
474		for key, value := range base {
475			out[key] = value
476		}
477		for key, value := range additional {
478			out[key] = value
479		}
480		return out
481	}
482	
483	func destructiveConditionsReady(conditions []Condition) error {
484		if availability := AvailabilityFor(conditions); availability != AvailabilityReady {
485			var evidence []string
486			for _, current := range conditions {
487				if current.Requirement == RequirementRequired && current.Verdict != VerdictMet {
488					evidence = append(evidence, string(current.Code)+": "+current.Evidence)
489				}
490			}
491			return staleBoundary("destructive safety is no longer ready (" + strings.Join(evidence, "; ") + ")")
492		}
493		return nil
494	}
495	
496	func compareAuthorityCategory(name, before, after string) error {
497		if before != after {
498			return staleBoundary(name + " authority changed")
499		}
500		return nil
501	}

24	// harness runs dev commands against an isolated HOME, config and scan root.
25	type harness struct {
26		t          *testing.T
27		home       string
28		configPath string
29		scanRoot   string
30		wtRoot     string
31		repo       *gittest.Repo
32	}
33	
34	func newHarness(t *testing.T) *harness {
35		t.Helper()
36		home := externalCLITestHome(t)
37		scanRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Program")
38		wtRoot := filepath.Join(home, "Worktrees")
39		if err := os.MkdirAll(scanRoot, 0o755); err != nil {
40			t.Fatal(err)
41		}
42	
43		// A repo inside the scan root, so `dev` discovers it the way it would in
44		// real use rather than via an absolute path.
45		r := gittest.New(t)
46		dest := filepath.Join(scanRoot, "demo")
47		if err := os.Rename(r.Root, dest); err != nil {
48			t.Fatal(err)
49		}
50		r.Root = dest
51	
52		// Isolate every path dev touches from the developer's real machine.
53		t.Setenv("HOME", home)
54		t.Setenv("USERPROFILE", home)
55		t.Setenv("XDG_DATA_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".local", "share"))
56		t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".config"))
57		t.Setenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME", filepath.Join(home, ".cache"))
58		gitConfig := "[user]\n\temail = dev@example.test\n\tname = dev test\n[init]\n\tdefaultBranch = main\n"
59		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(home, ".gitconfig"), []byte(gitConfig), 0o644); err != nil {
60			t.Fatal(err)
61		}
62	
63		configPath := filepath.Join(home, "config.toml")
64		// TOML basic strings treat backslash as an escape, so a Windows path like
65		// C:\Users\... is invalid there. Forward slashes are valid TOML and Go
66		// normalizes them back to the OS separator on use.
67		slash := filepath.ToSlash
68		cfg := "" +
69			"[paths]\n" +
70			"scan_roots = [\"" + slash(scanRoot) + "\"]\n" +
71			"project_root = \"" + slash(scanRoot) + "\"\n" +
72			"tries_root = \"" + slash(filepath.Join(home, "tries")) + "\"\n" +
73			"worktree_root = \"" + slash(wtRoot) + "\"\n" +
74			"state_dir = \"" + slash(filepath.Join(home, "state")) + "\"\n" +
75			"\n[runtime]\nbackend = \"none\"\n" +
76			"\n[worktree]\ninclude = [\".env\"]\npost_create = []\n"
77		if err := os.WriteFile(configPath, []byte(cfg), 0o644); err != nil {
78			t.Fatal(err)
79		}
80		return &harness{t: t, home: home, configPath: configPath, scanRoot: scanRoot, wtRoot: wtRoot, repo: r}
81	}

83	// run executes one dev invocation, capturing its output. Commands write
84	// through App, so the writers passed to NewRootCommandWithIO are all that is
85	// needed — no file-descriptor juggling.
86	func (h *harness) run(args ...string) (string, string, error) {
87		h.t.Helper()

193		var ws struct {

183		targets := make([]hygiene.WriterTarget, 0, len(paths))

210	// specStoryTranscriptPath limits preamble ownership proof to SpecStory history
211	// Markdown; plans and other artifacts never prove a different session.
212	func specStoryTranscriptPath(rel string) bool {
213		parts := strings.Split(rel, "/")
214		if len(parts) < 3 || !strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(parts[len(parts)-1]), ".md") {
215			return false
216		}
217		return strings.EqualFold(parts[len(parts)-3], ".specstory") && strings.EqualFold(parts[len(parts)-2], "history")
218	}
