225	func inspectReadinessCheckoutIdentity(ctx context.Context, checkout string) (readinessCheckoutIdentity, bool, error) {
226		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, checkout)
227		if errors.Is(err, gitx.ErrNotARepo) {
228			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, nil
229		}
230		if err != nil {
231			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, fmt.Errorf("discover artifact readiness checkout identity: %w", err)
232		}
233		commonDir, err := pathx.Canonical(repository.GitCommonDir)
234		if err != nil {
235			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact readiness Git common directory: %w", err)
236		}
237		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
238		if err != nil {
239			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, fmt.Errorf("observe artifact readiness checkout branch: %w", err)
240		}
241		if status.Detached || status.Branch == "" {
242			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, errors.New("artifact readiness checkout is detached; moved intent identity is ambiguous")
243		}
244		return readinessCheckoutIdentity{commonDir: commonDir, branch: status.Branch}, true, nil
245	}

247	func inspectIntentReadiness(ctx context.Context, checkout string, intent Intent) (IntentReadiness, error) {
248		evidence := IntentReadiness{Intent: intent, Finalized: intent.Status == Finalized}
249		var err error
250		switch intent.Status {
251		case Armed, Finalizing:
252			evidence.State = ReadinessPending
253		case Failed:
254			evidence.State = ReadinessFailed
255		case Discarded:
256			evidence.State = ReadinessDiscarded
257		case Finalized:
258			evidence.ReceiptReachable, err = receiptRemainsReachable(ctx, checkout, intent)
259			switch {
260			case err != nil:
261				err = fmt.Errorf("inspect artifact intent %s receipt: %w", intent.ID, err)
262				evidence.State = ReadinessObservationError
263				evidence.ObservationError = err
264			case evidence.ReceiptReachable:
265				evidence.State = ReadinessFinalizedReachable
266			default:
267				evidence.State = ReadinessFinalizedUnreachable
268			}
269		default:
270			// Store.List validates statuses, but fail closed if another Store
271			// implementation is introduced without preserving that contract.
272			err = fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s has unrecognized status %q", intent.ID, intent.Status)
273			evidence.State = ReadinessObservationError
274			evidence.ObservationError = err
275		}
276		return evidence, err
277	}

```text
133	Cold requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work, but not integration.
134	Retire additionally proves selected children are integrated into their recorded
135	base. Workspace-member intent is versioned separately from task TOML and is
136	used to reconstruct selected branches at the gitlinks when resuming.
137	
138	`--recursive` authorizes disposal of the workspace's independent child clones,
139	including private refs and objects. The outer branch stays unless separately
140	requested; canonical and shared repositories are never disposed. Omitting the
141	flag blocks parent removal when child repositories remain. `--force` cannot
142	bypass child recovery checks. `dev flow` offers explicit recursive managed and
143	unmanaged checkout actions; the done cleanup wizard asks about child disposal.
144	
145	Before mutation, each child is compared with fresh refs from its declared
146	recovery origin using an isolated fetch. A configured origin or ahead=0 alone
147	is not proof. Unpublished refs, local-only reflog/unreachable objects, stash,
148	dirty/untracked/ignored content, unfinished artifacts, other task claims,
149	runtime activity, and additional child worktrees block cleanup. Filtered/LFS
150	data, sparse/partial layouts and private Git configuration or files without a
151	complete preservation proof also block. Initialize missing children before
152	requesting a complete recursive recovery proof.
153	
154	The child origin must match its declared source. Remote failure or changing refs
155	halts cleanup. Raw Git/external writers and later remote history deletion remain
156	outside dev's cooperative locking and run-local proof guarantees.
157	
158	## Interrupted cleanup
159	
160	Children are staged from deepest to shallowest into a private temporary area on
161	the same filesystem. Empty gitlink directories remain until ordinary non-force
162	outer removal succeeds. The workflow does not use `submodule deinit` to rewrite
163	shared superproject settings.
164	
165	Each move has a synced journal. A failed outer removal restores original child
166	paths when they remain unclaimed. An interruption or reused path retains the
167	quarantine and reports its exact `journal.json`:
168	
169	```bash
170	dev submodule recover /exact/.dev-submodule-retirement-ID/journal.json --dry-run
171	dev submodule recover /exact/.dev-submodule-retirement-ID/journal.json
172	```
173	
174	Recovery restores rather than reusing an old proof to delete data. A removed
175	outer checkout can be reconstructed only when its retained branch still matches
176	the recorded commit. Reused or nonempty restore paths block restoration. Rerun
177	the ordinary recursive cleanup after recovery for a fresh plan and remote proof.
178	
179	Refresh shell integration after upgrading to use recursive post-done handoff.
180	Older wrappers reject the new recursive action instead of guessing its meaning.
```

| Initialized, privately owned | Existing local checks and complete fresh recovery proof |
| Safely empty | Exact child path absent or a genuinely empty regular directory; no retained child store; local checks only |
| Uninitialized with retained data | Block, even if its checkout is empty or missing |
| Unknown/unsafe | Block |

“Empty” must use filesystem enumeration, not Git status. Any checkout entry—including an ignored file, `.git` marker, or empty nested user directory—prevents the empty classification. Symlinks/reparse points, observation errors, unsupported identities, and special files remain blockers.

Retained Git repositories, orphan stores, arbitrary files, and links remain blocked. Directory-only administrative scaffolding may be classified separately for exact empty-directory pruning; do not mistake it for a proven child repository.

# dev-cli

Git owns durable code; worktrees are local checkouts; runtimes are host-local
sessions; dev records task intent.

## Discover what you need

Use `dev <command> --help` for current syntax and flags, and `dev help <topic>`
for workflow explanations. `dev --help` lists commands; `dev help` lists topics.
Prefer supported `--json` output for automation. Read the relevant command before
mutation: some actions execute immediately, while others require preview/apply.
Do not preload manuals, repeat `dev --skill`, or run diagnostics for every task.

## Preserve these boundaries

- Opening a repository needs no task. Choose direct, branch, or worktree
  deliberately; pass an explicit `--base` for branch/worktree creation. Keep
  managed worktrees outside repositories.
- `dev start` normally prepares a checkout/runtime. Agent launch is explicit.
  Parallel writers need coordinated ownership and verified launch targets.
- Completion, artifact finalization, retirement, and branch deletion are separate.
  Finalize agent artifacts after their writer stops; retire an agent checkout
  externally. A runtime's `done` state does not mean cleanup is safe.
- Unknown or cached observations, merged PRs, and command refusals do not grant
  cleanup authority. Resolve the reported conditions; do not improvise force
  removal or bypass trust checks.

## Read a reference for advanced operations

- Worktree provisioning or cross-host lifecycle: [ownership](references/worktree-ownership.md), [lifecycle](references/task-lifecycle.md).
- Parallel agent launches or prompt transports: [agents](references/parallel-agents.md), [handoffs](references/prompt-handoffs.md).
- History retention: [artifacts](references/ai-artifacts.md).
- Agent completion or cleanup batches: [retirement](references/agent-retirement.md), [triage](references/local-triage.md).
- Repository hygiene batches, scans or redaction: [hygiene](references/hygiene.md).
- Repository hooks, publication, or physical organization: [setup](references/repository-bootstrap.md), [bootstrap](references/bootstrap.md).
- SSH dashboard, diagnosis, discovery, tests/activity, keys, credentials and registration: [SSH](references/ssh-hosts.md).
- Dotfile setup, native chezmoi operations, or FLEET host actions: [dotfiles](references/dotfiles.md).
- Skill/MCP/instruction transfers, updates or removal: [transfers](references/agent-interop.md), [maintenance](references/skills-management.md).
- Recursive Git children: [submodules](references/submodules.md).

Use command help and its workflow topic for everyday operations.

## Unexpected dev failures

Read [feedback and repair](references/feedback-and-repair.md). Preserve the
original task; extra investigation, repair, subagents and publication need
explicit consent covering scope and cost.

40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:

51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:

54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `submodule` owns versioned workspace-member intent and reversible child-clone disposal mechanisms. `gitx` supplies the local gitlink graph; `taskflow` owns recursive lifecycle policy and fresh remote-proof ordering. 56	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints. Lifecycle callers use exact-record revisions and locked compare-and-update/delete transactions rather than treating a previously read task as current.
57	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. 58	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
59	- `taskflow` is the UI-agnostic lifecycle authority: it separates recorded intent, typed live observations, immutable guarded plans, approvals, and partial result ledgers. Apply locks and reloads task/Git/worktree/runtime/artifact/remote identity, then rejects stale authority before mutation.
60	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, all registered worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and UI projections consume this joined view.
61	- `agentinterop` owns explicit MCP/skill/instruction transfer plans, guarded apply, stanza/link ownership, private recovery, and optional recipes. 62	- `triage` owns read-only cross-repository findings, clone-bound local intent, ignored-directory policy and reviewed batch ledgers; `triagetui` is its independent UI. 101	## Behavioral contracts
102	
103	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
104	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
105	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
106	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
107	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
108	- Submodule initialization uses committed gitlinks, never implicitly advances to `main`. Whole child-clone disposal requires explicit recursive approval and fresh recovery proof for its private refs/objects; outer and shared canonical repositories are retained. Local graph refresh never performs remote proof. Child task/runtime/artifact claims block parent disposal.
109	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
110	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
111	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
112	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
113	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
114	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
115	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
116	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output, including `dev hygiene report --json` (`hygiene_summary` schema 1). Stored summaries are historical observations, not proof of current source bytes.
117	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
118	- Explicit SSH format/organize and fleet profile rename/remove are plan-first exceptions for user-selected files; retain comments, Include order, original metadata and private recovery. Never activate dormant files with a new broad Include. Herdr machine add may prepare/start a remote server; leave native approvals native, and remove/disable never stops remote sessions.
119	- SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. Full bootstrap requires an explicit existing key or explicit generation, registers fleet only when explicitly selected, and reports interrupted remote installation as unknown rather than pretending to roll it back.
120	- SSH wizard permission preflight may separately review and apply metadata-only tightening on exact current-user-owned canonical/selected paths. It never recursively chmods, changes ownership, guesses ACLs, or widens permissions; completed repairs survive later cancellation. Listing and dry-run never repair permissions. Local key listing evaluates OpenSSH only behind explicit `--alias`; selected key material remains service-bound and is revalidated before configuration changes and bootstrap.
121	- `dev ssh key doctor` exposes the same permission Plan/Apply with bounded metadata-only key discovery; `--key` restricts the reviewed scope, and `--fix` requires a complete safe plan plus confirmation. Default doctor never mutates, reads private contents, or queries agents/remotes. Batch repairs revalidate the whole reviewed union and retain successful tightening on partial failure.
122	- Source-aware SSH setup can use `--auth existing` without installing a key, and registers only explicitly selected `--to fleet|herdr|both` destinations. Tailscale SSH advertisement is advisory; its port-22 endpoint is not an authorized_keys bootstrap target. Preserve the key-authentication guard and never treat Tailscale policy login as proof that a selected public key worked. Names, ports and cached observations never authorize machine merges; binding/source changes invalidate reviewed plans.
123	- Fleet-source SSH discovery selects explicit hosts without recursive fleet traversal. Local ProxyJump imports never copy remote identity/agent/trust paths; cached route data cannot authorize apply. `connect --on` is one interactive fixed-helper session with no agent forwarding or arbitrary command payload. Normal SSH errors retain child exit status.
124	- Controller password brokerage uses a private per-operation Unix socket or protected Windows pipe, never password argv/environment/files. Exact host/user/port/route contexts gate replies and save evidence. Remote source-to-target credentials remain outside this feature; native key/passphrase interaction is separate.
125	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
126	
127	## Versioning and changelog
128	
129	The current published baseline is `v0.2.38` (2026-09-15). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
130	
131	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
132	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
133	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
134	
135	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
136	
137	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
138	
139	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
140	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
141	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
142	
143	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
144	
145	For a release:
146	
147	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
148	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
149	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
150	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
151	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
152	
153	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
154	
155	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
156	
157	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
158	
159	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.

167	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |

Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
173	
174	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
175	
176	## Hygiene and skill batch operations

178	`internal/hygiene` owns per-repository setup plans and batch ledgers. REPOS and
179	`hygiene manage` are adapters; JSON batch management previews only. Keep legacy
180	artifact finalizers until their independent lifecycle is replaced. Cached machine

1	# Submodule workspaces
2	
3	## Add a known repository
4	
5	```bash
6	dev submodule add owner/library libs/library --dry-run --json
7	dev submodule add owner/library libs/library --checkout=pinned --ref=v1.2.0 --yes --json
8	dev repo add-as-submodule owner/library libs/library --checkout=default-branch --yes
9	```
10	
11	Use the dry-run to verify the exact parent checkout, portable network source,
12	relative path and mode. Only apply the approved request. `--parent PATH` selects
13	an exact checkout; the default is the nearest repo containing cwd, not its
14	canonical or outermost checkout. Source selection combines known local remotes
15	and cached forge repositories without refreshing. Ambiguous names need an exact
16	URL or interactive selection. Local-only sources and existing targets/stores are
17	not adopted. REPOS/REMOTE `y u` copies the selected network clone URL locally.
18	
19	The wizard offers pinned/default-branch. Non-interactive default is pinned;
20	`--ref` is pinned-only, and a missing ref resolves the fresh clone's default
21	branch commit. Default-branch mode tracks the real default, not an assumed main.
22	Both stage a fixed gitlink; neither enables remote-following updates or creates
23	task-member intent. `--submodules=recursive|none` controls only new descendants.
24	Only `.gitmodules` and the new gitlink are staged; unrelated staged/dirty work
25	and other checkouts are preserved. No commit, push, task branch or runtime is
26	created. Use `develop` separately for managed task membership.
27	
28	**Gotchas:** `.gitmodules` must be absent or unchanged, including hidden index
29	edits; filters/encodings, conflicts, active Git operations, detached/unborn
30	parents and unsafe paths block addition. `--yes` is required for non-interactive
31	mutation; `--json` never prompts. A local `planned` result has no resolved HEAD.
32	An error may still return a partial result (`phase`, `git_dir`, `head`, `staged`,
33	`warnings`). Inspect retained paths and finish metadata/staging manually; for
34	`initialization-incomplete`, run `dev submodule init` inside the new child.
35	Never force-delete partial clones or replay add over them. The retirement
36	`recover` journal format does not apply to addition.
37	
38	## Initialize and develop existing gitlinks
39	
40	`dev repo clone`, clone-style `repo new`, and new linked worktrees initialize
41	recursively at committed gitlinks by default. Use `--submodules=none` to opt out;
42	`--no-provision` only skips environment provisioning. Global and project
43	`[submodules] init = "recursive"|"none"` control the default.
44	
45	Detached HEAD at a gitlink is intentional. Select development members with
46	repeatable `dev start --submodule PATH`; they get the task branch at the same
47	commit. `--submodule-base PATH=REF` records their integration target. Project
48	`submodules.develop` supplies optional default paths. Direct/branch-only modes
49	do not switch child branches. Later use `dev submodule develop PATH...` from
50	the managed worktree. Never infer permission to reset an existing child branch.
51	
52	`dev submodule init` fills missing checkouts, preserves existing ones and refuses
53	nonempty uninitialized directories. Initialization failure is not ready: retain
54	partial results, retry init, and do not launch an agent. `status --json` reports
55	the local graph without remote access; parent state never substitutes for child
56	state. Workspace-member intent is versioned separately from task TOML.
57	
58	Commit/integrate/push affected children before updating and publishing the
59	outer gitlinks. For dotfiles-all, both affected platform gitlinks belong in one
60	outer commit. Dev verifies ordering; it does not perform recursive commits,
61	pushes or merges. Outer `--push` never implies a child push.
62	
63	`park --cold --recursive`, `retire --recursive`, `wt rm --recursive` and

70

1	# Feedback and repair during another task
2	
3	Read this when dev panics, an internal error looks reproducible, or behavior and
4	help disagree. Ordinary usage errors, missing login and a safety refusal are not
5	by themselves dev bugs. For SSH failures first consult `dev help ssh`; diagnosis
6	is explicit network activity, not a passive inventory step.
7	
8	## Preserve the original task and the user's token budget
9	
10	1. Keep the failed command name, installed version, expected/actual behavior and
11	   smallest useful reproduction. Do not repeatedly rerun a failing operation or
12	   sweep environment, config, logs or conversation history.
13	2. Prepare a small local draft and an available source candidate, then offer
14	   report, repair, both or skipping the detour. Continue the original task through
15	   a safe alternative when possible; record its next action before a detour.
16	3. Deep investigation, dev-cli repair and an extra subagent need explicit consent
17	   covering their scope and added context/token cost. Do not launch a subagent
18	   merely because the provider supports one. If approved, use independent context
19	   and a separate repair checkout, with a bounded assignment and a short result.
20	   Existing scoped consent persists; do not ask repeatedly for an approved action.
21	4. Local repair consent does not grant issue/comment publication, fork/push/PR,
22	   binary replacement, merge or cleanup permission. Prepare concrete content and
23	   target identities before requesting any still-missing publication consent.
24	
25	Use this compact proposal:
26	
27	```text
28	Problem: observed behavior and minimal evidence
29	Original task: safe continuation or current blocker
30	Report: reviewed public draft location, exact target and operation
31	Repair: verified source, explicit base, planned isolated checkout
32	Extra work: proposed investigation/agent scope and cost, only if needed
33	```
34	
35	## Local draft and reviewed GitHub operation
36	
37	Check `dev feedback --help` for the installed binary's capability. An older or
38	broken binary must not block recovery: retain a manually prepared sanitized
39	Markdown draft and use explicitly authorized native gh steps if necessary.
40	
41	```bash
42	dev feedback draft --title 'Short symptom' --body-file report.md --json
43	dev feedback issue <id> --json
44	# Only when related-issue network lookup is authorized:
45	dev feedback issue <id> --search --json
46	# Only after reviewing and authorizing this exact target/operation/revision:
47	dev feedback issue <id> --publish --yes --revision <revision> --json
48	```
49	
50	The body should contain reproduction, expected/actual results and already-known
51	bounded evidence. `--diagnostic <file>` accepts local schema-v1 `ssh diagnose`
52	JSON and constructs a finite-code public attachment. Never attach raw doctor
53	stdout, SSH debug logs, complete config, key fingerprints, tokens or transcripts.
54	Redaction helps with known forms; inspect arbitrary names in free text manually.
55	Private `context.json` and rendered prompts are never publication bodies.
56	
57	The default issue destination is `github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli`, independent
58	of cwd and GH_HOST. `--repo [host/]owner/name` changes it explicitly. Related
59	issues are candidates, not automatic comment targets. Use `--existing <number>`
60	to preview an exact comment, then approve that preview's revision. `--yes` is a
61	CLI expression of existing consent, not permission for the agent to invent it.
62	
63	Missing gh, login, permission or network preserves the draft. An unknown POST
64	outcome must be reconciled by the exact marker before another attempt; do not
65	work around it by repeatedly creating new reports. Confirmed URLs and private
66	receipts are the recovery record. A report is durable state outside Git/cache.
67	
68	## Verified local repair
69	
70	```bash
71	dev feedback repair <id> --base main --json
72	dev feedback repair <id> --repo <source> --base <explicit-ref> --json
73	# After this exact plan is approved:
74	dev feedback repair <id> --apply --plan <plan-id> --yes --json
75	dev prompt render feedback-fix <id>
76	```
77	
78	Source precedence is explicit path, configured `[feedback].source_repo`, then
79	REPOS discovery. A bad explicit/configured path is an error; multiple matches
80	need selection. An exact upstream remote is required, including for a fork.
81	Do not treat the folder name as identity or the current HEAD as a safe default
82	base. With no source, explicitly acquire a retained Try via the suggested
83	`dev try --clone` workflow, inspect any reused Try, and preview again.
84	
85	The approved plan pins source filesystem identities, base ref/OID, relevant
86	configuration, new branch/task/path and report revision. Apply rechecks under the
87	repository lifecycle lock and calls the shared start service. It keeps source
88	edits in place and prepares a HOT worktree task without runtime, provisioning,
89	submodule acquisition or agent launch. Stale plans do nothing new; partial
90	failures retain the checkout and report the exact recovery location.
91	
92	The current agent can consume the rendered prompt directly. Use `dev prompt open
93	feedback-fix <id> --agent <profile>` only for an explicitly approved additional
94	agent with that profile. It does not choose a default profile for this recipe.
95	A changed/locked/partial checkout or changed task binding blocks handoff.
96	
97	Read the source AGENTS.md, reproduce, implement a focused fix, run meaningful
98	checks and synchronize the source's changelog/docs/help/skill. Deliver the diff,
99	test results, retained task/worktree/report and the original task's next action.
100	Load the private input only when needed; avoid spending context on whole logs.
101

103	
104	When separately authorized, use normal Git and gh to push the selected branch,

140	// Old gitlinks may leave independent repositories in modules/ after their
141	// paths disappear from the index. Every store being disposed must be in the
142	// observed graph; a clean current gitlink is not authority for orphan stores.
143	func inspectModuleStorage(root string, nodes []gitx.SubmoduleNode, originalRoot string) error {
144		known := map[string]bool{}
145		for _, n := range nodes {
146			rel, err := filepath.Rel(originalRoot, n.GitDir)
147			if err != nil {
148				return err
149			}
150			known[filepath.Join(root, rel)] = true
151		}
152		var walk func(string) error
153		walk = func(dir string) error {
154			entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
155			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
156				return nil
157			}
158			if err != nil {
159				return err
160			}
161			for _, entry := range entries {
162				path := filepath.Join(dir, entry.Name())
163				if !entry.IsDir() || entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
164					return fmt.Errorf("unclaimed private module data at %s", path)
165				}
166				if known[path] {
167					if err := walk(filepath.Join(path, "modules")); err != nil {
168						return err
169					}
170					continue
171				}
172				if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, "HEAD")); err == nil {
173					return fmt.Errorf("orphan submodule repository %s requires preservation", path)
174				}
175				if err := walk(path); err != nil {
176					return err
177				}
178			}
179			return nil
180		}
181		return walk(root)
182	}

184	func inspectPrivateState(ctx context.Context, root, gitdir string) error {
185		index, err := gitx.Run(ctx, root, "ls-files", "--stage", "-z")
186		if err != nil {
187			return err
188		}
189		gitlinks := map[string]bool{}
190		for _, record := range strings.Split(index, "\x00") {
191			meta, path, ok := strings.Cut(record, "\t")
192			if ok && strings.HasPrefix(meta, "160000 ") {
193				gitlinks[filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(path))] = true
194			}
195		}
196		visited := 0
197		if err := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
198			if err != nil {
199				return err
200			}
201			visited++
202			if visited > 500000 {
203				return errors.New("worktree inspection limit exceeded")
204			}
205			if path == root {
206				return nil
207			}
208			if gitlinks[path] && d.IsDir() {
209				return filepath.SkipDir
210			}
211			if strings.EqualFold(d.Name(), ".git") {
212				if filepath.Dir(path) != root {
213					return fmt.Errorf("nested repository %s requires independent preservation", filepath.Dir(path))
214				}
215				if d.IsDir() {
216					return filepath.SkipDir
217				}
218			}
219			return nil
220		}); err != nil {
221			return err
222		}
223		allowed := map[string]bool{"HEAD": true, "index": true, "config": true, "description": true, "objects": true, "refs": true, "logs": true, "hooks": true, "info": true, "packed-refs": true, "FETCH_HEAD": true, "ORIG_HEAD": true, "modules": true, "dev-taskflow": true, ".dev-taskflow.lock": true}
224		allowed["lfs"] = true
225		allowed["COMMIT_EDITMSG"] = true
226		if message, err := safefile.ReadRegular(ctx, filepath.Join(gitdir, "COMMIT_EDITMSG"), 1024*1024); err == nil {
227			committed, err := gitx.Run(ctx, root, "log", "-1", "--format=%B")
228			if err != nil {
229				return err
230			}
231			if strings.TrimSpace(string(message)) != strings.TrimSpace(committed) {
232				return errors.New("uncommitted commit-message draft requires preservation")
233			}
234		} else if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
235			return err
236		}
237		if description, err := safefile.ReadRegular(ctx, filepath.Join(gitdir, "description"), 1024*1024); err == nil {
238			if strings.TrimSpace(string(description)) != "Unnamed repository; edit this file 'description' to name the repository." {
239				return errors.New("private repository description requires preservation")
240			}
241		} else if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
242			return err
243		}
244		if err := filepath.WalkDir(filepath.Join(gitdir, "lfs"), func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
245			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
246				return nil
247			}

118	func (s *lifecycleService) submoduleClaims(ctx context.Context, g gitx.SubmoduleGraph, parentTask string) (string, error) {
119		records, diagnostics, err := s.tasks.ListRecords()
120		if err != nil || len(diagnostics) > 0 {
121			return "unknown", fmt.Errorf("child task inventory is incomplete")
122		}
123		var evidence []string
124		var blockers []string
125		for _, n := range g.Nodes {
126			child := filepath.Join(g.Root, filepath.FromSlash(n.Path))
127			for _, record := range records {
128				if record.Task.ID == parentTask {
129					continue
130				}
131				for _, path := range []string{record.Task.RepoPath, record.Task.WorktreePath} {
132					if path == "" {
133						continue
134					}
135					inside, err := pathx.Contains(child, path)
136					if err != nil {
137						return "unknown", err
138					}
139					if inside {
140						evidence = append(evidence, record.Task.ID+":"+record.Revision)
141						blockers = append(blockers, fmt.Sprintf("%s is claimed by task %s", n.Path, record.Task.ID))
142						break
143					}
144				}
145			}
146			inspection, err := s.inspectArtifacts(ctx, s.artifacts, child)
147			evidence = append(evidence, n.Path+":"+artifactAuthority(inspection, err))
148			if err != nil || !inspection.Ready() {
149				blockers = append(blockers, n.Path+" has unknown or unfinished artifacts")
150			}
151		}
152		hash := authorityHash("submodule-claims", evidence...)
153		if len(blockers) > 0 {
154			return hash, fmt.Errorf("%s", strings.Join(blockers, "; "))
155		}
156		return hash, nil
157	}

237		switch o := e.plan.Request.Options.(type) {
238		case RetireOptions:
239			options.CloseUnknown = o.CloseUnknown
240			options.AssumeNoRuntime = o.AssumeNoRuntime
241		case ParkColdOptions:
242			options.CloseUnknown = o.CloseUnknown
243			options.AssumeNoRuntime = o.AssumeNoRuntime
244		case RemoveCheckoutOptions:
245			options.CloseUnknown = o.CloseUnknown
246			options.AssumeNoRuntime = o.AssumeNoRuntime
247		}
248		paths := []string{p.Graph.Root}
249		for _, n := range p.Graph.Nodes {
250			paths = append(paths, filepath.Join(p.Graph.Root, filepath.FromSlash(n.Path)))
251		}
252		for _, path := range paths {
253			live, err := e.service.inspectCleanup(ctx, rt, path, options)
254			if err != nil {

256			}
257			if !live.Ready() || len(live.Sessions) > 0 {
258				return fmt.Errorf("submodule workspace %s has live or unknown runtime coverage", path)
259			}
260		}
261		return nil
262	}

122	// InspectReadiness gathers artifact finalization evidence for one checkout,
123	// including intents whose exact checkout moved but stable Git identity matches.
124	// It never reconciles receipts, finalizes intents, or writes either
125	// source files or intent records. The returned inspection retains partial
126	// evidence and the same wrapped error returned separately to ordinary callers.
127	func InspectReadiness(ctx context.Context, store *Store, checkout string) (ReadinessInspection, error) {
128		inspection := ReadinessInspection{}
129		if ctx == nil {
130			err := errors.New("artifact readiness inspection needs a context")
131			inspection.ObservationError = err
132			return inspection, err
133		}
134		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
135			inspection.ObservationError = err
136			return inspection, err
137		}
138		if store == nil {
139			err := errors.New("artifact readiness inspection needs a store")
140			inspection.ObservationError = err
141			return inspection, err
142		}
143	
144		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(checkout)
145		if err != nil {
146			err = fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact readiness checkout: %w", err)
147			inspection.ObservationError = err
148			return inspection, err
149		}
150		inspection.Checkout = canonical
151	
152		intents, err := store.List()
153		if err != nil {
154			err = fmt.Errorf("list artifact intents: %w", err)
155			inspection.ObservationError = err
156			return inspection, err
157		}
158		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
159			inspection.ObservationError = err
160			return inspection, err
161		}
162	
163		matched := make([]Intent, 0, len(intents))
164		unmatched := make([]Intent, 0, len(intents))
165		for _, intent := range intents {
166			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
167				inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, err)
168				break
169			}
170			intentCheckout, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(intent.WorktreePath)
171			if canonicalErr != nil {
172				canonicalErr = fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact intent %s checkout: %w", intent.ID, canonicalErr)
173				inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, canonicalErr)
174				continue
175			}
176			if intentCheckout == canonical {
177				matched = append(matched, intent)
178			} else {
179				unmatched = append(unmatched, intent)
180			}
181		}
182	
183		if len(unmatched) > 0 && inspection.ObservationError == nil {
184			identity, available, identityErr := inspectReadinessCheckoutIdentity(ctx, canonical)
185			if identityErr != nil {
186				inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, identityErr)
187			} else if available {
188				for _, intent := range unmatched {
189					intentCommon, commonErr := pathx.Canonical(intent.GitCommonDir)
190					if commonErr != nil {
191						inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError,
192							fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact intent %s Git common directory: %w", intent.ID, commonErr))
193						continue
194					}
195					if intentCommon == identity.commonDir && intent.Branch == identity.branch {
196						matched = append(matched, intent)

214		}

216		inspection.KnownEmpty = len(inspection.Intents) == 0 && inspection.ObservationError == nil

225	func inspectReadinessCheckoutIdentity(ctx context.Context, checkout string) (readinessCheckoutIdentity, bool, error) {
226		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, checkout)
227		if errors.Is(err, gitx.ErrNotARepo) {
228			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, nil
229		}
230		if err != nil {
231			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, fmt.Errorf("discover artifact readiness checkout identity: %w", err)
232		}
233		commonDir, err := pathx.Canonical(repository.GitCommonDir)
234		if err != nil {
235			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact readiness Git common directory: %w", err)
236		}
237		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
238		if err != nil {
239			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, fmt.Errorf("observe artifact readiness checkout branch: %w", err)
240		}
241		if status.Detached || status.Branch == "" {
242			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, errors.New("artifact readiness checkout is detached; moved intent identity is ambiguous")
243		}
244		return readinessCheckoutIdentity{commonDir: commonDir, branch: status.Branch}, true, nil
245	}
246	
247	func inspectIntentReadiness(ctx context.Context, checkout string, intent Intent) (IntentReadiness, error) {
248		evidence := IntentReadiness{Intent: intent, Finalized: intent.Status == Finalized}
249		var err error
250		switch intent.Status {
251		case Armed, Finalizing:
252			evidence.State = ReadinessPending
253		case Failed:
254			evidence.State = ReadinessFailed
255		case Discarded:
256			evidence.State = ReadinessDiscarded
257		case Finalized:
258			evidence.ReceiptReachable, err = receiptRemainsReachable(ctx, checkout, intent)
259			switch {
260			case err != nil:
261				err = fmt.Errorf("inspect artifact intent %s receipt: %w", intent.ID, err)
262				evidence.State = ReadinessObservationError
263				evidence.ObservationError = err
264			case evidence.ReceiptReachable:
265				evidence.State = ReadinessFinalizedReachable
266			default:
267				evidence.State = ReadinessFinalizedUnreachable
268			}
269		default:
270			// Store.List validates statuses, but fail closed if another Store
271			// implementation is introduced without preserving that contract.
272			err = fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s has unrecognized status %q", intent.ID, intent.Status)
273			evidence.State = ReadinessObservationError
274			evidence.ObservationError = err
275		}
276		return evidence, err
277	}

279	func receiptRemainsReachable(ctx context.Context, checkout string, intent Intent) (bool, error) {
280		if intent.Destination == "archive" {
281			h, e := agenthistory.Open(ctx, agenthistory.Options{Root: checkout, StateDir: intent.ArchiveStateDir})
282			if e != nil {
283				return false, e
284			}
285			commit, e := h.VerifyArchiveReceipt(ctx, intent.ArchivePlanID)
286			return e == nil && commit == intent.ArchiveCommit, e
287		}
288		if intent.ArtifactCommit == "" {
289			return false, nil
290		}
291		candidates := []struct {
292			dir string
293			ref string
294		}{
295			{checkout, "HEAD"},
296			{intent.RepoPath, intent.Branch},
297			{intent.RepoPath, intent.Base},
298		}
299		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(candidates))
300		var observationErr error
301		for _, candidate := range candidates {
302			if candidate.dir == "" || candidate.ref == "" {
303				continue
304			}
305			key := candidate.dir + "\x00" + candidate.ref
306			if seen[key] {
307				continue
308			}
309			seen[key] = true
310			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
311				return false, joinReadinessError(observationErr, err)
312			}
313			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, candidate.dir, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref); err == nil {
314				return true, nil
315			} else if !gitNotAncestor(err) {
316				observationErr = joinReadinessError(observationErr,
317					fmt.Errorf("check %s against %s in %s: %w", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref, candidate.dir, err))
318			}
319		}
320		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
321			observationErr = joinReadinessError(observationErr, err)
322		}
323		return false, observationErr
324	}
325	
326	func gitNotAncestor(err error) bool {
327		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
328		return errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1
329	}
330	
331	func joinReadinessError(current, next error) error {
332		if current == nil {
333			return next
334		}
335		if next == nil {
336			return current
337		}
338		return errors.Join(current, next)
339	}

342		if s.Store == nil {
343			return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact service needs a store")
344		}
345		provider, sessionID, err := ParseSession(request.Session)
346		if err != nil {
347			return nil, err
348		}
349		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, request.Worktree)
350		if err != nil {
351			return nil, err
352		}
353		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, repository.Root)
354		if err != nil {
355			return nil, err
356		}
357		if status.Detached || status.Branch == "" {
358			return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact preparation requires a named branch")
359		}
360		if operation, active, err := gitx.InProgress(repository.Root); err != nil {
361			return nil, err
362		} else if active {
363			return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact preparation refuses Git operation %s in progress", operation)
364		}
365		head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repository.Root, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
366		if err != nil {
367			return nil, err
368		}
369		changes, err := statusPaths(ctx, repository.Root)

100		}
101		return child, held, nil
102	}
103	
104	// VerifyRoot proves that path still names the previously held root directory.
105	func VerifyRoot(path string, expected fs.FileInfo) error {
106		current, err := os.Lstat(path)
107		if err != nil {
108			return err
109		}
110		if expected == nil || unsafeLink(current) || !current.IsDir() || !os.SameFile(expected, current) {
111			return fmt.Errorf("root path changed: %w", ErrChanged)
112		}
113		return nil
114	}
115	
116	// VerifyChildRoot proves that name below parent still names the previously held
117	// child directory.
118	func VerifyChildRoot(parent *os.Root, name string, expected fs.FileInfo) error {
119		if parent == nil {
120			return errors.New("verify child root: nil parent")
121		}
122		if err := pathx.ValidatePortableComponent(name, CompiledMaxComponentBytes); err != nil {
123			return err
124		}
125		current, err := parent.Lstat(name)
126		if err != nil {
127			return err
128		}
129		if expected == nil || unsafeLink(current) || !current.IsDir() || !os.SameFile(expected, current) {
130			return fmt.Errorf("component %q changed: %w", name, ErrChanged)
131		}
132		return nil
133	}
134	
135	// ReadStableRegular reads one child file while proving that the directory name,
136	// opened descriptor, and final directory name all identify the expected regular
137	// file with unchanged observable metadata. maxBytes must be non-negative; zero
138	// means unbounded. Supplying the FileInfo from an earlier directory listing
139	// detects replacement or mutation between selection and opening.
140	func ReadStableRegular(ctx context.Context, root *os.Root, name string, expected fs.FileInfo, maxBytes int64) ([]byte, fs.FileInfo, error) {
141		if root == nil {
142			return nil, nil, errors.New("read stable file: nil root")
143		}
144		if maxBytes < 0 {
145			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("negative maximum file size: %w", ErrFileLimit)
146		}
147		if err := pathx.ValidatePortableComponent(name, CompiledMaxComponentBytes); err != nil {
148			return nil, nil, err
149		}
150		before, err := root.Lstat(name)
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, nil, err
153		}
154		if expected == nil {
155			expected = before
156		}
157		if unsafeLink(before) || !before.Mode().IsRegular() {
158			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source is not a regular file: %w", ErrUnsafeType)
159		}
160		if !sameStableSourceState(expected, before) {
161			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source changed before opening file: %w", ErrChanged)
162		}
163		if maxBytes > 0 && before.Size() > maxBytes {
164			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source is %d bytes; maximum is %d: %w", before.Size(), maxBytes, ErrFileLimit)
165		}
166	
167		file, err := openRegularForRead(root, name)
168		if err != nil {
169			return nil, nil, err
170		}
171		defer file.Close()
172		opened, err := file.Stat()
173		if err != nil {
174			return nil, nil, err
175		}
176		if unsafeLink(opened) || !opened.Mode().IsRegular() || !sameStableSourceState(expected, opened) {
177			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source changed while opening file: %w", ErrChanged)
178		}
179		current, err := root.Lstat(name)
180		if err != nil {
181			return nil, nil, err
182		}
183		if unsafeLink(current) || !sameStableSourceState(opened, current) {
184			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source changed while opening file: %w", ErrChanged)
185		}
186	
187		data, err := readAllContext(ctx, file, maxBytes)
188		if err != nil {
189			return nil, nil, err
190		}
191		after, err := file.Stat()
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, nil, err
194		}
195		current, err = root.Lstat(name)
196		if err != nil {
197			return nil, nil, err
198		}
199		if unsafeLink(after) || unsafeLink(current) || !sameStableSourceState(opened, after) ||
200			!sameStableSourceState(after, current) || after.Size() != int64(len(data)) {
201			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source changed during read: %w", ErrChanged)
202		}
203		return data, opened, nil
204	}
205	
206	// SameFileState compares identity, mode, size, and modification time. Stable
207	// reads and observed-target replacement additionally compare platform change
208	// time where the operating system exposes it.
209	func SameFileState(left, right fs.FileInfo) bool {
210		return left != nil && right != nil && os.SameFile(left, right) &&
211			left.Mode() == right.Mode() && left.Size() == right.Size() && left.ModTime().Equal(right.ModTime())
212	}
213	
214	func sameStableSourceState(left, right fs.FileInfo) bool {
215		return SameFileState(left, right) && samePlatformState(left, right)
216	}
217	
218	func readAllContext(ctx context.Context, reader io.Reader, maxBytes int64) ([]byte, error) {
219		var data []byte
220		buffer := make([]byte, 64*1024)
221		for {
222			if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
223				return nil, err
224			}
225			read, err := reader.Read(buffer)
226			if read > 0 {
227				if maxBytes > 0 && int64(read) > maxBytes-int64(len(data)) {
228					return nil, fmt.Errorf("source exceeds %d bytes: %w", maxBytes, ErrFileLimit)
229				}
230				data = append(data, buffer[:read]...)
231			}
232			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
233				return data, nil
234			}
235			if err != nil {
236				return nil, err
237			}
238			if read == 0 {
239				return nil, io.ErrNoProgress
240			}
241		}
242	}
243	
244	func unsafeLink(info fs.FileInfo) bool {
245		return info != nil && (info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || isReparsePoint(info))
246	}

14	// ReadStablePath walks held directory handles and rejects links in every
15	// user-controlled component, then verifies the chain after reading. Only the
16	// fixed macOS /var and /tmp platform aliases may be resolved.
17	func ReadStablePath(ctx context.Context, path string, limit int64) ([]byte, error) {
18		if !filepath.IsAbs(path) || filepath.Clean(path) != path {
19			return nil, errors.New("stable read requires a clean absolute path")
20		}
21		if runtime.GOOS == "darwin" {
22			for _, alias := range []string{"/var", "/tmp"} {
23				if strings.HasPrefix(path, alias+"/") {
24					target, e := os.Readlink(alias)
25					if e == nil && (target == "private"+alias || target == "/private"+alias) {
26						path = "/private" + path
27					}
28				}
29			}
30		}
31		anchor, err := platformfs.Resolve(path)
32		if err != nil {
33			return nil, err
34		}
35		base := anchor.Path
36		parts := strings.Split(strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimPrefix(path, base), string(filepath.Separator)), string(filepath.Separator))
37		if len(parts) == 0 || len(parts) > 128 {
38			return nil, ErrUnsafeType
39		}
40		root, info, err := OpenRoot(base)
41		if err != nil {
42			return nil, err
43		}
44		defer root.Close()
45		type edge struct {
46			parent *os.Root
47			name   string
48			info   fs.FileInfo
49		}
50		var edges []edge
51		current := root
52		for _, part := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {
53			next, id, e := OpenChildRoot(current, part)
54			if e != nil {
55				return nil, e
56			}
57			defer next.Close()
58			edges = append(edges, edge{current, part, id})
59			current = next
60		}
61		data, _, err := ReadStableRegular(ctx, current, parts[len(parts)-1], nil, limit)
62		if err != nil {
63			return nil, err
64		}
65		for _, e := range edges {
66			if err = VerifyChildRoot(e.parent, e.name, e.info); err != nil {
67				return nil, err
68			}
69		}
70		if err = VerifyRoot(base, info); err != nil {
71			return nil, err
72		}
73		if err := anchor.Verify(); err != nil {
74			return nil, err
75		}
76		return data, nil
77	}

18	// SubmoduleNode describes one exact gitlink edge, relative to Graph.Root.
19	// Unknown is never represented as a clean initialized checkout.
20	type SubmoduleNode struct {
21		CheckoutIdentity string   `json:"checkout_identity,omitempty"`
22		GitIdentity      string   `json:"git_identity,omitempty"`
23		Path             string   `json:"path"`
24		Parent           string   `json:"parent"`

46	// SubmodulesOf never fetches and never descends across an unverified Git root.
47	func SubmodulesOf(ctx context.Context, dir string) (SubmoduleGraph, error) {

86				}
87				n := SubmoduleNode{Path: rel, Parent: parent, Name: entry.Name, URL: entry.URL, Gitlink: entry.Gitlink, State: "uninitialized"}
88				info, statErr := os.Lstat(child)
89				if statErr != nil && !os.IsNotExist(statErr) {
90					return gError(rel, statErr)
91				}
92				if statErr == nil && (!info.IsDir() || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0) {
93					return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s is not a regular directory", rel)
94				}
95				_, markerErr := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(child, ".git"))

116				}
117				n.Initialized, n.State, n.GitDir, n.CommonDir = true, "available", cr.GitDir, cr.GitCommonDir
118				n.CheckoutIdentity, err = submoduleDirectoryIdentity(child)
119				if err != nil {
120					return err
121				}
122				n.GitIdentity, err = submoduleDirectoryIdentity(cr.GitDir)
123				if err != nil {

125				}

173		h.Write([]byte(g.RootIdentity))

195	func gError(path string, err error) error { return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s: %w", path, err) }
196	
197	func validateSubmodulePath(root, rel string) error {
198		if rel == "" || rel == "." || filepath.IsAbs(rel) || strings.Contains(rel, "\\") || filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Clean(rel)) != rel || strings.HasPrefix(rel, "../") {
199			return fmt.Errorf("invalid submodule path %q", rel)
200		}
201		p := root
202		for _, part := range strings.Split(rel, "/") {
203			p = filepath.Join(p, part)
204			info, err := os.Lstat(p)
205			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
206				return nil
207			}
208			if err != nil {
209				return err
210			}
211			if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
212				return fmt.Errorf("submodule path %s crosses a symlink", rel)
213			}
214		}
215		return nil
216	}
217	
218	func submoduleEntries(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]SubmoduleNode, error) {
219		index, err := run(ctx, dir, "ls-files", "--stage", "-z")
220		if err != nil {
221			return nil, err
222		}
223		var entries []SubmoduleNode
224		for _, record := range nulLines(index) {
225			meta, path, ok := strings.Cut(record, "\t")
226			f := strings.Fields(meta)
227			if !ok || len(f) != 3 || f[0] != "160000" {
228				continue
229			}
230			if f[2] != "0" {
231				return nil, fmt.Errorf("conflicted gitlink %s", path)
232			}
233			entries = append(entries, SubmoduleNode{Path: path, Gitlink: f[1]})
234		}
235		if len(entries) == 0 {
236			return entries, nil
237		}
238		// Read the indexed .gitmodules, not a mutable working file or inherited
239		// global configuration. Names and paths are NUL-safe.
240		modules, err := run(ctx, dir, "config", "--null", "--blob", ":.gitmodules", "--get-regexp", `^submodule\..*\.(path|url)$`)
241		if err != nil {
242			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read indexed .gitmodules: %w", err)
243		}
244		paths, urls := map[string]string{}, map[string]string{}
245		for _, record := range nulLines(modules) {
246			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(record, "\n")
247			if !ok {
248				return nil, errors.New("invalid .gitmodules entry")
249			}
250			if strings.HasSuffix(key, ".path") {
251				paths[strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(key, "submodule."), ".path")] = value
252			}
253			if strings.HasSuffix(key, ".url") {
254				urls[strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(key, "submodule."), ".url")] = value
255			}
256		}
257		for i := range entries {
258			matches := 0
259			for name, path := range paths {
260				if path == entries[i].Path {
261					matches++
262					entries[i].Name = name
263					entries[i].URL = urls[name]
264				}
265			}
266			if matches != 1 || entries[i].URL == "" {
267				return nil, fmt.Errorf("gitlink %s has no unique .gitmodules mapping", entries[i].Path)
268			}
269		}
270		sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool { return entries[i].Path < entries[j].Path })

36	func (s *Store) Create(ctx context.Context, intent *Intent) error {
37		if intent == nil {
38			return fmt.Errorf("create nil artifact intent")
39		}
40		return lockx.WithDir(ctx, s.Dir, "artifact intent", func() error {
41			candidate := *intent
42			if candidate.ID == "" {
43				candidate.ID = s.newID()
44			}
45			candidate.SchemaVersion = SchemaVersion
46			candidate.Status = Armed
47			now := s.clock().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
48			candidate.CreatedAt, candidate.UpdatedAt = now, now
49			if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
50				return err
51			}
52			if _, err := os.Stat(s.path(candidate.ID)); err == nil {
53				return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s already exists", candidate.ID)
54			} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
55				return err
56			}
57			if err := s.write(candidate); err != nil {
58				return err
59			}
60			*intent = candidate
61			return nil
62		})
63	}

66		if !idPattern.MatchString(id) {

68		}

70		if err != nil {
71			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
72				return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s: %w", id, ErrIntentNotFound)
73			}
74			return nil, err
75		}
76		defer file.Close()
77		decoder := json.NewDecoder(file)
78		decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
79		var intent Intent
80		if err := decoder.Decode(&intent); err != nil {
81			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode artifact intent %s: %w", id, err)
82		}
83		if err := ensureJSONEOF(decoder); err != nil {
84			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode artifact intent %s: %w", id, err)
85		}
86		if intent.ID != id {
87			return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact intent filename %s disagrees with id %s", id, intent.ID)
88		}
89		if err := intent.Validate(); err != nil {
90			return nil, err

96		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)

98			return nil, nil
99		}
100		if err != nil {
101			return nil, err
102		}
103		var intents []Intent
104		for _, entry := range entries {

113		}
114		sort.Slice(intents, func(i, j int) bool { return intents[i].CreatedAt.Before(intents[j].CreatedAt) })
115		return intents, nil

242	// MoveWorktree relocates a linked worktree through Git so the shared
243	// administrative metadata keeps pointing at the checkout's new path. dir may
244	// be any checkout of the same repository.
245	func MoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, source, destination string) error {
246		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "move", source, destination)
247		return err
248	}
249	
250	// RemoveWorktree removes a linked worktree checkout. It never deletes the
251	// branch — that is a separate, explicit decision.
252	func RemoveWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, path string, force bool) error {
253		// A generic force flag never authorizes deleting a child repository's
254		// refs/objects. The recursive lifecycle stages those only after proof.
255		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
256			g, err := SubmodulesOf(ctx, path)
257			if err != nil {
258				return err
259			}
260			for _, n := range g.Nodes {
261				if n.Initialized || n.State != "uninitialized" {
262					return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s requires guarded --recursive cleanup", n.Path)
263				}
264			}
265			if r, err := Discover(ctx, path); err == nil {
266				if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(r.GitDir, "modules")); err == nil {
267					return errors.New("private submodule Git data requires guarded --recursive cleanup")
268				}
269			}
270		}
271		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
272		if err != nil {
273			return fmt.Errorf("resolve current directory before removing worktree: %w", err)
274		}
275		inside, err := pathx.Contains(path, cwd)
276		if err != nil {
277			return fmt.Errorf("compare current directory with worktree %s: %w", path, err)
278		}
279		if inside {
280			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to remove worktree %s while the caller is inside it", path)
281		}
282		args := []string{"worktree", "remove"}
283		if force {
284			args = append(args, "--force")
285		}
286		args = append(args, path)
287		_, err = run(ctx, dir, args...)
288		return err
289	}
290	
291	// PruneWorktrees clears administrative entries for checkouts whose directories
292	// were deleted behind git's back.
293	func PruneWorktrees(ctx context.Context, dir string) error {
294		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "worktree", "prune")
295		return err
296	}
297	
298	// BranchExists reports whether a local branch of that name exists.
299	func BranchExists(ctx context.Context, dir, branch string) bool {
300		if branch == "" {
301			return false
302		}
303		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+branch)
304		return err == nil
305	}
306	
307	// RefState reports whether any ref or commit-ish resolves while preserving
308	// observation failures. A normal rev-parse exit 1 with no diagnostic is an
309	// authoritative missing ref; every other failure remains an error.
310	func RefState(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) (bool, error) {
311		if ref == "" {
312			return false, nil
313		}
314		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", ref+"^{commit}")
315		if err == nil {
316			return true, nil
317		}
318		var commandErr *Error
319		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
320		if errors.As(err, &commandErr) && errors.As(commandErr.Err, &exitErr) &&
321			exitErr.ExitCode() == 1 && strings.TrimSpace(commandErr.Stderr) == "" {
322			return false, nil
323		}
324		return false, err
325	}
326	
327	// RefExists is the compatibility predicate for callers where probe failure is
328	// intentionally equivalent to absence. Guarded lifecycle code uses RefState.
329	func RefExists(ctx context.Context, dir, ref string) bool {
330		exists, _ := RefState(ctx, dir, ref)
331		return exists
332	}

11	// WorktreeInspection is the read-only aggregate of every artifact intent for a
12	// checkout. Ready means each intent was explicitly discarded or finalized to a
13	// commit still reachable from a recovery ref; it never changes an intent.
14	type WorktreeInspection struct {
15		IntentCount int      `json:"intent_count"`
16		Status      Status   `json:"status,omitempty"`

18		IntentIDs   []string `json:"intent_ids"`

21	// InspectWorktrees groups all intents once and verifies finalized commit
22	// reachability without reconciling or writing state.
23	func InspectWorktrees(ctx context.Context, store *Store) (map[string]WorktreeInspection, error) {
24		intents, err := store.List()
25		if err != nil {
26			return nil, err
27		}
28		out := map[string]WorktreeInspection{}
29		for _, intent := range intents {
30			path, err := pathx.Canonical(intent.WorktreePath)
31			if err != nil {
32				continue
33			}
34			inspection, exists := out[path]
35			if !exists {
36				inspection.Ready = true
37			}
38			inspection.IntentCount++
39			inspection.IntentIDs = append(inspection.IntentIDs, intent.ID)
40			if statusPriority(intent.Status) >= statusPriority(inspection.Status) {
41				inspection.Status = intent.Status
42			}
43			ready := intent.Status == Discarded ||
44				(intent.Status == Finalized && (intent.ArtifactCommit != "" || intent.ArchiveCommit != "") && CommitReachable(ctx, intent))
45			inspection.Ready = inspection.Ready && ready
46			out[path] = inspection
47		}
48		for path, inspection := range out {
49			sort.Strings(inspection.IntentIDs)
50			out[path] = inspection
51		}
52		return out, nil
53	}

83		return false

87		switch status {
88		case Discarded, Finalized:
89			return 1
90		case Armed:
91			return 2
92		case Finalizing:
93			return 3
94		case Failed:
95			return 4

## 修正 1：先以 repository 身分篩選 artifact，再檢查 moved-intent branch

關鍵檔案：`internal/artifact/service.go`、`service_test.go`、
`internal/taskflow/submodules.go`、`submodules_git_test.go`。

- 保留 `Store.List()` 完整性檢查、exact canonical checkout matching 與錯誤累積。
- 將 `inspectReadinessCheckoutIdentity` 的 Git common-directory discovery 與
  branch observation 分開。先 canonicalize 所選 checkout 與 unmatched intents
  的 common directories，排除已證明不屬於此 repository 的記錄。
- 只有仍有同一 common-directory 的 moved-intent 候選時才要求 branch 身分；
  此時 detached／不明 branch 繼續 fail closed。
- 不依 finalized/pending status 猜測某記錄是否無關；不跳過
  `inspectIntentReadiness`、`InspectHistoryReadiness`、receipt verification。
- `submoduleClaims` 分開「artifact observation error」與「已觀察到未完成 artifact」；
  保留前者的具體原因與 child path，讓 plan evidence 與 apply diagnostics 有用。
  公開輸出不得新增私有內容傾印。

測試沿用 `createReadinessIntent`、`isolateGitConfig`、
`submoduleLifecycleFixture`、`createPendingArtifact`：
- detached + unrelated finalized/pending intents：ready、zero matches、known empty。
- relevant exact pending、same-repo moved ambiguity、unreadable/corrupt store：仍阻擋。
- canonical aliases／branch matching 不改變 repository 邊界。
- detached child 的 submodule claims 不受無關 intent 影響；實際 observation error 保留原因。

## 修正 2：安全區分空 gitlink 與實際保留的 child repositories

**保留 `--recursive` 明確授權。** 安全空節點只豁免不存在之 child repository 的
復原／遠端證明，不豁免 cleanup 的 Plan／Apply。無 `--recursive` 仍顯示可操作的 blocker。

關鍵檔案：`internal/submodule/removal.go`、`removal_test.go`、
`internal/taskflow/submodules.go`、`completion_runtime.go`、`submodules_git_test.go`，
以及 `internal/safefile` 的 directory-only removal helper 與 native platform tests。

### Local observation 與 sealed authority

- 在 `InspectRemoval` 中建立 removal-local layout snapshot，分開觀察與授權。
  非 recursive 預覽可以提供 layout authority，但不可提供可執行的 disposal authority；
  `VerifyRemote`／`Apply` 必須仍拒絕未授權的 removal，不能依賴呼叫者忽略 error 來守住界線。
  記錄 checkout／Git-dir roots、empty child 的 exact identity 或 observed absence、
  administration directory 的路徑／身分／排序 listing，以及 initialized disposal subset。
- 分類為：owned initialized、safely empty、uninitialized with retained data、unknown/unsafe。
  安全空必須是缺席或真正空的一般目錄，且整個 private module storage 沒有 retained child store。
  任何 local/ignored file、`.git` marker、nested user directory、symlink/reparse point 或觀察錯誤都不算空。
- `inspectModuleStorage` 的 known repository set 只包含 initialized nodes；
  仍掃描全部 private administration，包括 nested `modules/`，拒絕 retained／orphan stores 與任意檔案。
  缺席的 modules root 是事實而非錯誤，不建立它；只有已審閱的 directory-only scaffolding 可待移除。
  零 gitlink 時也先檢查 storage：缺席為 no-op，空 scaffolding 需 recursive plan，實際 orphan data 阻擋。
- 用 deterministic `LayoutFingerprint` 封入 `submodule-removal` authority；
  `decorateSubmodules`、`prepareSubmodules` 及 `RetirementPreviewAuthority` 同步保存／重驗。
  現有 graph、workspace intent、claims 與 recursive authority 不移除。
- all-empty preflight 是 local/non-network，描述不得聲稱將處置 private refs/objects 或需要 push。
  `InspectPublication` 的原有整合／發布條件不變。

### Claims、Apply 與目錄移除

- 空／缺席 child 不呼叫會向上找到 parent repository 的 Git readiness discovery。
  task claims 保持 exact/subtree path matching；artifact claims 由 strict `Store.List()`
  和 canonical exact/subtree path matching 觀察，保留相關 intent identity/status/receipt
  與 unreadable inventory blockers。空路徑的 matching non-discarded intent 一律作為 ownership
  blocker（包含 finalized，不能借 parent Git 驗證）；discarded 不阻擋但仍封入 authority。
  不使用會吞觀察錯誤的便利 listing，initialized child 的正常 finalized receipt 語意不變。
  initialized child 保留完整 artifact receipt/readiness 檢查，runtime coverage 仍涵蓋整個 subtree。
- `VerifyRemote`／`Apply` 的 proof cardinality、origin queries、leases、private-state
  checks、moves 只處理 initialized subset；不使用空的 `CommonDir` 取得鎖。
- **all-empty：** 不建遠端 proof repository、不 quarantine、不搬 child，不要求 child push。
  仍重驗 graph／layout／workspace revision／claims，且 final claim callback 即使 zero initialized
  nodes 也至少執行一次。在 parent repository/task locks 內、第一次變更前及最終 removal 前驗證。
- **mixed：** 只 stage initialized children，保留 deepest-first 次序、完整 modules quarantine、
  journal/rollback/recovery；empty nodes 的 layout 也需重驗。沿用 `recover.go`，不重做復原架構。
- 保留 `gitx.RemoveWorktree` 對 modules storage 的保守拒絕；只有 recursive removal 層
  能 bottom-up prune 已審閱、身分仍相同且仍空的 administration directories，再呼叫
  普通 `git worktree remove`（force=false）。
- 在 safefile 新增窄化的 `RemoveEmptyChildDir(ctx context.Context, parent *os.Root, name string, expected fs.FileInfo) error`
  directory-only primitive：驗證 portable child name、`OpenChildRoot`／`VerifyChildRoot`／empty listing，
  再做 native directory-only delete（Unix dirfd `unlinkat(..., AT_REMOVEDIR)`；
  Windows relative-to-held-parent、verified non-reparse directory handle，驗證前不得設定 delete-on-close）。
  不使用會 unlink 替換檔案的 `os.Remove`／`os.Root.Remove`，不使用 `RemoveAll` 或 force；
  不具已驗證 backend 的平台 fail closed。
- Plan 後 absence→presence、初始化、新檔案、root 替換、symlink／claim 變更皆 stale；
  late nonempty content 必須由 directory-only primitive 拒絕。raw writers 仍不受 dev lock 保證。
  已 prune 部分空目錄後失敗，typed error／taskflow ledger 要列明 partial effect，
  不宣稱 worktree 已刪或 task 已 retired、不默默重建 administration。
- `objects/info/alternates` 及 squash ancestry 限制不是本次要繞過的 bug。

38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `submodule` owns versioned workspace-member intent and reversible child-clone disposal mechanisms. `gitx` supplies the local gitlink graph; `taskflow` owns recursive lifecycle policy and fresh remote-proof ordering. Gitlink checkouts are legitimate submodules, not nested managed linked worktrees.
56	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints. Lifecycle callers use exact-record revisions and locked compare-and-update/delete transactions rather than treating a previously read task as current.
57	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
58	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
59	- `taskflow` is the UI-agnostic lifecycle authority: it separates recorded intent, typed live observations, immutable guarded plans, approvals, and partial result ledgers. Apply locks and reloads task/Git/worktree/runtime/artifact/remote identity, then rejects stale authority before mutation.
60	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, all registered worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and UI projections consume this joined view.
61	- `agentinterop` owns explicit MCP/skill/instruction transfer plans, guarded apply, stanza/link ownership, private recovery, and optional recipes. Native agent files and skills locks remain authoritative; only explicit preparation/check/launch paths may execute a provider or MCP server. Recovery belongs outside Git, credentials remain runtime references, and native Windows writes fail closed pending verified ACL/identity support.
62	- `triage` owns read-only cross-repository findings, clone-bound local intent, ignored-directory policy and reviewed batch ledgers; `triagetui` is its independent UI. Synchronization uses taskflow plans, and protected cleanup adds guards inside the existing repository lock and immediately before removal. Local scans never reconcile Try catalog entries.
63	- `flowtui` is an independent Bubble Tea model for the preview `dev flow` repository state-machine UI. It receives repository reads and taskflow Plan/Apply callbacks; do not embed it in or add a mode to the dashboard's `tui` model.
64	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
65	- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
66	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
67	- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage`, note FTS, and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
68	- `agenthistory` owns explicit transcript/file retention policy, immutable source-bound archive copies, Git lookup/sync and isolated history migration. Archive bindings/recovery stay in private state, ordinary status never contacts remotes, and source writers/index bytes remain untouched by archiving. `artifact` keeps old commit handoffs and adds externally verified archive receipts; taskflow includes ignored capture readiness in its guarded authority.
69	- `hygiene` owns configurable secret/privacy policy, index/worktree/frozen-history scans, private identity rules and signed replacement plans. Raw findings/recovery stay outside Git; hook setup preserves foreign hooks. Large text transactions explicitly opt into configedit’s Windows backend; existing configuration flows retain their platform contracts.
70	- `feedback` owns durable private reports, sanitized public drafts, revision-bound issue/comment publication receipts and exact repair plans. CLI adapts its repair backend to the shared start flow; agent launch is explicit and prompt context never becomes a public issue body.
71	- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.
72	- `sshhost` owns bounded static discovery of the active user OpenSSH Include closure, canonical files under `~/.ssh/dev.d`, public-key selection/generation/bootstrap, fresh authentication proofs, and the explicit handoff into dev fleet. OpenSSH and plain `ssh -G` remain semantic authority; ordinary setup/remove never rewrite foreign connection definitions, copy private keys, weaken host-key policy, or treat every alias as a fleet member. Explicit format/organize may transform selected user-owned configuration with private guarded recovery; Include restores its caller scope after each file. Named agent providers (Bitwarden, 1Password, Secretive, custom sockets) are located by stat only and never executed; selecting a named-agent key publishes only its public line and writes a v2 fragment (`IdentityAgent`, `SecurityKeyProvider`), which older binaries treat as not dev-owned, while v1 files stay byte-identical. Explicit FIDO generation binds the reviewed native tools/provider, keeps capability observations stat-only, and reports hardware created/unknown effects independently of local publication; only verified SK recovery pairs may be retained. Never use resident-key download or provider loading as a passive probe, and keep automatic Secure Enclave creation blocked until exact native identity mapping is verified.
73	- `sshflow` owns the explicit SSH/fleet/Herdr machine inventory and Plan/Apply orchestration; `herdrremote` calls the native machine CLI without writing its catalog. `configedit` owns source-bound local file transactions and private recovery outside Git, with owner leases and macOS/Linux metadata checks.
74	- `machineregistry` owns controller-local canonical machine UUIDs, scoped provider bindings, explicit unlink suppression and merge redirects in durable private SQLite. 75	- `sshactivity` owns private durable per-profile usage and test observations. Usage records actual local dev-mediated SSH process starts; network/full tests never update usage. Observations retain source fingerprints and cannot authorize mutations or imply present connectivity.

77	- `selfupdate` selects exact release platform assets and stages native Go source builds when an asset is absent, preferring the checksummed compact source archive over legacy Go module source. 79	- `sshremote` owns strict bounded v1 SSH capability/inventory/resolve/key/connect protocols and private disposable source/route caches. Only explicit capability may initialize remote dev identity. Remote `dev` state remains host-local. `remote_os` selects target semantics: POSIX uses the shell launcher, while Windows uses an encoded PowerShell launcher that accepts only hidden fleet helpers, preserves sync stdin, and never applies controller path rules to remote paths.
85	
86	The principal task start flow spans `internal/cli/start.go`, `start_flow.go`, `gitx`/`wt`, `runtime`, and `task`: resolve the canonical repository and explicit base, create or select the checkout, provision/open it, then persist and annotate the task. 88	State is split intentionally:
89	
90	- Git remotes/branches are durable code truth.
91	- Worktrees are disposable local checkouts.
92	- Runtime sessions are per-host and re-derivable.
93	- Task TOML and catalog assets hold only intent/identity that Git cannot answer.
94	- Repository quick-note Markdown is durable sidecar data; `notes.db` is only its disposable search index.
95	- `stats.db` is durable observation data; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/*` is disposable.
96	- SSH source/route caches are disposable; remote dev UUIDs, local canonical machine UUIDs and fleet trust pins are separate identities.
