97	- The user's OpenSSH configuration is durable connection truth. 98	- Fleet intent is the merged primary `remotes.toml` plus generated sibling `remotes.d` fragments. 99	- `paths.state_dir/machines/registry.db` is durable controller-local identity and binding intent; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/ssh-discovery/` contains disposable dated Tailscale/LAN observations. The active SSH dashboard may refresh local Tailscale status when `[tui.ssh].background_refresh` is enabled; native discovery returns typed observations independently of cache writes. Candidate setup preserves source/scope provenance and per-stage retained effects.

101	## Behavioral contracts
102	
103	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
104	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
105	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
106	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
107	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
108	- Submodule initialization uses committed gitlinks, never implicitly advances to `main`. Whole child-clone disposal requires explicit recursive approval and fresh recovery proof for its private refs/objects; outer and shared canonical repositories are retained. Local graph refresh never performs remote proof. Child task/runtime/artifact claims block parent disposal.
109	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
110	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
111	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
112	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
113	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
114	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
115	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
116	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output, including `dev hygiene report --json` (`hygiene_summary` schema 1). Stored summaries are historical observations, not proof of current source bytes.
117	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
118	- Explicit SSH format/organize and fleet profile rename/remove are plan-first exceptions for user-selected files; retain comments, Include order, original metadata and private recovery. Never activate dormant files with a new broad Include. Herdr machine add may prepare/start a remote server; leave native approvals native, and remove/disable never stops remote sessions.
119	- SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. Full bootstrap requires an explicit existing key or explicit generation, registers fleet only when explicitly selected, and reports interrupted remote installation as unknown rather than pretending to roll it back.
120	- SSH wizard permission preflight may separately review and apply metadata-only tightening on exact current-user-owned canonical/selected paths. It never recursively chmods, changes ownership, guesses ACLs, or widens permissions; completed repairs survive later cancellation. Listing and dry-run never repair permissions. Local key listing evaluates OpenSSH only behind explicit `--alias`; selected key material remains service-bound and is revalidated before configuration changes and bootstrap.
121	- `dev ssh key doctor` exposes the same permission Plan/Apply with bounded metadata-only key discovery; `--key` restricts the reviewed scope, and `--fix` requires a complete safe plan plus confirmation. Default doctor never mutates, reads private contents, or queries agents/remotes. Batch repairs revalidate the whole reviewed union and retain successful tightening on partial failure.
122	- Source-aware SSH setup can use `--auth existing` without installing a key, and registers only explicitly selected `--to fleet|herdr|both` destinations. Tailscale SSH advertisement is advisory; its port-22 endpoint is not an authorized_keys bootstrap target. Preserve the key-authentication guard and never treat Tailscale policy login as proof that a selected public key worked. Names, ports and cached observations never authorize machine merges; binding/source changes invalidate reviewed plans.
123	- Fleet-source SSH discovery selects explicit hosts without recursive fleet traversal. 127	## Versioning and changelog
128	
129	The current published baseline is `v0.2.38` (2026-09-15). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
130	
131	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
132	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
133	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
134	
135	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
136	
137	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
138	
139	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
140	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
141	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
142	
143	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
144	
145	For a release:
146	
147	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
148	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
149	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
150	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
151	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
152	
153	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
154	
155	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
156

158	
159	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.

162	|---|---|
163	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
164	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
165	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
166	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. 167	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
168	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
169	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
170	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |

172	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
173

181	privacy imports use only bounded local cache readers and revalidate their source.
182	`internal/agentskill` owns selected-removal policy: exact native names/agent scopes
183	or bundled manifests, source/ownership/dependency proof and postconditions under
184	the provider lease. Never infer complete Windows validation from an advisory
185	step's success conclusion; inspect logs and require the dedicated native gates.

188	
189	`dev help ai-artifacts` separates source retention, archive location, protection
190	and distribution. New configuration is opt-in. Sources are SpecStory Markdown or
191	explicit files; provider IDs name the originating agent. Do not infer writer exit
192	from byte stability or close agents to finalize evidence. Archive mode verifies
193	ignored bytes before cleanup; existing tracked intents retain their original lane.
194	`git-filter-repo` only operates on new verified copies. Ordinary migration never
195	rewrites source refs or published tags, and raw backups are not secret audits.

Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
136	
137	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
138	
139	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
140	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
141	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
142	
143	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
144	
145	For a release:
146	
147	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
148	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
149	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
150	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
151	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
152	
153	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
154	
155	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
156	
157	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
158	
159	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
160	
161	| Change | Required synchronization |
162	|---|---|
163	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
164	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
165	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
166	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
167	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
168	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
169	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
170	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
171	
172	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
173	
174	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
175	
176	## Hygiene and skill batch operations
177	
178	`internal/hygiene` owns per-repository setup plans and batch ledgers. REPOS and
179	`hygiene manage` are adapters; JSON batch management previews only. Keep legacy
180	artifact finalizers until their independent lifecycle is replaced. Cached machine
181	privacy imports use only bounded local cache readers and revalidate their source.
182	`internal/agentskill` owns selected-removal policy: exact native names/agent scopes
183	or bundled manifests, source/ownership/dependency proof and postconditions under
184	the provider lease. Never infer complete Windows validation from an advisory
185	step's success conclusion; inspect logs and require the dedicated native gates.
186	
187	## Agent history policy
188	
189	`dev help ai-artifacts` separates source retention, archive location, protection
190	and distribution. New configuration is opt-in. Sources are SpecStory Markdown or
191	explicit files; provider IDs name the originating agent. Do not infer writer exit
192	from byte stability or close agents to finalize evidence. Archive mode verifies
193	ignored bytes before cleanup; existing tracked intents retain their original lane.
194	`git-filter-repo` only operates on new verified copies. Ordinary migration never
195	rewrites source refs or published tags, and raw backups are not secret audits.
196

76	// ReadinessInspection is a complete read-only observation for one selected

87	// Ready applies only the existing artifact finalization contract: an exact
88	// checkout is ready when it has no intents, or every intent was explicitly
89	// discarded or has a finalized receipt that is still reachable. Missing or
90	// incomplete evidence fails closed.
91	func (i ReadinessInspection) Ready() bool {
92		if i.History != nil && !i.History.Ready {
93			return false
94		}
95		if i.ObservationError != nil {
96			return false
97		}
98		if len(i.Intents) == 0 {
99			return i.KnownEmpty
100		}
101		if i.KnownEmpty {
102			return false
103		}
104		for _, intent := range i.Intents {
105			if intent.ObservationError != nil {
106				return false
107			}
108			switch intent.State {
109			case ReadinessDiscarded:
110				// Discard is the existing explicit operator escape hatch.
111			case ReadinessFinalizedReachable:
112				if !intent.Finalized || !intent.ReceiptReachable {
113					return false
114				}
115			default:
116				return false
117			}
118		}
119		return true
120	}

122	// InspectReadiness gathers artifact finalization evidence for one checkout,
123	// including intents whose exact checkout moved but stable Git identity matches.
124	// It never reconciles receipts, finalizes intents, or writes either
125	// source files or intent records. The returned inspection retains partial
126	// evidence and the same wrapped error returned separately to ordinary callers.
127	func InspectReadiness(ctx context.Context, store *Store, checkout string) (ReadinessInspection, error) {
128		inspection := ReadinessInspection{}
129		if ctx == nil {
130			err := errors.New("artifact readiness inspection needs a context")
131			inspection.ObservationError = err
132			return inspection, err
133		}
134		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
135			inspection.ObservationError = err
136			return inspection, err
137		}
138		if store == nil {
139			err := errors.New("artifact readiness inspection needs a store")
140			inspection.ObservationError = err
141			return inspection, err
142		}
143	
144		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(checkout)
145		if err != nil {
146			err = fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact readiness checkout: %w", err)
147			inspection.ObservationError = err
148			return inspection, err
149		}
150		inspection.Checkout = canonical
151	
152		intents, err := store.List()
153		if err != nil {
154			err = fmt.Errorf("list artifact intents: %w", err)
155			inspection.ObservationError = err
156			return inspection, err
157		}
158		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
159			inspection.ObservationError = err
160			return inspection, err
161		}
162	
163		matched := make([]Intent, 0, len(intents))
164		unmatched := make([]Intent, 0, len(intents))
165		for _, intent := range intents {
166			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
167				inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, err)
168				break
169			}
170			intentCheckout, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(intent.WorktreePath)
171			if canonicalErr != nil {
172				canonicalErr = fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact intent %s checkout: %w", intent.ID, canonicalErr)
173				inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, canonicalErr)
174				continue
175			}
176			if intentCheckout == canonical {
177				matched = append(matched, intent)
178			} else {
179				unmatched = append(unmatched, intent)
180			}
181		}
182	
183		if len(unmatched) > 0 && inspection.ObservationError == nil {
184			identity, available, identityErr := inspectReadinessCheckoutIdentity(ctx, canonical)
185			if identityErr != nil {
186				inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, identityErr)
187			} else if available {
188				for _, intent := range unmatched {
189					intentCommon, commonErr := pathx.Canonical(intent.GitCommonDir)
190					if commonErr != nil {
191						inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError,
192							fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact intent %s Git common directory: %w", intent.ID, commonErr))
193						continue
194					}
195					if intentCommon == identity.commonDir && intent.Branch == identity.branch {
196						matched = append(matched, intent)
197					}
198				}
199			}
200		}
201	
202		for _, intent := range matched {
203			evidence, evidenceErr := inspectIntentReadiness(ctx, canonical, intent)
204			if evidenceErr != nil {
205				inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, evidenceErr)
206			}
207			inspection.Intents = append(inspection.Intents, evidence)
208		}
209	
210		history, historyErr := InspectHistoryReadiness(ctx, store, canonical)
211		inspection.History = history
212		if historyErr != nil {
213			inspection.ObservationError = joinReadinessError(inspection.ObservationError, historyErr)
214		}
215	
216		inspection.KnownEmpty = len(inspection.Intents) == 0 && inspection.ObservationError == nil
217		return inspection, inspection.ObservationError
218	}

225	func inspectReadinessCheckoutIdentity(ctx context.Context, checkout string) (readinessCheckoutIdentity, bool, error) {
226		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, checkout)
227		if errors.Is(err, gitx.ErrNotARepo) {
228			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, nil
229		}
230		if err != nil {
231			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, fmt.Errorf("discover artifact readiness checkout identity: %w", err)
232		}
233		commonDir, err := pathx.Canonical(repository.GitCommonDir)
234		if err != nil {
235			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, fmt.Errorf("canonicalize artifact readiness Git common directory: %w", err)
236		}
237		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
238		if err != nil {
239			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, fmt.Errorf("observe artifact readiness checkout branch: %w", err)
240		}
241		if status.Detached || status.Branch == "" {
242			return readinessCheckoutIdentity{}, false, errors.New("artifact readiness checkout is detached; moved intent identity is ambiguous")
243		}
244		return readinessCheckoutIdentity{commonDir: commonDir, branch: status.Branch}, true, nil
245	}
246	
247	func inspectIntentReadiness(ctx context.Context, checkout string, intent Intent) (IntentReadiness, error) {
248		evidence := IntentReadiness{Intent: intent, Finalized: intent.Status == Finalized}
249		var err error
250		switch intent.Status {
251		case Armed, Finalizing:
252			evidence.State = ReadinessPending
253		case Failed:
254			evidence.State = ReadinessFailed
255		case Discarded:
256			evidence.State = ReadinessDiscarded
257		case Finalized:
258			evidence.ReceiptReachable, err = receiptRemainsReachable(ctx, checkout, intent)
259			switch {
260			case err != nil:
261				err = fmt.Errorf("inspect artifact intent %s receipt: %w", intent.ID, err)
262				evidence.State = ReadinessObservationError
263				evidence.ObservationError = err
264			case evidence.ReceiptReachable:
265				evidence.State = ReadinessFinalizedReachable
266			default:
267				evidence.State = ReadinessFinalizedUnreachable
268			}
269		default:
270			// Store.List validates statuses, but fail closed if another Store
271			// implementation is introduced without preserving that contract.
272			err = fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s has unrecognized status %q", intent.ID, intent.Status)
273			evidence.State = ReadinessObservationError
274			evidence.ObservationError = err
275		}
276		return evidence, err
277	}
278	
279	func receiptRemainsReachable(ctx context.Context, checkout string, intent Intent) (bool, error) {
280		if intent.Destination == "archive" {
281			h, e := agenthistory.Open(ctx, agenthistory.Options{Root: checkout, StateDir: intent.ArchiveStateDir})
282			if e != nil {
283				return false, e
284			}
285			commit, e := h.VerifyArchiveReceipt(ctx, intent.ArchivePlanID)
286			return e == nil && commit == intent.ArchiveCommit, e
287		}
288		if intent.ArtifactCommit == "" {
289			return false, nil
290		}
291		candidates := []struct {
292			dir string
293			ref string
294		}{
295			{checkout, "HEAD"},
296			{intent.RepoPath, intent.Branch},
297			{intent.RepoPath, intent.Base},
298		}
299		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(candidates))
300		var observationErr error
301		for _, candidate := range candidates {
302			if candidate.dir == "" || candidate.ref == "" {
303				continue
304			}
305			key := candidate.dir + "\x00" + candidate.ref
306			if seen[key] {
307				continue
308			}
309			seen[key] = true
310			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
311				return false, joinReadinessError(observationErr, err)
312			}
313			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, candidate.dir, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref); err == nil {
314				return true, nil
315			} else if !gitNotAncestor(err) {
316				observationErr = joinReadinessError(observationErr,
317					fmt.Errorf("check %s against %s in %s: %w", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref, candidate.dir, err))
318			}
319		}
320		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
321			observationErr = joinReadinessError(observationErr, err)
322		}
323		return false, observationErr
324	}
325	
326	func gitNotAncestor(err error) bool {
327		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
328		return errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1
329	}
330	
331	func joinReadinessError(current, next error) error {
332		if current == nil {
333			return next
334		}
335		if next == nil {
336			return current
337		}
338		return errors.Join(current, next)
339	}
340	
341	func (s *Service) Prepare(ctx context.Context, request PrepareRequest) (*Intent, error) {
342		if s.Store == nil {
343			return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact service needs a store")
344		}
345		provider, sessionID, err := ParseSession(request.Session)
346		if err != nil {
347			return nil, err
348		}
349		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, request.Worktree)
350		if err != nil {
351			return nil, err
352		}
353		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, repository.Root)
354		if err != nil {
355			return nil, err
356		}
357		if status.Detached || status.Branch == "" {
358			return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact preparation requires a named branch")
359		}
360		if operation, active, err := gitx.InProgress(repository.Root); err != nil {
361			return nil, err
362		} else if active {
363			return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact preparation refuses Git operation %s in progress", operation)
364		}
365		head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repository.Root, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
366		if err != nil {
367			return nil, err
368		}
369		changes, err := statusPaths(ctx, repository.Root)
370		if err != nil {
371			return nil, err
372		}
373		var unrelated []string
374		for _, change := range changes {
375			if change.Staged {
376				return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact preparation requires an empty index; staged path: %s", change.Path)
377			}
378			if !isRecognizedArtifact(change.Path) {
379				return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit product changes before prepare; dirty path: %s", change.Path)
380			}
381			unrelated = append(unrelated, change.Path)
382		}
383		var history *agenthistory.Service
384		if _, e := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(repository.Root, ".dev-cli", "artifacts.toml")); e == nil || !errors.Is(e, os.ErrNotExist) {
385			history, err = agenthistory.Open(ctx, agenthistory.Options{Root: repository.Root, StateDir: filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(s.Store.Dir))})
386			if err != nil {
387				return nil, err
388			}
389		}
390		archiveMode := history != nil && history.Policy.Mode == "archive"
391		var transcript Transcript
392		if archiveMode {
393			if len(request.Plans) > 0 {
394				return nil, fmt.Errorf("commit reviewed plans with product changes; archive prepared SpecStory sessions separately")
395			}
396			transcript.Path, err = history.LocateSession(ctx, request.Session)
397		} else {
398			transcript, err = FindTranscript(repository.Root, provider, sessionID)
399		}
400		if err != nil {
401			return nil, err
402		}
403		tracked := false
404		if !archiveMode {
405			tracked, err = gitTracked(ctx, repository.Root, transcript.Path)
406		}
407		if err != nil {
408			return nil, err
409		}
410		info, err := os.Stat(transcript.Path)
411		if err != nil {
412			return nil, err
413		}
414		limit := s.LargeLimit
415		if limit <= 0 {
416			limit = DefaultLargeLimit
417		}
418		if !archiveMode && !tracked && info.Size() > limit && !request.AllowLarge {
419			return nil, fmt.Errorf("untracked transcript is %d bytes; re-run with --allow-large after reviewing repository growth", info.Size())
420		}

140	// Old gitlinks may leave independent repositories in modules/ after their
141	// paths disappear from the index. Every store being disposed must be in the
142	// observed graph; a clean current gitlink is not authority for orphan stores.
143	func inspectModuleStorage(root string, nodes []gitx.SubmoduleNode, originalRoot string) error {
144		known := map[string]bool{}
145		for _, n := range nodes {
146			rel, err := filepath.Rel(originalRoot, n.GitDir)
147			if err != nil {
148				return err
149			}
150			known[filepath.Join(root, rel)] = true
151		}
152		var walk func(string) error
153		walk = func(dir string) error {
154			entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
155			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
156				return nil
157			}
158			if err != nil {
159				return err
160			}
161			for _, entry := range entries {
162				path := filepath.Join(dir, entry.Name())
163				if !entry.IsDir() || entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
164					return fmt.Errorf("unclaimed private module data at %s", path)
165				}
166				if known[path] {
167					if err := walk(filepath.Join(path, "modules")); err != nil {
168						return err
169					}
170					continue
171				}
172				if _, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(path, "HEAD")); err == nil {
173					return fmt.Errorf("orphan submodule repository %s requires preservation", path)
174				}
175				if err := walk(path); err != nil {
176					return err
177				}
178			}
179			return nil
180		}
181		return walk(root)
182	}

351	// VerifyRemote fetches into a fresh isolated bare repository. Reachability is
352	// proven against the remote's advertised refs, never local tracking refs or
353	// objects borrowed from the checkout about to be removed.
354	func (p *Removal) VerifyRemote(ctx context.Context) error {
355		if p == nil {
356			return nil
357		}
358		var removedIdentities []os.FileInfo
359		for _, node := range p.Graph.Nodes {
360			for _, path := range []string{filepath.Join(p.Graph.Root, filepath.FromSlash(node.Path)), node.GitDir, filepath.Join(p.Graph.Root, filepath.FromSlash(node.Path), ".git")} {
361				info, err := os.Stat(path)
362				if err != nil {
363					return err
364				}
365				removedIdentities = append(removedIdentities, info)
366			}
367		}
368		for _, n := range p.Graph.Nodes {
369			child := filepath.Join(p.Graph.Root, filepath.FromSlash(n.Path))
370			url, err := gitx.Run(ctx, child, "remote", "get-url", "origin")
371			if err != nil {
372				return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s has no recovery origin", n.Path)
373			}
374			expected, err := gitx.SubmoduleSourceURL(ctx, filepath.Join(p.Graph.Root, filepath.FromSlash(n.Parent)), n.URL)
375			if err != nil || expected != url {
376				return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s recovery origin differs from its declared source", n.Path)
377			}
378			local, localErr := localRecoveryPath(child, url)
379			if localErr != nil {
380				return localErr
381			}
382			if local != "" {
383				info, err := os.Stat(local)
384				if err != nil {
385					return fmt.Errorf("recovery origin is unavailable: %w", err)
386				}
387				for _, removed := range removedIdentities {
388					if os.SameFile(info, removed) {
389						return errors.New("recovery origin depends on the workspace being removed")
390					}
391				}
392				for _, removedRoot := range []string{p.Graph.Root, p.Repository.GitDir} {
393					inside, err := pathx.Contains(removedRoot, local)
394					if err != nil || inside {
395						return errors.New("recovery origin depends on the workspace being removed")
396					}
397				}
398			}
399			before, err := gitx.Run(ctx, child, "ls-remote", "--refs", "origin")
400			if err != nil {
401				return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s recovery origin unavailable", n.Path)
402			}
403			proof, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "dev-submodule-proof-")
404			if err != nil {
405				return err
406			}
407			err = func() error {
408				defer os.RemoveAll(proof)
409				if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, proof, "init", "--bare", "--quiet"); err != nil {
410					return err
411				}
412				if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, proof, "fetch", "--quiet", "--no-tags", "--no-write-fetch-head", "--", url, "+refs/*:refs/*"); err != nil {
413					return errors.New("could not fetch isolated recovery proof")
414				}
415				after, err := gitx.Run(ctx, child, "ls-remote", "--refs", "origin")
416				if err != nil || before != after {
417					return errors.New("recovery remote refs changed during proof")
418				}
419				objects, err := gitx.Run(ctx, proof, "rev-list", "--objects", "--all")
420				if err != nil {
421					return err
422				}
423				available := map[string]bool{}
424				for _, line := range strings.Split(objects, "\n") {
425					if f := strings.Fields(line); len(f) > 0 {
426						available[f[0]] = true
427					}
428				}
429				advertised := map[string]string{}
430				for _, line := range strings.Split(after, "\n") {
431					if f := strings.Fields(line); len(f) == 2 {
432						advertised[f[1]] = f[0]
433					}
434				}
435				refs, err := gitx.Run(ctx, child, "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname) %(objectname)")
436				if err != nil {
437					return err
438				}
439				for _, line := range strings.Split(refs, "\n") {
440					f := strings.Fields(line)
441					if len(f) != 2 {
442						continue
443					}
444					if strings.HasPrefix(f[0], "refs/remotes/") {
445						continue
446					}
447					if advertised[f[0]] == "" || !available[f[1]] {
448						return fmt.Errorf("local ref %s is not preserved by the recovery remote", f[0])
449					}
450				}
451				if !available[n.HEAD] || !available[n.Gitlink] {
452					return errors.New("HEAD or gitlink is not remotely reachable")
453				}
454				reflog, err := gitx.Run(ctx, child, "reflog", "show", "--all", "--format=%H")
455				if err != nil {
456					return err
457				}
458				for _, oid := range strings.Fields(reflog) {
459					if !available[oid] {
460						return errors.New("reflog retains a local-only commit")
461					}
462				}
463				unreachable, err := gitx.Run(ctx, child, "fsck", "--unreachable", "--no-reflogs", "--no-progress")
464				if err != nil {
465					return errors.New("object integrity inspection failed")
466				}
467				for _, line := range strings.Split(unreachable, "\n") {
468					f := strings.Fields(line)
469					if len(f) == 3 && (f[0] == "unreachable" || f[0] == "dangling") && !available[f[2]] {
470						return errors.New("unreachable local objects require preservation")
471					}
472				}
473				if p.Merged {
474					for _, m := range p.Workspace.Members {
475						if m.Path == n.Path {
476							base := strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimPrefix(m.Base, "refs/remotes/"), "origin/")
477							if !strings.HasPrefix(base, "refs/") {
478								base = "refs/heads/" + base
479							}
480							if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, proof, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", n.HEAD, base); err != nil {
481								return fmt.Errorf("member is not integrated into %s", base)
482							}
483						}
484					}
485				}
486				return nil
487			}()
488			if err != nil {
489				return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s: %w", n.Path, err)
490			}
491			p.remoteRefs[n.Path] = before
492		}
493		return nil
494	}

496	func localRecoveryPath(cwd, source string) (string, error) {
497		if strings.HasPrefix(source, "file://") {
498			u, err := url.Parse(source)
499			if err != nil {
500				return "", errors.New("invalid recovery file URL")
501			}
502			if u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "" || u.User != nil {
503				return "", errors.New("ambiguous recovery file URL")
504			}
505			path := u.Path
506			if u.Host != "" && !strings.EqualFold(u.Host, "localhost") {
507				path = "//" + u.Host + path
508			}
509			if filepath.Separator == '\\' && len(path) > 2 && path[0] == '/' && path[2] == ':' {
510				path = path[1:]
511			}
512			return filepath.FromSlash(path), nil
513		}
514		if filepath.IsAbs(source) {
515			return source, nil
516		}
517		if !strings.Contains(source, ":") {
518			return filepath.Join(cwd, source), nil
519		}
520		return "", nil
521	}
522	
523	type moveRecord struct {
524		From  string `json:"from"`
525		To    string `json:"to"`
526		Empty bool   `json:"empty_placeholder"`
527	}
528	type removalJournal struct {
529		Version    int          `json:"version"`
530		Root       string       `json:"root"`
531		GitDir     string       `json:"git_dir"`
532		Repository string       `json:"repository"`
533		Branch     string       `json:"branch"`
534		Head       string       `json:"head"`
535		Moves      []moveRecord `json:"moves"`
536		Removed    bool         `json:"outer_removed"`
537	}
538	
539	// Apply stages child data reversibly, leaves empty gitlinks, and invokes the
540	// existing guarded non-force outer removal. A receipt is synced before every
541	// rename. Failed operations restore original paths only when still unclaimed.
542	func (p *Removal) Apply(ctx context.Context, check func(context.Context, string) error, removeOuter func() error) error {
543		if p == nil {
544			return removeOuter()
545		}
546		if len(p.remoteRefs) != len(p.Graph.Nodes) {
547			return errors.New("recursive removal has no fresh remote proof")
548		}
549		// Same lock namespace as taskflow. Parent is already locked by the caller.
550		nodes := append([]gitx.SubmoduleNode(nil), p.Graph.Nodes...)
551		sort.Slice(nodes, func(i, j int) bool { return nodes[i].CommonDir < nodes[j].CommonDir })
552		var leases []*lockx.Lease
553		defer func() {
554			for i := len(leases) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
555				leases[i].Close()
556			}
557		}()
558		for _, n := range nodes {
559			lease, err := lockx.AcquireDir(ctx, filepath.Join(n.CommonDir, "dev-taskflow"), "submodule repository")
560			if err != nil {
561				return err
562			}
563			leases = append(leases, lease)
564		}
565		fresh, err := gitx.SubmodulesOf(ctx, p.Graph.Root)
566		if err != nil {
567			return err
568		}
569		if fresh.Fingerprint != p.Graph.Fingerprint {
570			return errors.New("stale submodule cleanup plan")
571		}
572		for path, info := range p.roots {
573			if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(path, info); err != nil {
574				return err
575			}
576		}
577		_, revision, err := Load(p.Config, p.Workspace.Repository, p.Workspace.Branch)
578		if err != nil {
579			return err
580		}
581		if revision != p.Revision {
582			return errors.New("stale workspace member intent")
583		}
584		for _, n := range nodes {
585			child := filepath.Join(p.Graph.Root, filepath.FromSlash(n.Path))
586			if check != nil {
587				if err := check(ctx, child); err != nil {
588					return err
589				}
590			}
591			refs, err := gitx.Run(ctx, child, "ls-remote", "--refs", "origin")
592			if err != nil || refs != p.remoteRefs[n.Path] {
593				return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s remote proof is stale", n.Path)
594			}
595			if err := inspectPrivateState(ctx, child, n.GitDir); err != nil {
596				return err
597			}
598		}
599		area, err := os.MkdirTemp(filepath.Dir(p.Graph.Root), ".dev-submodule-retirement-")
600		if err != nil {
601			return err
602		}
603		head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, p.Graph.Root, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
604		if err != nil {
605			return err
606		}
607		journal := removalJournal{Version: 1, Root: p.Graph.Root, GitDir: p.Repository.GitDir, Repository: p.Repository.MainRoot, Branch: p.Workspace.Branch, Head: head}
608		journalPath := filepath.Join(area, "journal.json")
609		persist := func() error { return writeJSON(journalPath, journal) }
610		rollback := func(cause error) error {
611			for i := len(journal.Moves) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
612				m := journal.Moves[i]
613				if _, err := os.Lstat(m.To); os.IsNotExist(err) {
614					continue
615				}
616				if _, err := os.Lstat(m.From); err == nil {
617					if !m.Empty {
618						return fmt.Errorf("%w; original path reused; inspect %s", cause, journalPath)
619					}
620					if err := os.Remove(m.From); err != nil {
621						return fmt.Errorf("%w; cannot restore; inspect %s", cause, journalPath)
622					}
623				}
624				if err := os.Rename(m.To, m.From); err != nil {
625					return fmt.Errorf("%w; restore failed; inspect %s", cause, journalPath)
626				}
627			}
628			os.RemoveAll(area)
629			return cause
630		}
631		move := func(from, to string, empty bool) error {
632			if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(from, p.roots[from]); err != nil {
633				return err
634			}
635			journal.Moves = append(journal.Moves, moveRecord{From: from, To: to, Empty: empty})
636			if err := persist(); err != nil {
637				return err
638			}
639			if err := os.Rename(from, to); err != nil {
640				return err
641			}
642			if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(to, p.roots[from]); err != nil {
643				return err
644			}
645			if empty {
646				return os.Mkdir(from, 0755)
647			}
648			return nil
649		}
650		// Children leave first; parent moves retain their empty placeholders.
651		for i := len(p.Graph.Nodes) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
652			n := p.Graph.Nodes[i]
653			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
654				return rollback(err)
655			}
656			if err := move(filepath.Join(p.Graph.Root, filepath.FromSlash(n.Path)), filepath.Join(area, fmt.Sprintf("checkout-%d", i)), true); err != nil {
657				return rollback(err)
658			}
659		}
660		// Release file handles before moving private admin directories on Windows.
661		for i := len(leases) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
662			if err := leases[i].Close(); err != nil {
663				return rollback(err)
664			}
665		}
666		if err := move(filepath.Join(p.Repository.GitDir, "modules"), filepath.Join(area, "git-modules"), false); err != nil {
667			return rollback(err)
668		}
669		if err := inspectModuleStorage(filepath.Join(area, "git-modules"), p.Graph.Nodes, filepath.Join(p.Repository.GitDir, "modules")); err != nil {
670			return rollback(err)
671		}
672		if err := removeOuter(); err != nil {
673			return rollback(err)
674		}
675		journal.Removed = true
676		if err := persist(); err != nil {
677			return fmt.Errorf("outer removed; cleanup receipt retained at %s: %w", journalPath, err)
678		}
679		if err := os.RemoveAll(area); err != nil {
680			return fmt.Errorf("outer removed; private submodule data retained at %s: %w", journalPath, err)
681		}
682		return nil
683	}
684

118	func (s *lifecycleService) submoduleClaims(ctx context.Context, g gitx.SubmoduleGraph, parentTask string) (string, error) {
119		records, diagnostics, err := s.tasks.ListRecords()
120		if err != nil || len(diagnostics) > 0 {
121			return "unknown", fmt.Errorf("child task inventory is incomplete")
122		}
123		var evidence []string
124		var blockers []string
125		for _, n := range g.Nodes {
126			child := filepath.Join(g.Root, filepath.FromSlash(n.Path))
127			for _, record := range records {
128				if record.Task.ID == parentTask {
129					continue
130				}
131				for _, path := range []string{record.Task.RepoPath, record.Task.WorktreePath} {
132					if path == "" {
133						continue
134					}
135					inside, err := pathx.Contains(child, path)
136					if err != nil {
137						return "unknown", err
138					}
139					if inside {
140						evidence = append(evidence, record.Task.ID+":"+record.Revision)
141						blockers = append(blockers, fmt.Sprintf("%s is claimed by task %s", n.Path, record.Task.ID))
142						break
143					}
144				}
145			}
146			inspection, err := s.inspectArtifacts(ctx, s.artifacts, child)
147			evidence = append(evidence, n.Path+":"+artifactAuthority(inspection, err))
148			if err != nil || !inspection.Ready() {
149				blockers = append(blockers, n.Path+" has unknown or unfinished artifacts")
150			}
151		}
152		hash := authorityHash("submodule-claims", evidence...)
153		if len(blockers) > 0 {
154			return hash, fmt.Errorf("%s", strings.Join(blockers, "; "))
155		}
156		return hash, nil
157	}

1	// Package safefile provides held-root filesystem operations for untrusted
2	// relative paths. It keeps traversal relative to os.Root handles, rejects links
3	// and special files, revalidates filesystem identity, and detects observable
4	// source mutation while reading.
5	package safefile
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"errors"
10		"fmt"
11		"io"
12		"io/fs"
13		"os"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
16	)
17	
18	var (
19		// ErrChanged reports that a named root, child, or file no longer identifies
20		// the object observed by the caller.
21		ErrChanged = errors.New("filesystem object changed")
22		// ErrUnsafeType reports a symlink, reparse point, directory, or other
23		// non-regular object where a regular file was required.
24		ErrUnsafeType = errors.New("unsafe filesystem object type")
25		// ErrFileLimit reports a regular file whose bytes exceed the read policy.
26		ErrFileLimit = errors.New("file size limit exceeded")
27	)
28	
29	// OpenRoot opens path as a held os.Root and proves that the pre-open and
30	// post-open names identify the held directory. Symlinks and reparse points are
31	// rejected rather than followed.
32	func OpenRoot(path string) (*os.Root, fs.FileInfo, error) {
33		before, err := os.Lstat(path)
34		if err != nil {
35			return nil, nil, err
36		}
37		if unsafeLink(before) {
38			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("root is a symlink or reparse point: %w", ErrUnsafeType)
39		}
40		if !before.IsDir() {
41			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("root is not a directory: %w", ErrUnsafeType)
42		}
43		root, err := os.OpenRoot(path)
44		if err != nil {
45			return nil, nil, err
46		}
47		held, err := root.Stat(".")
48		if err != nil {
49			_ = root.Close()
50			return nil, nil, err
51		}
52		current, err := os.Lstat(path)
53		if err != nil || unsafeLink(held) || unsafeLink(current) || !current.IsDir() ||
54			!os.SameFile(before, held) || !os.SameFile(current, held) {
55			_ = root.Close()
56			if err != nil {
57				return nil, nil, err
58			}
59			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("root changed while opening: %w", ErrChanged)
60		}
61		return root, held, nil
62	}
63	
64	// OpenChildRoot opens one child directory through parent and proves that its
65	// name still identifies the held directory.
66	func OpenChildRoot(parent *os.Root, name string) (*os.Root, fs.FileInfo, error) {
67		if parent == nil {
68			return nil, nil, errors.New("open child root: nil parent")
69		}
70		if err := pathx.ValidatePortableComponent(name, CompiledMaxComponentBytes); err != nil {
71			return nil, nil, err
72		}
73		before, err := parent.Lstat(name)
74		if err != nil {
75			return nil, nil, err
76		}
77		if unsafeLink(before) {
78			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("component %q is a symlink or reparse point: %w", name, ErrUnsafeType)
79		}
80		if !before.IsDir() {
81			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("component %q is not a directory: %w", name, ErrUnsafeType)
82		}
83		child, err := parent.OpenRoot(name)
84		if err != nil {
85			return nil, nil, err
86		}
87		held, err := child.Stat(".")
88		if err != nil {
89			_ = child.Close()
90			return nil, nil, err
91		}
92		current, err := parent.Lstat(name)
93		if err != nil || unsafeLink(held) || unsafeLink(current) || !current.IsDir() ||
94			!os.SameFile(before, held) || !os.SameFile(current, held) {
95			_ = child.Close()
96			if err != nil {
97				return nil, nil, err
98			}
99			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("component %q changed while opening: %w", name, ErrChanged)
100		}
101		return child, held, nil
102	}
103	
104	// VerifyRoot proves that path still names the previously held root directory.
105	func VerifyRoot(path string, expected fs.FileInfo) error {
106		current, err := os.Lstat(path)
107		if err != nil {
108			return err
109		}
110		if expected == nil || unsafeLink(current) || !current.IsDir() || !os.SameFile(expected, current) {
111			return fmt.Errorf("root path changed: %w", ErrChanged)
112		}
113		return nil
114	}
115	
116	// VerifyChildRoot proves that name below parent still names the previously held
117	// child directory.
118	func VerifyChildRoot(parent *os.Root, name string, expected fs.FileInfo) error {
119		if parent == nil {
120			return errors.New("verify child root: nil parent")
121		}
122		if err := pathx.ValidatePortableComponent(name, CompiledMaxComponentBytes); err != nil {
123			return err
124		}
125		current, err := parent.Lstat(name)
126		if err != nil {
127			return err
128		}
129		if expected == nil || unsafeLink(current) || !current.IsDir() || !os.SameFile(expected, current) {
130			return fmt.Errorf("component %q changed: %w", name, ErrChanged)
131		}
132		return nil
133	}
134	
135	// ReadStableRegular reads one child file while proving that the directory name,
136	// opened descriptor, and final directory name all identify the expected regular
137	// file with unchanged observable metadata. maxBytes must be non-negative; zero
138	// means unbounded. Supplying the FileInfo from an earlier directory listing
139	// detects replacement or mutation between selection and opening.
140	func ReadStableRegular(ctx context.Context, root *os.Root, name string, expected fs.FileInfo, maxBytes int64) ([]byte, fs.FileInfo, error) {
141		if root == nil {
142			return nil, nil, errors.New("read stable file: nil root")
143		}
144		if maxBytes < 0 {
145			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("negative maximum file size: %w", ErrFileLimit)
146		}
147		if err := pathx.ValidatePortableComponent(name, CompiledMaxComponentBytes); err != nil {
148			return nil, nil, err
149		}
150		before, err := root.Lstat(name)
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, nil, err
153		}
154		if expected == nil {
155			expected = before
156		}
157		if unsafeLink(before) || !before.Mode().IsRegular() {
158			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source is not a regular file: %w", ErrUnsafeType)
159		}
160		if !sameStableSourceState(expected, before) {
161			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source changed before opening file: %w", ErrChanged)
162		}
163		if maxBytes > 0 && before.Size() > maxBytes {
164			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source is %d bytes; maximum is %d: %w", before.Size(), maxBytes, ErrFileLimit)
165		}
166	
167		file, err := openRegularForRead(root, name)
168		if err != nil {
169			return nil, nil, err
170		}
171		defer file.Close()
172		opened, err := file.Stat()
173		if err != nil {
174			return nil, nil, err
175		}
176		if unsafeLink(opened) || !opened.Mode().IsRegular() || !sameStableSourceState(expected, opened) {
177			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source changed while opening file: %w", ErrChanged)
178		}
179		current, err := root.Lstat(name)
180		if err != nil {
181			return nil, nil, err
182		}
183		if unsafeLink(current) || !sameStableSourceState(opened, current) {
184			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source changed while opening file: %w", ErrChanged)
185		}
186	
187		data, err := readAllContext(ctx, file, maxBytes)
188		if err != nil {
189			return nil, nil, err
190		}
191		after, err := file.Stat()
192		if err != nil {
193			return nil, nil, err
194		}
195		current, err = root.Lstat(name)
196		if err != nil {
197			return nil, nil, err
198		}
199		if unsafeLink(after) || unsafeLink(current) || !sameStableSourceState(opened, after) ||
200			!sameStableSourceState(after, current) || after.Size() != int64(len(data)) {
201			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("source changed during read: %w", ErrChanged)
202		}
203		return data, opened, nil
204	}
205	
206	// SameFileState compares identity, mode, size, and modification time. Stable
207	// reads and observed-target replacement additionally compare platform change
208	// time where the operating system exposes it.
209	func SameFileState(left, right fs.FileInfo) bool {
210		return left != nil && right != nil && os.SameFile(left, right) &&
211			left.Mode() == right.Mode() && left.Size() == right.Size() && left.ModTime().Equal(right.ModTime())
212	}
213	
214	func sameStableSourceState(left, right fs.FileInfo) bool {
215		return SameFileState(left, right) && samePlatformState(left, right)
216	}
217	
218	func readAllContext(ctx context.Context, reader io.Reader, maxBytes int64) ([]byte, error) {
219		var data []byte
220		buffer := make([]byte, 64*1024)
221		for {
222			if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
223				return nil, err
224			}
225			read, err := reader.Read(buffer)
226			if read > 0 {
227				if maxBytes > 0 && int64(read) > maxBytes-int64(len(data)) {
228					return nil, fmt.Errorf("source exceeds %d bytes: %w", maxBytes, ErrFileLimit)
229				}
230				data = append(data, buffer[:read]...)
231			}
232			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
233				return data, nil
234			}
235			if err != nil {
236				return nil, err
237			}
238			if read == 0 {
239				return nil, io.ErrNoProgress
240			}
241		}
242	}
243	
244	func unsafeLink(info fs.FileInfo) bool {
245		return info != nil && (info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || isReparsePoint(info))
246	}
247

69	// CloseableTaskPanes is intentionally limited to linked task checkouts. It
70	// never offers canonical agents, callers, mixed or parent workspaces.
71	func CloseableTaskPanes(mode task.CheckoutMode, occupancy runtime.Occupancy) map[string]string {
72		eligible := make(map[string]string)
73		if mode != task.ModeWorktree || occupancy.Backend != "herdr" || occupancyObservationError(occupancy, nil) != nil {
74			return eligible
75		}
76		for _, agent := range occupancy.Agents {
77			if agent.IsCaller || (agent.Status != "idle" && agent.Status != "done") {
78				continue
79			}
80			for _, session := range occupancy.Sessions {
81				if session.Runtime.Handle != agent.SessionHandle || len(session.Mixed) > 0 || runtime.WorkspaceProtection(session.Runtime, occupancy.Target) != "" {
82					continue
83				}
84				for _, pane := range session.Panes {
85					if pane.ID != agent.Activity.PaneID || pane.Agent != agent.Activity.Agent || pane.AgentStatus != agent.Status {
86						continue
87					}
88					if pane.Process != nil && (pane.Process.State == runtime.ProcessUnknown || pane.Process.Error != "") {
89						continue
90					}
91					eligible[pane.ID] = runtime.PaneFingerprint(pane)
92				}
93			}
94		}
95		return eligible
96	}

217			Profile: runtime.OccupancyStrict, CallerWorkspaceID: o.taskflowCallerWorkspace, CallerPaneID: o.taskflowCallerPane, InspectProcesses: true,

226		delete(approved, paneID)

232	func (s *lifecycleService) completionTaskClaimError(ctx context.Context, o lifecycleObservation) error {
233		if len(o.completionRuntime.CloseTaskPanes.Entries()) == 0 {
234			return nil
235		}
236		records, diagnostics, err := s.tasks.ListRecords()
237		if err != nil || len(diagnostics) > 0 {
238			return fmt.Errorf("task inventory is incomplete; task agent panes cannot be closed")
239		}
240		for _, record := range records {
241			candidate := record.Task
242			if candidate.ID == o.task.ID {
243				continue
244			}
245			if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
246				return fmt.Errorf("task %s has invalid ownership metadata", candidate.ID)
247			}
248			if candidate.WorktreePath != "" {
249				path, err := s.canonicalPath(candidate.WorktreePath)
250				if err != nil {
251					return fmt.Errorf("task %s checkout ownership is unknown", candidate.ID)
252				}
253				if path == o.checkout {
254					return fmt.Errorf("task checkout is also claimed by task %s; preserve its panes and reconcile ownership", candidate.ID)
255				}
256			}
257			if candidate.Branch == o.task.Branch {
258				matches, complete, _ := s.taskRepositoryMatches(ctx, candidate, destructiveObservation{repoPath: o.repoPath, gitCommonDir: o.gitCommonDir})
259				if !complete || matches {
260					return fmt.Errorf("task %s also claims or may claim this branch; preserve its panes and reconcile ownership", candidate.ID)
261				}
262			}
263		}
264		return nil
265	}
266	
267	func withoutOccupancyPane(o runtime.Occupancy, paneID string) runtime.Occupancy {
268		out := o
269		out.Agents = nil
270		for _, a := range o.Agents {
271			if a.Activity.PaneID != paneID {
272				out.Agents = append(out.Agents, a)
273			}
274		}
275		out.Sessions = nil
276		for _, session := range o.Sessions {
277			session.Runtime.Panes = withoutPane(session.Runtime.Panes, paneID)
278			session.Panes = withoutPane(session.Panes, paneID)
279			session.Mixed = withoutPane(session.Mixed, paneID)
280			if len(session.Panes) > 0 {
281				out.Sessions = append(out.Sessions, session)
282			}
283		}
284		return out
285	}
286	
287	func withoutPane(panes []runtime.Pane, id string) []runtime.Pane {
288		var out []runtime.Pane
289		for _, p := range panes {
290			if p.ID != id {
291				out = append(out, p)
292			}
293		}
294		return out
295	}

21	var ErrIntentNotFound = errors.New("artifact intent not found")
22	
23	// Store keeps one strict JSON intent per finalization handoff.
24	type Store struct {
25		Dir   string
26		clock func() time.Time
27		newID func() string
28	}
29	
30	func NewStore(dir string) *Store {
31		return &Store{Dir: dir, clock: time.Now, newID: randomID}
32	}
33	
34	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".json") }
35	
36	func (s *Store) Create(ctx context.Context, intent *Intent) error {
37		if intent == nil {
38			return fmt.Errorf("create nil artifact intent")
39		}
40		return lockx.WithDir(ctx, s.Dir, "artifact intent", func() error {
41			candidate := *intent
42			if candidate.ID == "" {
43				candidate.ID = s.newID()
44			}
45			candidate.SchemaVersion = SchemaVersion
46			candidate.Status = Armed
47			now := s.clock().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
48			candidate.CreatedAt, candidate.UpdatedAt = now, now
49			if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
50				return err
51			}
52			if _, err := os.Stat(s.path(candidate.ID)); err == nil {
53				return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s already exists", candidate.ID)
54			} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
55				return err
56			}
57			if err := s.write(candidate); err != nil {
58				return err
59			}
60			*intent = candidate
61			return nil
62		})
63	}
64	
65	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Intent, error) {
66		if !idPattern.MatchString(id) {
67			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact intent id %q", id)
68		}
69		file, err := os.Open(s.path(id))
70		if err != nil {
71			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
72				return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s: %w", id, ErrIntentNotFound)
73			}
74			return nil, err
75		}
76		defer file.Close()
77		decoder := json.NewDecoder(file)
78		decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
79		var intent Intent
80		if err := decoder.Decode(&intent); err != nil {
81			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode artifact intent %s: %w", id, err)
82		}
83		if err := ensureJSONEOF(decoder); err != nil {
84			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode artifact intent %s: %w", id, err)
85		}
86		if intent.ID != id {
87			return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact intent filename %s disagrees with id %s", id, intent.ID)
88		}
89		if err := intent.Validate(); err != nil {
90			return nil, err
91		}
92		return &intent, nil
93	}
94	
95	func (s *Store) List() ([]Intent, error) {
96		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
97		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
98			return nil, nil
99		}
100		if err != nil {
101			return nil, err
102		}
103		var intents []Intent
104		for _, entry := range entries {
105			if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json") {
106				continue
107			}
108			intent, err := s.Get(strings.TrimSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json"))
109			if err != nil {
110				return nil, err
111			}
112			intents = append(intents, *intent)
113		}
114		sort.Slice(intents, func(i, j int) bool { return intents[i].CreatedAt.Before(intents[j].CreatedAt) })
115		return intents, nil
116	}

118	func (s *Store) FindByRunID(runID string) (*Intent, error) {
119		intents, err := s.List()
120		if err != nil {
121			return nil, err
122		}
123		for i := range intents {
124			if intents[i].RunID == runID {
125				return &intents[i], nil
126			}
127		}
128		return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact run %s: %w", runID, ErrIntentNotFound)
129	}
130	
131	func (s *Store) Update(ctx context.Context, id string, mutate func(*Intent) error) error {
132		if mutate == nil {
133			return fmt.Errorf("artifact update needs a mutation")
134		}
135		return lockx.WithDir(ctx, s.Dir, "artifact intent", func() error {
136			intent, err := s.Get(id)
137			if err != nil {
138				return err
139			}
140			if err := mutate(intent); err != nil {
141				return err
142			}
143			intent.UpdatedAt = s.clock().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
144			if err := intent.Validate(); err != nil {
145				return err
146			}
147			return s.write(*intent)
148		})
149	}

151	func (s *Store) write(intent Intent) error {
152		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o700); err != nil {
153			return err
154		}
155		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, ".intent-*.tmp")
156		if err != nil {
157			return err
158		}
159		name := tmp.Name()
160		defer os.Remove(name)
161		if err := tmp.Chmod(0o600); err != nil {
162			tmp.Close()
163			return err
164		}
165		encoder := json.NewEncoder(tmp)
166		encoder.SetIndent("", "  ")
167		if err := encoder.Encode(intent); err != nil {
168			tmp.Close()
169			return err
170		}
171		if err := tmp.Sync(); err != nil {
172			tmp.Close()
173			return err
174		}
175		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
176			return err
177		}
178		return os.Rename(name, s.path(intent.ID))
179	}

181	func ensureJSONEOF(decoder *json.Decoder) error {
182		var extra any
183		if err := decoder.Decode(&extra); errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
184			return nil
185		} else if err != nil {
186			return err
187		}

18	// SubmoduleNode describes one exact gitlink edge, relative to Graph.Root.
19	// Unknown is never represented as a clean initialized checkout.
20	type SubmoduleNode struct {
21		CheckoutIdentity string   `json:"checkout_identity,omitempty"`
22		GitIdentity      string   `json:"git_identity,omitempty"`
23		Path             string   `json:"path"`
24		Parent           string   `json:"parent"`
25		Name             string   `json:"name"`
26		URL              string   `json:"-"`
27		Gitlink          string   `json:"gitlink"`
28		HEAD             string   `json:"head,omitempty"`
29		Branch           string   `json:"branch,omitempty"`
30		GitDir           string   `json:"git_dir,omitempty"`
31		CommonDir        string   `json:"common_dir,omitempty"`
32		Initialized      bool     `json:"initialized"`
33		State            string   `json:"state"`
34		Status           Status   `json:"status"`
35		Ignored          int      `json:"ignored"`
36		Blockers         []string `json:"blockers,omitempty"`
37	}

39	type SubmoduleGraph struct {
40		RootIdentity string          `json:"root_identity"`
41		Root         string          `json:"root"`
42		Nodes        []SubmoduleNode `json:"submodules"`
43		Fingerprint  string          `json:"fingerprint"`
44	}

46	// SubmodulesOf never fetches and never descends across an unverified Git root.
47	func SubmodulesOf(ctx context.Context, dir string) (SubmoduleGraph, error) {
48		r, err := Discover(ctx, dir)
49		if err != nil {
50			return SubmoduleGraph{}, err
51		}
52		g := SubmoduleGraph{Root: r.Root, Nodes: []SubmoduleNode{}}
53		g.RootIdentity, err = submoduleDirectoryIdentity(r.Root)
54		if err != nil {
55			return g, err
56		}
57		seen := map[string]bool{}
58		var walk func(string, string, int) error
59		walk = func(root, parent string, depth int) error {
60			if depth > 32 || len(g.Nodes) > 1024 {
61				return errors.New("submodule graph exceeds inspection limit")
62			}
63			identity, err := Discover(ctx, root)
64			if err != nil {
65				return err
66			}
67			if !sameCanonicalPath(identity.Root, root) {
68				return fmt.Errorf("%s is not an exact submodule checkout", root)
69			}
70			if seen[identity.GitDir] {
71				return fmt.Errorf("repeated submodule Git directory %s", identity.GitDir)
72			}
73			seen[identity.GitDir] = true
74			entries, err := submoduleEntries(ctx, root)
75			if err != nil {
76				return err
77			}
78			for _, entry := range entries {
79				if err := validateSubmodulePath(root, entry.Path); err != nil {
80					return err
81				}
82				rel := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Join(parent, entry.Path))
83				child, err := pathx.CanonicalChild(root, filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(entry.Path)))
84				if err != nil {
85					return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s: %w", rel, err)
86				}
87				n := SubmoduleNode{Path: rel, Parent: parent, Name: entry.Name, URL: entry.URL, Gitlink: entry.Gitlink, State: "uninitialized"}
88				info, statErr := os.Lstat(child)
89				if statErr != nil && !os.IsNotExist(statErr) {
90					return gError(rel, statErr)
91				}
92				if statErr == nil && (!info.IsDir() || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0) {
93					return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s is not a regular directory", rel)
94				}
95				_, markerErr := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(child, ".git"))
96				if markerErr != nil && !os.IsNotExist(markerErr) {
97					return gError(rel, markerErr)
98				}
99				if os.IsNotExist(markerErr) {
100					if statErr == nil {
101						contents, err := os.ReadDir(child)
102						if err != nil {
103							return gError(rel, err)
104						}
105						if len(contents) != 0 {
106							n.State = "unknown"
107							n.Blockers = append(n.Blockers, "uninitialized directory contains files")
108						}
109					}
110					g.Nodes = append(g.Nodes, n)
111					continue
112				}
113				cr, err := Discover(ctx, child)
114				if err != nil || !sameCanonicalPath(cr.Root, child) {
115					return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s has invalid checkout identity", rel)
116				}
117				n.Initialized, n.State, n.GitDir, n.CommonDir = true, "available", cr.GitDir, cr.GitCommonDir
118				n.CheckoutIdentity, err = submoduleDirectoryIdentity(child)
119				if err != nil {
120					return err
121				}
122				n.GitIdentity, err = submoduleDirectoryIdentity(cr.GitDir)
123				if err != nil {
124					return err
125				}
126				n.HEAD, err = run(ctx, child, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
127				if err != nil {
128					return gError(rel, err)
129				}
130				raw, err := run(ctx, child, "status", "--porcelain=v2", "--branch", "--untracked-files=all", "--ignore-submodules=none", "-z")
131				if err != nil {
132					return gError(rel, err)
133				}
134				n.Status = statusFromOutput(child, raw)
135				n.Branch = n.Status.Branch
136				ignored, err := run(ctx, child, "ls-files", "--others", "--ignored", "--exclude-standard", "-z")
137				if err != nil {
138					return gError(rel, err)
139				}
140				n.Ignored = nonEmptyNULRecords(ignored)
141				if n.HEAD != n.Gitlink {
142					n.Blockers = append(n.Blockers, "HEAD differs from parent gitlink")
143				}
144				if n.Status.Dirty() {
145					n.Blockers = append(n.Blockers, "uncommitted content")
146				}
147				if n.Ignored > 0 {
148					n.Blockers = append(n.Blockers, "ignored content")
149				}
150				if operation, active, err := InProgress(child); err != nil {
151					return gError(rel, err)
152				} else if active {
153					n.Blockers = append(n.Blockers, "Git operation: "+operation)
154				}
155				if exists, err := RefState(ctx, child, "refs/stash"); err != nil {
156					return gError(rel, err)
157				} else if exists {
158					n.Blockers = append(n.Blockers, "stash requires independent preservation")
159				}
160				g.Nodes = append(g.Nodes, n)
161				if err := walk(child, rel, depth+1); err != nil {
162					return err
163				}
164			}
165			return nil
166		}
167		if err := walk(r.Root, "", 0); err != nil {
168			return g, err
169		}
170		// Include local refs and content, not only status counts: a same-count edit
171		// or newly created local branch must invalidate cleanup authority.
172		h := sha256.New()
173		h.Write([]byte(g.RootIdentity))
174		data, _ := json.Marshal(g.Nodes)
175		h.Write(data)
176		for _, n := range g.Nodes {
177			h.Write([]byte(n.URL))
178			if !n.Initialized {
179				continue
180			}
181			root := filepath.Join(g.Root, filepath.FromSlash(n.Path))
182			for _, args := range [][]string{{"for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname) %(objectname)"}, {"reflog", "show", "--all", "--format=%H"}, {"diff", "--binary", "HEAD", "--", "."}} {
183				out, err := run(ctx, root, args...)
184				if err != nil {
185					return g, err
186				}
187				h.Write([]byte(out))
188				h.Write([]byte{0})
189			}
190		}
191		g.Fingerprint = hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil))
192		return g, nil
193	}

195	func gError(path string, err error) error { return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s: %w", path, err) }
196	
197	func validateSubmodulePath(root, rel string) error {
198		if rel == "" || rel == "." || filepath.IsAbs(rel) || strings.Contains(rel, "\\") || filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Clean(rel)) != rel || strings.HasPrefix(rel, "../") {
199			return fmt.Errorf("invalid submodule path %q", rel)
200		}
201		p := root
202		for _, part := range strings.Split(rel, "/") {
203			p = filepath.Join(p, part)
204			info, err := os.Lstat(p)
205			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
206				return nil
207			}
208			if err != nil {
209				return err
210			}
211			if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
212				return fmt.Errorf("submodule path %s crosses a symlink", rel)
213			}
214		}
215		return nil
216	}
217	
218	func submoduleEntries(ctx context.Context, dir string) ([]SubmoduleNode, error) {
219		index, err := run(ctx, dir, "ls-files", "--stage", "-z")
220		if err != nil {
221			return nil, err
222		}
223		var entries []SubmoduleNode
224		for _, record := range nulLines(index) {
225			meta, path, ok := strings.Cut(record, "\t")
226			f := strings.Fields(meta)
227			if !ok || len(f) != 3 || f[0] != "160000" {
228				continue
229			}
230			if f[2] != "0" {
231				return nil, fmt.Errorf("conflicted gitlink %s", path)
232			}
233			entries = append(entries, SubmoduleNode{Path: path, Gitlink: f[1]})
234		}
235		if len(entries) == 0 {
236			return entries, nil
237		}
238		// Read the indexed .gitmodules, not a mutable working file or inherited
239		// global configuration. Names and paths are NUL-safe.
240		modules, err := run(ctx, dir, "config", "--null", "--blob", ":.gitmodules", "--get-regexp", `^submodule\..*\.(path|url)$`)
241		if err != nil {
242			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read indexed .gitmodules: %w", err)
243		}
244		paths, urls := map[string]string{}, map[string]string{}
245		for _, record := range nulLines(modules) {
246			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(record, "\n")
247			if !ok {
248				return nil, errors.New("invalid .gitmodules entry")
249			}
250			if strings.HasSuffix(key, ".path") {
251				paths[strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(key, "submodule."), ".path")] = value
252			}
253			if strings.HasSuffix(key, ".url") {
254				urls[strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(key, "submodule."), ".url")] = value
255			}
256		}
257		for i := range entries {
258			matches := 0
259			for name, path := range paths {
260				if path == entries[i].Path {
261					matches++
262					entries[i].Name = name
263					entries[i].URL = urls[name]
264				}
265			}
266			if matches != 1 || entries[i].URL == "" {
267				return nil, fmt.Errorf("gitlink %s has no unique .gitmodules mapping", entries[i].Path)
268			}
269		}
270		sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool { return entries[i].Path < entries[j].Path })
271		return entries, nil
272	}
273	
274	// InitSubmodules only materializes missing checkouts. Existing content/HEADs
275	// are never reset. Each level uses command-scoped configuration so shared
276	// superproject config is not rewritten by submodule init.
277	func InitSubmodules(ctx context.Context, dir string) (SubmoduleGraph, error) {
278		for {
279			g, err := SubmodulesOf(ctx, dir)
280			if err != nil {
281				return g, err
282			}
283			changed := false
284			for _, n := range g.Nodes {
285				if n.Initialized {
286					continue
287				}
288				if n.State != "uninitialized" {
289					return g, fmt.Errorf("submodule %s: %s", n.Path, strings.Join(n.Blockers, "; "))
290				}
291				parent := filepath.Join(g.Root, filepath.FromSlash(n.Parent))
292				url, err := resolveSubmoduleURL(ctx, parent, n.URL)
293				if err != nil {
294					return g, err
295				}
296				key := "submodule." + n.Name
297				_, err = run(ctx, parent, "-c", key+".url="+url, "-c", key+".active=true", "-c", key+".update=checkout", "submodule", "update", "--init", "--checkout", "--", relativeSubmodulePath(n))
298				if err != nil {
299					return g, fmt.Errorf("initialize submodule %s; checkout retained (retry dev submodule init)", n.Path)
300				}
301				changed = true
302			}
303			if !changed {
304				return g, nil
305			}
306		}
307	}
308	
309	func relativeSubmodulePath(n SubmoduleNode) string {
310		if n.Parent == "" {
311			return n.Path
312		}
313		return strings.TrimPrefix(n.Path, n.Parent+"/")
314	}
315	
316	func resolveSubmoduleURL(ctx context.Context, parent, url string) (string, error) {
317		if url == "" || strings.HasPrefix(url, "-") || strings.ContainsAny(url, "\x00\r\n") {
318			return "", errors.New("invalid submodule source URL")
319		}
320		if !strings.HasPrefix(url, "./") && !strings.HasPrefix(url, "../") {
321			return url, nil
322		}
323		base, err := run(ctx, parent, "remote", "get-url", "origin")
324		if err != nil {
325			return "", errors.New("relative submodule URL requires an origin remote")
326		}
327		// Git resolves relative submodule URLs against the repository URL itself.
328		for strings.HasPrefix(url, "../") {
329			url = strings.TrimPrefix(url, "../")
330			i := strings.LastIndex(strings.TrimSuffix(base, "/"), "/")
331			if i < 0 {
332				return "", errors.New("cannot resolve relative submodule URL")
333			}
334			base = base[:i]
335		}
336		return strings.TrimSuffix(base, "/") + "/" + strings.TrimPrefix(url, "./"), nil
337	}
338	
339	// SubmoduleSourceURL resolves only the declared gitlink source, not a child
340	// checkout's potentially redirected origin.
341	func SubmoduleSourceURL(ctx context.Context, parent, url string) (string, error) {
342		return resolveSubmoduleURL(ctx, parent, url)
343	}
344
