11	// Repo identifies one repository, independent of which worktree you are
12	// standing in. Two linked worktrees of the same clone share a Key.
13	type Repo struct {
14		// Root is the working-tree root of the checkout that was probed.
15		Root string
16		// GitDir is this checkout's administrative directory. A linked worktree has
17		// its own entry below the shared common directory.
18		GitDir string
19		// GitCommonDir is the shared .git directory — the same value for every
20		// worktree of a clone, which makes it the natural identity.
21		GitCommonDir string
22		// Name is the basename users recognise the repo by.
23		Name string
24		// IsLinkedWorktree reports whether Root is a linked worktree rather than
25		// the main checkout.
26		IsLinkedWorktree bool
27		// MainRoot is the main (non-linked) checkout of this clone.
28		MainRoot string
29		// Bare reports whether the main checkout is a bare repository.
30		Bare bool
31	}
32	
33	// Key is the stable identity of the clone, shared by all its worktrees.
34	func (r Repo) Key() string { return r.GitCommonDir }
35	
36	// Discover probes dir and reports the repository containing it.
37	func Discover(ctx context.Context, dir string) (Repo, error) {
38		// A single rev-parse call answers everything: batching avoids four
39		// process spawns per repo, which matters when scanning 39 of them.
40		out, err := run(ctx, dir,
41			"rev-parse",
42			"--path-format=absolute",
43			"--show-toplevel",
44			"--git-dir",
45			"--git-common-dir",
46			"--is-bare-repository",
47		)
48		if err != nil {
49			return Repo{}, err
50		}
51		f := lines(out)
52		r := Repo{}
53		// A bare repo has no toplevel, so git prints one fewer line.
54		switch len(f) {
55		case 4:
56			r.Root = f[0]
57			r.GitDir = f[1]
58			r.GitCommonDir = f[2]
59			r.Bare = f[3] == "true"
60		case 3:
61			r.GitDir = f[0]
62			r.GitCommonDir = f[1]
63			r.Bare = f[2] == "true"
64		default:
65			return Repo{}, ErrNotARepo
66		}
67	
68		// The main checkout is the parent of the common .git dir, except for a
69		// bare repo (where the common dir *is* the repo).
70		if r.Bare {
71			r.MainRoot = strings.TrimSuffix(r.GitCommonDir, string(filepath.Separator))
72		} else if r.GitDir == r.GitCommonDir {
73			// A normal checkout may use --separate-git-dir, so the common directory's
74			// parent is not necessarily the working-tree root.
75			r.MainRoot = r.Root
76		} else {
77			r.MainRoot = filepath.Dir(r.GitCommonDir)
78			// Absorbed submodules keep their repository below the superproject's
79			// modules directory. Its parent is metadata, not a checkout.
80			if configured, configErr := run(ctx, dir, "config", "--file", filepath.Join(r.GitCommonDir, "config"), "--get", "core.worktree"); configErr == nil && configured != "" {
81				if !filepath.IsAbs(configured) {
82					configured = filepath.Join(r.GitCommonDir, configured)
83				}
84				r.MainRoot = filepath.Clean(configured)
85			}
86			probe, probeErr := run(ctx, r.MainRoot, "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--show-toplevel", "--git-common-dir")
87			fields := lines(probe)
88			if probeErr != nil || len(fields) != 2 || !sameCanonicalPath(fields[1], r.GitCommonDir) {
89				return Repo{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot verify main checkout for Git common directory %s", r.GitCommonDir)
90			}
91			r.MainRoot = fields[0]
92		}
93		r.IsLinkedWorktree = r.Root != "" && r.GitDir != r.GitCommonDir
94		r.Name = filepath.Base(r.MainRoot)
95		if r.Bare {
96			// ".../foo/.bare" or ".../foo.git" should both read as "foo".
97			r.Name = strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(r.MainRoot), ".git")
98			if strings.HasPrefix(r.Name, ".") {
99				r.Name = filepath.Base(filepath.Dir(r.MainRoot))
100			}
101		}
102		return r, nil
103	}

105	// IsRepo reports whether dir is inside a git working tree, without the cost of
106	// a full Discover.
107	func IsRepo(ctx context.Context, dir string) bool {
108		_, err := run(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
109		return err == nil
110	}
111	
112	// DefaultBranch resolves the repository's default branch — origin/HEAD when the
113	// remote advertises it, else the first of main/master that exists locally.
114	// Returns "" when nothing can be determined, which callers must treat as
115	// "ask the user" rather than guessing.
116	func DefaultBranch(ctx context.Context, dir string) string {
117		if out, err := run(ctx, dir, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "refs/remotes/origin/HEAD"); err == nil {
118			if _, b, ok := strings.Cut(out, "/"); ok {
119				return b
120			}
121		}
122		for _, cand := range []string{"main", "master", "trunk", "develop"} {
123			if _, err := run(ctx, dir, "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", "refs/heads/"+cand); err == nil {
124				return cand
125			}
126		}
127		return ""
128	}
129	
130	// Remote returns the push URL of the named remote ("origin" when empty).
131	func Remote(ctx context.Context, dir, name string) string {
132		if name == "" {
133			name = "origin"
134		}
135		out, err := run(ctx, dir, "remote", "get-url", name)
136		if err != nil {
137			return ""
138		}
139		return out
140	}
141	
142	// RemoteFromConfig reads one remote URL directly from a Git common directory.
143	// It is the zero-process path used by whole-machine inventory, where spawning
144	// `git remote get-url` once per repo dominated startup. Includes and URL
145	// rewriting are deliberately not evaluated; callers that need Git's complete
146	// semantics should use Remote instead.
147	func RemoteFromConfig(commonDir, name string) string {
148		if commonDir == "" {
149			return ""
150		}
151		if name == "" {
152			name = "origin"
153		}
154		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(commonDir, "config"))
155		if err != nil {
156			return ""
157		}
158		want := `remote "` + name + `"`
159		section := ""
160		for _, raw := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
161			line := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
162			if line == "" || strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") || strings.HasPrefix(line, ";") {
163				continue
164			}
165			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "[") && strings.HasSuffix(line, "]") {
166				section = strings.TrimSpace(line[1 : len(line)-1])
167				continue
168			}
169			if section != want {
170				continue
171			}
172			key, value, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
173			if ok && strings.TrimSpace(key) == "url" {
174				return strings.Trim(strings.TrimSpace(value), `"`)
175			}
176		}
177		return ""
178	}

14	// Repo is a scratch repository under t.TempDir().

17		Root string
18	}

20	// New initialises a repository with one commit on branch "main".
21	func New(t *testing.T) *Repo {
22		t.Helper()
23		// Windows hands back an 8.3 short path (C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...) that git then
24		// reports in its long form, so canonicalize once up front.
25		tempDir := t.TempDir()
26		if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(tempDir); err == nil {
27			tempDir = resolved
28		}
29		root := filepath.Join(tempDir, "repo")
30		if err := os.MkdirAll(root, 0o755); err != nil {
31			t.Fatal(err)
32		}
33		r := &Repo{T: t, Root: root}
34		r.Git("init", "--initial-branch=main")
35		// Identity and signing are configured locally so the test never depends on
36		// (or is broken by) the developer's global git config.
37		r.Git("config", "user.email", "dev@example.test")
38		r.Git("config", "user.name", "dev test")
39		r.Git("config", "commit.gpgsign", "false")
40		// Keep line endings and symlinks byte-for-byte on every platform; the
41		// Windows CI runner defaults core.autocrlf to true.
42		r.Git("config", "core.autocrlf", "false")
43		r.Git("config", "core.symlinks", "true")
44		r.Write("README.md", "# test repo\n")
45		r.Git("add", "README.md")
46		r.Git("commit", "-m", "chore: initial commit")
47		return r
48	}
49	
50	// Git runs a git command in the repo root and fails the test on error.

53		return r.GitIn(r.Root, args...)
54	}

56	// GitIn runs a git command in an arbitrary directory (e.g. a linked worktree).
57	func (r *Repo) GitIn(dir string, args ...string) string {
58		r.T.Helper()
59		cmd := exec.Command("git", args...)
60		cmd.Dir = dir
61		cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
62			"GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL="+os.DevNull, // ignore the developer's ~/.gitconfig
63			"GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM="+os.DevNull,
64			"GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
65			"GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
66		)
67		out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
68		if err != nil {
69			r.T.Fatalf("git %s in %s: %v\n%s", strings.Join(args, " "), dir, err, out)
70		}

53		FailureCode    string    `json:"failure_code,omitempty"`
54		SessionEndedAt time.Time `json:"session_ended_at,omitempty"`
55		CreatedAt      time.Time `json:"created_at"`
56		UpdatedAt      time.Time `json:"updated_at"`
57	}

59	var (
60		idPattern      = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$`)
61		sessionPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+:[0-9a-fA-F-]{16,}$`)
62	)
63	
64	func (i Intent) Validate() error {
65		if i.Destination != "" && i.Destination != "archive" {
66			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported artifact destination")
67		}
68		if i.Destination == "archive" && (i.ArchiveStateDir == "" || i.ArchivePolicy == "") {
69			return fmt.Errorf("archive intent lacks policy/state binding")
70		}
71		switch {
72		case i.SchemaVersion != SchemaVersion:
73			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported artifact intent schema %d", i.SchemaVersion)
74		case !idPattern.MatchString(i.ID):
75			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact intent id %q", i.ID)
76		case i.RunID == "" || !idPattern.MatchString(i.RunID):
77			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact run id %q", i.RunID)
78		case i.Provider == "" || i.SessionID == "":
79			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs provider and session id")
80		case i.RepoPath == "" || i.WorktreePath == "" || i.GitCommonDir == "":
81			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs repository, worktree and git common-dir paths")
82		case i.Branch == "" || i.Head == "":
83			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs branch and head")
84		}
85		if !sessionPattern.MatchString(i.Provider + ":" + i.SessionID) {
86			return fmt.Errorf("invalid agent session %q", i.Provider+":"+i.SessionID)
87		}
88		switch i.Status {
89		case Armed, Finalizing, Finalized, Failed, Discarded:
90			return nil
91		default:
92			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact intent status %q", i.Status)
93		}
94	}
95	
96	func ParseSession(value string) (provider, sessionID string, err error) {
97		provider, sessionID, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(value), ":")
98		provider = strings.ToLower(provider)
99		if !ok || !sessionPattern.MatchString(provider+":"+sessionID) {
100			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("invalid session %q: want provider:uuid", value)
101		}
102		return provider, sessionID, nil
103	}

274	func (e *executionState) run(effect Effect, operation func() (string, error)) error {
275		step := StepResult{Effect: effect.Clone(), Status: StepAttempted, StartedAt: e.service.now()}
276		detail, err := operation()
277		step.FinishedAt = e.service.now()
278		step.Detail = detail
279		if err != nil {
280			step.Status = StepFailed
281			step.Failure = err.Error()
282			e.steps = append(e.steps, step)
283			return err
284		}
285		step.Status = StepCompleted
286		e.steps = append(e.steps, step)
287		return nil
288	}

292		if err != nil {
293			e.warnings = append(e.warnings, warningPrefix+": "+err.Error())
294		}

297	func (e *executionState) result() Result {
298		spec := ResultSpec{
299			Steps: e.steps, Warnings: e.warnings, Recovery: e.recovery,
300			PartialSuccess: e.partial,
301			Milestone:      e.milestone, Handoff: e.handoff, Remote: e.remote, FreshSnapshotRef: e.snapshot,
302		}
303		for _, step := range e.steps {
304			if step.Status == StepCompleted {
305				spec.PartialSuccess = true
306				break
307			}
308		}
309		if len(e.steps) > 0 && e.steps[len(e.steps)-1].Status == StepCompleted &&
310			(e.snapshot != "" || e.remote != nil) && len(e.recovery) == 0 {
311			// Successful completion is not partial merely because it had effects.
312			// Remote refresh is intentionally run-local and therefore completes with
313			// structured data rather than a persisted snapshot reference.
314			spec.PartialSuccess = false
315		}
316		return NewResult(spec)
317	}

21	var ErrIntentNotFound = errors.New("artifact intent not found")
22	
23	// Store keeps one strict JSON intent per finalization handoff.
24	type Store struct {
25		Dir   string
26		clock func() time.Time
27		newID func() string
28	}
29	
30	func NewStore(dir string) *Store {
31		return &Store{Dir: dir, clock: time.Now, newID: randomID}
32	}
33	
34	func (s *Store) path(id string) string { return filepath.Join(s.Dir, id+".json") }
35	
36	func (s *Store) Create(ctx context.Context, intent *Intent) error {
37		if intent == nil {
38			return fmt.Errorf("create nil artifact intent")
39		}
40		return lockx.WithDir(ctx, s.Dir, "artifact intent", func() error {
41			candidate := *intent
42			if candidate.ID == "" {
43				candidate.ID = s.newID()
44			}
45			candidate.SchemaVersion = SchemaVersion
46			candidate.Status = Armed
47			now := s.clock().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
48			candidate.CreatedAt, candidate.UpdatedAt = now, now
49			if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
50				return err
51			}
52			if _, err := os.Stat(s.path(candidate.ID)); err == nil {
53				return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s already exists", candidate.ID)
54			} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
55				return err
56			}
57			if err := s.write(candidate); err != nil {
58				return err
59			}
60			*intent = candidate
61			return nil
62		})
63	}
64	
65	func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Intent, error) {
66		if !idPattern.MatchString(id) {
67			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact intent id %q", id)
68		}
69		file, err := os.Open(s.path(id))
70		if err != nil {
71			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
72				return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s: %w", id, ErrIntentNotFound)
73			}
74			return nil, err
75		}
76		defer file.Close()
77		decoder := json.NewDecoder(file)
78		decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
79		var intent Intent
80		if err := decoder.Decode(&intent); err != nil {
81			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode artifact intent %s: %w", id, err)
82		}
83		if err := ensureJSONEOF(decoder); err != nil {
84			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode artifact intent %s: %w", id, err)
85		}
86		if intent.ID != id {
87			return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact intent filename %s disagrees with id %s", id, intent.ID)
88		}
89		if err := intent.Validate(); err != nil {
90			return nil, err
91		}
92		return &intent, nil
93	}
94	
95	func (s *Store) List() ([]Intent, error) {
96		entries, err := os.ReadDir(s.Dir)
97		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
98			return nil, nil
99		}
100		if err != nil {
101			return nil, err
102		}
103		var intents []Intent
104		for _, entry := range entries {
105			if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json") {
106				continue
107			}
108			intent, err := s.Get(strings.TrimSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json"))
109			if err != nil {
110				return nil, err
111			}
112			intents = append(intents, *intent)
113		}
114		sort.Slice(intents, func(i, j int) bool { return intents[i].CreatedAt.Before(intents[j].CreatedAt) })
115		return intents, nil
116	}
117	
118	func (s *Store) FindByRunID(runID string) (*Intent, error) {
119		intents, err := s.List()
120		if err != nil {
121			return nil, err
122		}
123		for i := range intents {
124			if intents[i].RunID == runID {
125				return &intents[i], nil
126			}
127		}
128		return nil, fmt.Errorf("artifact run %s: %w", runID, ErrIntentNotFound)
129	}
130	
131	func (s *Store) Update(ctx context.Context, id string, mutate func(*Intent) error) error {
132		if mutate == nil {
133			return fmt.Errorf("artifact update needs a mutation")
134		}
135		return lockx.WithDir(ctx, s.Dir, "artifact intent", func() error {
136			intent, err := s.Get(id)
137			if err != nil {
138				return err
139			}
140			if err := mutate(intent); err != nil {
141				return err
142			}
143			intent.UpdatedAt = s.clock().UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
144			if err := intent.Validate(); err != nil {
145				return err
146			}
147			return s.write(*intent)
148		})
149	}
150	
151	func (s *Store) write(intent Intent) error {
152		if err := os.MkdirAll(s.Dir, 0o700); err != nil {
153			return err
154		}
155		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(s.Dir, ".intent-*.tmp")
156		if err != nil {
157			return err
158		}
159		name := tmp.Name()
160		defer os.Remove(name)
161		if err := tmp.Chmod(0o600); err != nil {
162			tmp.Close()
163			return err
164		}
165		encoder := json.NewEncoder(tmp)
166		encoder.SetIndent("", "  ")
167		if err := encoder.Encode(intent); err != nil {
168			tmp.Close()
169			return err
170		}
171		if err := tmp.Sync(); err != nil {
172			tmp.Close()
173			return err
174		}
175		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
176			return err
177		}
178		return os.Rename(name, s.path(intent.ID))
179	}
180	
181	func ensureJSONEOF(decoder *json.Decoder) error {
182		var extra any
183		if err := decoder.Decode(&extra); errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
184			return nil
185		} else if err != nil {
186			return err
187		}
188		return fmt.Errorf("multiple JSON values")
189	}
190	
191	func randomID() string {
192		var raw [12]byte
193		if _, err := rand.Read(raw[:]); err != nil {
194			return fmt.Sprintf("intent-%d", time.Now().UnixNano())
195		}
196		return "intent-" + hex.EncodeToString(raw[:])
197	}
198
```

7	## Toolchain and commands
8	
9	- Go 1.26.4 (from `go.mod`) builds the CLI. Python 3.11+ and `uv` are used only for the documentation site.
10	- `make` / `make all` runs `fmt -> vet -> test -> build`. `make fmt` runs `gofmt -w .` and therefore modifies files.
11	- There is no working `make lint` recipe even though `lint` appears in `.PHONY`. The repository's static gates are formatting and `go vet`.
12	
13	```bash
14	make build                         # build ./dev with git-derived version metadata
15	make test                          # go test ./...
16	go test -race -timeout 20m ./...   # CI test command
17	go test ./internal/gitx -run '^TestAddWorktreeUsesExplicitBase$'  # one test
18	go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestName/Subtest$'                  # one subtest
19	make vet                           # go vet ./...
20	files="$(gofmt -l .)" && test -z "$files"  # format check that preserves gofmt failures
21	make e2e                           # real CLI lifecycle in an isolated temporary HOME
22	make skill-sync                    # regenerate command docs, then rebuild embedded skill
23	make skill-check                   # fail when command tree and generated skill reference drift
24	make install                       # binary under PREFIX; skill in user agent directories
25	```
26	
27	Documentation uses the same sequence as CI:
28	
29	```bash
30	uv sync --frozen --extra docs
31	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source
32	uv run mkdocs build --strict
33	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --site site
34	```
35	
36	If generated `docs/llms*.txt` files drift, regenerate them with `uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source --generate-llms` and then rerun the documentation checks.

38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `submodule` owns versioned workspace-member intent and reversible child-clone disposal mechanisms. `gitx` supplies the local gitlink graph; `taskflow` owns recursive lifecycle policy and fresh remote-proof ordering. Gitlink checkouts are legitimate submodules, not nested managed linked worktrees.
56	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints. Lifecycle callers use exact-record revisions and locked compare-and-update/delete transactions rather than treating a previously read task as current.
57	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
58	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
59	- `taskflow` is the UI-agnostic lifecycle authority: it separates recorded intent, typed live observations, immutable guarded plans, approvals, and partial result ledgers. Apply locks and reloads task/Git/worktree/runtime/artifact/remote identity, then rejects stale authority before mutation.
60	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, all registered worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and UI projections consume this joined view.
61	- `agentinterop` owns explicit MCP/skill/instruction transfer plans, guarded apply, stanza/link ownership, private recovery, and optional recipes. Native agent files and skills locks remain authoritative; only explicit preparation/check/launch paths may execute a provider or MCP server. Recovery belongs outside Git, credentials remain runtime references, and native Windows writes fail closed pending verified ACL/identity support.
62	- `triage` owns read-only cross-repository findings, clone-bound local intent, ignored-directory policy and reviewed batch ledgers; `triagetui` is its independent UI. Synchronization uses taskflow plans, and protected cleanup adds guards inside the existing repository lock and immediately before removal. Local scans never reconcile Try catalog entries.
63	- `flowtui` is an independent Bubble Tea model for the preview `dev flow` repository state-machine UI. It receives repository reads and taskflow Plan/Apply callbacks; do not embed it in or add a mode to the dashboard's `tui` model.
64	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
65	- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
66	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
67	- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage`, note FTS, and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
68	- `agenthistory` owns explicit transcript/file retention policy, immutable source-bound archive copies, Git lookup/sync and isolated history migration. Archive bindings/recovery stay in private state, ordinary status never contacts remotes, and source writers/index bytes remain untouched by archiving. `artifact` keeps old commit handoffs and adds externally verified archive receipts; taskflow includes ignored capture readiness in its guarded authority.
69	- `hygiene` owns configurable secret/privacy policy, index/worktree/frozen-history scans, private identity rules and signed replacement plans. Raw findings/recovery stay outside Git; hook setup preserves foreign hooks. Large text transactions explicitly opt into configedit’s Windows backend; existing configuration flows retain their platform contracts.
70	- `feedback` owns durable private reports, sanitized public drafts, revision-bound issue/comment publication receipts and exact repair plans. CLI adapts its repair backend to the shared start flow; agent launch is explicit and prompt context never becomes a public issue body.
71	- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.
72	- `sshhost` owns bounded static discovery of the active user OpenSSH Include closure, canonical files under `~/.ssh/dev.d`, public-key selection/generation/bootstrap, fresh authentication proofs, and the explicit handoff into dev fleet. OpenSSH and plain `ssh -G` remain semantic authority; ordinary setup/remove never rewrite foreign connection definitions, copy private keys, weaken host-key policy, or treat every alias as a fleet member. Explicit format/organize may transform selected user-owned configuration with private guarded recovery; Include restores its caller scope after each file. Named agent providers (Bitwarden, 1Password, Secretive, custom sockets) are located by stat only and never executed; selecting a named-agent key publishes only its public line and writes a v2 fragment (`IdentityAgent`, `SecurityKeyProvider`), which older binaries treat as not dev-owned, while v1 files stay byte-identical. Explicit FIDO generation binds the reviewed native tools/provider, keeps capability observations stat-only, and reports hardware created/unknown effects independently of local publication; only verified SK recovery pairs may be retained. Never use resident-key download or provider loading as a passive probe, and keep automatic Secure Enclave creation blocked until exact native identity mapping is verified.
73	- `sshflow` owns the explicit SSH/fleet/Herdr machine inventory and Plan/Apply orchestration; `herdrremote` calls the native machine CLI without writing its catalog. `configedit` owns source-bound local file transactions and private recovery outside Git, with owner leases and macOS/Linux metadata checks.
74	- `machineregistry` owns controller-local canonical machine UUIDs, scoped provider bindings, explicit unlink suppression and merge redirects in durable private SQLite. These UUIDs never replace the remote `fleet.machine_id` trust pin. `sshdiscovery` owns optional explicit Tailscale status and bounded on-link LAN observations; discovery caches are disposable and never create machine identities or prove authentication. `sshflow` joins these sources while retaining every distinct SSH connection profile; the dashboard SSH view is an adapter to the same services.
75	- `sshactivity` owns private durable per-profile usage and test observations. Usage records actual local dev-mediated SSH process starts; network/full tests never update usage. Observations retain source fingerprints and cannot authorize mutations or imply present connectivity.
76	- `tuiissue` owns typed problem guidance and reviewed native dependency installation recipes. UI actions use finite IDs and exact guarded service callbacks, never executable error text.
77	- `selfupdate` selects exact release platform assets and stages native Go source builds when an asset is absent, preferring the checksummed compact source archive over legacy Go module source. CLI owns confirmation and executable replacement; download/checksum failures never authorize a source fallback, and failed builds retain the installed binary.
78	- `platformfs` owns the native Android Termux home anchor, inherited app-data SELinux/encryption metadata recognition and no-replace publication. It also recognizes macOS kernel-managed provenance: observe it for same-file stale detection, but never restore or require it on a replacement. Verify the exact system/app prefix and all user-controlled descendants; never trust arbitrary UID-1000 directories, relabel files, chmod Android system paths or substitute an overwriting rename.
79	- `sshremote` owns strict bounded v1 SSH capability/inventory/resolve/key/connect protocols and private disposable source/route caches. Only explicit capability may initialize remote dev identity. Static inventory never evaluates SSH or agents; source profiles are scoped by observed UUID, user, root and alias. Local imports preserve native controller trust/authentication context, while remote connect reselects remote-local keys and never retries a started session.
80	- `sshcredential` owns per-context operation secrets, guarded ask/never metadata and exact provider references. System stores and explicitly selected Bitwarden contain saved passwords; the TOML ledger never does. Source-bound authentication evidence authorizes an optional save prompt, not arbitrary askpass, MFA or host-key text. Unknown provider writes stay unknown and are not retried automatically.
81	- `sshvault` owns explicit new vault-key creation, service-bound single-attempt plans, exact public receipts, and native account/profile execution context. It never imports existing private keys or writes new private material to files. Experimental Bitwarden memory creation and delegation to a native profile need separate approvals; freeze the actual environment/cwd and revalidate session/profile/tool identity without exposing session values or hashes. A session or base URL is not endpoint identity: native-context consistency and endpoint-unverified status remain separate from creation and agent visibility. Native no-interaction must prevent private JSON stdin from becoming a credential response; ambiguous writes retain receipts and never auto-retry/delete. Live vault/hardware checks remain separately consented.
82	
83	- `fleetnav` owns contextual host/repository navigation ordering, explicit Herdr profile/session selection and partial results. Repository checks precede profile changes; preparation uses a distinct versioned helper and session-scoped runtime with no focus or attach. Inside Herdr, navigation reports a native sidebar target; outside it attaches to the explicit session. Failures never implicitly switch to SSH.
84	- `fleet` merges the user-authored primary `remotes.toml` with strict dev-owned `remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` registrations. Remote `dev` state remains host-local. `remote_os` selects target semantics: POSIX uses the shell launcher, while Windows uses an encoded PowerShell launcher that accepts only hidden fleet helpers, preserves sync stdin, and never applies controller path rules to remote paths.
85	
86	The principal task start flow spans `internal/cli/start.go`, `start_flow.go`, `gitx`/`wt`, `runtime`, and `task`: resolve the canonical repository and explicit base, create or select the checkout, provision/open it, then persist and annotate the task. Task-backed park/resume/completion/retirement and exact unmanaged Adopt/Remove policy belong in `taskflow`; CLI commands, the dashboard, `sweep`, and `flowtui` are adapters. Preserve report-before-apply and no-data-loss ordering, including the isolated compatibility paths that have not migrated to taskflow.
87	
88	State is split intentionally:
89	
90	- Git remotes/branches are durable code truth.
91	- Worktrees are disposable local checkouts.
92	- Runtime sessions are per-host and re-derivable.
93	- Task TOML and catalog assets hold only intent/identity that Git cannot answer.
94	- Repository quick-note Markdown is durable sidecar data; `notes.db` is only its disposable search index.
95	- `stats.db` is durable observation data; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/*` is disposable.
96	- SSH source/route caches are disposable; remote dev UUIDs, local canonical machine UUIDs and fleet trust pins are separate identities. Credential policy/reference TOML is durable intent; its provider-owned secret is not a cache. Removing a reference does not erase a vault item or revoke a remote password.
97	- The user's OpenSSH configuration is durable connection truth. Ordinary setup/remove own only the exact top-level `Include ~/.ssh/dev.d/*.conf` and structurally valid fragments in `~/.ssh/dev.d`; key bootstrap sends public material only and has no private-key transfer or remote-key revocation lifecycle.
98	- Fleet intent is the merged primary `remotes.toml` plus generated sibling `remotes.d` fragments. A generated fragment exists only after explicit `dev ssh setup --fleet` / `--to fleet|both` or `dev ssh manage --action register --to fleet|both`, and a fresh ordinary alias login; controller caches and each remote machine's paths/tasks/runtime remain re-derivable or host-local.
99	- `paths.state_dir/machines/registry.db` is durable controller-local identity and binding intent; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/ssh-discovery/` contains disposable dated Tailscale/LAN observations. Plain `dev ssh list` stays static; `--tailscale` explicitly queries the optional local CLI and `--lan` reads cached observations. Neither list nor dashboard refresh scans the LAN. The active SSH dashboard may refresh local Tailscale status when `[tui.ssh].background_refresh` is enabled; native discovery returns typed observations independently of cache writes. Candidate setup preserves source/scope provenance and per-stage retained effects.
100	
101	## Behavioral contracts
102	
103	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
104	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
105	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
106	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
107	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
108	- Submodule initialization uses committed gitlinks, never implicitly advances to `main`. Whole child-clone disposal requires explicit recursive approval and fresh recovery proof for its private refs/objects; outer and shared canonical repositories are retained. Local graph refresh never performs remote proof. Child task/runtime/artifact claims block parent disposal.
109	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
110	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
111	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
112	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
113	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
114	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
115	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
116	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output, including `dev hygiene report --json` (`hygiene_summary` schema 1). Stored summaries are historical observations, not proof of current source bytes.
117	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
118	- Explicit SSH format/organize and fleet profile rename/remove are plan-first exceptions for user-selected files; retain comments, Include order, original metadata and private recovery. Never activate dormant files with a new broad Include. Herdr machine add may prepare/start a remote server; leave native approvals native, and remove/disable never stops remote sessions.
119	- SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. Full bootstrap requires an explicit existing key or explicit generation, registers fleet only when explicitly selected, and reports interrupted remote installation as unknown rather than pretending to roll it back.
120	- SSH wizard permission preflight may separately review and apply metadata-only tightening on exact current-user-owned canonical/selected paths. It never recursively chmods, changes ownership, guesses ACLs, or widens permissions; completed repairs survive later cancellation. Listing and dry-run never repair permissions. Local key listing evaluates OpenSSH only behind explicit `--alias`; selected key material remains service-bound and is revalidated before configuration changes and bootstrap.
121	- `dev ssh key doctor` exposes the same permission Plan/Apply with bounded metadata-only key discovery; `--key` restricts the reviewed scope, and `--fix` requires a complete safe plan plus confirmation. Default doctor never mutates, reads private contents, or queries agents/remotes. Batch repairs revalidate the whole reviewed union and retain successful tightening on partial failure.
122	- Source-aware SSH setup can use `--auth existing` without installing a key, and registers only explicitly selected `--to fleet|herdr|both` destinations. Tailscale SSH advertisement is advisory; its port-22 endpoint is not an authorized_keys bootstrap target. Preserve the key-authentication guard and never treat Tailscale policy login as proof that a selected public key worked. Names, ports and cached observations never authorize machine merges; binding/source changes invalidate reviewed plans.
123	- Fleet-source SSH discovery selects explicit hosts without recursive fleet traversal. Local ProxyJump imports never copy remote identity/agent/trust paths; cached route data cannot authorize apply. `connect --on` is one interactive fixed-helper session with no agent forwarding or arbitrary command payload. Normal SSH errors retain child exit status.
124	- Controller password brokerage uses a private per-operation Unix socket or protected Windows pipe, never password argv/environment/files. Exact host/user/port/route contexts gate replies and save evidence. Remote source-to-target credentials remain outside this feature; native key/passphrase interaction is separate.
125	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
126	
127	## Versioning and changelog
128	
129	The current published baseline is `v0.2.38` (2026-09-15). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
130	
131	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
132	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
133	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
134	
135	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
136	
137	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
138	
139	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
140	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
141	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
142	
143	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
144	
145	For a release:
146	
147	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
148	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
149	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
150	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
151	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
152	
153	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
154	
155	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
156	
157	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
158	
159	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
160	
161	| Change | Required synchronization |
162	|---|---|
163	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
164	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
165	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
166	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
167	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
168	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
169	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
170	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
171	
172	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
173	
174	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
175	
176	## Hygiene and skill batch operations
177	
178	`internal/hygiene` owns per-repository setup plans and batch ledgers. REPOS and
179	`hygiene manage` are adapters; JSON batch management previews only. Keep legacy
180	artifact finalizers until their independent lifecycle is replaced. Cached machine
181	privacy imports use only bounded local cache readers and revalidate their source.
182	`internal/agentskill` owns selected-removal policy: exact native names/agent scopes
183	or bundled manifests, source/ownership/dependency proof and postconditions under
184	the provider lease. Never infer complete Windows validation from an advisory
185	step's success conclusion; inspect logs and require the dedicated native gates.
186	
187	## Agent history policy
188	
189	`dev help ai-artifacts` separates source retention, archive location, protection
190	and distribution. New configuration is opt-in. Sources are SpecStory Markdown or
191	explicit files; provider IDs name the originating agent. Do not infer writer exit
192	from byte stability or close agents to finalize evidence. Archive mode verifies
193	ignored bytes before cleanup; existing tracked intents retain their original lane.
194	`git-filter-repo` only operates on new verified copies. Ordinary migration never
195	rewrites source refs or published tags, and raw backups are not secret audits.

10	func submoduleDirectoryIdentity(path string) (string, error) {
11		p, err := windows.UTF16PtrFromString(path)
12		if err != nil {
13			return "", err
14		}
15		h, err := windows.CreateFile(p, windows.FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES, windows.FILE_SHARE_READ|windows.FILE_SHARE_WRITE|windows.FILE_SHARE_DELETE, nil, windows.OPEN_EXISTING, windows.FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS|windows.FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, 0)
16		if err != nil {
17			return "", err
18		}
19		defer windows.CloseHandle(h)
20		var info windows.ByHandleFileInformation
21		if err := windows.GetFileInformationByHandle(h, &info); err != nil {
22			return "", err
23		}
24		if info.FileAttributes&windows.FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT != 0 || info.FileAttributes&windows.FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY == 0 {
25			return "", fmt.Errorf("unsafe submodule directory %s", path)
26		}
27		return fmt.Sprintf("%d:%d:%d", info.VolumeSerialNumber, info.FileIndexHigh, info.FileIndexLow), nil
28	}

41	// Canonical returns an absolute, clean path with symlinks resolved. If the final
42	// path does not exist yet, it resolves the nearest existing ancestor and then
43	// appends the missing suffix. This is the form needed to validate a destination
44	// before creating or moving anything into it.
45	func Canonical(path string) (string, error) {
46		if path == "" {
47			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonical path: empty path")
48		}
49		absolute, err := filepath.Abs(path)
50		if err != nil {
51			return "", fmt.Errorf("make %q absolute: %w", path, err)
52		}
53		absolute = filepath.Clean(absolute)
54	
55		probe := absolute
56		var missing []string
57		for {
58			resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(probe)
59			if err == nil {
60				slices.Reverse(missing)
61				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
62				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
63			}
64			if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
65				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: %w", path, err)
66			}
67			// EvalSymlinks reports ErrNotExist both for a genuinely missing component
68			// and for a symlink whose target is missing. Treating the latter as an
69			// ordinary lexical suffix would make an escape look as though it remained
70			// below its root. Resolve the link target explicitly before appending the
71			// still-missing suffix.
72			if info, lstatErr := os.Lstat(probe); lstatErr == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
73				target, readErr := os.Readlink(probe)
74				if readErr != nil {
75					return "", fmt.Errorf("read unresolved symlink %q: %w", probe, readErr)
76				}
77				if hasParentTraversal(target) {
78					return "", fmt.Errorf("unresolved symlink %q target %q: %w", probe, target, ErrTraversal)
79				}
80				if !filepath.IsAbs(target) {
81					target = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(probe), target)
82				}
83				resolved, resolveErr := Canonical(target)
84				if resolveErr != nil {
85					return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve target of %q: %w", probe, resolveErr)
86				}
87				slices.Reverse(missing)
88				parts := append([]string{resolved}, missing...)
89				return filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(parts...)), nil
90			} else if lstatErr != nil && !errors.Is(lstatErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
91				return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect unresolved path %q: %w", probe, lstatErr)
92			}
93			parent := filepath.Dir(probe)
94			if parent == probe {
95				return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve %q: no existing ancestor: %w", path, err)
96			}
97			missing = append(missing, filepath.Base(probe))
98			probe = parent
99		}
100	}

102	// CanonicalChild returns candidate in canonical form when it resolves strictly
103	// below root. It rejects root itself, lexical .. traversal, sibling-prefix
104	// confusion, and paths that escape through a symlink.
105	func CanonicalChild(root, candidate string) (string, error) {
106		if hasParentTraversal(candidate) {
107			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrTraversal)
108		}
109		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
110		if err != nil {
111			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize root: %w", err)
112		}
113		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
114		if err != nil {
115			return "", fmt.Errorf("canonicalize candidate: %w", err)
116		}
117	
118		rel, err := filepath.Rel(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
119		if err != nil {
120			// Rel only fails when the two paths cannot be expressed relative to one
121			// another — most often different Windows volumes. That is a definitive
122			// "not below root", not a filesystem error to surface.
123			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
124		}
125		switch {
126		case rel == ".":
127			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q: %w", candidate, ErrRoot)
128		case filepath.IsAbs(rel), rel == "..", strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)):
129			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is not below %q: %w", candidate, root, ErrOutsideRoot)
130		default:
131			return canonicalCandidate, nil
132		}
133	}
134	
135	// IsChild reports whether candidate resolves strictly below root. Policy
136	// rejections are returned as false without hiding filesystem errors.
137	func IsChild(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
138		_, err := CanonicalChild(root, candidate)
139		if err == nil {
140			return true, nil
141		}
142		if errors.Is(err, ErrOutsideRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrRoot) || errors.Is(err, ErrTraversal) {
143			return false, nil
144		}
145		return false, err
146	}
147	
148	// Contains reports whether candidate is root itself or resolves below it.
149	func Contains(root, candidate string) (bool, error) {
150		canonicalRoot, err := Canonical(root)
151		if err != nil {
152			return false, err
153		}
154		canonicalCandidate, err := Canonical(candidate)
155		if err != nil {
156			return false, err
157		}
158		if canonicalRoot == canonicalCandidate {
159			return true, nil
160		}
161		return IsChild(canonicalRoot, canonicalCandidate)
162	}

164	// ValidateComponent requires a non-empty relative value containing exactly one
165	// path component. Both slash styles are rejected so state synced between Unix
166	// and Windows cannot acquire a different meaning on another host.
167	func ValidateComponent(component string) error {
168		switch {
169		case strings.TrimSpace(component) == "":
170			return fmt.Errorf("empty component: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
171		case strings.ContainsRune(component, '\x00'):
172			return fmt.Errorf("component contains NUL: %w", ErrInvalidComponent)
173		case component == "." || component == "..":
174			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is reserved: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
175		case filepath.IsAbs(component) || filepath.VolumeName(component) != "" || driveQualified(component):
176			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is absolute or drive-qualified: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
177		case strings.ContainsAny(component, `/\\`):
178			return fmt.Errorf("component %q contains a path separator: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
179		case filepath.Clean(component) != component || filepath.Base(component) != component:
180			return fmt.Errorf("component %q is not a single clean name: %w", component, ErrInvalidComponent)
181		default:
182			return nil
183		}
184	}

Base directory for this skill: /Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dev-cli/.claude/skills/skill-author

# Skill Author

Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
once a draft exists).

## When to use this vs `skill-creator`

| Task | Use |
|---|---|
| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |

If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.

## Workflow

### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)

Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:

1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)

Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.

### 2. Scaffold

Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
```

Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):

| Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
|---|---|---|
| **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
| **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
| **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |

The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.

> **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
> but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
> available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this
> project (`--project`)?" before running the script. The script is
> non-interactive — once you've picked a scope, files land and symlinks fan
> out without further prompting.

After running, the script emits a single JSON object on stdout with
`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}` so you can chain
follow-up actions deterministically.

### 3. Author the SKILL.md

Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
that matter most:

- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
  this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
  501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
  loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
  escape hatches.

Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
happens"), not just that it exists.

### 4. Design any scripts

Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
requirements:

- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations

For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
have to set up an environment first.

### 5. Lint

Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
```

It checks three things:

1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; name is
   hyphen-case and <=64 chars; description has a "use when" trigger phrase,
   respects the 1024-char hard limit, and SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
   script).
3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).

Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.

### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator

Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
skill runs test cases and benchmarks."

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold the canonical skill dir
  (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/) and add discovery symlinks for
  non-universal agents. Auto-detects scope (LOCAL / PROJECT / GLOBAL); see
  table in step 2.
  - Scope flags (mutually exclusive): `--local` (force this repo's
    `skills/local/`), `--project` (force `<repo>/.agents/skills/`),
    `--global` (force `~/.agents/skills/`).
  - Other flags: `--vendor` (LOCAL only — `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead of
    `skills/local/`; rare, vendored skills normally come via `vendor.yaml`);
    `--root DIR` (override walk-up); `--no-symlinks` (skip the fan-out);
    `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite existing canonical dir + replace
    symlinks).
- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).
- **`scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh [PATH...]`** — YAML-parse the frontmatter of
  every `SKILL.md` under PATH (default `.`) with a real parser, and check that
  the root is a mapping with string `name` + `description`. Catches the
  breakage class `lint-skill.sh`'s awk extractor cannot see — an unquoted
  `description:` containing `": "` makes `npx skills` (and Claude Code /
  Cursor) **silently skip the skill**. `lint-skill.sh` calls this for the
  single-skill case; run it directly to sweep a whole collection.
  - Flags: `--parser auto|yq|python3|node` (`node` = the js `yaml` package,
    exactly what `npx skills` uses); `--quiet`.

## Bundled assets

Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:

- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.

## Reference files

- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.

## Gotchas

- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
  symlink with a real file.
- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
- **`description` is always-on context and has agent-specific hard limits.**
  Put concrete trigger phrases in frontmatter, but keep local skills in the
  120-500 char preferred range when possible. Treat >1024 chars as invalid:
  Codex and Cursor/spec-aligned validators can skip the skill entirely.
- **Quote any `description` containing `:`, `#`, or leading punctuation.** An
  unquoted YAML plain scalar cannot contain `": "` — `npx skills` fails with
  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings" and drops the skill
  from the picker without a non-zero exit. ` #` is worse: it parses, but YAML
  treats the rest as a comment and silently truncates your trigger string.
  Single quotes need no escaping except `'` itself. Run
  `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` to catch both; see
  `pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md` in this repo.
- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
  investing in authoring.
- **Scope auto-detect can surprise you.** `new-skill.sh` walks up looking for
  a publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
  `skills/.claude-plugin/`) *first*, then a `.git`. If you ran it from inside
  a clone of this repo while meaning to add a skill to your *other* project,
  it'll silently land in `skills/local/`. Pass `--project` or `--global`
  explicitly when intent isn't obvious, and prefer asking the user
  system-wide-vs-project-wide before running.
- **Discovery symlinks must be `../../`-relative**, not repo-root-relative —
  POSIX resolves symlink targets relative to the link's own directory. The
  script enforces this and verifies each link with `test -e <link>/SKILL.md`;
  if you ever hand-create one, see
  [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md).

## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)

Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
quantitative validation.

# dev-cli

Git owns durable code; worktrees are local checkouts; runtimes are host-local
sessions; dev records task intent.

## Discover what you need

Use `dev <command> --help` for current syntax and flags, and `dev help <topic>`
for workflow explanations. `dev --help` lists commands; `dev help` lists topics.
Prefer supported `--json` output for automation. Read the relevant command before
mutation: some actions execute immediately, while others require preview/apply.
Do not preload manuals, repeat `dev --skill`, or run diagnostics for every task.

## Preserve these boundaries

- Opening a repository needs no task. Choose direct, branch, or worktree
  deliberately; pass an explicit `--base` for branch/worktree creation. Keep
  managed worktrees outside repositories.
- `dev start` normally prepares a checkout/runtime. Agent launch is explicit.
  Parallel writers need coordinated ownership and verified launch targets.
- Completion, artifact finalization, retirement, and branch deletion are separate.
  Finalize agent artifacts after their writer stops; retire an agent checkout
  externally. A runtime's `done` state does not mean cleanup is safe.
- Unknown or cached observations, merged PRs, and command refusals do not grant
  cleanup authority. Resolve the reported conditions; do not improvise force
  removal or bypass trust checks.

## Read a reference for advanced operations

- Worktree provisioning or cross-host lifecycle: [ownership](references/worktree-ownership.md), [lifecycle](references/task-lifecycle.md).
- Parallel agent launches or prompt transports: [agents](references/parallel-agents.md), [handoffs](references/prompt-handoffs.md).
- History retention: [artifacts](references/ai-artifacts.md).
- Agent completion or cleanup batches: [retirement](references/agent-retirement.md), [triage](references/local-triage.md).
- Repository hygiene batches, scans or redaction: [hygiene](references/hygiene.md).
- Repository hooks, publication, or physical organization: [setup](references/repository-bootstrap.md), [bootstrap](references/bootstrap.md).
- SSH dashboard, diagnosis, discovery, tests/activity, keys, credentials and registration: [SSH](references/ssh-hosts.md).
- Dotfile setup, native chezmoi operations, or FLEET host actions: [dotfiles](references/dotfiles.md).
- Skill/MCP/instruction transfers, updates or removal: [transfers](references/agent-interop.md), [maintenance](references/skills-management.md).
- Recursive Git children: [submodules](references/submodules.md).

Use command help and its workflow topic for everyday operations.

## Unexpected dev failures

Read [feedback and repair](references/feedback-and-repair.md). Preserve the
original task; extra investigation, repair, subagents and publication need
explicit consent covering scope and cost.

2	description: Initialize complete submodule workspaces, select task branches, and retire child repositories before their parent.
3	authority: project

8	
9	# Submodule workspaces
10	
11	A superproject records commit IDs for its submodules. A complete workspace
12	contains the outer worktree and an independent checkout of each child repository.
13	It does not copy uncommitted work from the original checkout.
14	
15	## Add a repository as a submodule
16	
17	```bash
18	dev submodule add                           # source/path/mode wizard
19	dev submodule add owner/library libs/library --dry-run --json
20	dev submodule add owner/library libs/library --checkout=pinned --ref=v1.2.0 --yes
21	dev repo add-as-submodule owner/library libs/library --checkout=default-branch --yes
22	```
23	
24	`source` may be an exact known name, `owner/name`, or a network Git URL.
25	The picker merges known local remotes and the existing private forge cache;
26	it never refreshes providers implicitly. Ambiguous names need selection or an
27	exact URL. Local repositories supply a remote URL, not their working files or
28	local object store. Local-only sources, credential-bearing URLs and adoption of
29	existing directories are not supported. Use `dev repo remote --refresh` explicitly
30	when the cached inventory needs updating.
31	
32	The parent is the nearest checkout containing cwd, including a linked worktree
33	or a submodule; `--parent PATH` selects another exact checkout. Paths are relative
34	to that checkout's root, defaulting to the source name. A path crossing an existing
35	child repo is rejected: select that child as the parent instead. The parent must
36	have a commit and be on a branch. Existing targets/stores, symlinks, conflicts,
37	in-progress Git operations and modified `.gitmodules` block addition; unrelated
38	staged/dirty work is preserved. Filters/encodings on `.gitmodules` are unsupported.
39	
40	The wizard offers `pinned` and `default-branch`; non-interactive default is
41	`pinned`. `--ref` selects a fetched commit/tag/branch only in pinned mode;
42	otherwise the new clone's actual default branch determines the commit. Default-
43	branch mode creates a tracking branch without assuming its name is `main`.
44	Both modes stage a fixed gitlink. This is not an `update --remote` policy and
45	does not change future clone/worktree initialization or create task-member intent.
46	Use `dev submodule develop` separately when the child belongs to a managed task.
47	
48	`--submodules=recursive|none` overrides the parent's effective initialization
49	policy for the new child's descendants only. Addition stages `.gitmodules` and
50	the new gitlink, never commits, pushes, creates a runtime, or changes other
51	checkouts' shared submodule configuration. Non-interactive mutation needs a source
52	and `--yes`; `--json` never prompts. `--dry-run` neither writes nor connects and
53	marks unresolved refs as pending rather than claiming a verified commit.
54	
55	JSON includes `operation`, `parent`, `source`, relative `path`, `checkout`,
56	optional `ref`, `submodules`, `phase`, `git_dir`, optional `head`/`branch`,
57	`staged`, and optional `warnings`. Phases distinguish `planned`, `not-added`,
58	`clone-incomplete`, `cloned`, `added-unstaged`, `added`,
59	`initialization-incomplete`, and `complete`; failures exit nonzero while still
60	reporting any partial result. A failed clone/ref/staging step may retain files
61	and metadata. Inspect the exact paths, finish metadata/staging manually where
62	needed, and use `dev submodule init` inside the new child to retry missing
63	descendants. Do not rerun add over existing paths, force-delete partial clones,
64	or use the retirement-only `recover` command for an interrupted addition.
65	
66	REPOS/REMOTE `y u` copies a network clone URL; REPOS uses the selected checkout's
67	origin (or asks among remaining remotes), REMOTE uses CloneURL then SSHURL.
68	It never copies the browser URL as a substitute or fetches to resolve one.
69	
70	## Initialize and develop
71	
72	```bash
73	dev repo clone owner/dotfiles-all
74	dev start dotfiles-all --task platform-change --base main \
75	  --submodule dotfiles --submodule dotfiles-windows
76	# In the new managed worktree:
77	dev submodule status
78	dev submodule develop another/module --submodule-base another/module=origin/main
79	```
80	
81	Clone and worktree creation initialize recursively by default. Each child starts
82	at the parent's gitlink in detached HEAD; that is the reproducible starting
83	point, not an error. Selected children get the outer task's branch name at that
84	same commit. Existing branches are not overwritten or silently adopted. Direct
85	and branch-only task modes do not automatically switch child branches.
86	
87	```toml
88	[submodules]
89	init = "recursive" # or "none"
90	develop = ["dotfiles", "dotfiles-windows"]
91	```
92	
93	The global config and `.dev-cli/config.toml` support these settings. Explicit
94	flags/wizard choices override project settings, which override global settings.
95	The clone's project settings are read after acquiring the outer repository.
96	`--submodules=none` skips initialization. `--no-provision` skips dependency setup,
97	not Git initialization. No child is automatically advanced to the latest main.
98	
99	`dev submodule init --dry-run` inspects locally. Without `--dry-run`, it fills
100	missing checkouts and may contact their configured sources. It preserves existing
101	checkout HEADs and dirty content; a nonempty uninitialized directory is blocked.
102	Initialization failure retains partial results, reports a failure, and prevents
103	runtime handoff/agent dispatch. Retry initialization before continuing setup.
104	
105	## Integrate from the inside out
106	
107	For a cross-platform change, commit, integrate and push each affected child
108	first. Then stage the matching gitlinks together and commit the outer change.
109	For `dotfiles-all`, a change affecting both platforms gets one outer pointer
110	commit containing both gitlinks and matching cross-repository documentation.
111	
112	The manager verifies prerequisites; it does not automatically commit, push or
113	merge child work. Outer `--push` is not a recursive child push. Gitlink updates
114	and conflict resolution remain explicit.
115	
116	`dev status`, `dev repo context`, `dev ls --json`, and repository UI evidence
117	include submodule state. `dev submodule status --json` exposes the complete local
118	graph. Uninitialized, unavailable and failed observations never mean clean.
119	These reads do not fetch or query remotes.
120	
121	## Park and retire
122	
123	Run cleanup outside the target checkout and its runtime:
124	
125	```bash
126	dev park platform-change --cold --push --recursive
127	dev resume platform-change --fetch
128	# After the outer task has been integrated:
129	dev retire platform-change --recursive
130	dev sweep --merged-worktrees --recursive # report first
131	```
132	
133	Cold requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work, but not integration.
134	Retire additionally proves selected children are integrated into their recorded
135	base. Workspace-member intent is versioned separately from task TOML and is
136	used to reconstruct selected branches at the gitlinks when resuming.
137	
138	`--recursive` authorizes disposal of the workspace's independent child clones,
139	including private refs and objects. The outer branch stays unless separately
140	requested; canonical and shared repositories are never disposed. Omitting the
141	flag blocks parent removal when child repositories remain. `--force` cannot
142	bypass child recovery checks. `dev flow` offers explicit recursive managed and
143	unmanaged checkout actions; the done cleanup wizard asks about child disposal.
144	
145	Before mutation, each child is compared with fresh refs from its declared
146	recovery origin using an isolated fetch. A configured origin or ahead=0 alone
147	is not proof. Unpublished refs, local-only reflog/unreachable objects, stash,
148	dirty/untracked/ignored content, unfinished artifacts, other task claims,
149	runtime activity, and additional child worktrees block cleanup. Filtered/LFS
150	data, sparse/partial layouts and private Git configuration or files without a
151	complete preservation proof also block. Initialize missing children before
152	requesting a complete recursive recovery proof.
153	
154	The child origin must match its declared source. Remote failure or changing refs
155	halts cleanup. Raw Git/external writers and later remote history deletion remain
156	outside dev's cooperative locking and run-local proof guarantees.
157	
158	## Interrupted cleanup
159	
160	Children are staged from deepest to shallowest into a private temporary area on
161	the same filesystem. Empty gitlink directories remain until ordinary non-force
162	outer removal succeeds. The workflow does not use `submodule deinit` to rewrite
163	shared superproject settings.
164	
165	Each move has a synced journal. A failed outer removal restores original child
166	paths when they remain unclaimed. An interruption or reused path retains the
167	quarantine and reports its exact `journal.json`:
168	
169	```bash
170	dev submodule recover /exact/.dev-submodule-retirement-ID/journal.json --dry-run
171	dev submodule recover /exact/.dev-submodule-retirement-ID/journal.json
172	```
173	
174	Recovery restores rather than reusing an old proof to delete data. A removed
175	outer checkout can be reconstructed only when its retained branch still matches
176	the recorded commit. Reused or nonempty restore paths block restoration. Rerun
177	the ordinary recursive cleanup after recovery for a fresh plan and remote proof.
178	
179	Refresh shell integration after upgrading to use recursive post-done handoff.
180	Older wrappers reject the new recursive action instead of guessing its meaning.
181
```
