1	# AI artifacts: what to keep, archive, and ship
2	
3	Keep useful decisions, choose where transcripts live, and ship product inputs.
4	
5	## Decide by purpose
6	
7	| Material | Purpose | Usual treatment |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| Code, tests, current specs and docs | Current behavior and contracts | Maintain with the project |
10	| Reviewed plans, decisions and pitfalls | Requirements, rationale and lessons | Keep concise, with status and context |
11	| Raw transcripts, draft plans and tool output | Evidence of the development process | Choose per repository: track, archive elsewhere, or keep local |
12	| Native sessions and tool databases | Resume state, indexes or curation records | Follow each tool's backup contract |
13	
14	AI authorship alone does not determine where a file belongs. Promote useful
15	conclusions into the project's existing docs, decisions, backlog or pitfalls;
16	old transcripts are historical evidence, not current instructions. Do not ask
17	future contributors to read every exploratory conversation to understand code.
18	
19	## Four independent choices
20	
21	1. Does this material belong in the source repository's Git history?
22	2. Where is the durable copy, and how will another machine obtain it?
23	3. Should that copy be checked, redacted, or explicitly stored without scanning?
24	4. Does the material belong in a source distribution or installed product?
25	
26	A private experiment can keep raw chats in Git. A public or long-lived project
27	can keep reviewed decisions in Git and transcripts in a separate private Git
28	repository. A private destination does not itself change hygiene policy: choose
29	it explicitly. An unscanned copy is preserved evidence, not a clean scan.
30	
31	## SpecStory: capture is separate from publication
32	
33	SpecStory is the current transcript integration. The originating agent is the
34	provider, for example `codex:<uuid>` or `claude:<uuid>`; SpecStory is the recorder.
35	Its Markdown export is not the native agent session and does not guarantee resume.
36	
37	SpecStory can write per-worktree `.specstory/history/` files or use an explicit
38	`--output-dir`. Preserve project and session identity when combining histories.
39	A shared flat directory does not by itself retain project attribution. Tools
40	such as Lore have their own metadata and curation state; do not assume all of
41	their databases can be discarded and reconstructed from Markdown.
42	
43	For the existing tracked-history workflow:
44	
45	```bash
46	dev hygiene status
47	dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
48	dev prepare --session codex:<uuid>
49	# After the exact recorder has stopped, from outside its checkout:
50	dev artifact finalize --intent <id> --writer-stopped
51	```
52	
53	Preparation does not stop the writer. Never repeatedly redact a file that a
54	recorder is still rewriting from its native source. `dev hygiene redact` requires
55	an exact reviewed plan; artifact writes additionally require post-writer proof.
56	Private recovery and a stable byte snapshot do not prove that a process exited.
57	
58	The shared artifact writer guard covers hygiene redact/repair-encoding/restore/
59	manage and artifact finalize/archive/migrate. Other recognized live agents
60	covering the checkout always block, including idle/done agents. The calling
61	agent is exempt when Herdr's exact session ID (`agent_session` kind `id`, not a
62	title) differs from every target artifact's valid UUID in its actual
63	SpecStory-generated anchored preamble. Only `.specstory/history/*.md` supplies
64	this proof, not filenames or UUIDs later in the text. Plans or unprovable transcripts require global
65	`--allow-shared-checkout`: an explicit assertion of disjoint ownership after the
66	writer exits, never an automatic retry flag. Unknown caller identity needs
67	that explicit attestation. An identified caller-owned live transcript is refused
68	even with the override. Post-writer proof and source revalidation remain
69	required; restore checks the receipt's exact paths.
70	
71	If history is ignored, ordinary code commits need not scan it. An already tracked
72	file remains tracked after adding `.gitignore`: removing it from the index is a
73	separate reviewed operation. Keep or archive ignored history before deleting its
74	worktree; ignored does not mean disposable or backed up.
75	
76	## Choose and apply repository policy
77	
78	No policy means existing behavior is unchanged. `track` retains the existing
79	source-commit finalizer, `archive` preserves selected evidence in a separate Git
80	checkout, and `unmanaged` leaves retention to the user. Sources are `specstory`
81	(recorder Markdown) or `files` (explicit source-relative exports/plans).
82	
83	```bash
84	# Create the ordinary archive repository separately; configure its Git identity.
85	git init -b main /path/to/history
86	# Explicit private raw preservation; choose check or redact when wanted.
87	dev artifact setup --mode archive --source specstory --archive /path/to/history \
88	  --protection off --json
89	dev artifact setup --apply --plan <id> --yes
90	dev artifact status
91	# The same planner through repository setup:
92	dev repo setup --artifacts --mode unmanaged --json
93	```
94	
95	Setup edits only reviewed policy, local binding, ignore and export files; it
96	never untracks, commits, pushes or installs tools. `repo setup --artifacts` is
97	separate from a scaffold plan. Apply there with `--artifacts --apply --plan <id>
98	--yes`. Review and commit shared policy changes yourself.
99	
100	The shareable `.dev-cli/artifacts.toml` contains the stable project ID, retention
101	mode, source and literal paths. The archive path and protection binding stay in
102	private host state. Bind a cloned project to the desired archive on each host;
103	do not infer project identity from a folder basename or current branch.
104	
105	`--capture project` keeps normal per-worktree recorder output. `--capture external`
106	sets a checkout-specific local SpecStory output directory outside Git. It requires
107	untracked native config and enabled local Markdown export; tracked/complex config
108	requires manual review. Run setup in each new external-capture checkout. Existing
109	cloud settings and native session stores remain under SpecStory's control.
110	
111	## Preserve copies, then find them
112	
113	```bash
114	dev artifact archive --session codex:<uuid> --json
115	# Inspect the private review directory, then after the recorder exits:
116	dev artifact archive --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
117	dev artifact find --session codex:<uuid>
118	dev artifact find --commit <full-source-commit-id>
119	dev artifact find 'literal search text' --all
120	```
121	
122	For `--source files`, select exact configured paths with repeated `--file`.
123	Inventory is bounded to 10,000 files and each operation to 256 selected files;
124	current snapshots are limited to 128 MiB per file. Oversized or unsafe inputs
125	fail explicitly. Search reads committed records on the archive's current branch;
126	`--all` includes its other projects. Results contain locations and line numbers,
127	not snippets; no network, native history crawl or agent resume occurs.
128	
129	Archive commits contain ordinary snapshot files and metadata under `projects/`.
130	The metadata binds project/session, original and stored content digests and the
131	source commit. Source files and source index bytes stay untouched. The project
132	archive gets text/ident exclusions so CRLF and literal bytes survive Git; custom
133	content filters such as encryption, LFS or encoding transforms require the
134	archive's native workflow and are never silently bypassed. Existing Git hooks
135	still run. Archive access controls and off-host backups remain the operator's
136	responsibility.
137	
138	`off` saves raw input without a scanner. `check` uses enabled source-repository
139	hygiene policy. `redact` proposes replacements on the copy and checks the result
140	again. Disabled categories remain disabled; skipped is not clean. Blocking
141	reports contain safe finding IDs for the existing `dev hygiene rules allow`
142	workflow. Exact fixture exceptions need review and a reason. Snapshot scans
143	support inline gitleaks rules and useDefault, not external rule-file includes.
144	
145	Unchanged bytes reuse signed local scan evidence only when the path, policy,
146	exceptions, scanner inputs and executables match. Changed bytes or rules rescan.
147	Partial scans never pass. Review original/copy payloads privately; raw recovery,
148	reports and receipts stay under `paths.state_dir`, outside Git and cache clearing.
149	Filenames and metadata can still identify people or systems: review before sharing.
150	
151	After committing product/policy changes, `dev prepare` also supports an archive
152	policy. Off/check finalization creates the exact archive copy after writer exit.
153	For redact, preview and review `artifact archive` first, then pass its ID to
154	`artifact finalize --archive-plan <id> --writer-stopped`. Reviewed plans should
155	be committed with product changes; prepared SpecStory archive handoffs select one
156	exact transcript. Old intents keep their original destination and requirements.
157	The tracked-history finalizer still uses the compatibility skill's scripts.
158	
159	Retirement checks signed archive receipts and current ignored capture bytes.
160	New or changed evidence blocks cleanup until preserved. Local archive durability
161	is distinct from remote sync; ordinary status and readiness never query a remote.
162	
163	## Explicit Git synchronization and original backups
164	
165	```bash
166	dev artifact sync --push --json       # preview contacts the configured remote
167	dev artifact sync --apply --plan <id> --yes
168	dev artifact sync --pull --json       # separate pull preview; fast-forward only
169	
170	dev artifact migrate --mode untrack --path .specstory/history --json
171	dev artifact migrate --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
172	
173	dev artifact migrate --mode split --path .specstory/history --json
174	dev artifact migrate --apply --plan <id> --yes
175	# Optional: publish the original named refs to a separate empty destination.
176	dev artifact backup <completed-migration-id> --remote <git-url> --json
177	dev artifact backup --apply --plan <backup-plan-id> --yes
178	```
179	
180	Untrack saves original refs and selected working files, edits ignore rules and
181	removes only selected index entries. Other staged/unstaged work remains intact;
182	existing prepared handoffs must be resolved first. Untracking does not itself
183	configure future archive capture.
184	
185	Split requires git-filter-repo and complete local history. It produces verified
186	`original.bundle`, `original.git`, `history.git`, `filtered.git`, both commit maps,
187	selected working snapshots in `current/`, and a migration manifest. Every mapped
188	tree is checked against the selected-path projection. Empty commits/merge topology
189	and message bytes are retained; rewritten signatures cannot remain valid. A
190	restore clone verifies the original bundle. Neither source refs nor remotes change.
191	Raw backups are not a hygiene audit. Other worktrees' uncommitted files, reflogs,
192	unreachable objects, LFS payloads and submodule repositories are outside coverage.
193	Detached tips need a recovery ref before migration.
194	
195	Backup publication sends frozen named refs with empty-ref leases. Selected
196	uncommitted working snapshots stay in local `current/`; they are not in the Git
197	remote backup. Archive sync pins the reviewed destination and branch: push proves
198	ancestry before an exact lease, pull only fast-forwards. Resolve divergence with
199	native Git; dev does not force-overwrite or synthesize merges.
200	
201	Private operation ledgers retain partial effects, output and recovery paths.
202	After interruption inspect those paths and the remote, then prepare a new plan;
203	never blindly replay a partial operation. Original-remote cutover, release/tag
204	migration and force-with-lease publication of filtered history are separate,
205	operator-coordinated actions.
206	
207	## Distribution, untracking and history migration
208	
209	| Action | Effect | Earlier commits |
210	|---|---|---|
211	| `.gitattributes` `export-ignore` | Exclude selected paths from `git archive` source packages | Unchanged |
212	| Ignore and untrack | Stop including new versions in source commits; retain working files | Unchanged |
213	| Filter a separate repository copy | Build replacement history without selected paths | Different commit IDs in that copy |
214	
215	For example, this excludes chats from source archives while leaving them in Git:
216	
217	```gitattributes
218	/.specstory export-ignore
219	/.specstory/** export-ignore
220	```
221	
222	Verify the exported source still builds, including embedded resources. Packaging
223	systems have separate inclusion rules; an archive exclusion is not a universal
224	package filter. New rules affect new tagged snapshots, not old immutable tags.
225	
226	When an experiment becomes a maintained project, first inventory and verify a
227	recoverable original. Build and validate filtered history in a separate copy,
228	retain commit mappings, and separately coordinate remote replacement, tags,
229	releases and other clones/worktrees. A bundle covers selected Git objects/refs,
230	not automatically dirty files, LFS objects or submodule repositories.
231	
232	Sync, version control and backup are separate. A synchronized deletion is still
233	a deletion. Restoring a Markdown export is not restoring the native agent state.
234	Confirmed leaked credentials require revocation or rotation; filtering Git does
235	not revoke them or remove copies held by other people and services.
236	
237	See `dev help hygiene` for scanning and reviewed redaction, `dev help retirement`
238	for post-writer handoffs, `dev help repositories` for setup, and `dev help storage`
239	for durable data versus caches.
240

1	# Authoring patterns
2	
3	Condensed from <https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices>. Read this
4	before writing or editing a SKILL.md body.
5	
6	## Table of contents
7	
8	1. [Spending context wisely](#spending-context-wisely)
9	2. [Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility](#cross-agent-frontmatter-compatibility)
10	3. [Calibrating control](#calibrating-control)
11	4. [Gotchas sections](#gotchas-sections)
12	5. [Output templates](#output-templates)
13	6. [Checklists for multi-step workflows](#checklists-for-multi-step-workflows)
14	7. [Validation loops](#validation-loops)
15	8. [Plan-validate-execute](#plan-validate-execute)
16	9. [Bundling reusable scripts](#bundling-reusable-scripts)
17	10. [Quick checklist before commit](#quick-checklist-before-commit)
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Spending context wisely
22	
23	Every token in `SKILL.md` competes with the conversation history, the system
24	prompt, and every other active skill. Spend tokens on what the agent **wouldn't
25	know without you**:
26	
27	- Project-specific conventions (table names, repo layout, internal jargon)
28	- Domain-specific procedures with non-obvious steps
29	- Edge cases the agent will misjudge by default
30	- Specific tools/APIs to prefer (with the *why*, briefly)
31	
32	Don't spend tokens on:
33	
34	- Explaining what well-known things are (PDF, HTTP, REST, JSON)
35	- Generic "best practices" the agent already applies (handle errors, write tests)
36	- Comprehensive option enumerations — give a default and one escape hatch
37	
38	**Test:** for each paragraph, ask "would the agent get this wrong without it?"
39	If no, cut it.
40	
41	### Progressive disclosure
42	
43	Three loading levels:
44	
45	| Level | Loaded | Budget |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| Frontmatter (`name`, `description`) | always | 120-500 chars preferred, 1024 max |
48	| `SKILL.md` body | when skill triggers | <500 lines, <5000 tokens |
49	| `references/*.md`, `assets/*`, `scripts/*` | on demand | unlimited |
50	
51	If `SKILL.md` is creeping past 500 lines, move sections to `references/<topic>.md`
52	and reference them with **load conditions** ("Read X if Y happens"), not just
53	"see X for details". Conditions let the agent load on demand; bare pointers tend
54	to either get ignored or get pre-loaded out of caution.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility
59	
60	Use this as the portable baseline for coding agents that consume Agent Skills:
61	
62	- `name`: required, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens only, no leading/trailing
63	  hyphen, no `--`, <=64 characters.
64	- `description`: required, non-empty string, <=1024 characters. Include both
65	  what the skill does and concrete trigger contexts. Keep the first 60
66	  characters meaningful because `npx skills` truncates picker hints there.
67	- **Quoting**: a YAML plain (unquoted) scalar may not contain `": "`, and ` #`
68	  starts a comment. Long English descriptions hit both constantly
69	  (`"…debug a FastAPI app: choosing def vs async def"`). Wrap such values in
70	  single quotes — the whole skill is otherwise skipped at install time with
71	  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings", or installs with a
72	  silently truncated description. `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` gates this.
73	- Keep `name` and `description` as the only required frontmatter fields for
74	  portability. Agent-specific fields are allowed when needed, but isolate them
75	  intentionally: Cursor uses `disable-model-invocation`, Codex can read
76	  `agents/openai.yaml`, and some vendored skills carry upstream-only metadata.
77	
78	Description budget tiers:
79	
80	| Tier | Length | Meaning |
81	|---|---:|---|
82	| Green | 120-500 chars | Preferred for local skills: enough trigger surface without context bloat |
83	| Yellow | 501-900 chars | Valid, but context-heavy; move details to `SKILL.md` body |
84	| Orange | 901-1024 chars | Valid, but close to hard loader limits |
85	| Red | >1024 chars | Invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned validators |
86	
87	Agent notes:
88	
89	- **Codex** skips invalid `SKILL.md` files; OpenAI's validator enforces the
90	  64-char name and 1024-char description limits.
91	- **Cursor** managed `create-skill` guidance matches the same 64/1024 limits
92	  and supports `disable-model-invocation` for explicit-only skills.
93	- **Claude Code** uses descriptions for discovery and tolerates additional
94	  frontmatter in practice, but long descriptions still consume always-on
95	  context and are poor picker hints.
96	- **OpenCode** follows the Agent Skills convention and uses descriptions for
97	  invocation; stay within the portable baseline unless a target agent's docs
98	  say otherwise.
99	- **Claude.ai upload** may impose stricter UI limits. Treat that as a separate
100	  packaging target, not the default coding-agent baseline for this repo.
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Calibrating control
105	
106	Match instruction specificity to **task fragility**, not to "we should be thorough".
107	
108	### Be prescriptive when:
109	
110	- The operation is destructive or has side effects
111	- A specific sequence of steps must hold (migration, release, deploy)
112	- An external system requires exact format (API contract, parser input)
113	
114	```markdown
115	## Database migration
116	
117	Run exactly this sequence:
118	
119	    python scripts/migrate.py --verify --backup
120	
121	Do not modify the command or add flags. The `--verify` step seeds an
122	integrity check that later phases depend on.
123	```
124	
125	The trailing sentence is the trick — even when prescriptive, **explain why**.
126	Agents that understand the reason follow it more reliably than agents that just
127	see "DO NOT" in caps.
128	
129	### Give the agent freedom when:
130	
131	- Multiple valid approaches exist
132	- The output is judgment-driven (code review, refactor proposal)
133	- You'd be hand-coding policy if you wrote it all out
134	
135	```markdown
136	## Code review process
137	
138	1. Check database queries for SQL injection (use parameterized queries)
139	2. Verify auth checks on every endpoint
140	3. Look for race conditions in concurrent code paths
141	4. Confirm error messages don't leak internals
142	```
143	
144	Notice: *what to look for*, not *how to look for it*. The agent picks the
145	approach.
146	
147	### Defaults, not menus
148	
149	When several tools could work, pick one default and mention alternatives as
150	escape hatches.
151	
152	```markdown
153	Use pdfplumber for text extraction.
154	
155	For scanned PDFs requiring OCR, fall back to pdf2image with pytesseract.
156	```
157	
158	…not:
159	
160	```markdown
161	You can use pypdf, pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, or pdf2image depending on...
162	```
163	
164	### Procedures over declarations
165	
166	Teach the agent *how* to approach the class of problem, not *what* to produce
167	for one instance.
168	
169	```markdown
170	Bad — only useful for this exact query:
171	  Join `orders` to `customers` on `customer_id`, filter region='EMEA',
172	  sum `amount`.
173	
174	Good — works for any query:
175	  1. Read schema from `references/schema.yaml` to find relevant tables.
176	  2. Join via the `_id` foreign key convention.
177	  3. Apply user-requested filters as WHERE clauses.
178	  4. Aggregate numeric columns and format as a markdown table.
179	```
180	
181	Specifics still belong in the skill (output format templates, "never output
182	PII", tool-specific quirks) — but the *approach* should generalize.
183	
184	---
185	
186	## Gotchas sections
187	
188	Often the single highest-value section in a skill. **Concrete corrections to
189	mistakes the agent will make without being told.** Not generic advice.
190	
191	```markdown
192	## Gotchas
193	
194	- The `users` table uses soft deletes. Queries must include
195	  `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` or results will include deactivated accounts.
196	- The user ID is `user_id` in the database, `uid` in the auth service, and
197	  `accountId` in the billing API. All three refer to the same value.
198	- The `/health` endpoint returns 200 if the web server is up, even if the
199	  database is down. Use `/ready` to check full service health.
200	```
201	
202	Keep gotchas in `SKILL.md`, not in a separate reference. The whole point is
203	that the agent reads them **before** hitting the situation — by the time it
204	realizes it should load `references/gotchas.md`, the bug has happened.
205	
206	**Iteration tip:** every time you correct the agent during a real run, add the
207	correction here. Most skills' gotchas sections grow over weeks, not get written
208	all at once.
209	
210	---
211	
212	## Output templates
213	
214	Agents pattern-match against concrete structures more reliably than they
215	follow prose descriptions. When the output has a fixed shape, paste the shape:
216	
217	````markdown
218	## Report structure
219	
220	Use this template, adapting sections as needed:
221	
222	```markdown
223	# [Analysis Title]
224	
225	## Executive summary
226	[One paragraph]
227	
228	## Key findings
229	- Finding 1 with supporting data
230	- Finding 2 with supporting data
231	
232	## Recommendations
233	1. Specific actionable recommendation
234	2. Specific actionable recommendation
235	```
236	````
237	
238	Long templates or templates that only apply in some cases should live in
239	`assets/<name>.template` and be loaded on demand from `SKILL.md`.
240	
241	---
242	
243	## Checklists for multi-step workflows
244	
245	Make dependencies and validation gates visible:
246	
247	```markdown
248	## Form processing workflow
249	
250	Progress:
251	- [ ] 1. Analyze the form  → `scripts/analyze_form.py`
252	- [ ] 2. Create field mapping  → edit `fields.json`
253	- [ ] 3. Validate mapping  → `scripts/validate_fields.py`
254	- [ ] 4. Fill the form  → `scripts/fill_form.py`
255	- [ ] 5. Verify output  → `scripts/verify_output.py`
256	```
257	
258	The agent treats the checkboxes as state and won't skip to step 4 without
259	ticking 1-3. Dependency arrows make the wiring explicit.
260	
261	---
262	
263	## Validation loops
264	
265	For tasks where output quality is testable, instruct the agent to validate
266	and re-try, not "do your best and stop":
267	
268	```markdown
269	## Editing workflow
270	
271	1. Make your edits.
272	2. Run validation: `python scripts/validate.py output/`
273	3. If validation fails:
274	   - Read the error message.
275	   - Fix the issues.
276	   - Run validation again.
277	4. Only proceed when validation passes.
278	```
279	
280	The validator can be a script, a reference checklist, or a self-check prompt.
281	The pattern is identical: **do → validate → fix → re-validate → proceed**.
282	
283	---
284	
285	## Plan-validate-execute
286	
287	For batch or destructive operations, force the agent through an intermediate
288	**plan artifact** that gets validated before any side effects happen:
289	
290	```markdown
291	## PDF form filling
292	
293	1. Extract form fields:
294	   `python scripts/analyze_form.py input.pdf`  → `form_fields.json`
295	2. Create `field_values.json` mapping each field name to its intended value.
296	3. Validate:
297	   `python scripts/validate_fields.py form_fields.json field_values.json`
298	   (checks every field exists, types match, required fields present)
299	4. If validation fails, revise `field_values.json` and re-validate.
300	5. Fill the form:
301	   `python scripts/fill_form.py input.pdf field_values.json output.pdf`
302	```
303	
304	The magic is step 3. A validator that catches "field 'signature_date' not
305	found — available: customer_name, order_total, signature_date_signed" lets the
306	agent self-correct **before** the destructive step 5.
307	
308	This pattern eliminates an entire class of "oops, ran the wrong thing on prod"
309	failures. Use it any time the actual operation is hard to undo.
310	
311	---
312	
313	## Bundling reusable scripts
314	
315	When you iterate on a skill (with `skill-creator`), watch the agent transcripts
316	across test runs. If the agent independently reinvents the same logic each run
317	— building the same chart, parsing the same format, validating the same way —
318	that's a signal to write the script once and bundle it in `scripts/`.
319	
320	Heuristic: if you see the same ~20-line helper appearing in 2+ runs, bundle it.
321	
322	See `references/script-design.md` for **how** to design bundled scripts so an
323	agent can call them reliably.
324	
325	---
326	
327	## Quick checklist before commit
328	
329	Before considering a SKILL.md "done":
330	
331	- [ ] Description includes specific trigger contexts ("use when X, Y, Z"),
332	      not just a one-line summary
333	- [ ] Description is "pushy" but within budget: 120-500 chars preferred,
334	      <=1024 chars required
335	- [ ] First 60 description chars are useful in picker UIs
336	- [ ] Name is hyphen-case and <=64 chars
337	- [ ] SKILL.md is under 500 lines (move overflow into `references/`)
338	- [ ] Every `references/*.md` is mentioned with a load condition, not just
339	      listed at the bottom
340	- [ ] Has a `## Gotchas` section (or an honest reason it's empty)
341	- [ ] Output format, if structured, is shown as a literal template
342	- [ ] Multi-step procedures use checklists with dependencies marked
343	- [ ] Destructive operations go through plan-validate-execute or have
344	      `--dry-run` support
345	- [ ] Bundled scripts are listed under `## Available scripts` with their flags
346	- [ ] No "MUST" / "ALWAYS" / "NEVER" in caps without an accompanying *why*
347
```

2	
3	## Add a known repository
4	
5	```bash
6	dev submodule add owner/library libs/library --dry-run --json
7	dev submodule add owner/library libs/library --checkout=pinned --ref=v1.2.0 --yes --json
8	dev repo add-as-submodule owner/library libs/library --checkout=default-branch --yes
9	```
10	
11	Use the dry-run to verify the exact parent checkout, portable network source,
12	relative path and mode. Only apply the approved request. `--parent PATH` selects
13	an exact checkout; the default is the nearest repo containing cwd, not its
14	canonical or outermost checkout. Source selection combines known local remotes
15	and cached forge repositories without refreshing. Ambiguous names need an exact
16	URL or interactive selection. Local-only sources and existing targets/stores are
17	not adopted. REPOS/REMOTE `y u` copies the selected network clone URL locally.
18	
19	The wizard offers pinned/default-branch. Non-interactive default is pinned;
20	`--ref` is pinned-only, and a missing ref resolves the fresh clone's default
21	branch commit. Default-branch mode tracks the real default, not an assumed main.
22	Both stage a fixed gitlink; neither enables remote-following updates or creates
23	task-member intent. `--submodules=recursive|none` controls only new descendants.
24	Only `.gitmodules` and the new gitlink are staged; unrelated staged/dirty work
25	and other checkouts are preserved. No commit, push, task branch or runtime is
26	created. Use `develop` separately for managed task membership.
27	
28	**Gotchas:** `.gitmodules` must be absent or unchanged, including hidden index
29	edits; filters/encodings, conflicts, active Git operations, detached/unborn
30	parents and unsafe paths block addition. `--yes` is required for non-interactive
31	mutation; `--json` never prompts. A local `planned` result has no resolved HEAD.
32	An error may still return a partial result (`phase`, `git_dir`, `head`, `staged`,
33	`warnings`). Inspect retained paths and finish metadata/staging manually; for
34	`initialization-incomplete`, run `dev submodule init` inside the new child.
35	Never force-delete partial clones or replay add over them. The retirement
36	`recover` journal format does not apply to addition.
37	
38	## Initialize and develop existing gitlinks
39	
40	`dev repo clone`, clone-style `repo new`, and new linked worktrees initialize
41	recursively at committed gitlinks by default. Use `--submodules=none` to opt out;
42	`--no-provision` only skips environment provisioning. Global and project
43	`[submodules] init = "recursive"|"none"` control the default.
44	
45	Detached HEAD at a gitlink is intentional. Select development members with
46	repeatable `dev start --submodule PATH`; they get the task branch at the same
47	commit. `--submodule-base PATH=REF` records their integration target. Project
48	`submodules.develop` supplies optional default paths. Direct/branch-only modes
49	do not switch child branches. Later use `dev submodule develop PATH...` from
50	the managed worktree. Never infer permission to reset an existing child branch.
51	
52	`dev submodule init` fills missing checkouts, preserves existing ones and refuses
53	nonempty uninitialized directories. Initialization failure is not ready: retain
54	partial results, retry init, and do not launch an agent. `status --json` reports
55	the local graph without remote access; parent state never substitutes for child
56	state. Workspace-member intent is versioned separately from task TOML.
57	
58	Commit/integrate/push affected children before updating and publishing the

```text
1	# Task lifecycle
2	
3	For submodule workspaces, Cold verifies every child's remote recoverability; Retire also verifies recorded child integration. Explicit `--recursive` permits child-clone disposal before outer removal. Parent `--push` never implicitly pushes children. Read `submodules.md`; member intent is versioned separately from legacy task TOML.
4	
5	Read this when work needs to be paused, picked up on another machine, or when
6	a machine has accumulated more open sessions than anyone can hold in mind.
7	
8	## The problem
9	
10	A terminal multiplexer's sidebar is a *runtime* view: it shows what is running
11	now. When it is also the only record of what you are working on, nothing can be
12	closed, because closing it loses the thread. The sidebar grows until it stops
13	being scannable, which defeats its purpose.
14	
15	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home that is
16	not the runtime.
17	
18	## Pick a checkout mode before a lifecycle
19	
20	A task records human intent; it does not imply a worktree:
21	
22	| Command | Checkout boundary | Use when |
23	|---|---|---|
24	| `dev repo open api` | none; no task | browsing or truly ad-hoc work |
25	| `dev start api -t typo --direct` | current branch, usually main | one short tracked change |
26	| `dev start api -t small --branch-only --base main` | branch in canonical checkout | lightweight isolation, no concurrency |
27	| `dev start api -t auth --base main` | branch + linked worktree | interruption, experiment, parallel writer |
28	
29	In an interactive terminal, bare `dev start` opens the same managed flow as a
30	context-aware wizard. It prompts for repo, task, mode, branch, base and next,
31	then shows the computed checkout/runtime summary before creating anything.
32	`dev start -t <name>` remains the fast path; `--json` and non-TTY use never
33	prompt.
34	
35	With a newly created first-class Herdr worktree, `--run '<shell command>'` can
36	dispatch one reviewed command to the exact root pane. It is separate from the
37	pure `--json` contract, and `--focus` independently controls whether the caller
38	switches after dispatch.
39	
40	Direct tasks go HOT ↔ WARM and finish with plain `dev done`; they cannot go
41	COLD because the canonical checkout cannot be removed. Branch-only tasks can go
42	cold after push by switching the canonical checkout back to base. The full
43	state machine below describes the default worktree mode.
44	
45	Do not create isolation before it has a job. Equally, a new parallel worktree
46	starts from its committed base — it does not carry dirty main changes — so
47	checkpoint first when the new task depends on them.
48	
49	## The four states
50	
51	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
52	|---|---|---|---|
53	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
54	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | normally closed | back within days |
55	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
56	| ✅ `done` | merged | may still be open | MERGED; external retirement pending |
57	
58	Only the transitions between them cost anything:
59	
60	```
61	        dev start
62	            │
63	            ▼
64	         🔥 hot ── prepare/exit/finalize ──► READY
65	          │  ▲                                  │
66	   dev park│  │dev resume                       │ dev done
67	          ▼  │                                  ▼
68	        🌤 warm                             ✅ done / MERGED
69	          │  ▲                                  │
70	dev park  │  │dev resume                        │ external dev retire
71	  --cold  ▼  │  (rebuilds the worktree)          ▼
72	        ❄️ cold                              RETIRED (entry removed)
73	```
74	
75	The enforced graph is mode-aware: worktree/branch HOT or WARM can park WARM or
76	COLD; WARM/COLD resume HOT; HOT/WARM can complete or hand off review; DONE can
77	only Retire. Direct tasks omit COLD and branch integration. Review handoff is
78	state-preserving. COLD must resume before completion, and no ordinary action
79	moves DONE backward.
80	
81	### Plan it by repository
82	
83	`dev flow [repo]` is an independent preview-labelled, full-screen TUI, not a mode
84	of the dashboard. From a canonical or linked checkout it opens the canonical
85	repository and focuses that exact surface; outside Git it opens a repository
86	picker. It projects every Git-registered worktree plus task-only records such as
87	COLD/DONE tasks without a checkout.
88	
89	The UI shows three layers separately:
90	
91	1. persisted task intent: mode, HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, owner, next, branch/base, and
92	   expected checkout;
93	2. observed facts: exact worktree identity, Git status/operation/refs, runtime and
94	   agent occupancy, artifact readiness, each kept as known/unknown/error/skipped/
95	   loading rather than converting probe failure into false;
96	3. a guarded plan: availability, evidence/remediation, ordered effects, retained
97	   resources, confirmation, exact fallback, task revision, and PlanID.
98	
99	Enter creates the plan; it never applies. READY non-typed plans need `y`; typed
100	plans need the displayed token plus Enter. Apply locks and reloads the task
101	revision and exact repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact authority. If any
102	identity changed, it rejects the stale plan before a new effect. Apply itself is
103	not canceled by row movement/refresh/quit; the UI retains completed/failed steps
104	and recovery, then starts a new local read.
105	
106	The preview offers the normal managed choices but no dirty commit/discard, WIP,
107	shared-writer, ownership takeover, or unknown-runtime acknowledgement. Blocked
108	plans point to the compatible CLI fallback instead of adding a force path.
109	`r` reads local state only; `R` explicitly plans fetch, portable review query, or
110	both. Remote evidence is run-local and limited to named refs plus review
111	existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time—not checks or review decisions.
112	
113	**A machine should hold roughly three to seven hot tasks.** That is a
114	cognitive limit, not a technical one. Everything else belongs in `dev ls`.
115	
116	## Parking
117	
118	```bash
119	dev park --next "reproduce the token refresh race, then add a regression test"
120	```
121	
122	This is the move the whole design exists to make safe. It records what to do
123	next and leaves the checkout boundary exactly where it is. An external caller
124	may close an eligible runtime; when park is invoked from inside its own runtime,
125	it records WARM but deliberately leaves that runtime alive so the agent can exit
126	normally. In direct mode the boundary is the current branch; in worktree mode it
127	is the branch and linked checkout.
128	
129	`--next` is the important part. Without it, resuming means re-deriving where
130	you were from a diff, which is most of the cost of a context switch. Always
131	supply one.
132	
133	Before finishing agent work, run `dev prepare` with the exact session UUID and
134	exit normally. The post-writer finalizer—not the still-running agent—stages and
135	commits the exact transcript/plan. A settled Herdr `done` state is not evidence
136	that history, review or commits are complete.
137	
138	Useful variations:
139	
140	```bash
141	dev park --wip                    # checkpoint uncommitted work first
142	dev park --cold --push            # close session, push, remove worktree
143	dev park --keep-session           # warm only: record state, keep session
144	```
145	
146	`--cold --keep-session` is rejected because a runtime must not remain pointed at
147	a checkout that cold parking removes. A verified runtime-close failure likewise
148	stops cold cleanup before deleting the checkout; warm park reports the close
149	failure and keeps the recorded handle for reconciliation.
150	
151	## Checkpoint commits, not stashes
152	
153	`--wip` makes a `wip: checkpoint — <next>` commit rather than a `git stash`.
154	
155	A stash is invisible in the log, easy to forget, and **cannot be pushed** — so
156	it can never reach another machine. That last point is decisive: the whole
157	value of parking is that the work is recoverable from anywhere.
158	
159	Messy WIP commits on a feature branch are fine. Branch history is *construction
160	history*; the base branch's history is *product history*. They do not have to
161	match — clean the branch up at the integration boundary with an interactive
162	rebase, or squash it, and decide then.
163	
164	## Cold, and why it is safe
165	
166	Going cold removes the checkout. That feels lossy, and is not, because:
167	
168	- the branch still holds every commit;
169	- `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, so the remote holds
170	  them too;
171	- `dev resume` rebuilds the worktree from `origin/<branch>`.
172	
173	Resume rebuilds/reopens checkout and runtime state only. Persisted runtime
174	handles carry their backend name and are validated against live checkout
175	coverage; stale/missing handles reopen instead of making a task falsely HOT.
176	Production `dev` does not currently attach a Claude/Codex conversation; an agent
177	handoff must supply explicit session/launcher arguments.
178	
179	The directory is a cache. The branch is the identity. Once that is true, a
180	local filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished checkouts.
181	
182	## Moving work between machines
183	
184	The remote is the handoff boundary. Do not sync worktrees, runtime state, or
185	the multiplexer's database between machines — sync branches.
186	
187	On the machine holding the work:
188	
189	```bash
190	dev park --cold --push
191	```
192	
193	On the machine picking it up:
194	
195	```bash
196	dev resume <task> --fetch
197	```
198	
199	**One writer per branch at a time.** `dev` records an `owner` host and refuses
200	to resume a task owned by another machine without `--force`. Two machines
201	committing to one branch is the only reliable way to make this workflow produce
202	a conflict; the ownership check is what prevents it.
203	
204	If two machines genuinely need to work the same feature at once, split the
205	branch — `feat/auth-ui` and `feat/auth-api` — and integrate afterwards. That is
206	the same rule as for parallel agents: parallel writers get parallel branches.
207	
208	The task registry itself (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/`) is one small TOML file
209	per task, specifically so it can live in a private git repo and merge cleanly
210	across machines. Point `paths.state_dir` at one if you want a shared view.
211	
212	## Sweeping
213	
214	```bash
215	dev sweep            # report only
216	dev sweep --apply    # act, confirming each change
217	dev sweep --merged-worktrees  # from main, include untracked contained worktrees
218	```
219	
220	`sweep` reports two kinds of problem:
221	
222	- **Drift** — a task marked hot with no live session, a warm task with one, a
223	  recorded worktree git no longer knows about, or a branch-backed task whose
224	  branch git no longer has. That last one is dead rather than drifted: `done`,
225	  `resume` and `retire` all resolve the branch first, so the record is offered
226	  for reaping instead of repair.
227	- **Staleness** — a warm task nobody has touched in two weeks, clean and
228	  pushed, that could go cold.
229	
230	It also lists **live sessions no task claims** — the other half of a crowded
231	sidebar, and usually the larger half.
232	
233	From the canonical default-branch checkout, `--merged-worktrees` switches to a
234	focused audit of tracked and unmanaged linked worktrees whose named branches are
235	already contained in main. It suppresses unrelated stale-task/session noise so
236	the result can be presented directly for cleanup approval. Dirty trees, active
237	Git operations, pending artifact
238	intents, active/mixed runtimes, detached heads and unmerged branches are
239	reported as blockers. Safe candidates still require `--apply` and individual
240	confirmation; `--delete-branches` is a separate opt-in.
241	
242	`dev sweep --base <ref>` also forwards the selected base to DONE task retirement;
243	`--merged-worktrees` uses its verified base for managed tasks as well as unmanaged
244	checkouts. Reviewed retire/remove plans bind worktree-list authority only to the
245	same branch or paths equal to, containing, or nested under the target. Removing
246	an unrelated sibling no longer invalidates the rest of an approved
247	`--apply --yes` batch. A same-branch checkout or target lock/HEAD change still
248	makes the plan stale; containment and all other guards remain required.
249	
250	Agent workflow: show the report to the user as a concrete QA prompt, naming the
251	exact candidate paths and whether branches would be retained. Only after the
252	user approves that set may the agent add `--apply --yes`.
253	
254	`sweep` never deletes uncommitted work, and never acts without `--apply`. DONE
255	tasks with runtime/worktree resources are reported as cleanup pending and routed
256	through the same external-only retirement safety service; their records are not
257	reaped first.
258	
259	The dashboard does not silently reconcile these states. A normal COLD worktree
260	task points to explicit `dev resume`. A task whose recorded worktree is missing
261	or no longer registered points to `dev sweep`; generic Enter refuses to open
262	either the canonical checkout or an artifact-only directory. If sweep reports
263	unique agent artifacts, salvage them before approving a resume/reap action.
264	
265	## Integration
266	
267	```bash
268	dev done --ff     # rebase onto the base, then fast-forward it
269	dev done --pr     # push and open a pull/merge request via the detected forge CLI
270	dev done          # TTY: inspect commits/dirty content and choose interactively
271	```
272	
273	Which one depends on a single question: **are this branch's commits worth
274	keeping in the base's history?**
275	
276	- Yes → `--ff`. Linear history, no merge commit, `git bisect` and `git blame`
277	  stay legible.
278	- No, it is WIP noise → squash at the integration point.
279	- Someone (or CI) should look first → `--pr`.
280	
281	On a TTY, `dev done` reports branch ahead/behind plus which staged, unstaged and
282	untracked paths are already equivalent to the base. It can commit all changes,
283	discard all changes, or cancel before choosing FF/PR. Unique content requires
284	typing `DROP`; scripts use `--dirty=commit --message ...` or the deliberately
285	destructive `--dirty=discard --yes`. Ignored files are never discarded. If an
286	active writer changes the checkout during confirmation or immediately after a
287	commit, integration stops and the command must be rerun after that writer exits.
288	
289	After a bare interactive managed-worktree completion reaches MERGED, the
290	wizard previews covering runtime panes and agents. It can keep everything,
291	retire while preserving the branch, or retire and delete the contained branch.
292	Caller-owned Herdr workspaces are handed to a freshly created external
293	coordinator; unknown status needs explicit approval and active/mixed sessions
294	remain blockers.
295	
296	Before integration, the TTY wizard can select exact idle/done task-worktree
297	agent panes for closure only under the final guarded Apply. Parent/canonical
298	agents remain open and block FF; recheck, choose PR, or cancel. Foreground
299	non-agent programs require separate consent to changing files while they run.
300	Interactive retirement separately requires `CLOSE <workspace-id>` to terminate
301	known programs. Background jobs are unobserved. See `agent-retirement.md`. If FF is blocked by dirty
302	canonical-checkout bytes, it lists the paths and offers PR, typed `DROP`
303	discard, exact stash+restore, or cancel. Agent artifacts are labeled.
304	Stash+restore preserves staged, unstaged, and non-ignored untracked state under
305	an exact OID, restores the index/worktree after fast-forward, and drops only
306	that matching stash entry. A conflict retains the stash and task with an exact
307	recovery command. Dirty submodules and nested repositories remain blockers.
308	The discard is a separate explicit taskflow effect and no unrelated canonical
309	bytes are committed automatically.
310	
311	For branch/worktree tasks, non-interactive `dev done` without an integration
312	mode remains report-only. Direct tasks still finish without one. Conflicted
313	checkouts always require manual resolution.
314	
315	Explicit `--ff` integrates and records DONE/MERGED while retaining the worktree
316	and branch for `dev retire`. Any explicitly selected task agent pane closures
317	are recorded in the result ledger; no parent pane is closed. `--pr` only publishes and
318	opens review; after a commit-preserving external merge use
319	`dev done --merged --base-ref <ref>`. Squash requires explicit
320	`--confirm-squash <commit>` attestation. `--delete-branch` and `--keep-worktree`
321	are deprecated on `done`: the branch is deleted only by
322	`dev retire --delete-branch`, and only when git agrees it is fully contained in
323	the base. "Merged" is not always "finished", so branches survive by default.
324	
325	`dev retire --base <ref>` overrides the containment target, resolving a local
326	branch, then remote-tracking ref (for example `origin/main`), then commit. Apply
327	re-resolves that input; a changed kind/ref/OID makes the plan stale. A recorded
328	fork-point commit stays the base, not the default branch; when it cannot prove
329	integration, pass `--base <branch>` explicitly. `done --merged --base-ref X`
330	carries X into the cleanup hint, wizard and external coordinator handoff.
331	`--delete-branch` still uses Git's upstream/HEAD merged check via `branch -d`, so
332	a non-HEAD base can yield partial completion with the branch and DONE task kept.
333	
334	Cleanup is never inferred from agent lifecycle state. A user must select it in
335	the post-MERGED wizard or run `dev retire` from a different checkout/runtime;
336	both paths revalidate, close eligible sessions, wait for release, and remove
337	without force. Read `agent-retirement.md` before retiring an agent-owned checkout.
338	
339	Dashboard row actions now invoke these same finish/resume/retire workflows. Missing checkout recovery is scoped with `dev sweep --task <id>`. See [dashboard actions](dashboard-actions.md).
340

1	# Worktree ownership
2	
3	Submodule initialization is core Git acquisition, before provisioning/runtime, and defaults to recursive pinned checkouts. `--no-provision` does not skip it; `--submodules=none` does. Gitlink children are independent submodule clones, not nested managed linked worktrees. Read `submodules.md` for selection and explicit disposal rules.
4	
5	Read this before creating a worktree, sharing a checkout between agents, or when
6	a new checkout lacks dependencies, env files, or launcher backend state.
7	
8	## The rule
9	
10	| Change boundary | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
11	|---|---|---|---|
12	| Durable feature/fix/experiment/handoff | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path` | until external `dev retire` |
13	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation | Claude Code | `.claude/worktrees/` | managed by that harness; do not assume artifact relocation |
14	| Runtime workspace/panes | Herdr | per-host runtime | until explicitly closed |
15	| Rendered agent history | SpecStory | process launch checkout | until committed/removed with that checkout |
16	
17	Use a `dev` worktree for independent approaches or any change stream whose code,
18	history, or plan must remain reviewable. Agents with explicitly disjoint file
19	ownership may share one checkout, but `--allow-shared-checkout` is a deliberate
20	coordination override—not a default.
21	
22	`EnterWorktree` changes an agent's working location; it does not prove an
23	existing SpecStory wrapper/watcher rebound its source/output paths. Start the
24	new process from the target worktree root.
25	
26	## Why dev creates the checkout
27	
28	`dev` runs `git worktree add`, then asks Herdr to run
29	`worktree open --path <path> --no-focus`. Path policy therefore remains stable
30	on machines without Herdr, while Herdr still displays repo/branch provenance.
31	A fallback plain workspace is reported as such and is not an exact agent launch
32	target.
33	
34	Never nest a durable worktree inside another checkout. Every watcher, language
35	server, backup tool and search then sees a second copy of the repository.
36	
37	Herdr's native **New worktree** action is still valid for an external,
38	unmanaged checkout. When the canonical repository is under a configured scan
39	root, Git registration lets dev discover the checkout without scanning
40	`~/.herdr/worktrees`; dev does not auto-adopt, relocate, or provision it. Run
41	`dev wt provision <path>` if it needs the project environment and `dev adopt`
42	followed by `dev adopt --apply` only when it should enter the durable task
43	lifecycle. For one exact checkout, `dev flow [repo]` offers plan-first
44	metadata-only Adopt and clean branch-preserving Remove Checkout. It never removes
45	the canonical checkout or a harness/conflicting/locked/prunable/task-claimed row,
46	and it does not prune repository-wide stale registrations.
47	
48	## Paths
49	
50	Default:
51	
52	```text
53	~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>
54	```
55	
56	Configurable through `paths.worktree_root` and `paths.worktree_path`, with
57	`worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`, `host`, and `date`
58	variables plus `slug`, `lower`, and `base` filters.
59	
60	Always pass `--base` for unattended creation so the intended starting point is
61	explicit. `dev start` and `dev wt create` otherwise resolve the repository's
62	default branch; they do not use whichever feature happens to be checked out.
63	
64	## Provisioning
65	
66	A worktree is a clean checkout. `dev wt create` and `dev start` build and apply
67	an inspectable plan:
68	
69	```bash
70	dev wt plan
71	dev wt plan --write
72	dev wt provision --dry-run
73	```
74	
75	Effective settings come from global config or committed repo
76	`.dev-cli/config.toml` (legacy `.dev.toml` remains readable):
77	
78	```toml
79	[worktree]
80	include = [".env", ".env.local"]
81	link = []
82	post_create = "auto"
83	strategy = "reinstall"
84	```
85	
86	An executable `post_create` from `.dev-cli/config.toml` requires approval of its
87	exact content hash with `dev config trust <repo> --yes`. Legacy `.dev.toml`
88	retains its compatibility behavior.
89	
90	Only paths that are both explicitly included and genuinely gitignored are
91	copied. Tracked files already have the branch-correct version. Included files
92	must remain the same regular file from validation through open; source swaps and
93	symlinked destination parents are refused. Existing destinations are reported
94	as skipped, never falsely as copied, and file contents are never logged.
95	
96	This is local provisioning only. Off-machine `dev fleet files` deliberately uses
97	a separate `[local_files].include` allowlist plus explicit `--to`; never infer
98	export permission from `[worktree].include`.
99	
100	### Project-local Claude backend state
101	
102	`.claude/settings.local.json` stays gitignored and is **not** a universal default
103	include. The verified `claude-copilot-once` wrapper preserves an existing
104	Copilot pin and creates/removes only its own pin when one was absent;
105	`codex-copilot-once` injects its backend via CLI. Neither needs a copied project
106	file. Claude's Copilot proxy must already be running; the Codex path may
107	self-start its proxy flow.
108	
109	An explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude profile may opt in exactly:
110	
111	```toml
112	[worktree]
113	include = [".env", ".env.local", ".claude/settings.local.json"]
114	```
115	
116	Verify the file arrived before launch. If absent, stop instead of allowing the
117	launcher to fall back silently to another backend. `dev` logs the relative path
118	only, never its contents.
119	
120	## Dependency strategies
121	
122	- `reinstall`: safe default; run lockfile-derived installer.
123	- `copy`: duplicate path-independent dependency trees.
124	- `link`: explicit and usually unsafe for mutable dependencies.
125	- `skip`: for external/container-managed environments.
126	
127	`dev` refuses unsound choices, such as copied/linked Python virtualenvs, and
128	reports missing tools or failed setup without deleting the usable checkout.
129	
130	## Cleanup
131	
132	- `dev wt rm <branch>` removes only the checkout after external runtime safety checks; branch survives.
133	- `dev park` records WARM; when called from its own runtime it leaves that runtime alive for normal exit.
134	- `dev park --cold --push` closes eligible runtime state and removes the pushed worktree only from outside.
135	- `dev done --ff` integrates and records MERGED; runtime/worktree/branch survive.
136	- `dev done --pr` leaves everything active for review.
137	- `dev retire` is the only complete close/wait/remove/reap path.
138	- `dev sweep` reports first; `--apply` routes cleanup through retire.
139	- From canonical main, `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` also audits unmanaged
140	  linked worktrees whose branches are contained in main. Agents must present
141	  that report for user confirmation before applying; branches are retained
142	  unless `--delete-branches` was separately approved.
143	- From any canonical non-bare checkout, `dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees` audits
144	  Claude Workflow isolation through bounded provider metadata plus fresh Git,
145	  task, artifact, caller, and every available runtime. The path/branch naming
146	  pattern is only a candidate label and never deletion proof. Claude Code 2.1.259
147	  exposes no branch/HEAD/non-replayable registration identity, so its current
148	  claims remain unknown/report-only rather than authorizing a reused path.
149	- Ephemeral apply is TTY/per-item only and revalidates a stable fingerprint under
150	  a common-dir lock before plain non-force removal. It never closes runtimes,
151	  prunes, deletes provider metadata, or repairs dirty/ignored work. Branches stay
152	  by default; deletion needs separately approved `--delete-branches --base REF`
153	  and unchanged containment/zero-unique proof before `git branch -d`.
154	
155	Bare `dev done` on a TTY classifies dirty content against the base before
156	offering commit-all or discard-all; unique discard requires `DROP`. Dirty
157	checkout removal may require explicit force, but caller/runtime safety is never
158	bypassable. Herdr `done` is not a cleanup signal, and `--cold --keep-session` is
159	rejected. Never raw-force-remove an agent's cwd.
160	
161	When unrelated dirty bytes block the canonical fast-forward target, the same
162	wizard may use exact stash+restore for ordinary staged, unstaged, and untracked
163	work. Dirty submodules and nested repositories require separate preservation;
164	restore conflicts keep the exact stash and the task rather than claiming DONE.
165	
166	## Triage cleanup batches
167	
168	`dev triage` adds a strict ignored-data guard to its reviewed linked-checkout
169	cleanup. All ignored paths block by default. The operator may declare exact
170	clone-bound disposable relative directories; previews expose the affected paths
171	and sizes and removal requires the displayed CLEAN token. Nested repositories,
172	submodules, harness claims, unknown occupancy and canonical checkouts stay
173	protected. The extra guard runs inside the shared repository lock and directly
174	before removal. Branches and common directories are retained. See
175	[local triage](local-triage.md).
176

1	# AI artifacts: what to keep, archive, and ship
2	
3	Keep useful decisions, choose where transcripts live, and ship product inputs.
4	
5	## Decide by purpose
6	
7	| Material | Purpose | Usual treatment |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| Code, tests, current specs and docs | Current behavior and contracts | Maintain with the project |
10	| Reviewed plans, decisions and pitfalls | Requirements, rationale and lessons | Keep concise, with status and context |
11	| Raw transcripts, draft plans and tool output | Evidence of the development process | Choose per repository: track, archive elsewhere, or keep local |
12	| Native sessions and tool databases | Resume state, indexes or curation records | Follow each tool's backup contract |
13	
14	AI authorship alone does not determine where a file belongs. Promote useful
15	conclusions into the project's existing docs, decisions, backlog or pitfalls;
16	old transcripts are historical evidence, not current instructions. Do not ask
17	future contributors to read every exploratory conversation to understand code.
18	
19	## Four independent choices
20	
21	1. Does this material belong in the source repository's Git history?
22	2. Where is the durable copy, and how will another machine obtain it?
23	3. Should that copy be checked, redacted, or explicitly stored without scanning?
24	4. Does the material belong in a source distribution or installed product?
25	
26	A private experiment can keep raw chats in Git. A public or long-lived project
27	can keep reviewed decisions in Git and transcripts in a separate private Git
28	repository. A private destination does not itself change hygiene policy: choose
29	it explicitly. An unscanned copy is preserved evidence, not a clean scan.
30	
31	## SpecStory: capture is separate from publication
32	
33	SpecStory is the current transcript integration. The originating agent is the
34	provider, for example `codex:<uuid>` or `claude:<uuid>`; SpecStory is the recorder.
35	Its Markdown export is not the native agent session and does not guarantee resume.
36	
37	SpecStory can write per-worktree `.specstory/history/` files or use an explicit
38	`--output-dir`. Preserve project and session identity when combining histories.
39	A shared flat directory does not by itself retain project attribution. Tools
40	such as Lore have their own metadata and curation state; do not assume all of
41	their databases can be discarded and reconstructed from Markdown.
42	
43	For the existing tracked-history workflow:
44	
45	```bash
46	dev hygiene status
47	dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
48	dev prepare --session codex:<uuid>
49	# After the exact recorder has stopped, from outside its checkout:
50	dev artifact finalize --intent <id> --writer-stopped
51	```
52	
53	Preparation does not stop the writer. Never repeatedly redact a file that a
54	recorder is still rewriting from its native source. `dev hygiene redact` requires
55	an exact reviewed plan; artifact writes additionally require post-writer proof.
56	Private recovery and a stable byte snapshot do not prove that a process exited.
57	
58	The shared artifact writer guard covers hygiene redact/repair-encoding/restore/
59	manage and artifact finalize/archive/migrate. Other recognized live agents
60	covering the checkout always block, including idle/done agents. The calling
61	agent is exempt when Herdr's exact session ID (`agent_session` kind `id`, not a
62	title) differs from every target artifact's valid UUID in its actual
63	SpecStory-generated anchored preamble. Only `.specstory/history/*.md` supplies
64	this proof, not filenames or UUIDs later in the text. Plans or unprovable transcripts require global
65	`--allow-shared-checkout`: an explicit assertion of disjoint ownership after the
66	writer exits, never an automatic retry flag. Unknown caller identity needs
67	that explicit attestation. An identified caller-owned live transcript is refused
68	even with the override. Post-writer proof and source revalidation remain
69	required; restore checks the receipt's exact paths.
70	
71	If history is ignored, ordinary code commits need not scan it. An already tracked
72	file remains tracked after adding `.gitignore`: removing it from the index is a
73	separate reviewed operation. Keep or archive ignored history before deleting its
74	worktree; ignored does not mean disposable or backed up.
75	
76	## Choose and apply repository policy
77	
78	No policy means existing behavior is unchanged. `track` retains the existing
79	source-commit finalizer, `archive` preserves selected evidence in a separate Git
80	checkout, and `unmanaged` leaves retention to the user. Sources are `specstory`
81	(recorder Markdown) or `files` (explicit source-relative exports/plans).
82	
83	```bash
84	# Create the ordinary archive repository separately; configure its Git identity.
85	git init -b main /path/to/history
86	# Explicit private raw preservation; choose check or redact when wanted.
87	dev artifact setup --mode archive --source specstory --archive /path/to/history \
88	  --protection off --json
89	dev artifact setup --apply --plan <id> --yes
90	dev artifact status
91	# The same planner through repository setup:
92	dev repo setup --artifacts --mode unmanaged --json
93	```
94	
95	Setup edits only reviewed policy, local binding, ignore and export files; it
96	never untracks, commits, pushes or installs tools. `repo setup --artifacts` is
97	separate from a scaffold plan. Apply there with `--artifacts --apply --plan <id>
98	--yes`. Review and commit shared policy changes yourself.
99	
100	The shareable `.dev-cli/artifacts.toml` contains the stable project ID, retention
101	mode, source and literal paths. The archive path and protection binding stay in
102	private host state. Bind a cloned project to the desired archive on each host;
103	do not infer project identity from a folder basename or current branch.
104	
105	`--capture project` keeps normal per-worktree recorder output. `--capture external`
106	sets a checkout-specific local SpecStory output directory outside Git. It requires
107	untracked native config and enabled local Markdown export; tracked/complex config
108	requires manual review. Run setup in each new external-capture checkout. Existing
109	cloud settings and native session stores remain under SpecStory's control.
110	
111	## Preserve copies, then find them
112	
113	```bash
114	dev artifact archive --session codex:<uuid> --json
115	# Inspect the private review directory, then after the recorder exits:
116	dev artifact archive --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
117	dev artifact find --session codex:<uuid>
118	dev artifact find --commit <full-source-commit-id>
119	dev artifact find 'literal search text' --all
120	```
121	
122	For `--source files`, select exact configured paths with repeated `--file`.
123	Inventory is bounded to 10,000 files and each operation to 256 selected files;
124	current snapshots are limited to 128 MiB per file. Oversized or unsafe inputs
125	fail explicitly. Search reads committed records on the archive's current branch;
126	`--all` includes its other projects. Results contain locations and line numbers,
127	not snippets; no network, native history crawl or agent resume occurs.
128	
129	Archive commits contain ordinary snapshot files and metadata under `projects/`.
130	The metadata binds project/session, original and stored content digests and the
131	source commit. Source files and source index bytes stay untouched. The project
132	archive gets text/ident exclusions so CRLF and literal bytes survive Git; custom
133	content filters such as encryption, LFS or encoding transforms require the
134	archive's native workflow and are never silently bypassed. Existing Git hooks
135	still run. Archive access controls and off-host backups remain the operator's
136	responsibility.
137	
138	`off` saves raw input without a scanner. `check` uses enabled source-repository
139	hygiene policy. `redact` proposes replacements on the copy and checks the result
140	again. Disabled categories remain disabled; skipped is not clean. Blocking
141	reports contain safe finding IDs for the existing `dev hygiene rules allow`
142	workflow. Exact fixture exceptions need review and a reason. Snapshot scans
143	support inline gitleaks rules and useDefault, not external rule-file includes.
144	
145	Unchanged bytes reuse signed local scan evidence only when the path, policy,
146	exceptions, scanner inputs and executables match. Changed bytes or rules rescan.
147	Partial scans never pass. Review original/copy payloads privately; raw recovery,
148	reports and receipts stay under `paths.state_dir`, outside Git and cache clearing.
149	Filenames and metadata can still identify people or systems: review before sharing.
150	
151	After committing product/policy changes, `dev prepare` also supports an archive
152	policy. Off/check finalization creates the exact archive copy after writer exit.
153	For redact, preview and review `artifact archive` first, then pass its ID to
154	`artifact finalize --archive-plan <id> --writer-stopped`. Reviewed plans should
155	be committed with product changes; prepared SpecStory archive handoffs select one
156	exact transcript. Old intents keep their original destination and requirements.
157	The tracked-history finalizer still uses the compatibility skill's scripts.
158	
159	Retirement checks signed archive receipts and current ignored capture bytes.
160	New or changed evidence blocks cleanup until preserved. Local archive durability
161	is distinct from remote sync; ordinary status and readiness never query a remote.
162	
163	## Explicit Git synchronization and original backups
164	
165	```bash
166	dev artifact sync --push --json       # preview contacts the configured remote
167	dev artifact sync --apply --plan <id> --yes
168	dev artifact sync --pull --json       # separate pull preview; fast-forward only
169	
170	dev artifact migrate --mode untrack --path .specstory/history --json
171	dev artifact migrate --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
172	
173	dev artifact migrate --mode split --path .specstory/history --json
174	dev artifact migrate --apply --plan <id> --yes
175	# Optional: publish the original named refs to a separate empty destination.
176	dev artifact backup <completed-migration-id> --remote <git-url> --json
177	dev artifact backup --apply --plan <backup-plan-id> --yes
178	```
179	
180	Untrack saves original refs and selected working files, edits ignore rules and
181	removes only selected index entries. Other staged/unstaged work remains intact;
182	existing prepared handoffs must be resolved first. Untracking does not itself
183	configure future archive capture.
184	
185	Split requires git-filter-repo and complete local history. It produces verified
186	`original.bundle`, `original.git`, `history.git`, `filtered.git`, both commit maps,
187	selected working snapshots in `current/`, and a migration manifest. Every mapped
188	tree is checked against the selected-path projection. Empty commits/merge topology
189	and message bytes are retained; rewritten signatures cannot remain valid. A
190	restore clone verifies the original bundle. Neither source refs nor remotes change.
191	Raw backups are not a hygiene audit. Other worktrees' uncommitted files, reflogs,
192	unreachable objects, LFS payloads and submodule repositories are outside coverage.
193	Detached tips need a recovery ref before migration.
194	
195	Backup publication sends frozen named refs with empty-ref leases. Selected
196	uncommitted working snapshots stay in local `current/`; they are not in the Git
197	remote backup. Archive sync pins the reviewed destination and branch: push proves
198	ancestry before an exact lease, pull only fast-forwards. Resolve divergence with
199	native Git; dev does not force-overwrite or synthesize merges.
200	
201	Private operation ledgers retain partial effects, output and recovery paths.
202	After interruption inspect those paths and the remote, then prepare a new plan;
203	never blindly replay a partial operation. Original-remote cutover, release/tag
204	migration and force-with-lease publication of filtered history are separate,
205	operator-coordinated actions.
206	
207	## Distribution, untracking and history migration
208	
209	| Action | Effect | Earlier commits |
210	|---|---|---|
211	| `.gitattributes` `export-ignore` | Exclude selected paths from `git archive` source packages | Unchanged |
212	| Ignore and untrack | Stop including new versions in source commits; retain working files | Unchanged |
213	| Filter a separate repository copy | Build replacement history without selected paths | Different commit IDs in that copy |
214	
215	For example, this excludes chats from source archives while leaving them in Git:
216	
217	```gitattributes
218	/.specstory export-ignore
219	/.specstory/** export-ignore
220	```
221	
222	Verify the exported source still builds, including embedded resources. Packaging
223	systems have separate inclusion rules; an archive exclusion is not a universal
224	package filter. New rules affect new tagged snapshots, not old immutable tags.
225	
226	When an experiment becomes a maintained project, first inventory and verify a
227	recoverable original. Build and validate filtered history in a separate copy,
228	retain commit mappings, and separately coordinate remote replacement, tags,
229	releases and other clones/worktrees. A bundle covers selected Git objects/refs,
230	not automatically dirty files, LFS objects or submodule repositories.
231	
232	Sync, version control and backup are separate. A synchronized deletion is still
233	a deletion. Restoring a Markdown export is not restoring the native agent state.
234	Confirmed leaked credentials require revocation or rotation; filtering Git does
235	not revoke them or remove copies held by other people and services.
236	
237	See `dev help hygiene` for scanning and reviewed redaction, `dev help retirement`
238	for post-writer handoffs, `dev help repositories` for setup, and `dev help storage`
239	for durable data versus caches.
