```text
1	# Agent-safe worktree retirement
2	
3	Recursive submodule disposal is an explicit extension: verify child tasks/artifacts/runtime, local data and fresh remote recovery first, then stage children inside-out and remove the outer checkout without force. Preserve canonical/shared Git and the outer branch. A retained journal is recovered with `dev submodule recover`, not deleted using an old remote proof. See `submodules.md`.
4	
5	## The rule
6	
7	A feature agent may prepare and integrate work, but it must not destroy the
8	runtime or checkout containing its own process. Completion has three milestones:
9	
10	```text
11	READY     exact final transcript committed after the writer exits
12	MERGED    branch integrated; runtime/worktree may still exist
13	RETIRED   runtime absent, worktree removed, optional branch deleted, task reaped
14	```
15	
16	`hot/warm/cold/done` remain the persisted task states. `done` now means MERGED,
17	not "everything has already been deleted".
18	
19	## Normal local flow
20	
21	From the feature worktree:
22	
23	```bash
24	# Commit product changes first. Do not stage the moving transcript.
25	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid> --plan .claude/plans/task.md
26	# Exit the agent normally so SpecStory can write its final Markdown.
27	```
28	
29	The outer `specstory run` wrapper calls:
30	
31	```bash
32	dev artifact finalize --run-id "$DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID" --if-pending --writer-stopped
33	```
34	
35	Then an external main/integration workspace runs:
36	
37	```bash
38	dev done <task> --ff
39	dev retire <task> --delete-branch
40	```
41	
42	`done` only integrates and records MERGED. `retire` re-resolves every runtime
43	pane, closes eligible sessions, waits for them to disappear, revalidates Git,
44	and removes the worktree without force.
45	
46	`dev flow [repo]` offers Retire only for an exact DONE task. Enter first shows a
47	revision-bound plan with conditions, ordered effects, retained resources, and a
48	CLI fallback; branch deletion needs the displayed typed token. Apply locks and
49	reloads task/repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact authority, repeats safety
50	checks after closure and before removal, and deletes the task last. If a later
51	effect fails, its ledger reports completed work and recovery without claiming a
52	rollback.
53	
54	For periodic cleanup from the canonical main checkout:
55	
56	```bash
57	dev sweep --merged-worktrees
58	# Present the exact candidates/blockers to the user and ask for approval.
59	dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply --yes
60	```
61	
62	This includes unmanaged linked worktrees whose named branches are already
63	contained in main. It never treats containment alone as permission: dirty Git,
64	pending artifacts and runtime blockers still stop cleanup. Branches remain by
65	default; add `--delete-branches` only when the user approved that separately.
66	
67	`dev sweep --base <ref>` also forwards the selected base to DONE task retirement;
68	`--merged-worktrees` uses its verified base for managed tasks as well as unmanaged
69	checkouts. Reviewed retire/remove plans bind worktree-list authority only to the
70	same branch or paths equal to, containing, or nested under the target. Removing
71	an unrelated sibling no longer invalidates the rest of an approved
72	`--apply --yes` batch. A same-branch checkout or target lock/HEAD change still
73	makes the plan stale; containment and all other guards remain required.
74	
75	Claude Workflow ephemeral worktrees use a separate, stricter path:
76	
77	```bash
78	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --stale-days 14
79	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --json
80	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply
81	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply --delete-branches --base main
82	```
83	
84	Run it from the canonical non-bare checkout. The schema-v1 report joins one
85	bounded, fixed-depth `~/.claude/projects` mapping to live Git state without
86	decoding or emitting prompts, scripts, logs, result bodies, or transcript
87	content. V1 requires workflow `completed|killed`, matching agent `done`, journal
88	`started` and `result`, no same-ID resumed transcript, and provider inactivity
89	older than `--stale-days` (default 14, minimum 1). Killed/no-result, progress,
90	resume, malformed/mutating metadata, or unknown time stays `unknown`; there is no
91	operator-attestation bypass.
92	
93	Ownership must also bind provider-observed branch, HEAD, common-dir, and an opaque
94	non-replayable registration generation to the live target. Claude Code 2.1.259
95	records no such Git identity, so current Claude Workflow claims report
96	`provider-git-identity: unknown` and remain report-only even with `--apply`.
97	A path, derived branch name, or reusable GitDir pathname is never a substitute;
98	otherwise stale terminal metadata could authorize a replacement checkout at the
99	same path.
100	
101	The worktree must remain registered, present, non-main, named, unlocked and
102	non-prunable, with exact common-dir/branch/registry-HEAD/live-HEAD agreement. It
103	must have no staged/unstaged/conflicted/untracked/ignored/recursive-submodule
104	content, no Git operation, task claim, unsafe artifact intent, caller
105	containment, or covering runtime. Missing, prunable, unregistered, and orphan
106	paths are report only. Apply rejects `--yes`, `--close-unknown`,
107	`--assume-no-runtime`, `--no-runtime`, and JSON; it requires a TTY and per-item
108	confirmation. Under a common-dir cleanup lock it recollects every fact and
109	compares the stable candidate fingerprint before plain non-force removal. It
110	never prunes, closes sessions, deletes provider metadata, or rescues/stashes/
111	commits dirty work.
112	
113	A branch is retained by default, so a clean checkout with unique commits may be
114	removed safely. Optional branch deletion is a separate proof requiring an
115	explicit base, unchanged branch/base tips, containment, zero unique commits, and
116	ordinary `git branch -d`; any post-removal failure leaves the branch retained and
117	reports partial completion.
118	
119	## Choose the containment base
120	
121	`dev retire --base <ref>` overrides the containment target for a DONE task or
122	linked worktree without changing recorded task intent. Resolution checks a local
123	branch (`refs/heads/X`), then a remote-tracking branch (`refs/remotes/X`, such as
124	`origin/main`), then a commit. Fully qualified branch refs keep their named kind.
125	Apply re-resolves the same input and requires the same kind, ref and commit OID;
126	a moved base or a newly created same-name branch makes the reviewed plan stale.
127	Remote-tracking refs are local observations, not an implicit fetch.
128	
129	Without an override, task retirement keeps its recorded base. A recorded
130	fork-point commit is never silently replaced by the default branch: if it cannot
131	prove integration, retirement stays blocked with `pass --base <branch>` guidance.
132	After `dev done --merged --base-ref X`, cleanup hints, the cleanup wizard and the
133	external coordinator carry X forward as `dev retire --base X <task>`. If a shell
134	handoff cannot carry the override, dev prints the external command instead.
135	
136	Optional `--delete-branch` still runs ordinary `git branch -d`, whose own merged
137	check uses the branch's upstream or HEAD, not `--base`. Against a non-HEAD base,
138	branch deletion can therefore fail after the worktree was removed; the branch
139	and DONE task remain, and the result reports partial completion.
140	
141	## Pull-request flow
142	
143	```bash
144	dev done <task> --pr
145	# after CI/review and a commit-preserving merge
146	git fetch origin
147	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main
148	dev retire --base origin/main <task> --delete-branch
149	```
150	
151	A squash merge is not ancestry-equivalent. It requires an explicit operator
152	attestation:
153	
154	```bash
155	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main --confirm-squash <merge-commit>
156	```
157	
158	This proves only that the named squash commit is in the base; the operator is
159	asserting that it represents the feature.
160	
161	## Safety policy
162	
163	Retirement always refuses when:
164	
165	- the caller cwd is the target or below it;
166	- the caller Herdr workspace/pane or tmux pane covers the target;
167	- a workspace contains panes outside the target;
168	- an agent is `working`, `blocked`, or `waiting`;
169	- runtime enumeration fails;
170	- the checkout is dirty, on the wrong branch, or not contained in its base;
171	- artifact finalization is armed/finalizing/failed.
172	
173	`unknown` or empty agent status requires `--close-unknown` from outside the
174	target. Runtime enumeration failure requires external `--assume-no-runtime`.
175	Neither flag bypasses caller containment or active-agent states.
176	
177	Raw `git worktree remove --force` and configured external tools can bypass dev.
178	Never run them from an agent that occupies the target. dev's guarantee covers
179	only dev-mediated paths. Existing CLI expert acknowledgements remain compatible,
180	but flow intentionally omits them. Task-backed and exact unmanaged path
181	retirement use taskflow, with contained removal required for the latter. Some
182	record-only/salvage `sweep` actions remain isolated compatibility paths.
183	
184	## What self-deletion looks like
185	
186	A real Codex session deleted its own registered worktree and branch from another
187	checkout. Herdr kept the workspace and terminal alive because Unix processes can
188	hold an open cwd inode after the path is unlinked. SpecStory then recreated the
189	same path with only `.specstory/` content.
190	
191	The resulting shell looked alive but was no longer a Git checkout:
192	
193	```text
194	failed to reload config: No such file or directory
195	fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
196	```
197	
198	Config/skill reloads and new subprocesses failed while Herdr still displayed an
199	idle agent. Treat `runtime alive + Git registration absent + artifact-only path`
200	as an orphan requiring transcript salvage and external reconciliation, never as
201	RETIRED.
202	
203	## Artifact rules
204	
205	- Match SpecStory Markdown by the exact UUID in its fixed preamble, not filename
206	  or newest mtime.
207	- Finalize only after SessionEnd was observed or the outer wrapper supplies
208	  `--writer-stopped`; byte stability remains a second, independent check.
209	- Stage only that transcript and explicitly named plans.
210	- Never stage another provider/session implicitly.
211	- `.specstory/statistics.json` is derived and ignored.
212	- New untracked transcripts above 2 MiB need `--allow-large`.
213	- Scanner/redactor failure commits nothing and leaves a retryable intent.
214	- Artifact commits are on the same feature branch, not necessarily the same
215	  product commit; they carry `Agent-Artifact-Session` and
216	  `Dev-Artifact-Intent` trailers.
217	
218	## Task worktree scope
219	
220	Worktree-mode `dev start --focus -t <name>` creates a linked checkout; `--focus`
221	only changes focus. Finishing that task preserves its parent/canonical agent
222	sessions and other tasks' tabs. A recognized parent agent in any state blocks
223	FF: recheck after handling it independently in Herdr, choose PR, or cancel.
224	When integration is already proven and only retirement remains, a parent agent
225	does not prevent cleanup of the separate child worktree.
226	
227	The interactive finish plan may select exact idle/done **task-worktree** agent
228	panes for closure. Nothing closes until final Apply approval. Parent, other
229	checkout, mixed, or unverified Herdr workspaces are protected even when a pane
230	has changed into the target directory. If they still cover the worktree,
231	retirement stops and identifies the preserved panes. Working/blocked/waiting
232	agents remain blockers. General foreground programs (an editor, server, or
233	test command) require a separate FF confirmation: files in the displayed
234	checkout will change while those programs continue running. `--yes` does not
235	supply that confirmation; non-interactive calls requiring it stop.
236	
237	Interactive `dev done` cleanup and standalone `dev retire` share a preview of
238	the target, retained resources, workspace/tab/pane IDs, agent states, and
239	foreground program names, PIDs and directories. Closing known non-agent
240	programs requires typing `CLOSE <workspace-id>` for each affected workspace,
241	then approving the final retirement. `--close-unknown` does not authorize
242	known program termination. Only a proven foreground shell is labeled as such;
243	unavailable process evidence is shown as unknown, never idle. Herdr provides
244	foreground evidence; other backends keep their existing explicitly qualified
245	unknown-runtime policy. Background jobs are **not inspected** and may also stop
246	when their terminal closes. Raw argv and environment values are not displayed.
247	
248	Approvals bind exact task/checkout, terminal topology and program fingerprints.
249	A changed program, new tab or moved pane requires a refreshed preview. The
250	single-use version-2 coordinator handoff waits for the exact launching dev PID
251	to exit and verifies the original pane has returned to its foreground shell;
252	a replacement program is not exempt. Old handoffs must be recreated. Final
253	cancellation before Apply changes nothing; failures after effects begin list
254	completed closures and retained resources. Raw Git and Herdr actions remain
255	outside dev's locks and revalidation guarantees.
256	
257	## External archive policy
258	
259	`dev artifact setup` can select a separate Git archive. New prepared intents bind
260	that destination and policy; old intents keep the commit workflow. Off/check
261	finalization needs no compatibility redactor script. For redact copies, review
262	`dev artifact archive` and supply `--archive-plan` when finalizing. Commit reviewed
263	plans with product changes before preparing one exact SpecStory transcript.
264	Ignored capture bytes participate in lifecycle readiness; a new recorder write or
265	missing archive receipt blocks cleanup. See [AI artifacts](ai-artifacts.md).

//go:build aix || darwin || dragonfly || freebsd || linux || netbsd || openbsd || solaris

package safefile

import (
	"context"
	"io/fs"
	"os"

	"golang.org/x/sys/unix"
)

func removeEmptyChildDirNative(ctx context.Context, parent *os.Root, name string, expected fs.FileInfo) error {
	file, err := parent.Open(".")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer file.Close()
	held, err := file.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	root, err := parent.Stat(".")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !os.SameFile(held, root) || !held.IsDir() {
		return ErrChanged
	}
	if err := VerifyChildRoot(parent, name, expected); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	// Never fall back to unlink: a file substituted after the last check must
	// survive. A directory substituted by a raw writer in this narrow interval
	// cannot be compared atomically with rmdir on Unix.
	return unix.Unlinkat(int(file.Fd()), name, unix.AT_REMOVEDIR)
}

//go:build windows

package safefile

import (
	"context"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"unsafe"

	"golang.org/x/sys/windows"
)

func removeEmptyChildDirNative(ctx context.Context, parent *os.Root, name string, expected fs.FileInfo) error {
	dir, err := parent.Open(".")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer dir.Close()
	held, err := dir.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	root, err := parent.Stat(".")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !os.SameFile(held, root) || unsafeLink(held) || !held.IsDir() {
		return ErrChanged
	}
	childName, err := windows.NewNTUnicodeString(name)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	attributes := windows.OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES{
		Length: uint32(unsafe.Sizeof(windows.OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES{})),
		RootDirectory: windows.Handle(dir.Fd()), ObjectName: childName,
		Attributes: windows.OBJ_CASE_INSENSITIVE,
	}
	var handle windows.Handle
	var status windows.IO_STATUS_BLOCK
	// No delete-on-close: nothing may be deleted before type, identity and
	// emptiness are verified. DIRECTORY_FILE rejects a replaced ordinary file;
	// OPEN_REPARSE_POINT opens (and below rejects) rather than follows a link.
	if err := windows.NtCreateFile(&handle, windows.FILE_GENERIC_READ|windows.DELETE,
		&attributes, &status, nil, 0,
		windows.FILE_SHARE_READ|windows.FILE_SHARE_WRITE|windows.FILE_SHARE_DELETE,
		windows.FILE_OPEN, windows.FILE_DIRECTORY_FILE|windows.FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT|windows.FILE_SYNCHRONOUS_IO_NONALERT,
		0, 0); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	file := os.NewFile(uintptr(handle), name)
	defer file.Close()
	info, err := file.Stat()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if unsafeLink(info) || !info.IsDir() || !os.SameFile(info, expected) {
		return ErrChanged
	}
	if err := verifyEmptyDirectory(file); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := VerifyChildRoot(parent, name, expected); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	// FileDispositionInfo deletes this verified handle, not a newly resolved
	// path. The kernel refuses a directory that became nonempty.
	remove := byte(1)
	return windows.SetFileInformationByHandle(handle, windows.FileDispositionInfo, &remove, 1)
}

23

26	| core repository/task/worktree operations | Git | unavailable; Git is the only hard runtime dependency |
27	| rich grouped runtime and agent activity | Herdr server + CLI | `auto` tries tmux, then Zellij, then none |

29	| GitHub pull requests/remotes | `gh` authenticated | branch still pushes when Git works; browser/manual flow may be needed |
30	| GitLab merge requests/remotes | `glab` authenticated | same graceful fallback |

are disabled for source upgrades. To recover an older `dev` whose upgrade command

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- `dev hygiene report` summarizes the newest stored scan for the current
  checkout without scanning again (so the pre-commit hook's staged scan is
  readable right after a blocked commit), or `--report ID` / `--rescan`.
  Findings are grouped by severity, rule, file and category, ordered by
  disposition then occurrences, with `--top`, `--disposition`, `--rule`,
  `--category`, `--path` filters and a `--findings` drill-down. `--json` emits
  the new `hygiene_summary` schema-v1 document. `--values` shows masked
  distinct values per rule; raw values and their context go only to a private
  review file whose location `dev hygiene review-path <report-id>` prints.
  Scan findings gain additive keyed `value_id` and `file_id` fields, keeping
  private filenames distinct even when their displayed labels match. Stored
  summaries show the scan date without claiming current source freshness;
  legacy file counts are explicitly marked as lower bounds. Value capture is
  byte-bounded and skipped samples are visible; a failed values sidecar retains
  a partial scan receipt. Invalid path globs fail before scanning, and filter
  metadata is policy-masked.
- `dev retire --base <ref>` overrides the containment target used to prove a
  DONE task or linked worktree is integrated: a local branch, a remote-tracking
  branch such as `origin/main`, or a commit. `dev sweep --base` forwards the
  same override to DONE tasks, and `--merged-worktrees` proves managed tasks
  against the base it already verified. After `dev done --merged --base-ref`,
  cleanup hints and the cleanup wizard carry that ref forward.

### Fixed

- Guarded file replacements on macOS no longer fail with a metadata round-trip
  error when the source file was written by another application. The kernel
  assigns `com.apple.provenance` to each new file and ignores attempts to copy
  it, so hygiene redaction, encoding repair and recovery, and `dev ssh init`
  now leave that one tag to the kernel while still requiring every other
  extended attribute to survive and still detecting a changed source. Apply and
  recovery errors now keep their underlying cause instead of only pointing at
  the private receipt.
- `dev sweep --apply --yes` (including `--merged-worktrees`) now completes a
  batch in one pass. A reviewed retirement or removal plan is bound only to the
  worktrees that share its branch or path, so removing an unrelated sibling
  earlier in the batch no longer turns every remaining plan stale. A new
  checkout of the same branch, or a lock or HEAD change on the target, still
  invalidates the plan.
- Retirement and contained worktree removal no longer refuse a base recorded as
  a commit or remote-tracking ref (for example `base = "b509448"` from
  `dev start --base <commit>`) with "local base ref refs/heads/… does not
  exist". Bases resolve as a local branch, then a remote-tracking branch, then a
  commit, and apply re-resolves the same input. A recorded fork-point commit is
  never replaced by the default branch: when it cannot prove integration, the
  plan stays blocked and names `--base <branch>`.
- An agent can now repair or redact another session's stopped SpecStory
  transcript from its own pane. The artifact writer guard previously blocked
  the calling agent itself, leaving `--no-runtime` as the only way through.
  Other live agents still always block. The caller is exempt only when Herdr's
  exact session id differs from a valid UUID in every target's actual
  SpecStory-generated preamble, or when `--allow-shared-checkout` explicitly
  asserts disjoint ownership (for example plans or unknown session identities).
  An identified caller-owned live transcript is refused even with the override;
  malformed headers or body mentions never prove another session.
  `dev hygiene restore --apply` now guards the receipt's exact paths.

```go
package submodule

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/safefile"
)

const removalLayoutLimit = 8192

type layoutDirectory struct {
	Identity string   `json:"identity"`
	Mode     uint32   `json:"mode"`
	Listing  []string `json:"listing,omitempty"`
	Listed   bool     `json:"listed"`
	info     fs.FileInfo
}

type removalLayout struct {
	Directories map[string]layoutDirectory `json:"directories"`
	// Absence records the FIRST missing component, not merely a missing leaf.
	// Every existing ancestor below the held checkout/admin root is also bound.
	Absent      map[string]bool `json:"absent"`
	Initialized []string        `json:"initialized"`
	scaffolds   []string
}

func (l *removalLayout) fingerprint() string {
	data, _ := json.Marshal(l)
	h := sha256.Sum256(data)
	return hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
}

func (l *removalLayout) record(path string, root *os.Root, info fs.FileInfo, listing bool) error {
	if len(l.Directories)+len(l.Absent) >= removalLayoutLimit {
		return errors.New("submodule removal layout exceeds inspection limit")
	}
	identity, err := gitx.DirectoryIdentity(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	d := layoutDirectory{Identity: identity, Mode: uint32(info.Mode()), info: info}
	if prior, ok := l.Directories[path]; ok {
		if !os.SameFile(prior.info, info) {
			return safefile.ErrChanged
		}
		d = prior
	}
	if listing {
		file, err := root.Open(".")
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		names, readErr := file.Readdirnames(removalLayoutLimit + 1)
		closeErr := file.Close()
		if readErr != nil && !errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
			return readErr
		}
		if closeErr != nil {
			return closeErr
		}
		if len(names) > removalLayoutLimit {
			return errors.New("submodule administration listing exceeds inspection limit")
		}
		sort.Strings(names)
		d.Listing, d.Listed = names, true
	}
	if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(path, info); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	l.Directories[path] = d
	return nil
}

// path observes a bounded component-by-component walk. Empty leaves cannot hide
// nested user directories, .git markers, ignored files, links or reparse points.
func (l *removalLayout) path(ctx context.Context, base, relative string, empty bool) error {
	root, info, err := safefile.OpenRoot(base)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer func() { root.Close() }()
	if err := l.record(base, root, info, false); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	parts := strings.Split(filepath.ToSlash(relative), "/")
	if relative == "." {
		parts = nil
	}
	if len(parts) > 64 {
		return errors.New("submodule layout path exceeds inspection depth")
	}
	path := base
	for _, name := range parts {
		if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		child, childInfo, err := safefile.OpenChildRoot(root, name)
		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			// A failed open alone is not an absence observation: prove the name
			// really is missing relative to the same held ancestor.
			if _, statErr := root.Lstat(name); !errors.Is(statErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
				return errors.Join(safefile.ErrChanged, statErr)
			}
			l.Absent[filepath.Join(path, name)] = true
			return safefile.VerifyRoot(path, info)
		}
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(path, info); err != nil {
			child.Close()
			return err
		}
		root.Close()
		root, info, path = child, childInfo, filepath.Join(path, name)
		if err := l.record(path, root, info, false); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	if empty {
		if err := l.record(path, root, info, true); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if len(l.Directories[path].Listing) != 0 {
			return fmt.Errorf("uninitialized submodule %s contains retained data", relative)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func observeRemovalLayout(ctx context.Context, repo gitx.Repo, g gitx.SubmoduleGraph) (*removalLayout, error) {
	l := &removalLayout{Directories: map[string]layoutDirectory{}, Absent: map[string]bool{}}
	for _, path := range []string{repo.Root, repo.GitDir} {
		if err := l.path(ctx, path, ".", false); err != nil {
			return l, err
		}
	}
	known := map[string]bool{}
	modules := filepath.Join(repo.GitDir, "modules")
	for _, n := range g.Nodes {
		if err := l.path(ctx, repo.Root, n.Path, !n.Initialized); err != nil {
			return l, fmt.Errorf("submodule %s: %w", n.Path, err)
		}
		if n.Initialized {
			known[n.GitDir] = true
			l.Initialized = append(l.Initialized, n.Path)
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(l.Initialized)
	if err := l.storage(ctx, repo.GitDir, "modules", known, 0); err != nil {
		return l, err
	}
	for path := range known {
		if _, ok := l.Directories[path]; !ok {
			return l, fmt.Errorf("initialized submodule storage %s is outside observed %s", path, modules)
		}
	}
	return l, nil
}

func (l *removalLayout) storage(ctx context.Context, parentPath, name string, known map[string]bool, depth int) error {
	if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if depth > 64 {
		return errors.New("submodule administration exceeds inspection depth")
	}
	parent, parentInfo, err := safefile.OpenRoot(parentPath)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer parent.Close()
	if err := l.record(parentPath, parent, parentInfo, false); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	root, info, err := safefile.OpenChildRoot(parent, name)
	path := filepath.Join(parentPath, name)
	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		if _, statErr := parent.Lstat(name); !errors.Is(statErr, fs.ErrNotExist) {
			return errors.Join(safefile.ErrChanged, statErr)
		}
		l.Absent[path] = true
		return safefile.VerifyRoot(parentPath, parentInfo)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("unclaimed private module data at %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	defer root.Close()
	if err := l.record(path, root, info, true); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if known[path] {
		// Leases are self-created coordination data, not layout changes. Other
		// private Git entries remain listed and inspectPrivateState checks them.
		d := l.Directories[path]
		var names []string
		for _, entry := range d.Listing {
			if entry != "dev-taskflow" && entry != ".dev-taskflow.lock" {
				names = append(names, entry)
			}
		}
		d.Listing = names
		l.Directories[path] = d
		return l.storage(ctx, path, "modules", known, depth+1)
	}
	l.scaffolds = append(l.scaffolds, path)
	for _, entry := range l.Directories[path].Listing {
		if entry == "HEAD" {
			return fmt.Errorf("orphan submodule repository %s requires preservation", path)
		}
		if err := l.storage(ctx, path, entry, known, depth+1); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return safefile.VerifyChildRoot(parent, name, info)
}

func (p *Removal) revalidateLayout(ctx context.Context, expected *removalLayout) error {
	fresh, err := observeRemovalLayout(ctx, p.Repository, p.Graph)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if fresh.fingerprint() != expected.fingerprint() {
		return errors.New("stale submodule removal layout")
	}
	return nil
}

// PrunedDirectoriesError reports irreversible directory-only housekeeping before
// an outer removal failed. It never claims the worktree or task was removed.
type PrunedDirectoriesError struct {
	Paths []string
	Cause error
}

func (e *PrunedDirectoriesError) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("pruned empty submodule administration directories [%s]; outer cleanup incomplete: %v", strings.Join(e.Paths, ", "), e.Cause)
}
func (e *PrunedDirectoriesError) Unwrap() error { return e.Cause }

func (p *Removal) applyEmpty(ctx context.Context, check func(context.Context, string) error, removeOuter func() error) (err error) {
	// This lane creates no proof repository, lease, journal or quarantine.
	l, err := observeRemovalLayout(ctx, p.Repository, p.Graph)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if l.fingerprint() != p.LayoutFingerprint {
		return errors.New("stale submodule removal layout")
	}
	var pruned []string
	defer func() {
		if err != nil && len(pruned) > 0 {
			err = &PrunedDirectoriesError{Paths: append([]string(nil), pruned...), Cause: err}
		}
	}()
	sort.Slice(l.scaffolds, func(i, j int) bool {
		if len(l.scaffolds[i]) != len(l.scaffolds[j]) {
			return len(l.scaffolds[i]) > len(l.scaffolds[j])
		}
		return l.scaffolds[i] < l.scaffolds[j]
	})
	for _, path := range l.scaffolds {
		if err := p.revalidateLocal(ctx, l); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if check != nil {
			if err := check(ctx, p.Graph.Root); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
		if err := p.revalidateLayout(ctx, l); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		parentPath := filepath.Dir(path)
		parent, info, err := safefile.OpenRoot(parentPath)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if !os.SameFile(info, l.Directories[parentPath].info) {
			parent.Close()
			return safefile.ErrChanged
		}
		err = safefile.RemoveEmptyChildDir(ctx, parent, filepath.Base(path), l.Directories[path].info)
		parent.Close()
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		rel, _ := filepath.Rel(p.Repository.GitDir, path)
		pruned = append(pruned, filepath.ToSlash(rel))
		delete(l.Directories, path)
		if path == filepath.Join(p.Repository.GitDir, "modules") {
			l.Absent[path] = true
		} else {
			d := l.Directories[parentPath]
			var names []string
			for _, name := range d.Listing {
				if name != filepath.Base(path) {
					names = append(names, name)
				}
			}
			d.Listing = names
			l.Directories[parentPath] = d
		}
	}
	// Unconditional even for zero initialized children and absent modules/.
	if err := p.revalidateLocal(ctx, l); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if check != nil {
		if err := check(ctx, p.Graph.Root); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	if err := p.revalidateLocal(ctx, l); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return removeOuter()
}

127	## Versioning and changelog
128	
129	The current published baseline is `v0.2.38` (2026-09-15). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
130	
131	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
132	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
133	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
134	
135	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
136	
137	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
138

7	## [Unreleased]

14	  Findings are grouped by severity, rule, file and category, ordered by
15	  disposition then occurrences, with `--top`, `--disposition`, `--rule`,
16	  `--category`, `--path` filters and a `--findings` drill-down. `--json` emits
17	  the new `hygiene_summary` schema-v1 document. `--values` shows masked
18	  distinct values per rule; raw values and their context go only to a private
19	  review file whose location `dev hygiene review-path <report-id>` prints.
20	  Scan findings gain additive keyed `value_id` and `file_id` fields, keeping
21	  private filenames distinct even when their displayed labels match. Stored
22	  summaries show the scan date without claiming current source freshness;
23	  legacy file counts are explicitly marked as lower bounds. Value capture is
24	  byte-bounded and skipped samples are visible; a failed values sidecar retains
25	  a partial scan receipt. Invalid path globs fail before scanning, and filter
26	  metadata is policy-masked.
27	- `dev retire --base <ref>` overrides the containment target used to prove a
28	  DONE task or linked worktree is integrated: a local branch, a remote-tracking
29	  branch such as `origin/main`, or a commit. `dev sweep --base` forwards the
30	  same override to DONE tasks, and `--merged-worktrees` proves managed tasks
31	  against the base it already verified. After `dev done --merged --base-ref`,
32	  cleanup hints and the cleanup wizard carry that ref forward.
33	
34	### Fixed
35	
36	- Guarded file replacements on macOS no longer fail with a metadata round-trip
37	  error when the source file was written by another application. The kernel
38	  assigns `com.apple.provenance` to each new file and ignores attempts to copy
39	  it, so hygiene redaction, encoding repair and recovery, and `dev ssh init`
40	  now leave that one tag to the kernel while still requiring every other
41	  extended attribute to survive and still detecting a changed source. Apply and
42	  recovery errors now keep their underlying cause instead of only pointing at
43	  the private receipt.
44	- `dev sweep --apply --yes` (including `--merged-worktrees`) now completes a

20	 _, plainErr := submodule.InspectRemoval(t.Context(), cfg, root, false, false)
21	 _, missingErr := submodule.InspectRemoval(t.Context(), cfg, root, true, false)
22	 t.Logf("no child Git stores: without recursive=%v; recursive=%v", plainErr, missingErr)
23	 if missingErr != nil { t.Errorf("BUG: never-initialized checkout with no module storage cannot be removed: %v", missingErr) }

16	
17	// Recover restores interrupted cleanup. A previous remote proof never
18	// authorizes deletion of the quarantined data during recovery.
19	func Recover(ctx context.Context, journalPath string, check func(context.Context, string) error, dryRun bool) error {
20		journalPath, err := filepath.Abs(journalPath)
21		if err != nil {
22			return err
23		}
24		area := filepath.Dir(journalPath)
25		if filepath.Base(journalPath) != "journal.json" || !strings.HasPrefix(filepath.Base(area), ".dev-submodule-retirement-") {
26			return errors.New("not a submodule removal journal")
27		}
28		held, areaIdentity, err := safefile.OpenRoot(area)
29		if err != nil {
30			return err
31		}
32		info, err := held.Lstat("journal.json")
33		if err != nil {
34			held.Close()
35			return err
36		}
37		data, _, err := safefile.ReadStableRegular(ctx, held, "journal.json", info, 1024*1024)
38		held.Close()
39		if err != nil {
40			return err
41		}
42		area, err = pathx.Canonical(area)
43		if err != nil {
44			return err
45		}
46		if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(area, areaIdentity); err != nil {
47			return err
48		}
49		var j removalJournal
50		if err = json.Unmarshal(data, &j); err != nil {
51			return err
52		}
53		if j.Version != 1 || j.Root == "" || j.GitDir == "" || j.Repository == "" || j.Branch == "" || j.Head == "" {
54			return errors.New("incomplete removal journal")
55		}
56		if filepath.Dir(j.Root) != filepath.Dir(area) {
57			return errors.New("journal is not beside its recorded worktree")
58		}
59		r, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, j.Repository)
60		if err != nil {
61			return err
62		}
63		if inside, err := pathx.Contains(r.MainRoot, j.Root); err != nil || inside {
64			return errors.New("recovery target is inside the canonical repository")
65		}
66		if inside, err := pathx.Contains(filepath.Join(r.GitCommonDir, "worktrees"), j.GitDir); err != nil || !inside {
67			return errors.New("journal Git directory is not private worktree metadata")
68		}
69		for _, m := range j.Moves {
70			if filepath.Dir(m.To) != area || (!strings.HasPrefix(filepath.Base(m.To), "checkout-") && filepath.Base(m.To) != "git-modules") {
71				return errors.New("journal contains an unsafe quarantine path")
72			}
73			inside, err := pathx.Contains(j.Root, m.From)
74			if err != nil {
75				return err
76			}
77			if m.From == j.Root || (!inside && m.From != filepath.Join(j.GitDir, "modules")) {
78				return errors.New("journal contains an unsafe restore path")
79			}
80		}
81		if dryRun {
82			return nil
83		}
84		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
85		if err != nil {
86			return err
87		}
88		if inside, err := pathx.Contains(j.Root, cwd); err != nil || inside {
89			return errors.New("recover from outside the target worktree")
90		}
91		return gitx.WithLifecycleLock(ctx, r.GitCommonDir, func() error {
92			if check != nil {
93				if err := check(ctx, j.Root); err != nil {
94					return err
95				}
96			}
97			if _, err := os.Lstat(j.Root); os.IsNotExist(err) {
98				head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, r.MainRoot, "rev-parse", "refs/heads/"+j.Branch)
99				if err != nil || head != j.Head {
100					return errors.New("retained outer branch changed; recovery requires inspection")
101				}
102				if err := gitx.AddWorktree(ctx, r.MainRoot, j.Root, j.Branch, j.Head); err != nil {
103					return err
104				}
105			} else if err != nil {
106				return err
107			}
108			current, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, j.Root)
109			if err != nil {
110				return err
111			}
112			head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, j.Root, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
113			if err != nil {
114				return err
115			}
116			if !current.IsLinkedWorktree || current.GitDir != j.GitDir || head != j.Head {
117				return errors.New("original worktree identity was reused; quarantine retained")
118			}
119			for i := len(j.Moves) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
120				if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(area, areaIdentity); err != nil {
121					return err
122				}
123				m := j.Moves[i]
124				info, err := os.Lstat(m.To)
125				if os.IsNotExist(err) {
126					continue
127				}
128				if err != nil {
129					return err
130				}
131				if !info.IsDir() || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
132					return errors.New("quarantined directory identity changed")
133				}
134				if existing, err := os.Lstat(m.From); err == nil {
135					if !m.Empty || !existing.IsDir() || existing.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
136						return fmt.Errorf("restore path reused: %s; quarantine retained", m.From)
137					}
138					if err := os.Remove(m.From); err != nil {
139						return fmt.Errorf("restore path is not empty: %s; quarantine retained", m.From)
140					}
141				} else if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
142					return err
143				}
144				if err := os.Rename(m.To, m.From); err != nil {
145					return fmt.Errorf("restore %s: %w; journal retained", m.From, err)
146				}
147			}
148			if _, err := gitx.SubmodulesOf(ctx, j.Root); err != nil {
149				return err
150			}
151			if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(area, areaIdentity); err != nil {
152				return err
153			}
154			return os.RemoveAll(area)
155		})
156	}
157

this level, catching real bugs matters more than avoiding false positives — a

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (5 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 8 each)

Run **10 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 8 candidate findings**. Do NOT let one angle's conclusions
suppress another's — if two angles flag the same line for different reasons,
record both.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Angle D — language-pitfall specialist

Scan for the classic pitfalls of the diff's language/framework — for example:
JS falsy-zero, `==` coercion, closure-captured loop var; Python mutable default
args, late-binding closures; Go nil-map write, range-var capture; SQL injection;
timezone/DST drift; float equality. Flag any instance the diff introduces.

### Angle E — wrapper/proxy correctness

When the PR adds or modifies a type that wraps another (cache, proxy, decorator,
adapter): check that every method routes to the wrapped instance and not back
through a registry/session/global — e.g. a caching provider holding a
`delegate` field that resolves IDs via `session.get(...)` instead of
`delegate.get(...)` will re-enter the cache or recurse. Also check that the
wrapper forwards all the methods the callers actually use.

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity. Do NOT drop on uncertainty.

Take one more pass (same context — no subagent) as a fresh reviewer who has the deduplicated list. Re-read

import (

func TestCleanupRegressionEmptyDirectoryRemoval(t *testing.T) {
	for _, kind := range []string{"empty", "nonempty", "file", "replaced-directory", "symlink", "cancelled"} {
		t.Run(kind, func(t *testing.T) {
			base := t.TempDir()
			path := filepath.Join(base, "child")
			if err := os.Mkdir(path, 0700); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
			root, _, err := OpenRoot(base)
			if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
			defer root.Close()
			expected, err := root.Lstat("child")
			if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
			ctx := t.Context()
			switch kind {
			case "nonempty":
				if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(path, "keep"), []byte("keep"), 0600); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
			case "file", "replaced-directory", "symlink":
				if err := os.Rename(path, filepath.Join(base, "original")); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
				switch kind {
				case "file": err = os.WriteFile(path, []byte("keep"), 0600)
				case "replaced-directory": err = os.Mkdir(path, 0700)
				case "symlink":
					err = os.Symlink(t.TempDir(), path)
					if err != nil { t.Skipf("symlink creation unavailable: %v", err) }
				}
				if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
			case "cancelled":
				var cancel context.CancelFunc
				ctx, cancel = context.WithCancel(ctx)
				cancel()
			}
			err = RemoveEmptyChildDir(ctx, root, "child", expected)
			if kind == "empty" {
				if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
				if _, err := os.Lstat(path); !os.IsNotExist(err) { t.Fatalf("directory remains: %v", err) }
			} else {
				if err == nil { t.Fatalf("accepted %s", kind) }
				if _, err := os.Lstat(path); err != nil { t.Fatalf("removed protected path: %v", err) }
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCleanupRegressionEmptyDirectoryPortableNames(t *testing.T) {
	base := t.TempDir()
	if err := os.Mkdir(filepath.Join(base, "child"), 0700); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
	root, _, err := OpenRoot(base)
	if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
	defer root.Close()
	expected, err := root.Lstat("child")
	if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
	for _, name := range []string{"", ".", "..", "child/..", `child\..`, "C:child", "child:stream", "NUL", "child."} {
		if err := RemoveEmptyChildDir(t.Context(), root, name, expected); err == nil { t.Errorf("accepted %q", name) }
	}
	if err := RemoveEmptyChildDir(t.Context(), root, "child", nil); err == nil { t.Fatal("missing expected identity accepted") }
	if err := RemoveEmptyChildDir(t.Context(), nil, "child", expected); err == nil { t.Fatal("nil parent accepted") }
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(base, "child")); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
}

// The backend's final context check provides a deterministic external-writer
// interleaving immediately after identity checks and before native deletion.
// Value intentionally does not expose an embedded cancelCtx to context.Cause.
type directoryMutationContext struct {
	context.Context
	mutate func()
}
func (c *directoryMutationContext) Value(any) any { return nil }
func (c *directoryMutationContext) Err() error {
	if c.mutate != nil {
		mutate := c.mutate
		c.mutate = nil
		mutate()
	}
	return nil
}

func TestCleanupRegressionEmptyDirectoryLateSubstitution(t *testing.T) {
	for _, kind := range []string{"file", "nonempty"} {
		t.Run(kind, func(t *testing.T) {
			base := t.TempDir()
			path := filepath.Join(base, "child")
			if err := os.Mkdir(path, 0700); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
			root, _, err := OpenRoot(base)
			if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
			defer root.Close()
			expected, err := root.Lstat("child")
			if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
			mutated := false
			ctx := &directoryMutationContext{Context: context.Background(), mutate: func() {
				mutated = true
				if kind == "file" {
					if err := os.Rename(path, filepath.Join(base, "reviewed")); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
					if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte("keep"), 0600); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
				} else if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(path, "keep"), []byte("keep"), 0600); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
			}}
			err = removeEmptyChildDirNative(ctx, root, "child", expected)
			if !mutated { t.Fatalf("native deletion did not reach the race boundary: %v", err) }
			file := path
			if kind == "nonempty" {
				file = filepath.Join(path, "keep")
				if err == nil { t.Fatal("removed nonempty directory") }
			}
			data, readErr := os.ReadFile(file)
			if readErr != nil || string(data) != "keep" { t.Fatalf("late file was removed: %q %v (delete: %v)", data, readErr, err) }
		})
	}
}

}

101	## Behavioral contracts
102	
103	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
104	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
105	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
106	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
107	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
108	- Submodule initialization uses committed gitlinks, never implicitly advances to `main`. Whole child-clone disposal requires explicit recursive approval and fresh recovery proof for its private refs/objects; outer and shared canonical repositories are retained. Local graph refresh never performs remote proof. Child task/runtime/artifact claims block parent disposal.
109	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
110	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
111	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
112	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
113	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
114	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
115	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
116	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. 117	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.

127	## Versioning and changelog
128	
129	The current published baseline is `v0.2.39` (2026-09-17). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
130	
131	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
132	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
133	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
134	
135	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
136	
137	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
138	
139	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
140	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
141	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
142	
143	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
144	
145	For a release:
146	
147	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
148	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
149	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
150	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
151	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
152	
153	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
154	
155	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
156	
157	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
158	
159	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
160	
161	| Change | Required synchronization |
162	|---|---|
163	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
164	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
165	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
166	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
167	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
168	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
169	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
170	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
171	
172	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
173	
174	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
175	
176	## Hygiene and skill batch operations
177	
178	`internal/hygiene` owns per-repository setup plans and batch ledgers. REPOS and
179	`hygiene manage` are adapters; JSON batch management previews only. Keep legacy
180	artifact finalizers until their independent lifecycle is replaced. Cached machine
181	privacy imports use only bounded local cache readers and revalidate their source.
182	`internal/agentskill` owns selected-removal policy: exact native names/agent scopes
183	or bundled manifests, source/ownership/dependency proof and postconditions under
184	the provider lease. Never infer complete Windows validation from an advisory
185	step's success conclusion; inspect logs and require the dedicated native gates.
186	
187	## Agent history policy
188	
189	`dev help ai-artifacts` separates source retention, archive location, protection
190	and distribution. New configuration is opt-in. Sources are SpecStory Markdown or
191	explicit files; provider IDs name the originating agent. Do not infer writer exit
192	from byte stability or close agents to finalize evidence. Archive mode verifies
193	ignored bytes before cleanup; existing tracked intents retain their original lane.
194	`git-filter-repo` only operates on new verified copies. Ordinary migration never
195	rewrites source refs or published tags, and raw backups are not secret audits.

46	func (l *removalLayout) record(path string, root *os.Root, info fs.FileInfo, listing bool) error {
47		if len(l.Directories)+len(l.Absent) >= removalLayoutLimit {
48			return errors.New("submodule removal layout exceeds inspection limit")
49		}
50		identity, err := gitx.DirectoryIdentity(path)
51		if err != nil {
52			return err
53		}
54		d := layoutDirectory{Identity: identity, Mode: uint32(info.Mode()), info: info}
55		if prior, ok := l.Directories[path]; ok {
56			if !os.SameFile(prior.info, info) {
57				return safefile.ErrChanged
58			}
59			d = prior
60		}
61		if listing {
62			file, err := root.Open(".")
63			if err != nil {
64				return err
65			}
66			names, readErr := file.Readdirnames(removalLayoutLimit + 1)
67			closeErr := file.Close()
68			if readErr != nil && !errors.Is(readErr, io.EOF) {
69				return readErr
70			}
71			if closeErr != nil {
72				return closeErr
73			}
74			if len(names) > removalLayoutLimit {
75				return errors.New("submodule administration listing exceeds inspection limit")
76			}
77			sort.Strings(names)
78			d.Listing, d.Listed = names, true
79		}
80		if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(path, info); err != nil {
81			return err
82		}
83		l.Directories[path] = d
84		return nil

89	func (l *removalLayout) path(ctx context.Context, base, relative string, empty bool) error {
90		root, info, err := safefile.OpenRoot(base)
91		if err != nil {
92			return err
93		}
94		defer func() { root.Close() }()
95		if err := l.record(base, root, info, false); err != nil {
96			return err
97		}
98		parts := strings.Split(filepath.ToSlash(relative), "/")
99		if relative == "." {
100			parts = nil
101		}
102		if len(parts) > 64 {
103			return errors.New("submodule layout path exceeds inspection depth")
104		}
105		path := base
106		for _, name := range parts {
107			if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
108				return err
109			}
110			child, childInfo, err := safefile.OpenChildRoot(root, name)
111			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
112				// A failed open alone is not an absence observation: prove the name
113				// really is missing relative to the same held ancestor.

115					return errors.Join(safefile.ErrChanged, statErr)
116				}

118				return safefile.VerifyRoot(path, info)
119			}
120			if err != nil {
121				return err
122			}
123			if err := safefile.VerifyRoot(path, info); err != nil {
124				child.Close()
125				return err
126			}
127			root.Close()
128			root, info, path = child, childInfo, filepath.Join(path, name)
129			if err := l.record(path, root, info, false); err != nil {
130				return err
131			}

138				return fmt.Errorf("uninitialized submodule %s contains retained data", relative)
139			}
140		}

144	func observeRemovalLayout(ctx context.Context, repo gitx.Repo, g gitx.SubmoduleGraph) (*removalLayout, error) {
145		l := &removalLayout{Directories: map[string]layoutDirectory{}, Absent: map[string]bool{}}
146		for _, path := range []string{repo.Root, repo.GitDir} {
147			if err := l.path(ctx, path, ".", false); err != nil {
148				return l, err

150		}

152		modules := filepath.Join(repo.GitDir, "modules")

154			if err := l.path(ctx, repo.Root, n.Path, !n.Initialized); err != nil {
155				return l, fmt.Errorf("submodule %s: %w", n.Path, err)
156			}
157			if n.Initialized {
158				known[n.GitDir] = true
159				l.Initialized = append(l.Initialized, n.Path)
160			}
161		}
162		sort.Strings(l.Initialized)
163		if err := l.storage(ctx, repo.GitDir, "modules", known, 0); err != nil {
164			return l, err
165		}
166		for path := range known {
167			if _, ok := l.Directories[path]; !ok {
168				return l, fmt.Errorf("initialized submodule storage %s is outside observed %s", path, modules)
169			}
170		}
171		return l, nil

174	func (l *removalLayout) storage(ctx context.Context, parentPath, name string, known map[string]bool, depth int) error {
175		if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
176			return err
177		}
178		if depth > 64 {
179			return errors.New("submodule administration exceeds inspection depth")
180		}
181		parent, parentInfo, err := safefile.OpenRoot(parentPath)
182		if err != nil {
183			return err
184		}
185		defer parent.Close()
186		if err := l.record(parentPath, parent, parentInfo, false); err != nil {
187			return err
188		}
189		root, info, err := safefile.OpenChildRoot(parent, name)
190		path := filepath.Join(parentPath, name)
191		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {

193				return errors.Join(safefile.ErrChanged, statErr)
194			}
195			l.Absent[path] = true
196			return safefile.VerifyRoot(parentPath, parentInfo)

198		if err != nil {

203			return err
204		}
205		if known[path] {

207			// private Git entries remain listed and inspectPrivateState checks them.
208			d := l.Directories[path]

214			}
215			d.Listing = names

227		}

232		if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
233			return err

236		if err != nil {

252	// Staging relocates only initialized directories. Empty children and missing
253	// components still carry their original exact identity/absence at the mapped
254	// location, including those inside a moved initialized parent.
255	func (p *Removal) verifyStagedLayout(ctx context.Context, moves []moveRecord) error {
256		mapPath := func(path string) string {
257			best := ""
258			mapped := path
259			for _, move := range moves {
260				if (path == move.From || strings.HasPrefix(path, move.From+string(filepath.Separator))) && len(move.From) > len(best) {
261					best = move.From
262					mapped = move.To + strings.TrimPrefix(path, move.From)
263				}
264			}
265			return mapped
266		}
267		known := map[string]bool{}
268		for _, n := range p.initialized {
269			known[n.GitDir] = true
270		}
271		for path, expected := range p.layout.Directories {
272			if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
273				return err
274			}
275			mapped := mapPath(path)
276			root, info, err := safefile.OpenRoot(mapped)
277			if err != nil {
278				return err
279			}
280			if !os.SameFile(expected.info, info) {
281				root.Close()
282				return safefile.ErrChanged
283			}
284			l := &removalLayout{Directories: map[string]layoutDirectory{}, Absent: map[string]bool{}}
285			err = l.record(mapped, root, info, expected.Listed)
286			root.Close()
287			if err != nil {
288				return err
289			}
290			actual := l.Directories[mapped]
291			if known[path] {

295						names = append(names, name)
296					}
297				}
298				actual.Listing = names
299			}
300			a, _ := json.Marshal(actual)
301			b, _ := json.Marshal(expected)
302			if string(a) != string(b) {
303				return fmt.Errorf("staged submodule layout changed at %s", path)
304			}
305		}
306		for path := range p.layout.Absent {
307			mapped := mapPath(path)

344	func (p *Removal) applyEmpty(ctx context.Context, check func(context.Context, string) error, removeOuter func() error) (err error) {
345		// This lane creates no proof repository, lease, journal or quarantine.
346		l, err := observeRemovalLayout(ctx, p.Repository, p.Graph)
347		if err != nil {
348			return err
349		}
350		if l.fingerprint() != p.LayoutFingerprint {
351			return errors.New("stale submodule removal layout")
352		}
353		var pruned []string
354		defer func() {
355			if err != nil && len(pruned) > 0 {
356				err = &PrunedDirectoriesError{Paths: append([]string(nil), pruned...), Cause: err}
357			}
358		}()
359		sort.Slice(l.scaffolds, func(i, j int) bool {
360			if len(l.scaffolds[i]) != len(l.scaffolds[j]) {
361				return len(l.scaffolds[i]) > len(l.scaffolds[j])
362			}
363			return l.scaffolds[i] < l.scaffolds[j]
364		})
365		for _, path := range l.scaffolds {
366			if err := p.revalidateLocal(ctx, l); err != nil {
367				return err
368			}
369			if check != nil {
370				if err := check(ctx, p.Graph.Root); err != nil {
371					return err
372				}
373			}
374			if err := p.revalidateLayout(ctx, l); err != nil {
375				return err
376			}

383				parent.Close()

386			err = safefile.RemoveEmptyChildDir(ctx, parent, filepath.Base(path), l.Directories[path].info)

388			if err != nil {
389				return err
390			}
391			rel, _ := filepath.Rel(p.Repository.GitDir, path)
392			pruned = append(pruned, filepath.ToSlash(rel))
393			delete(l.Directories, path)
394			if path == filepath.Join(p.Repository.GitDir, "modules") {
395				l.Absent[path] = true
396			} else {

398				var names []string
399				for _, name := range d.Listing {
400					if name != filepath.Base(path) {
401						names = append(names, name)
402					}
403				}
404				d.Listing = names
405				l.Directories[parentPath] = d
406			}

409		if err := p.revalidateLocal(ctx, l); err != nil {
410			return err

414				return err
415			}
416		}
417		if err := p.revalidateLocal(ctx, l); err != nil {
418			return err

14	// RemoveEmptyChildDir removes only the reviewed empty directory, never a file
15	// substituted at its name. Traversal and identity checks use held roots. Native
16	// directory-only deletion also rejects late content. External writers do not
17	// share our locks: Unix cannot atomically compare an inode and rmdir its name.
18	func RemoveEmptyChildDir(ctx context.Context, parent *os.Root, name string, expected fs.FileInfo) error {
19		if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
20			return err
21		}
22		if err := pathx.ValidatePortableComponent(name, CompiledMaxComponentBytes); err != nil {
23			return err
24		}
25		if expected == nil || unsafeLink(expected) || !expected.IsDir() {
26			return fmt.Errorf("remove empty directory needs a normal directory identity: %w", ErrUnsafeType)
27		}
28		child, info, err := OpenChildRoot(parent, name)
29		if err != nil {
30			return err
31		}
32		defer child.Close()
33		if !os.SameFile(info, expected) {
34			return ErrChanged
35		}
36		file, err := child.Open(".")
37		if err != nil {
38			return err
39		}
40		err = verifyEmptyDirectory(file)
41		closeErr := file.Close()
42		if err := errors.Join(err, closeErr); err != nil {
43			return err
44		}
45		if err := VerifyChildRoot(parent, name, expected); err != nil {
46			return err
47		}
48		return removeEmptyChildDirNative(ctx, parent, name, expected)
49	}
50	
51	func verifyEmptyDirectory(file *os.File) error {
52		names, err := file.Readdirnames(1)
53		if len(names) != 0 {
54			return errors.New("directory is not empty")
55		}
56		if !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
57			if err == nil {
58				return io.ErrNoProgress
59			}
60			return err
61		}
62		return nil
63	}

13	func removeEmptyChildDirNative(ctx context.Context, parent *os.Root, name string, expected fs.FileInfo) error {
14		file, err := parent.Open(".")
15		if err != nil {
16			return err
17		}
18		defer file.Close()
19		held, err := file.Stat()
20		if err != nil {
21			return err
22		}
23		root, err := parent.Stat(".")
24		if err != nil {
25			return err
26		}

28			return ErrChanged
29		}

31			return err
32		}
33		if err := context.Cause(ctx); err != nil {
34			return err
35		}
36		// Never fall back to unlink: a file substituted after the last check must
37		// survive. A directory substituted by a raw writer in this narrow interval
38		// cannot be compared atomically with rmdir on Unix.
39		return unix.Unlinkat(int(file.Fd()), name, unix.AT_REMOVEDIR)

349	// VerifyRemote fetches into a fresh isolated bare repository. Reachability is
350	// proven against the remote's advertised refs, never local tracking refs or
351	// objects borrowed from the checkout about to be removed.
352	func (p *Removal) VerifyRemote(ctx context.Context) error {
353		if p == nil {
354			return nil
355		}
356		p.remoteVerified = false
357		p.remoteRefs = map[string]string{}
358		if !p.observed || (!p.publication && !p.cleanupConsent) {
359			return errors.New("submodule recovery requires a complete observation and explicit cleanup consent")
360		}
361		if !p.publication {
362			if err := p.revalidateLocal(ctx, p.layout); err != nil {
363				return err
364			}
365		}
366		var removedIdentities []os.FileInfo
367		for _, node := range p.initialized {
368			for _, path := range []string{filepath.Join(p.Graph.Root, filepath.FromSlash(node.Path)), node.GitDir, filepath.Join(p.Graph.Root, filepath.FromSlash(node.Path), ".git")} {
369				info, err := os.Stat(path)
370				if err != nil {
371					return err
372				}
373				removedIdentities = append(removedIdentities, info)
374			}
375		}
376		for _, n := range p.initialized {
377			child := filepath.Join(p.Graph.Root, filepath.FromSlash(n.Path))
378			url, err := gitx.Run(ctx, child, "remote", "get-url", "origin")
379			if err != nil {
380				return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s has no recovery origin", n.Path)
381			}
382			expected, err := gitx.SubmoduleSourceURL(ctx, filepath.Join(p.Graph.Root, filepath.FromSlash(n.Parent)), n.URL)
383			if err != nil || expected != url {
384				return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s recovery origin differs from its declared source", n.Path)
385			}
386			local, localErr := localRecoveryPath(child, url)
387			if localErr != nil {
388				return localErr
389			}
390			if local != "" {
391				info, err := os.Stat(local)
392				if err != nil {
393					return fmt.Errorf("recovery origin is unavailable: %w", err)
394				}
395				for _, removed := range removedIdentities {
396					if os.SameFile(info, removed) {
397						return errors.New("recovery origin depends on the workspace being removed")
398					}
399				}
400				for _, removedRoot := range []string{p.Graph.Root, p.Repository.GitDir} {
401					inside, err := pathx.Contains(removedRoot, local)
402					if err != nil || inside {
403						return errors.New("recovery origin depends on the workspace being removed")
404					}
405				}
406			}
407			before, err := gitx.Run(ctx, child, "ls-remote", "--refs", "origin")
408			if err != nil {
409				return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s recovery origin unavailable", n.Path)
410			}
411			proof, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "dev-submodule-proof-")
412			if err != nil {
413				return err
414			}
415			err = func() error {
416				defer os.RemoveAll(proof)
417				if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, proof, "init", "--bare", "--quiet"); err != nil {
418					return err
419				}
420				if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, proof, "fetch", "--quiet", "--no-tags", "--no-write-fetch-head", "--", url, "+refs/*:refs/*"); err != nil {
421					return errors.New("could not fetch isolated recovery proof")
422				}
423				after, err := gitx.Run(ctx, child, "ls-remote", "--refs", "origin")
424				if err != nil || before != after {
425					return errors.New("recovery remote refs changed during proof")
426				}
427				objects, err := gitx.Run(ctx, proof, "rev-list", "--objects", "--all")
428				if err != nil {
429					return err
430				}
431				available := map[string]bool{}
432				for _, line := range strings.Split(objects, "\n") {
433					if f := strings.Fields(line); len(f) > 0 {
434						available[f[0]] = true
435					}
436				}
437				advertised := map[string]string{}
438				for _, line := range strings.Split(after, "\n") {
439					if f := strings.Fields(line); len(f) == 2 {
440						advertised[f[1]] = f[0]
441					}
442				}
443				refs, err := gitx.Run(ctx, child, "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname) %(objectname)")
444				if err != nil {
445					return err
446				}
447				for _, line := range strings.Split(refs, "\n") {
448					f := strings.Fields(line)
449					if len(f) != 2 {
450						continue
451					}
452					if strings.HasPrefix(f[0], "refs/remotes/") {
453						continue
454					}
455					if advertised[f[0]] == "" || !available[f[1]] {
456						return fmt.Errorf("local ref %s is not preserved by the recovery remote", f[0])
457					}
458				}
459				if !available[n.HEAD] || !available[n.Gitlink] {
460					return errors.New("HEAD or gitlink is not remotely reachable")
461				}
462				reflog, err := gitx.Run(ctx, child, "reflog", "show", "--all", "--format=%H")
463				if err != nil {
464					return err
465				}
466				for _, oid := range strings.Fields(reflog) {
467					if !available[oid] {
468						return errors.New("reflog retains a local-only commit")
469					}
470				}
471				unreachable, err := gitx.Run(ctx, child, "fsck", "--unreachable", "--no-reflogs", "--no-progress")
472				if err != nil {
473					return errors.New("object integrity inspection failed")
474				}
475				for _, line := range strings.Split(unreachable, "\n") {
476					f := strings.Fields(line)
477					if len(f) == 3 && (f[0] == "unreachable" || f[0] == "dangling") && !available[f[2]] {
478						return errors.New("unreachable local objects require preservation")
479					}
480				}
481				if p.Merged {
482					for _, m := range p.Workspace.Members {
483						if m.Path == n.Path {
484							base := strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimPrefix(m.Base, "refs/remotes/"), "origin/")
485							if !strings.HasPrefix(base, "refs/") {
486								base = "refs/heads/" + base
487							}

489								return fmt.Errorf("member is not integrated into %s", base)
490							}
491						}
492					}
493				}
494				return nil
495			}()
496			if err != nil {
497				return fmt.Errorf("submodule %s: %w", n.Path, err)
498			}
499			p.remoteRefs[n.Path] = before
500		}
501		p.remoteVerified = true
502		return nil
503	}

505	func localRecoveryPath(cwd, source string) (string, error) {
506		if strings.HasPrefix(source, "file://") {
507			u, err := url.Parse(source)
508			if err != nil {
509				return "", errors.New("invalid recovery file URL")
510			}
511			if u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "" || u.User != nil {
512				return "", errors.New("ambiguous recovery file URL")
513			}
514			path := u.Path
515			if u.Host != "" && !strings.EqualFold(u.Host, "localhost") {
516				path = "//" + u.Host + path
517			}
518			if filepath.Separator == '\\' && len(path) > 2 && path[0] == '/' && path[2] == ':' {
519				path = path[1:]
520			}
521			return filepath.FromSlash(path), nil
522		}
523		if filepath.IsAbs(source) {
524			return source, nil
525		}
526		if !strings.Contains(source, ":") {
527			return filepath.Join(cwd, source), nil
528		}
529		return "", nil
530	}
