package submodule

import (
	"errors"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/gitx"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/safefile"
)

func TestCleanupRegressionSubmoduleLayoutPathSpelling(t *testing.T) {
	for _, initialized := range []bool{false, true} {
		state := "empty"
		if initialized {
			state = "initialized"
		}
		for _, spelling := range []string{"native", "git-slashes", "git-slashes-dot"} {
			t.Run(state+"-"+spelling, func(t *testing.T) {
				base := t.TempDir()
				repo := gitx.Repo{Root: filepath.Join(base, "Checkout"), GitDir: filepath.Join(base, "Admin")}
				modules := filepath.Join(repo.GitDir, "modules")
				store := filepath.Join(modules, "Child")
				for _, path := range []string{filepath.Join(repo.Root, "Child"), filepath.Join(modules, "unused", "nested")} {
					if err := os.MkdirAll(path, 0700); err != nil {
						t.Fatal(err)
					}
				}
				graph := gitx.SubmoduleGraph{Root: repo.Root, Nodes: []gitx.SubmoduleNode{{Path: "Child"}}}
				if initialized {
					if err := os.Mkdir(store, 0700); err != nil {
						t.Fatal(err)
					}
					if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(store, "HEAD"), []byte("retained repository data\n"), 0600); err != nil {
						t.Fatal(err)
					}
					graph.Nodes[0].Initialized = true
					graph.Nodes[0].GitDir, graph.Nodes[0].CommonDir = store, store
				}
				baseline, err := observeRemovalLayout(t.Context(), repo, graph)
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				adminInfo := baseline.Directories[repo.GitDir].info
				spell := func(path string) string {
					if spelling == "native" {
						return path
					}
					path = filepath.ToSlash(path)
					if spelling == "git-slashes-dot" {
						// Also exercise equivalent non-clean spelling on POSIX,
						// where Git and filepath otherwise use the same separator.
						path += "/."
					}
					return path
				}
				repo.Root, repo.GitDir = spell(repo.Root), spell(repo.GitDir)
				if initialized {
					graph.Nodes[0].GitDir = spell(store)
				}
				layout, err := observeRemovalLayout(t.Context(), repo, graph)
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				if layout.fingerprint() != baseline.fingerprint() {
					t.Fatal("path spelling changed physical layout authority")
				}
				// Empty-root pruning looks up the parent via filepath.Dir, not
				// the original Git-returned spelling. Its identity must be held.
				if !os.SameFile(adminInfo, layout.Directories[filepath.Dir(modules)].info) {
					t.Fatal("native parent lookup lost administration identity")
				}
				if !initialized {
					return
				}
				// Staging must recognize the same known store after a native-path
				// move, including the lease entries excluded during observation.
				if err := os.Mkdir(filepath.Join(store, "dev-taskflow"), 0700); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				staged := filepath.Join(base, "git-modules")
				if err := os.Rename(modules, staged); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				if err := inspectModuleStorage(staged, graph.Nodes, modules); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				plan := &Removal{layout: layout, initialized: graph.Nodes}
				if err := plan.verifyStagedLayout(t.Context(), []moveRecord{{From: modules, To: staged}}); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
			})
		}
	}
}

func TestCleanupRegressionSubmoduleLayoutPathSpellingRejectsReplacement(t *testing.T) {
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "Directory")
	if err := os.Mkdir(path, 0700); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	layout := &removalLayout{Directories: map[string]layoutDirectory{}, Absent: map[string]bool{}}
	if err := layout.path(t.Context(), path, ".", true); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	before := layout.fingerprint()
	alternate := filepath.ToSlash(path) + "/."
	if err := layout.path(t.Context(), alternate, ".", true); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if layout.fingerprint() != before || len(layout.Directories) != 1 {
		t.Fatal("equivalent path spelling created another directory identity")
	}
	if err := os.Rename(path, path+"-original"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := os.Mkdir(path, 0700); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := layout.path(t.Context(), alternate, ".", true); !errors.Is(err, safefile.ErrChanged) {
		t.Fatalf("replacement accepted through alternate path spelling: %v", err)
	}
}

package artifact

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
)

func TestCleanupRegressionArtifactStoreMissingDirectory(t *testing.T) {
	root := t.TempDir()
	file := filepath.Join(root, "not-a-directory")
	if err := os.WriteFile(file, []byte("not an empty intent store\n"), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name    string
		path    string
		missing bool
		bad     bool
	}{
		{name: "existing empty directory", path: root},
		{name: "missing directory", path: filepath.Join(root, "missing"), missing: true},
		{name: "missing parents", path: filepath.Join(root, "missing", "nested"), missing: true},
		{name: "ordinary file", path: file, bad: true},
		{name: "file ancestor", path: filepath.Join(file, "nested"), bad: true},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			missing, err := missingStoreDirectory(tc.path)
			if (err != nil) != tc.bad || missing != tc.missing {
				t.Fatalf("absence classification: missing=%v err=%v", missing, err)
			}
			intents, err := NewStore(tc.path).List()
			if (err != nil) != tc.bad || len(intents) != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("store list: %v, %v", intents, err)
			}
		})
	}
	if data, err := os.ReadFile(file); err != nil || string(data) != "not an empty intent store\n" {
		t.Fatal("store inspection changed the non-directory target", err)
	}
}

```text
Watch a run until it completes, showing its progress.

By default, all steps are displayed. The `--compact` option can be used to only
show the relevant/failed steps.

This command does not support authenticating via fine grained PATs
as it is not currently possible to create a PAT with the `checks:read` permission.


USAGE
  gh run watch <run-id> [flags]

FLAGS
      --compact        Show only relevant/failed steps
      --exit-status    Exit with non-zero status if run fails
  -i, --interval int   Refresh interval in seconds (default 3)

INHERITED FLAGS
      --help                     Show help for command
  -R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO   Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format

EXAMPLES
  # Watch a run until it's done
  $ gh run watch
  
  # Watch a run in compact mode
  $ gh run watch --compact
  
  # Run some other command when the run is finished
  $ gh run watch && notify-send 'run is done!'

LEARN MORE
  Use `gh <command> <subcommand> --help` for more information about a command.
  Read the manual at https://cli.github.com/manual
  Learn about exit codes using `gh help exit-codes`
  Learn about accessibility experiences using `gh help accessibility`

dev version v0.2.39
Manage the repositories under your scan roots, using forge CLIs for remote
inventory, cloning and review operations.

This is the "what projects do I have?" half of dev, kept separate from the
"what am I working on?" half that ls and the task commands answer.

TL;DR: acquire the checkout, then choose how ready it should be

  dev repo new/create --> scaffold --> optional upstream --> cd/open/start
  dev repo clone      --> checkout --> optional setup    --> cd/open/start
  dev repo setup      --> idempotent files/skills/hooks --> review or commit

  Local-only is the default. Project-owned executable config must be trusted
  by its exact content hash before dev runs it.

See also: dev help repositories

Usage:
  dev repo [flags]
  dev repo [command]

Available Commands:
  add-as-submodule Add a known repository or network URL as a submodule of this checkout
  browse           Open the repository homepage, or print its URL without opening
  clone            Clone a repository and optionally apply a setup preset
  context          Print agent-ready Git, worktree, runtime and task context
  list             List every repository under the scan roots
  mark             Add catalog tags or update a repository note
  new              Create a new repository or clone an explicit source
  open             Open a repository in the runtime
  remote           List and search repositories visible through configured forge CLIs
  setup            Apply a scaffold or preview agent-history policy for a repository
  sync             Fetch and prune, reporting what moved

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for repo

Global Flags:
      --allow-shared-checkout   allow a writer claim in a checkout occupied by another live agent
      --color string            colorize human output: auto, always or never (default "auto")
      --config string           path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)
      --no-runtime              do not touch any terminal multiplexer
      --remotes string          path to remotes.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml)
      --runtime string          override runtime backend: herdr, tmux, zellij or none
      --scaffolds string        path to scaffolds.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml)

Use "dev repo [command] --help" for more information about a command.
Show every change stream dev knows about, enriched with live git and
runtime state.

This is the answer to "what am I working on?" — the question a terminal
multiplexer's sidebar gets abused for. Only the state, owner and next action
come from dev's registry; branch, dirty, ahead/behind and the live session are
derived on every run, so the listing cannot go stale.

By default finished tasks are hidden; pass --all to include them.

Usage:
  dev ls [flags]

Aliases:
  ls, list

Flags:
  -a, --all             include done tasks
      --dirty           only tasks with uncommitted changes
  -h, --help            help for ls
      --json            emit JSON for scripting
      --live            only tasks with a running runtime session
      --no-session      skip the runtime query (faster)
  -r, --repo string     only tasks whose repo name contains this
  -s, --state strings   only these states (hot, warm, cold, done)

Global Flags:
      --allow-shared-checkout   allow a writer claim in a checkout occupied by another live agent
      --color string            colorize human output: auto, always or never (default "auto")
      --config string           path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)
      --no-runtime              do not touch any terminal multiplexer
      --remotes string          path to remotes.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml)
      --runtime string          override runtime backend: herdr, tmux, zellij or none
      --scaffolds string        path to scaffolds.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml)
```

Print a deterministic Markdown handoff or a versioned JSON report for one repository.

Local Git, task and runtime facts are always collected live. Forge and configured

age and collection errors; --refresh may contact forge providers and fleet hosts.
With no repository argument, the repository containing the current directory is
used, and a linked-worktree current directory remains the selected checkout while
the report still covers the whole clone.

# dev-cli

Git owns durable code; worktrees are local checkouts; runtimes are host-local
sessions; dev records task intent.

## Discover what you need

Use `dev <command> --help` for current syntax and flags, and `dev help <topic>`
for workflow explanations. `dev --help` lists commands; `dev help` lists topics.
Prefer supported `--json` output for automation. Read the relevant command before
mutation: some actions execute immediately, while others require preview/apply.
Do not preload manuals, repeat `dev --skill`, or run diagnostics for every task.

## Preserve these boundaries

- Opening a repository needs no task. Choose direct, branch, or worktree
  deliberately; pass an explicit `--base` for branch/worktree creation. Keep
  managed worktrees outside repositories.
- `dev start` normally prepares a checkout/runtime. Agent launch is explicit.
  Parallel writers need coordinated ownership and verified launch targets.
- Completion, artifact finalization, retirement, and branch deletion are separate.
  Finalize agent artifacts after their writer stops; retire an agent checkout
  externally. A runtime's `done` state does not mean cleanup is safe.
- Unknown or cached observations, merged PRs, and command refusals do not grant
  cleanup authority. Resolve the reported conditions; do not improvise force
  removal or bypass trust checks.

## Read a reference for advanced operations

- Worktree provisioning or cross-host lifecycle: [ownership](references/worktree-ownership.md), [lifecycle](references/task-lifecycle.md).
- Parallel agent launches or prompt transports: [agents](references/parallel-agents.md), [handoffs](references/prompt-handoffs.md).
- History retention: [artifacts](references/ai-artifacts.md).
- Agent completion or cleanup batches: [retirement](references/agent-retirement.md), [triage](references/local-triage.md).
- Repository hygiene batches, scans or redaction: [hygiene](references/hygiene.md).
- Repository hooks, publication, or physical organization: [setup](references/repository-bootstrap.md), [bootstrap](references/bootstrap.md).
- SSH dashboard, diagnosis, discovery, tests/activity, keys, credentials and registration: [SSH](references/ssh-hosts.md).
- Dotfile setup, native chezmoi operations, or FLEET host actions: [dotfiles](references/dotfiles.md).
- Skill/MCP/instruction transfers, updates or removal: [transfers](references/agent-interop.md), [maintenance](references/skills-management.md).
- Recursive Git children: [submodules](references/submodules.md).

Use command help and its workflow topic for everyday operations.

## Unexpected dev failures

Read [feedback and repair](references/feedback-and-repair.md). Preserve the
original task; extra investigation, repair, subagents and publication need
explicit consent covering scope and cost.

# Agent history hygiene

Preserve selected agent evidence under the repository's chosen policy. Read
`dev help ai-artifacts` and `dev artifact status` when supported: source tracking,
external archive, protection and distribution are separate choices. Commit
reviewed project knowledge; do not force-add raw history under archive/unmanaged
policy. Verify repository protection from the effective hook chain.

## Prefer the shared dev workflow

When the installed dev supports `hygiene`, use its domain for setup, scans,
private rules and reviewed text changes:

```bash
dev hygiene status
dev hygiene setup --json
dev hygiene setup --apply --plan <id> --yes
dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
dev hygiene scan --scope history --audit --timeout 40m --json
```

`pre-commit` and `gitleaks` are needed for this repository hook recipe. An explicitly unscanned archive copy needs neither. A global `core.hooksPath` can be
correct, but its script may skip all checks when repository configs are absent.
The shared setup preserves existing hooks/comments and refuses an unverified
chain. Repository new/setup's `agent-history-hygiene` initializer uses this same
service. New default hooks block; they do not rewrite or stage files.

Per-repo secret/known/generic policy supports block/warn/off, with private local
overrides and exact reasoned exceptions. Private visibility is advice, never an
automatic exemption. SSH imports are static and reviewed: no DNS, login, Match
exec, private-key reads or rule-value export. Personal rules stay outside Git;
CI checks public rules and must state the missing personal coverage.

Read the bundled dev reference `references/hygiene.md` through `dev help hygiene`
or the public hygiene guide before rule changes or redaction. The CLI supports
all regular text, rather than treating transcripts as the only leak surface.

## Preserve the review trail

1. Identify the exact provider/session UUID from the transcript preamble. Never
   select another session just because its file is newest.
2. Commit product changes and reviewed plans. Follow the selected retention
   policy for raw history; do not broadly stage every agent directory.
3. Use `dev prepare --session provider:uuid` and finalization after its writer
   exits when that lifecycle applies. Byte stability alone is not writer proof.
4. Scan exact staged content. Partial staging must not accidentally stage
   unrelated working-copy edits.
5. In archive mode, raw history may be ignored but must be preserved before
   checkout disposal. In track mode, retain the existing exact-session workflow.
   Exclude conversation evidence from product source archives independently.

Do not close, restart or spawn agents to make hygiene checks pass without the
applicable authorization. A new agent without SpecStory does not stop an older
writer. Preserve the user's original task while offering additional cleanup.

## Reviewed redaction

```bash
dev hygiene redact --report <report-id> --file <reviewed-file> --json
# After reviewing, and after the exact artifact writer exited:
dev hygiene redact --apply --plan <plan-id> --yes --writer-stopped
```

Plans bind native file identity, contents, policy and checkout state. Stale,
modified or partial plans are not authority to overwrite current data. Keep
private recovery and rerun scans/tests after source or configuration changes.
The running transcript is left for a manual external trigger after its writer
stops. No automatic history rewrite, agent launch, commit, push or cleanup occurs.

## External archive workflow

`dev artifact setup` and `dev repo setup --artifacts` preview explicit per-repo
policy. `archive --session provider:uuid` or `--file` creates reviewed snapshots;
apply only after the exact recorder exits. Off/check/redact affect the copy,
not the live source or its index. A disabled scan is recorded as skipped.
Checked snapshots produce masked finding IDs for reasoned fixture exceptions.

Commit reviewed plans with product work before `dev prepare`. New archive intents
bind the destination and policy; redact finalization requires a reviewed
`--archive-plan`. Old tracked intents retain the compatibility scripts below.
Keep those installations while any tracked workflow still depends on them.

`artifact find` reads local committed archive records. Sync and original-backup
publication are explicit Git operations; they never transfer native session DBs.
`artifact migrate` can untrack after verified backup or build separate original,
history and filtered Git copies with commit maps. It never force-pushes source
refs. For historical exposure, use the remediation section rather than treating
path removal as a secret audit. Private raw recovery is not cache.

## Legacy scripts

The scripts remain explicit compatibility utilities. Prefer dev for new setup
and partial-staging-safe edits; a separately published remote redactor hook has
its own version and is not silently updated by dev.

- `find-session.sh --json`: locate candidate transcript/plan metadata.
- `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --dry-run`: inspect exact staging;
  without session-only it may include other dirty artifacts, so use cautiously.
- `scan-staged.sh`: masked JSON-lines locations only, never raw Match/Secret.
  Exit 0 means clean; 20 means candidate findings; legacy `--redact` selects
  exit 10 but only masks output, never modifies files. Exit 30 means missing
  gitleaks; 40 means scanner/JSON/required-parser failure; 2 means not in Git.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py --fix`: explicit legacy artifact mutation. Scanner
  failure is an error, not an empty result; console output uses full sentinels.
  This utility can restage, so use the reviewed dev flow for partial staging.
- `bootstrap-project.sh`: legacy installer; new default templates require dev
  hygiene. Its old `--migrate` targets the separately published remote redactor,
  not the new dev policy migration. Prefer `dev hygiene setup`.

SpecStory may already redact on write, but provider behavior/version is not proof
that every secret class or artifact directory is covered. Preserve existing
`[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` markers. An inert marker must never exempt another secret
on the same line. `.gitleaksignore` contains exact finding fingerprints, not
file/path globs. Portable pattern exceptions need a narrow rule/path/match scope.

## Confirmed historical exposures

Read [remediation](references/remediation.md). First distinguish fixtures,
examples and scanner candidates from confirmed credentials. Revoke/rotate a
confirmed exposed credential at its provider before considering Git history.

Shared main and immutable release tags stay unchanged in ordinary hygiene work.
Correct HEAD in a new commit, and assess old commits, tags, PR references, forks,
clones, caches and distribution artifacts separately. A force push does not erase
all copies or revoke a credential. Personal names, Git author metadata and filenames
also need an explicit impact assessment; text replacement does not rewrite them.

Never echo matching bytes or raw process arguments into a chat to investigate a
finding. Use rule IDs, safe locations and private local reports. Keep raw reports,
recovery images and personal identity dictionaries outside Git and CI logs.

## Validation

Run the skill's fixture tests for redactor/scan-wrapper changes. For dev changes,
run native hygiene/storage/text-transaction tests and the real hook test:

```bash
python scripts/test-hygiene-hooks.py --dev <absolute-built-dev>
```

It uses an isolated HOME/repository and synthetic credentials. Validate same-line
placeholder bypasses, hidden files, partial staging, missing/malformed scanner
results, writer/stale-plan refusal and private recovery. Synchronize embedded
bootstrap assets and both locales of public documentation.

67	## Source categories and upstream sync
68	
69	- `skills/local/` — canonical skills authored in this repository.
70	- `skills/owned/` — first-party skills maintained in another repository owned by the maintainer. Edit the source project, then sync its distribution copy here.
71	- `skills/vendor/` — third-party upstream skills; preserve upstream content.
72	
73	`vendor.yaml` remains the shared sync manifest. `collection: owned` selects
74	`skills/owned/`; an omitted collection defaults to `vendor`. Both support `series`,
75	`license_path`, `frozen`, and upstream commit tracking. Add published owned sources
76	with `scripts/add-vendor.sh --owned <owner/repo/path>`. A cross-repository symlink
77	cannot serve as a distributable copy.
78	
79	An unpublished owned skill may use `pending_upstream: true`. Its bootstrap mirror
80	contains real files but claims no remote SHA; routine sync/check preserves it.
81	After publishing the canonical source, run `scripts/sync-vendor.sh --activate <name>`.
82	Only a successful sync clears pending. See [owned workflow](docs/workflows/adding-owned-skills.md).
83	
84	## Vendor System (also used for owned sources)
85	
86	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
87	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
88	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
89	
90	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
91	
92	`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml` runs `make sync` weekly (Mon 03:00 UTC,
93	plus `workflow_dispatch` with an optional single-skill filter) and opens/updates
94	a PR on the fixed branch `chore/vendor-sync` — never a direct commit to `main`,
95	because vendored content ships to downstream agents via `npx skills update` and
96	a broken frontmatter is silently skipped rather than erroring. PRs created with
97	`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `validate.yml`, so the sync job runs the publish
98	gates itself. A red sync job usually means an upstream rename/removal — handle
99	it with `renamed_from:` or `frozen:` as below.
100	
101	Active series in this repo:
102	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
103	
104	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
105	
106	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
107	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
108	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
109	
110	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
111	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
112	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
113	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
114	  `skills@1.5.24` writes `skills-lock.json`, but a renamed skill is still a
115	  different install ID; review the lock and explicitly reinstall the new name.
116	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
117	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
118	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
119	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
120	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
121	
122	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
123	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
124	
125	## Marketplace Catalog
126	
127	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
128	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
129	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
130	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
131	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
132	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
133	for the full mechanism.
134	
135	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
136	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
137	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
138	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
139	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>`, `./owned/<name>`, or
140	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
141	
142	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
143	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
144	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
145	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
146	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
147	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
148	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
149	within-group caveat in
150	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
151	
152	## SKILL.md Format
153	
154	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
155	
156	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
157	
158	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
159	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
160	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
161	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
162	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
163	
164	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
165	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
166	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
167	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
168	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
169	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
170	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
171	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
172	
173	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
174	
175	```bash
176	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
177	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
178	
179	# …or remove them afterward
180	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
181	```
182	
183	## Project Memory Workflow
184	
185	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
186	
187	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
188	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
189	
190	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
191	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
192	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
193	
194	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
195	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
196	
197	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
198	
199	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
200	
201	   ```bash
202	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
203	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
204	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
205	   ```
206	
207	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
208	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
209	
210	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
211	
212	   ```bash
213	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
214	   ```
215	
216	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
217	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
218	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
219	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
220	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
221	
222	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
223	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
224	   afterwards to catch drift.
225	
226	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
227	
228	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
229	
230	```bash
231	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
232	```
233	
234	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
235	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
236	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
237	
238	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
239	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
240	
241	### External skill / MCP / domain / curiosity catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
242	
243	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
244	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
245	own conventions). It has four subareas:
246	
247	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
248	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
249	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
250	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
251	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
252	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
253	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
254	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
255	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
256	- `docs/catalog/curiosities.md` — docs-only shelf for interesting,
257	  provocative, or highly personal skills that are deliberately excluded
258	  from `vendor.yaml`, marketplace grouping, and routine skill discovery.
259	  Entries use `skipped` with the reason they remain docs-only.
260	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
261	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
262	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
263	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
264	  status / license / last_verified`).
265	
266	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
267	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
268	
269	| Status | Meaning |
270	|---|---|
271	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
272	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
273	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
274	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
275	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
276	
277	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
278	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
279	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
280	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
281	
282	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
283	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
284	
285	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
286	
287	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
288	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
289	
290	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
291	2. The root cause
292	3. The workaround
293	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
294	
295	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
296	the explanation they do not know yet.
297
```

7	## Toolchain and commands
8	
9	- Go 1.26.4 (from `go.mod`) builds the CLI. Python 3.11+ and `uv` are used only for the documentation site.
10	- `make` / `make all` runs `fmt -> vet -> test -> build`. `make fmt` runs `gofmt -w .` and therefore modifies files.
11	- There is no working `make lint` recipe even though `lint` appears in `.PHONY`. The repository's static gates are formatting and `go vet`.
12	
13	```bash
14	make build                         # build ./dev with git-derived version metadata
15	make test                          # go test ./...
16	go test -race -timeout 20m ./...   # CI test command
17	go test ./internal/gitx -run '^TestAddWorktreeUsesExplicitBase$'  # one test
18	go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestName/Subtest$'                  # one subtest
19	make vet                           # go vet ./...
20	files="$(gofmt -l .)" && test -z "$files"  # format check that preserves gofmt failures
21	make e2e                           # real CLI lifecycle in an isolated temporary HOME
22	make skill-sync                    # regenerate command docs, then rebuild embedded skill
23	make skill-check                   # fail when command tree and generated skill reference drift
24	make install                       # binary under PREFIX; skill in user agent directories
25	```
26	
27	Documentation uses the same sequence as CI:
28	
29	```bash
30	uv sync --frozen --extra docs
31	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source
32	uv run mkdocs build --strict
33	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --site site
34	```
35	
36	If generated `docs/llms*.txt` files drift, regenerate them with `uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source --generate-llms` and then rerun the documentation checks.

38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `submodule` owns versioned workspace-member intent and reversible child-clone disposal mechanisms. `gitx` supplies the local gitlink graph; `taskflow` owns recursive lifecycle policy and fresh remote-proof ordering. Gitlink checkouts are legitimate submodules, not nested managed linked worktrees.
56	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints. Lifecycle callers use exact-record revisions and locked compare-and-update/delete transactions rather than treating a previously read task as current.
57	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
58	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
59	- `taskflow` is the UI-agnostic lifecycle authority: it separates recorded intent, typed live observations, immutable guarded plans, approvals, and partial result ledgers. Apply locks and reloads task/Git/worktree/runtime/artifact/remote identity, then rejects stale authority before mutation.
60	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, all registered worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and UI projections consume this joined view.
61	- `agentinterop` owns explicit MCP/skill/instruction transfer plans, guarded apply, stanza/link ownership, private recovery, and optional recipes. Native agent files and skills locks remain authoritative; only explicit preparation/check/launch paths may execute a provider or MCP server. Recovery belongs outside Git, credentials remain runtime references, and native Windows writes fail closed pending verified ACL/identity support.
62	- `triage` owns read-only cross-repository findings, clone-bound local intent, ignored-directory policy and reviewed batch ledgers; `triagetui` is its independent UI. Synchronization uses taskflow plans, and protected cleanup adds guards inside the existing repository lock and immediately before removal. Local scans never reconcile Try catalog entries.
63	- `flowtui` is an independent Bubble Tea model for the preview `dev flow` repository state-machine UI. It receives repository reads and taskflow Plan/Apply callbacks; do not embed it in or add a mode to the dashboard's `tui` model.
64	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
65	- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
66	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
67	- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage`, note FTS, and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
68	- `agenthistory` owns explicit transcript/file retention policy, immutable source-bound archive copies, Git lookup/sync and isolated history migration. Archive bindings/recovery stay in private state, ordinary status never contacts remotes, and source writers/index bytes remain untouched by archiving. `artifact` keeps old commit handoffs and adds externally verified archive receipts; taskflow includes ignored capture readiness in its guarded authority.
69	- `hygiene` owns configurable secret/privacy policy, index/worktree/frozen-history scans, private identity rules and signed replacement plans. Raw findings/recovery stay outside Git; hook setup preserves foreign hooks. Large text transactions explicitly opt into configedit’s Windows backend; existing configuration flows retain their platform contracts.
70	- `feedback` owns durable private reports, sanitized public drafts, revision-bound issue/comment publication receipts and exact repair plans. CLI adapts its repair backend to the shared start flow; agent launch is explicit and prompt context never becomes a public issue body.
71	- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.
72	- `sshhost` owns bounded static discovery of the active user OpenSSH Include closure, canonical files under `~/.ssh/dev.d`, public-key selection/generation/bootstrap, fresh authentication proofs, and the explicit handoff into dev fleet. OpenSSH and plain `ssh -G` remain semantic authority; ordinary setup/remove never rewrite foreign connection definitions, copy private keys, weaken host-key policy, or treat every alias as a fleet member. Explicit format/organize may transform selected user-owned configuration with private guarded recovery; Include restores its caller scope after each file. Named agent providers (Bitwarden, 1Password, Secretive, custom sockets) are located by stat only and never executed; selecting a named-agent key publishes only its public line and writes a v2 fragment (`IdentityAgent`, `SecurityKeyProvider`), which older binaries treat as not dev-owned, while v1 files stay byte-identical. Explicit FIDO generation binds the reviewed native tools/provider, keeps capability observations stat-only, and reports hardware created/unknown effects independently of local publication; only verified SK recovery pairs may be retained. Never use resident-key download or provider loading as a passive probe, and keep automatic Secure Enclave creation blocked until exact native identity mapping is verified.

103	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.

106	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
107	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
108	- Submodule initialization uses committed gitlinks, never implicitly advances to `main`. 115	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.

127	## Versioning and changelog
128	
129	The current published baseline is `v0.2.39` (2026-09-17). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
130	
131	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
132	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
133	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
134	
135	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
136	
137	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
138	
139	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
140	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
141	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
142	
143	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
144	
145	For a release:
146	
147	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
148	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
149	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
150	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
151	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
152	
153	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
154	
155	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.

+# NautilusTrader v1 reports 10x leverage despite migration guidance saying 1x
+
+Observed on 2026-09-17 during paired output-quality evaluations of the
+NautilusTrader skill. Python 3.12.10, `nautilus_trader==1.231.0` and
+`nautilus_trader==2.0.0rc5`, in separate environments on macOS ARM64.
+
+## Symptom
+
+The rc5 `MIGRATION_V2.md` says an omitted backtest leverage changed from v1's
+1x to v2's 10x. The original v1 fixture omitted `default_leverage`, but inspecting
+its initialized margin account produced:
+
+```text
+ACTUAL_DEFAULT_LEVERAGE 10
+```
+
+Consequently, setting `default_leverage=Decimal(1)` as a supposed compatibility
+fix would change this project's original margin assumptions tenfold.
+
+## Cause
+
+The installed 1.231.0 Cython implementation contradicts the general migration
+table. Its `nautilus_trader/backtest/engine.pyx:653-657` selects:
+
+```python
+if default_leverage is None:
+    if account_type == AccountType.MARGIN:
+        default_leverage = Decimal(10)
+    else:
+        default_leverage = Decimal(1)
+```
+
+Version-matched official documentation is useful but is not a substitute for
+checking the actual installed implementation and account state.
+
+## Verified workaround
+
+Inspect the source project's initialized account **before** engine disposal:
+
+```python
+print("ACTUAL_DEFAULT_LEVERAGE", engine.cache.account_for_venue(venue).default_leverage)
+```
+
+Preserve that observed value explicitly in the target `add_venue` configuration.
+In this fixture, 10x preserved 400 fills, 200 closed positions, and a final
+USD 997168.31 balance under both versions. Raw reports still differed at a few
+cent-level fee and margin rounding boundaries; equal ending equity did not
+mean byte-identical economic history.
+
+## Prevention
+
+- Verify source and target defaults independently for the exact release pair.
+- Compare initialized account state, fills and intermediate margin reports,
+  not only return/PnL or whether a script executes.
+- Separate an intentional unleveraged policy change from compatibility work.
+- Treat migration tables as change-discovery aids. Resolve conflicts using
+  installed source and deterministic runtime tests, and document discrepancies.
+- Do not encode an unverified documentation assertion into an eval oracle.
+  This evaluation excluded its original 1x assertion symmetrically after the
+  independent runtime probe disproved it.
+
+## Sources
+
+- [1.231.0 backtest engine](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/blob/v1.231.0/nautilus_trader/backtest/engine.pyx)
+- [2.0.0rc5 migration guide](https://github.com/nautechsystems/nautilus_trader/blob/v2.0.0rc5/MIGRATION_V2.md)
diff --git a/skills/local/nautilus-trader/SKILL.md b/skills/local/nautilus-trader/SKILL.md
index 0f2e0b4..142092d 100644
--- a/skills/local/nautilus-trader/SKILL.md
+++ b/skills/local/nautilus-trader/SKILL.md
@@ -95,6 +95,9 @@ check, `--offline` uses only valid cache, and `stale` must be reported as such.
 3. Check the orders, fills and positions reports, not only final PnL. Generate
    reports before `dispose()`. State the fill model, bar-based execution,
    `default_leverage`, `use_mark_prices` and fees whenever they affect results.
+   For time-based exits, test deadlines between bars and across data gaps. Use
+   engine-clock alerts for elapsed-time guarantees; polling only in `on_bar`
+   limits exit timing to incoming bars, regardless of the configured duration.
 4. Run the saved code in a fresh project-interpreter process. One node per
    process: run configs sequentially with `dispose()`, or in separate processes.
    For wide parameter grids, screen with `vectorbt` and confirm here.
@@ -137,8 +140,9 @@ live node. Hard gates:
 - Wheels cover Python 3.12–3.14 on Linux x86_64/ARM64, macOS ARM64 and Windows
   x86_64. There are no Intel macOS wheels.
 - v2 `Order.avg_px` is a `Decimal`, so `Decimal("0.70000") == 0.7` is `False`.
-- An omitted backtest `default_leverage` means 10x for margin accounts in v2
-  (1x in v1).

 - `generate_*_report()` after `engine.dispose()` returns empty frames without
   an error (verified on 2.0.0rc5).
 - Python callbacks run synchronously on the event thread. Offload blocking I/O

6	# agent-history-hygiene
7	
8	Keep agent transcripts and plan files in the commit that records their feature,
9	without leaking secrets or mutating a file while its recorder is active.
10	
11	Surfaces, separated by purpose:
12	
13	| Surface | Question it answers |
14	|---|---|
15	| `run-specstory-session.sh` | "How do I prove the recorder exited before finalization?" |
16	| `queue-agent-commit.sh` | "How do I queue this exact authorized commit without touching live history?" |
17	| `finalize-agent-commit.sh` | "How is the exact post-session snapshot sanitized and committed?" |
18	| `find-session.sh` | "Which transcript / plan file is my current session?" |
19	| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` | "Which exact agent files belong in the prepared index?" |
20	| `agent-commit-metadata.sh` | "Which provenance trailers belong in the commit?" |
21	| `bootstrap-project.sh` | "How do I install validation-only hooks?" |
22	| `scan-staged.sh` | "Is the effective staged index clean?" |
23	| `probe-specstory-redaction.py` | "What does SpecStory redact natively?" |
24	
25	## Core invariants
26	
27	1. **Commit the transcript and plan with the feature they produced.** Never
28	   ignore `.specstory/history/` or silently drop dirty agent artifacts from the
29	   review trail.
30	2. **SpecStory state is not review history.** Ignore only
31	   `.specstory/.project.json` and `.specstory/statistics.json`; both are
32	   machine-local/regenerable.
33	3. **Quiescence comes before Git history movement.** An active recorder blocks
34	   commit, `pull --rebase`, rebase/update-base, integration, and worktree/session
35	   retirement. Required order:
36	
37	   ```text
38	   recorder quiescence
39	     -> exact artifact + message finalization
40	     -> ordinary hook-enabled commit proven
41	     -> history/ref movement or retirement
42	   ```
43	
44	4. **Provenance comes from the staged snapshot.** Use exact session, transcript,
45	   and plan selectors; never point a trailer at an unstaged artifact or guess an
46	   unknown model.
47	5. **Rotate at the provider before any Git rewrite.** Redaction prevents new
48	   reachability; it does not revoke a credential or erase every local copy.
49	6. **Never use plain `git push --force` as leak remediation.** It can destroy
50	   teammate work and does not remove bytes from existing clones/caches.
51	7. **Shipped files must be scanner-safe.** `npx skills add` installs this whole
52	   directory under a consumer's scan scope. Never embed a literal private-key
53	   header; build it at test runtime or use synthetic placeholders. Enforced by
54	   `tests/test_shipped_file_hygiene.py`.
55	
56	## When to use
57	
58	Use this skill when:
59	
60	- the user asks to commit/save a SpecStory session, transcript, or plan;
61	- dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
62	  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or another configured artifact accompanies a feature;
63	- `.specstory/.project.json` or `statistics.json` keeps churning;
64	- the user asks to install pre-commit/gitleaks for agent artifacts;
65	- a scanner finds a secret in an agent artifact; or
66	- a credential was committed or pushed—read
67	  [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) before any rewrite.
68	
69	Do not use it when the user explicitly wants agent history excluded, or when no
70	agent artifacts exist. If a leak is already on shared `main`/release, do not
71	suggest rewriting that branch; use the remediation runbook.
72	
73	## Default lifecycle: queue now, finalize after exit
74	
75	Read
76	[`references/post-session-finalization.md`](references/post-session-finalization.md)
77	before running or recovering this lifecycle. It defines every state, exit code,
78	recovery action, and no-retry boundary.
79	
80	### 1. Launch the synchronous wrapper
81	
82	From the intended worktree, before starting Claude:
83	
84	```bash
85	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/run-specstory-session.sh \
86	  --allow-commit claude
87	```
88	
89	`--allow-commit` gives the **outer parent** a one-run finalizer capability. It
90	does not let the child infer user consent. The agent still waits for explicit
91	commit authorization before queueing.
92	
93	Do not replace the wrapper with a Stop hook, detached watcher/daemon, or live
94	checkpoint. A Stop hook runs before process/recorder quiescence is proven; a
95	daemon separates recorder lifetime from the session; a live checkpoint commits
96	while the file can still change.
97	
98	### 2. Work normally; stage only feature paths
99	
100	Take the canonical lowercase UUID from Claude `/status`. Resolve the exact
101	SpecStory path and plan policy; if one UUID has multiple rendered aliases, pass
102	both UUID and path to disambiguate.
103	
104	```bash
105	SESSION_ID=01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
106	TRANSCRIPT='.specstory/history/2026-09-01_02-14-50Z.md'
107	PLAN='.claude/plans/exact-change.md'
108	
109	git add -- path/to/feature-a path/to/feature-b
110	```
111	
112	Do **not** stage the live transcript or plan. The finalizer owns exact artifact
113	staging and sanitation after SpecStory exits.
114	
115	### 3. After explicit user commit authorization, queue once
116	
117	Create a UTF-8 base subject/body without lifecycle-managed trailers, then queue
118	with exact selectors:
119	
120	```bash
121	MESSAGE_FILE="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/agent-commit-message.txt"
122	printf '%s\n' \
123	  'feat(scope): summarize the change' \
124	  '' \
125	  'Explain why the change is needed.' > "$MESSAGE_FILE"
126	
127	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/queue-agent-commit.sh \
128	  --commit \
129	  --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
130	  --specstory-path "$TRANSCRIPT" \
131	  --plan "$PLAN" \
132	  --message-file "$MESSAGE_FILE"
133	# Use --no-plan instead of --plan only when no plan exists.
134	```
135	
136	The queue copies only the base message into private per-worktree state. It does
137	not read, stage, scan, redact, or commit the live transcript.
138	
139	On `status=queued`, report **"finalization queued"** and exit the agent session.
140	Perform no further repository/index operation—not even `git status`, a diff, a
141	message edit, sync, or a finalizer call.
142	
143	### 4. Let the outer runner finish
144	
145	Only after child exit `0`, the runner:
146	
147	1. records lifecycle proof;
148	2. runs one exact quiet `specstory sync claude -s UUID --silent`;
149	3. re-proves the exact session/path;
150	4. calls the finalizer with its parent-held token;
151	5. stages and sanitizes exact artifacts in a locked alternate index;
152	6. derives canonical trailers, writes private handoff drafts, and calls one
153	   ordinary `git commit -F` with normal hooks enabled; and
154	7. proves the resulting parent, tree, branch, and
155	   `Agent-History-Request` trailer.
156	
157	Normal pre-commit execution is unsafe while a writer is active: when unstaged
158	changes exist, pre-commit can stash them, check out/modify staged content, then
159	restore the stash. That checkout/restore sequence can race a recorder and
160	clobber, conflict with, or reintroduce bytes. Therefore the pre-commit checker is
161	validation-only; the quiescent finalizer is the sole sanctioned mutator.
162	
163	## Finalization outcomes
164	
165	- **Success (`committed` / exit 0):** an ordinary hook-enabled commit is proven.
166	  Only now may rebase/update-base, integration, or retirement proceed.
167	- **Sanitation (`rotation_required` / exit 10):** exact index and live artifacts
168	  are sanitized, drafts are ready, no commit was attempted. Rotate first, then
169	  resume with fresh `--allow-commit --rotation-confirmed`; recovery does not
170	  restage.
171	- **Hook/commit failure (`commit_failed` / exit 11):** HEAD is unchanged and the
172	  exact prepared tree plus drafts remain. Fix the hook without changing that
173	  snapshot, then make one explicit recovery call with fresh `--allow-commit`.
174	  There is no automatic retry.
175	- **Uncertain outcome (exit 8):** reconcile only. Never issue another commit
176	  automatically; prove the exact HEAD or escalate for inspection.
177	- **Manual handoff:** LazyGit reads per-worktree
178	  `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT`; standard Git uses per-worktree `COMMIT_EDITMSG`.
179	  A draft makes recovery possible but is not proof that a commit happened.
180	
181	An actual rebase is identified by Git's state directories (`rebase-merge` or
182	`rebase-apply`), not by a stale `REBASE_HEAD` file alone. Other active operation
183	markers and `index.lock` also block queue/finalization.

188	[`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
189	before bootstrap or migration.
190

194	> fix. Updating only the ahh tag does not rewrite an existing root
195	> `.gitleaks.toml`; follow the rollout steps in the reference for existing repos.
196	
197	```bash
198	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
199	  --install-hook
200	pre-commit run --all-files
201	```
202	
203	Bootstrap installs:
204	
205	- a validation-only staged-index checker plus gitleaks;
206	- precise nested SpecStory state ignores, keeping `history/` visible;
207	- generic hygiene hooks whose mutators exclude every agent/archive/install root:
208	  `.agents`, `.claude`, `.codex`, `.cursor`, `.opencode`, `.specify`,
209	  `.specstory`; and
210	- optionally a validation-only `prepare-commit-msg` exact-selector gate.
211	
212	Security checkers retain coverage of those roots. Excluding only `.specstory`
213	from whitespace/EOF/formatters is insufficient: `.agents/skills/` contains
214	installed vendored code, and `.claude/skills/` may symlink to it.
215	
216	For old `ahh-v1.1.0` or exact local-redactor layouts, the post-release migration
217	is transactional and fail-closed:
218	
219	```bash
220	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
221	```
222	
223	It preserves compatible sibling hooks/options, validates a candidate before
224	publishing, and refuses ambiguous/customized legacy commands.
225	
226	## Post-leak remediation
227	
228	When a scan finds a real credential, or the user says it was committed/pushed:
229	
230	1. stop any reflexive force-push;
231	2. read [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) end-to-end;
232	3. rotate at the provider regardless of blast radius; and
233	4. only then choose the least disruptive Git action from the runbook.
234	
235	## Gotchas
236	
237	- `.gitignore` does not untrack existing state. Use
238	  `bootstrap-project.sh --untrack-specstory-state`; never broaden the ignore to
239	  `.specstory/`.
240	- SpecStory >= 2.4.0 redacts on write but has context/rule gaps. Keep native
241	  redaction enabled and retain the finalizer check. Read
242	  [`references/specstory-native-redaction.md`](references/specstory-native-redaction.md)
243	  before changing placeholders or coverage.
244	- SpecStory 2.10 is checkout-path scoped, not branch scoped. Create the worktree
245	  first, then start one wrapper/session per change stream. `EnterWorktree` does
246	  not rebind an existing recorder.
247	- Exact discovery rejects incomplete JSONL, aliases, symlinks, unsafe bytes, and
248	  cross-worktree identity. Read
249	  [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
250	  when resolution is empty or ambiguous.
251	- `plansDirectory` may be ignored at project scope in some Claude Code versions.
252	  Verify where the plan landed; user-level `"plansDirectory":
253	  "./.claude/plans"` is the recommended default.
254	- `pre-commit install` is per clone. CI is a second chance, not the last gate.
255	- `--install-hook` requires `core.hooksPath` genuinely unset. Empty, relative,
256	  global, or custom values are refused; integrate the validation-only gate in
