1	# Post-session finalization
2	
3	Use this runbook for the default SpecStory/Claude lifecycle, any finalizer
4	recovery, and every rebase/integration/retirement decision that follows it.
5	
6	## Hard boundary
7	
8	An active transcript recorder blocks:
9	
10	- `git commit` (including amend/fixup);
11	- `git pull --rebase`, `git rebase`, and update-base helpers;
12	- merge/cherry-pick/integration into another ref; and
13	- worktree, branch, or agent-session retirement.
14	
15	Required order:
16	
17	```text
18	recorder exits and the exact session is synced
19	  -> exact artifacts are staged/sanitized and the message is finalized
20	  -> one ordinary hook-enabled commit is proven
21	  -> only then may history/ref movement or retirement begin
22	```
23	
24	A commit draft, a queued request, a clean scan, or a manual commit command is not
25	proof of completion by itself.
26	
27	## Lifecycle diagram
28	
29	```text
30	shell parent
31	  |
32	  | run-specstory-session.sh --allow-commit claude
33	  v
34	running: foreground `specstory run claude`
35	  |
36	  | child stages feature paths only
37	  | explicit user commit authorization
38	  | queue-agent-commit.sh + exact selectors
39	  v
40	pending: inert metadata-only request (no transcript read/mutation/commit)
41	  |
42	  | child reports "finalization queued" and exits; no more repo operations
43	  v
44	child_exited (must be exit 0)
45	  |
46	  | one exact `specstory sync claude -s UUID --silent`
47	  | exact selector/path proof
48	  v
49	synced
50	  |
51	  | parent-held token authorizes one finalizer call
52	  | prove no writer + unchanged HEAD/ref/index tree
53	  | stage/sanitize exact artifacts in locked alternate index
54	  v
55	prepared ----------------------------+
56	  |                                    |
57	  | sanitation changed bytes           | message + provenance validation
58	  v                                    | handoff drafts
59	rotation_required                      v
60	  |                                  committing
61	  | rotate credential                  |
62	  | fresh manual authorization          | one ordinary `git commit -F`
63	  | + --rotation-confirmed              v
64	  +----------------------------------> done (exact commit proven)
65	
66	Any uncertain commit outcome remains `committing`: reconcile only, never retry.
67	```
68	
69	No request means `done/no_request`. A nonzero/signaled child or failed exact sync
70	does not enter finalization.
71	
72	## Authorization model
73	
74	Three separate facts are required:
75	
76	1. **Launcher capability:** `run-specstory-session.sh --allow-commit` lets the
77	   outer parent call the finalizer once after successful child exit and sync.
78	2. **User intent:** the child queues only after the user explicitly authorizes
79	   the commit. Launcher capability is not permission to infer that intent.
80	3. **Recovery authorization:** every manual finalizer invocation repeats
81	   `--allow-commit`. A stored request, journal, message, or draft is never commit
82	   authority.
83	
84	`queue-agent-commit.sh --commit` names the requested action; it does not execute
85	or independently authorize a commit. `--runner-token` belongs only to the outer
86	runner and must never be passed to the child.
87	
88	## Default commands
89	
90	### 1. Start in the intended worktree
91	
92	Create the worktree before the recorder. Then launch:
93	
94	```bash
95	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/run-specstory-session.sh \
96	  --allow-commit claude
97	```
98	
99	Pass SpecStory options only after `--`, for example:
100	
101	```bash
102	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/run-specstory-session.sh \
103	  --allow-commit claude -- --resume SESSION_UUID
104	```
105	
106	The child receives only `AGENT_HISTORY_REQUEST_PATH` and
107	`AGENT_HISTORY_RUN_ID`. Neither value authorizes finalization.
108	
109	### 2. Prepare exact inputs inside Claude
110	
111	Take the lowercase UUID from `/status`. Resolve an exact direct child of
112	`.specstory/history/`; if the UUID has aliases, supply the path as well. Decide
113	explicitly between one exact plan and no plan.
114	
115	```bash
116	SESSION_ID=01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
117	TRANSCRIPT='.specstory/history/2026-09-01_02-14-50Z.md'
118	PLAN='.claude/plans/exact-change.md'
119	
120	git add -- path/to/feature-a path/to/feature-b
121	```
122	
123	Stage only intended non-artifact feature paths. Do not stage the live transcript
124	or plan; do not use broad `git add -A`.
125	
126	### 3. Queue only after explicit user commit authorization
127	
128	The base message must be nonempty UTF-8 subject/body and must not already carry
129	`AI-Assisted-By`, `Agent-Transcript`, `Agent-Plan`, or
130	`Agent-History-Request`; the finalizer owns those trailers.
131	
132	```bash
133	MESSAGE_FILE="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/agent-commit-message.txt"
134	printf '%s\n' \
135	  'feat(scope): summarize the change' \
136	  '' \
137	  'Explain the reason for the change.' > "$MESSAGE_FILE"
138	
139	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/queue-agent-commit.sh \
140	  --commit \
141	  --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
142	  --specstory-path "$TRANSCRIPT" \
143	  --plan "$PLAN" \
144	  --message-file "$MESSAGE_FILE"
145	```
146	
147	Use `--no-plan` instead of `--plan` only when no plan exists. Version 1 of the
148	post-session queue always requires a rendered SpecStory path.
149	
150	A successful response is one bounded JSON object with `status=queued`. An
151	identical second request is idempotent; a different request conflicts and the
152	first remains authoritative.
153	
154	After success:
155	
156	1. say **"finalization queued"**;
157	2. exit the Claude session; and
158	3. perform no more repository/index operations—not status, diff, staging,
159	   message editing, sync, finalizer, rebase, integration, or retirement.
160	
161	The queue captures the attached branch, HEAD object, and staged index tree. Any
162	later branch/index change makes it stale.
163	
164	## Why finalization waits for process exit
165	
166	### Normal pre-commit is unsafe during an active writer
167	
168	When staged files also have unstaged changes, pre-commit can stash the unstaged
169	patch, check out or rewrite the staged view for hooks, and restore the patch
170	afterward. An active recorder can append between those checkout/restore steps.
171	The restore may conflict, clobber a generation, or reintroduce bytes that a hook
172	just removed. Even without a mutating hook, the recorder can change content
173	after validation but before the commit object is created.
174	
175	Therefore:
176	
177	- `check-agent-artifact-secrets` is validation-only;
178	- generic mutating hooks/formatters exclude all agent/archive/install roots;
179	- no hook sanitizes or re-stages a working-tree transcript; and
180	- the post-session finalizer is the sole sanctioned mutator.
181	
182	### Why not a Stop hook, daemon, or live checkpoint
183	
184	- A Claude Stop hook runs before child/process and recorder quiescence are
185	  proven. It cannot establish the post-exit sync boundary.
186	- A detached `specstory watch` daemon outlives the agent and breaks the parent's
187	  recorder-lifetime proof.
188	- A live checkpoint necessarily snapshots a file that can still be appended and
189	  invites repeated pre-commit/stash races.
190	
191	The synchronous foreground wrapper is deliberate: the outer parent owns the
192	process group, forwards termination signals, waits for real exit, records proof,
193	then syncs and finalizes.
194	
195	## What the finalizer proves and changes
196	
197	On an initial authorized pass, the finalizer:
198	
199	1. validates private run state, request digest, per-worktree path, successful
200	   child exit, exact completed sync, and parent authorization;
201	2. rejects active Git operations, locks, changed branch/HEAD/index tree, unsafe
202	   paths, and an active/changing transcript writer;
203	3. revalidates the exact UUID + SpecStory path and exact plan policy;
204	4. calls `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only ... --sanitize-index
205	   --materialize-sanitized`;
206	5. derives provenance from staged blobs, composes one canonical message, and
207	   validates it;
208	6. writes owned per-worktree handoff drafts;
209	7. calls one ordinary `git commit -F` with `SKIP` removed and all hooks enabled;
210	   and
211	8. proves the new commit's branch, single parent, tree, and unique
212	   `Agent-History-Request` trailer.
213	
214	Artifact staging runs under the real index lock against a copied alternate
215	index. `--sanitize-index` edits only exact selected stage-0 blobs, then requires
216	a clean post-check. `--materialize-sanitized` writes only those sanitized bytes
217	through Git checkout filters after proving the live clean hashes still match the
218	pre-sanitize blobs. The real index is atomically published only after success.
219	
220	## Redactor and scanner safety
221	
222	`redact_secrets.py --check-index` may inspect the canonical index or Git's
223	commit-time temporary index. `--fix-index` refuses mutation unless
224	`GIT_INDEX_FILE` explicitly names an existing, user-owned, nonsymlink,
225	noncanonical regular file; it also requires exact unique `--files` under the
226	configured artifact roots.
227	
228	Complete PEM/OpenVPN/PuTTY private-key records are replaced wholesale. A header
229	without a complete bounded record fails closed: partial redaction could leave
230	private material behind, so no index/worktree publication occurs.
231	
232	Public wrapper/finalizer output is scanner-safe:
233	
234	- raw gitleaks stdout/stderr is suppressed;
235	- `Secret` and `Match` never appear in `scan-staged.sh` JSONL, even with
236	  `--no-redact`;
237	- emitted fields are bounded/validated path, rule id, line, and commit marker;
238	- finalizer JSON reports status/ids only; and
239	- unsafe selectors and private hook/scanner diagnostics are not reflected.
240	
241	`--redact` on `scan-staged.sh` masks scanner report output only; it never changes
242	files or an index.
243	
244	### Local raw-object caveat
245	
246	The exact staging transaction may cause Git to write the original live blob to
247	the local object database before the alternate index entry is replaced by its
248	sanitized blob. The raw object is then unreachable and is not included in the
249	prepared commit, but it can remain locally until Git garbage collection. This
250	is not secure erasure and does not cover shell history, recorder storage,
251	backups, or prior clones. Rotation is mandatory whenever sanitation changed
252	bytes.
253	
254	## States
255	
256	| State | Meaning | Commit permitted? |
257	|---|---|---|
258	| `running` | foreground recorder/Claude child is active | No |
259	| `pending` | one inert exact request was queued | No |
260	| `child_exited` | child returned 0; sync not yet proven | No |
261	| `syncing` | one exact quiet sync is in progress | No |
262	| `synced` | exit 0 + exact sync/session proof recorded | Finalizer may prepare |
263	| `prepared` | exact sanitized tree and message proof retained | One freshly authorized finalizer recovery |
264	| `rotation_required` | sanitation changed bytes; commit was not attempted | Only after rotation + fresh two-flag confirmation |
265	| `committing` | a prior ordinary commit outcome may be uncertain | Reconcile only; never retry |
266	| `done` | no request, or exact commit object proven | History movement allowed only for proven commit |
267	| `failed` | lifecycle stopped before a safe/proven completion | Follow status-specific recovery |
268	
269	Private run directories are `0700`; request, journal, and owned messages are
270	`0600` under the current worktree's Git directory. A linked worktree cannot
271	consume another worktree's request.
272	
273	## Outcome contracts
274	
275	### Success
276	
277	`status=committed`, exit 0 means:
278	
279	- one ordinary commit returned success;
280	- all configured hooks ran normally;
281	- the exact parent/tree/ref and request trailer were proven; and
282	- the matching LazyGit pending draft was removed.
283	
284	`status=already_committed`, exit 0 means a later reconciliation re-proved the
285	recorded commit without another commit attempt. Only these proven outcomes open
286	the rebase/integration/retirement gate.
287	
288	### Rotation stop
289	
290	`status=rotation_required`, exit 10 means:
291	
292	- exact index and matching live artifacts were sanitized;
293	- prepared parent/tree and both drafts are ready;
294	- no commit or hook was attempted; and
295	- rotation is now required, including because of the unreachable-local-object
296	  caveat above.
297	
298	After rotation, resume exactly once with fresh manual authorization:
299	
300	```bash
301	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/finalize-agent-commit.sh \
302	  --request "$ABSOLUTE_REQUEST_PATH" \
303	  --allow-commit \
304	  --rotation-confirmed
305	```
306	
307	The recovery validates the retained tree and clean index; it does not re-stage.
308	The runner never supplies `--rotation-confirmed`.
309	
310	### Ordinary hook/commit failure
311	
312	`status=commit_failed`, exit 11 means HEAD and the expected prepared tree are
313	unchanged. The prepared snapshot and drafts remain. Fix the hook/dependency
314	without altering that snapshot, then issue one fresh, explicit recovery:
315	
316	```bash
317	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/finalize-agent-commit.sh \
318	  --request "$ABSOLUTE_REQUEST_PATH" \
319	  --allow-commit
320	```
321	
322	There is no automatic retry. If the index/HEAD changed, the status becomes
323	`commit_failed_snapshot_changed` or `stale_prepared_state`; retire that request
324	and queue a fresh run rather than retrying it.
325	
326	### Manual handoff
327	
328	The finalizer writes the complete composed message to both per-worktree Git
329	paths:
330	
331	- LazyGit reads `LAZYGIT_PENDING_COMMIT`;
332	- standard Git uses `COMMIT_EDITMSG`.
333	
334	Resolve them with `git rev-parse --git-path ...`; do not assume the primary
335	checkout's `.git/` path in a linked worktree. Foreign or user-edited drafts are
336	never overwritten.
337	
338	Prefer authorized finalizer recovery. If the user deliberately commits from a
339	handoff draft, that is a manual escape hatch outside the managed proof path. The
340	draft is recoverable input, not proof; verify the actual commit parent/tree,
341	hooks, canonical trailers, and `Agent-History-Request` before allowing any
342	history movement. A `prepared` journal does not certify a manual commit.
343	
344	## Exit codes
345	
346	### Queue
347	
348	| Exit | Contract |
349	|---:|---|
350	| 0 | request written, or identical request already exists |
351	| 1 | invalid/incomplete arguments |
352	| 2 | not in a Git worktree |
353	| 3 | dependency unavailable |
354	| 4 | selector/message validation failed |
355	| 5 | unsafe/stale state, no staged feature diff, or conflicting request |
356	| 6 | Git/lifecycle operation lock active |
357	
358	### Runner
359	
360	| Exit | Contract |
361	|---:|---|
362	| 0 | child succeeded; no automatic finalizer failed (may be no request or authorization-required) |
363	| 1–255 | nonzero child status preserved exactly |
364	| 2 | invalid runner arguments |
365	| 3 | dependency unavailable |
366	| 10 | finalizer stopped for rotation |
367	| 11 | ordinary commit failed; prepared snapshot/drafts retained |
368	| 21 | exact sync failed; no finalizer call |
369	| 22 | child process group remained live; request retained, no sync/finalizer |
370	| 23 | successful child exit could not be durably proven |
371	| 128+N | child terminated by signal N; request retained, no sync/finalizer |
372	
373	### Finalizer
374	
375	| Exit | Contract |
376	|---:|---|
377	| 0 | commit completed or already-completed commit re-proven |
378	| 1 | invalid arguments |
379	| 2 | not in a Git worktree |
380	| 3 | dependency unavailable |
381	| 4 | malformed/unsafe request or journal |
382	| 5 | authorization/path mismatch |
383	| 6 | stale Git state, active operation/lock, or missing lifecycle proof |
384	| 7 | exact selector, staging, scanner, metadata, or message validation failed |
385	| 8 | prior commit outcome unproven; reconciliation only, never retry |
386	| 9 | unrelated/edited draft would be overwritten |
387	| 10 | sanitation changed content; rotate and explicitly confirm recovery |
388	| 11 | ordinary commit failed; retry only when exact prepared snapshot is retained |
389	
390	## Recovery and no-retry table
391	
392	Every manual attempt requires fresh `--allow-commit`. Never loop on a finalizer
393	exit.
394	
395	| Status/symptom | Safe next action | Forbidden action |
396	|---|---|---|
397	| `authorization_required` after runner exit 0 | run finalizer once with request path + `--allow-commit` | treating request as authority |
398	| child nonzero/signal | fix cause; start a fresh wrapper and requeue | syncing/finalizing the unproven run |
399	| `sync_failed` | fix sync; start a fresh wrapper/run so sync proof is journaled; requeue | hand-editing journal or calling commit directly |
400	| `active_writer` / transient exact validation failure | stop writer, preserve branch/index, retry once with fresh authorization | staging while writer remains active |
401	| `stale_state` before preparation | restage intended feature paths and queue a new run | forcing old request over changed tree/ref |
402	| `draft_conflict` | preserve or deliberately remove the foreign draft, then recover with fresh authorization | overwriting a nonmatching draft |
403	| `rotation_required` | rotate; use fresh `--allow-commit --rotation-confirmed` | committing before rotation; re-staging raw artifacts |
404	| `commit_failed` with prepared snapshot retained | fix hook only; fresh `--allow-commit` | automatic retry or changing the prepared tree |
405	| `commit_failed_snapshot_changed` | inspect and queue a new request | retrying old request |
406	| exit 8 / state `committing` | invoke only for reconciliation or inspect exact HEAD/journal | another `git commit` |
407	| manual commit from draft | independently verify exact commit and hooks | calling draft existence “proven” |
408	
409	For state `committing`, a repeated finalizer invocation may only prove the exact
410	HEAD and return `already_committed`; it must never issue a second commit. If it
411	cannot prove the outcome, stop and inspect.
412	
413	## Rebase and history boundary
414	
415	Queue/finalization rejects merge, cherry-pick, revert, bisect, sequencer,
416	`rebase-merge`, `rebase-apply`, and index-lock state. This is both a consistency
417	gate and a history-safety gate: the queued request binds one attached branch,
418	parent, and index tree.
419	
420	A stale `REBASE_HEAD` file alone is **not** an active rebase and must not block a
421	valid finalization. Detect real rebase state via the actual per-worktree Git
422	state directories:
423	
424	```bash
425	git rev-parse --git-path rebase-merge
426	git rev-parse --git-path rebase-apply
427	```
428	
429	Do not run update-base, `pull --rebase`, merge/integration, or retirement merely
430	because the finalizer wrote drafts or returned a recoverable status. Wait for a
431	proven `committed`/`already_committed` result, then begin a separate ordinary Git
432	operation.
433

2	# Run one foreground SpecStory/Claude session, then finalize only after exit 0.
3	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
4	
5	set -euo pipefail
6	
7	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd -P)"
8	HELPER="$SCRIPT_DIR/_post_session.py"
9	
10	usage() {
11	  cat <<'EOF'
12	Usage: run-specstory-session.sh [--allow-commit] claude [-- SPECSTORY_OPTIONS...]
13	       run-specstory-session.sh --provider claude [--allow-commit] [-- SPECSTORY_OPTIONS...]
14	
15	Run `specstory run claude` synchronously on the foreground TTY. The child gets
16	only AGENT_HISTORY_REQUEST_PATH and AGENT_HISTORY_RUN_ID as lifecycle context.
17	An agent may queue one inert request; it cannot authorize or run the finalizer.
18	
19	Required:
20	  claude                Explicit provider position (recommended).
21	  --provider claude     Equivalent flag form. Version 1 supports Claude only.
22	
23	Options:
24	  --allow-commit        Parent authorization for one automatic finalizer call,
25	                        only after the SpecStory child exits normally with 0,
26	                        its process group is empty, one exact quiet sync succeeds,
27	                        and a request exists.
28	  --                    Pass every remaining argument to `specstory run claude`.
29	  --help, -h            Show this help and exit.

35	Without --allow-commit, a successful queued run is synced and retained, and
36	exits 0 with status=authorization_required. The run succeeded; only the commit
37	is outstanding. Read `status`, not just the exit code, before treating history
38	as committed. Finish explicitly with `finalize-agent-commit.sh --allow-commit`.
39	
40	Exit codes:
41	  0       child succeeded: no request was queued, finalization completed, or a
42	          queued request awaits explicit finalization (status=authorization_required)

44	  2       invalid runner arguments
45	  3       required command missing
46	  10      sanitation changed content; rotate, then recover explicitly
47	  11      ordinary commit failed; prepared snapshot and drafts retained
48	  21      exact SpecStory sync failed; request retained
49	  22      child process group remained live; request retained, no sync/finalizer
50	  23      lifecycle proof could not be persisted
51	  128+N   child terminated by signal N; request retained, no finalizer
52	EOF
53	}

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# Global git-lfs post-commit hook — managed by chezmoi (do not edit directly).
3	#
4	# Differs from the stock `git lfs install` hook in two deliberate ways, because
5	# core.hooksPath is GLOBAL (set in ~/.gitconfig so the managed pre-commit hook
6	# covers every repo) — so this runs for EVERY clone/checkout, including the ones
7	# `brew tap` performs in Homebrew's stripped superenv PATH where /usr/local/bin
8	# (and thus git-lfs) is invisible:
9	#   1. Augment PATH with the Homebrew prefixes + ~/.local/bin so git-lfs is found
10	#      even under a restricted PATH.
11	#   2. If git-lfs is still genuinely absent, exit 0 silently instead of `exit 2`
12	#      — a missing optional tool must never abort the host git operation.
13	# See pitfalls/git-lfs-global-hook-breaks-brew-tap.md
14	PATH="$PATH:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$HOME/.local/bin"; export PATH
15	command -v git-lfs >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
16	git lfs post-commit "$@"
17
```

2	
3	## Context — 評估結論：值得做，而且現在正是時機
4	
5	`TODO.md:36` 已有 `[?/M] Nautilus Trader skill`，quant-research catalog hub 也列為 backlog。2026-09-17 實查（PyPI JSON、GitHub trees、官方 docs）後的判斷：
6	
7	- **v1/v2 斷層正處於最容易踩雷的時點**：PyPI stable 是 `1.231.0`（官方宣告為最後一版 Cython v1），`2.0.0rc1..rc5` 是 Rust core + PyO3 的 v2 預發布版。`pip install nautilus_trader` 不加 `--pre` 會裝到 v1；但 README、`docs/latest`、Python API reference 全都在寫 v2。兩代都 `import nautilus_trader`，v1 docs 已不再 host（只剩 git tag / `develop_v1`）。舊訓練資料會產出 `TradingNode`、`on_quote_tick`、msgspec config 這類 v1 API，丟進 v2 就是 `ImportError`/`TypeError`。
8	- **跟 vectorbt 定位互補，不重疊**：VectorBT 負責向量化研究與參數掃描（Nautilus ROADMAP 明確把 hyper-parameter optimization、大規模平行 backtest 列為 out of scope，而且一個 process 只能跑一個 node）。Nautilus 負責事件驅動的高擬真回測（order book、延遲、fill model），再用同一份 strategy code 接 sandbox/paper → live，並透過 adapters 串 Binance、IB、Databento、Tardis 等資料流。它自己也能出 plotly tearsheet，但不是拿來做快速掃參數的。
9	- **沒有能直接 vendor 的現成 skill**：`aysuio/nt-skill`、`clay584/nautilus-trader-skill` 都沒有 license，而 clay584 只驗證到 1.228.0（v1）。官方沒有 MCP，但有 `llms.txt`、各頁 raw markdown、`MIGRATION_V2.md`、`AGENTS.md`（那份是給 contributor 的規則）。
10	- **Rust 已經可以單獨寫 strategy/backtest/live**：`nautilus-*` crates 0.64.0 對應 2.0.0rc5，MSRV 1.98.1。但官方明說 Rust API 簽名仍會變動，所以照已選方向，以 Python 為主、Rust 放 reference。
11	
12	使用者已選定：**doctor + docs sync helper**（比照 vectorbt）、**Python-first + Rust reference**。
13

26	```

31	`'Use when writing, debugging, reviewing, or migrating code that uses NautilusTrader (nautilus_trader in Python or nautilus-* Rust crates): strategies, actors, event-driven backtests, data catalogs, adapters, and sandbox or live nodes. Detects the Cython v1 (1.x) vs Rust/PyO3 v2 (2.x) generation before using any example, syncs version-matched docs into an XDG cache, and applies live-trading safety gates.'`

33	段落大綱：
34	1. **簡介 + 範圍**：API 以 generation + 確切版本為準。純向量化研究、參數掃描交給 `vectorbt`，一般金融問題不需要載入這個 skill。
35	2. **Identify the generation**：先跑 `python3 scripts/nt_context.py doctor --project … [--python …]`。判斷優先序：使用者明說 > lock/pin 的確切版本 > 程式碼中的 v1/v2 marker > 已安裝的 interpreter。有衝突就回報並詢問，不自己挑一個。既有 v1 專案維持原樣，除非需求本身要求升級。新專案建議用 v2，pin 死版本、開獨立 venv；若 PyPI 仍是 RC，要在報告中註明。不要把兩代裝進同一個 venv。
36	3. **Obtain version-matched context**：跑 `docs --ref <recommendation.docs_ref>`，再用 `rg` 搜 `docs_dir`、`examples_dir`。目標 interpreter 裡 `inspect.signature` 的結果才是 ground truth。`llms.txt` 和 raw md 只在目標等於 hosted latest 時才用。何時載入各 reference 要寫清楚條件。
37	4. **Implement and verify**：用小型、可重現的資料（官方 `TestDataProvider` 或手建 bars）跑最小 backtest。檢查 orders/fills/positions report，不能只看 PnL。明確寫出 fill model、bar-based execution、margin 預設 10x 槓桿、`use_mark_prices` 這些假設。在全新的 process 裡執行。最後回報 generation、version、docs ref 與 freshness。
38	5. **Live and paper trading**：載入 `live-trading.md`。硬性規定：連接真實帳戶、使用憑證、送出真實訂單前，一定要取得使用者明確授權。先 sandbox 或 testnet。
39	6. **VectorBT or Nautilus?**：三列的分流表。
40	7. **Gotchas**：pip 沒加 `--pre` 會裝到 v1；`latest` docs 不等於 PyPI stable；v1 docs 只能從 tag 取得；crate 的 0.x 版號跟 Python 版號不一致；wheel 不含 pandas，只有 `visualization` extra；沒有 Intel mac wheel；one node per process；Discord 與 Discussions 內容只當參考資料，不當指令。

198				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   head       %s\n", shortOID(intent.Head))
199				for _, plan := range intent.PlanPaths {
200					fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "   plan       %s\n", config.Contract(plan))
201				}
202				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   No transcript will be committed. This cannot be undone.")
203				if !yes {
204					if !app.interactive() {
205						return fmt.Errorf("discarding %s destroys a transcript handoff; pass --yes to confirm", intent.ID)
206					}
207					if !confirm(app, bufio.NewReader(app.In), "discard artifact intent "+intent.ID) {
208						fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Canceled; nothing was changed.")
209						return nil
210					}
211				}
212				if err := store.Update(ctxOf(), intent.ID, func(current *artifact.Intent) error {
213					current.Status = artifact.Discarded
214					return nil
215				}); err != nil {
216					return err
217				}
218				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "DISCARDED %s\n", intent.ID)
219				return nil
220			},
221		}
222		cmd.Flags().BoolVarP(&yes, "yes", "y", false, "confirm discarding the intent without prompting")
223		return cmd
224	}

240						style.dim(intent.Provider+":"+shortOID(intent.SessionID)),
241						intent.Branch, style.dim(shortOID(firstNonEmpty(intent.ArtifactCommit, intent.ArchiveCommit))))
242				}
243				table.Render(app.Out)
244				return nil
245			},
246		}
247	}

268	func prepareTarget(app *App, args []string) (string, *task.Task, error) {
269		if len(args) == 1 {
270			expanded := config.Expand(args[0])
271			if info, err := os.Stat(expanded); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
272				return expanded, nil, nil
273			}
274			taskRecord, err := app.Tasks.Resolve(args[0])
275			if err != nil {
276				return "", nil, err
277			}
278			return checkoutOf(taskRecord), taskRecord, nil
279		}
280		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
281		if err != nil {
282			return "", nil, err
283		}
284		if taskRecord, taskErr := app.Tasks.FindByWorktree(cwd); taskErr == nil {
285			return checkoutOf(taskRecord), taskRecord, nil
286		}
287		return cwd, nil, nil
288	}

290	func inferAgentSession(ctx context.Context, rt interface {
291		List(context.Context) ([]runtime.Session, error)
292	}, worktree string) (string, error) {
293		sessions, err := rt.List(ctx)
294		if err != nil {
295			return "", err
296		}
297		set := make(map[string]bool)
298		for _, session := range sessions {
299			if session.Covers(worktree) {
300				for _, id := range session.AgentSessions {
301					set[id] = true
302				}
303			}
304		}
305		if len(set) != 1 {
306			return "", fmt.Errorf("cannot infer one agent session for %s; pass --session provider:uuid", config.Contract(worktree))
307		}
308		for id := range set {
309			return id, nil
310		}
311		panic("unreachable")
312	}

314	func scanAgentArtifacts(ctx context.Context, repo string, paths []string) error {
315		script := findArtifactScanner(repo)
316		if script == "" {
317			return fmt.Errorf("agent-history-hygiene scan-staged.sh not found")
318		}
319		redactor := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(script)), "assets", "redact_secrets.py")
320		if info, err := os.Stat(redactor); err != nil || !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
321			return fmt.Errorf("agent-history-hygiene redactor not found")
322		}
323		parents := make(map[string]bool)
324		for _, path := range paths {
325			rel, err := filepath.Rel(repo, filepath.Dir(path))
326			if err != nil || strings.HasPrefix(rel, "..") {
327				return fmt.Errorf("artifact path is outside repository")
328			}
329			parents[filepath.ToSlash(rel)] = true
330		}
331		redactArgs := []string{redactor, "--fix", "--paths"}
332		for parent := range parents {
333			redactArgs = append(redactArgs, parent)
334		}
335		if err := runSanitized(ctx, repo, "python3", redactArgs...); err != nil {
336			return fmt.Errorf("artifact redactor failed: %w", err)
337		}
338		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repo, append([]string{"add", "--"}, paths...)...); err != nil {
339			return fmt.Errorf("restage redacted artifacts")
340		}
341		if err := runSanitized(ctx, repo, "bash", script); err != nil {
342			return fmt.Errorf("artifact scanner failed: %w", err)
343		}
344		return nil
345	}
346	
347	func runSanitized(ctx context.Context, dir, name string, args ...string) error {
348		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, name, args...)
349		cmd.Dir = dir
350		var output bytes.Buffer
351		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &output, &output
352		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
353			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
354			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
355				return fmt.Errorf("exit %d", exitErr.ExitCode())
356			}
357			return fmt.Errorf("execute %s", name)
358		}
359		return nil
360	}
361	
362	func findArtifactScanner(repo string) string {
363		candidates := []string{
364			filepath.Join(repo, ".claude", "skills", "agent-history-hygiene", "scripts", "scan-staged.sh"),
365			filepath.Join(repo, ".agents", "skills", "agent-history-hygiene", "scripts", "scan-staged.sh"),
366			filepath.Join(os.Getenv("HOME"), ".agents", "skills", "agent-history-hygiene", "scripts", "scan-staged.sh"),
367		}
368		for _, candidate := range candidates {
369			if info, err := os.Stat(candidate); err == nil && info.Mode().IsRegular() {
370				return candidate
371			}
372		}
373		return ""
374	}

376	func shortOID(value string) string {
377		if len(value) > 12 {
378			return value[:12]
379		}
380		return value
381	}

383	func ensureArtifactsFinalized(app *App, worktree string) error {
384		store := artifactStore(app)
385		intents, err := store.List()
386		if err != nil {
387			return err
388		}
389		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(worktree)
390		if err != nil {
391			return err
392		}
393		proof, e := artifact.InspectHistoryReadiness(context.Background(), store, worktree)
394		if e != nil {
395			return e
396		}
397		if proof != nil && !proof.Ready {
398			return errors.New("ignored agent history still needs a verified external archive before integration or retirement")
399		}
400		for _, intent := range intents {
401			intentPath, canonicalErr := pathx.Canonical(intent.WorktreePath)
402			if canonicalErr != nil || intentPath != canonical {
403				continue
404			}
405			if intent.Status == artifact.Discarded {
406				continue
407			}
408			if intent.Status != artifact.Finalized {
409				return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent for %s is %s; finalize it, or discard it with `dev artifact discard %s`, before integration or retirement",
410					config.Contract(worktree), intent.Status, intent.ID)
411			}
412			reconciled, reconcileErr := (&artifact.Service{Store: store}).Finalize(context.Background(), artifact.FinalizeRequest{IntentID: intent.ID})
413			if reconcileErr != nil {
414				return reconcileErr
415			}
416			intent = *reconciled
417			if (intent.ArtifactCommit == "" && intent.ArchiveCommit == "") || !artifactCommitReachable(intent) {
418				return fmt.Errorf("artifact commit for %s is no longer reachable; restore or re-finalize intent %s before integration or retirement",
419					config.Contract(worktree), intent.ID)
420			}
421		}
422		return nil
423	}
424	
425	func artifactCommitReachable(intent artifact.Intent) bool {
426		return artifact.CommitReachable(context.Background(), intent)
427	}

429	func artifactStatuses(app *App) (map[string]string, error) {
430		inspections, err := artifact.InspectWorktrees(context.Background(), artifactStore(app))
431		if err != nil {
432			return nil, err
433		}
434		statuses := make(map[string]string, len(inspections))
435		for path, inspection := range inspections {
436			statuses[path] = string(inspection.Status)
437		}
438		return statuses, nil
439	}
440	
441	func artifactStatusForPath(statuses map[string]string, path string) string {
442		canonical, err := pathx.Canonical(path)
443		if err != nil {
444			return ""
445		}
446		return statuses[canonical]
447	}
448	
449	func firstNonEmpty(values ...string) string {
450		for _, value := range values {
451			if strings.TrimSpace(value) != "" {
452				return value
453			}
454		}
455		return ""
456	}

Finish integration while leaving runtime and filesystem cleanup to an
external coordinator.

  --ff       rebase onto the base and fast-forward it locally. Use when the
             branch's commits are worth keeping in the base's history.
  --pr       push and open a pull/merge request with the detected forge CLI,
             leaving the merge to review and CI.
  --merged   verify an externally merged branch against --base-ref, for a merge
             performed outside dev.

For branch/worktree tasks, omitting every mode opens a finish wizard on an
interactive terminal. A non-interactive caller still gets a report and must
pass a mode explicitly. Direct tasks need no integration mode.

Parent/canonical agents and workspaces are preserved. An occupied parent blocks
fast-forward: recheck after handling it independently, choose PR, or cancel.
The wizard can include exact idle/done task-worktree agent panes in the final
plan; they close only after final approval. General foreground programs require
a separate confirmation that FF will change files while they keep running.
Neither --yes nor --close-unknown supplies this program consent. A dirty canonical
integration checkout can switch to PR, be discarded under typed DROP
confirmation, or cancel; unrelated canonical bytes are never auto-committed.

A dirty checkout is analyzed against the base, not rejected as one opaque
condition. Interactive use can commit everything, discard everything, or
cancel. Unique content requires typing DROP before discard. Scripts select an
explicit --dirty policy; destructive discard also requires --yes.

A successful local or externally verified merge records DONE, meaning MERGED
with cleanup possibly pending. The bare interactive wizard can then preview
covering runtime/agent state and hand retirement to a freshly revalidated
external coordinator. Interactive dev retire shares its pane/process preview
and requires CLOSE <workspace-id> to terminate listed non-agent programs.
Background jobs are not inspected. Active agents and protected/mixed workspaces
remain blockers. Explicit integration modes keep the worktree and branch for
a later dev retire; selected task-pane closures are reported separately.

See also: dev help retirement

Usage:
  dev done [task] [flags]

Flags:
      --base-ref string         base ref used to verify --merged (default: recorded base)
      --confirm-squash string   attest that this contained commit represents a squash merge
      --delete-branch           deprecated here: use dev retire --delete-branch
      --dirty string            dirty checkout policy: auto, fail, commit or discard (default "auto")
      --ff                      rebase onto the base and fast-forward it
  -h, --help                    help for done
      --keep-worktree           deprecated: worktrees are always kept until dev retire
      --merged                  verify an externally merged branch and mark the task done
  -m, --message string          commit message for --dirty=commit
      --pr                      push and open a pull/merge request instead of merging locally
      --push                    push the resulting base (direct mode pushes its current branch)
  -y, --yes                     confirm the selected finish plan (required for non-interactive discard)

Global Flags:
      --allow-shared-checkout   allow a writer claim in a checkout occupied by another live agent
      --color string            colorize human output: auto, always or never (default "auto")
      --config string           path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)
      --no-runtime              do not touch any terminal multiplexer
      --remotes string          path to remotes.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml)
      --runtime string          override runtime backend: herdr, tmux, zellij or none
      --scaffolds string        path to scaffolds.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml)
Retire local execution state after a change has been integrated.

Run this from outside the target worktree and runtime. dev re-resolves every
covering session, refuses active agents and mixed-purpose workspaces, waits for
runtime closure, revalidates Git state, and only then removes a linked worktree
without force. A task is deleted only after every requested cleanup step works.

Unknown runtime status fails closed. An external coordinator may acknowledge it
with --close-unknown; working, blocked and waiting agents are never overridden.

Interactive linked-worktree retirement lists workspace/tab/pane identities,
agent states and foreground programs before final approval. Non-agent programs
require typing CLOSE <workspace-id>; --close-unknown does not authorize known
program termination. Non-interactive calls requiring this approval stop.
Background jobs are not inspected. Parent/canonical and other-checkout Herdr
workspaces stay open, even when a pane has changed into the target directory.
A managed worktree's caller-owned Herdr workspace can be handed to a fresh
external coordinator that waits for this command to exit into its shell.

TL;DR: integrate, exit, then clean up from outside

  dev done --ff --> MERGED   (runtime and worktree deliberately kept)
                      |
    the agent exits,  |  dev prepare arms its transcript to finalize later
    or another shell  v
  dev retire <task> --> close runtime --> remove worktree --> keep the branch

  dev retire refuses to run inside the workspace it would delete, and refuses
  a live agent, dirty state, or an unfinalized artifact.

See also: dev help retirement

Usage:
  dev retire [task-or-worktree] [flags]

Flags:
      --assume-no-runtime   continue when runtime enumeration fails (external callers only)
      --base string         containment base override: local branch, remote-tracking ref such as origin/main, or commit
      --close-unknown       allow an external caller to close unknown/empty runtime status
      --delete-branch       delete the contained local branch after worktree removal
  -h, --help                help for retire
      --recursive           verify and dispose workspace-owned submodule clones from the inside out
      --timeout duration    maximum time to wait for runtime sessions to close (default 5s)

Global Flags:
      --allow-shared-checkout   allow a writer claim in a checkout occupied by another live agent
      --color string            colorize human output: auto, always or never (default "auto")
      --config string           path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)
      --no-runtime              do not touch any terminal multiplexer
      --remotes string          path to remotes.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml)
      --runtime string          override runtime backend: herdr, tmux, zellij or none
      --scaffolds string        path to scaffolds.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml)

```text
1	---
2	name: git-workflow
3	description: Opinionated, scale-aware git workflow — English Conventional Commits, cross-harness AI provenance (`AI-Assisted-By` + transcript/plan trailers), linear history, main-vs-PR tiers, worktrees for parallel agents, SemVer releases, and pre-merge hygiene. Use when committing, writing commit bodies, recording Claude/Codex/Cursor attribution, signing commits, branching, merging, opening a PR, tagging a release, or cleaning stale branches — incl. "幫我 commit / 整理 git" and "git 工作流".
4	---
5	
6	# git-workflow
7	
8	One consistent, opinionated git workflow that scales from a solo weekend
9	project to a multi-person, multi-month repo — so you (and your agents) stop
10	improvising commit messages, branch names, and release habits per project.
11	The defaults here favor a **clean, linear, reviewable history**.
12	
13	Surfaces, separated by the question they answer:
14	
15	| Surface | Question it answers |
16	|---|---|
17	| `references/project-tiers.md` | "Do I commit to `main`, use a `dev` branch, or open PRs?" |
18	| `references/conventional-commits.md` | "What exactly goes in the commit message, including AI provenance?" |
19	| `references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md` | "How do I run parallel agents without collisions?" |
20	| `references/versioning-and-releases.md` | "When and how do I tag a version?" |
21	| `references/branch-hygiene.md` | "Which local branches are done vs still in-dev?" |
22	| `scripts/branch-status.sh` | Same, as data — classify every local branch. |
23	| `scripts/check-commit-msg.sh` | "Is this commit message valid?" |
24	| `references/lazygit-cheatsheet.md` | "How do I do this in lazygit?" (learning aid) |
25	
26	## Core principles
27	
28	1. **Commit messages are English and follow Conventional Commits**, even when
29	   the prompt/conversation is in Chinese. Code history is read by tooling
30	   (changelogs, SemVer bumps) and future collaborators; a mixed-language log
31	   is harder to grep and automate. Prompts stay whatever language you like.
32	2. **Prefer a linear history.** Default to `pull --rebase` and fast-forward
33	   merges; reserve merge commits and squashes for PR integration points. A
34	   linear log makes `git bisect`, `git revert`, and blame legible.
35	3. **One logical change = one commit; one workflow phase = one commit.** For
36	   multi-phase / `/workflows` work, commit at each phase boundary so you can
37	   roll back or resume cleanly if interrupted. Don't batch unrelated changes.
38	4. **Never leak secrets into history.** Secret scanning + agent-transcript
39	   handling is owned by the [`agent-history-hygiene`](../agent-history-hygiene/SKILL.md)
40	   skill — this skill *defers* to it at commit/merge time rather than
41	   reimplementing it.
42	5. **Keep authorship, AI provenance, and cryptographic signing separate.** The
43	   human remains Git author/committer; agent harness + model live in canonical
44	   trailers; SSH/GPG signing proves key possession, not who wrote each line.
45	
46	## Pick your tier first
47	
48	Match the workflow to the project's real collaboration needs, not its
49	ambitions. Promote a tier only when the **signal** actually appears.
50	
51	| Tier | Shape | Branching | Integration | Promote when… |
52	|---|---|---|---|---|
53	| **1 — Solo / early** | one `main` | commit to `main`; short-lived local branches optional | `pull --rebase`, `merge --ff-only` | you need a stable line separate from WIP |
54	| **2 — prod/dev split** | `main` = released, `dev` = integration | feature branches off `dev` | merge to `dev`; fast-forward `dev`→`main` at release | others rely on a deployed/tagged version |
55	| **3 — Team / grown vibe-coding** | `main` always deployable | short-lived `feat/…` etc. → PR | PR review/CI → squash-merge | ≥2 contributors, or you want a per-feature ship+review gate |
56	
57	A **solo vibe-coding** project can jump straight to Tier 3 even with one human:
58	the PR becomes the "ship a feature" boundary that separates finished work from
59	in-progress work, and gives CI a place to run. See
60	`references/project-tiers.md` for per-tier command recipes and the GitHub-Flow
61	summary. Read it when deciding whether to branch/PR or when a project outgrows
62	committing straight to `main`.
63	
64	## Commit messages
65	
66	Format (full spec + type table in `references/conventional-commits.md` — read
67	it when writing a non-obvious commit or wiring `check-commit-msg.sh`):
68	
69	```
70	<type>(<optional scope>): <subject>
71	
72	<body — the "why" for non-trivial agent commits, wrapped ~72 cols>
73	
74	<optional standard/native footers>
75	<canonical agent trailers — AI-Assisted-By / Agent-Transcript / Agent-Plan>
76	```
77	
78	- **Types**: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`,
79	  `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`.
80	- **Subject**: imperative mood, lowercase start, no trailing period, keep the
81	  header ≤ ~72 chars. "add retry to client", not "Added retry." / "Adds…".
82	- **Breaking change**: `feat!:` / `refactor(api)!:` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:`
83	  footer → drives a **major** SemVer bump.
84	- Validate before committing when unsure:
85	
86	```bash
87	printf 'feat(auth): add token refresh\n' | \
88	  bash skills/local/git-workflow/scripts/check-commit-msg.sh
89	```
90	
91	- Install the message template so the shape is always in front of you:
92	
93	```bash
94	git config commit.template skills/local/git-workflow/assets/commit-template.txt
95	```
96	
97	### Agentic commit contract
98	
99	Use this portable minimum for commits produced with Claude Code, Codex,
100	Cursor, OpenCode, or another coding-agent harness:
101	
102	```text
103	feat(scope): add concise imperative summary
104	
105	Explain why the change was needed, the resulting behavior, and meaningful
106	validation. Keep this in English even when the prompt was not English.
107	
108	AI-Assisted-By: Codex CLI (gpt-5.6-sol)
109	Agent-Transcript: .specstory/history/session.md
110	Agent-Plan: .claude/plans/plan.md
111	```
112	
113	- A non-trivial agent commit requires a body. Use the validator's
114	  `--allow-no-body` only for a genuinely self-explanatory change such as a typo.
115	- Repeat `AI-Assisted-By` for every distinct harness/model that materially
116	  contributed. Never invent a vendor email merely to make GitHub show an AI as
117	  a co-author.
118	- Repeat transcript/plan trailers for every staged artifact, using repo-relative
119	  paths. Omit `Agent-Plan` when no plan file is in the commit.
120	- Preserve tool-native metadata (for example Claude's `Co-Authored-By`) as
121	  additive evidence. Put the canonical fields in the **final Git trailer
122	  block** so `git interpret-trailers --parse` can query them.
123	- When `agent-history-hygiene` is installed, generate the block from the staged
124	  snapshot instead of copying paths/model names by hand:
125	
126	```bash
127	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/agent-commit-metadata.sh
128	```
129	
130	Validate the complete message before committing:
131	
132	```bash
133	bash skills/local/git-workflow/scripts/check-commit-msg.sh \
134	  --agentic --staged --file /path/to/commit-message.txt
135	```
136	
137	Cryptographic signing is opt-in and user-owned. Configure SSH/GPG signing only
138	when the user explicitly asks; never silently change global Git or harness
139	settings. A vendor-signed cloud-agent commit must not be amended solely to add
140	metadata, because amending replaces the signed commit object.
141	
142	## Branch naming
143	
144	Use a `<prefix>/<kebab-desc>` namespace so branches sort and clean up by
145	intent, and so agent-generated branches are visually distinct from yours:
146	
147	- **Human intent**: `feat/…`, `fix/…`, `chore/…`, `docs/…`, `refactor/…`,
148	  `exp/…` (throwaway experiments). Optionally embed an issue: `feat/123-oauth`.
149	- **Agent / vibe-coding**: `agent/<desc>` — a dedicated namespace you can bulk-
150	  triage or delete separately from hand-authored branches.
151	- **Claude worktrees**: `worktree-<name>` (auto-created by `claude --worktree`)
152	  is a third namespace — see below.
153	
154	Keeping these separate is what makes `branch-status.sh` and
155	`git branch --list 'agent/*'` cleanup targeted rather than risky.
156	
157	## Merge & sync
158	
159	Set linear-history defaults (per-repo, or `--global` to your taste):
160	
161	```bash
162	git config pull.rebase true      # rebase local work onto upstream on pull
163	git config merge.ff only         # refuse merges that can't fast-forward
164	```
165	
166	- **Solo/local**: `git pull --rebase`, then `git merge --ff-only <branch>` to
167	  land a short-lived branch with no merge commit.
168	- **PRs (Tier 3)**: prefer **squash-merge** for vibe-coding branches (collapses
169	  noisy WIP into one clean `feat: …` commit on `main`); use **rebase-merge**
170	  when every commit is already meaningful and you want them preserved.
171	- Drive PRs from the terminal with the **forge CLI** — `gh` (GitHub) or `glab`
172	  (GitLab). These are strongly recommended (not required — the scripts here
173	  degrade to plain git if absent):
174	
175	```bash
176	gh pr create --fill            # or: glab mr create --fill
177	gh pr checks                   # watch CI
178	gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch   # glab mr merge --squash --remove-source-branch
179	```
180	
181	  The vendored `create-pull-request` skill (github-workflow group) is a
182	  companion for richer PR bodies.
183	
184	## Worktrees for parallel agents
185	
186	Run each parallel agent/session in its own git worktree so file edits never
187	collide. Full mechanics + caveats in `references/worktrees-parallel-agents.md`
188	— read it before setting up parallel agents or debugging a missing `.env` in
189	a worktree.
190	
191	Essentials:
192	
193	```bash
194	claude --worktree feature-auth   # → .claude/worktrees/worktree-feature-auth/
195	```
196	
197	- Worktrees branch from `origin/HEAD` by default; set `worktree.baseRef: "head"`
198	  in settings to branch from your local HEAD (unpushed work).
199	- Subagents: add `isolation: worktree` frontmatter, or ask Claude to "use
200	  worktrees for your agents".
201	- **Gitignore `.claude/worktrees/`** so worktree contents don't show as
202	  untracked files in the main checkout.
203	- Bring **gitignored** files (e.g. `.env`) into new worktrees with a
204	  `.worktreeinclude` at the repo root (see `assets/worktreeinclude.template`).
205	  It uses `.gitignore` syntax and copies **only gitignored** matches — already-
206	  tracked files are in the checkout already, so don't list them.
```

36	// FindTranscript selects exactly one SpecStory transcript by its anchored
37	// preamble session UUID. UUID mentions later in a transcript are never used.
38	func FindTranscript(worktree, provider, sessionID string) (Transcript, error) {
39		history := filepath.Join(worktree, ".specstory", "history")
40		entries, err := os.ReadDir(history)
41		if err != nil {
42			return Transcript{}, err
43		}
44		var matches []Transcript
45		for _, entry := range entries {
46			if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".md") {

48			}

50			inside, err := pathx.Contains(history, path)
51			if err != nil || !inside {
52				continue
53			}
54			gotProvider, gotSession, err := transcriptPreamble(path)
55			if err != nil || gotSession != sessionID || (provider != "" && gotProvider != provider) {
56				continue
57			}
58			matches = append(matches, Transcript{Path: path, Provider: gotProvider, SessionID: gotSession})
59		}
60		switch len(matches) {
61		case 1:
62			return matches[0], nil
63		case 0:
64			return Transcript{}, fmt.Errorf("no SpecStory transcript with preamble session %s:%s", provider, sessionID)
65		default:
66			return Transcript{}, fmt.Errorf("multiple SpecStory transcripts have preamble session %s:%s", provider, sessionID)

3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

5	## Project Overview

7	A personal agent skills collection installable via `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`. 67	## Source categories and upstream sync
68	
69	- `skills/local/` — canonical skills authored in this repository.
70	- `skills/owned/` — first-party skills maintained in another repository owned by the maintainer. Edit the source project, then sync its distribution copy here.
71	- `skills/vendor/` — third-party upstream skills; preserve upstream content.
72	
73	`vendor.yaml` remains the shared sync manifest. `collection: owned` selects
74	`skills/owned/`; an omitted collection defaults to `vendor`. Both support `series`,
75	`license_path`, `frozen`, and upstream commit tracking. Add published owned sources
76	with `scripts/add-vendor.sh --owned <owner/repo/path>`. A cross-repository symlink
77	cannot serve as a distributable copy.
78	
79	An unpublished owned skill may use `pending_upstream: true`. Its bootstrap mirror
80	contains real files but claims no remote SHA; routine sync/check preserves it.
81	After publishing the canonical source, run `scripts/sync-vendor.sh --activate <name>`.
82	Only a successful sync clears pending. See [owned workflow](docs/workflows/adding-owned-skills.md).
83	
84	## Vendor System (also used for owned sources)
85	
86	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
87	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
88	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
89	
90	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
91	
92	`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml` runs `make sync` weekly (Mon 03:00 UTC,
93	plus `workflow_dispatch` with an optional single-skill filter) and opens/updates
94	a PR on the fixed branch `chore/vendor-sync` — never a direct commit to `main`,
95	because vendored content ships to downstream agents via `npx skills update` and
96	a broken frontmatter is silently skipped rather than erroring. PRs created with
97	`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `validate.yml`, so the sync job runs the publish
98	gates itself. A red sync job usually means an upstream rename/removal — handle
99	it with `renamed_from:` or `frozen:` as below.
100	
101	Active series in this repo:
102	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
103	
104	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
105	
106	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
107	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
108	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
109	
110	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
111	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
112	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
113	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
114	  `skills@1.5.24` writes `skills-lock.json`, but a renamed skill is still a
115	  different install ID; review the lock and explicitly reinstall the new name.
116	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
117	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
118	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
119	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
120	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
121	
122	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
123	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.

126	
127	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
128	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
129	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in

137	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
138	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
139	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>`, `./owned/<name>`, or
140	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
141	
142	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
143	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
144	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a

148	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
149	within-group caveat in

153	
154	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.

156	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
157	
158	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
159	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
160	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
161	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
162	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
163	
164	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
165	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
166	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
167	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
168	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
169	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
170	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
171	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
172	
173	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
174	
175	```bash
176	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
177	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
178	
179	# …or remove them afterward
180	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
181	```

183	## Project Memory Workflow
184	
185	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
186	
187	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
188	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
189	
190	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
191	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
192	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
193	
194	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
195	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
196	
197	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
198	
199	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
200	
201	   ```bash
202	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
203	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
204	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
205	   ```
206	
207	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
208	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
209	
210	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
211	
212	   ```bash
213	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
214	   ```
215	
216	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
217	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
218	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
219	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
220	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
221	
222	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
223	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
224	   afterwards to catch drift.
225	
226	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
227	
228	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
229	
230	```bash
231	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
232	```
233	
234	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
235	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
236	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
237	
238	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
239	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
240	
241	### External skill / MCP / domain / curiosity catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
242	
243	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
244	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
245	own conventions). It has four subareas:
246	
247	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
248	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
249	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
250	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
251	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
252	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
253	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
254	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
255	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
256	- `docs/catalog/curiosities.md` — docs-only shelf for interesting,
257	  provocative, or highly personal skills that are deliberately excluded
258	  from `vendor.yaml`, marketplace grouping, and routine skill discovery.
259	  Entries use `skipped` with the reason they remain docs-only.
260	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
261	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
262	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
263	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
264	  status / license / last_verified`).
265	
266	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
267	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
268	
269	| Status | Meaning |
270	|---|---|
271	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
272	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
273	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
274	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
275	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
276	
277	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
278	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
279	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
280	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
281	
282	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
283	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
284	
285	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
286	
287	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
288	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
289	
290	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
291	2. The root cause
292	3. The workaround
293	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
294	
295	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
296	the explanation they do not know yet.

```text
1	# Post-session finalization
2	
3	Use this runbook for the default SpecStory/Claude lifecycle, any finalizer
4	recovery, and every rebase/integration/retirement decision that follows it.
5	
6	## Hard boundary
7	
8	An active transcript recorder blocks:
9	
10	- `git commit` (including amend/fixup);
11	- `git pull --rebase`, `git rebase`, and update-base helpers;
12	- merge/cherry-pick/integration into another ref; and
13	- worktree, branch, or agent-session retirement.
14	
15	Required order:
16	
17	```text
18	recorder exits and the exact session is synced
19	  -> exact artifacts are staged/sanitized and the message is finalized
20	  -> one ordinary hook-enabled commit is proven
21	  -> only then may history/ref movement or retirement begin
22	```
23	
24	A commit draft, a queued request, a clean scan, or a manual commit command is not
25	proof of completion by itself.
26	
27	## Lifecycle diagram
28	
29	```text
30	shell parent
31	  |
32	  | run-specstory-session.sh --allow-commit claude
33	  v
34	running: foreground `specstory run claude`
35	  |
36	  | child stages feature paths only
37	  | explicit user commit authorization
38	  | queue-agent-commit.sh + exact selectors
39	  v
40	pending: inert metadata-only request (no transcript read/mutation/commit)
41	  |
42	  | child reports "finalization queued" and exits; no more repo operations
43	  v
44	child_exited (must be exit 0)
45	  |
46	  | one exact `specstory sync claude -s UUID --silent`
47	  | exact selector/path proof
48	  v
49	synced
50	  |
51	  | parent-held token authorizes one finalizer call
52	  | prove no writer + unchanged HEAD/ref/index tree
53	  | stage/sanitize exact artifacts in locked alternate index
54	  v
55	prepared ----------------------------+
56	  |                                    |
57	  | sanitation changed bytes           | message + provenance validation
58	  v                                    | handoff drafts
59	rotation_required                      v
60	  |                                  committing
61	  | rotate credential                  |
62	  | fresh manual authorization          | one ordinary `git commit -F`
63	  | + --rotation-confirmed              v
64	  +----------------------------------> done (exact commit proven)
65	
66	Any uncertain commit outcome remains `committing`: reconcile only, never retry.
67	```
68	
69	No request means `done/no_request`. A nonzero/signaled child or failed exact sync
70	does not enter finalization.
71	
72	## Authorization model
73	
74	Three separate facts are required:
75	
76	1. **Launcher capability:** `run-specstory-session.sh --allow-commit` lets the
77	   outer parent call the finalizer once after successful child exit and sync.
78	2. **User intent:** the child queues only after the user explicitly authorizes
79	   the commit. Launcher capability is not permission to infer that intent.
80	3. **Recovery authorization:** every manual finalizer invocation repeats
81	   `--allow-commit`. A stored request, journal, message, or draft is never commit
82	   authority.
83	
84	`queue-agent-commit.sh --commit` names the requested action; it does not execute
85	or independently authorize a commit. `--runner-token` belongs only to the outer
86	runner and must never be passed to the child.
87	
88	## Default commands
89	
90	### 1. Start in the intended worktree
91	
92	Create the worktree before the recorder. Then launch:
93	
94	```bash
95	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/run-specstory-session.sh \
96	  --allow-commit claude
97	```
98	
99	Pass SpecStory options only after `--`, for example:
100	
101	```bash
102	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/run-specstory-session.sh \
103	  --allow-commit claude -- --resume SESSION_UUID
104	```
105	
106	The child receives only `AGENT_HISTORY_REQUEST_PATH` and
107	`AGENT_HISTORY_RUN_ID`. Neither value authorizes finalization.
108	
109	### 2. Prepare exact inputs inside Claude
110	
111	Take the lowercase UUID from `/status`. Resolve an exact direct child of
112	`.specstory/history/`; if the UUID has aliases, supply the path as well. Decide
113	explicitly between one exact plan and no plan.
114	
115	```bash
116	SESSION_ID=01234567-89ab-4cde-8fab-0123456789ab
117	TRANSCRIPT='.specstory/history/2026-09-01_02-14-50Z.md'
118	PLAN='.claude/plans/exact-change.md'
119	
120	git add -- path/to/feature-a path/to/feature-b
121	```
122	
123	Stage only intended non-artifact feature paths. Do not stage the live transcript
124	or plan; do not use broad `git add -A`.
125	
126	### 3. Queue only after explicit user commit authorization
127	
128	The base message must be nonempty UTF-8 subject/body and must not already carry
129	`AI-Assisted-By`, `Agent-Transcript`, `Agent-Plan`, or
130	`Agent-History-Request`; the finalizer owns those trailers.
131	
132	```bash
133	MESSAGE_FILE="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/agent-commit-message.txt"
134	printf '%s\n' \
135	  'feat(scope): summarize the change' \
136	  '' \
137	  'Explain the reason for the change.' > "$MESSAGE_FILE"
138	
139	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/queue-agent-commit.sh \
140	  --commit \
141	  --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
142	  --specstory-path "$TRANSCRIPT" \
143	  --plan "$PLAN" \
144	  --message-file "$MESSAGE_FILE"
145	```
146	
147	Use `--no-plan` instead of `--plan` only when no plan exists. Version 1 of the
148	post-session queue always requires a rendered SpecStory path.
149	
150	A successful response is one bounded JSON object with `status=queued`. An
151	identical second request is idempotent; a different request conflicts and the
152	first remains authoritative.
153	
154	After success:
155	
156	1. say **"finalization queued"**;
157	2. exit the Claude session; and
158	3. perform no more repository/index operations—not status, diff, staging,
159	   message editing, sync, finalizer, rebase, integration, or retirement.
160	
161	The queue captures the attached branch, HEAD object, and staged index tree. Any
162	later branch/index change makes it stale.
163	
164	## Why finalization waits for process exit
165	
166	### Normal pre-commit is unsafe during an active writer
167	
168	When staged files also have unstaged changes, pre-commit can stash the unstaged
169	patch, check out or rewrite the staged view for hooks, and restore the patch
170	afterward. An active recorder can append between those checkout/restore steps.
171	The restore may conflict, clobber a generation, or reintroduce bytes that a hook
172	just removed. Even without a mutating hook, the recorder can change content
173	after validation but before the commit object is created.
174	
175	Therefore:
176	
177	- `check-agent-artifact-secrets` is validation-only;
178	- generic mutating hooks/formatters exclude all agent/archive/install roots;
179	- no hook sanitizes or re-stages a working-tree transcript; and
180	- the post-session finalizer is the sole sanctioned mutator.
181	
182	### Why not a Stop hook, daemon, or live checkpoint
183	
184	- A Claude Stop hook runs before child/process and recorder quiescence are
185	  proven. It cannot establish the post-exit sync boundary.
186	- A detached `specstory watch` daemon outlives the agent and breaks the parent's
187	  recorder-lifetime proof.
188	- A live checkpoint necessarily snapshots a file that can still be appended and
189	  invites repeated pre-commit/stash races.
190	
191	The synchronous foreground wrapper is deliberate: the outer parent owns the
192	process group, forwards termination signals, waits for real exit, records proof,
193	then syncs and finalizes.
194	
195	## What the finalizer proves and changes
196	
197	On an initial authorized pass, the finalizer:
198	
199	1. validates private run state, request digest, per-worktree path, successful
200	   child exit, exact completed sync, and parent authorization;
201	2. rejects active Git operations, locks, changed branch/HEAD/index tree, unsafe
202	   paths, and an active/changing transcript writer;
203	3. revalidates the exact UUID + SpecStory path and exact plan policy;
204	4. calls `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only ... --sanitize-index
205	   --materialize-sanitized`;
206	5. derives provenance from staged blobs, composes one canonical message, and
207	   validates it;
208	6. writes owned per-worktree handoff drafts;
209	7. calls one ordinary `git commit -F` with `SKIP` removed and all hooks enabled;
210	   and
211	8. proves the new commit's branch, single parent, tree, and unique
212	   `Agent-History-Request` trailer.
213	
214	Artifact staging runs under the real index lock against a copied alternate
215	index. `--sanitize-index` edits only exact selected stage-0 blobs, then requires
216	a clean post-check. `--materialize-sanitized` writes only those sanitized bytes
217	through Git checkout filters after proving the live clean hashes still match the
218	pre-sanitize blobs. The real index is atomically published only after success.
219	
220	## Redactor and scanner safety
221	
222	`redact_secrets.py --check-index` may inspect the canonical index or Git's
223	commit-time temporary index. `--fix-index` refuses mutation unless
224	`GIT_INDEX_FILE` explicitly names an existing, user-owned, nonsymlink,
225	noncanonical regular file; it also requires exact unique `--files` under the
226	configured artifact roots.
227	
228	Complete PEM/OpenVPN/PuTTY private-key records are replaced wholesale. A header
229	without a complete bounded record fails closed: partial redaction could leave
230	private material behind, so no index/worktree publication occurs.
```
