# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos`, OS `darwin`/`arm64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

- **External editor** — init default `nvim` (independent of `enableVimMode`); `editorcfg status/list/use/reset/doctor` manages the local override. `EDITOR`/`VISUAL` name `dotfiles-editor`, which resolves and waits on each invocation. Micro is baseline devtools; code/cursor presets add `--wait`. See `docs/tools/editor.md`. Local `editor-choice` is not chezmoi-managed.

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, Pi (`pi`), Oh My Pi (`omp`), the `pia` Git-managed harness-combo manager, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). `pia doctor` checks the stack; `pia list --tree` / `pia use pi/base` select presets. The external checkout is `~/.local/share/pi-agents`; `08_pi_agents.sh` makes its canonical commands beat mise/Bun shadows, while runtime state and credentials stay elsewhere. See `docs/tools/pi-agents.md`, `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **summarize** — `summarize <url|file>` turns a YouTube video, podcast, webpage, PDF or local media into a summary. Output defaults to 繁體中文 via the managed `~/.summarize/config.json` overlay. Wrappers in `32_summarize.sh`: `ytsum` (video, with timestamps), `sumq` (30-second triage), `suml` (long), `sumj` (JSON). `--cli claude|codex|gemini` reuses an already-authenticated agent instead of an API key. See `docs/tools/summarize.md`.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **mole** (`mo`, macOS only) — `mo purge` reclaims dev build artifacts (`node_modules`, `target`, `.venv`) across the roots listed in `~/.config/mole/purge_paths`; `mo analyze` is a disk explorer, `mo clean` clears caches (always `--dry-run` first, or use the `moclean` wrapper). Helpers in `33_mole.sh`: `moa`, `moclean`, `mowl`. Both config files are chezmoi `create_` seeds, and the whitelist **replaces** rather than extends mole's built-in defaults. See `docs/tools/mole.md`.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared (expose localhost to the **public** internet).
- **Tailscale** — WireGuard mesh VPN (tailnet-only, the opposite of the tunnel tools). Helper CLI: `tsnet`. Picker: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`, `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`.
- **Bitwarden** — `bw` CLI (+ SSH agent integration). See `docs/tools` Bitwarden notes.
- **GUI apps (brew)** — terminals/browsers/utilities (macOS also: AeroSpace).
- **Input method** — McBopomofo + RIME (Traditional Chinese).
- **Agent sounds** — audio notifications on agent Stop/Notification hooks. See `docs/tools/agent-sounds.md`.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Package-managed personal CLIs

- **`dev`** — repository/task/worktree command center with a TUI, parent-shell navigation, generated completion, agent-safe prepare/finalize/done/retire lifecycle, and receipt-backed `dev git` transactions. macOS installs `daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli`; Linux uses the `go_tools` role. Source: `github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli`.
- **`translate`** — terminal translator (CLI + TUI). macOS installs `daviddwlee84/tap/translate`; Linux uses the `go_tools` role.

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
- **`agent-warmup`** — Tyro CLI that drives a real interactive Claude TUI at a scheduled time through an existing Herdr session (preferred) or tmux, with uv-first daemon bootstrap and safe fallback. See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
- **`raid-perm-check`** — read-only auditor for a group+ACL-shared data mount (`summary`/`orphans`/`groups`/`units`/`user`/`all`, default `/mnt/raid`). Catches the two silent breakages: orphaned uid/gid after an account is deleted, and a stale `systemd --user` manager whose frozen groups make timers hit EACCES on paths your shell reads fine. Never modifies — prints the fix. See `docs/sysadmin/shared-storage-permissions.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`ytmv`** — download YouTube music videos for **old MP3 players**: mp3 + sidecar `.lrc` + ID3v2.3/USLT lyrics, or mp4 with soft/burned-in subtitles. Subcommands `get` / `lyrics` / `tag` / `doctor`; `ytmv help` is the complete setup/cookie-safety guide and `doctor --cookies` explicitly tests a configured source. Public downloads use packaged EJS + managed Node 22+ cookie-free first (doctor flags legacy Node 20/16). Compatibility profiles (`safe`, `cjk-big5`, `cjk-gbk`, `ipod`, `modern`) are re-appliable offline via `ytmv tag`. Needs ffmpeg (`installMediaTools`); `--burn-subs` needs the keg-only `ffmpeg-full`. No `tv` channel by design. See `docs/tools/ytmv.md`.
- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
- **`herdr-grep`** — search visible or retained content across panes in the current, one named, or all running local Herdr sessions; reports exact session/workspace/tab/pane coordinates, supports `--json`, and `--pick` pipes matches to fzf then exact-focuses/attaches the selection. Inside Herdr, `prefix+Alt+F` opens a visible-content picker (Alt+S = scrollback, Alt+V = visible). Remote use runs the CLI through SSH. See `docs/tools/herdr.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, binary-matched global skill from `herdr --skill`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with `prefix+d` for the interactive `dev` dashboard, `prefix+G` lazygit temporary pane, `prefix+Y` for a Yazi filesystem popup rooted at the focused pane cwd, low-frequency copy helpers under `prefix+y` Quick Actions, `prefix+t` to translate the focused pane (bilingual `translate -2` popup; scope variants — current page / last 200-1000 lines — are `prefix+y` Quick Actions, because an alternate-screen agent pane has NO scrollback and `pane read` caps at 1000 lines), three metadata pickers (`tv herdr-agent-panes`, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`), and `herdr-grep` for pane-content search. Yazi itself displays guarded `git.yazi` status signs on Yazi 26.8.15+. See `docs/tools/{herdr,yazi}.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).

`prefix+Alt+e` edits only `$HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` (or `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`), validates that exact live target, and reloads; it never invokes chezmoi. Editor/validation failure preserves the rejected candidate and atomically restores the previous valid config; reload failure keeps the valid edit and backup. A later `chezmoi apply` reasserts canonical `[theme]`, `[ui]`, `[terminal]`, and `[keys]`. Persist selectively by manually editing `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`; never `chezmoi add` or `chezmoi re-add` this `modify_` target.

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~50 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `tailnet`, `ssh-config`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`,
`kill-process`, `services`, `sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`,
`mac-apps`/`linux-apps`, the agent trio (`agent-panes`, `agent-sessions`,
`agent-wakeup`, dual tmux/Herdr with stable agent-session scheduling) and the `herdr-*` family. Full reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` opens the action menu. There is **no `prefix + e`** —
  that alias was removed, and `prefix + E` is "break every pane into its own
  window", so do not guess it. `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools.
  Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

## SSH layout and machine management

New SSH seeds use grouped directories and explicit Include order with four-space
indentation; existing flat/wildcard layouts stay create-only. Use `dev ssh format`
for indentation preview and opt into `dev ssh organize` for complete Host-block
and comment moves with private recovery. `dev ssh manage` handles explicit
SSH/fleet/Herdr registrations; dotfiles apply never registers machines. The SSH
Television channel prefers dev's static active-alias listing and has a grouped-file
fallback. See `docs/tutorials/setup_ssh_key_on_remote.md` in the source repository.

 `https://docs.specstory.com/integrations/terminal-coding-agents/usage`

```text
## Preventing Cloud publication

- **CLI flag:** `--no-cloud-sync` is documented to “Disable cloud sync even when authenticated.” It is shown for `run`, so use:
  ```bash
  specstory run claude --no-cloud-sync
  specstory sync claude --no-cloud-sync
  ```
  The flag is listed among the general CLI flags; the page does not show a separate `sync` example, but does not restrict the flag to `run`.

- **Configuration:** Set this in either configuration file:
  ```toml
  [cloud_sync]
  enabled = false
  ```
  The section is `[cloud_sync]`; the boolean is `enabled = false`, documented as equivalent to `--no-cloud-sync`. This disables cloud sync for both `run` and `sync`.

- **Precedence:** CLI flags take priority, followed by the project file (`./.specstory/cli/config.toml`), then the user file (`~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`). The documented rule is: “CLI flags — always win”.

- **Environment variables:** No environment variable for disabling SpecStory Cloud publication is documented in the supplied page. The only named variable is `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED`, which controls telemetry when an OTLP endpoint is configured, not cloud sync.

## Resuming Claude sessions

The supplied documentation does **not** document `specstory run claude --resume UUID`, `--resume-session`, or a resume-specific `-s` option.

The documented resume command is:

```bash
specstory resume claude
```

The documented `-s, --session` flag is for converting a session to Markdown with `sync`, not for `run` resumption. To pass custom arguments to the underlying agent, the documented option is `-c, --command`; however, the page does not provide an exact Claude resume invocation using it.
```
</details></tool-use>

# dev-cli

Git owns durable code; worktrees are local checkouts; runtimes are host-local
sessions; dev records task intent.

## Discover what you need

Use `dev <command> --help` for current syntax and flags, and `dev help <topic>`
for workflow explanations. `dev --help` lists commands; `dev help` lists topics.
Prefer supported `--json` output for automation. Read the relevant command before
mutation: some actions execute immediately, while others require preview/apply.
Do not preload manuals, repeat `dev --skill`, or run diagnostics for every task.

## Preserve these boundaries

- Opening a repository needs no task. Choose direct, branch, or worktree
  deliberately; pass an explicit `--base` for branch/worktree creation. Keep
  managed worktrees outside repositories.
- `dev start` normally prepares a checkout/runtime. Agent launch is explicit.
  Parallel writers need coordinated ownership and verified launch targets.
- Completion, artifact finalization, retirement, and branch deletion are separate.
  Finalize agent artifacts after their writer stops; retire an agent checkout
  externally. A runtime's `done` state does not mean cleanup is safe.
- Unknown or cached observations, merged PRs, and command refusals do not grant
  cleanup authority. Resolve the reported conditions; do not improvise force
  removal or bypass trust checks.

## Read a reference for advanced operations

- Worktree provisioning or cross-host lifecycle: [ownership](references/worktree-ownership.md), [lifecycle](references/task-lifecycle.md).
- Parallel agent launches or prompt transports: [agents](references/parallel-agents.md), [handoffs](references/prompt-handoffs.md).
- History retention: [artifacts](references/ai-artifacts.md).
- Agent completion or cleanup batches: [retirement](references/agent-retirement.md), [triage](references/local-triage.md).
- Repository hygiene batches, scans or redaction: [hygiene](references/hygiene.md).
- Repository hooks, publication, or physical organization: [setup](references/repository-bootstrap.md), [bootstrap](references/bootstrap.md).
- SSH dashboard, diagnosis, discovery, tests/activity, keys, credentials and registration: [SSH](references/ssh-hosts.md).
- Dotfile setup, native chezmoi operations, or FLEET host actions: [dotfiles](references/dotfiles.md).
- Skill/MCP/instruction transfers, updates or removal: [transfers](references/agent-interop.md), [maintenance](references/skills-management.md).
- Recursive Git children: [submodules](references/submodules.md).

Use command help and its workflow topic for everyday operations.

## Unexpected dev failures

Read [feedback and repair](references/feedback-and-repair.md). Preserve the
original task; extra investigation, repair, subagents and publication need
explicit consent covering scope and cost.

# Agent history hygiene

Preserve selected agent evidence under the repository's chosen policy. Read
`dev help ai-artifacts` and `dev artifact status` when supported: source tracking,
external archive, protection and distribution are separate choices. Commit
reviewed project knowledge; do not force-add raw history under archive/unmanaged
policy. Verify repository protection from the effective hook chain.

## Prefer the shared dev workflow

When the installed dev supports `hygiene`, use its domain for setup, scans,
private rules and reviewed text changes:

```bash
dev hygiene status
dev hygiene setup --json
dev hygiene setup --apply --plan <id> --yes
dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
dev hygiene scan --scope history --audit --timeout 40m --json
```

`pre-commit` and `gitleaks` are needed for this repository hook recipe. An explicitly unscanned archive copy needs neither. A global `core.hooksPath` can be
correct, but its script may skip all checks when repository configs are absent.
The shared setup preserves existing hooks/comments and refuses an unverified
chain. Repository new/setup's `agent-history-hygiene` initializer uses this same
service. New default hooks block; they do not rewrite or stage files.

Per-repo secret/known/generic policy supports block/warn/off, with private local
overrides and exact reasoned exceptions. Private visibility is advice, never an
automatic exemption. SSH imports are static and reviewed: no DNS, login, Match
exec, private-key reads or rule-value export. Personal rules stay outside Git;
CI checks public rules and must state the missing personal coverage.

Read the bundled dev reference `references/hygiene.md` through `dev help hygiene`
or the public hygiene guide before rule changes or redaction. The CLI supports
all regular text, rather than treating transcripts as the only leak surface.

## Preserve the review trail

1. Identify the exact provider/session UUID from the transcript preamble. Never
   select another session just because its file is newest.
2. Commit product changes and reviewed plans. Follow the selected retention
   policy for raw history; do not broadly stage every agent directory.
3. Use `dev prepare --session provider:uuid` and finalization after its writer
   exits when that lifecycle applies. Byte stability alone is not writer proof.
4. Scan exact staged content. Partial staging must not accidentally stage
   unrelated working-copy edits.
5. In archive mode, raw history may be ignored but must be preserved before
   checkout disposal. In track mode, retain the existing exact-session workflow.
   Exclude conversation evidence from product source archives independently.

Do not close, restart or spawn agents to make hygiene checks pass without the
applicable authorization. A new agent without SpecStory does not stop an older
writer. Preserve the user's original task while offering additional cleanup.

## Reviewed redaction

```bash
dev hygiene redact --report <report-id> --file <reviewed-file> --json
# After reviewing, and after the exact artifact writer exited:
dev hygiene redact --apply --plan <plan-id> --yes --writer-stopped
```

Plans bind native file identity, contents, policy and checkout state. Stale,
modified or partial plans are not authority to overwrite current data. Keep
private recovery and rerun scans/tests after source or configuration changes.
The running transcript is left for a manual external trigger after its writer
stops. No automatic history rewrite, agent launch, commit, push or cleanup occurs.

## External archive workflow

`dev artifact setup` and `dev repo setup --artifacts` preview explicit per-repo
policy. `archive --session provider:uuid` or `--file` creates reviewed snapshots;
apply only after the exact recorder exits. Off/check/redact affect the copy,
not the live source or its index. A disabled scan is recorded as skipped.
Checked snapshots produce masked finding IDs for reasoned fixture exceptions.

Commit reviewed plans with product work before `dev prepare`. New archive intents
bind the destination and policy; redact finalization requires a reviewed
`--archive-plan`. Old tracked intents retain the compatibility scripts below.
Keep those installations while any tracked workflow still depends on them.

`artifact find` reads local committed archive records. Sync and original-backup
publication are explicit Git operations; they never transfer native session DBs.
`artifact migrate` can untrack after verified backup or build separate original,
history and filtered Git copies with commit maps. It never force-pushes source
refs. For historical exposure, use the remediation section rather than treating
path removal as a secret audit. Private raw recovery is not cache.

## Legacy scripts

The scripts remain explicit compatibility utilities. Prefer dev for new setup
and partial-staging-safe edits; a separately published remote redactor hook has
its own version and is not silently updated by dev.

- `find-session.sh --json`: locate candidate transcript/plan metadata.
- `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --dry-run`: inspect exact staging;
  without session-only it may include other dirty artifacts, so use cautiously.
- `scan-staged.sh`: masked JSON-lines locations only, never raw Match/Secret.
  Exit 0 means clean; 20 means candidate findings; legacy `--redact` selects
  exit 10 but only masks output, never modifies files. Exit 30 means missing
  gitleaks; 40 means scanner/JSON/required-parser failure; 2 means not in Git.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py --fix`: explicit legacy artifact mutation. Scanner
  failure is an error, not an empty result; console output uses full sentinels.
  This utility can restage, so use the reviewed dev flow for partial staging.
- `bootstrap-project.sh`: legacy installer; new default templates require dev
  hygiene. Its old `--migrate` targets the separately published remote redactor,
  not the new dev policy migration. Prefer `dev hygiene setup`.

SpecStory may already redact on write, but provider behavior/version is not proof
that every secret class or artifact directory is covered. Preserve existing
`[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` markers. An inert marker must never exempt another secret
on the same line. `.gitleaksignore` contains exact finding fingerprints, not
file/path globs. Portable pattern exceptions need a narrow rule/path/match scope.

## Confirmed historical exposures

Read [remediation](references/remediation.md). First distinguish fixtures,
examples and scanner candidates from confirmed credentials. Revoke/rotate a
confirmed exposed credential at its provider before considering Git history.

Shared main and immutable release tags stay unchanged in ordinary hygiene work.
Correct HEAD in a new commit, and assess old commits, tags, PR references, forks,
clones, caches and distribution artifacts separately. A force push does not erase
all copies or revoke a credential. Personal names, Git author metadata and filenames
also need an explicit impact assessment; text replacement does not rewrite them.

Never echo matching bytes or raw process arguments into a chat to investigate a
finding. Use rule IDs, safe locations and private local reports. Keep raw reports,
recovery images and personal identity dictionaries outside Git and CI logs.

## Validation

Run the skill's fixture tests for redactor/scan-wrapper changes. For dev changes,
run native hygiene/storage/text-transaction tests and the real hook test:

```bash
python scripts/test-hygiene-hooks.py --dev <absolute-built-dev>
```

It uses an isolated HOME/repository and synthetic credentials. Validate same-line
placeholder bypasses, hidden files, partial staging, missing/malformed scanner
results, writer/stale-plan refusal and private recovery. Synchronize embedded
bootstrap assets and both locales of public documentation.

1	# CLAUDE.md
2

5	`AGENTS.md` is the canonical repository guidance file. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to it; edit this file rather than replacing the symlink.

7	## Toolchain and commands
8	
9	- Go 1.26.4 (from `go.mod`) builds the CLI. Python 3.11+ and `uv` are used only for the documentation site.
10	- `make` / `make all` runs `fmt -> vet -> test -> build`. `make fmt` runs `gofmt -w .` and therefore modifies files.
11	- There is no working `make lint` recipe even though `lint` appears in `.PHONY`. The repository's static gates are formatting and `go vet`.
12	
13	```bash
14	make build                         # build ./dev with git-derived version metadata
15	make test                          # go test ./...
16	go test -race -timeout 20m ./...   # CI test command
17	go test ./internal/gitx -run '^TestAddWorktreeUsesExplicitBase$'  # one test
18	go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestName/Subtest$'                  # one subtest
19	make vet                           # go vet ./...
20	files="$(gofmt -l .)" && test -z "$files"  # format check that preserves gofmt failures
21	make e2e                           # real CLI lifecycle in an isolated temporary HOME
22	make skill-sync                    # regenerate command docs, then rebuild embedded skill
23	make skill-check                   # fail when command tree and generated skill reference drift
24	make install                       # binary under PREFIX; skill in user agent directories
25	```
26	
27	Documentation uses the same sequence as CI:
28	
29	```bash
30	uv sync --frozen --extra docs
31	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source
32	uv run mkdocs build --strict
33	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --site site
34	```
35	
36	If generated `docs/llms*.txt` files drift, regenerate them with `uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source --generate-llms` and then rerun the documentation checks.
37	
38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `submodule` owns versioned workspace-member intent and reversible child-clone disposal mechanisms. `gitx` supplies the local gitlink graph; `taskflow` owns recursive lifecycle policy and fresh remote-proof ordering. Gitlink checkouts are legitimate submodules, not nested managed linked worktrees.
56	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints. Lifecycle callers use exact-record revisions and locked compare-and-update/delete transactions rather than treating a previously read task as current.
57	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
58	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
59	- `taskflow` is the UI-agnostic lifecycle authority: it separates recorded intent, typed live observations, immutable guarded plans, approvals, and partial result ledgers. Apply locks and reloads task/Git/worktree/runtime/artifact/remote identity, then rejects stale authority before mutation.
60	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, all registered worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and UI projections consume this joined view.
61	- `agentinterop` owns explicit MCP/skill/instruction transfer plans, guarded apply, stanza/link ownership, private recovery, and optional recipes. Native agent files and skills locks remain authoritative; only explicit preparation/check/launch paths may execute a provider or MCP server. Recovery belongs outside Git, credentials remain runtime references, and native Windows writes fail closed pending verified ACL/identity support.
62	- `triage` owns read-only cross-repository findings, clone-bound local intent, ignored-directory policy and reviewed batch ledgers; `triagetui` is its independent UI. Synchronization uses taskflow plans, and protected cleanup adds guards inside the existing repository lock and immediately before removal. Local scans never reconcile Try catalog entries.
63	- `flowtui` is an independent Bubble Tea model for the preview `dev flow` repository state-machine UI. It receives repository reads and taskflow Plan/Apply callbacks; do not embed it in or add a mode to the dashboard's `tui` model.
64	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
65	- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
66	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
67	- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage`, note FTS, and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
68	- `agenthistory` owns explicit transcript/file retention policy, immutable source-bound archive copies, Git lookup/sync and isolated history migration. Archive bindings/recovery stay in private state, ordinary status never contacts remotes, and source writers/index bytes remain untouched by archiving. `artifact` keeps old commit handoffs and adds externally verified archive receipts; taskflow includes ignored capture readiness in its guarded authority.
69	- `hygiene` owns configurable secret/privacy policy, index/worktree/frozen-history scans, private identity rules and signed replacement plans. Raw findings/recovery stay outside Git; hook setup preserves foreign hooks. Large text transactions explicitly opt into configedit’s Windows backend; existing configuration flows retain their platform contracts.
70	- `feedback` owns durable private reports, sanitized public drafts, revision-bound issue/comment publication receipts and exact repair plans. CLI adapts its repair backend to the shared start flow; agent launch is explicit and prompt context never becomes a public issue body.
71	- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.
72	- `sshhost` owns bounded static discovery of the active user OpenSSH Include closure, canonical files under `~/.ssh/dev.d`, public-key selection/generation/bootstrap, fresh authentication proofs, and the explicit handoff into dev fleet. OpenSSH and plain `ssh -G` remain semantic authority; ordinary setup/remove never rewrite foreign connection definitions, copy private keys, weaken host-key policy, or treat every alias as a fleet member. Explicit format/organize may transform selected user-owned configuration with private guarded recovery; Include restores its caller scope after each file. Named agent providers (Bitwarden, 1Password, Secretive, custom sockets) are located by stat only and never executed; selecting a named-agent key publishes only its public line and writes a v2 fragment (`IdentityAgent`, `SecurityKeyProvider`), which older binaries treat as not dev-owned, while v1 files stay byte-identical. Explicit FIDO generation binds the reviewed native tools/provider, keeps capability observations stat-only, and reports hardware created/unknown effects independently of local publication; only verified SK recovery pairs may be retained. Never use resident-key download or provider loading as a passive probe, and keep automatic Secure Enclave creation blocked until exact native identity mapping is verified.
73	- `sshflow` owns the explicit SSH/fleet/Herdr machine inventory and Plan/Apply orchestration; `herdrremote` calls the native machine CLI without writing its catalog. `configedit` owns source-bound local file transactions and private recovery outside Git, with owner leases and macOS/Linux metadata checks.
74	- `machineregistry` owns controller-local canonical machine UUIDs, scoped provider bindings, explicit unlink suppression and merge redirects in durable private SQLite. These UUIDs never replace the remote `fleet.machine_id` trust pin. `sshdiscovery` owns optional explicit Tailscale status and bounded on-link LAN observations; discovery caches are disposable and never create machine identities or prove authentication. `sshflow` joins these sources while retaining every distinct SSH connection profile; the dashboard SSH view is an adapter to the same services.
75	- `sshactivity` owns private durable per-profile usage and test observations. Usage records actual local dev-mediated SSH process starts; network/full tests never update usage. Observations retain source fingerprints and cannot authorize mutations or imply present connectivity.
76	- `tuiissue` owns typed problem guidance and reviewed native dependency installation recipes. UI actions use finite IDs and exact guarded service callbacks, never executable error text.
77	- `selfupdate` selects exact release platform assets and stages native Go source builds when an asset is absent, preferring the checksummed compact source archive over legacy Go module source. CLI owns confirmation and executable replacement; download/checksum failures never authorize a source fallback, and failed builds retain the installed binary.
78	- `platformfs` owns the native Android Termux home anchor, inherited app-data SELinux/encryption metadata recognition and no-replace publication. It also recognizes macOS kernel-managed provenance: observe it for same-file stale detection, but never restore or require it on a replacement. Verify the exact system/app prefix and all user-controlled descendants; never trust arbitrary UID-1000 directories, relabel files, chmod Android system paths or substitute an overwriting rename.
79	- `sshremote` owns strict bounded v1 SSH capability/inventory/resolve/key/connect protocols and private disposable source/route caches. Only explicit capability may initialize remote dev identity. Static inventory never evaluates SSH or agents; source profiles are scoped by observed UUID, user, root and alias. Local imports preserve native controller trust/authentication context, while remote connect reselects remote-local keys and never retries a started session.
80	- `sshcredential` owns per-context operation secrets, guarded ask/never metadata and exact provider references. System stores and explicitly selected Bitwarden contain saved passwords; the TOML ledger never does. Source-bound authentication evidence authorizes an optional save prompt, not arbitrary askpass, MFA or host-key text. Unknown provider writes stay unknown and are not retried automatically.
81	- `sshvault` owns explicit new vault-key creation, service-bound single-attempt plans, exact public receipts, and native account/profile execution context. It never imports existing private keys or writes new private material to files. Experimental Bitwarden memory creation and delegation to a native profile need separate approvals; freeze the actual environment/cwd and revalidate session/profile/tool identity without exposing session values or hashes. A session or base URL is not endpoint identity: native-context consistency and endpoint-unverified status remain separate from creation and agent visibility. Native no-interaction must prevent private JSON stdin from becoming a credential response; ambiguous writes retain receipts and never auto-retry/delete. Live vault/hardware checks remain separately consented.
82	
83	- `fleetnav` owns contextual host/repository navigation ordering, explicit Herdr profile/session selection and partial results. Repository checks precede profile changes; preparation uses a distinct versioned helper and session-scoped runtime with no focus or attach. Inside Herdr, navigation reports a native sidebar target; outside it attaches to the explicit session. Failures never implicitly switch to SSH.
84	- `fleet` merges the user-authored primary `remotes.toml` with strict dev-owned `remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` registrations. Remote `dev` state remains host-local. `remote_os` selects target semantics: POSIX uses the shell launcher, while Windows uses an encoded PowerShell launcher that accepts only hidden fleet helpers, preserves sync stdin, and never applies controller path rules to remote paths.
85	
86	The principal task start flow spans `internal/cli/start.go`, `start_flow.go`, `gitx`/`wt`, `runtime`, and `task`: resolve the canonical repository and explicit base, create or select the checkout, provision/open it, then persist and annotate the task. Task-backed park/resume/completion/retirement and exact unmanaged Adopt/Remove policy belong in `taskflow`; CLI commands, the dashboard, `sweep`, and `flowtui` are adapters. Preserve report-before-apply and no-data-loss ordering, including the isolated compatibility paths that have not migrated to taskflow.
87	
88	State is split intentionally:
89	
90	- Git remotes/branches are durable code truth.
91	- Worktrees are disposable local checkouts.
92	- Runtime sessions are per-host and re-derivable.
93	- Task TOML and catalog assets hold only intent/identity that Git cannot answer.
94	- Repository quick-note Markdown is durable sidecar data; `notes.db` is only its disposable search index.
95	- `stats.db` is durable observation data; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/*` is disposable.
96	- SSH source/route caches are disposable; remote dev UUIDs, local canonical machine UUIDs and fleet trust pins are separate identities. Credential policy/reference TOML is durable intent; its provider-owned secret is not a cache. Removing a reference does not erase a vault item or revoke a remote password.
97	- The user's OpenSSH configuration is durable connection truth. Ordinary setup/remove own only the exact top-level `Include ~/.ssh/dev.d/*.conf` and structurally valid fragments in `~/.ssh/dev.d`; key bootstrap sends public material only and has no private-key transfer or remote-key revocation lifecycle.
98	- Fleet intent is the merged primary `remotes.toml` plus generated sibling `remotes.d` fragments. A generated fragment exists only after explicit `dev ssh setup --fleet` / `--to fleet|both` or `dev ssh manage --action register --to fleet|both`, and a fresh ordinary alias login; controller caches and each remote machine's paths/tasks/runtime remain re-derivable or host-local.
99	- `paths.state_dir/machines/registry.db` is durable controller-local identity and binding intent; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/ssh-discovery/` contains disposable dated Tailscale/LAN observations. Plain `dev ssh list` stays static; `--tailscale` explicitly queries the optional local CLI and `--lan` reads cached observations. Neither list nor dashboard refresh scans the LAN. The active SSH dashboard may refresh local Tailscale status when `[tui.ssh].background_refresh` is enabled; native discovery returns typed observations independently of cache writes. Candidate setup preserves source/scope provenance and per-stage retained effects.
100	
101	## Behavioral contracts
102	
103	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
104	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
105	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
106	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
107	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
108	- Submodule initialization uses committed gitlinks, never implicitly advances to `main`. Whole child-clone disposal requires explicit recursive approval and fresh recovery proof for its private refs/objects; outer and shared canonical repositories are retained. Local graph refresh never performs remote proof. Child task/runtime/artifact claims block parent disposal.
109	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
110	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
111	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
112	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
113	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
114	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
115	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
116	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output, including `dev hygiene report --json` (`hygiene_summary` schema 1). Stored summaries are historical observations, not proof of current source bytes.
117	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
118	- Explicit SSH format/organize and fleet profile rename/remove are plan-first exceptions for user-selected files; retain comments, Include order, original metadata and private recovery. Never activate dormant files with a new broad Include. Herdr machine add may prepare/start a remote server; leave native approvals native, and remove/disable never stops remote sessions.
119	- SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. Full bootstrap requires an explicit existing key or explicit generation, registers fleet only when explicitly selected, and reports interrupted remote installation as unknown rather than pretending to roll it back.
120	- SSH wizard permission preflight may separately review and apply metadata-only tightening on exact current-user-owned canonical/selected paths. It never recursively chmods, changes ownership, guesses ACLs, or widens permissions; completed repairs survive later cancellation. Listing and dry-run never repair permissions. Local key listing evaluates OpenSSH only behind explicit `--alias`; selected key material remains service-bound and is revalidated before configuration changes and bootstrap.
121	- `dev ssh key doctor` exposes the same permission Plan/Apply with bounded metadata-only key discovery; `--key` restricts the reviewed scope, and `--fix` requires a complete safe plan plus confirmation. Default doctor never mutates, reads private contents, or queries agents/remotes. Batch repairs revalidate the whole reviewed union and retain successful tightening on partial failure.
122	- Source-aware SSH setup can use `--auth existing` without installing a key, and registers only explicitly selected `--to fleet|herdr|both` destinations. Tailscale SSH advertisement is advisory; its port-22 endpoint is not an authorized_keys bootstrap target. Preserve the key-authentication guard and never treat Tailscale policy login as proof that a selected public key worked. Names, ports and cached observations never authorize machine merges; binding/source changes invalidate reviewed plans.
123	- Fleet-source SSH discovery selects explicit hosts without recursive fleet traversal. Local ProxyJump imports never copy remote identity/agent/trust paths; cached route data cannot authorize apply. `connect --on` is one interactive fixed-helper session with no agent forwarding or arbitrary command payload. Normal SSH errors retain child exit status.
124	- Controller password brokerage uses a private per-operation Unix socket or protected Windows pipe, never password argv/environment/files. Exact host/user/port/route contexts gate replies and save evidence. Remote source-to-target credentials remain outside this feature; native key/passphrase interaction is separate.
125	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
126	
127	## Versioning and changelog
128	
129	The current published baseline is `v0.2.39` (2026-09-17). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
130	
131	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
132	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
133	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
134	
135	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
136	
137	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
138	
139	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
140	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
141	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
142	
143	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
144	
145	For a release:
146	
147	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
148	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
149	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
150	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
151	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
152	
153	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
154	
155	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
156	
157	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
158	
159	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
160	
161	| Change | Required synchronization |
162	|---|---|
163	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
164	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
165	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
166	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
167	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
168	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
169	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
170	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
171	
172	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
173	
174	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
175	
176	## Hygiene and skill batch operations
177	
178	`internal/hygiene` owns per-repository setup plans and batch ledgers. REPOS and
179	`hygiene manage` are adapters; JSON batch management previews only. Keep legacy
180	artifact finalizers until their independent lifecycle is replaced. Cached machine
181	privacy imports use only bounded local cache readers and revalidate their source.
182	`internal/agentskill` owns selected-removal policy: exact native names/agent scopes
183	or bundled manifests, source/ownership/dependency proof and postconditions under
184	the provider lease. Never infer complete Windows validation from an advisory
185	step's success conclusion; inspect logs and require the dedicated native gates.
186	
187	## Agent history policy
188	
189	`dev help ai-artifacts` separates source retention, archive location, protection
190	and distribution. New configuration is opt-in. Sources are SpecStory Markdown or
191	explicit files; provider IDs name the originating agent. Do not infer writer exit
192	from byte stability or close agents to finalize evidence. Archive mode verifies
193	ignored bytes before cleanup; existing tracked intents retain their original lane.
194	`git-filter-repo` only operates on new verified copies. Ordinary migration never
195	rewrites source refs or published tags, and raw backups are not secret audits.

54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.

98	- Fleet intent is the merged primary `remotes.toml` plus generated sibling `remotes.d` fragments. 99	- `paths.state_dir/machines/registry.db` is durable controller-local identity and binding intent; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/ssh-discovery/` contains disposable dated Tailscale/LAN observations. Plain `dev ssh list` stays static; `--tailscale` explicitly queries the optional local CLI and `--lan` reads cached observations. Neither list nor dashboard refresh scans the LAN. The active SSH dashboard may refresh local Tailscale status when `[tui.ssh].background_refresh` is enabled; native discovery returns typed observations independently of cache writes. Candidate setup preserves source/scope provenance and per-stage retained effects.

101	## Behavioral contracts
102	
103	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
104	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
105	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
106	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
107	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
108	- Submodule initialization uses committed gitlinks, never implicitly advances to `main`. Whole child-clone disposal requires explicit recursive approval and fresh recovery proof for its private refs/objects; outer and shared canonical repositories are retained. Local graph refresh never performs remote proof. Child task/runtime/artifact claims block parent disposal.
109	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
110	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
111	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
112	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
113	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
114	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
115	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
116	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output, including `dev hygiene report --json` (`hygiene_summary` schema 1). Stored summaries are historical observations, not proof of current source bytes.
117	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
118	- Explicit SSH format/organize and fleet profile rename/remove are plan-first exceptions for user-selected files; retain comments, Include order, original metadata and private recovery. Never activate dormant files with a new broad Include. Herdr machine add may prepare/start a remote server; leave native approvals native, and remove/disable never stops remote sessions.
119	- SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. Full bootstrap requires an explicit existing key or explicit generation, registers fleet only when explicitly selected, and reports interrupted remote installation as unknown rather than pretending to roll it back.
120	- SSH wizard permission preflight may separately review and apply metadata-only tightening on exact current-user-owned canonical/selected paths. It never recursively chmods, changes ownership, guesses ACLs, or widens permissions; completed repairs survive later cancellation. Listing and dry-run never repair permissions. Local key listing evaluates OpenSSH only behind explicit `--alias`; selected key material remains service-bound and is revalidated before configuration changes and bootstrap.
121	- `dev ssh key doctor` exposes the same permission Plan/Apply with bounded metadata-only key discovery; `--key` restricts the reviewed scope, and `--fix` requires a complete safe plan plus confirmation. Default doctor never mutates, reads private contents, or queries agents/remotes. Batch repairs revalidate the whole reviewed union and retain successful tightening on partial failure.
122	- Source-aware SSH setup can use `--auth existing` without installing a key, and registers only explicitly selected `--to fleet|herdr|both` destinations. Tailscale SSH advertisement is advisory; its port-22 endpoint is not an authorized_keys bootstrap target. Preserve the key-authentication guard and never treat Tailscale policy login as proof that a selected public key worked. Names, ports and cached observations never authorize machine merges; binding/source changes invalidate reviewed plans.
123	- Fleet-source SSH discovery selects explicit hosts without recursive fleet traversal. Local ProxyJump imports never copy remote identity/agent/trust paths; cached route data cannot authorize apply. `connect --on` is one interactive fixed-helper session with no agent forwarding or arbitrary command payload. Normal SSH errors retain child exit status.
124	- Controller password brokerage uses a private per-operation Unix socket or protected Windows pipe, never password argv/environment/files. Exact host/user/port/route contexts gate replies and save evidence. Remote source-to-target credentials remain outside this feature; native key/passphrase interaction is separate.
125	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.

127	## Versioning and changelog
128	
129	The current published baseline is `v0.2.39` (2026-09-17). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
130	
131	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
132	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
133	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
134	
135	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
136	
137	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
138	
139	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
140	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
141	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
142	
143	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
144	
145	For a release:
146	
147	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
148	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
149	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
150	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
151	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
152	
153	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
154	
155	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.

158	
159	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.

166	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. 167	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
168	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
169	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
170	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
171	
172	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
173	
174	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.

188	
189	`dev help ai-artifacts` separates source retention, archive location, protection

191	explicit files; provider IDs name the originating agent. Do not infer writer exit
192	from byte stability or close agents to finalize evidence. Archive mode verifies
193	ignored bytes before cleanup; existing tracked intents retain their original lane.

2	
3	`dev hygiene` joins optional gitleaks and pre-commit with repository policy,
4	private local identity rules and guarded text changes. It does not equate a

7	## Inspect and configure

9	Install `gitleaks` and `pre-commit` first. Setup reports missing dependencies;
10	it does not install packages or replace a global hook silently.
11

14	dev hygiene status --check-remote              # explicit GitHub visibility query
15	dev hygiene setup --json
16	dev hygiene setup --apply --plan <id> --yes
17	```
18	
19	Status reads the effective `core.hooksPath`, existing hook and project config.
20	A recognized hook chain is configuration evidence, not proof that every commit
21	was scanned. Hooks can be bypassed by raw Git or external tools.

23	Setup adds the blocking `dev-hygiene` pre-commit hook, safe gitleaks rules and
24	`.dev-cli/hygiene.toml`. It preserves other hooks and YAML comments. Unknown
25	hook chains and conflicting same-name hooks require manual integration. An
26	existing gitleaks config is retained by default. `--migrate-hooks` permits narrow
27	recognized rule migration; `--migrate-rules` proposes whole-config replacement.
28	Review either change against custom rules first.

30	
31	The hook checks index content. It never rewrites files or stages user changes.
32	A missing dev/gitleaks executable, invalid report or failed scan blocks it.

34	
35	Setup writes project configuration. It first respects Git's effective

39	hook. Missing or unverified configured hooks require manual integration, not an
40	automatic local override. There is no `--global` setup option.

42	## Batch setup and gradual migration
43	
44	The normal commit path is `Git -> pre-commit -> dev hygiene scan -> gitleaks +
45	private/public privacy policy`. Setup is a separate configuration operation;
46	commits do not call setup again and do not require an agent.
47	
48	```bash
49	dev hygiene manage --all                 # choose repositories, preview, then apply
50	dev hygiene manage /path/to/a /path/to/b --json  # preview only
51	dev hygiene setup --migrate-hooks --json # one repository, narrow migration
52	```
53	
54	REPOS offers the same single/filtered-repository workflow. Repositories do not
55	need a skills lock. Plans show files, retained dependencies and blockers; choose
56	which prepared plans to apply. Shared Git repositories are processed once. A new
57	common-directory hook requires readable sibling worktree configurations, checked
58	again before installation. Unknown/custom scanner commands need manual review.
59	
60	Migration replaces only recognized equivalent `gitleaks-system` hooks. It keeps

64	the separate explicit whole-config replacement. Re-scan after rule updates;
65	changed detector IDs can require fresh fixture exceptions.

68	Passive status checks presence without executing the scanner. Ensure the hook's

70	upgrade an older `dev` on PATH. Tools are not installed automatically.
71	
72	Batch results retain per-repository completed, blocked, skipped, stale, partial

75	The JSON batch preview contains exact child plan IDs; apply one with the existing

77	
78	The staged checker itself does not mutate files. Pre-commit can temporarily stash

84	## Choose policy
85	
86	Precedence is built-in defaults, user defaults (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/hygiene.toml`),
87	repo policy, private local repo overrides, then explicit scan/status flags.
88	The recommended defaults are `secrets = "block"`, `known = "block"` and
89	`generic = "warn"`. Each category supports `block`, `warn` and `off`. A rule
90	may override its enabled category's disposition; category `off` disables it.
91	
92	```toml
93	version = 1
94	secrets = "block"
95	known = "block"
96	generic = "warn"
97	```
98	
99	Setting all three categories to `off` returns an explicit `skipped` result without
100	reading repository file contents or running the engine; it is not a clean scan.
101	
102	Private visibility supplies advice only. It does not silently weaken policy;
103	unknown or unsupported visibility is never treated as private. GitHub lookup
104	requires `status --check-remote`; `--remote` selects its remote (default origin).
105

108	dev hygiene rules apply --plan <id> --yes
109	```

111	Policy/rule changes are separate reviewed plans. One invocation's scan overrides

115	## Local identity rules and exceptions
116	
117	```bash
118	dev hygiene rules import --from ssh --json
119	dev hygiene rules import --from ssh --select <candidate-id> --json
120	dev hygiene rules import --from local --json
121	dev hygiene rules add --id private-network --kind cidr --value-file network.txt \
122	  --replacement 192.0.2.1 --json
123	dev hygiene rules apply --plan <id> --yes
124	```
125	
126	Imports require explicit candidate selection. SSH uses the bounded static
127	OpenSSH Include closure, including literal aliases, HostName, User and key-path
128	references. It never executes `ssh -G`, `Match exec`, DNS or a remote command,
129	and never reads key material. An incomplete Include closure blocks import.
130	Common public names and generic accounts are recommendations for warnings.
131	Local import supplies home path, account, Git name and Git email candidates.
132	
133	`rules import --from machines` reads existing Tailscale/LAN and Fleet inventory
134	caches only. IPs, hostnames and remote usernames become selectable private
135	candidates; credential stores, keys, discovery commands and remote connections
136	are never queried. Observation timestamps and stale markers remain visible.
137	Missing caches are reported without creating them; incomplete/corrupt caches
138	block imports. Source changes after preview invalidate the saved import plan.
139	
140	Quoted password literals remain detectable in source files. Unquoted assignments
141	are scoped to configuration/script/prose formats, avoiding Go boolean fields and
142	variable expressions. Format-complete test/demo keys still block until a reviewed
143	exact exception is added. Do not exclude tests/docs or an entire line beside a
144	placeholder; prefer inert placeholders or construct detector fixtures at runtime.
145	
146	
147	Literal, CIDR and Go RE2 rules accept optional relative path globs. `directory/**`
148	selects descendants. Rule values come from a file or `--value-file -`; do not
149	put sensitive values in command arguments. Edit or disable existing private
150	rules through a reviewed same-ID rule plan or the private policy file.
151	
152	Private rules, HMAC identifiers, scan records and recovery are stored outside
153	Git under `paths.state_dir/hygiene/repos/<native-repo-id>/`. Linked worktrees
154	share local policy but plans remain bound to an exact checkout. Windows uses
155	protected current-user/SYSTEM ACLs; Unix uses private ownership and permissions.
156	There is no automatic deletion or export of this state.
157	
158	```bash
159	dev hygiene rules allow --report <report-id> --finding <finding-id> \
160	  --reason 'Reviewed synthetic test fixture' --json
161	```
162	
163	Local exceptions bind an exact value/rule/path finding. Shareable TOML exceptions
164	require `rule`, `path`, an anchored `pattern` and a reason. Keep private values
165	out of shareable rules. `.gitleaksignore` contains finding fingerprints, not path
166	globs. `scan --audit` ignores local finding exceptions, that file and inline

168	Placeholders never automatically allow an unrelated key on the same line.
