170	## Scan with an honest scope
171	
172	```bash
173	dev hygiene scan --scope worktree --json
174	dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
175	dev hygiene scan --scope history --audit --timeout 40m --json
176	dev hygiene --public-only --known off --generic off scan --scope history \
177	  --range <full-from-oid>..<full-to-oid> --json
178	```
179	
180	Working-file scans include tracked files and nonignored untracked files. Already
181	tracked files remain in scope after a later `.gitignore` addition. Staged scans
182	use actual index bytes, including hidden files and partial staging. Selected
183	`--file` arguments must already belong to that scope.
184	
185	An explicit range checks versions changed in its selected commits, leaving
186	untouched older files for the full audit. History freezes locally available refs
187	(or an explicit full-OID range), includes
188	merge-only content and removed files, and never fetches implicitly. It does not
189	scan reflogs, unreachable objects, uncommitted work in other checkouts or remote
190	submodule repositories. Nonregular entries and recognized binary formats are
191	listed as exclusions from text scanning. Unsupported text encodings, unreadable
192	or oversized files, changing sources/refs, shallow history, cancellation and
193	scanner failures produce incomplete results. The per-file text limit is 128 MiB;
194	large files are never silently called clean.
195	
196	Public JSON schema 1 records status, scope, frozen refs, counts, safe finding
197	locations, dispositions, exclusions and coverage gaps. It omits source snippets
198	and credential values. Finding IDs and public file/plan digests use private HMAC
199	keys. `complete` describes the declared text scope; a blocking finding or
200	incomplete scan exits unsuccessfully. No findings is not a credential-validity
201	check. Reports may contain identifying filenames not covered by selected rules;
202	review them before sharing.
203	
204	CI uses public repository rules, without global/personal values. It cannot
205	claim to have checked private SSH identities. PR/push scans select the changed
206	commit range; manual workflow dispatch audits all locally fetched history.
207	
208	## Repair invalid UTF-8
209	
210	Warning findings alone do not block a commit. A coverage gap such as
211	`unsupported_text_encoding` makes a scan incomplete even with zero blocking
212	findings. Encoding gaps retain that code and add an `encoding` object with
213	`reason`, zero-based `byte_offset`, one-based `line`, `invalid_bytes`,
214	`invalid_sequences` (contiguous invalid runs) and optional `nul_bytes`.
215	Historical gaps also identify the observed `commit`. Diagnostics contain no
216	source excerpts. Fixing a working file does not repair old Git objects.
217	
218	```bash
219	dev hygiene repair-encoding --file .specstory/history/session.md --json
220	# Optional explicit deletion instead of the default replacement character:
221	dev hygiene repair-encoding --file notes.txt --invalid remove --json
222	# Review the private proposal; only after the exact artifact writer has exited:
223	dev hygiene repair-encoding --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
224	# Review and stage only the intended repair, then check the actual index:
225	dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
226	```
227	
228	The default `--invalid replace` replaces each contiguous invalid byte run with
229	one `�`; `remove` deletes that run. All valid bytes, including existing `�`,
230	UTF-8 BOMs and line endings, remain unchanged. Explicit files may be selected
231	with repeated `--file`; each source and result must fit 128 MiB, with at most
232	256 files and 192 MiB of proposed output per plan. Valid text is a no-op. Known binary extensions,
233	NUL bytes and UTF-16/32 BOMs require separate encoding review; this command does
234	not guess a legacy encoding or recover the original character.
235	
236	Repair uses signed plans, fresh file identity checks and private raw-byte
237	recovery through `dev hygiene restore`. It does not need a secret scanner.
238	Artifact edits require writer attestation and live occupancy checks, including
239	case variants and nested artifact directories. Encoding repair requires long
240	canonical path components without trailing dots/spaces or DOS short-name spellings. The hook
241	never repairs automatically. Apply changes working files only: a partially
242	staged file keeps its exact index contents, so a staged scan still fails until
243	you review and stage the repair. Do not broadly stage newly appended history.
244	Encoding repair does not redact secrets or prove a complete hygiene scan.
245	
246	## Review and apply replacements
247	
248	```bash
249	dev hygiene redact --report <report-id> --file notes.md --json
250	dev hygiene redact --report <report-id> --finding <finding-id> --json
251	dev hygiene review-path <id>                 # open privately; never paste contents
252	dev hygiene redact --apply --plan <id> --yes
253	# Only after the exact artifact writer exited:
254	dev hygiene redact --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
255	```
256	
257	All supported regular text files may be selected. Plans bind the checkout,
258	HEAD/branch, effective policy, scanner inputs, native file identity and content.
259	They are signed private records. An edited plan or stale input requires a new
260	preview. Overlapping matches prefer secret, then known, then generic rules;
261	within a category the longer span wins. The terminal output shows paths, opaque before/after digests and replacement
262	counts. `review-path <id>` locates a private full-content proposal for human
263	inspection. Its integrity is bound to the plan; never paste that file into chat,
264	Git or CI logs. The default output does not echo the original secret.
265	
266	Apply checks the whole selection, then publishes individual guarded transactions
267	with original metadata and private recovery. It retains a partial ledger on
268	failure; never repeat an interrupted operation blindly. Index contents, Git
269	history and installed binaries are not changed. Native Windows protections are
270	specific to these opted-in text transactions; other configedit workflows retain
271	their own platform support contracts. Windows preserves owner/group/DACL
272	semantics; files with alternate streams, explicit integrity labels or special
273	attributes require manual preservation.
274	
275	```bash
276	dev hygiene restore --receipt <receipt-id> --json
277	dev hygiene restore --receipt <receipt-id> --apply --yes
278	```
279	
280	Restore refuses files replaced or edited since the recorded transaction. Artifact
281	recovery also needs `--writer-stopped`. Runtime observations reject recognized
282	writers; a disabled/unavailable runtime cannot prove process absence. The
283	post-writer attestation and source revalidation remain necessary, and raw external
284	writers remain outside dev-mediated locks.
285	
286	Use the [manual dogfood checklist](../reference/hygiene-dogfood.md) for this repo.
287

91	func (m Model) startupOutside() bool {
92		s := m.startupRepo
93		state := m.viewLoad(ViewRepos)

96			!state.hasSnapshot || state.loading || m.viewError(ViewRepos) != nil {

154	func (m Model) beginRegistration(scope repo.DiscoveryScope) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
155		if !m.startupOutside() || m.actions.Discovery.Plan == nil || m.remoteClone.active() {

162		m.overlay = overlayState{kind: overlayActionMenu, title: "discovery configuration", subject: "Preparing preview…", registration: id}
163		m.overlay.addOption(listActionRegistrationCancel, "cancel")
164		return m, func() tea.Msg {
165			p, err := m.actions.Discovery.Plan(m.baseContext(), m.startupRepo.repository, scope)
166			return registrationPlanMsg{sequence: id, plan: p, err: err}

170	func (m Model) acceptRegistrationPlan(msg registrationPlanMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
171		if m.overlay.registration != msg.sequence || m.overlay.kind != overlayActionMenu {
172			return m, nil
173		}
174		if msg.err != nil {
175			m.overlay = overlayState{}
176			m.err = msg.err
177			return m, nil
178		}
179		m.startupRepo.plan = msg.plan
180		p := msg.plan
181		body := fmt.Sprintf("Config: %q\nRepository: %q\n", p.File, p.RepoPath)
182		if p.Before != "" {
183			body += "Before:\n" + p.Before + "\n"
184		}
185		body += "After:\n" + p.After
186		if p.Field == string(repo.DiscoveryParent) {
187			body += "\nScans the parent and sibling projects using the normal depth-3 discovery rules."
188		} else {
189			body += "\nAdds only this repository to discovery."
190		}
191		o := overlayState{kind: overlayActionMenu, title: "review discovery configuration", subject: "Review the path before saving", body: body, registration: msg.sequence}
192		if p.Blocked != "" {
193			o.body += "\nManual edit required: " + p.Blocked + "\nPreserve existing entries when adding the path."
194			if m.actions.EditConfig != nil {
195				o.addOption(listActionRegistrationEdit, "open configuration in editor")
196			}
197		} else if m.actions.Discovery.Apply != nil {
198			o.addOption(listActionRegistrationConfirm, "confirm and save")
199		}
200		o.addOption(listActionRegistrationCancel, "cancel")
201		m.overlay = o
202		return m, nil
203	}

219		m.startupRepo.applying = false
220		m.overlay = overlayState{}
221		if msg.err != nil {
222			m.err = fmt.Errorf("configuration update: %w", msg.err)
223			m.status = msg.status
224			return m, nil
225		}
226		m.startupRepo.saved = true
227		m.startupRepo.refocusAfterSave = true
228		m.status = strings.TrimSpace(msg.status + " — reloading local repositories…")
229		m.beginConfigLoad()
230		return m, m.reloadConfig(false)
231	}
232	
233	func (m *Model) finishRegistrationReload() {
234		s := &m.startupRepo
235		state := m.viewLoad(ViewRepos)
236		if s.savedReposGeneration == 0 || state.generation != s.savedReposGeneration || state.loading {
237			return
238		}
239		s.savedReposGeneration = 0
240		if state.outcome == perftrace.OutcomeSuccess && state.hasSnapshot {
241			s.saved = false
242			m.status = "Configuration saved; local repositories refreshed"
243			return
244		}
245		reason := m.viewError(ViewRepos)
246		if reason == nil {
247			reason = fmt.Errorf("repository inventory is incomplete")
248		}
249		m.err = fmt.Errorf("configuration saved, but repository refresh failed (press r to retry): %w", reason)
250	}

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	`AGENTS.md` is the canonical repository guidance file. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to it; edit this file rather than replacing the symlink.
6	
7	## Toolchain and commands
8	
9	- Go 1.26.4 (from `go.mod`) builds the CLI. Python 3.11+ and `uv` are used only for the documentation site.
10	- `make` / `make all` runs `fmt -> vet -> test -> build`. `make fmt` runs `gofmt -w .` and therefore modifies files.
11	- There is no working `make lint` recipe even though `lint` appears in `.PHONY`. The repository's static gates are formatting and `go vet`.
12	
13	```bash
14	make build                         # build ./dev with git-derived version metadata
15	make test                          # go test ./...
16	go test -race -timeout 20m ./...   # CI test command
17	go test ./internal/gitx -run '^TestAddWorktreeUsesExplicitBase$'  # one test
18	go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestName/Subtest$'                  # one subtest
19	make vet                           # go vet ./...
20	files="$(gofmt -l .)" && test -z "$files"  # format check that preserves gofmt failures
21	make e2e                           # real CLI lifecycle in an isolated temporary HOME
22	make skill-sync                    # regenerate command docs, then rebuild embedded skill
23	make skill-check                   # fail when command tree and generated skill reference drift
24	make install                       # binary under PREFIX; skill in user agent directories
25	```
26	
27	Documentation uses the same sequence as CI:
28	
29	```bash
30	uv sync --frozen --extra docs
31	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source
32	uv run mkdocs build --strict
33	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --site site
34	```
35	
36	If generated `docs/llms*.txt` files drift, regenerate them with `uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source --generate-llms` and then rerun the documentation checks.
37	
38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `submodule` owns versioned workspace-member intent and reversible child-clone disposal mechanisms. `gitx` supplies the local gitlink graph; `taskflow` owns recursive lifecycle policy and fresh remote-proof ordering. Gitlink checkouts are legitimate submodules, not nested managed linked worktrees.
56	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints. Lifecycle callers use exact-record revisions and locked compare-and-update/delete transactions rather than treating a previously read task as current.
57	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
58	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
59	- `taskflow` is the UI-agnostic lifecycle authority: it separates recorded intent, typed live observations, immutable guarded plans, approvals, and partial result ledgers. Apply locks and reloads task/Git/worktree/runtime/artifact/remote identity, then rejects stale authority before mutation.
60	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, all registered worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and UI projections consume this joined view.
61	- `agentinterop` owns explicit MCP/skill/instruction transfer plans, guarded apply, stanza/link ownership, private recovery, and optional recipes. Native agent files and skills locks remain authoritative; only explicit preparation/check/launch paths may execute a provider or MCP server. Recovery belongs outside Git, credentials remain runtime references, and native Windows writes fail closed pending verified ACL/identity support.
62	- `triage` owns read-only cross-repository findings, clone-bound local intent, ignored-directory policy and reviewed batch ledgers; `triagetui` is its independent UI. Synchronization uses taskflow plans, and protected cleanup adds guards inside the existing repository lock and immediately before removal. Local scans never reconcile Try catalog entries.
63	- `flowtui` is an independent Bubble Tea model for the preview `dev flow` repository state-machine UI. It receives repository reads and taskflow Plan/Apply callbacks; do not embed it in or add a mode to the dashboard's `tui` model.
64	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
65	- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
66	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
67	- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage`, note FTS, and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
68	- `agenthistory` owns explicit transcript/file retention policy, immutable source-bound archive copies, Git lookup/sync and isolated history migration. Archive bindings/recovery stay in private state, ordinary status never contacts remotes, and source writers/index bytes remain untouched by archiving. `artifact` keeps old commit handoffs and adds externally verified archive receipts; taskflow includes ignored capture readiness in its guarded authority.
69	- `hygiene` owns configurable secret/privacy policy, index/worktree/frozen-history scans, private identity rules and signed replacement plans. Raw findings/recovery stay outside Git; hook setup preserves foreign hooks. Large text transactions explicitly opt into configedit’s Windows backend; existing configuration flows retain their platform contracts.
70	- `feedback` owns durable private reports, sanitized public drafts, revision-bound issue/comment publication receipts and exact repair plans. CLI adapts its repair backend to the shared start flow; agent launch is explicit and prompt context never becomes a public issue body.
71	- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.
72	- `sshhost` owns bounded static discovery of the active user OpenSSH Include closure, canonical files under `~/.ssh/dev.d`, public-key selection/generation/bootstrap, fresh authentication proofs, and the explicit handoff into dev fleet. OpenSSH and plain `ssh -G` remain semantic authority; ordinary setup/remove never rewrite foreign connection definitions, copy private keys, weaken host-key policy, or treat every alias as a fleet member. Explicit format/organize may transform selected user-owned configuration with private guarded recovery; Include restores its caller scope after each file. Named agent providers (Bitwarden, 1Password, Secretive, custom sockets) are located by stat only and never executed; selecting a named-agent key publishes only its public line and writes a v2 fragment (`IdentityAgent`, `SecurityKeyProvider`), which older binaries treat as not dev-owned, while v1 files stay byte-identical. Explicit FIDO generation binds the reviewed native tools/provider, keeps capability observations stat-only, and reports hardware created/unknown effects independently of local publication; only verified SK recovery pairs may be retained. Never use resident-key download or provider loading as a passive probe, and keep automatic Secure Enclave creation blocked until exact native identity mapping is verified.
73	- `sshflow` owns the explicit SSH/fleet/Herdr machine inventory and Plan/Apply orchestration; `herdrremote` calls the native machine CLI without writing its catalog. `configedit` owns source-bound local file transactions and private recovery outside Git, with owner leases and macOS/Linux metadata checks.
74	- `machineregistry` owns controller-local canonical machine UUIDs, scoped provider bindings, explicit unlink suppression and merge redirects in durable private SQLite. These UUIDs never replace the remote `fleet.machine_id` trust pin. `sshdiscovery` owns optional explicit Tailscale status and bounded on-link LAN observations; discovery caches are disposable and never create machine identities or prove authentication. `sshflow` joins these sources while retaining every distinct SSH connection profile; the dashboard SSH view is an adapter to the same services.
75	- `sshactivity` owns private durable per-profile usage and test observations. Usage records actual local dev-mediated SSH process starts; network/full tests never update usage. Observations retain source fingerprints and cannot authorize mutations or imply present connectivity.
76	- `tuiissue` owns typed problem guidance and reviewed native dependency installation recipes. UI actions use finite IDs and exact guarded service callbacks, never executable error text.
77	- `selfupdate` selects exact release platform assets and stages native Go source builds when an asset is absent, preferring the checksummed compact source archive over legacy Go module source. CLI owns confirmation and executable replacement; download/checksum failures never authorize a source fallback, and failed builds retain the installed binary.
78	- `platformfs` owns the native Android Termux home anchor, inherited app-data SELinux/encryption metadata recognition and no-replace publication. It also recognizes macOS kernel-managed provenance: observe it for same-file stale detection, but never restore or require it on a replacement. Verify the exact system/app prefix and all user-controlled descendants; never trust arbitrary UID-1000 directories, relabel files, chmod Android system paths or substitute an overwriting rename.
79	- `sshremote` owns strict bounded v1 SSH capability/inventory/resolve/key/connect protocols and private disposable source/route caches. Only explicit capability may initialize remote dev identity. Static inventory never evaluates SSH or agents; source profiles are scoped by observed UUID, user, root and alias. Local imports preserve native controller trust/authentication context, while remote connect reselects remote-local keys and never retries a started session.
80	- `sshcredential` owns per-context operation secrets, guarded ask/never metadata and exact provider references. System stores and explicitly selected Bitwarden contain saved passwords; the TOML ledger never does. Source-bound authentication evidence authorizes an optional save prompt, not arbitrary askpass, MFA or host-key text. Unknown provider writes stay unknown and are not retried automatically.
81	- `sshvault` owns explicit new vault-key creation, service-bound single-attempt plans, exact public receipts, and native account/profile execution context. It never imports existing private keys or writes new private material to files. Experimental Bitwarden memory creation and delegation to a native profile need separate approvals; freeze the actual environment/cwd and revalidate session/profile/tool identity without exposing session values or hashes. A session or base URL is not endpoint identity: native-context consistency and endpoint-unverified status remain separate from creation and agent visibility. Native no-interaction must prevent private JSON stdin from becoming a credential response; ambiguous writes retain receipts and never auto-retry/delete. Live vault/hardware checks remain separately consented.
82	
83	- `fleetnav` owns contextual host/repository navigation ordering, explicit Herdr profile/session selection and partial results. Repository checks precede profile changes; preparation uses a distinct versioned helper and session-scoped runtime with no focus or attach. Inside Herdr, navigation reports a native sidebar target; outside it attaches to the explicit session. Failures never implicitly switch to SSH.
84	- `fleet` merges the user-authored primary `remotes.toml` with strict dev-owned `remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` registrations. Remote `dev` state remains host-local. `remote_os` selects target semantics: POSIX uses the shell launcher, while Windows uses an encoded PowerShell launcher that accepts only hidden fleet helpers, preserves sync stdin, and never applies controller path rules to remote paths.
85	
86	The principal task start flow spans `internal/cli/start.go`, `start_flow.go`, `gitx`/`wt`, `runtime`, and `task`: resolve the canonical repository and explicit base, create or select the checkout, provision/open it, then persist and annotate the task. Task-backed park/resume/completion/retirement and exact unmanaged Adopt/Remove policy belong in `taskflow`; CLI commands, the dashboard, `sweep`, and `flowtui` are adapters. Preserve report-before-apply and no-data-loss ordering, including the isolated compatibility paths that have not migrated to taskflow.
87	
88	State is split intentionally:
89	
90	- Git remotes/branches are durable code truth.
91	- Worktrees are disposable local checkouts.
92	- Runtime sessions are per-host and re-derivable.
93	- Task TOML and catalog assets hold only intent/identity that Git cannot answer.
94	- Repository quick-note Markdown is durable sidecar data; `notes.db` is only its disposable search index.
95	- `stats.db` is durable observation data; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/*` is disposable.
96	- SSH source/route caches are disposable; remote dev UUIDs, local canonical machine UUIDs and fleet trust pins are separate identities. Credential policy/reference TOML is durable intent; its provider-owned secret is not a cache. Removing a reference does not erase a vault item or revoke a remote password.
97	- The user's OpenSSH configuration is durable connection truth. Ordinary setup/remove own only the exact top-level `Include ~/.ssh/dev.d/*.conf` and structurally valid fragments in `~/.ssh/dev.d`; key bootstrap sends public material only and has no private-key transfer or remote-key revocation lifecycle.
98	- Fleet intent is the merged primary `remotes.toml` plus generated sibling `remotes.d` fragments. A generated fragment exists only after explicit `dev ssh setup --fleet` / `--to fleet|both` or `dev ssh manage --action register --to fleet|both`, and a fresh ordinary alias login; controller caches and each remote machine's paths/tasks/runtime remain re-derivable or host-local.
99	- `paths.state_dir/machines/registry.db` is durable controller-local identity and binding intent; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/ssh-discovery/` contains disposable dated Tailscale/LAN observations. Plain `dev ssh list` stays static; `--tailscale` explicitly queries the optional local CLI and `--lan` reads cached observations. Neither list nor dashboard refresh scans the LAN. The active SSH dashboard may refresh local Tailscale status when `[tui.ssh].background_refresh` is enabled; native discovery returns typed observations independently of cache writes. Candidate setup preserves source/scope provenance and per-stage retained effects.
100	
101	## Behavioral contracts
102	
103	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
104	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
105	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
106	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
107	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
108	- Submodule initialization uses committed gitlinks, never implicitly advances to `main`. Whole child-clone disposal requires explicit recursive approval and fresh recovery proof for its private refs/objects; outer and shared canonical repositories are retained. Local graph refresh never performs remote proof. Child task/runtime/artifact claims block parent disposal.
109	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
110	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
111	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
112	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
113	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
114	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
115	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
116	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output, including `dev hygiene report --json` (`hygiene_summary` schema 1). Stored summaries are historical observations, not proof of current source bytes.
117	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
118	- Explicit SSH format/organize and fleet profile rename/remove are plan-first exceptions for user-selected files; retain comments, Include order, original metadata and private recovery. Never activate dormant files with a new broad Include. Herdr machine add may prepare/start a remote server; leave native approvals native, and remove/disable never stops remote sessions.
119	- SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. Full bootstrap requires an explicit existing key or explicit generation, registers fleet only when explicitly selected, and reports interrupted remote installation as unknown rather than pretending to roll it back.
120	- SSH wizard permission preflight may separately review and apply metadata-only tightening on exact current-user-owned canonical/selected paths. It never recursively chmods, changes ownership, guesses ACLs, or widens permissions; completed repairs survive later cancellation. Listing and dry-run never repair permissions. Local key listing evaluates OpenSSH only behind explicit `--alias`; selected key material remains service-bound and is revalidated before configuration changes and bootstrap.
121	- `dev ssh key doctor` exposes the same permission Plan/Apply with bounded metadata-only key discovery; `--key` restricts the reviewed scope, and `--fix` requires a complete safe plan plus confirmation. Default doctor never mutates, reads private contents, or queries agents/remotes. Batch repairs revalidate the whole reviewed union and retain successful tightening on partial failure.
122	- Source-aware SSH setup can use `--auth existing` without installing a key, and registers only explicitly selected `--to fleet|herdr|both` destinations. Tailscale SSH advertisement is advisory; its port-22 endpoint is not an authorized_keys bootstrap target. Preserve the key-authentication guard and never treat Tailscale policy login as proof that a selected public key worked. Names, ports and cached observations never authorize machine merges; binding/source changes invalidate reviewed plans.
123	- Fleet-source SSH discovery selects explicit hosts without recursive fleet traversal. Local ProxyJump imports never copy remote identity/agent/trust paths; cached route data cannot authorize apply. `connect --on` is one interactive fixed-helper session with no agent forwarding or arbitrary command payload. Normal SSH errors retain child exit status.
124	- Controller password brokerage uses a private per-operation Unix socket or protected Windows pipe, never password argv/environment/files. Exact host/user/port/route contexts gate replies and save evidence. Remote source-to-target credentials remain outside this feature; native key/passphrase interaction is separate.
125	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
126	
127	## Versioning and changelog
128	
129	The current published baseline is `v0.2.39` (2026-09-17). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
130	
131	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
132	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
133	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
134	
135	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
136	
137	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
138	
139	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
140	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
141	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
142	
143	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
144	
145	For a release:
146	
147	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
148	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
149	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
150	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
151	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
152	
153	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
154	
155	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
156	
157	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
158	
159	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
160	
161	| Change | Required synchronization |
162	|---|---|
163	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
164	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
165	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
166	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
167	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
168	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
169	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
170	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
171	
172	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
173	
174	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
175	
176	## Hygiene and skill batch operations
177	
178	`internal/hygiene` owns per-repository setup plans and batch ledgers. REPOS and
179	`hygiene manage` are adapters; JSON batch management previews only. Keep legacy
180	artifact finalizers until their independent lifecycle is replaced. Cached machine
181	privacy imports use only bounded local cache readers and revalidate their source.
182	`internal/agentskill` owns selected-removal policy: exact native names/agent scopes
183	or bundled manifests, source/ownership/dependency proof and postconditions under
184	the provider lease. Never infer complete Windows validation from an advisory
185	step's success conclusion; inspect logs and require the dedicated native gates.
186	
187	## Agent history policy
188	
189	`dev help ai-artifacts` separates source retention, archive location, protection
190	and distribution. New configuration is opt-in. Sources are SpecStory Markdown or
191	explicit files; provider IDs name the originating agent. Do not infer writer exit
192	from byte stability or close agents to finalize evidence. Archive mode verifies
193	ignored bytes before cleanup; existing tracked intents retain their original lane.
194	`git-filter-repo` only operates on new verified copies. Ordinary migration never
195	rewrites source refs or published tags, and raw backups are not secret audits.

70	- `skills/owned/` — first-party skills maintained in another repository owned by the maintainer. Edit the source project, then sync its distribution copy here.

75	`license_path`, `frozen`, and upstream commit tracking. Add published owned sources

77	cannot serve as a distributable copy.

86	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). 87	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
88	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
89	
90	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.

104	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
105	
106	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
107	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
108	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:

111	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in

114	  `skills@1.5.24` writes `skills-lock.json`, but a renamed skill is still a

118	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
119	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because

242	
243	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
244	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
245	own conventions). It has four subareas:
246	
247	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
248	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
249	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
250	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
251	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
252	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
253	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
254	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
255	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
256	- `docs/catalog/curiosities.md` — docs-only shelf for interesting,
257	  provocative, or highly personal skills that are deliberately excluded
258	  from `vendor.yaml`, marketplace grouping, and routine skill discovery.
259	  Entries use `skipped` with the reason they remain docs-only.
260	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
261	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
262	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
263	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
264	  status / license / last_verified`).
265	
266	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
267	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
268	
269	| Status | Meaning |
270	|---|---|
271	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
272	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
273	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
274	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
275	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
276	
277	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
278	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
279	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
280	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
281	
282	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
283	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
284	
285	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
286	
287	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
288	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
289	
290	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
291	2. The root cause
292	3. The workaround
293	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
294	
295	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
296	the explanation they do not know yet.
297
```
</details></tool-use>

491	// New builds the dashboard.
492	func New(actions Actions, rows []inventory.Row, repos []RepoRow) Model {
493		in := textinput.New()
494		in.CharLimit = 200
495		cloneSpinner := spinner.MiniDot
496		cloneSpinner.FPS = 200 * time.Millisecond
497	
498		m := Model{
499			actions:            actions,
500			rows:               rows,
501			repos:              repos,
502			input:              in,
503			remoteCloneSpinner: spinner.New(spinner.WithSpinner(cloneSpinner)),
504			width:              100,
505			height:             30,
506			firstViewReady:     make(chan struct{}),
507			firstViewOnce:      &sync.Once{},
508			fleetTree:          fleetTreeState{background: true, generation: 1, maxParallel: 4},
509			fleetWarmupAt:      time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second),
510		}
511		if len(actions.Tools) > 0 {
512			m.toolGeneration = 1
513		}
514		if rows != nil {
515			m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewTasks, perftrace.SourceLive, perftrace.FreshnessFresh, true)
516		}
517		if repos != nil {
518			m.seedViewSnapshot(ViewRepos, perftrace.SourceLive, perftrace.FreshnessFresh, true)
519		}
520		return m
521	}
522	
523	// WithTrace observes performance boundaries without controlling model state.
524	func (m Model) WithTrace(trace *perftrace.Recorder) Model {
525		m.trace = trace
526		return m
527	}

529	// WithContext bounds asynchronous read/probe commands to one dashboard run.
530	func (m Model) WithContext(ctx context.Context) Model {
531		m.runContext = ctx
532		return m
533	}

535	// WithRemotes seeds the lazy forge view from a fresh on-disk cache. The first

592	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
593		if m.resumeInitial {

596		commands := []tea.Cmd{textinput.Blink}

598			commands = append(commands, command)

605		}
606		if m.actions.LoadRemoteCache != nil {
607			commands = append(commands, m.loadRemoteCache())
608		}
609		if m.hostFleetEnabled() {
610			commands = append(commands, m.loadFleetHosts())
611			if m.fleetTree.background {
612				commands = append(commands, tea.Tick(max(0, time.Until(m.fleetWarmupAt)), func(time.Time) tea.Msg { return fleetWarmupMsg{} }))
613			}
614		} else if m.actions.LoadFleetCache != nil {
615			commands = append(commands, m.loadFleetCache())
616		}
617		if m.actions.AfterFirstView != nil {
618			commands = append(commands, m.runAfterFirstView())
619		}
620		return tea.Batch(commands...)

```text
1	# AI artifacts: what to keep, archive, and ship
2	
3	Keep useful decisions, choose where transcripts live, and ship product inputs.
4	
5	## Decide by purpose
6	
7	| Material | Purpose | Usual treatment |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| Code, tests, current specs and docs | Current behavior and contracts | Maintain with the project |
10	| Reviewed plans, decisions and pitfalls | Requirements, rationale and lessons | Keep concise, with status and context |
11	| Raw transcripts, draft plans and tool output | Evidence of the development process | Choose per repository: track, archive elsewhere, or keep local |
12	| Native sessions and tool databases | Resume state, indexes or curation records | Follow each tool's backup contract |
13	
14	AI authorship alone does not determine where a file belongs. Promote useful
15	conclusions into the project's existing docs, decisions, backlog or pitfalls;
16	old transcripts are historical evidence, not current instructions. Do not ask
17	future contributors to read every exploratory conversation to understand code.
18	
19	## Four independent choices
20	
21	1. Does this material belong in the source repository's Git history?
22	2. Where is the durable copy, and how will another machine obtain it?
23	3. Should that copy be checked, redacted, or explicitly stored without scanning?
24	4. Does the material belong in a source distribution or installed product?
25	
26	A private experiment can keep raw chats in Git. A public or long-lived project
27	can keep reviewed decisions in Git and transcripts in a separate private Git
28	repository. A private destination does not itself change hygiene policy: choose
29	it explicitly. An unscanned copy is preserved evidence, not a clean scan.
30	
31	## SpecStory: capture is separate from publication
32	
33	SpecStory is the current transcript integration. The originating agent is the
34	provider, for example `codex:<uuid>` or `claude:<uuid>`; SpecStory is the recorder.
35	Its Markdown export is not the native agent session and does not guarantee resume.
36	
37	SpecStory can write per-worktree `.specstory/history/` files or use an explicit
38	`--output-dir`. Preserve project and session identity when combining histories.
39	A shared flat directory does not by itself retain project attribution. Tools
40	such as Lore have their own metadata and curation state; do not assume all of
41	their databases can be discarded and reconstructed from Markdown.
42	
43	For the existing tracked-history workflow:
44	
45	```bash
46	dev hygiene status
47	dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
48	dev prepare --session codex:<uuid>
49	# After the exact recorder has stopped, from outside its checkout:
50	dev artifact finalize --intent <id> --writer-stopped
51	```
52	
53	Preparation does not stop the writer. Never repeatedly redact a file that a
54	recorder is still rewriting from its native source. `dev hygiene redact` requires
55	an exact reviewed plan; artifact writes additionally require post-writer proof.
56	Private recovery and a stable byte snapshot do not prove that a process exited.
57	
58	The shared artifact writer guard covers hygiene redact/repair-encoding/restore/
59	manage and artifact finalize/archive/migrate. Other recognized live agents
60	covering the checkout always block, including idle/done agents. The calling
61	agent is exempt when Herdr's exact session ID (`agent_session` kind `id`, not a
62	title) differs from every target artifact's valid UUID in its actual
63	SpecStory-generated anchored preamble. Only `.specstory/history/*.md` supplies
64	this proof, not filenames or UUIDs later in the text. Plans or unprovable transcripts require global
65	`--allow-shared-checkout`: an explicit assertion of disjoint ownership after the
66	writer exits, never an automatic retry flag. Unknown caller identity needs
67	that explicit attestation. An identified caller-owned live transcript is refused
68	even with the override. Post-writer proof and source revalidation remain
69	required; restore checks the receipt's exact paths.
70	
71	If history is ignored, ordinary code commits need not scan it. An already tracked
72	file remains tracked after adding `.gitignore`: removing it from the index is a
73	separate reviewed operation. Keep or archive ignored history before deleting its
74	worktree; ignored does not mean disposable or backed up.
75	
76	## Choose and apply repository policy
77	
78	No policy means existing behavior is unchanged. `track` retains the existing
79	source-commit finalizer, `archive` preserves selected evidence in a separate Git
80	checkout, and `unmanaged` leaves retention to the user. Sources are `specstory`
81	(recorder Markdown) or `files` (explicit source-relative exports/plans).
82	
83	```bash
84	# Create the ordinary archive repository separately; configure its Git identity.
85	git init -b main /path/to/history
86	# Explicit private raw preservation; choose check or redact when wanted.
87	dev artifact setup --mode archive --source specstory --archive /path/to/history \
88	  --protection off --json
89	dev artifact setup --apply --plan <id> --yes
90	dev artifact status
91	# The same planner through repository setup:
92	dev repo setup --artifacts --mode unmanaged --json
93	```
94	
95	Setup edits only reviewed policy, local binding, ignore and export files; it
96	never untracks, commits, pushes or installs tools. `repo setup --artifacts` is
97	separate from a scaffold plan. Apply there with `--artifacts --apply --plan <id>
98	--yes`. Review and commit shared policy changes yourself.
99	
100	The shareable `.dev-cli/artifacts.toml` contains the stable project ID, retention
101	mode, source and literal paths. The archive path and protection binding stay in
102	private host state. Bind a cloned project to the desired archive on each host;
103	do not infer project identity from a folder basename or current branch.
104	
105	`--capture project` keeps normal per-worktree recorder output. `--capture external`
106	sets a checkout-specific local SpecStory output directory outside Git. It requires
107	untracked native config and enabled local Markdown export; tracked/complex config
108	requires manual review. Run setup in each new external-capture checkout. Existing
109	cloud settings and native session stores remain under SpecStory's control.
110	
111	## Preserve copies, then find them
112	
113	```bash
114	dev artifact archive --session codex:<uuid> --json
115	# Inspect the private review directory, then after the recorder exits:
116	dev artifact archive --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
117	dev artifact find --session codex:<uuid>
118	dev artifact find --commit <full-source-commit-id>
119	dev artifact find 'literal search text' --all
120	```
121	
122	For `--source files`, select exact configured paths with repeated `--file`.
123	Inventory is bounded to 10,000 files and each operation to 256 selected files;
124	current snapshots are limited to 128 MiB per file. Oversized or unsafe inputs
125	fail explicitly. Search reads committed records on the archive's current branch;
126	`--all` includes its other projects. Results contain locations and line numbers,
127	not snippets; no network, native history crawl or agent resume occurs.
128	
129	Archive commits contain ordinary snapshot files and metadata under `projects/`.
130	The metadata binds project/session, original and stored content digests and the
131	source commit. Source files and source index bytes stay untouched. The project
132	archive gets text/ident exclusions so CRLF and literal bytes survive Git; custom
133	content filters such as encryption, LFS or encoding transforms require the
134	archive's native workflow and are never silently bypassed. Existing Git hooks
135	still run. Archive access controls and off-host backups remain the operator's
136	responsibility.
137	
138	`off` saves raw input without a scanner. `check` uses enabled source-repository
139	hygiene policy. `redact` proposes replacements on the copy and checks the result
140	again. Disabled categories remain disabled; skipped is not clean. Blocking
141	reports contain safe finding IDs for the existing `dev hygiene rules allow`
142	workflow. Exact fixture exceptions need review and a reason. Snapshot scans
143	support inline gitleaks rules and useDefault, not external rule-file includes.
144	
145	Unchanged bytes reuse signed local scan evidence only when the path, policy,
146	exceptions, scanner inputs and executables match. Changed bytes or rules rescan.
147	Partial scans never pass. Review original/copy payloads privately; raw recovery,
148	reports and receipts stay under `paths.state_dir`, outside Git and cache clearing.
149	Filenames and metadata can still identify people or systems: review before sharing.
150	
151	After committing product/policy changes, `dev prepare` also supports an archive
152	policy. Off/check finalization creates the exact archive copy after writer exit.
153	For redact, preview and review `artifact archive` first, then pass its ID to
154	`artifact finalize --archive-plan <id> --writer-stopped`. Reviewed plans should
155	be committed with product changes; prepared SpecStory archive handoffs select one
156	exact transcript. Old intents keep their original destination and requirements.
157	The tracked-history finalizer still uses the compatibility skill's scripts.
158	
159	Retirement checks signed archive receipts and current ignored capture bytes.
160	New or changed evidence blocks cleanup until preserved. Local archive durability
161	is distinct from remote sync; ordinary status and readiness never query a remote.
162	
163	For an intent not matched to the checkout path, readiness checks canonical Git
164	common-directory identity before requiring a branch to resolve a moved intent.
165	Pending or finalized records proven to belong to another repository therefore do
166	not block a detached checkout; detached HEAD is normal for pinned submodules.
167	Relevant pending intents, ambiguous repository or moved-intent identity, and an
168	unreadable intent store still block. Exact finalized-receipt requirements are
169	unchanged. Failed child artifact observations report their underlying cause,
170	never a false clean result.
171	
172	Empty gitlink children have separate path-based task/artifact claim checks,
173	without inheriting the parent's Git identity. Any matching non-discarded artifact
174	intent, even finalized, conservatively blocks recursive empty-child removal;
175	discarded records still bind the reviewed plan's authority.
176	
177	## Explicit Git synchronization and original backups
178	
179	```bash
180	dev artifact sync --push --json       # preview contacts the configured remote
181	dev artifact sync --apply --plan <id> --yes
182	dev artifact sync --pull --json       # separate pull preview; fast-forward only
183	
184	dev artifact migrate --mode untrack --path .specstory/history --json
185	dev artifact migrate --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
186	
187	dev artifact migrate --mode split --path .specstory/history --json
188	dev artifact migrate --apply --plan <id> --yes
189	# Optional: publish the original named refs to a separate empty destination.
190	dev artifact backup <completed-migration-id> --remote <git-url> --json
191	dev artifact backup --apply --plan <backup-plan-id> --yes
192	```
193	
194	Untrack saves original refs and selected working files, edits ignore rules and
195	removes only selected index entries. Other staged/unstaged work remains intact;
196	existing prepared handoffs must be resolved first. Untracking does not itself
197	configure future archive capture.
198	
199	Split requires git-filter-repo and complete local history. It produces verified
200	`original.bundle`, `original.git`, `history.git`, `filtered.git`, both commit maps,
201	selected working snapshots in `current/`, and a migration manifest. Every mapped
202	tree is checked against the selected-path projection. Empty commits/merge topology
203	and message bytes are retained; rewritten signatures cannot remain valid. A
204	restore clone verifies the original bundle. Neither source refs nor remotes change.
205	Raw backups are not a hygiene audit. Other worktrees' uncommitted files, reflogs,
206	unreachable objects, LFS payloads and submodule repositories are outside coverage.
207	Detached tips need a recovery ref before migration.
208	
209	Backup publication sends frozen named refs with empty-ref leases. Selected
210	uncommitted working snapshots stay in local `current/`; they are not in the Git
211	remote backup. Archive sync pins the reviewed destination and branch: push proves
212	ancestry before an exact lease, pull only fast-forwards. Resolve divergence with
213	native Git; dev does not force-overwrite or synthesize merges.
214	
215	Private operation ledgers retain partial effects, output and recovery paths.
216	After interruption inspect those paths and the remote, then prepare a new plan;
217	never blindly replay a partial operation. Original-remote cutover, release/tag
218	migration and force-with-lease publication of filtered history are separate,
219	operator-coordinated actions.
220	
221	## Distribution, untracking and history migration
222	
223	| Action | Effect | Earlier commits |
224	|---|---|---|
225	| `.gitattributes` `export-ignore` | Exclude selected paths from `git archive` source packages | Unchanged |
226	| Ignore and untrack | Stop including new versions in source commits; retain working files | Unchanged |
227	| Filter a separate repository copy | Build replacement history without selected paths | Different commit IDs in that copy |
228	
229	For example, this excludes chats from source archives while leaving them in Git:
230	
231	```gitattributes
232	/.specstory export-ignore
233	/.specstory/** export-ignore
234	```
235	
236	Verify the exported source still builds, including embedded resources. Packaging
237	systems have separate inclusion rules; an archive exclusion is not a universal
238	package filter. New rules affect new tagged snapshots, not old immutable tags.
239	
240	When an experiment becomes a maintained project, first inventory and verify a
241	recoverable original. Build and validate filtered history in a separate copy,
242	retain commit mappings, and separately coordinate remote replacement, tags,
243	releases and other clones/worktrees. A bundle covers selected Git objects/refs,
244	not automatically dirty files, LFS objects or submodule repositories.
245	
246	Sync, version control and backup are separate. A synchronized deletion is still
247	a deletion. Restoring a Markdown export is not restoring the native agent state.
248	Confirmed leaked credentials require revocation or rotation; filtering Git does
249	not revoke them or remove copies held by other people and services.
250	
251	See `dev help hygiene` for scanning and reviewed redaction, `dev help retirement`
252	for post-writer handoffs, `dev help repositories` for setup, and `dev help storage`
253	for durable data versus caches.
254

# Amend blocker、post-session 收尾補強與 dashboard UX

## Context

v0.2.39 的實作、發布及 dev-cli 本機 branch/worktree/task 清理已完成；本計畫取代先前已結束的 release 計畫。

本次需求：
1. 只讀查明 main 上將 `.specstory/history/2026-09-17_04-44-06Z-git-commit-amend-no.md` amend 到 `Backup chat history` 被何者阻擋，區分真實 hook failure、writer 生命週期與已發布歷史問題。
2. 修正先前 agent-skills 收尾發現的 co-commit、精確 transcript alias／sync freshness、synthetic fixture review、cloud sync 設定傳遞缺口。
3. REPOS 啟動後按 `n` 不應在尚可安全輸入時被全域 repository refresh 擋住。
4. `/` filter 輸入中讓上下鍵選取 item，保留各畫面必要的 Enter 確認／執行／遠端查詢語意。

## 保留界線

- 計畫階段不 amend、commit、stage、sync、redact、修改設定、啟動／退出 agent，亦不執行會建立私有報告的 scan。
- 不輸出 raw credentials／完整 transcript／private review 值；只讀既有報告並回報規則、數量與安全位置。
- dev-cli 目前 session 的 live transcript 不當成 quiescent；不因 bytes 穩定或 runtime idle 宣稱 writer 已停止。
- agent-skills 的 `rotation_required` prepared index、journal、草稿及私有備份保持原樣；不偽造 rotation、runner token 或 lifecycle proof。
- 既有 remote branches、tags 不動，不從這次修正推定 push／PR／release 授權。

## 調查中

- Amend：有效 hook chain、確切 staged bytes／UTF-8、既有 hygiene receipt、HEAD 與 cached upstream 的可达性。
- TUI：REPOS `n` 的實際 action/freshness guard、filter input routing、可重用 selection 與 query helpers/tests。
- 收尾：dev 原生 artifact／agenthistory／hygiene API 與 agent-skills canonical wrapper/finalizer 的權責、可重用 guard/review/receipt，以及現有 prepared run 的安全恢復可能性。

## 建議方向（待程式碼核對後細化）

- 先報告已證實的 amend blocker；只為可證明的 fixture／誤判建立窄化處理，不關閉掃描或寬鬆放行整份 transcript。
- 明確區分產品先提交的既有 artifact lane 與 repo 選擇的 co-commit lane，避免把已有 index 或外部 helper state 偷渡成授權。
- alias selection 綁定 exact provider/session/path；sync identity 與 freshness 分開證明。
- 將真實 credential rotation 與已審閱 noncredential fixture 分開，保留 exact source／prepared tree／policy／approval guards。
- REPOS 可立即開啟不具副作用的輸入表單，最後 mutation 仍重驗所需 fresh authority。
- filter 中上下鍵只移動當前結果；`j/k` 等可列印字元繼續是搜尋文字，Enter 不改成隱式執行選中項目。

## 驗證（待定位測試檔）

21		// never be finalized — its transcript is gone, or its HEAD no longer

62	)
63	
64	func (i Intent) Validate() error {
65		if i.Destination != "" && i.Destination != "archive" {
66			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported artifact destination")
67		}
68		if i.Destination == "archive" && (i.ArchiveStateDir == "" || i.ArchivePolicy == "") {
69			return fmt.Errorf("archive intent lacks policy/state binding")
70		}
71		switch {
72		case i.SchemaVersion != SchemaVersion:
73			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported artifact intent schema %d", i.SchemaVersion)
74		case !idPattern.MatchString(i.ID):
75			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact intent id %q", i.ID)
76		case i.RunID == "" || !idPattern.MatchString(i.RunID):
77			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact run id %q", i.RunID)
78		case i.Provider == "" || i.SessionID == "":
79			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs provider and session id")
80		case i.RepoPath == "" || i.WorktreePath == "" || i.GitCommonDir == "":
81			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs repository, worktree and git common-dir paths")
82		case i.Branch == "" || i.Head == "":
83			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs branch and head")
84		}
85		if !sessionPattern.MatchString(i.Provider + ":" + i.SessionID) {
86			return fmt.Errorf("invalid agent session %q", i.Provider+":"+i.SessionID)
87		}
88		switch i.Status {
89		case Armed, Finalizing, Finalized, Failed, Discarded:
90			return nil
91		default:
92			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact intent status %q", i.Status)
93		}
94	}
95	
96	func ParseSession(value string) (provider, sessionID string, err error) {
97		provider, sessionID, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(value), ":")
98		provider = strings.ToLower(provider)
99		if !ok || !sessionPattern.MatchString(provider+":"+sessionID) {
100			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("invalid session %q: want provider:uuid", value)
101		}
102		return provider, sessionID, nil
103	}
104

91	func (i ReadinessInspection) Ready() bool {

159			inspection.ObservationError = err

164		unmatched := make([]Intent, 0, len(intents))

261	func inspectIntentReadiness(ctx context.Context, checkout string, intent Intent) (IntentReadiness, error) {
262		evidence := IntentReadiness{Intent: intent, Finalized: intent.Status == Finalized}
263		var err error
264		switch intent.Status {
265		case Armed, Finalizing:
266			evidence.State = ReadinessPending
267		case Failed:
268			evidence.State = ReadinessFailed
269		case Discarded:
270			evidence.State = ReadinessDiscarded
271		case Finalized:
272			evidence.ReceiptReachable, err = receiptRemainsReachable(ctx, checkout, intent)
273			switch {
274			case err != nil:
275				err = fmt.Errorf("inspect artifact intent %s receipt: %w", intent.ID, err)
276				evidence.State = ReadinessObservationError
277				evidence.ObservationError = err
278			case evidence.ReceiptReachable:
279				evidence.State = ReadinessFinalizedReachable
280			default:
281				evidence.State = ReadinessFinalizedUnreachable
282			}
283		default:
284			// Store.List validates statuses, but fail closed if another Store
285			// implementation is introduced without preserving that contract.
286			err = fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s has unrecognized status %q", intent.ID, intent.Status)
287			evidence.State = ReadinessObservationError
288			evidence.ObservationError = err
289		}
290		return evidence, err
291	}

293	func receiptRemainsReachable(ctx context.Context, checkout string, intent Intent) (bool, error) {
294		if intent.Destination == "archive" {
295			h, e := agenthistory.Open(ctx, agenthistory.Options{Root: checkout, StateDir: intent.ArchiveStateDir})
296			if e != nil {
297				return false, e
298			}
299			commit, e := h.VerifyArchiveReceipt(ctx, intent.ArchivePlanID)
300			return e == nil && commit == intent.ArchiveCommit, e
301		}
302		if intent.ArtifactCommit == "" {
303			return false, nil
304		}
305		candidates := []struct {
306			dir string
307			ref string
308		}{
309			{checkout, "HEAD"},
310			{intent.RepoPath, intent.Branch},
311			{intent.RepoPath, intent.Base},
312		}
313		seen := make(map[string]bool, len(candidates))
314		var observationErr error
315		for _, candidate := range candidates {
316			if candidate.dir == "" || candidate.ref == "" {
317				continue
318			}
319			key := candidate.dir + "\x00" + candidate.ref
320			if seen[key] {
321				continue
322			}
323			seen[key] = true
324			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
325				return false, joinReadinessError(observationErr, err)
326			}
327			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, candidate.dir, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref); err == nil {
328				return true, nil
329			} else if !gitNotAncestor(err) {
330				observationErr = joinReadinessError(observationErr,
331					fmt.Errorf("check %s against %s in %s: %w", intent.ArtifactCommit, candidate.ref, candidate.dir, err))
332			}
333		}
334		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
335			observationErr = joinReadinessError(observationErr, err)
336		}
337		return false, observationErr
338	}
339	
340	func gitNotAncestor(err error) bool {
341		var exitErr *exec.ExitError
342		return errors.As(err, &exitErr) && exitErr.ExitCode() == 1
343	}
344	
345	func joinReadinessError(current, next error) error {
346		if current == nil {
347			return next
348		}
349		if next == nil {
350			return current
351		}
352		return errors.Join(current, next)
353	}

497	func revalidatePreparedIntent(ctx context.Context, intent *Intent) error {
498		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, intent.WorktreePath)
499		if err != nil {
500			return fmt.Errorf("revalidate artifact checkout before arming intent: %w", err)
501		}
502		checkout, err := pathx.Canonical(repository.Root)
503		if err != nil {
504			return fmt.Errorf("canonicalize revalidated artifact checkout: %w", err)
505		}
506		expectedCheckout, err := pathx.Canonical(intent.WorktreePath)
507		if err != nil {
508			return fmt.Errorf("canonicalize prepared artifact checkout: %w", err)
509		}
510		commonDir, err := pathx.Canonical(repository.GitCommonDir)
511		if err != nil {
512			return fmt.Errorf("canonicalize revalidated artifact Git common directory: %w", err)
513		}
514		expectedCommon, err := pathx.Canonical(intent.GitCommonDir)
515		if err != nil {
516			return fmt.Errorf("canonicalize prepared artifact Git common directory: %w", err)
517		}
518		if checkout != expectedCheckout || commonDir != expectedCommon {
519			return fmt.Errorf("artifact checkout identity changed before intent creation")
520		}
521		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, checkout)
522		if err != nil {
523			return fmt.Errorf("revalidate artifact checkout status: %w", err)
524		}
525		if status.Detached || status.Branch != intent.Branch {
526			return fmt.Errorf("artifact checkout branch changed from %s to %s before intent creation", intent.Branch, status.Branch)
527		}
528		if operation, active, err := gitx.InProgress(checkout); err != nil {
529			return fmt.Errorf("revalidate artifact Git operation: %w", err)
530		} else if active {
531			return fmt.Errorf("artifact preparation refuses Git operation %s that started before intent creation", operation)
532		}
533		head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, checkout, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
534		if err != nil {
535			return fmt.Errorf("revalidate artifact checkout HEAD: %w", err)
536		}
537		if strings.TrimSpace(head) != strings.TrimSpace(intent.Head) {
538			return fmt.Errorf("artifact checkout HEAD changed before intent creation")
539		}
540		return nil
541	}

543	func (s *Service) ObserveSessionEnd(ctx context.Context, runID string, when time.Time) error {
544		intent, err := s.Store.FindByRunID(runID)
545		if err != nil {
546			return nil // SessionEnd without an armed intent is deliberately a no-op.
547		}
548		if when.IsZero() {
549			when = time.Now()
550		}
551		return s.Store.Update(ctx, intent.ID, func(candidate *Intent) error {
552			candidate.SessionEndedAt = when.UTC().Truncate(time.Second)
553			return nil
554		})

575		return finalized, err
576	}

578	func (s *Service) finalizeLocked(ctx context.Context, request FinalizeRequest, intent *Intent) (*Intent, error) {
579		if intent.Destination == "archive" {
580			return s.finalizeArchive(ctx, request, intent)
581		}
582		if intent.Status == Finalized {
583			if commit, ok := findReceipt(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, intent.ID); ok && commit != intent.ArtifactCommit {
584				if err := s.markFinalized(ctx, intent.ID, intent.TranscriptPath, commit); err != nil {
585					return nil, err
586				}
587				return s.Store.Get(intent.ID)
588			}
589			return intent, nil
590		}
591		if commit, ok := findReceipt(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, intent.ID); ok {
592			if err := s.markFinalized(ctx, intent.ID, intent.TranscriptPath, commit); err != nil {
593				return nil, err
594			}
595			return s.Store.Get(intent.ID)
596		}
597		if s.ScanStaged == nil {
598			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "scanner-missing", fmt.Errorf("artifact finalization requires a staged secret scanner"))
599		}
600		if err := s.revalidate(ctx, intent); err != nil {
601			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "git-drift", err)
602		}
603		if intent.SessionEndedAt.IsZero() && !request.WriterStopped {
604			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "writer-unproven",
605				fmt.Errorf("finalization requires SessionEnd observation or explicit post-writer proof"))
606		}
607		transcript, err := FindTranscript(intent.WorktreePath, intent.Provider, intent.SessionID)
608		if err != nil {
609			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "transcript-missing", err)
610		}
611		if err := s.Store.Update(ctx, intent.ID, func(candidate *Intent) error {
612			candidate.Status = Finalizing
613			candidate.TranscriptPath = transcript.Path
614			candidate.FailureCode = ""
615			return nil
616		}); err != nil {
617			return nil, err
618		}
619		if _, err := StableSnapshot(ctx, transcript.Path, request.Settle); err != nil {
620			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "writer-active", err)
621		}
622		paths := append([]string{transcript.Path}, intent.PlanPaths...)
623		if err := ensureOnlyAllowedIndex(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, nil); err != nil {
624			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "index-not-empty", err)
625		}
626		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, append([]string{"add", "--"}, paths...)...); err != nil {
627			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "stage-failed", err)
628		}
629		cleanup := func() {
630			_, _ = gitx.Run(context.Background(), intent.WorktreePath, append([]string{"reset", "--"}, paths...)...)
631		}
632		if err := s.ScanStaged(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, paths); err != nil {
633			cleanup()
634			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "scan-failed", err)
635		}
636		if _, err := StableSnapshot(ctx, transcript.Path, request.Settle); err != nil {
637			cleanup()
638			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "writer-active", err)
639		}
640		if err := ensureOnlyAllowedIndex(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, paths); err != nil {
641			cleanup()
642			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "index-drift", err)
643		}
644		if err := stagedFilesMatch(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, paths); err != nil {
645			cleanup()
646			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "index-drift", err)
647		}
648		message := fmt.Sprintf("chore: finalize %s agent session", intent.Provider)
649		trailers := fmt.Sprintf("Agent-Artifact-Session: %s:%s\nDev-Artifact-Intent: %s", intent.Provider, intent.SessionID, intent.ID)
650		if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, "commit", "-m", message, "-m", trailers); err != nil {
651			cleanup()
652			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "commit-failed", err)
653		}
654		commit, err := gitx.Run(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
655		if err != nil {
656			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent.ID, "receipt-failed", err)
657		}
658		if err := s.markFinalized(ctx, intent.ID, transcript.Path, commit); err != nil {
659			return nil, err
660		}
661		return s.Store.Get(intent.ID)
662	}

664	func (s *Service) resolveIntent(request FinalizeRequest) (*Intent, error) {
665		if request.IntentID != "" {
666			return s.Store.Get(request.IntentID)
667		}

674	func (s *Service) revalidate(ctx context.Context, intent *Intent) error {
675		repository, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, intent.WorktreePath)
676		if err != nil {
677			return err
678		}
679		if repository.GitCommonDir != intent.GitCommonDir {
680			return fmt.Errorf("Git common-dir changed")
681		}
682		status, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, intent.WorktreePath)
683		if err != nil {
684			return err
685		}
686		if status.Branch != intent.Branch || status.Detached {
687			return fmt.Errorf("branch changed from %s to %s", intent.Branch, status.Branch)
688		}
689		if operation, active, err := gitx.InProgress(intent.WorktreePath); err != nil {
690			return err
691		} else if active {
692			return fmt.Errorf("Git operation %s is in progress", operation)
693		}
694		head, err := gitx.Run(ctx, intent.WorktreePath, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
695		if err != nil {
696			return err
697		}
698		if head != intent.Head {
699			return fmt.Errorf("HEAD changed from %s to %s", intent.Head, head)
700		}
701		return nil
702	}

704	func (s *Service) fail(ctx context.Context, id, code string, cause error) error {

706			intent.Status = Failed
707			intent.FailureCode = code
708			return nil
709		})
710		return fmt.Errorf("artifact finalization %s: %w", code, cause)
711	}
