40	func supportedScannerVersion(value string) bool {
41		parts := regexp.MustCompile(`^v?(8)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)$`).FindStringSubmatch(strings.TrimSpace(value))
42		if len(parts) != 4 {
43			return false
44		}
45		minor, err := strconv.Atoi(parts[2])
46		return err == nil && minor >= 30
47	}
48	
49	func supportedScannerBuild(info *debug.BuildInfo) bool {
50		if info == nil || info.Main.Replace != nil {
51			return false
52		}
53		if info.Main.Path != "github.com/zricethezav/gitleaks/v8" && info.Main.Path != "github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/v8" {
54			return false
55		}
56		return supportedScannerVersion(info.Main.Version)
57	}
58	
59	// CheckVersion rejects versions that can silently ignore scoped allowlists.
60	// This explicit execution is used by setup/scan, not passive status/inventory.
61	func (g Gitleaks) CheckVersion(ctx context.Context) error {
62		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
63		defer cancel()
64		name := g.Binary
65		if name == "" {
66			name = "gitleaks"
67		}
68		r, err := (sshhost.ExecRunner{}).Run(ctx, sshhost.RunRequest{Name: name, Args: []string{"version"}, UnsetEnv: gitEnvironmentNames(), Display: "hygiene scanner version"})
69		if err != nil || r.ExitCode != 0 || r.StdoutTruncated {
70			return errors.New("gitleaks 8.30.0 or newer compatible 8.x is required; check the installed scanner")
71		}
72		if supportedScannerVersion(string(r.Stdout)) {
73			return nil
74		}
75		// go install preserves the module version even when upstream's ldflag-only
76		// version string is empty/development. Do not accept unknown/replaced modules.
77		if path, err := exec.LookPath(name); err == nil {
78			if stat, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil && stat.Mode().IsRegular() && stat.Size() <= 256<<20 {
79				if info, err := buildinfo.ReadFile(path); err == nil && supportedScannerBuild(info) {
80					return nil
81				}
82			}
83		}
84		return errors.New("gitleaks 8.30.0 or newer compatible 8.x is required; check the installed scanner")
85	}
86	
87	func (g Gitleaks) Scan(ctx context.Context, q EngineRequest) ([]Detection, error) {
88		if err := g.CheckVersion(ctx); err != nil {
89			return nil, err
90		}
91		configPath := filepath.Join(q.PrivateDir, "engine.toml")
92		reportPath := filepath.Join(q.PrivateDir, "engine.json")
93		ignorePath := filepath.Join(q.PrivateDir, "ignore")
94		for p, b := range map[string][]byte{configPath: q.Config, ignorePath: q.Ignore} {
95			if err := os.WriteFile(p, b, 0o600); err != nil {
96				return nil, errors.New("cannot prepare private scanner input")
97			}
98		}
99		args := []string{"git", q.Root, "--config", configPath, "--gitleaks-ignore-path", ignorePath, "--report-format=json", "--report-path", reportPath, "--exit-code=10", "--no-banner", "--no-color", "--redact=100"}
100		if q.Audit {
101			args = append(args, "--ignore-gitleaks-allow")
102		}
103		if q.History {
104			args = append(args, "--log-opts=--full-history --diff-merges=first-parent --no-ext-diff --no-textconv "+strings.Join(q.Refs, " "))
105		} else {
106			args = append(args, "--staged")
107		}
108		// Machine output must retain secret bytes for exact-span plans. It is never
109		// forwarded to stdout/stderr and lives only in this private, removed directory.
110		args = append(args, "--redact=0")
111		name := g.Binary
112		if name == "" {
113			name = "gitleaks"
114		}
115		r, err := (sshhost.ExecRunner{}).Run(ctx, sshhost.RunRequest{Name: name, Args: args, UnsetEnv: gitEnvironmentNames(), Env: []string{"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1", "GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.longpaths", "GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=true", "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1", "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=" + os.DevNull, "GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=" + os.DevNull, "GIT_PAGER=cat", "GITLEAKS_CONFIG=", "GITLEAKS_CONFIG_TOML="}, Display: "hygiene scanner"})
116		if err != nil {
117			return nil, errors.New("gitleaks unavailable, canceled or failed to launch")
118		}
119		if r.ExitCode != 0 && r.ExitCode != 10 {
120			return nil, errors.New("gitleaks scan failed (exit " + strconv.Itoa(r.ExitCode) + "); result is incomplete")
121		}
122		b, err := safefile.ReadStablePath(ctx, reportPath, MaxRecordBytes)
123		if err != nil {
124			return nil, errors.New("gitleaks report missing or oversized")
125		}
126		var rows []Detection
127		if len(b) == 0 || json.Unmarshal(b, &rows) != nil {
128			return nil, errors.New("gitleaks report invalid; result is incomplete")
129		}
130		for _, d := range rows {
131			if d.RuleID == "" || d.File == "" || d.StartLine < 1 || d.Secret == "" {
132				return nil, errors.New("gitleaks finding is incomplete")
133			}
134		}
135		return rows, nil
136	}

41	// AcquireResult is a local checkout ready for scaffolding or handoff.
42	type AcquireResult struct {
43		Kind      AcquireKind `json:"kind"`
44		Name      string      `json:"name"`
45		Path      string      `json:"path"`
46		CloneRef  string      `json:"clone_ref,omitempty"`

52	// Acquire creates a new main-branch repository or clones an existing one into
53	// an exact, previously absent destination. It refuses nested repositories: a
54	// caller that intentionally wants a submodule should use Git's submodule flow,
55	// where ownership and checkout semantics are explicit.
56	func Acquire(ctx context.Context, request AcquireRequest) (AcquireResult, error) {
57		var result AcquireResult
58		if err := (config.Submodules{Init: request.Submodules}).Validate(); err != nil {
59			return result, err
60		}
61		request.Name = strings.TrimSpace(request.Name)
62		request.CloneRef = strings.TrimSpace(request.CloneRef)
63		request.Destination = strings.TrimSpace(request.Destination)
64		if request.Destination == "" {
65			return result, errors.New("repository destination is required")
66		}
67		if request.Kind != AcquireNew && request.Kind != AcquireClone {
68			return result, fmt.Errorf("unknown repository acquisition kind %q", request.Kind)
69		}
70		if request.Kind == AcquireNew && request.Name == "" {
71			return result, errors.New("repository name is required")
72		}
73		if request.Kind == AcquireClone && request.CloneRef == "" {
74			return result, errors.New("clone reference is required")
75		}
76	
77		destination, err := pathx.Canonical(request.Destination)
78		if err != nil {
79			return result, fmt.Errorf("resolve repository destination: %w", err)
80		}
81		if _, err := os.Lstat(destination); err == nil {
82			return result, fmt.Errorf("%s already exists", destination)
83		} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
84			return result, fmt.Errorf("inspect repository destination: %w", err)
85		}
86		if err := rejectNestedRepository(ctx, filepath.Dir(destination)); err != nil {
87			return result, err
88		}
89		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(destination), 0o755); err != nil {
90			return result, fmt.Errorf("create repository parent: %w", err)
91		}
92	
93		result = AcquireResult{Kind: request.Kind, Name: request.Name, Path: destination}
94		switch request.Kind {
95		case AcquireNew:
96			if err := os.Mkdir(destination, 0o755); err != nil {
97				return result, fmt.Errorf("create repository directory: %w", err)
98			}
99			result.Created = true
100			branch := strings.TrimSpace(request.InitialBranch)
101			if branch == "" {
102				branch = "main"
103			}
104			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, destination, "init", "-b", branch); err != nil {
105				return result, fmt.Errorf("initialize repository: %w", err)
106			}
107			result.GitInited = true
108		case AcquireClone:
109			cloneRef := NormalizeCloneRef(request.CloneRef)
110			result.CloneRef = RedactCloneRef(cloneRef)
111			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, filepath.Dir(destination), "clone", cloneRef, destination); err != nil {
112				return result, fmt.Errorf("clone repository: %w", RedactCloneError(err, cloneRef, request.CloneRef))
113			}
114			result.Created, result.Cloned, result.GitInited = true, true, true
115			settings, settingsErr := submodule.Settings(request.Config, destination, request.Submodules)
116			if settingsErr != nil {
117				return result, fmt.Errorf("clone retained at %s: %w", destination, settingsErr)
118			}
119			if settings.Init == "recursive" {
120				if _, initErr := gitx.InitSubmodules(ctx, destination); initErr != nil {
121					return result, fmt.Errorf("clone retained at %s; submodules not ready: %w", destination, initErr)
122				}
123			}
124			if result.Name == "" {
125				result.Name = NameFromRef(RedactCloneRef(request.CloneRef))
126			}
127		}
128		return result, nil
129	}

131	func rejectNestedRepository(ctx context.Context, parent string) error {
132		probe := parent
133		for {
134			if _, err := os.Stat(probe); err == nil {
135				break
136			} else if !errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
137				return fmt.Errorf("inspect repository destination parent: %w", err)
138			}
139			next := filepath.Dir(probe)
140			if next == probe {
141				break
142			}
143			probe = next
144		}
145		if discovered, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, probe); err == nil && discovered.Root != "" {
146			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to create a nested repository inside %s", discovered.Root)
147		}
148		return nil
149	}
150	
151	// NormalizeCloneRef expands forge shorthand while leaving explicit URLs, SCP
152	// references and local paths unchanged.
153	func NormalizeCloneRef(ref string) string {
154		ref = strings.TrimSpace(ref)
155		if ref == "" {
156			return ref
157		}
158		if filepath.IsAbs(ref) {
159			return filepath.Clean(ref)
160		}
161		if ref == "~" || strings.HasPrefix(ref, "~/") {
162			return config.Expand(ref)
163		}
164		if strings.HasPrefix(ref, "./") || strings.HasPrefix(ref, "../") {
165			if absolute, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
166				return absolute
167			}
168		}
169		if strings.HasPrefix(ref, "file://") || (!strings.Contains(ref, "://") && strings.ContainsAny(ref, "@:")) {
170			return ref
171		}
172		if info, err := os.Stat(ref); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
173			if absolute, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
174				return absolute
175			}
176		}
177		if kind := forge.FromURL(ref); kind != forge.Unknown {
178			if adapter, err := forge.For(kind); err == nil {
179				return adapter.CloneURL(ref)
180			}
181			return ref
182		}
183		if !strings.Contains(ref, "://") && strings.Contains(ref, "/") {
184			if adapter, err := forge.Preferred(); err == nil {
185				return adapter.CloneURL(ref)
186			}
187		}
188		return ref
189	}
190	
191	// NameFromRef derives the checkout directory name from a clone reference.
192	func NameFromRef(ref string) string {
193		ref = strings.TrimSpace(ref)
194		ref = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSuffix(ref, "/"), ".git")
195		if index := strings.LastIndexAny(ref, "/:\\"); index >= 0 {
196			return ref[index+1:]
197		}
198		return ref
199	}

35					}

49			preserveFocus = true

51			focusModel.view = ViewRepos
52			focus, path = focusModel.currentToken(), focusModel.repoFocusPath()
53		}
54		next, command := m.update(msg)
55		model, ok := next.(Model)
56		if !ok || model.quitting {

61			model.fleetTree.searchQuery = model.filter
62			model.fleetTree.searchExpansions = nil
63		}

65			model.popupExpanded = false

22	`make test-skill` uses `SYSTEM_BASH ?= /bin/bash` and
23	`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, including the post-session lifecycle suite.
24	Shell suites print `BASH_VERSION` and fail on Darwin unless they are actually
25	running under Bash 3.x, so Homebrew Bash cannot make the compatibility claim
26	vacuous. The metadata regression additionally invokes its helper directly as
27	`PATH=/usr/bin:/bin /bin/bash` to exercise stock Bash 3.2 with a restricted
28	lookup path. The isolated Git config prevents host hooks from changing
29	throwaway commits.

34	
35	- `test_post_session_finalize.sh` exercises the public help/argument contracts,
36	  foreground runner process group, exact single sync, child/signal status
37	  preservation, inert queue boundary, strict per-worktree request/journal
38	  ownership, exact selectors, and stale branch/index rejection.
39	- It proves no sync, sanitation, draft, hook, or commit occurs before child exit
40	  0; the child receives only request path/run id and cannot obtain the parent
41	  finalizer token.
42	- Success runs one ordinary commit with pre-commit, prepare-commit-msg,
43	  commit-msg, and post-commit once in the original worktree, then proves exact
44	  feature/artifact paths and canonical provenance/request trailers.
45	- Recovery coverage includes missing parent authorization, cross-worktree and
46	  symlink refusal, foreign/edited draft preservation, hook failure with retained
47	  prepared tree, uncertain `committing` reconciliation without retry, active
48	  writer refusal, rotation stop, and fresh
49	  `--allow-commit --rotation-confirmed` recovery without restaging.
50	- The rebase regression proves a stale `REBASE_HEAD` file alone is accepted,
51	  while real operation markers (for example `MERGE_HEAD`; implementation also
52	  checks `rebase-merge` / `rebase-apply`) block finalization.
53	- Output assertions capture status JSON/stdout and stderr separately, then use
54	  exact values or scoped matches. Test labels, fixture inputs, and expected
55	  diagnostic text are never searched as subject output, preventing false
56	  positives in leakage and absence checks.
57	- Those assertions ensure private hook/scanner diagnostics, unsafe selectors,
58	  transcript data, and credential bytes do not leak through status JSON/stderr.

21	See [startup repository and discovery](tui-repos-bootstrap.md#startup-repository-and-discovery-v0224).
22	
23	Ctrl+O and Help share a floating popup with clickable **Expand**, **Close** and
24	a draggable scrollbar. The normal maximum is 104 columns × 32 rows; below 80
25	columns or 22 rows it fills the screen. `/` filters the current action menu;
26	arrows choose and Enter continues. Esc stops typing or clears the query before
27	closing, and `q` closes outside input. Clicking outside closes without passing
28	the click to the dashboard. Existing action eligibility and confirmations apply.
29	
30	Press `?` or click footer **Help** for the current view's **Keys**, then **Guide**
31	for colors, symbols and captured selected-row details, or **Manual** for all
32	embedded `dev help` topics. `1–3`, `v`, `/`, `j/k` and `f` navigate tabs, scope,
33	search, entries and expansion. Search, scope, Back and article pan controls are
34	also clickable. Help reads existing observations and embedded documents without
35	executing actions or probing tools. See [contextual Help](tui-repos-bootstrap.md#contextual-help-v0224)
36	for search scope, article navigation and the layered Esc behavior.
37	
38	TASKS finish, resume, retirement and recovery use the existing CLI workflows.
39	The dashboard suspends during their prompts and refreshes when they finish,
40	including after an error. Task ID/revision checks prevent using a stale selection.
41	`dev sweep --task <id>` reports only the selected task; add `--apply` to confirm
42	its eligible suggestions. Other worktree-wide sweep modes cannot be combined
43	with `--task`.
44	
45	Finishing through PR preserves HOT/WARM intent. Integration records DONE;
46	retirement separately removes eligible execution state and keeps the branch by
47	default. These actions retain the existing taskflow safety rules.
48	
49	## Start and open work
50	
51	REPOS Enter opens the selected repository without creating a task. `s` and `d`
52	open the full start wizard with worktree or direct preselected. The wizard asks
53	for the task and necessary branch/base/next action, then offers open (default)
54	or stay before final creation confirmation. A base is explicit in the reviewed
55	plan, never inferred from an arbitrary checked-out branch.
56	
57	The dashboard releases its terminal before an attach, shell-directory handoff,
58	or external retirement coordinator runs. An ordinary completion/cancellation
59	returns to the dashboard. No agent is launched automatically.
60	
61	## Dispose of a Try
62	
63	```bash
64	dev tries delete <ref> --dry-run
65	dev tries delete <ref>
66	dev tries delete <id> --permanent --confirm-delete <id>
67	```
```

554	// Update is the Bubble Tea update loop.
555	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (Model, tea.Cmd) {
556		if !m.focus {
557			return m, nil
558		}
559	
560		// Need to check for completion before, because key is configurable and might be double assigned
561		keyMsg, ok := msg.(tea.KeyMsg)
562		if ok && key.Matches(keyMsg, m.KeyMap.AcceptSuggestion) {
563			if m.canAcceptSuggestion() {
564				m.value = append(m.value, m.matchedSuggestions[m.currentSuggestionIndex][len(m.value):]...)
565				m.CursorEnd()
566			}
567		}
568	
569		// Let's remember where the position of the cursor currently is so that if
570		// the cursor position changes, we can reset the blink.
571		oldPos := m.pos
572	
573		switch msg := msg.(type) {
574		case tea.KeyMsg:
575			switch {
576			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.DeleteWordBackward):
577				m.deleteWordBackward()
578			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.DeleteCharacterBackward):
579				m.Err = nil
580				if len(m.value) > 0 {
581					m.value = append(m.value[:max(0, m.pos-1)], m.value[m.pos:]...)
582					m.Err = m.validate(m.value)
583					if m.pos > 0 {
584						m.SetCursor(m.pos - 1)
585					}
586				}
587			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.WordBackward):
588				m.wordBackward()
589			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.CharacterBackward):
590				if m.pos > 0 {
591					m.SetCursor(m.pos - 1)
592				}
593			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.WordForward):
594				m.wordForward()
595			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.CharacterForward):
596				if m.pos < len(m.value) {
597					m.SetCursor(m.pos + 1)
598				}
599			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.LineStart):
600				m.CursorStart()
601			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.DeleteCharacterForward):
602				if len(m.value) > 0 && m.pos < len(m.value) {
603					m.value = append(m.value[:m.pos], m.value[m.pos+1:]...)
604					m.Err = m.validate(m.value)
605				}
606			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.LineEnd):
607				m.CursorEnd()
608			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.DeleteAfterCursor):
609				m.deleteAfterCursor()
610			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.DeleteBeforeCursor):
611				m.deleteBeforeCursor()
612			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.Paste):
613				return m, Paste
614			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.DeleteWordForward):
615				m.deleteWordForward()
616			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.NextSuggestion):
617				m.nextSuggestion()
618			case key.Matches(msg, m.KeyMap.PrevSuggestion):
619				m.previousSuggestion()
620			default:
621				// Input one or more regular characters.
622				m.insertRunesFromUserInput(msg.Runes)
623			}
624	
625			// Check again if can be completed
626			// because value might be something that does not match the completion prefix
627			m.updateSuggestions()
628	
629		case pasteMsg:
630			m.insertRunesFromUserInput([]rune(msg))
631	
632		case pasteErrMsg:
633			m.Err = msg
634		}
635	
636		var cmds []tea.Cmd
637		var cmd tea.Cmd
638	
639		m.Cursor, cmd = m.Cursor.Update(msg)
640		cmds = append(cmds, cmd)
641	
642		if oldPos != m.pos && m.Cursor.Mode() == cursor.CursorBlink {
643			m.Cursor.Blink = false
644			cmds = append(cmds, m.Cursor.BlinkCmd())
645		}
646	
647		m.handleOverflow()
648		return m, tea.Batch(cmds...)
649	}

651	// View renders the textinput in its current state.
652	func (m Model) View() string {
653		// Placeholder text
654		if len(m.value) == 0 && m.Placeholder != "" {
655			return m.placeholderView()
656		}
657	
658		styleText := m.TextStyle.Inline(true).Render
659	
660		value := m.value[m.offset:m.offsetRight]
661		pos := max(0, m.pos-m.offset)
662		v := styleText(m.echoTransform(string(value[:pos])))
663	
664		if pos < len(value) { //nolint:nestif
665			char := m.echoTransform(string(value[pos]))
666			m.Cursor.SetChar(char)
667			v += m.Cursor.View()                                   // cursor and text under it
668			v += styleText(m.echoTransform(string(value[pos+1:]))) // text after cursor
669			v += m.completionView(0)                               // suggested completion
670		} else {
671			if m.focus && m.canAcceptSuggestion() {
672				suggestion := m.matchedSuggestions[m.currentSuggestionIndex]
673				if len(value) < len(suggestion) {
674					m.Cursor.TextStyle = m.CompletionStyle
675					m.Cursor.SetChar(m.echoTransform(string(suggestion[pos])))
676					v += m.Cursor.View()
677					v += m.completionView(1)
678				} else {
679					m.Cursor.SetChar(" ")
680					v += m.Cursor.View()
681				}
682			} else {
683				m.Cursor.SetChar(" ")
684				v += m.Cursor.View()
685			}
686		}
687	
688		// If a max width and background color were set fill the empty spaces with
689		// the background color.
690		valWidth := uniseg.StringWidth(string(value))
691		if m.Width > 0 && valWidth <= m.Width {
692			padding := max(0, m.Width-valWidth)
693			if valWidth+padding <= m.Width && pos < len(value) {
694				padding++
695			}
696			v += styleText(strings.Repeat(" ", padding))
697		}
```

7	## Eight views
8	
9	Switch with `tab`, `l`/`h`, right/left, or by left-clicking a visible tab:
10	
11	| View | Answers | Data source |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| TASKS | What am I working on? | task registry + live Git/runtime state |
14	| REPOS | What durable repositories exist here? | configured scan roots + asset catalog |
15	| FLEET | What exists and is active on my other machines? | remote `dev` snapshots over SSH |
16	| TRY | Which experiments can I resume, archive or graduate? | experiment catalog + live Git/runtime state |
17	| REMOTE | What can I open or clone? | authenticated forge CLI inventories |
18	| SKILLS | Which skills would an agent launched from this context read? | context-first targets plus an `A` all-repositories toggle |
19	| MCP | Which MCP declarations would that agent context expose? | sanitized static agent configuration with the same shared scope |
20	| SSH | How do I connect to a machine? | local aliases, canonical registry, cached discovery and provider membership |

23	lookup, cache decoding, shell tool probes or the optional release refresh can

25	load cycle; REMOTE, SKILLS, MCP and SSH remain lazy; FLEET warms hosts after a delay. Each view
26	has its own generation: `r` supersedes the old read, late results are ignored,
27	failed refreshes keep usable rows, and a successful empty result clears old
28	rows. Warning-only SKILLS/MCP diagnostics remain fresh partial snapshots instead
29	of causing revisit loops; a visible dependent view automatically resumes after
30	REPOS recovers. Cached rows and current live results are separate readiness
31	stages; there is no all-tabs-ready state for views that may never be opened.

34	visible row or tab; clicking the selected row opens its action menu, including
35	keyboard/startup selections and without double-click timing. The wheel moves three
36	rows, and right-click selects a row then opens its menu. Releases, motion and
37	modified row clicks do not activate rows. Opening a menu executes no option; Enter/`o` opens
38	the row. Depending on the terminal, hold Shift/Option for native text selection.
39

41	keeping the configured order and scrolling it into view. Subdirectories, aliases

491	func verifyCommitPaths(ctx context.Context, root, parent, commit string, expected map[string]string) error {
492		args := []string{"diff-tree", "--root", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", "-z"}
493		if parent != "unborn" {
494			args = append(args, parent)
495		}
496		args = append(args, commit)
497		changed, e := runGit(ctx, root, nil, 8<<20, args...)
498		if e != nil {
499			return e
500		}
501		for _, path := range strings.Split(string(changed), "\x00") {
502			if path != "" && expected[path] == "" {
503				return errors.New("archive hook changed an unrelated path; inspect the partial receipt")
504			}
505		}
506		for path, want := range expected {

508			if e != nil || got != want {

510			}

517		}
518		return nil
519	}

530			return errors.New("archive commit is no longer reachable")
531		}
532		for _, item := range p.Snapshots {

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Run one foreground SpecStory/Claude session, then finalize only after exit 0.
3	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
4	
5	set -euo pipefail
6	
7	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd -P)"
8	HELPER="$SCRIPT_DIR/_post_session.py"
9	
10	usage() {
11	  cat <<'EOF'
12	Usage: run-specstory-session.sh [--allow-commit] claude [-- SPECSTORY_OPTIONS...]
13	       run-specstory-session.sh --provider claude [--allow-commit] [-- SPECSTORY_OPTIONS...]
14	
15	Run `specstory run claude` synchronously on the foreground TTY. The child gets
16	only AGENT_HISTORY_REQUEST_PATH and AGENT_HISTORY_RUN_ID as lifecycle context.
17	An agent may queue one inert request; it cannot authorize or run the finalizer.
18	
19	Required:
20	  claude                Explicit provider position (recommended).
21	  --provider claude     Equivalent flag form. Version 1 supports Claude only.
22	
23	Options:
24	  --allow-commit        Parent authorization for one automatic finalizer call,
25	                        only after the SpecStory child exits normally with 0,
26	                        its process group is empty, one exact quiet sync succeeds,
27	                        and a request exists.
28	  --                    Pass every remaining argument to `specstory run claude`.
29	  --help, -h            Show this help and exit.
30	
31	Noninteractive examples:
32	  run-specstory-session.sh claude -- --resume SESSION_UUID
33	  run-specstory-session.sh --allow-commit claude -- --no-cloud-sync
34	
35	Without --allow-commit, a successful queued run is synced and retained, and
36	exits 0 with status=authorization_required. The run succeeded; only the commit
37	is outstanding. Read `status`, not just the exit code, before treating history
38	as committed. Finish explicitly with `finalize-agent-commit.sh --allow-commit`.
39	
40	Exit codes:
41	  0       child succeeded: no request was queued, finalization completed, or a
42	          queued request awaits explicit finalization (status=authorization_required)
43	  1-255   nonzero child status is preserved exactly
44	  2       invalid runner arguments
45	  3       required command missing
46	  10      sanitation changed content; rotate, then recover explicitly
47	  11      ordinary commit failed; prepared snapshot and drafts retained
48	  21      exact SpecStory sync failed; request retained
49	  22      child process group remained live; request retained, no sync/finalizer
50	  23      lifecycle proof could not be persisted
51	  128+N   child terminated by signal N; request retained, no finalizer
52	EOF
53	}
54	
55	die() { printf 'error: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit "${2:-2}"; }
56	
57	PROVIDER=""
58	PROVIDER_SET=0
59	ALLOW_COMMIT=0
60	SPECSTORY_ARGS=()
61	
62	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do

64	    --provider)

66	      shift
67	      [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ -n "$1" ] || die "--provider requires claude"

72	      [ -n "$PROVIDER" ] || die "--provider requires claude"
73	      shift ;;
74	    --allow-commit)

78	    --)
79	      shift

85	      PROVIDER=claude; PROVIDER_SET=1; shift ;;
86	    *) die "unsupported positional provider (expected claude; try --help)" ;;

130	func keyedID(key []byte, parts ...string) string {
131		h := hmac.New(sha256.New, key)
132		for _, p := range parts {
133			h.Write([]byte(p))
134			h.Write([]byte{0})

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env sh
2	# Global git-lfs post-commit hook — managed by chezmoi (do not edit directly).
3	#
4	# Differs from the stock `git lfs install` hook in two deliberate ways, because
5	# core.hooksPath is GLOBAL (set in ~/.gitconfig so the managed pre-commit hook
6	# covers every repo) — so this runs for EVERY clone/checkout, including the ones
7	# `brew tap` performs in Homebrew's stripped superenv PATH where /usr/local/bin
8	# (and thus git-lfs) is invisible:
9	#   1. Augment PATH with the Homebrew prefixes + ~/.local/bin so git-lfs is found
10	#      even under a restricted PATH.
11	#   2. If git-lfs is still genuinely absent, exit 0 silently instead of `exit 2`
12	#      — a missing optional tool must never abort the host git operation.
13	# See pitfalls/git-lfs-global-hook-breaks-brew-tap.md
14	PATH="$PATH:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$HOME/.local/bin"; export PATH
15	command -v git-lfs >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
16	git lfs post-commit "$@"
17

507	func (s *Service) savePlan(ctx context.Context, p *planRecord) error {
508		var review bytes.Buffer
509		fmt.Fprintf(&review, "PRIVATE REVIEW: %s\nPlan: %s\nHook action: %s\nNever paste this file into chat, Git or CI logs. It may contain private values.\n", p.Plan.Kind, p.Plan.ID, p.Plan.HookAction)
510		for _, c := range p.Changes {
511			fmt.Fprintf(&review, "\n=== Proposed full content: %s ===\n", c.Path)
512			review.Write(c.Desired)
513			review.WriteByte('\n')
514		}
515		if review.Len() > MaxRecordBytes {
516			return errors.New("review exceeds byte limit; select fewer files")
517		}
518		p.Plan.ReviewFile = p.Plan.ID + ".review.txt"
519		p.ReviewDigest = keyedID(s.key, review.String())
520		if err := configedit.WritePrivate(ctx, filepath.Join(s.Dir, p.Plan.ReviewFile), review.Bytes(), false); err != nil {
521			return err
522		}
523		p.Plan.Revision = s.planRevision(*p)
524		return s.save(ctx, p.Plan.ID, *p)
525	}

530		if err := s.prepare(ctx); err != nil {
531			return "", err
532		}
533		var probe struct {
534			Report struct {
535				ID string `json:"id"`
536			}
537		}
538		if err := s.load(ctx, id, &probe); err != nil {
539			return "", err
540		}
541		if probe.Report.ID != "" {
542			return s.valuesReviewPath(ctx, id)
543		}
544		var p planRecord
545		if err := s.load(ctx, id, &p); err != nil {
546			return "", err
547		}
548		if p.Plan.ID != id || p.Plan.ReviewFile != id+".review.txt" || !hmac.Equal([]byte(p.Plan.Revision), []byte(s.planRevision(p))) {
549			return "", ErrStale
550		}
551		path := filepath.Join(s.Dir, p.Plan.ReviewFile)
552		body, err := safefile.ReadStablePath(ctx, path, MaxRecordBytes)
553		if err != nil || keyedID(s.key, string(body)) != p.ReviewDigest {
554			return "", ErrStale
555		}
556		return path, nil
557	}

# dev-cli

Git owns durable code; worktrees are local checkouts; runtimes are host-local
sessions; dev records task intent.

## Discover what you need

Use `dev <command> --help` for current syntax and flags, and `dev help <topic>`
for workflow explanations. `dev --help` lists commands; `dev help` lists topics.
Prefer supported `--json` output for automation. Read the relevant command before
mutation: some actions execute immediately, while others require preview/apply.
Do not preload manuals, repeat `dev --skill`, or run routine diagnostics.

## Preserve these boundaries

- Opening a repository needs no task. Choose direct, branch, or worktree
  deliberately; pass an explicit `--base` for branch/worktree creation. Keep
  managed worktrees outside repositories.
- `dev start` normally prepares a checkout/runtime. Agent launch is explicit.
  Parallel writers need coordinated ownership and verified launch targets.
- Completion, artifact finalization, retirement and branch deletion are separate.
  Finalize after writer exit; retire externally. Use `retire --base` when a fork
  point cannot prove integration. Runtime `done` is not cleanup-ready.
- Unknown or cached observations, merged PRs, and command refusals do not grant
  cleanup authority. Resolve the reported conditions; do not improvise force
  removal or bypass trust checks.

## Read a reference for advanced operations

- Worktree provisioning or cross-host lifecycle: [ownership](references/worktree-ownership.md), [lifecycle](references/task-lifecycle.md).
- Parallel agent launches or prompt transports: [agents](references/parallel-agents.md), [handoffs](references/prompt-handoffs.md).
- History retention: [artifacts](references/ai-artifacts.md).
- Agent completion or cleanup batches: [retirement](references/agent-retirement.md), [triage](references/local-triage.md).
- Repository hygiene batches, `report --json` summaries, scans or redaction: [hygiene](references/hygiene.md).
- Repository hooks, publication, or physical organization: [setup](references/repository-bootstrap.md), [bootstrap](references/bootstrap.md).
- SSH dashboard, diagnosis, discovery, tests/activity, keys, credentials and registration: [SSH](references/ssh-hosts.md).
- Dotfile setup, native chezmoi operations, or FLEET host actions: [dotfiles](references/dotfiles.md).
- Skill/MCP/instruction transfers, updates or removal: [transfers](references/agent-interop.md), [maintenance](references/skills-management.md).
- Recursive Git children: [submodules](references/submodules.md).

Use command help and its workflow topic for everyday operations.

## Unexpected dev failures

Read [feedback and repair](references/feedback-and-repair.md). Preserve the
original task; extra investigation, repair, subagents and publication need
explicit consent covering scope and cost.

# Agent history hygiene

Preserve selected agent evidence under the repository's chosen policy. Read
`dev help ai-artifacts` and `dev artifact status` when supported: source tracking,
external archive, protection and distribution are separate choices. Commit
reviewed project knowledge; do not force-add raw history under archive/unmanaged
policy. Verify repository protection from the effective hook chain.

## Prefer the shared dev workflow

When the installed dev supports `hygiene`, use its domain for setup, scans,
private rules and reviewed text changes:

```bash
dev hygiene status
dev hygiene setup --json
dev hygiene setup --apply --plan <id> --yes
dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
dev hygiene scan --scope history --audit --timeout 40m --json
```

`pre-commit` and `gitleaks` are needed for this repository hook recipe. An explicitly unscanned archive copy needs neither. A global `core.hooksPath` can be
correct, but its script may skip all checks when repository configs are absent.
The shared setup preserves existing hooks/comments and refuses an unverified
chain. Repository new/setup's `agent-history-hygiene` initializer uses this same
service. New default hooks block; they do not rewrite or stage files.

Per-repo secret/known/generic policy supports block/warn/off, with private local
overrides and exact reasoned exceptions. Private visibility is advice, never an
automatic exemption. SSH imports are static and reviewed: no DNS, login, Match
exec, private-key reads or rule-value export. Personal rules stay outside Git;
CI checks public rules and must state the missing personal coverage.

Read the bundled dev reference `references/hygiene.md` through `dev help hygiene`
or the public hygiene guide before rule changes or redaction. The CLI supports
all regular text, rather than treating transcripts as the only leak surface.

## Preserve the review trail

1. Identify the exact provider/session UUID from the transcript preamble. Never
   select another session just because its file is newest.
2. Commit product changes and reviewed plans. Follow the selected retention
   policy for raw history; do not broadly stage every agent directory.
3. Use `dev prepare --session provider:uuid` and finalization after its writer
   exits when that lifecycle applies. Byte stability alone is not writer proof.
4. Scan exact staged content. Partial staging must not accidentally stage
   unrelated working-copy edits.
5. In archive mode, raw history may be ignored but must be preserved before
   checkout disposal. In track mode, retain the existing exact-session workflow.
   Exclude conversation evidence from product source archives independently.

Do not close, restart or spawn agents to make hygiene checks pass without the
applicable authorization. A new agent without SpecStory does not stop an older
writer. Preserve the user's original task while offering additional cleanup.

## Reviewed redaction

```bash
dev hygiene redact --report <report-id> --file <reviewed-file> --json
# After reviewing, and after the exact artifact writer exited:
dev hygiene redact --apply --plan <plan-id> --yes --writer-stopped
```

Plans bind native file identity, contents, policy and checkout state. Stale,
modified or partial plans are not authority to overwrite current data. Keep
private recovery and rerun scans/tests after source or configuration changes.
The running transcript is left for a manual external trigger after its writer
stops. No automatic history rewrite, agent launch, commit, push or cleanup occurs.

## External archive workflow

`dev artifact setup` and `dev repo setup --artifacts` preview explicit per-repo
policy. `archive --session provider:uuid` or `--file` creates reviewed snapshots;
apply only after the exact recorder exits. Off/check/redact affect the copy,
not the live source or its index. A disabled scan is recorded as skipped.
Checked snapshots produce masked finding IDs for reasoned fixture exceptions.

Commit reviewed plans with product work before `dev prepare`. New archive intents
bind the destination and policy; redact finalization requires a reviewed
`--archive-plan`. Old tracked intents retain the compatibility scripts below.
Keep those installations while any tracked workflow still depends on them.

`artifact find` reads local committed archive records. Sync and original-backup
publication are explicit Git operations; they never transfer native session DBs.
`artifact migrate` can untrack after verified backup or build separate original,
history and filtered Git copies with commit maps. It never force-pushes source
refs. For historical exposure, use the remediation section rather than treating
path removal as a secret audit. Private raw recovery is not cache.

## Legacy scripts

The scripts remain explicit compatibility utilities. Prefer dev for new setup
and partial-staging-safe edits; a separately published remote redactor hook has
its own version and is not silently updated by dev.

- `find-session.sh --json`: locate candidate transcript/plan metadata.
- `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --dry-run`: inspect exact staging;
  without session-only it may include other dirty artifacts, so use cautiously.
- `scan-staged.sh`: masked JSON-lines locations only, never raw Match/Secret.
  Exit 0 means clean; 20 means candidate findings; legacy `--redact` selects
  exit 10 but only masks output, never modifies files. Exit 30 means missing
  gitleaks; 40 means scanner/JSON/required-parser failure; 2 means not in Git.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py --fix`: explicit legacy artifact mutation. Scanner
  failure is an error, not an empty result; console output uses full sentinels.
  This utility can restage, so use the reviewed dev flow for partial staging.
- `bootstrap-project.sh`: legacy installer; new default templates require dev
  hygiene. Its old `--migrate` targets the separately published remote redactor,
  not the new dev policy migration. Prefer `dev hygiene setup`.

SpecStory may already redact on write, but provider behavior/version is not proof
that every secret class or artifact directory is covered. Preserve existing
`[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` markers. An inert marker must never exempt another secret
on the same line. `.gitleaksignore` contains exact finding fingerprints, not
file/path globs. Portable pattern exceptions need a narrow rule/path/match scope.

Read [remediation](references/remediation.md). First distinguish fixtures,
examples and scanner candidates from confirmed credentials. Revoke/rotate a
confirmed exposed credential at its provider before considering Git history.

Shared main and immutable release tags stay unchanged in ordinary hygiene work.

clones, caches and distribution artifacts separately. A force push does not erase
all copies or revoke a credential. Personal names, Git author metadata and filenames
also need an explicit impact assessment; text replacement does not rewrite them.

Never echo matching bytes or raw process arguments into a chat to investigate a
finding. Use rule IDs, safe locations and private local reports. Keep raw reports,
recovery images and personal identity dictionaries outside Git and CI logs.

101	## Behavioral contracts
102	
103	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
104	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
105	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
106	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
107	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
108	- Submodule initialization uses committed gitlinks, never implicitly advances to `main`. Whole child-clone disposal requires explicit recursive approval and fresh recovery proof for its private refs/objects; outer and shared canonical repositories are retained. Local graph refresh never performs remote proof. Child task/runtime/artifact claims block parent disposal.
109	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
110	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
111	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
112	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
113	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
114	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
115	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
116	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output, including `dev hygiene report --json` (`hygiene_summary` schema 1). Stored summaries are historical observations, not proof of current source bytes.
117	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
118	- Explicit SSH format/organize and fleet profile rename/remove are plan-first exceptions for user-selected files; retain comments, Include order, original metadata and private recovery. Never activate dormant files with a new broad Include. Herdr machine add may prepare/start a remote server; leave native approvals native, and remove/disable never stops remote sessions.
119	- SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. Full bootstrap requires an explicit existing key or explicit generation, registers fleet only when explicitly selected, and reports interrupted remote installation as unknown rather than pretending to roll it back.
120	- SSH wizard permission preflight may separately review and apply metadata-only tightening on exact current-user-owned canonical/selected paths. It never recursively chmods, changes ownership, guesses ACLs, or widens permissions; completed repairs survive later cancellation. Listing and dry-run never repair permissions. Local key listing evaluates OpenSSH only behind explicit `--alias`; selected key material remains service-bound and is revalidated before configuration changes and bootstrap.
121	- `dev ssh key doctor` exposes the same permission Plan/Apply with bounded metadata-only key discovery; `--key` restricts the reviewed scope, and `--fix` requires a complete safe plan plus confirmation. Default doctor never mutates, reads private contents, or queries agents/remotes. Batch repairs revalidate the whole reviewed union and retain successful tightening on partial failure.
122	- Source-aware SSH setup can use `--auth existing` without installing a key, and registers only explicitly selected `--to fleet|herdr|both` destinations. Tailscale SSH advertisement is advisory; its port-22 endpoint is not an authorized_keys bootstrap target. Preserve the key-authentication guard and never treat Tailscale policy login as proof that a selected public key worked. Names, ports and cached observations never authorize machine merges; binding/source changes invalidate reviewed plans.
123	- Fleet-source SSH discovery selects explicit hosts without recursive fleet traversal. Local ProxyJump imports never copy remote identity/agent/trust paths; cached route data cannot authorize apply. `connect --on` is one interactive fixed-helper session with no agent forwarding or arbitrary command payload. Normal SSH errors retain child exit status.
124	- Controller password brokerage uses a private per-operation Unix socket or protected Windows pipe, never password argv/environment/files. Exact host/user/port/route contexts gate replies and save evidence. Remote source-to-target credentials remain outside this feature; native key/passphrase interaction is separate.
125	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
126	
127	## Versioning and changelog
128	
129	The current published baseline is `v0.2.39` (2026-09-17). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
130	
131	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
132	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
133	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
134	
135	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
136	
137	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
138	
139	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
140	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
141	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
142	
143	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
144	
145	For a release:
146	
147	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
148	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
149	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
150	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
151	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
152	
153	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
154	
155	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
156	
157	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
158	
159	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
160	
161	| Change | Required synchronization |
162	|---|---|
163	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
164	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
165	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
166	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
167	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
168	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
169	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
170	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
171	
172	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
173	
174	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
175	
176	## Hygiene and skill batch operations
177	
178	`internal/hygiene` owns per-repository setup plans and batch ledgers. REPOS and
179	`hygiene manage` are adapters; JSON batch management previews only. Keep legacy
180	artifact finalizers until their independent lifecycle is replaced. Cached machine
181	privacy imports use only bounded local cache readers and revalidate their source.
182	`internal/agentskill` owns selected-removal policy: exact native names/agent scopes
183	or bundled manifests, source/ownership/dependency proof and postconditions under
184	the provider lease. Never infer complete Windows validation from an advisory
185	step's success conclusion; inspect logs and require the dedicated native gates.
186	
187	## Agent history policy
188	
189	`dev help ai-artifacts` separates source retention, archive location, protection
190	and distribution. New configuration is opt-in. Sources are SpecStory Markdown or
191	explicit files; provider IDs name the originating agent. Do not infer writer exit
192	from byte stability or close agents to finalize evidence. Archive mode verifies
193	ignored bytes before cleanup; existing tracked intents retain their original lane.
194	`git-filter-repo` only operates on new verified copies. Ordinary migration never
195	rewrites source refs or published tags, and raw backups are not secret audits.

88	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir

105

45			if err == nil && provider == p && found == id {
46				paths = append(paths, path)

## 2. `/` filtering: cause and implementation boundary

### Shared dashboard filter

All eight views—TASKS, REPOS, FLEET, TRY, REMOTE, SKILLS, MCP, SSH—share `modeFilter`.

- View definitions: `/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dev-cli/internal/tui/model.go:37–60`.
- `/` enters and focuses the shared input: lines `3167–3173`.
- `updateFilter`: lines `4143–4162`.

Currently `updateFilter` handles only Esc/Enter specially, sends everything else to `textinput.Update`, then **unconditionally calls `m.setAt(0)`**. Thus arrows never move the list, and even Left/Right/Home/End reset the list selection despite not changing the query.

### Recommended behavior

In `updateFilter`:

- Intercept **Up/Down** before the text input and call `m.setAt(m.at() ± 1)`.
- Keep `modeFilter`, input focus, query, and text-cursor position unchanged.
- Optionally support Ctrl+N/P consistently with list navigation.
- For other input, compare the previous and new query; reset selection only when the query actually changes.
- Preserve existing semantics:
  - Enter finishes editing and keeps the filter/selection; it does **not** immediately open the item.
  - Esc clears the filter, leaves editing, and resets selection.
  - `j`/`k`, `g`/`G`, `q`, numeric shortcuts, etc. remain literal text while editing.
  - Left/Right/Home/End and deletion chords remain text editing.

Do **not** forward filter input wholesale to `updateList`. That would turn typed characters into commands and steal editing bindings. The dependency’s actual mappings confirm the collision:

`/Users/zhouhanru/go/pkg/mod/github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles@v1.0.0/textinput/textinput.go:69–85`

- Up/Down and Ctrl+P/N: suggestion navigation.
- Ctrl+D: delete forward.
- Ctrl+U: delete before cursor.
- Home/End and Left/Right: text-cursor movement.

### REMOTE is not a submitted remote search

Dashboard REMOTE `/` filters already-loaded inventory locally through `visibleRemotes()`:

`/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dev-cli/internal/tui/model.go:1361–1379`.

Its network refresh is separate (`afterViewSwitch`, `r`, reload callbacks). Arrow navigation while filtering must not issue a query, refresh, clone, or open.

### Related rendering problem

`/Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dev-cli/internal/tui/view.go:1119–1126` renders pending-row details **before** checking `modeFilter`. Consequently, a pending startup selection hides the filter input and its instructions.

For coherent startup filtering, render the active filter prompt before this passive pending-row detail. This is a rendering adjustment, not permission to execute row actions.

36	// FindTranscript selects exactly one SpecStory transcript by its anchored
37	// preamble session UUID. UUID mentions later in a transcript are never used.
38	func FindTranscript(worktree, provider, sessionID string) (Transcript, error) {
39		history := filepath.Join(worktree, ".specstory", "history")
40		entries, err := os.ReadDir(history)
41		if err != nil {

43		}

56				continue
57			}
58			matches = append(matches, Transcript{Path: path, Provider: gotProvider, SessionID: gotSession})
59		}
60		switch len(matches) {
61		case 1:
62			return matches[0], nil
63		case 0:
64			return Transcript{}, fmt.Errorf("no SpecStory transcript with preamble session %s:%s", provider, sessionID)

697		}

699			return fmt.Errorf("HEAD changed from %s to %s", intent.Head, head)
700		}
701		return nil
702	}

61		sessionPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+:[0-9a-fA-F-]{16,}$`)

64	func (i Intent) Validate() error {
65		if i.Destination != "" && i.Destination != "archive" {
66			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported artifact destination")
67		}
68		if i.Destination == "archive" && (i.ArchiveStateDir == "" || i.ArchivePolicy == "") {
69			return fmt.Errorf("archive intent lacks policy/state binding")
70		}
71		switch {
72		case i.SchemaVersion != SchemaVersion:
73			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported artifact intent schema %d", i.SchemaVersion)
74		case !idPattern.MatchString(i.ID):
75			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact intent id %q", i.ID)
76		case i.RunID == "" || !idPattern.MatchString(i.RunID):
77			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact run id %q", i.RunID)
78		case i.Provider == "" || i.SessionID == "":
79			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs provider and session id")
80		case i.RepoPath == "" || i.WorktreePath == "" || i.GitCommonDir == "":
81			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs repository, worktree and git common-dir paths")
82		case i.Branch == "" || i.Head == "":
83			return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent needs branch and head")
84		}
85		if !sessionPattern.MatchString(i.Provider + ":" + i.SessionID) {
86			return fmt.Errorf("invalid agent session %q", i.Provider+":"+i.SessionID)
87		}
88		switch i.Status {
89		case Armed, Finalizing, Finalized, Failed, Discarded:
90			return nil
91		default:
92			return fmt.Errorf("invalid artifact intent status %q", i.Status)
93		}
94	}
95	
96	func ParseSession(value string) (provider, sessionID string, err error) {
97		provider, sessionID, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(value), ":")
98		provider = strings.ToLower(provider)
99		if !ok || !sessionPattern.MatchString(provider+":"+sessionID) {
100			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("invalid session %q: want provider:uuid", value)
101		}
102		return provider, sessionID, nil
103	}

13	       finalize-agent-commit.sh --request ABSOLUTE_PATH --runner-token TOKEN
14	
15	Validate one private post-session request against its exact worktree, journal,
16	HEAD/ref/index tree, session selectors, and successful outer-run lifecycle.
17	A request file alone is never commit authority.
18	
19	Authorization (choose exactly one):
20	  --allow-commit        Explicit manual recovery authorization. Must be passed
21	                        again on every recovery attempt.
22	  --runner-token TOKEN  Parent-held one-run token supplied directly by
23	                        run-specstory-session.sh; not for child-agent use.
24	  --rotation-confirmed  Manual recovery acknowledgement after sanitation has
25	                        already returned status=rotation_required. Requires
26	                        --allow-commit and is never supplied by the runner.
27	
28	Required:
29	  --request PATH        Absolute .../agent-history-hygiene/runs/UUID/request.json.
30	  --help, -h            Show this help and exit.
31	
32	The initial authorized pass stages and sanitizes exact artifacts, composes and
33	validates provenance, writes private drafts, then invokes one ordinary `git commit -F`.
34	If sanitation changes content it stops for credential rotation;
35	resume only with fresh --allow-commit --rotation-confirmed. Prepared recovery
36	never re-stages, and uncertain committing state is reconciliation-only.
37	
38	Output (stdout): one bounded JSON status object. Diagnostics go to stderr.
39	No transcript, diff, message, scanner output, or credential content is printed.
40	
41	Exit codes:
42	  0   commit completed, or an already-completed commit was proven
43	  1   invalid arguments
44	  2   not inside a Git worktree
45	  3   required dependency unavailable
46	  4   malformed/unsafe request or journal
47	  5   authorization missing/invalid or wrong per-worktree request path
48	  6   stale Git state, active Git operation, lock, or missing lifecycle proof
49	  7   exact selector, staging, scanner, metadata, or message validation failed
50	  8   prior commit outcome cannot be proven; reconciliation only, never retry
51	  9   unrelated commit-message draft would be overwritten
52	  10  sanitation changed content; rotate credentials, then confirm recovery
53	  11  ordinary commit failed with HEAD unchanged; prepared snapshot retained
54	EOF
55	}

28			return "", e
29		}
30		if s.Policy.Source != "specstory" {
31			return "", errors.New("prepared sessions require SpecStory; use artifact archive --file for exported plans")
32		}
33		p, id, e := parseSession(session)
34		if e != nil {
35			return "", e
36		}
37		files, e := s.sources(ctx)
38		if e != nil {
39			return "", e
40		}
41		var paths []string
42		for _, file := range files {
43			path := s.capturePath(file)
44			provider, found, err := prefixIdentity(path)
45			if err == nil && provider == p && found == id {
46				paths = append(paths, path)
47			}
48		}
49		if len(paths) != 1 {
50			return "", errors.New("session does not identify one exact SpecStory transcript")
51		}
52		return paths[0], nil
53	}

47			candidate.Status = Armed

49			candidate.CreatedAt, candidate.UpdatedAt = now, now
50			if err := candidate.Validate(); err != nil {
51				return err
52			}
53			if _, err := os.Stat(s.path(candidate.ID)); err == nil {
54				return fmt.Errorf("artifact intent %s already exists", candidate.ID)

67		if !idPattern.MatchString(id) {

148			}
149		}

- 審閱結果必須涵蓋全部 finding／occurrence，綁定原 request/journal 的 exact revision、selected paths、parent/tree/policy，並區分舊的真實 lifecycle proof 與新建的 review proof。
- 使用明確 versioned import/recovery receipt；不修改舊 journal 來「補出」過去未有的證据。不足就保留 blocked。
- 真正消費恢復計畫／commit、或改用新 wrapper session，需看到 preview 後的另一個明確授權；本次 codefix approval 不代表已核准未知恢復結果。

## 5. Canonical helper：完整證據、fixture review 與 exact sync

主要檔案（agent-skills repo）：
`skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/{_post_session.py,run-specstory-session.sh,queue-agent-commit.sh,finalize-agent-commit.sh,stage-agent-artifacts.sh}`、`assets/redact_secrets.py`。

### 5.1 新 run 的 versioned evidence

- 新 run 使用明確 v2 protocol／journal，提供 side-effect-free capabilities；v1 的嚴格 parser、existing state 與恢復語意保留，不默默加欄位或升級。
- 重用目前 alternate-index sanitation／materialization／frozen-commit transaction，在改動前持久化 private sanitation receipt：完整 post-sync before-images、pre/post blob IDs、每個 finding/occurrence 與完整 transformation、path/native identity、request/session/root/ref/parent/index/prepared tree、scanner/config identity、coverage 與 revision。
- 證據寫入失败／不完整時不得發布 sanitized index／來源或宣稱 clean。Raw bytes 與 full values 不進公開輸出。

### 5.2 真實的 run-scoped finding review

- Finalizer 增加只讀 `--preview-review --json`：輸出 masked findings、receipt revision、可審閱狀態與 private review 位置，不 commit。
- `--review-file <private versioned decisions>` 對 exact finding IDs 填寫 reason／disposition，與 receipt、prepared state 綁定；仍須新的明確 `--allow-commit` 才可提交。
- 區分 `reviewed_noncredential`、`credential_rotation_required`、`unresolved`；sanitation 本身不證明真實 credential exposure。全部 occurrence 必須有完整證據，未知／partial／stale／mixed unresolved 繼續阻擋。
- 已審閱 fixture 只解除**本次已 sanitized snapshot**不適用的 rotation gate；不還原 raw bytes、不豁免未來掃描、不略過 hooks，也不假裝 `--rotation-confirmed`。
- Apply 在既有 finalizer lock 內重驗 exact receipt/review/request、來源／policy、HEAD/ref/index/tree；既有 uncertain commit 只 reconcile，絕不第二次 commit。
- 與 native `PreviewAllow` 的持續性 policy exceptions 保持區別，不再造一套 scanner。
- 提交前重用既有 staged checker，確認整個 frozen prepared index 的適用檔案都有 policy/scanner coverage；sanitation 只改 exact selected artifacts，product findings 只阻擋、不順便重寫。Global hook 因缺少 repo config 而跳過不能當作保護已生效；本輪不自動安裝／修改既有 hook chain。

### 5.3 Sync freshness 與禁止 cloud publication

- Run 的 no-cloud 選擇明確傳至真正 post-exit sync／export；使用原生支援 flags，不透過臨時改寫使用者 config。v2 的自動交接預設 no-cloud；不默默啟用 cloud。
- 保留真實 child exit／process-group quiescence proof；UUID、mtime 或「bytes 有變」都不能代替 freshness。
- 在同一明確 UUID／root、已停止 native source 下，以原生 exact export 證明所選檔內容：正常 sync 後，使用支援的 `sync --print`（加 silent/no-cloud/no-stats 等受支援選項）取得 bounded private candidate，核對 native source identity 與所選 alias 的完整 rendered digest。這是一次實際 sync 加只讀 export verification，不是重试 sync。
- 凍結／核對 native source generation，防止 sync 與 export 之間改變；候選必須通過 exact preamble／root/session proof。若原生版本無法提供已驗證的 export，明確 `freshness_unproven`，不退回 mtime／nonce 字串猜測。
- 若 sync 更新另一個 alias 而 selected path stale，就停下保留資料；不自動改 selector、不刪其他 alias、不手造 recorder 證據。
- 原生 flag／output 真實行為需以隔離 fixture integration test 核實；不把 fake-provider unit test 當成實際版本相容性證明。

## 6. 薄型 dev co-commit adapter：不建立第二個 commit engine

在上述 guard/revision 與 canonical v2 完成後加入；per-invocation opt-in，**不新增全域預設政策**。

建議介面：

```text
dev prepare [task-or-worktree] --closeout co-commit \
  --session provider:uuid --specstory-path <exact-path> \
  (--plan <one-path> | --no-plan) --message-file <base-message> [--json]
```

- `--closeout` 預設 `product-first`，舊命令不變；co-commit 與 archive policy 不混用。
- 明確解析已安裝 canonical helper、核對 v2 capability／tool/source identity；缺少或不支援就回報可操作的 blocker，不下載／安裝／执行未知 helper。
- 只在真實 wrapper context 下 queue。無 authentic run 时回報 `requires_wrapper` 及正確啟動方式，不猜 run ID、不生成 parent token／journal、不自动關閉或重啟 agent。
- Helper 繼續獨占 staging／sanitation／commit／reconciliation。Native 只記錄 expected-revision binding，包含 helper request/revision、repo/root/ref/HEAD／staged product tree、exact selectors；不呼叫 legacy scanner/restage。
- Native status/readiness 讀取并核對 helper receipt；不是看 exit 0、trailer 或 draft 就當成功。Finalize 的 co-commit path 僅委派 canonical backend，帶入真正的外部 approval／writer guard；不得落入 product-first executor。
- Queue 前要求 feature-only index；已 staged artifact 不會被偷偷移出。相同 request 可重入查證，不同 request 衝突。
- 明確處理 partial outcomes：helper 已 queued 但 native binding 未寫入，回傳 `queued_but_not_bound`，保留 request並停止子 agent 的 repo 操作；只允許 idempotent bind repair，不另 queue。Helper 已 commit 而 native persistence 失敗，只驗證 exact commit並補 receipt，不重 commit。
- 定義 repo/run/native-store lock ordering，不持有 native store lock 跨 helper／hooks；返回時以 expected revision CAS，stale 即拒絕新作用。
- 新 JSON 輸出使用獨立 versioned schema，既有 documented JSON／human defaults 不改名移除。

    subprocess.run(['git','-C',root,'worktree','add','-b',branch,destination,expected],check=True)
    if hashlib.sha256(idx.read_bytes()).hexdigest()!=before:raise SystemExit('Original index changed during creation: '+root)

6	
7	## Toolchain and commands
8	
9	- Go 1.26.4 (from `go.mod`) builds the CLI. Python 3.11+ and `uv` are used only for the documentation site.
10	- `make` / `make all` runs `fmt -> vet -> test -> build`. `make fmt` runs `gofmt -w .` and therefore modifies files.
11	- There is no working `make lint` recipe even though `lint` appears in `.PHONY`. The repository's static gates are formatting and `go vet`.
12	
13	```bash
14	make build                         # build ./dev with git-derived version metadata
15	make test                          # go test ./...
16	go test -race -timeout 20m ./...   # CI test command
17	go test ./internal/gitx -run '^TestAddWorktreeUsesExplicitBase$'  # one test
18	go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestName/Subtest$'                  # one subtest
19	make vet                           # go vet ./...
20	files="$(gofmt -l .)" && test -z "$files"  # format check that preserves gofmt failures
21	make e2e                           # real CLI lifecycle in an isolated temporary HOME
22	make skill-sync                    # regenerate command docs, then rebuild embedded skill
23	make skill-check                   # fail when command tree and generated skill reference drift
24	make install                       # binary under PREFIX; skill in user agent directories
25	```
26	
27	Documentation uses the same sequence as CI:
28	
29	```bash
30	uv sync --frozen --extra docs
31	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source
32	uv run mkdocs build --strict
33	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --site site
34	```
35	
36	If generated `docs/llms*.txt` files drift, regenerate them with `uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source --generate-llms` and then rerun the documentation checks.
37	
38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `submodule` owns versioned workspace-member intent and reversible child-clone disposal mechanisms. `gitx` supplies the local gitlink graph; `taskflow` owns recursive lifecycle policy and fresh remote-proof ordering. Gitlink checkouts are legitimate submodules, not nested managed linked worktrees.
56	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints. Lifecycle callers use exact-record revisions and locked compare-and-update/delete transactions rather than treating a previously read task as current.
57	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
58	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
59	- `taskflow` is the UI-agnostic lifecycle authority: it separates recorded intent, typed live observations, immutable guarded plans, approvals, and partial result ledgers. Apply locks and reloads task/Git/worktree/runtime/artifact/remote identity, then rejects stale authority before mutation.
60	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, all registered worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and UI projections consume this joined view.
61	- `agentinterop` owns explicit MCP/skill/instruction transfer plans, guarded apply, stanza/link ownership, private recovery, and optional recipes. Native agent files and skills locks remain authoritative; only explicit preparation/check/launch paths may execute a provider or MCP server. Recovery belongs outside Git, credentials remain runtime references, and native Windows writes fail closed pending verified ACL/identity support.
62	- `triage` owns read-only cross-repository findings, clone-bound local intent, ignored-directory policy and reviewed batch ledgers; `triagetui` is its independent UI. Synchronization uses taskflow plans, and protected cleanup adds guards inside the existing repository lock and immediately before removal. Local scans never reconcile Try catalog entries.
63	- `flowtui` is an independent Bubble Tea model for the preview `dev flow` repository state-machine UI. It receives repository reads and taskflow Plan/Apply callbacks; do not embed it in or add a mode to the dashboard's `tui` model.
64	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
65	- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
66	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.

101	## Behavioral contracts
102	
103	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
104	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
105	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
106	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
107	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
108	- Submodule initialization uses committed gitlinks, never implicitly advances to `main`. Whole child-clone disposal requires explicit recursive approval and fresh recovery proof for its private refs/objects; outer and shared canonical repositories are retained. Local graph refresh never performs remote proof. Child task/runtime/artifact claims block parent disposal.
109	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
110	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
111	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
112	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
113	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
114	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
115	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
116	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output, including `dev hygiene report --json` (`hygiene_summary` schema 1). Stored summaries are historical observations, not proof of current source bytes.
117	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
118	- Explicit SSH format/organize and fleet profile rename/remove are plan-first exceptions for user-selected files; retain comments, Include order, original metadata and private recovery. Never activate dormant files with a new broad Include. Herdr machine add may prepare/start a remote server; leave native approvals native, and remove/disable never stops remote sessions.
119	- SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. 120	- SSH wizard permission preflight may separately review and apply metadata-only tightening on exact current-user-owned canonical/selected paths. Local key listing evaluates OpenSSH only behind explicit `--alias`; selected key material remains service-bound and is revalidated before configuration changes and bootstrap.
121	- `dev ssh key doctor` exposes the same permission Plan/Apply with bounded metadata-only key discovery; `--key` restricts the reviewed scope, and `--fix` requires a complete safe plan plus confirmation.
