1	# Agent-safe retirement
2	
3	A process must not delete the worktree that contains its own current directory.
4	The terminal can remain visible after Unix unlinks the path, but config reloads,
5	relative files and new subprocesses then fail. Herdr still showing a pane does
6	not mean the Git checkout is healthy.
7	
8	Use three separate milestones:
9	
10	1. **READY** — commit product work, run `dev prepare`, then exit normally so the
11	   post-SpecStory finalizer can preserve the exact final transcript in its selected source-commit or external-archive destination. A manual
12	   external finalizer must pass `--writer-stopped`; a Claude SessionEnd observer
13	   can provide the same durable proof without staging during teardown.
14	2. **MERGED** — `dev done --ff`, or external-merge verification with
15	   `dev done --merged --base-ref <ref>`, records DONE. Explicit and
16	   non-interactive completion keeps worktree/branch; selected interactive task
17	   pane closures are reported separately. Bare interactive
18	   completion may continue into a separately confirmed cleanup preview.
19	3. **RETIRED** — from outside the target workspace run `dev retire`. It closes
20	   eligible runtime sessions, waits until they disappear, revalidates Git, and
21	   removes the worktree without force.
22	
23	`dev flow [repo]` exposes Retire only for an exact DONE task. It first shows
24	conditions, ordered effects, resources retained, and a fallback command; branch
25	deletion is a separate typed option. Apply reloads the exact task revision and
26	Git/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identity under locks, repeats safety checks
27	after runtime closure and before removal, and deletes the task record last.
28	Completed steps remain visible if a later step fails; no rollback is implied.
29	
30	## Recursive submodule removal
31	
32	`--recursive` is required even when every gitlink is empty. For linked-worktree
33	removal only, a child path that is absent or truly empty with no retained Git
34	store may use local empty proof; no initialization, download, remote proof or
35	push is needed merely for removal. Deinitialized retained data, orphan stores,
36	local/ignored files, unexpected `.git`, symlinks/reparse points, external claims
37	and incomplete observations block. Empty-child task/artifact claims use paths,
38	not parent-inherited Git discovery; any non-discarded matching artifact intent
39	blocks, even finalized, and discarded records still bind the reviewed authority.
40	
41	Initialized child clones retain full remote recovery requirements and inside-out
42	journaled staging/rollback, including mixed workspaces. Only exact reviewed empty
43	modules admin directories may be pruned under locks after immediate native
44	directory identity/emptiness revalidation. Empty checkout directories stay for
45	ordinary non-force `git worktree remove`; no recursive file-deletion workaround
46	is used. Layout changes, new initialization or claims invalidate plans. Partial
47	admin pruning failure is reported, never task-retired success. Canonical/shared
48	Git and the outer branch remain; initialization/publication policy is unchanged.
49	`objects/info/alternates` remains an intentional blocker.
50	
51	## Choose the containment base
52	
53	`dev retire --base <ref>` overrides the containment target for a DONE task or
54	linked worktree without changing recorded task intent. Resolution checks a local
55	branch (`refs/heads/X`), then a remote-tracking branch (`refs/remotes/X`, such as
56	`origin/main`), then a commit. Fully qualified branch refs keep their named kind.
57	Apply re-resolves the same input and requires the same kind, ref and commit OID;
58	a moved base or a newly created same-name branch makes the reviewed plan stale.
59	Remote-tracking refs are local observations, not an implicit fetch. Equal trees
60	after a squash are not ancestry proof and do not waive containment checks.
61	
62	Without an override, task retirement keeps its recorded base. A recorded
63	fork-point commit is never silently replaced by the default branch: if it cannot
64	prove integration, retirement stays blocked with `pass --base <branch>` guidance.
65	After `dev done --merged --base-ref X`, cleanup hints, the cleanup wizard and the
66	external coordinator carry X forward as `dev retire --base X <task>`. If a shell
67	handoff cannot carry the override, dev prints the external command instead.
68	
69	Optional `--delete-branch` still runs ordinary `git branch -d`, whose own merged
70	check uses the branch's upstream or HEAD, not `--base`. Against a non-HEAD base,
71	branch deletion can therefore fail after the worktree was removed; the branch
72	and DONE task remain, and the result reports partial completion.
73	
74	Retirement never overrides `working`, `blocked`, or `waiting` agents. Unknown
75	status needs external `--close-unknown`. A workspace containing panes outside
76	the target is mixed-purpose and must be reorganized or closed manually.
77	
78	The bare interactive `dev done` cleanup preview shows those workspace panes and
79	agent states before offering keep, retire, or retire plus branch deletion. If
80	the target is the caller's Herdr workspace, dev creates a fresh exact-root-pane
81	workspace in the canonical checkout and hands a short-lived, single-use intent
82	to that external coordinator. It revalidates task, checkout HEAD, runtime
83	fingerprint, and the full ordinary retirement plan before closing anything.
84	
85	Before MERGED, parent/canonical agents are preserved and block FF: recheck,
86	choose PR, or cancel. Exact idle/done task-worktree panes can be selected for
87	closure, but only final Apply closes them. Other active agents remain blockers.
88	General foreground programs require independent FF file-change consent while
89	they keep running. Interactive done/retire cleanup lists workspace/tab/pane IDs
90	and program names/PIDs/directories. Known programs require CLOSE <workspace-id>
91	and final retirement approval; --close-unknown does not grant this consent.
92	A foreground shell is not proof of no background jobs: those are not inspected.
93	Parent/mixed workspaces remain open. Cancellation before Apply closes nothing;
94	partial failures list completed closures. Old coordinator handoffs must be
95	recreated; version 2 verifies the launching PID has returned to a shell. If the canonical
96	integration checkout is dirty, dev lists its paths and offers PR handoff,
97	typed-`DROP` guarded discard, or cancel. It never silently commits unrelated
98	canonical bytes.
99	
100	Raw `git worktree remove --force` and configured external tools bypass these
101	protections. Do not use them on an agent-owned checkout. Existing expert CLI
102	acknowledgements remain available, but the flow preview deliberately omits dirty
103	discard, shared-writer/takeover, and unknown-runtime overrides.
104	
105	Task-backed `dev retire` and exact unmanaged path retirement use taskflow
106	(the latter requires contained removal). Some record-only/orphan-salvage `sweep`
107	reconciliation paths remain separate; not every cleanup uses the same planner.
108	
109	From the canonical main checkout, `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` reports both
110	tracked and unmanaged linked worktrees whose named branches are contained in
111	main. Review the exact candidates and blockers first; apply only after user
112	confirmation. Worktree retirement keeps branches unless `--delete-branches`
113	was separately requested.
114	
115	`dev sweep --base <ref>` also forwards the selected base to DONE task retirement;
116	`--merged-worktrees` uses its verified base for managed tasks as well as unmanaged
117	checkouts. Reviewed retire/remove plans bind worktree-list authority only to the
118	same branch or paths equal to, containing, or nested under the target. Removing
119	an unrelated sibling no longer invalidates the rest of an approved
120	`--apply --yes` batch. A same-branch checkout or target lock/HEAD change still
121	makes the plan stale; containment and all other guards remain required.
122	
123	Claude Workflow turn-scoped worktrees have a separate strict V1 audit:
124	
125	```bash
126	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees [--stale-days 14] [--json]
127	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply
128	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply --delete-branches --base main
129	```
130	
131	Run it only from the canonical non-bare checkout. The report verifies one exact
132	bounded mapping under `~/.claude/projects`, terminal workflow plus done agent,
133	matching journal start/result, no same-ID resumed transcript, provider inactivity,
134	and every live Git/task/artifact/runtime/caller fact. `killed` without a child
135	result, progress, resume, missing/prunable/unregistered/orphan paths, dirty or

1	# Agent-safe worktree retirement
2	
3	Recursive submodule disposal requires explicit `--recursive`. Initialized child
4	clones need task/artifact/runtime checks and fresh remote recovery proof before
5	inside-out staging. For linked-worktree removal only, an absent/truly empty child
6	path with no retained Git store can instead use local empty proof; do not
7	initialize or download it merely for cleanup. Path-based claims and incomplete
8	observations still block. Only exact reviewed empty modules admin scaffolding
9	may be pruned under locks with native directory-only identity/emptiness guards;
10	empty checkout directories stay for non-force Git removal. Canonical/shared Git
11	and the outer branch remain. Partial pruning failure is not RETIRED; real-store
12	journals/rollback remain, including mixed workspaces. Recover retained journals
13	with `dev submodule recover`, never delete them using old proof. See `submodules.md`.
14	
15	## The rule
16	
17	A feature agent may prepare and integrate work, but it must not destroy the
18	runtime or checkout containing its own process. Completion has three milestones:
19	
20	```text
21	READY     exact final transcript committed after the writer exits
22	MERGED    branch integrated; runtime/worktree may still exist
23	RETIRED   runtime absent, worktree removed, optional branch deleted, task reaped
24	```
25	
26	`hot/warm/cold/done` remain the persisted task states. `done` now means MERGED,
27	not "everything has already been deleted".
28	
29	## Normal local flow
30	
31	From the feature worktree:
32	
33	```bash
34	# Commit product changes first. Do not stage the moving transcript.
35	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid> --plan .claude/plans/task.md
36	# Exit the agent normally so SpecStory can write its final Markdown.
37	```
38	
39	The outer `specstory run` wrapper calls:
40	
41	```bash
42	dev artifact finalize --run-id "$DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID" --if-pending --writer-stopped
43	```
44	
45	Then an external main/integration workspace runs:
46	
47	```bash
48	dev done <task> --ff
49	dev retire <task> --delete-branch
50	```
51	
52	`done` only integrates and records MERGED. `retire` re-resolves every runtime
53	pane, closes eligible sessions, waits for them to disappear, revalidates Git,
54	and removes the worktree without force.
55	
56	`dev flow [repo]` offers Retire only for an exact DONE task. Enter first shows a
57	revision-bound plan with conditions, ordered effects, retained resources, and a
58	CLI fallback; branch deletion needs the displayed typed token. Apply locks and
59	reloads task/repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact authority, repeats safety
60	checks after closure and before removal, and deletes the task last. If a later
61	effect fails, its ledger reports completed work and recovery without claiming a
62	rollback.
63	
64	For periodic cleanup from the canonical main checkout:
65	
66	```bash
67	dev sweep --merged-worktrees
68	# Present the exact candidates/blockers to the user and ask for approval.
69	dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply --yes
70	```
71	
72	This includes unmanaged linked worktrees whose named branches are already
73	contained in main. It never treats containment alone as permission: dirty Git,
74	pending artifacts and runtime blockers still stop cleanup. Branches remain by
75	default; add `--delete-branches` only when the user approved that separately.
76	
77	`dev sweep --base <ref>` also forwards the selected base to DONE task retirement;
78	`--merged-worktrees` uses its verified base for managed tasks as well as unmanaged
79	checkouts. Reviewed retire/remove plans bind worktree-list authority only to the
80	same branch or paths equal to, containing, or nested under the target. Removing
81	an unrelated sibling no longer invalidates the rest of an approved
82	`--apply --yes` batch. A same-branch checkout or target lock/HEAD change still
83	makes the plan stale; containment and all other guards remain required.
84	
85	Claude Workflow ephemeral worktrees use a separate, stricter path:
86	
87	```bash
88	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --stale-days 14
89	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --json
90	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply
91	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply --delete-branches --base main
92	```
93	
94	Run it from the canonical non-bare checkout. The schema-v1 report joins one
95	bounded, fixed-depth `~/.claude/projects` mapping to live Git state without
96	decoding or emitting prompts, scripts, logs, result bodies, or transcript
97	content. V1 requires workflow `completed|killed`, matching agent `done`, journal
98	`started` and `result`, no same-ID resumed transcript, and provider inactivity
99	older than `--stale-days` (default 14, minimum 1). Killed/no-result, progress,
100	resume, malformed/mutating metadata, or unknown time stays `unknown`; there is no
101	operator-attestation bypass.
102	
103	Ownership must also bind provider-observed branch, HEAD, common-dir, and an opaque
104	non-replayable registration generation to the live target. Claude Code 2.1.259
105	records no such Git identity, so current Claude Workflow claims report
106	`provider-git-identity: unknown` and remain report-only even with `--apply`.
107	A path, derived branch name, or reusable GitDir pathname is never a substitute;
108	otherwise stale terminal metadata could authorize a replacement checkout at the
109	same path.
110	
111	The worktree must remain registered, present, non-main, named, unlocked and
112	non-prunable, with exact common-dir/branch/registry-HEAD/live-HEAD agreement. It
113	must have no staged/unstaged/conflicted/untracked/ignored/recursive-submodule
114	content, no Git operation, task claim, unsafe artifact intent, caller
115	containment, or covering runtime. Missing, prunable, unregistered, and orphan
116	paths are report only. Apply rejects `--yes`, `--close-unknown`,
117	`--assume-no-runtime`, `--no-runtime`, and JSON; it requires a TTY and per-item
118	confirmation. Under a common-dir cleanup lock it recollects every fact and
119	compares the stable candidate fingerprint before plain non-force removal. It
120	never prunes, closes sessions, deletes provider metadata, or rescues/stashes/
121	commits dirty work.
122	
123	A branch is retained by default, so a clean checkout with unique commits may be
124	removed safely. Optional branch deletion is a separate proof requiring an
125	explicit base, unchanged branch/base tips, containment, zero unique commits, and
126	ordinary `git branch -d`; any post-removal failure leaves the branch retained and
127	reports partial completion.
128	
129	## Choose the containment base
130	
131	`dev retire --base <ref>` overrides the containment target for a DONE task or
132	linked worktree without changing recorded task intent. Resolution checks a local
133	branch (`refs/heads/X`), then a remote-tracking branch (`refs/remotes/X`, such as
134	`origin/main`), then a commit. Fully qualified branch refs keep their named kind.
135	Apply re-resolves the same input and requires the same kind, ref and commit OID;
136	a moved base or a newly created same-name branch makes the reviewed plan stale.
137	Remote-tracking refs are local observations, not an implicit fetch.
138	
139	Without an override, task retirement keeps its recorded base. A recorded
140	fork-point commit is never silently replaced by the default branch: if it cannot
141	prove integration, retirement stays blocked with `pass --base <branch>` guidance.
142	After `dev done --merged --base-ref X`, cleanup hints, the cleanup wizard and the
143	external coordinator carry X forward as `dev retire --base X <task>`. If a shell
144	handoff cannot carry the override, dev prints the external command instead.
145	
146	Optional `--delete-branch` still runs ordinary `git branch -d`, whose own merged
147	check uses the branch's upstream or HEAD, not `--base`. Against a non-HEAD base,
148	branch deletion can therefore fail after the worktree was removed; the branch
149	and DONE task remain, and the result reports partial completion.
150	
151	## Pull-request flow
152	
153	```bash
154	dev done <task> --pr
155	# after CI/review and a commit-preserving merge
156	git fetch origin
157	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main
158	dev retire --base origin/main <task> --delete-branch
159	```
160	
161	A squash merge is not ancestry-equivalent. It requires an explicit operator
162	attestation:
163	
164	```bash
165	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main --confirm-squash <merge-commit>
166	```
167	
168	This proves only that the named squash commit is in the base; the operator is
169	asserting that it represents the feature. Equal trees after a squash are not
170	ancestry proof and do not waive retirement's containment checks.
171	
172	## Safety policy
173	
174	Retirement always refuses when:
175	
176	- the caller cwd is the target or below it;
177	- the caller Herdr workspace/pane or tmux pane covers the target;
178	- a workspace contains panes outside the target;
179	- an agent is `working`, `blocked`, or `waiting`;
180	- runtime enumeration fails;
181	- the checkout is dirty, on the wrong branch, or not contained in its base;
182	- a relevant artifact finalization is armed/finalizing/failed.
183	
184	`unknown` or empty agent status requires `--close-unknown` from outside the
185	target. Runtime enumeration failure requires external `--assume-no-runtime`.
186	Neither flag bypasses caller containment or active-agent states.
187	
188	Raw `git worktree remove --force` and configured external tools can bypass dev.
189	Never run them from an agent that occupies the target. dev's guarantee covers
190	only dev-mediated paths. Existing CLI expert acknowledgements remain compatible,
191	but flow intentionally omits them. Task-backed and exact unmanaged path
192	retirement use taskflow, with contained removal required for the latter. Some
193	record-only/salvage `sweep` actions remain isolated compatibility paths.
194	
195	## What self-deletion looks like
196	
197	A real Codex session deleted its own registered worktree and branch from another
198	checkout. Herdr kept the workspace and terminal alive because Unix processes can
199	hold an open cwd inode after the path is unlinked. SpecStory then recreated the
200	same path with only `.specstory/` content.
201	
202	The resulting shell looked alive but was no longer a Git checkout:
203	
204	```text
205	failed to reload config: No such file or directory
206	fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
207	```
208	
209	Config/skill reloads and new subprocesses failed while Herdr still displayed an
210	idle agent. Treat `runtime alive + Git registration absent + artifact-only path`
211	as an orphan requiring transcript salvage and external reconciliation, never as
212	RETIRED.
213	
214	## Artifact rules
215	
216	- Match SpecStory Markdown by the exact UUID in its fixed preamble, not filename
217	  or newest mtime.
218	- Finalize only after SessionEnd was observed or the outer wrapper supplies
219	  `--writer-stopped`; byte stability remains a second, independent check.
220	- Stage only that transcript and explicitly named plans.
221	- Never stage another provider/session implicitly.
222	- `.specstory/statistics.json` is derived and ignored.
223	- New untracked transcripts above 2 MiB need `--allow-large`.
224	- Scanner/redactor failure commits nothing and leaves a retryable intent.
225	- Artifact commits are on the same feature branch, not necessarily the same
226	  product commit; they carry `Agent-Artifact-Session` and
227	  `Dev-Artifact-Intent` trailers.
228	
229	## Task worktree scope
230	
231	Worktree-mode `dev start --focus -t <name>` creates a linked checkout; `--focus`
232	only changes focus. Finishing that task preserves its parent/canonical agent
233	sessions and other tasks' tabs. A recognized parent agent in any state blocks
234	FF: recheck after handling it independently in Herdr, choose PR, or cancel.
235	When integration is already proven and only retirement remains, a parent agent
236	does not prevent cleanup of the separate child worktree.
237	
238	The interactive finish plan may select exact idle/done **task-worktree** agent
239	panes for closure. Nothing closes until final Apply approval. Parent, other
240	checkout, mixed, or unverified Herdr workspaces are protected even when a pane
241	has changed into the target directory. If they still cover the worktree,
242	retirement stops and identifies the preserved panes. Working/blocked/waiting
243	agents remain blockers. General foreground programs (an editor, server, or
244	test command) require a separate FF confirmation: files in the displayed
245	checkout will change while those programs continue running. `--yes` does not
246	supply that confirmation; non-interactive calls requiring it stop.
247	
248	Interactive `dev done` cleanup and standalone `dev retire` share a preview of
249	the target, retained resources, workspace/tab/pane IDs, agent states, and
250	foreground program names, PIDs and directories. Closing known non-agent
251	programs requires typing `CLOSE <workspace-id>` for each affected workspace,
252	then approving the final retirement. `--close-unknown` does not authorize
253	known program termination. Only a proven foreground shell is labeled as such;
254	unavailable process evidence is shown as unknown, never idle. Herdr provides
255	foreground evidence; other backends keep their existing explicitly qualified
256	unknown-runtime policy. Background jobs are **not inspected** and may also stop
257	when their terminal closes. Raw argv and environment values are not displayed.
258	
259	Approvals bind exact task/checkout, terminal topology and program fingerprints.
260	A changed program, new tab or moved pane requires a refreshed preview. The
261	single-use version-2 coordinator handoff waits for the exact launching dev PID
262	to exit and verifies the original pane has returned to its foreground shell;
263	a replacement program is not exempt. Old handoffs must be recreated. Final
264	cancellation before Apply changes nothing; failures after effects begin list
265	completed closures and retained resources. Raw Git and Herdr actions remain
266	outside dev's locks and revalidation guarantees.
267	
268	## External archive policy
269	
270	`dev artifact setup` can select a separate Git archive. New prepared intents bind
271	that destination and policy; old intents keep the commit workflow. Off/check
272	finalization needs no compatibility redactor script. For redact copies, review
273	`dev artifact archive` and supply `--archive-plan` when finalizing. Commit reviewed
274	plans with product changes before preparing one exact SpecStory transcript.
275	Ignored capture bytes participate in lifecycle readiness; a new recorder write or
276	missing archive receipt blocks cleanup. See [AI artifacts](ai-artifacts.md).

```text
1	# Task lifecycle
2	
3	For submodule workspaces, Cold verifies initialized child clones' remote
4	recoverability; Retire also verifies recorded child integration. Linked-worktree
5	removal can instead prove a child locally empty only when its path is absent or
6	truly empty, no child Git store remains, and ownership/observation guards pass.
7	`--recursive` is still required; such empty children need no initialization,
8	download, remote proof or push merely for removal. Retained/deinitialized data
9	and incomplete observations remain blockers. Parent `--push` never implicitly
10	pushes children. Read `submodules.md` for claim checks, guarded admin pruning and
11	recovery; member intent is versioned separately from legacy task TOML.
12	
13	Read this when work needs to be paused, picked up on another machine, or when
14	a machine has accumulated more open sessions than anyone can hold in mind.
15	
16	## The problem
17	
18	A terminal multiplexer's sidebar is a *runtime* view: it shows what is running
19	now. When it is also the only record of what you are working on, nothing can be
20	closed, because closing it loses the thread. The sidebar grows until it stops
21	being scannable, which defeats its purpose.
22	
23	The fix is not discipline. It is giving "what am I working on" a home that is
24	not the runtime.
25	
26	## Pick a checkout mode before a lifecycle
27	
28	A task records human intent; it does not imply a worktree:
29	
30	| Command | Checkout boundary | Use when |
31	|---|---|---|
32	| `dev repo open api` | none; no task | browsing or truly ad-hoc work |
33	| `dev start api -t typo --direct` | current branch, usually main | one short tracked change |
34	| `dev start api -t small --branch-only --base main` | branch in canonical checkout | lightweight isolation, no concurrency |
35	| `dev start api -t auth --base main` | branch + linked worktree | interruption, experiment, parallel writer |
36	
37	In an interactive terminal, bare `dev start` opens the same managed flow as a
38	context-aware wizard. It prompts for repo, task, mode, branch, base and next,
39	then shows the computed checkout/runtime summary before creating anything.
40	`dev start -t <name>` remains the fast path; `--json` and non-TTY use never
41	prompt.
42	
43	With a newly created first-class Herdr worktree, `--run '<shell command>'` can
44	dispatch one reviewed command to the exact root pane. It is separate from the
45	pure `--json` contract, and `--focus` independently controls whether the caller
46	switches after dispatch.
47	
48	Direct tasks go HOT ↔ WARM and finish with plain `dev done`; they cannot go
49	COLD because the canonical checkout cannot be removed. Branch-only tasks can go
50	cold after push by switching the canonical checkout back to base. The full
51	state machine below describes the default worktree mode.
52	
53	Do not create isolation before it has a job. Equally, a new parallel worktree
54	starts from its committed base — it does not carry dirty main changes — so
55	checkpoint first when the new task depends on them.
56	
57	## The four states
58	
59	| State | Git | Runtime | Meaning |
60	|---|---|---|---|
61	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
62	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | normally closed | back within days |
63	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
64	| ✅ `done` | merged | may still be open | MERGED; external retirement pending |
65	
66	Only the transitions between them cost anything:
67	
68	```
69	        dev start
70	            │
71	            ▼
72	         🔥 hot ── prepare/exit/finalize ──► READY
73	          │  ▲                                  │
74	   dev park│  │dev resume                       │ dev done
75	          ▼  │                                  ▼
76	        🌤 warm                             ✅ done / MERGED
77	          │  ▲                                  │
78	dev park  │  │dev resume                        │ external dev retire
79	  --cold  ▼  │  (rebuilds the worktree)          ▼
80	        ❄️ cold                              RETIRED (entry removed)
81	```
82	
83	The enforced graph is mode-aware: worktree/branch HOT or WARM can park WARM or
84	COLD; WARM/COLD resume HOT; HOT/WARM can complete or hand off review; DONE can
85	only Retire. Direct tasks omit COLD and branch integration. Review handoff is
86	state-preserving. COLD must resume before completion, and no ordinary action
87	moves DONE backward.
88	
89	### Plan it by repository
90	
91	`dev flow [repo]` is an independent preview-labelled, full-screen TUI, not a mode
92	of the dashboard. From a canonical or linked checkout it opens the canonical
93	repository and focuses that exact surface; outside Git it opens a repository
94	picker. It projects every Git-registered worktree plus task-only records such as
95	COLD/DONE tasks without a checkout.
96	
97	The UI shows three layers separately:
98	
99	1. persisted task intent: mode, HOT/WARM/COLD/DONE, owner, next, branch/base, and
100	   expected checkout;
101	2. observed facts: exact worktree identity, Git status/operation/refs, runtime and
102	   agent occupancy, artifact readiness, each kept as known/unknown/error/skipped/
103	   loading rather than converting probe failure into false;
104	3. a guarded plan: availability, evidence/remediation, ordered effects, retained
105	   resources, confirmation, exact fallback, task revision, and PlanID.
106	
107	Enter creates the plan; it never applies. READY non-typed plans need `y`; typed
108	plans need the displayed token plus Enter. Apply locks and reloads the task
109	revision and exact repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact authority. If any
110	identity changed, it rejects the stale plan before a new effect. Apply itself is
111	not canceled by row movement/refresh/quit; the UI retains completed/failed steps
112	and recovery, then starts a new local read.
113	
114	The preview offers the normal managed choices but no dirty commit/discard, WIP,
115	shared-writer, ownership takeover, or unknown-runtime acknowledgement. Blocked
116	plans point to the compatible CLI fallback instead of adding a force path.
117	`r` reads local state only; `R` explicitly plans fetch, portable review query, or
118	both. Remote evidence is run-local and limited to named refs plus review
119	existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time—not checks or review decisions.
120	
121	**A machine should hold roughly three to seven hot tasks.** That is a
122	cognitive limit, not a technical one. Everything else belongs in `dev ls`.
123	
124	## Parking
125	
126	```bash
127	dev park --next "reproduce the token refresh race, then add a regression test"
128	```
129	
130	This is the move the whole design exists to make safe. It records what to do
131	next and leaves the checkout boundary exactly where it is. An external caller
132	may close an eligible runtime; when park is invoked from inside its own runtime,
133	it records WARM but deliberately leaves that runtime alive so the agent can exit
134	normally. In direct mode the boundary is the current branch; in worktree mode it
135	is the branch and linked checkout.
136	
137	`--next` is the important part. Without it, resuming means re-deriving where
138	you were from a diff, which is most of the cost of a context switch. Always
139	supply one.
140	
141	Before finishing agent work, run `dev prepare` with the exact session UUID and
142	exit normally. The post-writer finalizer—not the still-running agent—stages and
143	commits the exact transcript/plan. A settled Herdr `done` state is not evidence
144	that history, review or commits are complete.
145	
146	Useful variations:
147	
148	```bash
149	dev park --wip                    # checkpoint uncommitted work first
150	dev park --cold --push            # close session, push, remove worktree
151	dev park --keep-session           # warm only: record state, keep session
152	```
153	
154	`--cold --keep-session` is rejected because a runtime must not remain pointed at
155	a checkout that cold parking removes. A verified runtime-close failure likewise
156	stops cold cleanup before deleting the checkout; warm park reports the close
157	failure and keeps the recorded handle for reconciliation.
158	
159	## Checkpoint commits, not stashes
160	
161	`--wip` makes a `wip: checkpoint — <next>` commit rather than a `git stash`.
162	
163	A stash is invisible in the log, easy to forget, and **cannot be pushed** — so
164	it can never reach another machine. That last point is decisive: the whole
165	value of parking is that the work is recoverable from anywhere.
166	
167	Messy WIP commits on a feature branch are fine. Branch history is *construction
168	history*; the base branch's history is *product history*. They do not have to
169	match — clean the branch up at the integration boundary with an interactive
170	rebase, or squash it, and decide then.
171	
172	## Cold, and why it is safe
173	
174	Going cold removes the checkout. That feels lossy, and is not, because:
175	
176	- the branch still holds every commit;
177	- `dev park --cold` refuses unless the branch is pushed, so the remote holds
178	  them too;
179	- `dev resume` rebuilds the worktree from `origin/<branch>`.
180	
181	Resume rebuilds/reopens checkout and runtime state only. Persisted runtime
182	handles carry their backend name and are validated against live checkout
183	coverage; stale/missing handles reopen instead of making a task falsely HOT.
184	Production `dev` does not currently attach a Claude/Codex conversation; an agent
185	handoff must supply explicit session/launcher arguments.
186	
187	The directory is a cache. The branch is the identity. Once that is true, a
188	local filesystem stops being a graveyard of half-finished checkouts.
189	
190	## Moving work between machines
191	
192	The remote is the handoff boundary. Do not sync worktrees, runtime state, or
193	the multiplexer's database between machines — sync branches.
194	
195	On the machine holding the work:
196	
197	```bash
198	dev park --cold --push
199	```
200	
201	On the machine picking it up:
202	
203	```bash
204	dev resume <task> --fetch
205	```
206	
207	**One writer per branch at a time.** `dev` records an `owner` host and refuses
208	to resume a task owned by another machine without `--force`. Two machines
209	committing to one branch is the only reliable way to make this workflow produce
210	a conflict; the ownership check is what prevents it.
211	
212	If two machines genuinely need to work the same feature at once, split the
213	branch — `feat/auth-ui` and `feat/auth-api` — and integrate afterwards. That is
214	the same rule as for parallel agents: parallel writers get parallel branches.
215	
216	The task registry itself (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/dev/tasks/`) is one small TOML file
217	per task, specifically so it can live in a private git repo and merge cleanly
218	across machines. Point `paths.state_dir` at one if you want a shared view.
219	
220	## Sweeping
221	
222	```bash
223	dev sweep            # report only
224	dev sweep --apply    # act, confirming each change
225	dev sweep --merged-worktrees  # from main, include untracked contained worktrees
226	```
227	
228	`sweep` reports two kinds of problem:
229	
230	- **Drift** — a task marked hot with no live session, a warm task with one, a
231	  recorded worktree git no longer knows about, or a branch-backed task whose
232	  branch git no longer has. That last one is dead rather than drifted: `done`,
233	  `resume` and `retire` all resolve the branch first, so the record is offered
234	  for reaping instead of repair.
235	- **Staleness** — a warm task nobody has touched in two weeks, clean and
236	  pushed, that could go cold.
237	
238	It also lists **live sessions no task claims** — the other half of a crowded
239	sidebar, and usually the larger half.
240	
241	From the canonical default-branch checkout, `--merged-worktrees` switches to a
242	focused audit of tracked and unmanaged linked worktrees whose named branches are
243	already contained in main. It suppresses unrelated stale-task/session noise so
244	the result can be presented directly for cleanup approval. Dirty trees, active
245	Git operations, pending artifact
246	intents, active/mixed runtimes, detached heads and unmerged branches are
247	reported as blockers. Safe candidates still require `--apply` and individual
248	confirmation; `--delete-branches` is a separate opt-in.
249	
250	`dev sweep --base <ref>` also forwards the selected base to DONE task retirement;
251	`--merged-worktrees` uses its verified base for managed tasks as well as unmanaged
252	checkouts. Reviewed retire/remove plans bind worktree-list authority only to the
253	same branch or paths equal to, containing, or nested under the target. Removing
254	an unrelated sibling no longer invalidates the rest of an approved
255	`--apply --yes` batch. A same-branch checkout or target lock/HEAD change still
256	makes the plan stale; containment and all other guards remain required.
257	
258	Agent workflow: show the report to the user as a concrete QA prompt, naming the
259	exact candidate paths and whether branches would be retained. Only after the
260	user approves that set may the agent add `--apply --yes`.
261	
262	`sweep` never deletes uncommitted work, and never acts without `--apply`. DONE
263	tasks with runtime/worktree resources are reported as cleanup pending and routed
264	through the same external-only retirement safety service; their records are not
265	reaped first.
266	
267	The dashboard does not silently reconcile these states. A normal COLD worktree
268	task points to explicit `dev resume`. A task whose recorded worktree is missing
269	or no longer registered points to `dev sweep`; generic Enter refuses to open
270	either the canonical checkout or an artifact-only directory. If sweep reports
271	unique agent artifacts, salvage them before approving a resume/reap action.
272	
273	## Integration
274	
275	```bash
276	dev done --ff     # rebase onto the base, then fast-forward it
277	dev done --pr     # push and open a pull/merge request via the detected forge CLI
278	dev done          # TTY: inspect commits/dirty content and choose interactively
279	```
280	
281	Which one depends on a single question: **are this branch's commits worth
282	keeping in the base's history?**
283	
284	- Yes → `--ff`. Linear history, no merge commit, `git bisect` and `git blame`
285	  stay legible.
286	- No, it is WIP noise → squash at the integration point.
287	- Someone (or CI) should look first → `--pr`.
288	
289	On a TTY, `dev done` reports branch ahead/behind plus which staged, unstaged and
290	untracked paths are already equivalent to the base. It can commit all changes,
291	discard all changes, or cancel before choosing FF/PR. Unique content requires
292	typing `DROP`; scripts use `--dirty=commit --message ...` or the deliberately
293	destructive `--dirty=discard --yes`. Ignored files are never discarded. If an
294	active writer changes the checkout during confirmation or immediately after a
295	commit, integration stops and the command must be rerun after that writer exits.
296	
297	After a bare interactive managed-worktree completion reaches MERGED, the
298	wizard previews covering runtime panes and agents. It can keep everything,
299	retire while preserving the branch, or retire and delete the contained branch.
300	Caller-owned Herdr workspaces are handed to a freshly created external
301	coordinator; unknown status needs explicit approval and active/mixed sessions
302	remain blockers.
303	
304	Before integration, the TTY wizard can select exact idle/done task-worktree
305	agent panes for closure only under the final guarded Apply. Parent/canonical
306	agents remain open and block FF; recheck, choose PR, or cancel. Foreground
307	non-agent programs require separate consent to changing files while they run.
308	Interactive retirement separately requires `CLOSE <workspace-id>` to terminate
309	known programs. Background jobs are unobserved. See `agent-retirement.md`. If FF is blocked by dirty
310	canonical-checkout bytes, it lists the paths and offers PR, typed `DROP`
311	discard, exact stash+restore, or cancel. Agent artifacts are labeled.
312	Stash+restore preserves staged, unstaged, and non-ignored untracked state under
313	an exact OID, restores the index/worktree after fast-forward, and drops only
314	that matching stash entry. A conflict retains the stash and task with an exact
315	recovery command. Dirty submodules and nested repositories remain blockers.
316	The discard is a separate explicit taskflow effect and no unrelated canonical
317	bytes are committed automatically.
318	
319	For branch/worktree tasks, non-interactive `dev done` without an integration
320	mode remains report-only. Direct tasks still finish without one. Conflicted
321	checkouts always require manual resolution.
322	
323	Explicit `--ff` integrates and records DONE/MERGED while retaining the worktree
324	and branch for `dev retire`. Any explicitly selected task agent pane closures
325	are recorded in the result ledger; no parent pane is closed. `--pr` only publishes and
326	opens review; after a commit-preserving external merge use
327	`dev done --merged --base-ref <ref>`. Squash requires explicit
328	`--confirm-squash <commit>` attestation. `--delete-branch` and `--keep-worktree`
329	are deprecated on `done`: the branch is deleted only by
330	`dev retire --delete-branch`, and only when git agrees it is fully contained in
331	the base. "Merged" is not always "finished", so branches survive by default.
332	
333	`dev retire --base <ref>` overrides the containment target, resolving a local
334	branch, then remote-tracking ref (for example `origin/main`), then commit. Apply
335	re-resolves that input; a changed kind/ref/OID makes the plan stale. A recorded
336	fork-point commit stays the base, not the default branch; when it cannot prove
337	integration, pass `--base <branch>` explicitly. `done --merged --base-ref X`
338	carries X into the cleanup hint, wizard and external coordinator handoff.
339	`--delete-branch` still uses Git's upstream/HEAD merged check via `branch -d`, so
340	a non-HEAD base can yield partial completion with the branch and DONE task kept.
341	
342	Cleanup is never inferred from agent lifecycle state. A user must select it in
343	the post-MERGED wizard or run `dev retire` from a different checkout/runtime;
344	both paths revalidate, close eligible sessions, wait for release, and remove
345	without force. Read `agent-retirement.md` before retiring an agent-owned checkout.
346	
347	Dashboard row actions now invoke these same finish/resume/retire workflows. Missing checkout recovery is scoped with `dev sweep --task <id>`. See [dashboard actions](dashboard-actions.md).
348

1	---
2	description: Retire an integrated dev-cli worktree and runtime safely, from outside the workspace being removed.
3	authority: project

5	verified_on: 2026-09-17

7	
8	# Agent-safe retirement
9	
10	Submodule workspaces still require explicit `--recursive` approval for
11	linked-worktree removal. Initialized child clones require fresh remote recovery
12	proof and leave before the outer worktree. A child whose path is absent or truly
13	empty, with no retained Git store and no ownership/observation blockers, can
14	instead be proved empty locally; no initialization, download or remote proof is
15	needed merely for its removal. Canonical/shared Git and the outer branch remain.
16	
17	Only exact reviewed empty modules admin scaffolding may be pruned under locks,
18	with directory identity and emptiness rechecked immediately before native
19	directory-only removal. Empty checkout directories stay for non-force Git
20	removal. Partial pruning failure is not RETIRED; mixed workspaces retain real-store
21	journals and rollback. See [Submodule workspaces](submodule-workspaces.md).
22	
23	Recursive cleanup preserves the version-2 coordinator's caller and foreground-program consent checks. Child graph, workspace intent and artifact ownership remain bound to the approved preview; changed child refs or state require a new preview before runtime closure or removal.
24	
25	A `dev` change stream reaches full retirement only after an external caller closes its runtime and removes its worktree — a feature agent must never destroy the checkout or runtime containing its own process.
26	
27	## Three milestones, not one
28	
29	Completion is three separate milestones, and the persisted task state `done` now means the middle one, not the last:
30	
31	```text
32	READY     exact transcript preserved in its chosen destination after writer exit
33	MERGED    branch integrated; runtime/worktree may still exist
34	RETIRED   runtime absent, worktree removed, optional branch deleted, task reaped
35	```
36	
37	`hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done` remain the only persisted task states — `done` means MERGED, with cleanup possibly still pending. It does **not** mean the runtime or worktree has already been deleted.
38	
39	## Commands
40	
41	| Command | What it does |
42	|---|---|
43	| `dev prepare --session <provider:uuid> --plan <path>` | Arms post-writer artifact finalization without closing the running agent. Product changes must already be committed; the transcript itself is deliberately not staged yet. |
44	| `dev artifact finalize --run-id "$DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID" --if-pending --writer-stopped` | Preserves the exact stable transcript in the intent's source-commit or external-archive destination after its writer stops. `--if-pending` no-ops silently when no armed intent matches the run id; `--writer-stopped` confirms the outer wrapper has returned. |
45	| `dev done --ff` | Rebases the task branch onto its base and fast-forwards it locally. Records MERGED and retains worktree/branch; explicitly selected task-pane closures are reported separately. |
46	| `dev done --pr` | Pushes the branch and opens a pull/merge request through an available forge CLI. The task stays under review, not MERGED. |
47	| `dev done --merged --base-ref <ref>` | Verifies an externally merged branch is contained in `<ref>` and records MERGED. |
48	| `dev done --merged --base-ref <ref> --confirm-squash <merge-commit>` | Same, but for a squash merge: attests that the named commit, already proven contained in `<ref>`, represents the feature branch. This is an operator assertion dev cannot verify on its own. |
49	| `dev artifact discard <intent> --yes` | Records that an intent can never be finalized — its transcript was never written, or its HEAD is gone after a rebase — so it stops blocking integration and retirement. It commits and recovers nothing, prints exactly what is being abandoned, and refuses an intent that is still `armed`, because finalization is the path that preserves a transcript. |
50	| `dev retire [task-or-worktree] [--base <ref>] [--close-unknown] [--assume-no-runtime] [--delete-branch] [--timeout <duration>]` | Re-resolves every covering runtime session, refuses active agents and mixed-purpose workspaces, waits for closure, revalidates Git state, and only then removes the linked worktree without force. Deletes the task record only after every requested step succeeds. |
51	| `dev flow [repo]` | Preview UI for an exact DONE task: Enter builds a revision-bound Retire plan, then approval applies it. Branch deletion requires the displayed typed token. |
52	| `dev sweep --merged-worktrees [--base <ref>] [--apply] [--yes] [--close-unknown] [--assume-no-runtime] [--delete-branches]` | From the canonical checkout, reports (and, with `--apply`, retires) both task-tracked and unmanaged linked worktrees whose branches are already contained in the base. |
53	| `dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees [--stale-days <n>] [--json]` | From a canonical non-bare checkout, emits a strict Claude Workflow V1 report; JSON schema 1 is report-only. |
54	| `dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply [--delete-branches --base <ref>]` | Requires a TTY and per-item confirmation, then revalidates each approved fingerprint under the common-dir cleanup lock before plain non-force removal. |
55	
56	A dirty checkout does not fail here: `dev done` classifies it against the base
57	first, offering commit or discard interactively, or taking an explicit
58	`--dirty` policy from a script. See
59	[Change-stream workflow](change-stream-workflow.md) for that wizard. The
60	`--keep-worktree` flag on `dev done` warns as a no-op; `--delete-branch`
61	fails and points at `dev retire --delete-branch`.
62	
63	If fast-forward is blocked by unrelated dirty bytes in the canonical checkout,
64	the interactive wizard can preserve them with an exact stash+restore
65	transaction. It restores staged state and untracked files after integration;
66	dirty submodules and nested repositories still require independent handling.
67	
68	After a bare interactive `dev done` reaches MERGED, its cleanup step performs
69	a read-only retirement preview and asks whether to keep, retire, or retire and
70	delete the contained branch. Covering Herdr panes and recognized agent states
71	are shown before approval. Caller-owned Herdr workspaces use a fresh exact-pane
72	external coordinator; working/blocked/waiting agents and mixed workspaces are
73	never overridden.
74	
75	For a read-only explanation before acting, render or open the generic
76	`workspace-closeout` recipe from the exact checkout:
77	
78	```bash
79	dev prompt render workspace-closeout .
80	dev prompt open workspace-closeout . --agent my-agent
81	```
82	
83	The recipe includes the full retirement audit, but its result is advisory.
84	`eligible` and a merged PR never authorize cleanup; an external `dev retire`
85	still recollects and revalidates every gate. If `dev done --ff` or

222	
223	Current-provider ownership is not proved by path continuity. Apply additionally
224	requires provider-observed branch, HEAD, common-dir, and an opaque non-replayable
225	registration generation matching the live registry. Claude Code 2.1.259 records
226	none of those Git identity facts, so current Claude claims report
227	`provider-git-identity: unknown` and remain report-only even when `--apply` is
228	requested. This prevents stale terminal metadata from attaching to a replacement
229	checkout at the same path. A path, branch convention, or reusable GitDir pathname
230	must never be treated as the missing generation.
231	
232	The independent safety audit also requires a present, registered, non-main,
233	named, unlocked, non-prunable linked worktree with exact common-dir, live branch,
234	registry HEAD, and live HEAD agreement. Staged, unstaged, conflicted, untracked,
235	ignored, or recursively inspected submodule content blocks cleanup, as do Git
236	operations, task claims, unsafe artifact intents, caller containment, unknown
237	runtime inventory, or any covering runtime. Missing, prunable, unregistered, and
238	orphan paths remain report only.
239	
240	JSON schema 1 contains only normalized identity/state/time, Git/path/branch/HEAD
241	facts, checks, actions, diagnostics, fingerprints, and counts. It is report-only.
242	Apply rejects `--yes`, `--close-unknown`, `--assume-no-runtime`, `--no-runtime`,
243	and JSON; it requires a terminal and confirms each item. Under a common-dir
244	cleanup lock it rediscovers the repository and recollects provider, Git, task,
245	artifact, runtime, and caller proof immediately before each removal. A changed
246	fingerprint is `skipped-changed`.
247	
248	Removal uses plain `git worktree remove` without force and verifies both path and
249	registration are gone. It never closes sessions, prunes, deletes Claude metadata,
250	or rescues/stashes/commits dirty work. The named branch survives by default, so
251	unique commits remain recoverable. Optional deletion separately requires
252	`--delete-branches --base <ref>`, unchanged base/branch tips, containment, zero
253	unique commits, and ordinary `git branch -d`; any failure after removal keeps the
254	branch and reports partial completion.
255	
256	## Safety boundaries
257	
258	Raw `git worktree remove --force` and configured external tools bypass dev entirely — never run them from an agent that occupies the target. dev's guarantee is only for dev-mediated paths; it cannot stop an operator or script from calling Git directly.
259	
260	Normal task-backed retirement and the exact unmanaged path form of `dev retire`
261	use `internal/taskflow`; the latter requires contained removal. Some `sweep`
262	record-only/orphan-salvage actions remain outside taskflow. Existing
263	CLI acknowledgement flags remain compatible; the flow preview intentionally
264	offers none of them.
265	
266	A real Codex session once deleted its own registered worktree and branch from another checkout. Herdr kept the workspace and terminal alive because a Unix process can hold an open cwd inode after the path is unlinked, and SpecStory then recreated the same path containing only `.specstory/` content. The shell looked alive but was no longer a Git checkout:
267	
268	```text
269	failed to reload config: No such file or directory
270	fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
271	```
272	
273	Treat `runtime alive + Git registration absent + artifact-only path` as an orphan that needs transcript salvage and external reconciliation — **never** as RETIRED.
274	
275	`dev sweep` now recognises that shape rather than leaving it to be spotted by eye. When a task records a checkout that exists but Git does not register, and the directory holds nothing but agent artifact folders, sweep reports it as an abandoned agent workspace. It offers to remove it only when every file inside is byte-identical to one the repository already has; anything that differs is listed as salvage work and left untouched, including by `--apply`.
276	
277	Byte equality rather than mere presence is the point. A transcript writer that outlives its worktree usually flushes a longer final version than the copy committed earlier, so a same-named file in the repository is not evidence that the tail was saved.
278

9	# Agent-safe retirement
10	
11	Submodule 工作區移除 linked worktree 仍需明確 `--recursive` 核准。已初始化
12	的子 clone 須取得當次遠端恢復證明，先處理內層，再移除外層。只有子路徑不存在
13	或真正為空、沒有保留的 Git store，且通過所有權／觀測檢查時，才可改由本地
14	證明為空，不必僅為移除而初始化、下載或取得遠端證明。Canonical／共享 Git
15	與外層分支保留。
16	
17	只可在鎖內修剪精確審閱的空 modules 管理目錄；native directory-only removal
18	前立即重新驗證目錄身分與空狀態。空 checkout 目錄留給不帶 force 的 Git 移除。
19	修剪部分失敗不算 RETIRED；混合工作區中的真實 Git store 仍保有 journal 與
20	rollback。見 [Submodule 工作區](submodule-workspaces.md)。
21	
22	遞迴清理保留 version-2 coordinator 對 caller 與前景程序關閉授權的檢查。子模組結構、工作區意圖與 artifact 歸屬都綁定核准時的預覽；子模組 refs 或狀態改變後，必須重新預覽，才能關閉 runtime 或移除 checkout。
23	
24	!!! note "術語規則"
25	    有公認中文譯名且本文使用中文時，首次以「中文 (English original)」呈現。產品名稱與 Git／CLI／agent domain terms 可直接保留英文；沒有公認譯名不得自創。程式碼、API／tool 名稱、CLI flag、套件名與路徑一律不翻譯。
26	
27	一條 `dev` change stream 只有在外部呼叫者關閉其 runtime、移除其 worktree 之後，才算真正完成 retirement——feature agent 絕不能自行摧毀自己所在的 checkout 或 runtime。

29	## 三個里程碑，不是一個
30	
31	Completion 分成三個獨立里程碑，且目前 persisted task state 的 `done` 對應的是中間那個，不是最後一個：
32	
33	```text
34	READY     writer 離開後，exact transcript 保存到選定目的地
35	MERGED    branch 已整合；runtime/worktree 可能仍存在
36	RETIRED   runtime 已消失、worktree 已移除、可選擇刪除 branch、task 已 reap
37	```
38	
39	`hot`、`warm`、`cold`、`done` 仍是唯一的 persisted task state——`done` 代表 MERGED，cleanup 可能仍待執行，**不代表** runtime 或 worktree 已經被刪除。
40	
41	## 命令
42	
43	| 命令 | 作用 |
44	|---|---|
45	| `dev prepare --session <provider:uuid> --plan <path>` | 在不關閉目前執行中 agent 的情況下，arm post-writer artifact finalization。Product changes 必須已先 commit；transcript 本身刻意尚未 stage。 |
46	| `dev artifact finalize --run-id "$DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID" --if-pending --writer-stopped` | 在 writer 停止後，把 exact、stable transcript 存進 intent 選定的 source commit 或外部 archive。`--if-pending` 在沒有對應 armed intent 時靜默 no-op；`--writer-stopped` 確認外層 wrapper 已 return。 |
47	| `dev done --ff` | 把 task branch rebase 到其 base 上並在本機 fast-forward。記錄為 MERGED，保留 worktree/branch；明確選定的 task pane 關閉另行記錄，parent 保留。 |
48	| `dev done --pr` | Push branch，並透過可用的 forge CLI 開啟 pull/merge request。Task 保持在 review 狀態，不是 MERGED。 |
49	| `dev done --merged --base-ref <ref>` | 驗證某個已在外部 merge 的 branch 是否被 `<ref>` 包含，並記錄為 MERGED。 |
50	| `dev done --merged --base-ref <ref> --confirm-squash <merge-commit>` | 同上，但用於 squash merge：attest（斷言）已證明被 `<ref>` 包含的該 commit 代表這條 feature branch。這是 dev 無法自行驗證的 operator assertion。 |
51	| `dev flow [repo]` | 在獨立 TTY preview 中顯示 DONE row 的 Retire (Keep Branch) 或 typed Retire + Delete Contained Branch plan；Enter 只規劃，第二次 approval 才套用。 |
52	| `dev artifact discard <intent> --yes` | 記錄某個 intent 永遠無法 finalize——transcript 從未被寫出，或 rebase 之後 HEAD 已不存在——使它不再阻擋 integration 與 retirement。它不會 commit 也不會復原任何東西，會先印出確切將被放棄的內容，並拒絕仍為 `armed` 的 intent，因為 finalize 才是保存 transcript 的路徑。 |
53	| `dev retire [task-or-worktree] [--base <ref>] [--close-unknown] [--assume-no-runtime] [--delete-branch] [--timeout <duration>]` | 重新解析每一個 covering runtime session，拒絕 active agent 與 mixed-purpose workspace，等待其關閉，重新驗證 Git state，才移除 linked worktree（不使用 force）。只有在所有要求的步驟都成功後，才刪除 task record。 |
54	| `dev sweep --merged-worktrees [--base <ref>] [--apply] [--yes] [--close-unknown] [--assume-no-runtime] [--delete-branches]` | 從 canonical checkout 執行，回報（加上 `--apply` 時則 retire）branch 已被 base 包含的 task-tracked 與 unmanaged linked worktree。 |
55	| `dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees [--stale-days <n>] [--json]` | 從 canonical non-bare checkout 產生 strict Claude Workflow V1 report；JSON schema 1 僅供 report。 |
56	| `dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply [--delete-branches --base <ref>]` | 要求 TTY 與逐項 confirmation，接著在 common-dir cleanup lock 下重新驗證每個已核可 fingerprint，才用 plain non-force removal。 |
57	
58	Dirty checkout 在這裡不會直接失敗：`dev done` 會先把它與 base 比對分類，在
59	interactive 時提供 commit 或 discard，在 script 中則接受明確的 `--dirty`
60	policy。該 wizard 詳見[變更流工作流程](change-stream-workflow.zh-TW.md)。
61	`dev done` 上的 `--keep-worktree` 以 no-op 警告；`--delete-branch` 則報錯並
62	指向 `dev retire --delete-branch`。
63	
64	若 fast-forward 只被 canonical checkout 中無關的 dirty bytes 阻擋，互動式
65	wizard 可用 exact stash+restore 保存它們，並在 integration 後恢復 staged state

68	Bare interactive `dev done` 到達 MERGED 後，cleanup step 會先做 read-only
69	retirement preview，再詢問保留、retire，或 retire 並刪除 contained branch。
70	核可前會列出 covering Herdr panes 與 recognized agent 狀態；caller-owned Herdr
71	workspace 改由 fresh exact-pane external coordinator 處理。Working、blocked、
72	waiting agent 與 mixed workspace 永遠不能被 override。

74	## Flow 中的 DONE 與 Retire
75	
76	`dev flow` 把 persisted `DONE` intent 與 live cleanup evidence 分開。DONE/MERGED row 仍可顯示 runtime、worktree、branch 與 task record；只有 Retire result 完成最後的 CAS task deletion 才是 RETIRED。UNMANAGED row 使用的是永遠保留 branch 的 Remove Checkout，不會製造 DONE/RETIRED task milestone；canonical 與 harness row 不能 Remove Checkout。
77	
78	Flow TUI 沒有 `--close-unknown`、`--assume-no-runtime`、dirty discard 或 generic force。`runtime=none` 會保留「session/agent unobserved」，不冒充已證明 closed。需要 expert acknowledgement 時，離開 Flow 並明確執行 plan 顯示的 fallback CLI，再接受該 command 自己的 guards。完整 row/action matrix 見 [Repository Flow 預覽](repository-flow.zh-TW.md)。
79	
80	Action 前若需要 read-only explanation，從 exact checkout render 或 open generic
81	`workspace-closeout` recipe：
82	
83	```bash
84	dev prompt render workspace-closeout .
85	dev prompt open workspace-closeout . --agent my-agent
86	```
87	
88	Recipe 內含完整 retirement audit，但結果只是 advisory。`eligible` 與 merged PR 都不
89	授權 cleanup；外部 `dev retire` 仍會重新收集並驗證所有 gate。若 `dev done --ff` 或
90	`dev git pull-rebase` 停在 conflict，只用 `prompt open` 討論 semantic resolution，
91	接著明確 continue/abort Git，再重新執行 lifecycle command。詳見
92	[Prompt handoff](prompt-handoffs.zh-TW.md)。
93	
94	## 一般 local flow
95	
96	在 feature worktree 中：
97	
98	```bash
99	# 先 commit product changes，不要 stage 仍在變動中的 transcript。
100	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid> --plan .claude/plans/task.md
101	# 正常結束 agent，讓 SpecStory 寫出最終 Markdown。
102	```
103	
104	外層 `specstory run` wrapper 接著呼叫：
105	
106	```bash
107	dev artifact finalize --run-id "$DEV_AGENT_RUN_ID" --if-pending --writer-stopped
108	```
109	
110	外部的 main/integration workspace 完成剩下的工作：
111	
112	```bash
113	dev done <task> --ff
114	dev retire <task> --delete-branch
115	```
116	
117	`dev done` 只負責整合並記錄為 MERGED。`dev retire` 會重新解析每個 runtime pane、關閉符合條件的 session、等待它們消失、重新驗證 Git，再移除 worktree（不使用 force）。
118	
119	## 選擇 containment base
120	
121	`dev retire --base <ref>` 可覆寫 DONE task 或 linked worktree 的整合驗證目標，不會
122	改寫 task 記錄的意圖。解析依序檢查本機分支（`refs/heads/X`）、remote-tracking
123	分支（`refs/remotes/X`，例如 `origin/main`），最後才是 commit。完整分支 ref
124	維持指名的類型。Apply 重新解析同一輸入，要求類型、ref 與 commit OID 完全一致；
125	base 移動或新增同名分支都會使已審閱 plan 過期。Remote-tracking ref 是本機觀測，
126	不會暗中 fetch。
127	
128	未指定 override 時，task retirement 沿用記錄的 base。記錄為 fork-point commit
129	時，絕不暗中改用預設分支；若無法證明整合，仍會阻擋並提示 `pass --base <branch>`。
130	`dev done --merged --base-ref X` 會將 X 帶入 cleanup 提示、wizard 與外部
131	coordinator，對應命令是 `dev retire --base X <task>`。若 shell handoff 無法攜帶
132	該 override，dev 會改為列出從外部執行的命令。
133	
134	可選的 `--delete-branch` 仍執行一般 `git branch -d`；Git 自己的 merged 檢查使用
135	分支的 upstream 或 HEAD，不是 `--base`。因此對非 HEAD base 清理時，可能已移除
136	worktree 卻無法刪除分支；分支與 DONE task 會保留，結果回報部分完成。
137	
138	## Pull-request 流程
139	
140	```bash
141	dev done <task> --pr
142	# CI/review 完成，且以保留 commit 的方式 merge 之後
143	git fetch origin
144	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main
145	dev retire --base origin/main <task> --delete-branch
146	```
147	
148	Squash merge 並不等同於 ancestry-equivalent，因此需要明確的 operator attestation：
149	
150	```bash
151	dev done <task> --merged --base-ref origin/main --confirm-squash <merge-commit>
152	```
153	
154	這只證明所指名的 squash commit 被包含在 base 中；operator 是在斷言它確實代表這條 feature branch。
155	Squash 後 tree 相同不是 ancestry 證明，也不會免除 retirement 的 containment
156	檢查。
157	
158	## 拒絕條件
159	
160	只要符合以下任一條件，`retire.Inspect` 就會拒絕繼續執行；且它會在關閉 session 後重新檢查，而不是信任過期的視圖：
161	
162	- 呼叫者目前所在目錄就是 target checkout 或其下層；
163	- 呼叫者的 `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`、`HERDR_PANE_ID` 或 `TMUX_PANE` 對應到一個涵蓋 target 的 runtime session；
164	- 某個涵蓋 target 的 runtime workspace 同時也包含 target 以外的 pane（mixed-purpose workspace）；
165	- 任何涵蓋中的 agent status 為 `working`、`running`、`busy`、`blocked` 或 `waiting`——**任何 flag 都無法 override**；
166	- Agent status 為空或 `unknown`，**除非**呼叫者從 target 外部傳入 `--close-unknown`；
167	- Agent status 無法辨識（不在已知集合內）——一律阻擋；
168	- Runtime enumeration 本身失敗，**除非**呼叫者傳入 `--assume-no-runtime`。
169	
170	`--close-unknown` 與 `--assume-no-runtime` 只放寬 fail-closed 的*觀測結果*（無法讀取的 status、無法列舉的 runtime list）。這兩個 flag 都絕不會 bypass caller containment 或 active-agent state。`retirement.Service.Retire` 在 runtime session 關閉後，也會重新驗證 target identity、Git ancestry、進行中的 Git operation（`gitx.InProgress`，檢查 `MERGE_HEAD`、`CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`、`REVERT_HEAD`、`BISECT_LOG`、`rebase-merge`、`rebase-apply`、`sequencer`；不含 `REBASE_HEAD`，因為 Git 在 rebase 完成後仍會保留它）以及 worktree 是否 clean——因為 runtime draining 期間現實可能已改變，先前的驗證結果不會跨越這個邊界沿用。
171	
172	Taskflow Apply 也不信任畫面時的 snapshot：它鎖定 canonical repository/task store、重新讀取 task revision 與 authority fingerprint，並在 runtime closure、worktree removal、optional branch deletion 與最後 task reap 前逐段 revalidate。Result ledger 依序保留 `ATTEMPTED`/`COMPLETED`/`FAILED`；若前段 cleanup 已完成而後段失敗，會回報 partial success 與 recovery，而不宣稱 rollback。
173	
174	## 用 sweep 做定期 cleanup
175	
176	```bash
177	dev sweep --merged-worktrees
178	# 把確切的 candidates/blockers 呈現給使用者，並徵求核可。
179	dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply --yes
180	```
181	
182	這會同時列出 task-tracked 的 DONE worktree，以及 named branch 已被 base 包含的 unmanaged linked worktree——請從 canonical checkout 執行。它會先回報再套用：containment 本身絕不等於許可。Dirty 的 Git state、pending 或無法到達的 artifact、locked 或 prunable 的 worktree registration、進行中的 Git operation，以及與 `dev retire` 相同的 runtime 拒絕條件，都仍會阻擋 cleanup。Retirement 完成後預設保留 branch；只有在使用者另外核可刪除時，才加上 `--delete-branches`。
183	
184	`dev sweep --base <ref>` 也會把選定 base 傳入 DONE task retirement；
185	`--merged-worktrees` 對 managed task 與 unmanaged checkout 都使用已驗證的 base。
186	已審閱 retire／remove plan 的 worktree-list authority 只涵蓋同分支，或路徑與
187	目標相同、包含目標、位於目標之下的 worktree。先移除無關的 sibling 不再使
188	`--apply --yes` 批次剩餘項目過期；同分支新增 checkout 或目標 lock／HEAD 改變
189	仍會使 plan 過期。Containment 與其他安全檢查仍不可省略。
190	
191	### 經驗證的 Claude Workflow ephemeral cleanup
192	
193	Claude Workflow 的 turn-scoped worktree 使用另一條 strict V1 路徑：
194	
195	```bash
196	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --stale-days 14
197	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --json
198	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply
199	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply --delete-branches --base main
200	```
201	
202	此 command 只能從 canonical non-bare checkout 執行。Bounded、fixed-depth adapter
203	只讀取 `~/.claude/projects` 下的 private metadata，驗證 workflow/agent ID、exact
204	canonical worktree mapping、`spawnedWithWorktree`、`isolation=worktree` 與 matching
205	journal linkage；絕不 decode 或輸出 prompt、script、log、result body 或 transcript
206	content。Unknown add-only fields 可接受；required type 錯誤、path mismatch、duplicate
207	claim、不安全／symlink／reparse／group-or-world-writable metadata、讀取中 mutation、
208	bound exhaustion，以及 future/conflicting/unparseable time 都會 fail closed。
209	
210	V1 terminal liveness 要求 workflow 為 `completed|killed`、matching agent 為 `done`、
211	journal 同時有一筆 `started` 與 `result`，且不存在 same-ID resumed transcript。
212	Killed 但沒有 result、progress，或已 resume 的狀態無論多舊都維持 `unknown`；沒有
213	attestation bypass。`--stale-days` 衡量 provider inactivity，預設 14，最小 1。
214	
215	Path continuity 無法證明 current-provider ownership。Apply 另外要求 provider-observed
216	branch、HEAD、common-dir 與 opaque non-replayable registration generation 都和 live
217	registry 一致。Claude Code 2.1.259 不會記錄這些 Git identity facts，因此目前 Claude
218	claim 會回報 `provider-git-identity: unknown`，即使要求 `--apply` 也只供 report。
219	這可防止 stale terminal metadata 綁到同一路徑的 replacement checkout。Path、branch
220	convention 或可重用的 GitDir pathname 都不能取代缺少的 generation。
221	
222	獨立 safety audit 還要求 worktree present、registered、non-main、named、unlocked、
223	non-prunable，並且 common-dir、live branch、registry HEAD、live HEAD 完全一致。
224	Staged、unstaged、conflicted、untracked、ignored 或 recursively inspected submodule
225	content 都會阻擋；Git operation、task claim、不安全 artifact intent、caller
226	containment、unknown runtime inventory 或任何 covering runtime 也會阻擋。Missing、
227	prunable、unregistered 與 orphan path 僅供 report。
228	
229	JSON schema 1 只包含 normalized identity/state/time、Git/path/branch/HEAD facts、
230	checks、actions、diagnostics、fingerprints 與 counts，且只供 report。Apply 拒絕
231	`--yes`、`--close-unknown`、`--assume-no-runtime`、`--no-runtime` 與 JSON；它要求
232	terminal 並逐項確認。在 common-dir cleanup lock 下，每次 remove 前都會重新 discover
233	repository，並重新收集 provider、Git、task、artifact、runtime 與 caller proof；
234	fingerprint 改變時回報 `skipped-changed`。
235	
236	Removal 使用 plain `git worktree remove`、不加 force，並驗證 path 與 registration 都已
237	消失。它不會關閉 session、prune、刪除 Claude metadata，或 rescue/stash/commit dirty
238	work。Named branch 預設保留，因此 unique commits 仍可復原。Optional deletion 另外要求
239	`--delete-branches --base <ref>`、unchanged base/branch tips、containment、zero unique
240	commits 與 ordinary `git branch -d`；remove 後任何 failure 都會保留 branch，並回報
241	partial completion。
242	
243	## 安全邊界
244	
245	原始的 `git worktree remove --force` 會完全繞過 dev——絕不要在佔用 target 的 agent 中執行它。dev 的保證僅止於：沒有任何 dev-mediated 路徑會執行 forced removal；它無法阻止 operator 或 script 直接呼叫 Git。Bare dashboard 的 configured `[[tui.tools]]` command 同樣是任意 external-tool escape boundary，不會繼承 Flow 的 PlanID、conditions、ledger 或 revalidation。
246	
247	一般 task-backed retirement 與 exact unmanaged path 形式的 `dev retire` 都使用 `internal/taskflow`；後者要求 contained removal。部分 `sweep` record-only/orphan-salvage actions 仍在 taskflow 之外。既有 CLI acknowledgement flags 維持相容，但 Flow preview 不提供其中任何一個；不能把本頁的 shared planner claim 擴張到所有 historical cleanup path。
248	
249	曾經真實發生過：一個 Codex session 從另一個 checkout 刪除了自己已註冊的 worktree 與 branch。Herdr 仍讓該 workspace 與 terminal 保持存活，因為 Unix process 在路徑被 unlink 之後仍可持有開啟中的 cwd inode；接著 SpecStory 又在同一路徑重新建立、但內容只剩 `.specstory/`。這個 shell 看起來還活著，但已經不再是一個 Git checkout：
250	
251	```text
252	failed to reload config: No such file or directory
253	fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
254	```
255	
256	請把「runtime 存活 + Git registration 不存在 + artifact-only path」視為需要 transcript salvage 與外部 reconciliation 的 orphan——**絕不能**視為 RETIRED。
257	
258	`dev sweep` 現在會自行辨識這個形狀，不再只能靠人眼察覺。當某個 task 記錄的 checkout 存在、但 Git 並未註冊它，且該目錄裡只有 agent artifact 資料夾時，sweep 會將它回報為 abandoned agent workspace。只有在其中每個檔案都與 repository 已有的檔案 byte-identical 時，sweep 才會提議移除；任何內容不同的檔案都會被列為 salvage 工作並保持原狀，`--apply` 也不會動它。
259	
260	這裡採用 byte equality 而非僅檢查檔案是否存在，正是重點所在。比 worktree 活得更久的 transcript writer，通常會 flush 出比先前 commit 版本更長的最終稿，因此 repository 中存在同名檔案並不能證明結尾內容已被保存。
261

279	## Task worktree scope
280	
281	Worktree 模式的 `dev start --focus -t <name>` 會建立 linked checkout；`--focus`
282	只負責切換焦點。完成該 task 會保留 parent／canonical agent session 與其他 task
283	的 tabs。Parent 有任何狀態的 recognized agent 都會阻擋 FF：先獨立透過 Herdr
284	處理再重新檢查、改走 PR，或取消。若 integration 已證明完成而只剩 retirement，
285	parent agent 不會阻擋獨立 child worktree 的清理。
286	
287	Interactive finish plan 可以選擇關閉 **task worktree** 中 exact idle/done agent
288	pane，但最後核可 Apply 前不會關閉任何 pane。Parent、其他 checkout、mixed 或
289	無法確認歸屬的 Herdr workspace 都會保留，即使其中 pane 已切換到目標目錄。
290	這些 workspace 仍有 pane 使用 worktree 時，retire 會阻擋並列出須保留的 pane。
291	Working／blocked／waiting agent 仍不可強制關閉。一般前景程序（編輯器、server、
292	測試指令）則需要另外確認 FF 將更新畫面所列 checkout 的檔案，程序仍繼續執行。
293	`--yes` 不提供這項授權；需要此確認的 non-interactive 呼叫會停止。
294	
295	Interactive `dev done` cleanup 與獨立 `dev retire` 共用預覽，列出目標、保留資源、
296	workspace／tab／pane ID、agent 狀態，以及前景程序名稱、PID、目錄。終止已知的
297	非 agent 程序，必須對每個受影響 workspace 輸入 `CLOSE <workspace-id>`，再核可
298	最後的 retirement。`--close-unknown` 不授權終止已知程序。只有證明 shell 位於前景
299	才會這樣標示；觀測失敗顯示 unknown，不冒充 idle。Herdr 提供前景資訊；其他
300	backend 維持原有明確標示的 unknown-runtime 政策。**背景 jobs 未檢查**，關閉
301	terminal 可能一併停止它們。畫面不輸出完整 argv 或環境變數。
302	
303	授權綁定精確 task／checkout、terminal topology 與程序 fingerprint。程序替換、
304	新增 tab 或移動 pane 都需要重新預覽。單次使用的 version-2 coordinator handoff
305	會等待本次 dev PID 結束，並驗證原 pane 已回到前景 shell；新程序不會繼承 caller
306	豁免。舊 handoff 需要重建。Apply 前最後取消不產生變更；開始執行後若失敗，會
307	如實列出已完成的關閉及保留資源。Raw Git／Herdr 操作仍在 dev 的鎖與再驗證
308	保證之外。
309	
310	## 外部 history archives
311	
312	Archive mode 使用同一套 post-writer handoff，把精確的 SpecStory transcript
313	存進另一個 Git checkout。審閱過的 plans 跟 product changes commit。Redact
314	副本需提供審閱過的 `--archive-plan`；舊 intents 保留 source-commit 流程。
315	清理會驗證 archive receipt 與 ignored capture bytes，拒絕已改變或缺失的
316	證據。詳見 [AI 產物](ai-artifacts.md)。

194	// Executables are observed, never replaced. Unlike configuration transactions,
195	// this permits root-owned system tools and standard package-manager ancestors.
196	// The held-path read and persistent inode/content identity still reject drift.
197	func coCommitExecutableToken(ctx context.Context, path string) (string, error) {
198		before, err := os.Lstat(path)
199		if err != nil || !before.Mode().IsRegular() || before.Mode().Perm()&0o111 == 0 || before.Mode().Perm()&0o022 != 0 {
200			return "", errors.New("unverified executable")
201		}
202		metadata := reflect.Indirect(reflect.ValueOf(before.Sys()))
203		if metadata.Kind() != reflect.Struct {
204			return "", errors.New("unsupported executable identity")
205		}
206		dev, ino, uid, gid := metadata.FieldByName("Dev"), metadata.FieldByName("Ino"), metadata.FieldByName("Uid"), metadata.FieldByName("Gid")
207		if !dev.IsValid() || !ino.IsValid() || !uid.IsValid() || !gid.IsValid() || !uid.CanUint() || (uid.Uint() != 0 && uid.Uint() != uint64(os.Getuid())) {
208			return "", errors.New("unsupported executable ownership")
209		}
210		data, err := safefile.ReadStablePath(ctx, path, 128<<20)
211		if err != nil {
212			return "", err
213		}
214		after, err := os.Lstat(path)
215		if err != nil || !os.SameFile(before, after) || before.Mode() != after.Mode() || before.Size() != after.Size() || !before.ModTime().Equal(after.ModTime()) {
216			return "", errors.New("executable changed during observation")
217		}
218		hash := sha256.New()
219		fmt.Fprintf(hash, "%s\x00%v:%v:%v:%v:%d:%d:%d\x00", path, dev.Interface(), ino.Interface(), uid.Interface(), gid.Interface(), before.Size(), before.ModTime().UnixNano(), before.Mode())
220		_, _ = hash.Write(data)
221		return hex.EncodeToString(hash.Sum(nil)), nil
222	}

233			err := filepath.WalkDir(base, func(path string, entry fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
234				if err != nil {
235					return err
236				}
237				if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
238					return err
239				}
240				info, err := entry.Info()

242					return err

244				if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 || info.Mode().Perm()&0o022 != 0 {
245					return errors.New("unsafe co-commit helper member")
246				}
247				if entry.IsDir() {
248					return nil
249				}
250				if !info.Mode().IsRegular() || len(members) >= 256 || info.Size() > 8<<20 {
251					return errors.New("unsupported co-commit helper layout")
252				}
253				total += info.Size()
254				if total > 32<<20 {
255					return errors.New("co-commit helper exceeds source limit")
256				}
257				token, err := configedit.InspectToken(ctx, path)
258				if err != nil {
259					return err
260				}
261				relative, err := filepath.Rel(root, path)
262				if err != nil {
263					return err
264				}
265				members = append(members, filepath.ToSlash(relative)+"\x00"+token)
266				return nil
267			})
268			if err != nil {
269				return "", err
270			}
271		}
272		for _, name := range []string{"_post_session.py", "queue-agent-commit.sh", "finalize-agent-commit.sh"} {
273			info, err := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(dir, name))
274			if err != nil || !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
275				return "", errors.New("canonical co-commit helper is unavailable")
276			}
277		}
278		sort.Strings(members)
279		digest := sha256.Sum256([]byte(dir + "\x00" + strings.Join(members, "\x00")))
280		return hex.EncodeToString(digest[:]), nil
281	}

42		case "not_required", "unresolved", "reviewed_noncredential", "credential_rotation_required", "stale":
43		default:
44			return coCommitFailure("invalid_review_preview", "inspect_private_canonical_receipt")
45		}
46		runDir := filepath.Dir(intent.CoCommit.RequestPath)
47		for _, path := range []string{p.PrivateReceiptPath, p.PrivateReviewPath} {
48			if !filepath.IsAbs(path) || filepath.Clean(path) != path || filepath.Dir(path) != runDir || strings.ContainsAny(path, "\x00\r\n") {
49				return coCommitFailure("invalid_review_path", "inspect_private_canonical_receipt")
50			}
51		}
52		allowed := make(map[string]bool)
53		for _, path := range append([]string{intent.SpecStoryPath}, intent.PlanPaths...) {
54			relative, err := coCommitRelative(intent.WorktreePath, path)
55			if err != nil {
56				return err
57			}
58			allowed[relative] = true
59		}
60		seen := make(map[string]bool)
61		for _, finding := range p.Findings {
62			if !coCommitDigest.MatchString(finding.FindingID) || seen[finding.FindingID] || !allowed[finding.Path] || (finding.Kind != "scanner" && finding.Kind != "structure") || finding.MaskedValue != "[REDACTED]" || finding.OccurrenceCount < 1 || finding.OccurrenceCount > 10000000 || p.Reviewable && !finding.Complete {
63				return coCommitFailure("invalid_review_finding", "inspect_private_canonical_receipt")
64			}
65			seen[finding.FindingID] = true
66		}
67		return nil
68	}
69	
70	func (s *Service) PreviewCoCommitReview(ctx context.Context, intentID string) (*CoCommitReview, error) {
71		if s.Store == nil {
72			return nil, coCommitFailure("store_missing", "inspect_native_configuration")
73		}
74		record, err := s.Store.GetRecord(intentID)
75		if err != nil {
76			return nil, err
77		}
78		helper, err := boundCoCommitHelper(ctx, record.Intent)
79		if err != nil {
80			return nil, err
81		}
82		observation, err := helper.inspect(ctx, record.Intent.CoCommit.RequestPath, false)
83		if err != nil {
84			return nil, err
85		}
86		if err := coCommitBindingMatches(record.Intent, observation); err != nil {
87			return nil, err
88		}
89		var preview CoCommitReview
90		if err := helper.call(ctx, "finalize", []string{"--request", record.Intent.CoCommit.RequestPath, "--preview-review", "--json"}, &preview); err != nil {
91			return nil, err
92		}
93		if err := preview.validate(record.Intent, observation); err != nil {
94			return nil, err
95		}
96		current, err := s.Store.GetRecord(intentID)
97		if err != nil || current.Revision != record.Revision {
98			return nil, ErrStaleRevision
99		}
100		preview.NativeIntentID, preview.NativeRevision = record.Intent.ID, record.Revision
101		return &preview, nil
102	}
103
