```text
1	# Authoring patterns
2	
3	Condensed from <https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices>. Read this
4	before writing or editing a SKILL.md body.
5	
6	## Table of contents
7	
8	1. [Spending context wisely](#spending-context-wisely)
9	2. [Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility](#cross-agent-frontmatter-compatibility)
10	3. [Calibrating control](#calibrating-control)
11	4. [Gotchas sections](#gotchas-sections)
12	5. [Output templates](#output-templates)
13	6. [Checklists for multi-step workflows](#checklists-for-multi-step-workflows)
14	7. [Validation loops](#validation-loops)
15	8. [Plan-validate-execute](#plan-validate-execute)
16	9. [Bundling reusable scripts](#bundling-reusable-scripts)
17	10. [Quick checklist before commit](#quick-checklist-before-commit)
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Spending context wisely
22	
23	Every token in `SKILL.md` competes with the conversation history, the system
24	prompt, and every other active skill. Spend tokens on what the agent **wouldn't
25	know without you**:
26	
27	- Project-specific conventions (table names, repo layout, internal jargon)
28	- Domain-specific procedures with non-obvious steps
29	- Edge cases the agent will misjudge by default
30	- Specific tools/APIs to prefer (with the *why*, briefly)
31	
32	Don't spend tokens on:
33	
34	- Explaining what well-known things are (PDF, HTTP, REST, JSON)
35	- Generic "best practices" the agent already applies (handle errors, write tests)
36	- Comprehensive option enumerations — give a default and one escape hatch
37	
38	**Test:** for each paragraph, ask "would the agent get this wrong without it?"
39	If no, cut it.
40	
41	### Progressive disclosure
42	
43	Three loading levels:
44	
45	| Level | Loaded | Budget |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| Frontmatter (`name`, `description`) | always | 120-500 chars preferred, 1024 max |
48	| `SKILL.md` body | when skill triggers | <500 lines, <5000 tokens |
49	| `references/*.md`, `assets/*`, `scripts/*` | on demand | unlimited |
50	
51	If `SKILL.md` is creeping past 500 lines, move sections to `references/<topic>.md`
52	and reference them with **load conditions** ("Read X if Y happens"), not just
53	"see X for details". Conditions let the agent load on demand; bare pointers tend
54	to either get ignored or get pre-loaded out of caution.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility
59	
60	Use this as the portable baseline for coding agents that consume Agent Skills:
61	
62	- `name`: required, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens only, no leading/trailing
63	  hyphen, no `--`, <=64 characters.
64	- `description`: required, non-empty string, <=1024 characters. Include both
65	  what the skill does and concrete trigger contexts. Keep the first 60
66	  characters meaningful because `npx skills` truncates picker hints there.
67	- **Quoting**: a YAML plain (unquoted) scalar may not contain `": "`, and ` #`
68	  starts a comment. Long English descriptions hit both constantly
69	  (`"…debug a FastAPI app: choosing def vs async def"`). Wrap such values in
70	  single quotes — the whole skill is otherwise skipped at install time with
71	  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings", or installs with a
72	  silently truncated description. `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` gates this.
73	- Keep `name` and `description` as the only required frontmatter fields for
74	  portability. Agent-specific fields are allowed when needed, but isolate them
75	  intentionally: Cursor uses `disable-model-invocation`, Codex can read
76	  `agents/openai.yaml`, and some vendored skills carry upstream-only metadata.
77	
78	Description budget tiers:
79	
80	| Tier | Length | Meaning |
81	|---|---:|---|
82	| Green | 120-500 chars | Preferred for local skills: enough trigger surface without context bloat |
83	| Yellow | 501-900 chars | Valid, but context-heavy; move details to `SKILL.md` body |
84	| Orange | 901-1024 chars | Valid, but close to hard loader limits |
85	| Red | >1024 chars | Invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned validators |
86	
87	Agent notes:
88	
89	- **Codex** skips invalid `SKILL.md` files; OpenAI's validator enforces the
90	  64-char name and 1024-char description limits.
91	- **Cursor** managed `create-skill` guidance matches the same 64/1024 limits
92	  and supports `disable-model-invocation` for explicit-only skills.
93	- **Claude Code** uses descriptions for discovery and tolerates additional
94	  frontmatter in practice, but long descriptions still consume always-on
95	  context and are poor picker hints.
96	- **OpenCode** follows the Agent Skills convention and uses descriptions for
97	  invocation; stay within the portable baseline unless a target agent's docs
98	  say otherwise.
99	- **Claude.ai upload** may impose stricter UI limits. Treat that as a separate
100	  packaging target, not the default coding-agent baseline for this repo.
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Calibrating control
105	
106	Match instruction specificity to **task fragility**, not to "we should be thorough".
107	
108	### Be prescriptive when:
109	
110	- The operation is destructive or has side effects
111	- A specific sequence of steps must hold (migration, release, deploy)
112	- An external system requires exact format (API contract, parser input)
113	
114	```markdown
115	## Database migration
116	
117	Run exactly this sequence:
118	
119	    python scripts/migrate.py --verify --backup
120	
121	Do not modify the command or add flags. The `--verify` step seeds an
122	integrity check that later phases depend on.
123	```
124	
125	The trailing sentence is the trick — even when prescriptive, **explain why**.
126	Agents that understand the reason follow it more reliably than agents that just
127	see "DO NOT" in caps.
128	
129	### Give the agent freedom when:
130	
131	- Multiple valid approaches exist
132	- The output is judgment-driven (code review, refactor proposal)
133	- You'd be hand-coding policy if you wrote it all out
134	
135	```markdown
136	## Code review process
137	
138	1. Check database queries for SQL injection (use parameterized queries)
139	2. Verify auth checks on every endpoint
140	3. Look for race conditions in concurrent code paths
141	4. Confirm error messages don't leak internals
142	```
143	
144	Notice: *what to look for*, not *how to look for it*. The agent picks the
145	approach.
146	
147	### Defaults, not menus
148	
149	When several tools could work, pick one default and mention alternatives as
150	escape hatches.
151	
152	```markdown
153	Use pdfplumber for text extraction.
154	
155	For scanned PDFs requiring OCR, fall back to pdf2image with pytesseract.
156	```
157	
158	…not:
159	
160	```markdown
161	You can use pypdf, pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, or pdf2image depending on...
162	```
163	
164	### Procedures over declarations
165	
166	Teach the agent *how* to approach the class of problem, not *what* to produce
167	for one instance.
168	
169	```markdown
170	Bad — only useful for this exact query:
171	  Join `orders` to `customers` on `customer_id`, filter region='EMEA',
172	  sum `amount`.
173	
174	Good — works for any query:
175	  1. Read schema from `references/schema.yaml` to find relevant tables.
176	  2. Join via the `_id` foreign key convention.
177	  3. Apply user-requested filters as WHERE clauses.
178	  4. Aggregate numeric columns and format as a markdown table.
179	```
180	
181	Specifics still belong in the skill (output format templates, "never output
182	PII", tool-specific quirks) — but the *approach* should generalize.
183	
184	---
185	
186	## Gotchas sections
187	
188	Often the single highest-value section in a skill. **Concrete corrections to
189	mistakes the agent will make without being told.** Not generic advice.
190	
191	```markdown
192	## Gotchas
193	
194	- The `users` table uses soft deletes. Queries must include
195	  `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` or results will include deactivated accounts.
196	- The user ID is `user_id` in the database, `uid` in the auth service, and
197	  `accountId` in the billing API. All three refer to the same value.
198	- The `/health` endpoint returns 200 if the web server is up, even if the
199	  database is down. Use `/ready` to check full service health.
200	```
201	
202	Keep gotchas in `SKILL.md`, not in a separate reference. The whole point is
203	that the agent reads them **before** hitting the situation — by the time it
204	realizes it should load `references/gotchas.md`, the bug has happened.
205	
206	**Iteration tip:** every time you correct the agent during a real run, add the
207	correction here. Most skills' gotchas sections grow over weeks, not get written
208	all at once.
209	
210	---
211	
212	## Output templates
213	
214	Agents pattern-match against concrete structures more reliably than they
215	follow prose descriptions. When the output has a fixed shape, paste the shape:
216	
217	````markdown
218	## Report structure
219	
220	Use this template, adapting sections as needed:
221	
222	```markdown
223	# [Analysis Title]
224	
225	## Executive summary
226	[One paragraph]
227	
228	## Key findings
229	- Finding 1 with supporting data
230	- Finding 2 with supporting data
231	
232	## Recommendations
233	1. Specific actionable recommendation
234	2. Specific actionable recommendation
235	```
236	````
237	
238	Long templates or templates that only apply in some cases should live in
239	`assets/<name>.template` and be loaded on demand from `SKILL.md`.
240	
241	---
242	
243	## Checklists for multi-step workflows
244	
245	Make dependencies and validation gates visible:
246	
247	```markdown
248	## Form processing workflow
249	
250	Progress:
251	- [ ] 1. Analyze the form  → `scripts/analyze_form.py`
252	- [ ] 2. Create field mapping  → edit `fields.json`
253	- [ ] 3. Validate mapping  → `scripts/validate_fields.py`
254	- [ ] 4. Fill the form  → `scripts/fill_form.py`
255	- [ ] 5. Verify output  → `scripts/verify_output.py`
256	```
257	
258	The agent treats the checkboxes as state and won't skip to step 4 without
259	ticking 1-3. Dependency arrows make the wiring explicit.
260	
261	---
262	
263	## Validation loops
264	
265	For tasks where output quality is testable, instruct the agent to validate
266	and re-try, not "do your best and stop":
267	
268	```markdown
269	## Editing workflow
270	
271	1. Make your edits.
272	2. Run validation: `python scripts/validate.py output/`
273	3. If validation fails:
274	   - Read the error message.
275	   - Fix the issues.
276	   - Run validation again.
277	4. Only proceed when validation passes.
278	```
279	
280	The validator can be a script, a reference checklist, or a self-check prompt.
281	The pattern is identical: **do → validate → fix → re-validate → proceed**.
282	
283	---
284	
285	## Plan-validate-execute
286	
287	For batch or destructive operations, force the agent through an intermediate
288	**plan artifact** that gets validated before any side effects happen:
289	
290	```markdown
291	## PDF form filling
292	
293	1. Extract form fields:
294	   `python scripts/analyze_form.py input.pdf`  → `form_fields.json`
295	2. Create `field_values.json` mapping each field name to its intended value.
296	3. Validate:
297	   `python scripts/validate_fields.py form_fields.json field_values.json`
298	   (checks every field exists, types match, required fields present)
299	4. If validation fails, revise `field_values.json` and re-validate.
300	5. Fill the form:
301	   `python scripts/fill_form.py input.pdf field_values.json output.pdf`
302	```
303	
304	The magic is step 3. A validator that catches "field 'signature_date' not
305	found — available: customer_name, order_total, signature_date_signed" lets the
306	agent self-correct **before** the destructive step 5.
307	
308	This pattern eliminates an entire class of "oops, ran the wrong thing on prod"
309	failures. Use it any time the actual operation is hard to undo.
310	
311	---
312	
313	## Bundling reusable scripts
314	
315	When you iterate on a skill (with `skill-creator`), watch the agent transcripts
316	across test runs. If the agent independently reinvents the same logic each run
317	— building the same chart, parsing the same format, validating the same way —
318	that's a signal to write the script once and bundle it in `scripts/`.
319	
320	Heuristic: if you see the same ~20-line helper appearing in 2+ runs, bundle it.
321	
322	See `references/script-design.md` for **how** to design bundled scripts so an
323	agent can call them reliably.
324	
325	---
326	
327	## Quick checklist before commit
328	
329	Before considering a SKILL.md "done":
330	
331	- [ ] Description includes specific trigger contexts ("use when X, Y, Z"),
332	      not just a one-line summary
333	- [ ] Description is "pushy" but within budget: 120-500 chars preferred,
334	      <=1024 chars required
335	- [ ] First 60 description chars are useful in picker UIs
336	- [ ] Name is hyphen-case and <=64 chars
337	- [ ] SKILL.md is under 500 lines (move overflow into `references/`)
338	- [ ] Every `references/*.md` is mentioned with a load condition, not just
339	      listed at the bottom
340	- [ ] Has a `## Gotchas` section (or an honest reason it's empty)
341	- [ ] Output format, if structured, is shown as a literal template
342	- [ ] Multi-step procedures use checklists with dependencies marked
343	- [ ] Destructive operations go through plan-validate-execute or have
344	      `--dry-run` support
345	- [ ] Bundled scripts are listed under `## Available scripts` with their flags
346	- [ ] No "MUST" / "ALWAYS" / "NEVER" in caps without an accompanying *why*
347
```
</details></tool-use>

34	// FindTranscript selects exactly one SpecStory transcript by its anchored
35	// preamble session UUID. UUID mentions later in a transcript are never used.
36	func FindTranscript(worktree, provider, sessionID string) (Transcript, error) {
37		history := filepath.Join(worktree, ".specstory", "history")
38		entries, err := os.ReadDir(history)
39		if err != nil {
40			return Transcript{}, err
41		}
42		var matches []Transcript
43		for _, entry := range entries {
44			if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".md") {
45				continue
46			}
47			path := filepath.Join(history, entry.Name())
48			inside, err := pathx.Contains(history, path)
49			if err != nil || !inside {
50				continue
51			}
52			gotProvider, gotSession, err := transcriptPreamble(path)
53			if err != nil || gotSession != sessionID || (provider != "" && gotProvider != provider) {
54				continue
55			}
56			matches = append(matches, Transcript{Path: path, Provider: gotProvider, SessionID: gotSession})
57		}
58		switch len(matches) {
59		case 1:
60			return matches[0], nil
61		case 0:
62			return Transcript{}, fmt.Errorf("no SpecStory transcript with preamble session %s:%s", provider, sessionID)
63		default:
64			return Transcript{}, fmt.Errorf("multiple SpecStory transcripts have preamble session %s:%s", provider, sessionID)
65		}
66	}
67	
68	// ReadTranscriptSession proves one regular file's strict bounded SpecStory preamble.
69	func ReadTranscriptSession(path string) (provider, sessionID string, err error) {
70		return agenthistory.ReadTranscriptSession(path)
71	}

73	// SelectTranscript binds a strict session proof to an exact checkout history path.
74	func SelectTranscript(worktree, path, provider, sessionID string) (Transcript, error) {
75		selected, err := agenthistory.SelectTranscript(worktree, path, provider, sessionID)
76		if err != nil {
77			return Transcript{}, err
78		}
79		root, err := pathx.Canonical(worktree)
80		if err != nil {
81			return Transcript{}, err
82		}
83		rel, err := filepath.Rel(root, selected)
84		if err != nil || !strings.HasPrefix(filepath.ToSlash(rel), ".specstory/history/") {
85			return Transcript{}, fmt.Errorf("selected transcript is outside .specstory/history")
86		}
87		return Transcript{Path: selected, Provider: provider, SessionID: sessionID}, nil
88	}

90	func transcriptPreamble(path string) (provider, sessionID string, err error) {
91		file, err := os.Open(path)
92		if err != nil {
93			return "", "", err
94		}
95		defer file.Close()
96		scanner := bufio.NewScanner(io.LimitReader(file, 16<<10))
97		for line := 0; scanner.Scan() && line < 12; line++ {
98			match := transcriptSessionLine.FindStringSubmatch(scanner.Text())
99			if len(match) != 3 {
100				continue
101			}
102			return normalizeProvider(match[1]), match[2], nil
103		}
104		if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
105			return "", "", err
106		}
107		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("SpecStory session preamble not found")
108	}

110	func normalizeProvider(label string) string {
111		label = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(label))
112		for _, provider := range []string{"claude", "codex", "cursor", "gemini", "antigravity", "deepseek", "droid"} {
113			if strings.Contains(label, provider) {
114				return provider
115			}
116		}
117		if first, _, ok := strings.Cut(label, " "); ok {
118			return first
119		}
120		return label
121	}
122	
123	// StableSnapshot requires the transcript bytes and metadata to remain unchanged
124	// across a settle interval.
125	func StableSnapshot(ctx context.Context, path string, settle time.Duration) (Snapshot, error) {
126		if settle <= 0 {
127			settle = 250 * time.Millisecond
128		}
129		first, err := snapshot(path)
130		if err != nil {
131			return Snapshot{}, err
132		}
133		select {
134		case <-ctx.Done():
135			return Snapshot{}, ctx.Err()
136		case <-time.After(settle):
137		}
138		second, err := snapshot(path)
139		if err != nil {
140			return Snapshot{}, err
141		}
142		if first.Size != second.Size || !first.ModTime.Equal(second.ModTime) || first.SHA256 != second.SHA256 {
143			return Snapshot{}, fmt.Errorf("transcript is still changing")
144		}
145		return second, nil
146	}
147	
148	func snapshot(path string) (Snapshot, error) {
149		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
150		if err != nil {
151			return Snapshot{}, err
152		}
153		if !info.Mode().IsRegular() {
154			return Snapshot{}, fmt.Errorf("transcript is not a regular file")
155		}
156		file, err := os.Open(path)
157		if err != nil {
158			return Snapshot{}, err
159		}
160		defer file.Close()
161		hash := sha256.New()
162		if _, err := io.Copy(hash, file); err != nil {
163			return Snapshot{}, err
164		}
165		return Snapshot{Size: info.Size(), ModTime: info.ModTime(), SHA256: hex.EncodeToString(hash.Sum(nil))}, nil
166	}

90	// Ready applies only the existing artifact finalization contract: an exact
91	// checkout is ready when it has no intents, or every intent was explicitly
92	// discarded or has a finalized receipt that is still reachable. Missing or
93	// incomplete evidence fails closed.
94	func (i ReadinessInspection) Ready() bool {
95		if i.History != nil && !i.History.Ready {
96			return false
97		}
98		if i.ObservationError != nil {
99			return false
100		}
101		if len(i.Intents) == 0 {
102			return i.KnownEmpty
103		}
104		if i.KnownEmpty {
105			return false
106		}
107		for _, intent := range i.Intents {
108			if intent.ObservationError != nil {
109				return false
110			}
111			switch intent.State {
112			case ReadinessDiscarded:
113				// Discard is the existing explicit operator escape hatch.
114			case ReadinessFinalizedReachable:
115				if !intent.Finalized || !intent.ReceiptReachable {
116					return false
117				}
118			default:
119				return false
120			}
121		}
122		return true
123	}

21			if e != nil || commit != intent.ArchiveCommit {
22				return nil, errors.New("finalized archive receipt is unavailable")
23			}
24			return intent, nil
25		}
26		if err = s.revalidate(ctx, intent); err != nil {

28		}
29		policy, err := h.PolicyFingerprint(ctx)
30		if err != nil || policy != intent.ArchivePolicy {
31			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent, "policy-drift", errors.New("archive policy changed after preparation"))
32		}
33		if intent.SessionEndedAt.IsZero() && !request.WriterStopped {

37		if err != nil {
38			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent, "archive-source", err)
39		}
40		if err := s.finalizeGuard(ctx, request, intent, []string{path}); err != nil {
41			return nil, s.fail(ctx, intent, "writer-guard", err)
42		}
43		planID := intent.ArchivePlanID
44		if request.ArchivePlanID != "" {
45			if planID != "" && planID != request.ArchivePlanID {
46				return nil, errors.New("this intent already has an archive plan; inspect its receipt before replacing the handoff")
47			}

49		}

60	## AI artifacts and source distributions
61	
62	`dev help ai-artifacts` explains what to keep in Git, archive privately, and ship.
63	Choose transcript retention separately from scanning and packaging. SpecStory
64	histories remain trackable, but `.gitattributes` excludes `.specstory` from source
65	archives so Homebrew does not download conversation evidence to build the CLI.
66	Use `dev artifact setup --mode archive --source specstory --archive /path/to/history
67	--protection off --json` to preview explicit raw preservation, or choose `check` /
68	`redact`. Apply the reviewed plan with `dev artifact setup --apply --plan <id> --yes`.
69	`dev repo setup --artifacts` uses the same planner. Archive, find, sync, migrate and
70	backup are separate operations; they never start an agent or replace the source
71	remote automatically. See the [AI artifact guide](docs/guides/ai-artifacts.md).
72	
73	## Repository hygiene
74	
75	Use `dev hygiene manage --all` to preview and deploy commit checks across selected
76	repositories, independently of agent skills. Use `dev hygiene status` to inspect effective hooks and `dev hygiene setup` to
77	preview configuration. `scan --scope staged|worktree|history` checks secret/privacy
78	policy. `dev hygiene report` summarizes the latest stored scan for this checkout;
79	use `--json` for automation or `--values` for a fresh masked-value report. Raw
80	values stay in private review files. Reviewed `rules` and `redact` plans keep
81	private values and recovery outside Git. Hooks block rather than auto-stage.
82	Final transcript cleanup requires the writer to stop first. `dev hygiene repair-encoding --file <path>` previews
83	invalid UTF-8 repair with private raw-byte recovery; apply preserves the index,
84	so review and stage the repair before rescanning. Setup writes project policy
85	and respects an existing effective hook, including a global one.
86	See the [hygiene guide](docs/guides/hygiene.md).
87	
88	## Install

632	| 🔥 `hot` | worktree + branch | session open | working on it now |
633	| 🌤 `warm` | worktree + branch kept | session normally closed | back within days |
634	| ❄️ `cold` | committed and pushed; worktree removed | nothing | paused, reconstructible anywhere |
635	| ✅ `done` | merged | may still be open | **MERGED**, waiting for external retirement |
636	
637	READY/MERGED/RETIRED are derived milestones, not new persisted task states.
638	An agent prepares and exits; an external coordinator integrates and retires it.
639	
640	```bash
641	dev start                                            # interactive managed-task wizard
642	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main     # non-interactive fast path → hot
643	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main \
644	  --run 'specstory run codex -c "codex"' --focus      # dispatch, then switch to the exact new pane
645	dev park --next "add the regression test" --wip      # → warm; self-runtime stays alive until exit
646	dev park --cold --push                               # → cold, only from outside the target runtime
647	dev resume "token refresh"                           # → hot, rebuilt if needed
648	dev flow api                                          # preview the repository lifecycle, plan first
649	
650	dev prepare --session claude:<uuid> --plan .claude/plans/task.md
651	dev artifact finalize --intent <id> --writer-stopped # manual post-wrapper proof
652	dev done                                             # TTY finish wizard
653	dev done --ff                                        # → done/MERGED; runtime + worktree kept
654	dev retire "token refresh" --delete-branch           # external close/wait/remove → RETIRED
655	
656	dev done --pr                                        # open review; keep task/worktree
657	dev done --merged --base-ref origin/main             # verify commit-preserving merge
658	dev retire --base origin/main "token refresh"        # retire against that verified base
659	dev sweep                                            # report drift and cleanup-pending work
660	dev sweep --merged-worktrees                         # from main: audit contained linked worktrees
661	dev sweep --merged-worktrees --apply                 # confirm each safe retirement
662	```
663	
664	`dev retire --base <ref>` selects a local branch, remote-tracking ref or commit
665	for containment; `dev sweep --base` also forwards it to DONE task retirement.
666	A recorded fork-point commit is never silently replaced by the default branch.
667	Optional branch deletion still uses Git's own `branch -d` merged check and can
668	report partial completion against a non-HEAD base.
669	
670	On a TTY, bare `dev done` reports branch ahead/behind and classifies every
671	staged, unstaged and untracked path against the base before offering
672	commit-all, discard-all or cancel. Unique discard requires typing `DROP`;
673	scripts use `--dirty=commit --message ...` or `--dirty=discard --yes`. After a
674	managed worktree reaches MERGED, the bare wizard also previews covering
675	runtime panes and agents, then offers keep, retire while keeping the branch, or
676	retire and delete the freshly contained branch. A caller-owned Herdr workspace

108	// SelectTranscript proves an exact regular Markdown file under root. Only the
109	// trusted root's ancestors may contain platform aliases (for example /var on
110	// macOS); no symlink in the selected subtree is accepted, even an internal alias.
111	func SelectTranscript(root, path, provider, sessionID string) (string, error) {
112		root, err := pathx.Canonical(root)
113		if err != nil {
114			return "", err
115		}
116		rootInfo, err := os.Stat(root)
117		if err != nil || !rootInfo.IsDir() {
118			return "", errors.New("transcript root is unavailable")
119		}
120		for _, component := range strings.Split(filepath.ToSlash(path), "/") {
121			if component == ".." {
122				return "", errors.New("selected transcript contains path traversal")
123			}
124		}
125		if !filepath.IsAbs(path) {
126			path = filepath.Join(root, path)
127		}
128		path = filepath.Clean(path)
129		if !strings.HasSuffix(path, ".md") {
130			return "", errors.New("selected transcript must be Markdown")
131		}
132		for probe := path; ; probe = filepath.Dir(probe) {
133			info, e := os.Lstat(probe)
134			if e != nil {
135				return "", e
136			}
137			if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
138				return "", errors.New("selected transcript contains a symlink")
139			}
140			if os.SameFile(rootInfo, info) {
141				break
142			}
143			if filepath.Dir(probe) == probe {
144				return "", errors.New("selected transcript is outside its capture root")
145			}
146		}
147		selected, err := pathx.Canonical(path)
148		if err != nil {
149			return "", err
150		}
151		inside, err := pathx.Contains(root, selected)
152		if err != nil || !inside || selected == root {
153			return "", errors.New("selected transcript is outside its capture root")
154		}
155		gotProvider, gotID, err := ReadTranscriptSession(selected)
156		if err != nil {

158		}
159		if gotProvider != provider || !strings.EqualFold(gotID, sessionID) {
160			return "", errors.New("selected transcript does not match the requested provider/session")
161		}
162		return selected, nil
163	}

62	    language: str
63	
64	
65	class LinkParser(html.parser.HTMLParser):
66	    def __init__(self) -> None:
67	        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
68	        self.hrefs: list[str] = []
69	        self.scripts: list[str] = []
70	        self.stylesheets: list[str] = []
71	        self.anchors: set[str] = set()
72	        self.mermaid_blocks = 0
73	
74	    def handle_starttag(self, tag: str, attrs: list[tuple[str, str | None]]) -> None:
75	        values = dict(attrs)
76	        if tag == "a" and values.get("href"):
77	            self.hrefs.append(values["href"] or "")
78	        if tag == "script" and values.get("src"):
79	            self.scripts.append(values["src"] or "")
80	        if tag == "link" and values.get("href") and values.get("rel") == "stylesheet":
81	            self.stylesheets.append(values["href"] or "")
82	        if tag == "pre" and "mermaid" in (values.get("class") or "").split():
83	            self.mermaid_blocks += 1
84	        if values.get("id"):
85	            self.anchors.add(values["id"] or "")

731	## Hygiene rollout and selected skill removal
732	
733	Repository hygiene is a developer commit procedure and needs no installed agent
734	skill. Batch migration retains specialized legacy finalizers and custom settings;
735	it does not yet replace the full agent-history-hygiene lifecycle. Gitleaks 8.30+
736	compatible 8.x is required by setup/scan. Cached machine imports never query
737	remote hosts or credential providers.
738	
739	Skill removal requires verified native ownership or a bundled install manifest,
740	explicit agent scopes and dependency checks. Windows npm-shim removal uses system
741	PowerShell and bounded process-tree cancellation; unsupported shell syntax or
742	other shim mutation actions fail closed. The dedicated native removal tests are
743	required; broad advisory Windows test conclusions are not proof that every
744	legacy suite passed.
745	
746	## Agent history archives
747	
748	History policy is opt-in through `artifact setup` or `repo setup --artifacts`.
749	Only SpecStory Markdown and explicitly selected files are capture sources.
750	Archive copies require post-writer proof; off stores unscanned input, while
751	check/redact use enabled source hygiene rules. Native session databases, cloud
752	resume, automatic knowledge mining, encrypted/LFS archive filters and original
753	remote history replacement are outside this integration.
754	
755	Current file snapshots cap at 128 MiB, inventories at 10,000 files and plans at
756	256 selected files. Split migration requires git-filter-repo (native CI pins
757	2.47.0) and complete locally recoverable refs. Backup coverage and partial results
758	remain explicit. Existing commit finalizers and intent fields retain their lane;
759	older binaries cannot consume new external-archive intent fields.

761	Readiness checks canonical Git common-directory identity for intents not matched
762	to the checkout path before requiring branch identity for a moved intent.

765	pending intents, ambiguous repository/moved-intent identity and unreadable stores
766	still block; exact finalized-receipt checks are unchanged. Child artifact
767	observation failures report the underlying cause. Empty children use the stricter

629	`<report-id>.values.review.txt`，不進入 stdout／JSON／scan 紀錄。
630	`dev hygiene review-path <plan-or-report-id>` 只印出私人路徑；勿將其內容貼入聊天、
631	Git 或 CI。擷取有數量與 byte 上限；過大的值會省略並標記 `values_truncated`。
632	附屬檔寫入失敗仍保存 partial 報告，附 `values_capture_failed` gap 與
633	`values_status: "failed"`，不提供 review-path 提示。
634	
635	Hygiene redact／repair-encoding／restore／manage 與 artifact finalize／archive／
636	migrate 共用 artifact writer guard。其他涵蓋此 checkout 的 live agent 一律阻擋。
637	自動豁免呼叫者需每個目標 artifact 實際由 SpecStory 產生的固定 preamble 都含
638	合法且不同的 UUID。否則（包含呼叫者身分未知），須以全域
639	`--allow-shared-checkout` 明確聲明歸屬互不重疊；已識別為呼叫者自己的 live
640	transcript 即使有 override 也拒絕。`restore --apply` 檢查 receipt 的確切路徑；見
641	[writer 規則](../guides/hygiene.zh-TW.md#artifact-writer-guard)。
642	
643	## Hygiene rollout 與勾選 skill 移除
644	
645	Repo hygiene 是普通 commit procedure，不需安裝 agent skill。批次遷移保留專用
646	legacy finalizer 和自訂設定，尚未完整取代 agent-history-hygiene lifecycle。
647	Setup／scan 要求相容 gitleaks 8.x、最低 8.30；機器快取匯入不查詢遠端或 vault。
648	
649	Skill 移除要求已驗證 native ownership 或 bundled manifest、明確 agent scope
650	與依賴檢查。Windows npm shim 移除使用系統 PowerShell 與 process-tree 取消；
651	不支援的 shell syntax 或其他 shim mutation 會拒絕。獨立 native removal tests
652	是必要 gate；Windows 廣泛 advisory job 的成功結論不表示所有 legacy suites 通過。
653	
654	## Agent history archives
655	
656	History policy 需透過 `artifact setup` 或 `repo setup --artifacts` 主動選用。
657	Capture 來源為 SpecStory Markdown 與明確選取的檔案；archive copy 需要 writer
658	結束的證據。Off 保存未掃描原稿，check/redact 使用 source 已啟用的 hygiene
659	規則。Native session DB、cloud resume、自動知識提煉、加密／LFS archive
660	filters 與原 remote 歷史替換不在此次整合內。
661	
662	目前每檔 snapshot 上限 128 MiB、盤點上限 10,000 檔、每 plan 最多 256 檔。
663	Split 需要 git-filter-repo（native CI 固定 2.47.0）與完整可回復的本機 refs。
664	備份範圍及 partial results 明確列出。舊 commit finalizers 維持原流程；舊版
665	binary 無法讀取新增的 external-archive intent 欄位。
666	
667	Intent 未直接符合 checkout 路徑時，readiness 先核對 canonical Git common directory
668	身分，再要求 moved intent 的分支身分。已證明屬於其他 repository
669	的 pending／finalized 紀錄不再阻擋 detached checkout，包含正常的 pinned
670	submodule。相關 pending intent、repository／moved-intent 身分歧義與無法
671	讀取的 store 仍會阻擋；精確 finalized receipt 檢查不變。子 artifact 觀測
672	失敗會回報實際原因。空子項目則使用前述較嚴格的路徑 claim 檢查，不繼承
673	parent 的 Git 探索結果。
674	
675	## SSH dashboard observations (v0.2.34)
676	
677	SSH dashboard 提供原生 discovery／setup 與 profile 樹狀清單。缺少 registry 是空狀態，不安全的 registry 則提供問題引導，不可推定 bindings 不存在。Cache 失敗仍保留本次 discovery。`[tui.ssh].background_refresh` 控制 Tailscale 背景狀態，不會掃 LAN 或驗證 SSH。活動紀錄是與 cache 分離的 durable 資料；Ping 可略過且不阻止 SSH，proxy 的直連層級維持未觀測。新增 diagnostic flags／fields 為增補，既有 alias／list JSON 契約不變。
678

func testQueueAck() *artifact.CoCommitQueueAck {
	return &artifact.CoCommitQueueAck{
		Kind: "agent_history_queue_ack", SchemaVersion: 2,
		RequestID: "9bd5ed58-1d35-47c8-b3b7-20445e6d7489",

	}

func TestCoCommitHumanOutputRetainsCanonicalQueueAck(t *testing.T) {
	var out bytes.Buffer
	app := &App{Out: &out}
	ack := testQueueAck()
	result := &artifact.CoCommitResult{Kind: "co_commit_handoff", SchemaVersion: 1, Status: "queued", RequestID: ack.RequestID, QueueAck: ack, NextAction: "report_finalization_queued_then_exit_agent"}
	if err := renderCoCommitResult(app, result, nil, false); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	line, rest, found := strings.Cut(out.String(), "\n")
	var decoded artifact.CoCommitQueueAck
	if !found || json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &decoded) != nil || decoded != *ack {
		t.Fatal("human output did not retain one exact typed queue acknowledgement")
	}
	if !strings.Contains(rest, "finalization queued") || !strings.Contains(rest, "do not perform more repository/index operations") {
		t.Fatalf("missing post-queue boundary: %s", rest)
	}
}

func TestCoCommitJSONRetainsPartialAckAndSanitizesError(t *testing.T) {
	const privateDiagnostic = "synthetic-private-native-diagnostic"
	var out bytes.Buffer
	app := &App{Out: &out}
	ack := testQueueAck()
	result := &artifact.CoCommitResult{Kind: "co_commit_handoff", SchemaVersion: 1, Status: "queued_but_not_bound", RequestID: ack.RequestID, QueueAck: ack, NextAction: "exit_agent_then_repair_exact_binding"}
	err := renderCoCommitResult(app, result, errors.New(privateDiagnostic), true)
	if err == nil || strings.Contains(err.Error(), privateDiagnostic) || strings.Contains(out.String(), privateDiagnostic) {
		t.Fatal("private diagnostic leaked or failure disappeared")
	}
	var decoded struct {
		Kind string `json:"kind"`
		Status string `json:"status"`
		QueueAck *artifact.CoCommitQueueAck `json:"queue_ack"`
		Error *artifact.CoCommitError `json:"error"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(out.Bytes(), &decoded); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if decoded.Kind != "co_commit_handoff" || decoded.Status != "queued_but_not_bound" || decoded.QueueAck == nil || *decoded.QueueAck != *ack || decoded.Error == nil || decoded.Error.Code != "observation_unavailable" {
		t.Fatalf("partial result lost: %+v", decoded)
	}
}

func TestCoCommitJSONFailureBeforeQueueDoesNotInventAck(t *testing.T) {
	var out bytes.Buffer

}

package cli_test

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestCoCommitCLIRejectsMixedLanesWithoutIndexEffects(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness(t)
	h.repo.Write("feature.txt", "reviewed product\n")
	h.repo.Git("add", "feature.txt")
	before := h.repo.Git("diff", "--cached", "--binary")
	head := h.repo.Git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
	for _, args := range [][]string{
		{"prepare", h.repo.Root, "--closeout", "unknown"},
		{"prepare", h.repo.Root, "--no-plan"},
		{"prepare", h.repo.Root, "--message-file", "message.txt"},
		{"prepare", h.repo.Root, "--closeout", "co-commit"},
		{"prepare", h.repo.Root, "--closeout", "co-commit", "--no-plan", "--plan", "one.md"},
		{"prepare", h.repo.Root, "--closeout", "co-commit", "--plan", "one.md", "--plan", "two.md"},
	} {
		if _, _, err := h.run(args...); err == nil {
			t.Fatalf("invalid lane arguments succeeded: %v", args)
		}
		if h.repo.Git("rev-parse", "HEAD") != head || h.repo.Git("diff", "--cached", "--binary") != before {
			t.Fatalf("invalid lane arguments mutated Git: %v", args)
		}
	}
}

func TestArtifactPreparationJSONKeepsDefaultLane(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness(t)
	const id = "72b5c55e-d964-45cd-b040-cb29d0d7af05"
	h.repo.Write(".specstory/history/selected.md", "<!-- Generated by SpecStory, Markdown v2.1.0 -->\n# Review\n<!-- Claude Code Session "+id+" (now) -->\nbody\n")
	out := h.mustRun("prepare", h.repo.Root, "--session", "claude:"+id, "--specstory-path", ".specstory/history/selected.md", "--json")
	var preparation struct {
		Kind string `json:"kind"`
		SchemaVersion int `json:"schema_version"`
		Intent struct {
			ID string `json:"id"`
			Destination string `json:"destination"`
			SpecStoryPath string `json:"specstory_path"`
		} `json:"intent"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(out), &preparation); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if preparation.Kind != "artifact_preparation" || preparation.SchemaVersion != 1 || preparation.Intent.ID == "" || preparation.Intent.Destination != "" || !strings.HasSuffix(preparation.Intent.SpecStoryPath, "/.specstory/history/selected.md") {
		t.Fatalf("default lane JSON changed semantics: %s", out)
	}
	head := h.repo.Git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
	if _, _, err := h.run("artifact", "finalize", "--intent", preparation.Intent.ID, "--allow-commit"); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "co-commit") {
		t.Fatalf("co-commit flags applied to legacy intent: %v", err)
	}
	if h.repo.Git("rev-parse", "HEAD") != head || h.repo.Git("diff", "--cached", "--name-only") != "" {
		t.Fatal("lane refusal staged or committed artifacts")
	}
}

func TestArtifactListJSONHasVersionedEmptyCollection(t *testing.T) {
	h := newHarness(t)
	out := h.mustRun("artifact", "list", "--json")
	var result struct {
		Kind string `json:"kind"`
		SchemaVersion int `json:"schema_version"`
		Handoffs []json.RawMessage `json:"handoffs"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(out), &result); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if result.Kind != "artifact_handoffs" || result.SchemaVersion != 1 || result.Handoffs == nil || len(result.Handoffs) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("invalid empty handoff collection: %s", out)
	}
}

# dev-cli

Git owns durable code; worktrees are local checkouts; runtimes are host-local
sessions; dev records task intent.

## Discover what you need

Use `dev <command> --help` for current syntax and flags, and `dev help <topic>`
for workflow explanations. `dev --help` lists commands; `dev help` lists topics.
Prefer supported `--json` output for automation. Read the relevant command before
mutation: some actions execute immediately, while others require preview/apply.
Do not preload manuals, repeat `dev --skill`, or run routine diagnostics.

## Preserve these boundaries

- Opening a repository needs no task. Choose direct, branch, or worktree
  deliberately; pass an explicit `--base` for branch/worktree creation. Keep
  managed worktrees outside repositories.
- `dev start` normally prepares a checkout/runtime. Agent launch is explicit.
  Parallel writers need coordinated ownership and verified launch targets.
- Completion, artifact finalization, retirement and branch deletion are separate.
  Finalize after writer exit; retire externally. Use `retire --base` when a fork
  point cannot prove integration. Runtime `done` is not cleanup-ready.
- Unknown or cached observations, merged PRs, and command refusals do not grant
  cleanup authority. Resolve the reported conditions; do not improvise force
  removal or bypass trust checks.

## Read a reference for advanced operations

- Worktree provisioning or cross-host lifecycle: [ownership](references/worktree-ownership.md), [lifecycle](references/task-lifecycle.md).
- Parallel agent launches or prompt transports: [agents](references/parallel-agents.md), [handoffs](references/prompt-handoffs.md).
- History retention: [artifacts](references/ai-artifacts.md).
- Agent completion or cleanup batches: [retirement](references/agent-retirement.md), [triage](references/local-triage.md).
- Repository hygiene batches, `report --json` summaries, scans or redaction: [hygiene](references/hygiene.md).
- Repository hooks, publication, or physical organization: [setup](references/repository-bootstrap.md), [bootstrap](references/bootstrap.md).
- SSH dashboard, diagnosis, discovery, tests/activity, keys, credentials and registration: [SSH](references/ssh-hosts.md).
- Dotfile setup, native chezmoi operations, or FLEET host actions: [dotfiles](references/dotfiles.md).
- Skill/MCP/instruction transfers, updates or removal: [transfers](references/agent-interop.md), [maintenance](references/skills-management.md).
- Recursive Git children: [submodules](references/submodules.md).

Use command help and its workflow topic for everyday operations.

## Unexpected dev failures

Read [feedback and repair](references/feedback-and-repair.md). Preserve the
original task; extra investigation, repair, subagents and publication need
explicit consent covering scope and cost.

# Agent history hygiene

Preserve selected agent evidence under the repository's chosen policy. Read
`dev help ai-artifacts` and `dev artifact status` when supported: source tracking,
external archive, protection and distribution are separate choices. Commit
reviewed project knowledge; do not force-add raw history under archive/unmanaged
policy. Verify repository protection from the effective hook chain.

## Prefer the shared dev workflow

When the installed dev supports `hygiene`, use its domain for setup, scans,
private rules and reviewed text changes:

```bash
dev hygiene status
dev hygiene setup --json
dev hygiene setup --apply --plan <id> --yes
dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
dev hygiene scan --scope history --audit --timeout 40m --json
```

`pre-commit` and `gitleaks` are needed for this repository hook recipe. An explicitly unscanned archive copy needs neither. A global `core.hooksPath` can be
correct, but its script may skip all checks when repository configs are absent.
The shared setup preserves existing hooks/comments and refuses an unverified
chain. Repository new/setup's `agent-history-hygiene` initializer uses this same
service. New default hooks block; they do not rewrite or stage files.

Per-repo secret/known/generic policy supports block/warn/off, with private local
overrides and exact reasoned exceptions. Private visibility is advice, never an
automatic exemption. SSH imports are static and reviewed: no DNS, login, Match
exec, private-key reads or rule-value export. Personal rules stay outside Git;
CI checks public rules and must state the missing personal coverage.

Read the bundled dev reference `references/hygiene.md` through `dev help hygiene`
or the public hygiene guide before rule changes or redaction. The CLI supports
all regular text, rather than treating transcripts as the only leak surface.

## Preserve the review trail

1. Identify the exact provider/session UUID from the transcript preamble. Never
   select another session just because its file is newest.
2. Commit product changes and reviewed plans. Follow the selected retention
   policy for raw history; do not broadly stage every agent directory.
3. Use `dev prepare --session provider:uuid` and finalization after its writer
   exits when that lifecycle applies. Byte stability alone is not writer proof.
4. Scan exact staged content. Partial staging must not accidentally stage
   unrelated working-copy edits.
5. In archive mode, raw history may be ignored but must be preserved before
   checkout disposal. In track mode, retain the existing exact-session workflow.
   Exclude conversation evidence from product source archives independently.

Do not close, restart or spawn agents to make hygiene checks pass without the
applicable authorization. A new agent without SpecStory does not stop an older
writer. Preserve the user's original task while offering additional cleanup.

## Reviewed redaction

```bash
dev hygiene redact --report <report-id> --file <reviewed-file> --json
# After reviewing, and after the exact artifact writer exited:
dev hygiene redact --apply --plan <plan-id> --yes --writer-stopped
```

Plans bind native file identity, contents, policy and checkout state. Stale,
modified or partial plans are not authority to overwrite current data. Keep
private recovery and rerun scans/tests after source or configuration changes.
The running transcript is left for a manual external trigger after its writer
stops. No automatic history rewrite, agent launch, commit, push or cleanup occurs.

## External archive workflow

`dev artifact setup` and `dev repo setup --artifacts` preview explicit per-repo
policy. `archive --session provider:uuid` or `--file` creates reviewed snapshots;
apply only after the exact recorder exits. Off/check/redact affect the copy,
not the live source or its index. A disabled scan is recorded as skipped.
Checked snapshots produce masked finding IDs for reasoned fixture exceptions.

Commit reviewed plans with product work before `dev prepare`. New archive intents
bind the destination and policy; redact finalization requires a reviewed
`--archive-plan`. Old tracked intents retain the compatibility scripts below.
Keep those installations while any tracked workflow still depends on them.

`artifact find` reads local committed archive records. Sync and original-backup
publication are explicit Git operations; they never transfer native session DBs.
`artifact migrate` can untrack after verified backup or build separate original,
history and filtered Git copies with commit maps. It never force-pushes source
refs. For historical exposure, use the remediation section rather than treating
path removal as a secret audit. Private raw recovery is not cache.

## Legacy scripts

The scripts remain explicit compatibility utilities. Prefer dev for new setup
and partial-staging-safe edits; a separately published remote redactor hook has
its own version and is not silently updated by dev.

- `find-session.sh --json`: locate candidate transcript/plan metadata.
- `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --dry-run`: inspect exact staging;
  without session-only it may include other dirty artifacts, so use cautiously.
- `scan-staged.sh`: masked JSON-lines locations only, never raw Match/Secret.
  Exit 0 means clean; 20 means candidate findings; legacy `--redact` selects
  exit 10 but only masks output, never modifies files. Exit 30 means missing
  gitleaks; 40 means scanner/JSON/required-parser failure; 2 means not in Git.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py --fix`: explicit legacy artifact mutation. Scanner
  failure is an error, not an empty result; console output uses full sentinels.
  This utility can restage, so use the reviewed dev flow for partial staging.
- `bootstrap-project.sh`: legacy installer; new default templates require dev
  hygiene. Its old `--migrate` targets the separately published remote redactor,
  not the new dev policy migration. Prefer `dev hygiene setup`.

SpecStory may already redact on write, but provider behavior/version is not proof
that every secret class or artifact directory is covered. Preserve existing
`[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` markers. An inert marker must never exempt another secret
on the same line. `.gitleaksignore` contains exact finding fingerprints, not
file/path globs. Portable pattern exceptions need a narrow rule/path/match scope.

## Confirmed historical exposures

Read [remediation](references/remediation.md). First distinguish fixtures,
examples and scanner candidates from confirmed credentials. Revoke/rotate a
confirmed exposed credential at its provider before considering Git history.

Shared main and immutable release tags stay unchanged in ordinary hygiene work.
Correct HEAD in a new commit, and assess old commits, tags, PR references, forks,
clones, caches and distribution artifacts separately. A force push does not erase
all copies or revoke a credential. Personal names, Git author metadata and filenames
also need an explicit impact assessment; text replacement does not rewrite them.

Never echo matching bytes or raw process arguments into a chat to investigate a
finding. Use rule IDs, safe locations and private local reports. Keep raw reports,
recovery images and personal identity dictionaries outside Git and CI logs.

## Validation

Run the skill's fixture tests for redactor/scan-wrapper changes. For dev changes,
run native hygiene/storage/text-transaction tests and the real hook test:

```bash
python scripts/test-hygiene-hooks.py --dev <absolute-built-dev>
```

It uses an isolated HOME/repository and synthetic credentials. Validate same-line
placeholder bypasses, hidden files, partial staging, missing/malformed scanner
results, writer/stale-plan refusal and private recovery. Synchronize embedded
bootstrap assets and both locales of public documentation.

39	hook. Missing or unverified configured hooks require manual integration, not an
40	automatic local override. There is no `--global` setup option.

46	commits do not call setup again and do not require an agent.

49	dev hygiene manage --all                 # choose repositories, preview, then apply
50	dev hygiene manage /path/to/a /path/to/b --json  # preview only
51	dev hygiene setup --migrate-hooks --json # one repository, narrow migration
52	```
53	
54	REPOS offers the same single/filtered-repository workflow. Repositories do not
55	need a skills lock. Plans show files, retained dependencies and blockers; choose

85	
86	Precedence is built-in defaults, user defaults (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/hygiene.toml`),
87	repo policy, private local repo overrides, then explicit scan/status flags.
88	The recommended defaults are `secrets = "block"`, `known = "block"` and
89	`generic = "warn"`. Each category supports `block`, `warn` and `off`. A rule
90	may override its enabled category's disposition; category `off` disables it.
91	
92	```toml
93	version = 1
94	secrets = "block"
95	known = "block"
96	generic = "warn"
97	```
98	
99	Setting all three categories to `off` returns an explicit `skipped` result without
100	reading repository file contents or running the engine; it is not a clean scan.
101	
102	Private visibility supplies advice only. It does not silently weaken policy;
103	unknown or unsupported visibility is never treated as private. GitHub lookup
104	requires `status --check-remote`; `--remote` selects its remote (default origin).
105	
106	```bash
107	dev hygiene rules policy --known warn --generic off --json
108	dev hygiene rules apply --plan <id> --yes
109	```
110	
111	Policy/rule changes are separate reviewed plans. One invocation's scan overrides
112	are not persisted. Obtain a fresh scan using the persistent policy before
113	creating a redaction plan.
114	
115	## Local identity rules and exceptions
116	
117	```bash
118	dev hygiene rules import --from ssh --json
119	dev hygiene rules import --from ssh --select <candidate-id> --json
120	dev hygiene rules import --from local --json
121	dev hygiene rules add --id private-network --kind cidr --value-file network.txt \
122	  --replacement 192.0.2.1 --json
123	dev hygiene rules apply --plan <id> --yes
124	```
125	
126	Imports require explicit candidate selection. SSH uses the bounded static
127	OpenSSH Include closure, including literal aliases, HostName, User and key-path
128	references. It never executes `ssh -G`, `Match exec`, DNS or a remote command,
129	and never reads key material. An incomplete Include closure blocks import.
130	Common public names and generic accounts are recommendations for warnings.
131	Local import supplies home path, account, Git name and Git email candidates.
132	
133	`rules import --from machines` reads existing Tailscale/LAN and Fleet inventory
134	caches only. IPs, hostnames and remote usernames become selectable private
135	candidates; credential stores, keys, discovery commands and remote connections
136	are never queried. Observation timestamps and stale markers remain visible.
137	Missing caches are reported without creating them; incomplete/corrupt caches
138	block imports. Source changes after preview invalidate the saved import plan.
139	
140	Quoted password literals remain detectable in source files. Unquoted assignments
141	are scoped to configuration/script/prose formats, avoiding Go boolean fields and
142	variable expressions. Format-complete test/demo keys still block until a reviewed
143	exact exception is added. Do not exclude tests/docs or an entire line beside a
144	placeholder; prefer inert placeholders or construct detector fixtures at runtime.
145	
146	
147	Literal, CIDR and Go RE2 rules accept optional relative path globs. `directory/**`
148	selects descendants. Rule values come from a file or `--value-file -`; do not
149	put sensitive values in command arguments. Edit or disable existing private
150	rules through a reviewed same-ID rule plan or the private policy file.
151	
152	Private rules, HMAC identifiers, scan records and recovery are stored outside
153	Git under `paths.state_dir/hygiene/repos/<native-repo-id>/`. Linked worktrees
154	share local policy but plans remain bound to an exact checkout. Windows uses
155	protected current-user/SYSTEM ACLs; Unix uses private ownership and permissions.
156	There is no automatic deletion or export of this state.
157	
158	```bash
159	dev hygiene rules allow --report <report-id> --finding <finding-id> \
160	  --reason 'Reviewed synthetic test fixture' --json
161	```
162	
163	Local exceptions bind an exact value/rule/path finding. Shareable TOML exceptions
164	require `rule`, `path`, an anchored `pattern` and a reason. Keep private values
165	out of shareable rules. `.gitleaksignore` contains finding fingerprints, not path
166	globs. `scan --audit` ignores local finding exceptions, that file and inline
167	`gitleaks:allow`; scanner-config allowlists still apply and must be reviewed.
168	Placeholders never automatically allow an unrelated key on the same line.
169	
170	## Scan with an honest scope
171	
172	```bash
173	dev hygiene scan --scope worktree --json
174	dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
175	dev hygiene scan --scope history --audit --timeout 40m --json
176	dev hygiene --public-only --known off --generic off scan --scope history \
177	  --range <full-from-oid>..<full-to-oid> --json
178	```
179	
180	Working-file scans include tracked files and nonignored untracked files. Already
181	tracked files remain in scope after a later `.gitignore` addition. Staged scans
182	use actual index bytes, including hidden files and partial staging. Selected
183	`--file` arguments must already belong to that scope.
184	
185	An explicit range checks versions changed in its selected commits, leaving
186	untouched older files for the full audit. History freezes locally available refs
187	(or an explicit full-OID range), includes
188	merge-only content and removed files, and never fetches implicitly. It does not
189	scan reflogs, unreachable objects, uncommitted work in other checkouts or remote
190	submodule repositories. Nonregular entries and recognized binary formats are
191	listed as exclusions from text scanning. Unsupported text encodings, unreadable
192	or oversized files, changing sources/refs, shallow history, cancellation and
193	scanner failures produce incomplete results. The per-file text limit is 128 MiB;
194	large files are never silently called clean.
195	
196	Public JSON schema 1 records status, scope, frozen refs, counts, safe finding
197	locations, dispositions, exclusions and coverage gaps. It omits source snippets
198	and credential values. Finding IDs and public file/plan digests use private HMAC
199	keys. `complete` describes the declared text scope; a blocking finding or
200	incomplete scan exits unsuccessfully. No findings is not a credential-validity
201	check. Reports may contain identifying filenames not covered by selected rules;
202	review them before sharing. Findings may add a `value_id`: a private-keyed
203	digest of the matched value within its rule, so identical values aggregate
204	across files without revealing them. Additive `file_id` identifies the exact
205	path with a private key, keeping distinct files separate even if their displayed
206	paths mask to the same text.
207	
208	CI uses public repository rules, without global/personal values. It cannot
209	claim to have checked private SSH identities. PR/push scans select the changed
210	commit range; manual workflow dispatch audits all locally fetched history.
211	
212	## Summarize a scan
213	
214	```bash
215	dev hygiene report                                 # newest stored scan for this checkout
216	dev hygiene report --scope staged --by rule --top 5 --findings
217	dev hygiene report --report <report-id> --disposition block,warn --path 'docs/**'
218	dev hygiene report --rescan --scope history --range <full-from-oid>..<full-to-oid>
219	dev hygiene report --rule privacy-email --values  # masked values; implies --rescan
220	dev hygiene report --json                          # hygiene_summary schema 1
221	```
222	
223	`report` summarizes one scan instead of printing every finding. By default it
224	reads the newest scan recorded for this checkout without scanning again, so the
225	pre-commit hook's staged scan is readable right after a blocked commit. Latest
226	pointers are per checkout: linked worktrees share hygiene state, but the default
227	lookup never selects a sibling's scan. Snapshot reports never become the latest.
228	`--scope` selects the newest scan of that scope, `--report ID` an exact report and
229	`--rescan` a fresh scan; `--range`, `--file`, `--timeout` and `--audit` require
230	`--rescan`. The output warns when policy changed since the scan or the report
231	came from another checkout. Stored reports are historical observations:
232	`checkout_current` compares checkout roots only, not current source bytes.
233	Stored-summary output shows the scan date and notes "source bytes were not
234	rechecked". Use `--rescan` for a new observation; it cannot combine with `--report`.
235	
236	`--by` selects `severity`, `rule`, `file` and/or `category` groups (default
237	`severity,rule,file`). `--top N` limits each group (default 10, `0` shows all)
238	and counts omitted rows. `--disposition`, `--rule`, `--category` and repeatable
239	`--path <glob>` filter findings before aggregation; `--findings` lists them
240	individually. Rows order block, warn, then accepted, followed by occurrences
241	descending, findings descending and name ascending. A stored summary exits 0
242	whatever it contains; a rescan with coverage gaps prints its summary, then exits
243	unsuccessfully.
244	
245	`--json` emits `kind: "hygiene_summary"`, `schema_version: 1`: `report_id`,
246	`report_kind`, `scope`, `status`, `created`, `policy_current`,
247	`checkout_current`, `audit`, `public_only`, `rescanned`, `sections`, `top`,
248	`filters`, `totals`, `file_counts_complete`, selected
249	`severities`/`rules`/`files`/`categories` (file rows include `file_id`),
250	optional `findings`, `gaps`, `skipped`, `omitted` counts and `values_shown`.
251	A rule reports `distinct_values` only when every finding has a `value_id`.
252	With `--values`, rules add masked `values` and `omitted_values`;
253	`values_truncated` warns when capture hit its limit. `values_status` is
254	`complete`, `truncated` or `failed` (empty/absent if not captured or legacy).
255	Legacy findings without file IDs make `file_counts_complete` false: file counts
256	then describe lower-bound masked-path groups. Private path metadata lets
257	`--path` match raw filenames while the echoed filter stays policy-masked; invalid
258	path globs are rejected. Agents should prefer
259	`dev hygiene report --json` over parsing `scan` output or tables.
260	
261	`--values` adds masked distinct values per rule and implies `--rescan` unless
262	`--report` names a scan captured with values. Secrets keep their first and last
263	two characters plus length (length only below 12 characters); private rules show
264	`[private:N]`, emails `a•••@d•••.tld`, IPv4 `a.b.•.•`, IPv6 `first:•••` and
265	home paths `Users/x•••`. Raw values and line context never enter stdout, JSON or
266	scan records: they go only to a private 0600 `<report-id>.values.review.txt`, whose
267	location `dev hygiene review-path <report-id>` prints. Never paste that file into
268	chat, Git or CI logs. Capture allows 10,000 values and 20 samples per value,
269	with at most 64 KiB per raw value and 16 MiB combined raw/context/location/rule
270	metadata; the rendered review caps at 64 MiB. Oversized values are skipped whole,
271	not sliced, and limits set `values_truncated`. A failed values sidecar leaves a
272	saved partial report with a `values_capture_failed` gap and no private review-path
273	hint.
274	
275	## Repair invalid UTF-8
276	
277	Warning findings alone do not block a commit. A coverage gap such as
278	`unsupported_text_encoding` makes a scan incomplete even with zero blocking
279	findings. Encoding gaps retain that code and add an `encoding` object with
280	`reason`, zero-based `byte_offset`, one-based `line`, `invalid_bytes`,
281	`invalid_sequences` (contiguous invalid runs) and optional `nul_bytes`.
282	Historical gaps also identify the observed `commit`. Diagnostics contain no
283	source excerpts. Fixing a working file does not repair old Git objects.
284	
285	```bash
286	dev hygiene repair-encoding --file .specstory/history/session.md --json
287	# Optional explicit deletion instead of the default replacement character:
288	dev hygiene repair-encoding --file notes.txt --invalid remove --json
289	# Review the private proposal; only after the exact artifact writer has exited:
290	dev hygiene repair-encoding --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
291	# Review and stage only the intended repair, then check the actual index:
292	dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
293	```
294	
295	The default `--invalid replace` replaces each contiguous invalid byte run with
296	one `�`; `remove` deletes that run. All valid bytes, including existing `�`,
297	UTF-8 BOMs and line endings, remain unchanged. Explicit files may be selected
298	with repeated `--file`; each source and result must fit 128 MiB, with at most
299	256 files and 192 MiB of proposed output per plan. Valid text is a no-op. Known binary extensions,
300	NUL bytes and UTF-16/32 BOMs require separate encoding review; this command does
301	not guess a legacy encoding or recover the original character.
302	
303	Repair uses signed plans, fresh file identity checks and private raw-byte
304	recovery through `dev hygiene restore`. It does not need a secret scanner.
305	Artifact edits require writer attestation and the live writer guard below,
306	including case variants and nested artifact directories. Encoding repair requires long
307	canonical path components without trailing dots/spaces or DOS short-name spellings. The hook
308	never repairs automatically. Apply changes working files only: a partially
309	staged file keeps its exact index contents, so a staged scan still fails until
310	you review and stage the repair. Do not broadly stage newly appended history.
311	Encoding repair does not redact secrets or prove a complete hygiene scan.
312	
313	## Review and apply replacements
314	
315	```bash
316	dev hygiene redact --report <report-id> --file notes.md --json
317	dev hygiene redact --report <report-id> --finding <finding-id> --json
318	dev hygiene review-path <id>                 # open privately; never paste contents
319	dev hygiene redact --apply --plan <id> --yes
320	# Only after the exact artifact writer exited:
321	dev hygiene redact --apply --plan <id> --yes --writer-stopped
322	```
323	
324	All supported regular text files may be selected. Plans bind the checkout,
325	HEAD/branch, effective policy, scanner inputs, native file identity and content.
326	They are signed private records. An edited plan or stale input requires a new
327	preview. Overlapping matches prefer secret, then known, then generic rules;
328	within a category the longer span wins. The terminal output shows paths, opaque before/after digests and replacement
329	counts. `review-path <id>` locates a private full-content proposal for human
330	inspection. Its integrity is bound to the plan; never paste that file into chat,
331	Git or CI logs. The default output does not echo the original secret.
332	
333	Apply checks the whole selection, then publishes individual guarded transactions
334	with original metadata and private recovery. It retains a partial ledger on
335	failure; never repeat an interrupted operation blindly. Apply and recovery errors
336	keep their underlying cause. On macOS the kernel tags every new file with the
337	writing process's `com.apple.provenance` and ignores attempts to copy it, so a
338	replacement carries the writer's tag rather than the source's. Every other
339	extended attribute must still round-trip, and a changed tag on the source file
340	still makes the operation stale. Index contents, Git history and installed
341	binaries are not changed. Native Windows protections are specific to these
342	opted-in text transactions; other configedit workflows retain their own platform
343	support contracts. Windows preserves owner/group/DACL semantics; files with
344	alternate streams, explicit integrity labels or special attributes require
345	manual preservation.
346	
347	```bash
348	dev hygiene restore --receipt <receipt-id> --json
349	dev hygiene restore --receipt <receipt-id> --apply --yes
350	```
351	
352	Restore refuses files replaced or edited since the recorded transaction. Artifact
353	recovery also needs `--writer-stopped`, and `restore --apply` guards the
354	receipt's exact paths. A disabled/unavailable runtime cannot prove process
355	absence. The post-writer attestation and source revalidation remain necessary,
356	and raw external writers remain outside dev-mediated locks.
357	
358	## Artifact writer guard
359	
360	Redaction, encoding repair, restore, batch `manage` and `dev artifact`
361	finalize/archive/migrate share one live-writer check over their reviewed target
362	files; archiving still leaves source bytes untouched. Any other recognized agent
363	covering the checkout blocks an artifact edit, whatever its status. The calling agent's own pane is exempt only when:
364	
365	- Herdr reports its exact agent session ID (`agent_session` kind `id`, not a
366	  title) and every artifact target is a `.specstory/history/*.md` transcript
367	  with a valid UUID in its actual
368	  SpecStory-generated anchored preamble, proving a different session; or
369	- the caller passes global `--allow-shared-checkout`, asserting disjoint
370	  ownership after confirming the writer exited (for example plans, or
371	  transcripts without a provable preamble).
372	
373	An identified caller-owned live transcript is refused even with the override.
374	Unknown caller identity needs the explicit disjoint-ownership attestation.
375	`--writer-stopped` still attests that the exact recorder exited; neither flag skips
376	source revalidation.
377	
378	Use the [manual dogfood checklist](../reference/hygiene-dogfood.md) for this repo.
379

52		repo, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, o.Root)
53		if err != nil {
54			return nil, errors.New("hygiene requires a Git checkout")
55		}
56		id, err := gitx.DirectoryIdentity(repo.GitCommonDir)
57		if err != nil {
58			return nil, errors.New("cannot identify repository")
59		}
60		s := &Service{Root: repo.Root, CacheDir: o.CacheDir, Common: repo.GitCommonDir, RepoID: digest([]byte(id)), Global: o.GlobalPolicy, Policy: DefaultPolicy(), Engine: o.Engine, policyInputs: map[string]string{}, PublicOnly: o.PublicOnly}
61		state, e := pathx.Canonical(o.StateDir)
62		if e != nil {
63			return nil, errors.New("private hygiene state path unavailable")
64		}
65		s.Dir = filepath.Join(state, "hygiene", "repos", s.RepoID)
66		for parent := s.Dir; ; parent = filepath.Dir(parent) {
67			if _, e := os.Lstat(filepath.Join(parent, ".git")); e == nil {
68				return nil, errors.New("private hygiene state must be outside Git")
69			}
70			if filepath.Dir(parent) == parent {
71				break
72			}
73		}
74		if s.Engine == nil {
75			s.Engine = Gitleaks{}
76		}
77		for _, layer := range []struct {
78			label, path string
79			private     bool
80		}{{"global", o.GlobalPolicy, false}, {"repository", filepath.Join(s.Root, ".dev-cli", "hygiene.toml"), false}, {"local", filepath.Join(s.Dir, "policy.toml"), true}} {
81			if layer.path == "" || (o.PublicOnly && layer.label != "repository") {
82				continue
83			}
84			b, err := safefile.ReadStablePath(ctx, layer.path, 1<<20)

88			}
89			if err != nil {
90				return nil, errors.New("cannot read hygiene policy safely")
91			}
92			if layer.private {
93				info, e := os.Lstat(layer.path)

95					return nil, e
96				}
97				if e = privatefile.Check(layer.path, info, false); e != nil {

100			}

120	func (s *Service) checkInputs(ctx context.Context) error {
121		id, err := gitx.DirectoryIdentity(s.Common)
122		if err != nil || digest([]byte(id)) != s.RepoID {
123			return ErrStale
124		}
125		for p, want := range s.policyInputs {
126			b, err := safefile.ReadStablePath(ctx, p, 1<<20)
127			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) && want == "absent" {
128				continue
129			}
130			if err != nil || digest(b) != want {
131				return ErrStale
132			}
133		}
134		return nil
135	}
136	func (s *Service) prepare(ctx context.Context) error {
137		if err := privatefile.EnsureDir(s.Dir); err != nil {
138			return err
139		}
140		return lockx.WithDir(ctx, s.Dir, "hygiene", func() error {
141			p := filepath.Join(s.Dir, "key")
142			b, err := safefile.ReadStablePath(ctx, p, 64)
143			if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
144				b = make([]byte, 32)
145				if _, err = rand.Read(b); err != nil {
146					return err
147				}
148				if err = configedit.WritePrivate(ctx, p, b, false); err != nil {
149					return errors.New("cannot create private hygiene key: " + feedback.Sanitize(err.Error()))
150				}
151			} else if err != nil {
152				return err
153			}
154			info, err := os.Lstat(p)
155			if err != nil || len(b) != 32 {
156				return errors.New("invalid private hygiene key")
157			}
158			if err = privatefile.Check(p, info, false); err != nil {
159				return err
160			}
161			s.key = b
162			return nil
163		})
164	}
165	func newID() string { return uuid.NewString() }
166	func safeRecordID(id string) bool {
167		_, err := uuid.Parse(id)
168		return err == nil && strings.ToLower(id) == id
169	}
170	func (s *Service) save(ctx context.Context, id string, v any) error {
171		if !safeRecordID(id) {
172			return errors.New("invalid hygiene record ID")
173		}
174		b, err := json.Marshal(v)
175		if err != nil || len(b) > MaxRecordBytes {
176			return errors.New("hygiene record exceeds byte limit")
177		}
178		if err = ctx.Err(); err != nil {
179			return err
180		}

2	package hygiene
3	
4	import (

19	type Mode string
20	
21	const (
22		Block Mode = "block"
23		Warn  Mode = "warn"
24		Off   Mode = "off"
25	)
26	
27	func validMode(m Mode) bool { return m == Block || m == Warn || m == Off }
28	
29	var identifier = regexp.MustCompile(`^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]{0,95}$`)
30	
31	type Rule struct {
32		ID          string   `toml:"id" json:"id"`
33		Kind        string   `toml:"kind" json:"kind"`
34		Value       string   `toml:"value" json:"-"`
35		Replacement string   `toml:"replacement" json:"replacement"`
36		Action      Mode     `toml:"action" json:"action,omitempty"`
37		Paths       []string `toml:"paths" json:"paths,omitempty"`
38	}
39	type Exception struct {
40		Finding string `toml:"finding" json:"finding,omitempty"`
41		Rule    string `toml:"rule" json:"rule,omitempty"`
42		Path    string `toml:"path" json:"path,omitempty"`
43		Pattern string `toml:"pattern" json:"-"`
44		Reason  string `toml:"reason" json:"reason"`
45	}
46	type Policy struct {
47		Version    int         `toml:"version" json:"version"`
48		Secrets    Mode        `toml:"secrets" json:"secrets"`
49		Known      Mode        `toml:"known" json:"known"`
50		Generic    Mode        `toml:"generic" json:"generic"`
51		Rules      []Rule      `toml:"rules" json:"rules,omitempty"`
52		Exceptions []Exception `toml:"exceptions" json:"exceptions,omitempty"`
53	}
54	
55	func DefaultPolicy() Policy { return Policy{Version: 1, Secrets: Block, Known: Block, Generic: Warn} }
56	func DecodePolicy(data []byte) (Policy, error) {
57		var p Policy
58		meta, err := toml.Decode(string(data), &p)
59		if err != nil || len(meta.Undecoded()) != 0 {
60			return p, errors.New("invalid hygiene policy; check keys and TOML locally")
61		}
62		if p.Version != 1 {
63			return p, errors.New("unsupported hygiene policy version")
64		}
65		for _, m := range []Mode{p.Secrets, p.Known, p.Generic} {
66			if m != "" && !validMode(m) {
67				return p, errors.New("hygiene modes must be block, warn or off")
68			}
69		}
70		seen := map[string]bool{}
71		for _, r := range p.Rules {
72			if seen[r.ID] {
73				return p, errors.New("duplicate hygiene rule ID")
74			}
75			seen[r.ID] = true
76			if _, err := compileRule(r); err != nil {
77				return p, err
78			}
79		}
80		for _, e := range p.Exceptions {
81			if strings.TrimSpace(e.Reason) == "" {
82				return p, errors.New("exceptions require a reason")
83			}
84			if e.Finding != "" {
85				if len(e.Finding) != 64 {
86					return p, errors.New("invalid finding exception")
87				}
88				continue
89			}
90			if !identifier.MatchString(e.Rule) || e.Path == "" || !strings.HasPrefix(e.Pattern, "^") || !strings.HasSuffix(e.Pattern, "$") {
91				return p, errors.New("portable exceptions require rule, path, anchored match pattern and reason")
92			}
93			if _, err := regexp.Compile(e.Pattern); err != nil {
94				return p, errors.New("invalid exception pattern")
95			}
96		}
97		return p, nil
98	}
99	func MergePolicy(a, b Policy) Policy {
100		if b.Secrets != "" {
101			a.Secrets = b.Secrets
102		}
103		if b.Known != "" {
104			a.Known = b.Known
105		}
106		if b.Generic != "" {
107			a.Generic = b.Generic
108		}
109		rules := map[string]Rule{}
110		for _, r := range a.Rules {
111			rules[r.ID] = r
112		}
113		for _, r := range b.Rules {
114			rules[r.ID] = r
115		}
116		a.Rules = nil
117		for _, r := range rules {
118			a.Rules = append(a.Rules, r)
119		}
120		sort.Slice(a.Rules, func(i, j int) bool { return a.Rules[i].ID < a.Rules[j].ID })
121		a.Exceptions = append(a.Exceptions, b.Exceptions...)
122		return a
123	}
124	func policyBytes(p Policy) ([]byte, error) {
125		var b strings.Builder
126		err := toml.NewEncoder(&b).Encode(p)
127		return []byte(b.String()), err
128	}
129	func digest(b []byte) string { v := sha256.Sum256(b); return hex.EncodeToString(v[:]) }
130	func keyedID(key []byte, parts ...string) string {
131		h := hmac.New(sha256.New, key)
132		for _, p := range parts {
133			h.Write([]byte(p))
134			h.Write([]byte{0})
135		}
136		return hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil))
137	}
138	func policyDigest(p Policy) string { b, _ := policyBytes(p); return digest(b) }
139

141		rule Rule
142		re   *regexp.Regexp
143		cidr netip.Prefix
144	}

66	func (s *Service) repoToken(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
67		id, err := gitx.DirectoryIdentity(s.Root)
68		if err != nil {
69			return "", err
70		}
71		head, headErr := gitBytes(ctx, s.Root, nil, "rev-parse", "--verify", "HEAD")
72		branch, branchErr := gitBytes(ctx, s.Root, nil, "symbolic-ref", "-q", "HEAD")
73		if headErr != nil {
74			if branchErr != nil {
75				return "", headErr
76			}
77			present, e := gitBytes(ctx, s.Root, nil, "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname)", strings.TrimSpace(string(branch)))
78			if e != nil || len(present) != 0 {
79				return "", headErr
80			}
81			head = []byte("unborn")
82		}
83		return digest([]byte(id + string(head) + string(branch))), nil
84	}
85	func (s *Service) newPlan(ctx context.Context, kind string) (planRecord, error) {
86		if err := s.prepare(ctx); err != nil {
87			return planRecord{}, err
88		}
89		token, err := s.repoToken(ctx)
90		if err != nil {
91			return planRecord{}, err
92		}
93		return planRecord{Plan: Plan{SchemaVersion: 1, Kind: kind, ID: newID(), Status: "prepared", Files: []FileChange{}}, Root: s.Root, RepoID: s.RepoID, RepoToken: token, PolicyDigest: policyDigest(s.Policy)}, nil
94	}

96		editor, err := configedit.NewTextFile(ctx, path, desired)

109		p.Plan.Files = append(p.Plan.Files, FileChange{File: s.displayPath(file), Replacements: replacements, BeforeDigest: keyedID(s.key, c.BeforeDigest), AfterDigest: keyedID(s.key, c.AfterDigest)})

22	                     Git index.
23	  --no-redact        Disable gitleaks output masking. The wrapper still never
24	                     emits Secret or Match fields.

26	  --verbose          Print bounded wrapper progress; scanner output remains
27	                     suppressed because it may contain secret material.
