361	// inside Herdr the existing client switches immediately; outside Herdr a new
362	// client attaches after the caller has left any alternate-screen UI.
363	func (h *Herdr) Activate(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
364		if handle == "" {
365			return nil
366		}
367		if err := h.Focus(ctx, handle); err != nil {
368			return err
369		}
370		if os.Getenv("HERDR_ENV") != "" {
371			return nil
372		}
373		return runInteractive(ctx, h.bin)
374	}
375	
376	// Focus selects a workspace on the ordinary local adapter. Session-scoped
377	// remote preparation forbids this server-wide operation; its caller must use
378	// an explicit native client activation capability separately.
379	func (h *Herdr) Focus(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
380		if h.session != "" {
381			return errors.New("scoped remote preparation cannot change server-wide client focus")
382		}
383		if handle == "" {
384			return nil
385		}
386		return h.call(ctx, nil, "workspace", "focus", handle)
387	}
388	
389	// OpenWorktree implements WorktreeOpener: it registers an already-created git
390	// worktree as a herdr workspace, which is what makes the checkout appear in
391	// the sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and
392	// ahead/behind row.
393	func (h *Herdr) OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
394		args := []string{"worktree", "open"}
395		if source := h.parentWorktreeSource(ctx, path); source != "" {
396			// Pin the canonical parent checkout instead of relying on the calling
397			// pane. This preserves native nested grouping even when dev is invoked
398			// from a different Herdr workspace.
399			args = append(args, "--cwd", source)
400		} else if h.session != "" {
401			return OpenResult{}, errors.New("cannot resolve an explicit parent checkout for scoped Herdr preparation")
402		}
403		args = append(args, "--path", path, "--no-focus")
404		if label != "" {
405			args = append(args, "--label", label)
406		}
407		var res struct {
408			Workspace   herdrWorkspace `json:"workspace"`
409			Worktree    herdrWorktree  `json:"worktree"`
410			RootPane    herdrPane      `json:"root_pane"`
411			AlreadyOpen *bool          `json:"already_open"`
412		}
413		if err := h.call(ctx, &res, args...); err != nil {
414			if h.session != "" {
415				return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("scoped Herdr worktree open failed; any partial workspace is retained for inspection: %w", err)
416			}
417			// Fall back to a plain workspace: the checkout being visible matters
418			// more than it being tagged with git provenance. A fallback root pane is
419			// withheld so callers cannot mistake it for a first-class worktree target.
420			fallback, fallbackErr := h.Open(ctx, path, label)
421			fallback.RootPaneID = ""
422			fallback.Surface = "workspace"
423			return fallback, fallbackErr
424		}
425		handle := res.Workspace.WorkspaceID
426		if handle == "" {
427			handle = res.Worktree.OpenWorkspaceID
428		}
429		if handle == "" {
430			return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("herdr worktree open: response has no workspace id")
431		}
432		if res.AlreadyOpen == nil {
433			// Without this protocol field, the handle may belong to a reused
434			// workspace. Do not close it or expose its pane as newly created.
435			return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("herdr worktree open: response does not say whether the workspace was reused")
436		}
437		created := !*res.AlreadyOpen
438		if created && (res.RootPane.PaneID == "" || res.RootPane.WorkspaceID != handle) {
439			return OpenResult{}, h.rejectCreatedWorkspace(ctx, handle,
440				"herdr worktree open: new workspace response has no correlated root pane")
441		}
442		rootPaneID := ""
443		if created {
444			rootPaneID = res.RootPane.PaneID
445		}
446		return OpenResult{
447			Handle: handle, Surface: "worktree", Opened: true,
448			Created: created, RootPaneID: rootPaneID,
449		}, nil
450	}
451	
452	func (h *Herdr) rejectCreatedWorkspace(ctx context.Context, handle, reason string) error {
453		if h.session != "" {
454			return fmt.Errorf("%s; retained incomplete workspace %s in Herdr session %s for inspection", reason, handle, h.session)
455		}
456		if err := h.Close(ctx, handle); err != nil {
457			return fmt.Errorf("%s; could not close incomplete workspace %s: %w", reason, handle, err)
458		}
459		return fmt.Errorf("%s; closed incomplete workspace %s", reason, handle)
460	}
461	
462	func (h *Herdr) parentWorktreeSource(ctx context.Context, path string) string {
463		if h.worktreeSource != nil {
464			return h.worktreeSource(ctx, path)
465		}
466		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "-C", path, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain")
467		out, err := cmd.Output()
468		if err != nil {
469			return ""
470		}
471		var parent string
472		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(out), "\n") {
473			switch {
474			case strings.HasPrefix(line, "worktree ") && parent == "":
475				parent = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "worktree "))
476			case line == "" && parent != "":
477				if info, err := os.Stat(parent); err == nil && info.IsDir() {
478					return filepath.Clean(parent)
479				}
480				return ""
481			}
482		}
483		return ""
484	}
485	
486	// Close implements Runtime. This ends herdr's session state only — it never
487	// removes the checkout, the worktree or the branch, matching herdr's own
488	// separation of `workspace close` from `worktree remove`.
489	func (h *Herdr) Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
490		if handle == "" {
491			return nil
492		}
493		return h.call(ctx, nil, "workspace", "close", handle)
494	}

163	// scanRepo collects everything in one repository that looks like work in
164	// flight but is not yet recorded.
165	func scanRepo(ctx context.Context, app *App, r repo.Repo, sessions []runtime.Session,
166		known map[string]bool, target task.State, doWorktrees, doSessions, doBranches bool) []candidate {
167	
168		var out []candidate
169		seen := map[string]bool{}
170	
171		add := func(branch, worktree, reason string, state task.State) {
172			if branch == "" || seen[branch] {
173				return
174			}
175			id := task.MakeID(r.Name, branch)
176			if known[id] {
177				return
178			}
179			seen[branch] = true
180			mode := task.ModeBranch
181			if worktree != "" {
182				mode = task.ModeWorktree
183			}
184			out = append(out, candidate{
185				Reason: reason,
186				Task: &task.Task{
187					ID:           id,
188					Name:         branch,
189					Repo:         r.Name,
190					RepoPath:     r.Path,
191					Branch:       branch,
192					Base:         gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, r.Path),
193					WorktreePath: worktree,
194					Mode:         mode,
195					State:        state,
196					Owner:        config.Hostname(),
197				},
198			})
199		}
200	
201		worktrees, err := gitx.Worktrees(ctx, r.Path)
202		if err != nil {
203			return nil
204		}
205	
206		if doWorktrees {
207			for _, w := range worktrees {
208				if w.Main || w.Branch == "" || w.Prunable {
209					continue
210				}
211				// A harness's turn-scoped worktree is not a change stream a human
212				// tracks; adopting those would fill the inventory with noise that
213				// the harness will delete on its own.
214				if inventory.IsEphemeralWorktree(w.Path, w.Branch) {
215					continue
216				}
217				state := target
218				reason := "existing worktree"
219				if sessionAt(sessions, w.Path) != nil {
220					state, reason = task.Hot, "worktree with a live session"
221				}
222				add(w.Branch, w.Path, reason, state)
223			}
224		}
225	
226		if doSessions {
227			for i := range sessions {
228				for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
229					if d != r.Path {
230						continue
231					}
232					st, err := gitx.StatusOf(ctx, r.Path)
233					if err != nil || st.Branch == "" {
234						continue
235					}
236					add(st.Branch, "", "live session in the main checkout", task.Hot)
237				}
238			}
239		}
240	
241		if doBranches {
242			for _, branch := range unmergedBranches(ctx, r.Path) {
243				add(branch, worktreePathFor(worktrees, branch), "branch ahead of the base", target)
244			}
245		}
246		return out
247	}
248	
249	func sessionAt(sessions []runtime.Session, dir string) *runtime.Session {
250		for i := range sessions {
251			for _, d := range sessions[i].Dirs {
252				if d == dir {
253					return &sessions[i]
254				}
255			}
256		}
257		return nil
258	}
259	
260	func worktreePathFor(worktrees []gitx.Worktree, branch string) string {
261		for _, w := range worktrees {
262			if w.Branch == branch && !w.Main {
263				return w.Path
264			}
265		}
266		return ""
267	}
268	
269	// unmergedBranches lists local branches carrying commits the default branch
270	// does not — unfinished work that would otherwise be invisible to dev.
271	func unmergedBranches(ctx context.Context, repoPath string) []string {
272		base := gitx.DefaultBranch(ctx, repoPath)
273		if base == "" {
274			return nil
275		}
276		out, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname:short)", "refs/heads/")
277		if err != nil {
278			return nil
279		}
280		var branches []string
281		for _, b := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
282			b = strings.TrimSpace(b)
283			if b == "" || b == base || inventory.IsEphemeralWorktree("", b) {
284				continue
285			}
286			// Contained in the base means the work has already landed.
287			if _, err := gitx.Run(ctx, repoPath, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", b, base); err == nil {
288				continue
289			}
290			branches = append(branches, b)
291		}
292		return branches
293	}

1	// Package runtime abstracts the terminal multiplexer that hosts a checkout.
2	//
3	// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
4	// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.
8	package runtime
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"fmt"
13		"os"
14		"os/exec"
15		"strings"
16	
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
18	)

38		Handle string
39		Label  string
40		// Herdr's first-class workspace identity is independent of pane cwd.
41		// An observed parent/generic workspace must not be retired as a child.
42		WorkspaceIdentityObserved bool

51		AgentStatus string
52		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
53		AgentSessions []string

55		// mixed-workspace retirement checks.
56		Panes   []Pane
57		Focused bool
58	}

60	// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
61	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
62		for _, d := range s.Dirs {
63			// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
64			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
65			// $HOME active.
66			if inside, err := pathx.Contains(dir, d); err == nil && inside {
67				return true
68			}
69		}
70		return false
71	}

78		Surface    string
79		Opened     bool

82	}

89		WorkspaceID string
90		Agent       string
91		Name        string
92		Status      string
93		CWD         string
94		// Session is the runtime-reported agent session identity as
95		// "provider:id", empty unless the backend reports an exact session id.
96		Session string
97	}

99	// AgentActivityLister is an optional runtime capability. Core runtimes need not
100	// know about agents; Herdr implements it because its pane model can identify the

104	}

109	type CurrentPaneResolver interface {
110		CurrentPaneID(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
111	}

114	// Open deliberately remains detached so creation commands can run in the
115	// background. Navigation commands call Activate after their own terminal UI
116	// has been torn down: inside a multiplexer this switches the current client;
117	// outside it attaches a new client and blocks until the user detaches.
118	type Activator interface {
119		Activate(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
120	}
121	
122	// PaneRunner is the optional exact-pane command surface. The command is shell
123	// text for the pane's existing interactive shell, not argv for a child process
124	// started by dev. Implementations must not include command text in errors.
125	type PaneRunner interface {

127	}

133	}

136	// A reused workspace is never acceptable because destructive coordination must

139		OpenExternalCoordinator(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error)
140	}

142	// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
143	// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
144	// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
145	type Runtime interface {
146		// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
147		Name() string
148		// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
149		// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
150		Available() bool
151		// Open makes dir live. Its result distinguishes a newly created surface from
152		// a reused one and may carry a root pane proven by that same create response.
153		Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error)
154		// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
155		// task entry.
156		Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
157		// List enumerates live sessions.
158		List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
159		// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
160		// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
161		Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
162	}

164	// WorktreeOpener is implemented by backends that understand git worktrees and
165	// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
166	// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
167	type WorktreeOpener interface {
168		OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (OpenResult, error)
169	}

171	// ErrUnavailable reports a backend that is not usable on this machine.
172	type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }
173	
174	func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
175		return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
176	}
177	
178	// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
179	//
180	// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
181	// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then zellij,
182	// then None.
183	// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
184	func Select(backend string) Runtime {
185		herdr, tmux, zellij, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), NewZellij(), None{}
186		switch backend {
187		case "herdr":
188			return herdr
189		case "tmux":
190			return tmux
191		case "zellij":
192			return zellij
193		case "none":
194			return none
195		case "", "auto":
196			if herdr.Available() {
197				return herdr
198			}
199			if tmux.Available() {
200				return tmux
201			}
202			if zellij.Available() {
203				return zellij
204			}
205			return none
206		}
207		return none
208	}
209	
210	// All returns every backend, for `dev doctor` to report on.
211	func All() []Runtime { return []Runtime{NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), NewZellij(), None{}} }
212	
213	// haveBinary reports whether name is on PATH.
214	func haveBinary(name string) bool {
215		_, err := exec.LookPath(name)
216		return err == nil
217	}
218	
219	// runInteractive connects a multiplexer client directly to dev's terminal.
220	// Runtime protocol calls use captured stdout/stderr; attach clients must not,
221	// because they own the terminal until the user detaches.
222	func runInteractive(ctx context.Context, bin string, args ...string) error {
223		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bin, args...)
224		cmd.Stdin, cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr
225		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
226			return fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %w", bin, strings.Join(args, " "), err)
227		}
228		return nil
229	}

10	// openCheckout makes a directory live, asking the backend to treat it as a git
11	// worktree when it knows how — that is what groups the checkout under its
12	// parent repo in a sidebar instead of listing it as an unrelated directory.
13	func openCheckout(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, dir, label string) (runtime.OpenResult, error) {
14		if wo, ok := rt.(runtime.WorktreeOpener); ok {
15			return wo.OpenWorktree(ctx, dir, label)
16		}
17		return rt.Open(ctx, dir, label)
18	}
19	
20	// activateRuntime performs the interactive half of navigation. Runtime Open
21	// calls are detached by design; explicit open/resume actions opt into either
22	// switching the current multiplexer client or attaching from a plain shell.
23	func activateRuntime(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, handle string) error {
24		if rt == nil || rt.Name() == "none" || handle == "" {
25			return nil
26		}
27		activator, ok := rt.(runtime.Activator)
28		if !ok {
29			return errors.New("runtime " + rt.Name() + " cannot activate sessions")
30		}
31		return activator.Activate(ctx, handle)
32	}

35		if rt == nil || rt.Name() == "none" {
36			return ""
37		}
38		return opened.Handle
39	}

215		root.SetHelpCommand(&cobra.Command{Hidden: true, Use: "no-help"})
216		// Inherited by every subcommand, so a bad flag anywhere in the tree is
217		// reported as a usage mistake rather than a bare error line.
218		root.SetFlagErrorFunc(func(_ *cobra.Command, err error) error {
219			return asUsageError(err)
220		})
221		root.SetOut(out)
222		root.SetErr(errOut)
223		defaultHelp := root.HelpFunc()
224		root.SetHelpFunc(func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
225			var buf bytes.Buffer
226			previous := cmd.OutOrStdout()
227			cmd.SetOut(&buf)
228			defaultHelp(cmd, args)
229			cmd.SetOut(previous)
230			fmt.Fprint(previous, renderCobraHelp(buf.String(), app.outStyle()))
231		})
232		enforceUsageErrors(root)
233		annotateHelp(root)
234		return root
235	}

237	// Execute runs the CLI and maps errors to exit codes. SilenceErrors and
238	// SilenceUsage are set on the root, so nothing reaches the terminal unless it
239	// is printed here; ExecuteC hands back the command that failed so a usage
240	// mistake can be answered with that command's usage rather than the root's.
241	func Execute() int {
242		trace, tracePath, traceErr := traceFromEnvironment()
243		app := &App{
244			In: os.Stdin, Out: os.Stdout, Err: os.Stderr,
245			trace: trace, tracePath: tracePath, traceOnce: &sync.Once{},
246		}
247		if traceErr != nil {
248			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dev: warning: performance trace disabled: %v\n", traceErr)
249		}
250		app.trace.Mark(perftrace.CLIExecuteBegin, perftrace.Fields{})
251		defer app.finishTrace()
252	
253		finishRoot := app.trace.Start(perftrace.CLIRootBuild, perftrace.Fields{})
254		root := newRootCommand(app)
255		finishRoot(perftrace.OutcomeSuccess)
256		cmd, err := root.ExecuteC()
257		if err == nil {
258			return 0
259		}
260		var childExit interface{ ExitCode() int }
261		if errors.As(err, &childExit) {
262			if code := childExit.ExitCode(); code >= 0 && code <= 255 {
263				return code
264			}
265		}
266		style := styleForWriter(os.Stderr, colorModeFromArgs(os.Args[1:]))
267		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, style.danger("dev:")+" "+err.Error())
268		if cmd != nil && wantsUsage(err) {
269			fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, renderCobraHelp(cmd.UsageString(), style))
270		}
271		var nativeError *dotfile.NativeError
272		if errors.As(err, &nativeError) {
273			return nativeError.ExitCode()
274		}
275		return 1
276	}

61	func sameCleanPath(a, b string) bool {

70			left = filepath.Clean(resolved)

73			right = filepath.Clean(resolved)

```text
1	# Worktree ownership
2	
3	Submodule initialization is core Git acquisition, before provisioning/runtime, and defaults to recursive pinned checkouts. `--no-provision` does not skip it; `--submodules=none` does. Gitlink children are independent submodule clones, not nested managed linked worktrees. Read `submodules.md` for selection and explicit disposal rules.
4	
5	Read this before creating a worktree, sharing a checkout between agents, or when
6	a new checkout lacks dependencies, env files, or launcher backend state.
7	
8	## The rule
9	
10	| Change boundary | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
11	|---|---|---|---|
12	| Durable feature/fix/experiment/handoff | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path` | until external `dev retire` |
13	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation | Claude Code | `.claude/worktrees/` | managed by that harness; do not assume artifact relocation |
14	| Runtime workspace/panes | Herdr | per-host runtime | until explicitly closed |
15	| Rendered agent history | SpecStory | process launch checkout | until committed/removed with that checkout |
16	
17	Use a `dev` worktree for independent approaches or any change stream whose code,
18	history, or plan must remain reviewable. Agents with explicitly disjoint file
19	ownership may share one checkout, but `--allow-shared-checkout` is a deliberate
20	coordination override—not a default.
21	
22	`EnterWorktree` changes an agent's working location; it does not prove an
23	existing SpecStory wrapper/watcher rebound its source/output paths. Start the
24	new process from the target worktree root.
25	
26	## Why dev creates the checkout
27	
28	`dev` runs `git worktree add`, then asks Herdr to run
29	`worktree open --path <path> --no-focus`. Path policy therefore remains stable
30	on machines without Herdr, while Herdr still displays repo/branch provenance.
31	A fallback plain workspace is reported as such and is not an exact agent launch
32	target.
33	
34	Never nest a durable worktree inside another checkout. Every watcher, language
35	server, backup tool and search then sees a second copy of the repository.
36	
37	Herdr's native **New worktree** action is still valid for an external,
38	unmanaged checkout. When the canonical repository is under a configured scan
39	root, Git registration lets dev discover the checkout without scanning
40	`~/.herdr/worktrees`; dev does not auto-adopt, relocate, or provision it. Run
41	`dev wt provision <path>` if it needs the project environment and `dev adopt`
42	followed by `dev adopt --apply` only when it should enter the durable task
43	lifecycle. For one exact checkout, `dev flow [repo]` offers plan-first
44	metadata-only Adopt and clean branch-preserving Remove Checkout. It never removes
45	the canonical checkout or a harness/conflicting/locked/prunable/task-claimed row,
46	and it does not prune repository-wide stale registrations.
47	
48	## Paths
49	
50	Default:
51	
52	```text
53	~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>
54	```
55	
56	Configurable through `paths.worktree_root` and `paths.worktree_path`, with
57	`worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`, `host`, and `date`
58	variables plus `slug`, `lower`, and `base` filters.
59	
60	Always pass `--base` for unattended creation so the intended starting point is
61	explicit. `dev start` and `dev wt create` otherwise resolve the repository's
62	default branch; they do not use whichever feature happens to be checked out.
63	
64	## Provisioning
65	
66	A worktree is a clean checkout. `dev wt create` and `dev start` build and apply
67	an inspectable plan:
68	
69	```bash
70	dev wt plan
71	dev wt plan --write
72	dev wt provision --dry-run
73	```
74	
75	Effective settings come from global config or committed repo
76	`.dev-cli/config.toml` (legacy `.dev.toml` remains readable):
77	
78	```toml
79	[worktree]
80	include = [".env", ".env.local"]
81	link = []
82	post_create = "auto"
83	strategy = "reinstall"
84	```
85	
86	An executable `post_create` from `.dev-cli/config.toml` requires approval of its
87	exact content hash with `dev config trust <repo> --yes`. Legacy `.dev.toml`
88	retains its compatibility behavior.
89	
90	Only paths that are both explicitly included and genuinely gitignored are
91	copied. Tracked files already have the branch-correct version. Included files
92	must remain the same regular file from validation through open; source swaps and
93	symlinked destination parents are refused. Existing destinations are reported
94	as skipped, never falsely as copied, and file contents are never logged.
95	
96	This is local provisioning only. Off-machine `dev fleet files` deliberately uses
97	a separate `[local_files].include` allowlist plus explicit `--to`; never infer
98	export permission from `[worktree].include`.
99	
100	### Project-local Claude backend state
101	
102	`.claude/settings.local.json` stays gitignored and is **not** a universal default
103	include. The verified `claude-copilot-once` wrapper preserves an existing
104	Copilot pin and creates/removes only its own pin when one was absent;
105	`codex-copilot-once` injects its backend via CLI. Neither needs a copied project
106	file. Claude's Copilot proxy must already be running; the Codex path may
107	self-start its proxy flow.
108	
109	An explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude profile may opt in exactly:
110	
111	```toml
112	[worktree]
113	include = [".env", ".env.local", ".claude/settings.local.json"]
114	```
115	
116	Verify the file arrived before launch. If absent, stop instead of allowing the
117	launcher to fall back silently to another backend. `dev` logs the relative path
118	only, never its contents.
119	
120	## Dependency strategies
121	
122	- `reinstall`: safe default; run lockfile-derived installer.
123	- `copy`: duplicate path-independent dependency trees.
124	- `link`: explicit and usually unsafe for mutable dependencies.
125	- `skip`: for external/container-managed environments.
126	
127	`dev` refuses unsound choices, such as copied/linked Python virtualenvs, and
128	reports missing tools or failed setup without deleting the usable checkout.
129	
130	## Cleanup
131	
132	- `dev wt rm <branch>` removes only the checkout after external runtime safety checks; branch survives.
133	- `dev park` records WARM; when called from its own runtime it leaves that runtime alive for normal exit.
134	- `dev park --cold --push` closes eligible runtime state and removes the pushed worktree only from outside.
135	- `dev done --ff` integrates and records MERGED; runtime/worktree/branch survive.
136	- `dev done --pr` leaves everything active for review.
137	- `dev retire` is the only complete close/wait/remove/reap path.
138	- `dev sweep` reports first; `--apply` routes cleanup through retire.
139	- From canonical main, `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` also audits unmanaged
140	  linked worktrees whose branches are contained in main. Agents must present
141	  that report for user confirmation before applying; branches are retained
142	  unless `--delete-branches` was separately approved.
143	- From any canonical non-bare checkout, `dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees` audits
144	  Claude Workflow isolation through bounded provider metadata plus fresh Git,
145	  task, artifact, caller, and every available runtime. The path/branch naming
146	  pattern is only a candidate label and never deletion proof. Claude Code 2.1.259
147	  exposes no branch/HEAD/non-replayable registration identity, so its current
148	  claims remain unknown/report-only rather than authorizing a reused path.
149	- Ephemeral apply is TTY/per-item only and revalidates a stable fingerprint under
150	  a common-dir lock before plain non-force removal. It never closes runtimes,
151	  prunes, deletes provider metadata, or repairs dirty/ignored work. Branches stay
152	  by default; deletion needs separately approved `--delete-branches --base REF`
153	  and unchanged containment/zero-unique proof before `git branch -d`.
154	
155	Linked-worktree removal with gitlinks still requires `--recursive`. A child path
156	that is absent or truly empty, with no retained Git store and no ownership or
157	observation blockers, needs no initialization or remote proof merely for removal.
158	Deinitialized data and orphan stores are not empty. Exact reviewed empty modules
159	admin directories may be pruned under locks with native directory-only guards;
160	empty checkout directories stay for ordinary non-force Git removal. Real child
161	stores retain full recovery proofs, journals and rollback. Never replace a
162	refusal with recursive file deletion. See `submodules.md`.
163	
164	Bare `dev done` on a TTY classifies dirty content against the base before
165	offering commit-all or discard-all; unique discard requires `DROP`. Dirty
166	checkout removal may require explicit force, but caller/runtime safety is never
167	bypassable. Herdr `done` is not a cleanup signal, and `--cold --keep-session` is
168	rejected. Never raw-force-remove an agent's cwd.
169	
170	When unrelated dirty bytes block the canonical fast-forward target, the same
171	wizard may use exact stash+restore for ordinary staged, unstaged, and untracked
172	work. Dirty submodules and nested repositories require separate preservation;
173	restore conflicts keep the exact stash and the task rather than claiming DONE.
174	
175	## Triage cleanup batches
176	
177	`dev triage` adds a strict ignored-data guard to its reviewed linked-checkout
178	cleanup. All ignored paths block by default. The operator may declare exact
179	clone-bound disposable relative directories; previews expose the affected paths
180	and sizes and removal requires the displayed CLEAN token. Nested repositories,
181	submodules, harness claims, unknown occupancy and canonical checkouts stay
182	protected. The extra guard runs inside the shared repository lock and directly
183	before removal. Branches and common directories are retained. See
184	[local triage](local-triage.md).
185
```

```text
1	# dev and Herdr
2	
3	Read this on a Herdr machine, when task state should appear in the sidebar, or
4	when a `dev start --json` result will be used to launch an agent.
5	
6	## Division of responsibility
7	
8	```
9	Herdr       per-host workspace, pane, process and live-agent state
10	dev         durable task, branch and checkout lifecycle
11	SpecStory   history writer rooted at the launched process checkout
12	Git         durable commits, transcript and plan
13	```
14	
15	Herdr is not synced between machines. `dev` persists an advisory runtime handle
16	with its owning backend name, revalidates the handle against live checkout
17	coverage before close/resume, and reopens stale handles. This prevents a Herdr
18	handle being sent to Tmux/none after config changes. Legacy nameless handles are
19	used only after exact current-backend validation. Root-pane data stays transient.
20	
21	## What dev asks Herdr to do
22	
23	| dev operation | Herdr command |
24	|---|---|
25	| list live sessions | `workspace list` + `pane list` |
26	| list pane-level agent activity | `agent list` |
27	| inspect exact foreground programs | `pane process-info --pane <id>` |
28	| open a checkout | `workspace create --cwd <dir> --no-focus --label <name>` |
29	| open a worktree | `worktree open --cwd <parent-root> --path <path> --no-focus --label <repo/branch>` |
30	| activate an opened checkout | `workspace focus <id>`; outside Herdr, attach the default client |
31	| dispatch an explicit start command | `pane run <exact-root-pane-id> <command>` |
32	| close a session | `workspace close <id>` |
33	| show task state | `workspace report-metadata <id> --source dev --token …` |
34	
35	`dev` creates worktrees with Git and only asks Herdr to open them. It derives
36	the canonical parent checkout from Git and passes it with `--cwd`, so grouping
37	does not depend on whichever Herdr pane invoked `dev`. First-class `worktree
38	open` gives the child native repository/worktree grouping plus branch/ahead-
39	behind data. Worktree-mode `dev start` uses the same `repo/branch`
40	label as `dev wt create`; no special origin labels or metadata are needed.
41	
42	A plain-workspace fallback reports `surface=workspace` honestly. A root pane is
43	automatically launchable only when the same successful `worktree open` response
44	proves a newly created layout. Reuse, fallback, missing/malformed responses,
45	Tmux, and the `none` runtime never supply a launchable pane. `--no-focus`
46	preserves the caller's context; never substitute the focused/current pane.
47	
48	`dev start --run '<shell command>'` consumes that proof directly, dispatches
49	opaque shell text without persisting or echoing it, and returns after Herdr
50	accepts the command. It does not wait for completion or report the command's
51	exit status. `--focus` remains independent and runs only after successful
52	dispatch. `--json` stays a separate pure creation contract.
53	
54	Read `parallel-agents.md` for exact machine validation, pane verification,
55	SpecStory profiles and permission-mode rules.
56	
57	## Collision preflight
58	
59	On Herdr, `dev` compares recognized agent cwd values by canonical Git worktree
60	root before writer-claiming direct/branch starts and resume. It resolves
61	`herdr pane current --current` before excluding the caller, because inherited
62	`HERDR_PANE_ID` may be stale after a pane move. Every recognized state—including
63	`idle`, `done`, and `unknown`—is occupied; malformed/missing activity data fails
64	closed.
65	
66	Pure local repo/worktree open and TUI Enter reuse the live owner's workspace and
67	do not claim a second writer. Inside Herdr they request runtime focus;
68	outside Herdr the TUI first restores the terminal and then attaches, matching
69	`hhere`. The root `--allow-shared-checkout` escape hatch is
70	only for coordinated writer ownership. A default worktree start remains
71	separate and needs no override.
72	
73	For artifact operations, only an exact agent session ID (`agent_session` kind
74	`id`, not a title) can prove the caller differs from a stopped transcript's
75	valid UUID in the actual SpecStory-generated anchored preamble. Other live
76	agents always block. Unknown caller identity or artifact ownership needs explicit
77	`--allow-shared-checkout`; an identified caller-owned live transcript remains
78	forbidden. This does not prove recorder exit. See the
79	[artifact writer guard](hygiene.md#artifact-writer-guard).
80	
81	`dev status` shows recognized activities for the current worktree.
82	
83	## Sidebar metadata
84	
85	Task annotations use `$stage` and `$next`. Tokens render only if the local Herdr
86	row layout names them; reporting an unused token succeeds silently.
87	
88	```toml
89	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
90	rows = [
91	  ["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"],
92	  ["branch", "git_status"],
93	  ["$next"],
94	]
95	```
96	
97	## Cleanup semantics
98	
99	Recursive submodule retirement retains the version-2 coordinator's exact caller,
100	foreground-program consent, and task/Git/artifact preview checks. Child graph,
101	workspace intent and artifact ownership are bound to that same preview; changed
102	child refs or state require a new preview before runtime closure or removal.
103	
104	Herdr agent `done` means the latest turn settled. It does not establish that
105	history is synced, review is complete, code is committed, or cleanup is safe.
106	Never auto-close based on agent state.
107	
108	- `dev park` records WARM; inside its own workspace it leaves runtime alive for normal agent exit.
109	- `dev park --cold --push` closes/removes only from an external safe caller.
110	- `dev done --ff` integrates and keeps worktree/branch; selected task pane closures are explicit and reported.
111	- `dev done --pr` leaves task/runtime/worktree for review.
112	- `dev retire` externally closes, waits, revalidates and removes.
113	- `dev sweep` reports first and routes DONE cleanup through retire.
114	
115	`workspace close` itself touches no branch or checkout, but it can kill the
116	caller before later cleanup runs. Retirement therefore refuses caller
117	workspace/pane containment, mixed workspaces, and working/blocked/waiting
118	agents. Unknown status needs external `--close-unknown`; close failure or timeout
```

71		if r.closePaneErr != nil {
72			return r.closePaneErr
73		}
74		var kept []runtime.AgentActivity
75		for _, activity := range r.activities {
76			if activity.PaneID != paneID {
77				kept = append(kept, activity)
78			}
79		}
80		r.activities = kept
81		for index := range r.sessions {
82			var panes []runtime.Pane
83			for _, pane := range r.sessions[index].Panes {
84				if pane.ID != paneID {
85					panes = append(panes, pane)
86				}
87			}
88			r.sessions[index].Panes = panes
89		}
90		return nil
91	}

96	}

479	## Thin native adapter protocol
480	
481	The canonical helper remains the only queue/stage/sanitize/commit/reconcile
482	authority. A native caller may invoke the same Python subcommands through a
483	bound interpreter with `-I -B`; sibling code is loaded explicitly, not through
484	ambient `PYTHONPATH`.
485	
486	```text
487	_post_session.py capabilities --json
488	_post_session.py inspect --context --json
489	_post_session.py inspect --request ABSOLUTE_PATH --json
490	_post_session.py queue --script-dir S --session-id UUID --specstory-path PATH \
491	  (--plan PATH|--no-plan) --message-file PATH
492	_post_session.py finalize --script-dir S --request PATH --allow-commit \
493	  --expected-revision JOURNAL_DIGEST [--prepare-only|--reconcile-only]
494	```
495	
496	The public Bash queue's `--commit` is consumed by that wrapper; the direct
497	Python queue subcommand names the same intent without that flag. No native
498	caller may synthesize a journal, token, writer proof, receipt, or fallback commit.
499	
500	`capabilities` returns schema/protocol version 2, helper content revision, and
501	finite capabilities including `inspect_v2`, `authentic_context_v2`,
502	`queue_idempotent_v2`, `sanitation_receipt_v2`, `review_v2`, `exact_export_v2`,
503	`no_cloud_v2`, `prepare_only_v2`, `revision_guard_v2`, `reconcile_only_v2`.
504	`inspect` returns request/journal digests, exact worktree/Git directory/ref/HEAD,
505	input index and prepared trees, provider/session/artifact selectors, base and
506	composed/normalized message digests (never bodies), commit OID, child/group/sync/
507	freshness/review status, receipt revision, authentic-context and commit-proof
508	booleans. `automatic_commit` is the launcher's frozen `--allow-commit` choice
509	(v1: null); `cloud_sync` similarly reports the explicit per-run cloud choice.
510	On macOS, helper subprocesses use the supported stock `/bin/bash`, not a
511	PATH-selected substitute. Historical done inspection re-proves the immutable original parent,
512	tree, whole normalized message and request trailer without requiring current
513	HEAD/index to remain at that old commit; native readiness checks reachability
514	separately.
515	
516	Native co-commit integration starts the wrapper **without `--allow-commit`**, so
517	the parent cannot bypass a later native guard. New queue requires authentic
518	running context and `automatic_commit=false`. Queue succeeds before a native
519	binding CAS: failed native persistence must report `queued_but_not_bound`, retain
520	the exact request, and permit only idempotent inspect/bind repair. Do not hold a
521	native store lock across helper processes, scans, hooks, or commits.
522	
523	To preserve actual session linkage when capturing helper stdout, the native
524	caller includes this exact secret-free object as its outer JSON `queue_ack`
525	field (and emits the same standalone JSON line in human mode):
526	
527	```json
528	{"kind":"agent_history_queue_ack","schema_version":2,"request_id":"<run UUID>","request_path":"<absolute request>","request_revision":"<request digest>","helper_revision":"<helper digest>"}
529	```
530	
531	The real recorder must capture this in a typed tool result; user prose and
532	manual native-history edits do not count. `queued_but_not_bound` also carries the
533	acknowledgement because the canonical queue really happened.
534	
535	For a freshly authorized finalization, native may delegate `--prepare-only`,
536	inspect the exact retained receipt, recheck its own runtime/policy guard, then
537	call actual finalization with the new `--expected-revision`. The revision is
538	checked under the helper's existing finalizer lock before any effect.
539	`--prepare-only` never commits; rotation/unresolved findings remain a stop.
540	`--reconcile-only` can only re-prove/repair `committing` or `done`; another state
541	returns `reconciliation_required` without starting a commit. Never infer success
542	from exit zero, a draft, or a trailer alone.
543

615	Queue/finalization rejects merge, cherry-pick, revert, bisect, sequencer,
616	`rebase-merge`, `rebase-apply`, and index-lock state. This is both a consistency
617	gate and a history-safety gate: the queued request binds one attached branch,
618	parent, and index tree.
619	
620	A stale `REBASE_HEAD` file alone is **not** an active rebase and must not block a
621	valid finalization. Detect real rebase state via the actual per-worktree Git
622	state directories:
623	
624	```bash
625	git rev-parse --git-path rebase-merge
626	git rev-parse --git-path rebase-apply
627	```
628	
629	Do not run update-base, `pull --rebase`, merge/integration, or retirement merely
630	because the finalizer wrote drafts or returned a recoverable status. Wait for a
631	proven `committed`/`already_committed` result, then begin a separate ordinary Git
632	operation.

404	// Resolve finds a repo by name, display name, or path.
405	//
406	// Matching is deliberately layered: an exact name or path wins outright, and
407	// only then does a substring search run — so a repo literally named "web"
408	// is never shadowed by "web-frontend".
409	func Resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
410		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, DefaultOptions())
411	}
412	
413	// ResolveCompletion resolves the same references without launching one Git
414	// process per repository in the scan roots.
415	func ResolveCompletion(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
416		return resolve(ctx, roots, ref, CompletionOptions())
417	}
418	
419	func resolve(ctx context.Context, roots []string, ref string, opts Options) (Repo, []Repo, error) {
420		if abs, err := filepath.Abs(ref); err == nil {
421			if g, err := gitx.Discover(ctx, abs); err == nil {
422				real, _ := filepath.EvalSymlinks(abs)
423				if real == "" {
424					real = g.MainRoot
425				}
426				// Preserve an explicit navigation alias. The caller named this
427				// path on purpose; resolving it to the physical checkout would
428				// defeat a bootstrap symlink catalog.
429				return Repo{
430					Name: filepath.Base(abs), Path: abs, RealPath: real,
431					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
432				}, nil, nil
433			}
434		}
435		all, err := Discover(ctx, roots, opts)
436		if err != nil {
437			return Repo{}, nil, err
438		}
439		for _, r := range all {
440			if r.Name == ref || r.Display() == ref || r.Path == ref {
441				return r, nil, nil
442			}
443		}
444		needle := strings.ToLower(ref)
445		var hits []Repo
446		for _, r := range all {
447			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(r.Display()), needle) {
448				hits = append(hits, r)
449			}
450		}
451		switch len(hits) {
452		case 1:
453			return hits[0], nil, nil
454		case 0:
455			return Repo{}, nil, &NotFoundError{Ref: ref}
456		default:
457			return Repo{}, hits, &AmbiguousError{Ref: ref, Candidates: hits}
458		}
459	}
460	
461	// NotFoundError reports a repo reference that matched nothing.
462	type NotFoundError struct{ Ref string }
463	
464	func (e *NotFoundError) Error() string { return "no repository matching " + e.Ref }
465	
466	// AmbiguousError reports a repo reference that matched several repos.
467	type AmbiguousError struct {
468		Ref        string
469		Candidates []Repo
470	}
471	
472	func (e *AmbiguousError) Error() string {
473		names := make([]string, len(e.Candidates))
474		for i, c := range e.Candidates {
475			names[i] = c.Display()
476		}
477		return e.Ref + " is ambiguous: " + strings.Join(names, ", ")
478	}

4	Use `--submodules=none` to skip, or `start --submodule PATH` to select children
5	for task branches. `dev submodule status/init/develop/recover` inspects, prepares
6	and restores child checkouts. Explicit `--recursive` cleanup verifies initialized
7	child clones' remote recovery before removing them and the outer linked worktree;
8	canonical repositories and the outer branch are retained.
9	
10	A worktree is a second working directory for the same repository: its own
11	files, its own checked-out branch, sharing one history and one remote.
12	
13	## What they are actually for
14	
15	**Preventing two writers from editing the same files at once.** Not feature
16	management — that is what branches are for.
17	
18	So the question is never "how many agents am I running?" It is:
19	
20	> Could these two writers touch the same file?
21	
22	- Different files, one goal → one checkout is fine. Several agents, several
23	  panes, one branch.
24	- Different *approaches* to the same problem → one worktree each, so they can
25	  be compared and the loser discarded.
26	- Anything where the file ranges are unknown → worktrees.
27	
28	## Who owns which worktree
29	
30	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
31	|---|---|---|---|
32	| Feature, fix, experiment, handoff | `dev` | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until external retirement |
33	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation | Claude Code | `.claude/worktrees/` | owned by that harness; no transcript-relocation guarantee |
34	
35	**Might you review or return to the code/history/plan later → `dev`.**
36	
37	Never put a long-lived worktree inside the repository. Every file watcher,
38	language server, indexer and `rg` run in the outer repo then sees a second copy
39	of the whole tree.
40	
41	## Commands
42	
43	```bash
44	dev wt create feat/auth --base main   # create at the configured path
45	dev wt list                           # every worktree of this repo
46	dev wt open feat/auth                 # open an existing one
47	dev wt rm feat/auth                   # remove the checkout; branch survives
48	dev wt provision                      # re-run setup on an existing checkout
49	```
50	
51	## Always pass a base
52	
53	```bash
54	dev wt create fix/orderbook --base main
55	```
56	
57	Without `--base`, dev uses the repository's default branch. Passing it
58	explicitly is still preferred for scripts and agent-driven creation because
59	the intended committed starting point stays reviewable in the command.
60	
61	## Worktrees created directly in Herdr
62	
63	Herdr's **New worktree** action is allowed. Git registers that checkout with
64	the canonical repository, so dev can display it as an external worktree as
65	long as the canonical repo is discoverable through `paths.scan_roots` or
66	`paths.repo_paths`—even
67	when the checkout lives under `~/.herdr/worktrees` and that directory is not a
68	scan root.
69	
70	It remains deliberately unmanaged: dev does not silently create a task, move
71	the checkout, or run provisioning. If the work becomes durable, opt in:
72	
73	```bash
74	dev wt provision /path/to/worktree  # optional: env files + dependencies
75	dev adopt                           # report candidates; changes nothing
76	dev adopt --apply                   # record the selected candidates as tasks
77	```
78	
79	Until adoption, `dev park`, `dev resume`, and `dev done` have no task lifecycle
80	to operate on. Use `dev start` when that lifecycle is wanted from the outset.
81	
82	`dev flow [repo]` also shows every registered checkout. An eligible unmanaged
83	linked row offers plan-first **Adopt** (task metadata only; bytes stay untouched)
84	and **Remove Checkout** (clean, non-force, branch always preserved). Canonical,
85	harness, locked/prunable, task-claimed, or ambiguous rows have no destructive
86	path. Flow does not prune repository-wide stale registrations; inspect and repair
87	those explicitly.
88	
89	## A worktree starts empty of everything untracked
90	
91	No `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`. `dev` fixes this on create:
92	
93	- copies the gitignored files listed in `worktree.include`;
94	- symlinks anything in `worktree.link` (opt-in);
95	- runs `post_create`, detected from lockfiles when set to `"auto"`.
96	
97	Only files that are **both listed and gitignored** are copied. A tracked file
98	is already in the checkout on the correct branch — copying the other branch's
99	version over it would be wrong.
100	
101	## Removing one
102	
103	```bash
104	dev wt rm feat/auth
105	```
106	
107	Never deletes the branch. A dirty checkout needs an explicit `--force`, and
108	that refusal is the feature, not an obstacle.
109	
110	Gitlinks still need `--recursive`, even if never initialized. For linked-worktree
```

1	---
2	name: dev-cli
3	description: Use dev for repository discovery and setup, task and worktree lifecycle, agent handoffs, SSH hosts, fleet operations, dotfile setup, repository notes, skill or MCP inventory, secret/privacy hygiene, and feedback for unexpected dev failures.
4	---
5	
6	# dev-cli
7	
8	Git owns durable code; worktrees are local checkouts; runtimes are host-local
9	sessions; dev records task intent.
10	
11	## Discover what you need
12	
13	Use `dev <command> --help` for current syntax and flags, and `dev help <topic>`
14	for workflow explanations. `dev --help` lists commands; `dev help` lists topics.
15	Prefer supported `--json` output for automation. Read the relevant command before
16	mutation: some actions execute immediately, while others require preview/apply.
17	Do not preload manuals, repeat `dev --skill`, or run routine diagnostics.
18	
19	## Preserve these boundaries
20	
21	- Opening a repository needs no task. Choose direct, branch, or worktree
22	  deliberately; pass an explicit `--base` for branch/worktree creation. Keep
23	  managed worktrees outside repositories.
24	- `dev start` normally prepares a checkout/runtime. Agent launch is explicit.
25	  Parallel writers need coordinated ownership and verified launch targets.
26	- Completion, artifact finalization, retirement and branch deletion are separate.
27	  Finalize after writer exit; retire externally. Use `retire --base` when a fork
28	  point cannot prove integration. Runtime `done` is not cleanup-ready.
29	- Unknown or cached observations, merged PRs, and command refusals do not grant
30	  cleanup authority. Resolve the reported conditions; do not improvise force
31	  removal or bypass trust checks.
32	
33	## Read a reference for advanced operations
34	
35	- Worktree provisioning or cross-host lifecycle: [ownership](references/worktree-ownership.md), [lifecycle](references/task-lifecycle.md).
36	- Parallel agent launches or prompt transports: [agents](references/parallel-agents.md), [handoffs](references/prompt-handoffs.md).
37	- History retention, exact sessions and co-commit: [artifacts](references/ai-artifacts.md).
38	- Agent completion or cleanup batches: [retirement](references/agent-retirement.md), [triage](references/local-triage.md).
39	- Repository hygiene batches, `report --json` summaries, scans or redaction: [hygiene](references/hygiene.md).
40	- Repository hooks, publication, or physical organization: [setup](references/repository-bootstrap.md), [bootstrap](references/bootstrap.md).
41	- SSH dashboard, diagnosis, discovery, tests/activity, keys, credentials and registration: [SSH](references/ssh-hosts.md).
42	- Dotfile setup, native chezmoi operations, or FLEET host actions: [dotfiles](references/dotfiles.md).
43	- Skill/MCP/instruction transfers, updates or removal: [transfers](references/agent-interop.md), [maintenance](references/skills-management.md).
44	- Recursive Git children: [submodules](references/submodules.md).
45	
46	## Unexpected dev failures
47	
48	Read [feedback and repair](references/feedback-and-repair.md). Preserve the
49	original task; extra investigation, repair, subagents and publication need
50	explicit consent covering scope and cost.

279	salvage, and other narrow reconciliation paths. Do not assume every cleanup path
280	has the same planner. Raw Git and configured external tools also bypass dev's
281	PlanID, locks, revalidation, and result ledger.
282	
283	## Current behaviors that are implemented
284	
285	These were historical gaps and should not be reintroduced as limitations:
286	
287	- `dev repo new|create`, `repo clone`, and `repo setup` share a preset-driven bootstrap pipeline. A plain explicit `repo new NAME` remains minimal, while a clear Git URL, local Git path, or owner/name routes through clone acquisition and preserves source history/remote. The no-argument new-repository wizard detects the same reference in its first field; for a new repository, a default-no customization gate keeps the normal `agent-ready` flow concise. Bare `repo clone` selects exact URLs from the existing forge cache; outside a checkout, bare `start` selects a fast-discovered local repository, while the in-repository path keeps its immediate current default. Both retain manual entry. A configured line selector is optional, with a built-in fallback. Text fields use a TTY inline editor, so cursor keys edit rather than inserting raw escape bytes; non-TTY readers retain line-oriented behavior.
288	- `repo new` can snapshot a local directory/repository or Git source at an optional branch, tag, or commit and confined subdirectory into a fresh history. An unpinned local Git tree includes tracked plus untracked non-ignored files; a non-Git directory includes its full current tree. Source `.git` metadata is excluded, URL userinfo is redacted, unsafe file types/paths fail before destination creation, and held root/file handles confine mutable-path races. Human plans preview paths and warn when the snapshot is live; presets can select catalog-repository subfolders.
289	- Repository setup supports `--check-in=commit|stage|none` (`auto` for preset compatibility). Staged setup runs before-commit setup and `git add -A` without an `after_commit` phase, cannot publish or hand off to `start`, and may prefill lazygit lowercase `c` as described above.
290	- `agent-ready` uses one explicitly incomplete, non-fabricating `AGENTS.md` starter across built-in and native setup paths. Its common top-level ignore excludes only `.specstory/statistics.json`; history, project identity, and config remain visible. Selected skills with matching source and agent targets share one installer invocation. The optional `agent-history-hygiene` initializer additionally writes pre-commit/gitleaks policy and merges missing machine-local `.project.json`/`statistics.json` rules into `.specstory/.gitignore`; custom content and transcript history remain trackable.
291	- Project `.dev-cli/config.toml` and `.dev-cli/scaffolds.toml` are constrained to portable setup policy. Executable project configuration is keyed to the canonical Git common directory and an exact content hash; a changed hash is untrusted until approved again.
292	- `dev ssh init/list/show/setup/probe/remove` provides explicit OpenSSH host onboarding without a separate host database. Dev owns only its dedicated Include, canonical `dev.d` fragments, and opt-in generated fleet registrations; all public SSH JSON is one versioned object, and TSV listing is a documented six-field selector.
293	- Fleet merges user-authored primary `remotes.toml` with strict generated `remotes.d` fragments, tracks `remote_os`, and uses a hidden-helper-only encoded PowerShell launcher for Windows targets. Primary duplicate aliases remain compatible; any generated alias collision fails closed.
294	- `dev repo context --json` exposes additive schema-v1 local/remote evidence with source, age, freshness, completeness, null/error preservation, and scoped readiness; external probes happen only with `--refresh`. `dev status` reuses the cheap local readiness projection without network access.
295	- `dev fleet machine-id` reports an observed UUID without changing configuration. `dev fleet files` is report-only by default, uses a separate `[local_files]` allowlist, negotiates downward-only limits before content, and requires explicit apply/replacement controls plus a matching target pin.
296	
297	- `dev start --focus` activates the runtime after non-JSON creation.
298	- `dev start --run '<shell command>'` dispatches only to an exact root pane from
299	  a newly created first-class Herdr worktree. It is incompatible with `--json`,
300	  non-worktree modes, and non-Herdr runtimes, and does not wait for command exit.
301	- TUI navigation refuses to open a missing COLD checkout and directs the user to `dev resume`.
302	- Preview-labelled `dev flow [repo]` is an independent full-screen TTY model. It resolves canonical/linked cwd to the exact surface, uses a picker outside Git, shows every registered worktree plus task-only records, and makes every mutation Enter-to-plan then approve. Apply revalidates task revision and exact repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact authority and retains partial step results. Local `r` is network-free; `R` explicitly selects fetch/query/both and keeps minimal review evidence run-local.
303	- `DEV_TUI_TRACE` starts at `cli.Execute`; it cannot include OS process loading. `tui.initial_view_returned` measures model construction, not renderer flush or physical terminal paint. Use it for same-profile comparisons rather than universal hardware/network guarantees.
304	- Runtime handles now record backend provenance and are revalidated before cleanup.
305	- `auto` runtime selection includes Zellij between tmux and none.
306	
307	- `dev done` opens an interactive finish wizard on a TTY when `--ff`/`--pr` are both omitted, analyzing a dirty checkout against the base (commit, discard, or cancel) instead of rejecting any uncommitted change outright; a non-interactive caller still passes an explicit `--dirty` policy and `--yes` for a destructive discard.
308	- Human-readable output now carries semantic color (`--color auto|always|never`), automatically disabled when `NO_COLOR` is set, `TERM=dumb`, or stdout/stderr is not a terminal.
309	- Explicit `dev done` records MERGED and keeps worktree/branch; any selected task-pane closures are separately reported. Non-interactive invocation never grants implicit program or pane-closure consent. Bare interactive completion may continue into a separate cleanup wizard: it previews runtime agents and can hand caller-owned Herdr cleanup to a newly created external coordinator, which still uses ordinary `dev retire` guards. Active agents and mixed-purpose workspaces remain blockers. `dev done --delete-branch` remains an error pointing at `dev retire --delete-branch`, and `--keep-worktree` warns as a no-op.
310	- Interactive FF preserves parent/canonical agents and other task workspaces; parent occupancy offers recheck/PR/cancel. Only exact idle/done task-worktree panes can close under final Apply. General foreground programs require separate FF file-change consent, and interactive done/retire requires `CLOSE <workspace-id>` for known program termination. Background jobs are unobserved; failed supported probes block. Programs/topology changing during confirmation require a refreshed preview. Old coordinator handoffs must be recreated. Existing unknown-runtime flags do not authorize known programs.
311	- `dev retire --base <ref>` overrides task/path containment, resolving local branch, then remote-tracking branch, then commit. Apply re-resolves the same input; changed kind/ref/OID invalidates the plan. A recorded fork-point commit is never replaced by the default branch: unproved integration stays blocked with `--base <branch>` guidance. `done --merged --base-ref X` carries X through cleanup hints, wizard and external coordinator. Branch deletion still uses Git's own upstream/HEAD `branch -d` check; a non-HEAD base can leave partial completion with the branch and DONE task retained.
312	- `dev sweep --base` forwards to DONE retirement; `--merged-worktrees` passes its verified base to managed tasks too. Retire/remove worktree-list authority includes only same-branch or equal/nested/containing paths, so an unrelated sibling removal no longer stales later plans in an approved `--apply --yes` batch. Target lock/HEAD or same-branch checkout changes still invalidate them.
313	- `dev sweep --merged-worktrees` enumerates linked worktrees from Git rather than from the task registry, so unmanaged worktrees whose branches are contained in the base become retirable. Containment alone is never permission; dirty state, unfinalized artifacts, in-progress Git operations, and runtime refusals all still block it, and branches survive unless `--delete-branches` is passed.
314	- `dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees` adds a separate schema-v1 Claude Workflow report. The path/branch convention is only discovery; exact bounded provider linkage plus fresh Git/task/artifact/caller/runtime evidence authorizes TTY/per-item apply. Apply locks and re-fingerprints, removes without force, retains branches by default, and allows only explicit-base unchanged/contained/zero-unique `branch -d`.
315	- `dev sweep` reports a branch-backed task whose branch Git no longer has as dead and offers to reap the record. Such a task cannot be finished, resumed, or retired, because every one of those paths resolves the branch first; the suggestion stays report-only until `--apply`.
316	- An unknown command is reported instead of discarded. `dev` silences cobra's own error printing and previously also skipped printing anything whose message began with `unknown command`, so a mistyped command produced no output at all on either stream. The message, cobra's "Did you mean this?" suggestions, and a pointer to `--help` are now printed to stderr with exit status 1.
317	- A stray argument to a command family is an error rather than a silent help render. `dev wt bogus` used to print `dev wt` help and exit 0 because a family has no `Run` of its own; every family node now reports the unknown subcommand and exits 1, while a bare family still prints its help and exits 0.
318	- Argument-count and flag errors print the failing command's usage block. `--color` still governs whether that block is colorized.
319	- Each command family's help carries an ASCII orientation diagram and a `See also: dev help <topic>` pointer, and `dev help <command>` resolves a command name or alias to its topic, so `dev help wt` reaches the worktrees page.
320	- Semantic color covers every human-readable surface, including the interactive dashboard: `dev --color never`, `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb` now disable dashboard color too, which they previously did not.
321	- `dev sweep` reaps a task whose repository directory no longer exists. Such a record was unreachable by every command in the binary: `done`, `resume`, `park` and `retire` all resolve the repository first, the dead-branch rule excludes direct mode, and the stale-worktree rule requires a recorded worktree path. A live runtime session rules the suggestion out, and reaping removes only dev's record of intent.
322	- `dev sweep` reports a task-recorded checkout that exists but Git does not register and that holds nothing but agent artifact directories. Removal is offered only when every file inside is byte-identical to one already in the repository; anything else is reported as salvage work and is never removed, including under `--apply`.
323	- `dev sweep` acts on a cold task whose worktree is still on disk. Inventory has always computed that drift for `dev ls` and the dashboard, but sweep never consulted it, so it was displayed and not actionable.
324	- `dev retire <path>` reaps the matching task record. Only the by-task form set the task identity, so retiring the same checkout by path left the record behind; the DONE-state and identity checks are unchanged.
325	- `dev version` reports whether the running build is a published release, and `dev doctor` carries the same line plus the install owner, invoked/resolved executable path, and warnings for distinct `dev` copies on `PATH`. Nothing in the tool answered "am I current?" before, and `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so an untagged feature was invisible to anyone installing it.
326	- A release publishes platform archives and `SHA256SUMS` and takes its notes from `CHANGELOG.md`. Earlier releases published a GitHub release object and nothing else, so their assets are absent by construction.
327	- A release publishes Windows `.zip` archives alongside the Unix `.tar.gz` set, refreshes an in-repo Scoop manifest attached to the release (and pushed to the bucket when a token is configured), and publishes the matching source formula to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`. Homebrew publication is a required release step and fails visibly when its repository token is missing or rejected. A manual workflow can retry or backfill the formula for an existing stable release without creating or moving a tag.

## Recommendation

For durable agent-created work, **explicitly surfacing the checkout in Herdr is useful**. Do not add automatic watching, task adoption, or agent launching.

The immediate cause is the raw `git worktree add`: it bypassed dev’s runtime-opening step. `--skill` only prints guidance; [static-output tests](/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui/internal/cli/static_output_test.go:14) verify it skips application startup and filesystem effects.

### Existing safe no-focus command

This uses precisely the native command already invoked by dev’s Herdr adapter; **not executed**:

```bash
herdr worktree open \
  --cwd /Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dev-cli \
  --path /Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui \
  --no-focus \
  --label dev-cli/fix/closeout-review-tui
```

It surfaces an existing checkout, not creates a Git worktree. No Git/index/branch changes, provisioning, task adoption, or agent dispatch are involved.

## Current command boundaries

- **`dev wt open <branch> --repo <repo>`** selects an existing registered checkout, including a dirty one, and prints **branch, path, runtime name/handle**. However, it unconditionally activates afterward. There is **no CLI `--no-focus` today**. See [worktree.go:216–255](/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui/internal/cli/worktree.go:216).
- **`dev repo open <exact-worktree-path>`** also works: [explicit-path resolution preserves the requested path](/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui/internal/repo/discover.go:419). It likewise activates unconditionally and reports directory name/path/handle, not branch. See [repo.go:408](/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui/internal/cli/repo.go:408).
- **`dev start`** is detached by default; `--focus` opts in, and JSON never activates. But it persists task intent; worktree mode refuses an existing branch checkout. It is not the appropriate visibility-only workaround. See [start.go](/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui/internal/cli/start.go:149) and [start_flow.go:181](/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui/internal/cli/start_flow.go:181).
- Creation is **`dev wt create`**, not `wt add`; no top-level `dev open` exists. Creation’s `--path` specifies the new checkout location, not an attach target.
- **`dev adopt --apply`** writes task metadata; it does not open a runtime. Avoid adoption solely for sidebar visibility.

## Runtime matching—reuse existing implementation

[openCheckout](/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui/internal/cli/helpers.go:10) prefers `WorktreeOpener.OpenWorktree`, so the existing command already has the correct integration.

[Herdr.OpenWorktree](/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui/internal/runtime/herdr.go:389):
- Derives the canonical parent and passes `--cwd`, exact `--path`, `--no-focus`, and `repo/branch` label.
- Uses native `already_open` to distinguish reuse.
- Falls back to detached generic `Open` when native worktree opening fails; fallback/reuse is not an agent-launch target.

Generic `Herdr.Open` reuses the **first session whose observed shell/foreground directory is at or beneath the requested directory**—not a label match or exact workspace-identity match. A pane at `$HOME` does not cover a child repository. See [Herdr.Open](/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui/internal/runtime/herdr.go:314) and [Session.Covers](/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui/internal/runtime/runtime.go:60). Do not alter this matching for the proposed fix.

## Smallest useful shipped improvement

**Add only `dev wt open --no-focus`**, default false, guarding the existing final `activateRuntime` call. Preserve ordinary navigation, current no-runtime behavior, and existing output. The verified branch here is uniquely `fix/closeout-review-tui`; no new path selector is necessary.

Then document an agent practice: explicitly surface durable checkouts when appropriate and report **branch + actual checkout path + runtime handle/outcome**. Distinguish this from harness-owned temporary isolation. Keep task adoption optional.

**No new JSON schema is necessary.** `wt open` has none; preserve `start --json`’s existing absolute paths and transient runtime fields unchanged.

6	// guarantees dev's core inventory and worktree commands work on a bare machine
7	// with nothing but git installed.
8	//
9	// Open returns the directory itself as the handle: the shell wrapper installed
10	// by `dev shell-init` turns that into a cd in the calling shell, since a child
11	// process can never change its parent's working directory.
12	type None struct{}
13	
14	// Name implements Runtime.
15	func (None) Name() string { return "none" }
16	
17	// Available implements Runtime; the null backend always is.
18	func (None) Available() bool { return true }
19	
20	// Open implements Runtime by reporting the directory to change into. None does
21	// not open a runtime surface, so the result is never launchable.
22	func (None) Open(_ context.Context, dir, _ string) (OpenResult, error) {
23		return OpenResult{Handle: dir}, nil
24	}
25	
26	// Close implements Runtime as a no-op: there is no session to end.
27	func (None) Close(context.Context, string) error { return nil }
28	
29	// List implements Runtime; without a multiplexer nothing is tracked as live.
30	func (None) List(context.Context) ([]Session, error) { return nil, nil }
31	
32	// Annotate implements Runtime as a no-op.
33	func (None) Annotate(context.Context, string, map[string]string) error { return nil }
34

1	---
2	description: Choose the owner and location of each worktree, then provision ignored files and dependencies safely.
3	authority: project
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-08-29
6	---
7	
8	# Worktrees and provisioning
9	
10	Submodule Git initialization precedes environment provisioning and defaults to recursive pinned checkouts. `--no-provision` does not disable it; use `--submodules=none`. Initialization failure retains the worktree without opening its runtime. See [Submodule workspaces](submodule-workspaces.md).
11	
12	A Git worktree begins as a clean checkout. `dev` owns durable change-stream worktrees and builds an inspectable plan for the ignored files and dependencies needed to make them usable.
13	
14	## Choose one lifecycle owner
15	
16	| Worktree kind | Owner | Typical location | Lifetime |
17	|---|---|---|---|
18	| feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | `dev` | configured `paths.worktree_path` | `dev done` records MERGED only; a later `dev retire`, explicit `dev wt rm`, or approved sweep removes it |
19	| harness-scoped isolation | Claude Code or another harness | harness-owned directory such as `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` | governed by that harness's retention and safe-cleanup rules; Flow never adopts or removes it |
20	| externally created linked worktree | external until adopted | tool-specific | visible to `dev`/`dev flow`; unmanaged until explicit adoption |
21	
22	Use `dev` when code, history, or plans must remain reviewable or a human may return later. Do not nest a long-lived `dev` worktree inside a repository; file watchers, language servers, backup tools, and searches in the outer checkout would see a second copy of the tree.
23	
24	`dev` creates the checkout with Git at its configured path. Herdr only opens that existing path, so worktree placement remains identical on machines without Herdr.
25	
26	`dev flow [repo]` uses Git's authoritative worktree records to show canonical,
27	managed, unmanaged, and strict `.claude/worktrees/` harness rows, plus task-only
28	rows that have no checkout. It never guesses ownership from a `worktree-*`
29	branch prefix; ambiguous path/task binding is labelled CONFLICT and stops
30	lifecycle mutation. See [Repository lifecycle flow](repository-flow.md).
31	
32	## Inspect before creating
33	
34	```bash
35	dev wt plan
36	dev wt plan --write          # seed repository-owned .dev-cli/config.toml
37	dev wt create feat/auth --base main
38	dev wt list
39	```
40	
41	`dev wt plan` reads lockfiles, tool availability, configured include/link rules, and Git ignore state without changing the checkout. The resulting plan shows every runnable or skipped step and any safety downgrade.
42	
43	## Carry ignored files by allowlist
44	
45	```toml
46	[worktree]
47	include = [".env", ".env.local", "config/local.json"]
48	link = []
49	post_create = "auto"
50	strategy = "reinstall"
51	```
52	
53	Only paths that are both listed and confirmed by Git as ignored are copied. A tracked file already arrives through the branch; copying a different checkout's version over it would violate branch isolation.
54	
55	Included files are copied as files, not logged. Current provisioning also rechecks the source and destination path shape while opening/copying so source swaps and symlinked destination parents are refused.
56	
57	Do not add `.claude/settings.local.json` globally. Include that exact file only for a deliberately chosen launcher whose behavior depends on it, and verify the copy in the plan.
58	
59	## Select dependency strategy by correctness
60	
61	| Strategy | Effect | Guidance |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| `reinstall` | run the lockfile-derived install command | safe default |
64	| `copy` | duplicate an installed dependency directory | use only where paths are portable |
65	| `link` | share one dependency directory | fastest and usually unsafe for concurrent writers |
66	| `skip` | leave dependencies absent | container- or CI-driven development |
67	
68	Per-ecosystem overrides live in the project or global config:
69	
70	```toml
71	[worktree.strategies]
72	node = "copy"
73	```
74	
75	New project-owned overrides belong in `.dev-cli/config.toml`; legacy
76	`.dev.toml` remains readable under its compatibility behavior. A `post_create`
77	command from `.dev-cli/config.toml` does not run until its exact
78	executable-config hash is approved with `dev config trust . --yes`. Changing
79	the command invalidates that approval.
80	
81	Important built-in decisions:
82	
83	- Python virtual environments cannot be copied or linked because they embed absolute paths; `uv sync` can reuse its global cache.
84	- Node `node_modules` may be copied, but sharing is refused because either checkout can mutate it.
85	- Go uses a global content-addressed module cache, so there is no checkout-local dependency tree to copy.
```

# dev-cli

Git owns durable code; worktrees are local checkouts; runtimes are host-local
sessions; dev records task intent.

## Discover what you need

Use `dev <command> --help` for current syntax and flags, and `dev help <topic>`
for workflow explanations. `dev --help` lists commands; `dev help` lists topics.
Prefer supported `--json` output for automation. Read the relevant command before
mutation: some actions execute immediately, while others require preview/apply.
Do not preload manuals, repeat `dev --skill`, or run routine diagnostics.

## Preserve these boundaries

- Opening a repository needs no task. Choose direct, branch, or worktree
  deliberately; pass an explicit `--base` for branch/worktree creation. Keep
  managed worktrees outside repositories.
- `dev start` normally prepares a checkout/runtime. Agent launch is explicit.
  Parallel writers need coordinated ownership and verified launch targets.
- Completion, artifact finalization, retirement and branch deletion are separate.
  Finalize after writer exit; retire externally. Use `retire --base` when a fork
  point cannot prove integration. Runtime `done` is not cleanup-ready.
- Unknown or cached observations, merged PRs, and command refusals do not grant
  cleanup authority. Resolve the reported conditions; do not improvise force
  removal or bypass trust checks.

## Read a reference for advanced operations

- Worktree provisioning or cross-host lifecycle: [ownership](references/worktree-ownership.md), [lifecycle](references/task-lifecycle.md).
- Parallel agent launches or prompt transports: [agents](references/parallel-agents.md), [handoffs](references/prompt-handoffs.md).
- History retention: [artifacts](references/ai-artifacts.md).
- Agent completion or cleanup batches: [retirement](references/agent-retirement.md), [triage](references/local-triage.md).
- Repository hygiene batches, `report --json` summaries, scans or redaction: [hygiene](references/hygiene.md).
- Repository hooks, publication, or physical organization: [setup](references/repository-bootstrap.md), [bootstrap](references/bootstrap.md).
- SSH dashboard, diagnosis, discovery, tests/activity, keys, credentials and registration: [SSH](references/ssh-hosts.md).
- Dotfile setup, native chezmoi operations, or FLEET host actions: [dotfiles](references/dotfiles.md).
- Skill/MCP/instruction transfers, updates or removal: [transfers](references/agent-interop.md), [maintenance](references/skills-management.md).
- Recursive Git children: [submodules](references/submodules.md).

Use command help and its workflow topic for everyday operations.

## Unexpected dev failures

Read [feedback and repair](references/feedback-and-repair.md). Preserve the
original task; extra investigation, repair, subagents and publication need
explicit consent covering scope and cost.
