38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `submodule` owns versioned workspace-member intent and reversible child-clone disposal mechanisms. `gitx` supplies the local gitlink graph; `taskflow` owns recursive lifecycle policy and fresh remote-proof ordering. Gitlink checkouts are legitimate submodules, not nested managed linked worktrees.
56	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints. Lifecycle callers use exact-record revisions and locked compare-and-update/delete transactions rather than treating a previously read task as current.
57	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
58	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
59	- `taskflow` is the UI-agnostic lifecycle authority: it separates recorded intent, typed live observations, immutable guarded plans, approvals, and partial result ledgers. Apply locks and reloads task/Git/worktree/runtime/artifact/remote identity, then rejects stale authority before mutation.
60	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, all registered worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and UI projections consume this joined view.
61	- `agentinterop` owns explicit MCP/skill/instruction transfer plans, guarded apply, stanza/link ownership, private recovery, and optional recipes. Native agent files and skills locks remain authoritative; only explicit preparation/check/launch paths may execute a provider or MCP server. Recovery belongs outside Git, credentials remain runtime references, and native Windows writes fail closed pending verified ACL/identity support.
62	- `triage` owns read-only cross-repository findings, clone-bound local intent, ignored-directory policy and reviewed batch ledgers; `triagetui` is its independent UI. Synchronization uses taskflow plans, and protected cleanup adds guards inside the existing repository lock and immediately before removal. Local scans never reconcile Try catalog entries.
63	- `flowtui` is an independent Bubble Tea model for the preview `dev flow` repository state-machine UI. It receives repository reads and taskflow Plan/Apply callbacks; do not embed it in or add a mode to the dashboard's `tui` model.
64	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
65	- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
66	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
67	- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage`, note FTS, and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
68	- `agenthistory` owns explicit transcript/file retention policy, immutable source-bound archive copies, Git lookup/sync and isolated history migration. Archive bindings/recovery stay in private state, ordinary status never contacts remotes, and source writers/index bytes remain untouched by archiving. `artifact` keeps old commit handoffs and adds externally verified archive receipts; taskflow includes ignored capture readiness in its guarded authority.
69	- `hygiene` owns configurable secret/privacy policy, index/worktree/frozen-history scans, private identity rules and signed replacement plans. Raw findings/recovery stay outside Git; hook setup preserves foreign hooks. Large text transactions explicitly opt into configedit’s Windows backend; existing configuration flows retain their platform contracts.
70	- `feedback` owns durable private reports, sanitized public drafts, revision-bound issue/comment publication receipts and exact repair plans. CLI adapts its repair backend to the shared start flow; agent launch is explicit and prompt context never becomes a public issue body.
71	- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.
72	- `sshhost` owns bounded static discovery of the active user OpenSSH Include closure, canonical files under `~/.ssh/dev.d`, public-key selection/generation/bootstrap, fresh authentication proofs, and the explicit handoff into dev fleet. OpenSSH and plain `ssh -G` remain semantic authority; ordinary setup/remove never rewrite foreign connection definitions, copy private keys, weaken host-key policy, or treat every alias as a fleet member. Explicit format/organize may transform selected user-owned configuration with private guarded recovery; Include restores its caller scope after each file. Named agent providers (Bitwarden, 1Password, Secretive, custom sockets) are located by stat only and never executed; selecting a named-agent key publishes only its public line and writes a v2 fragment (`IdentityAgent`, `SecurityKeyProvider`), which older binaries treat as not dev-owned, while v1 files stay byte-identical. Explicit FIDO generation binds the reviewed native tools/provider, keeps capability observations stat-only, and reports hardware created/unknown effects independently of local publication; only verified SK recovery pairs may be retained. Never use resident-key download or provider loading as a passive probe, and keep automatic Secure Enclave creation blocked until exact native identity mapping is verified.
73	- `sshflow` owns the explicit SSH/fleet/Herdr machine inventory and Plan/Apply orchestration; `herdrremote` calls the native machine CLI without writing its catalog. `configedit` owns source-bound local file transactions and private recovery outside Git, with owner leases and macOS/Linux metadata checks.
74	- `machineregistry` owns controller-local canonical machine UUIDs, scoped provider bindings, explicit unlink suppression and merge redirects in durable private SQLite. These UUIDs never replace the remote `fleet.machine_id` trust pin. `sshdiscovery` owns optional explicit Tailscale status and bounded on-link LAN observations; discovery caches are disposable and never create machine identities or prove authentication. `sshflow` joins these sources while retaining every distinct SSH connection profile; the dashboard SSH view is an adapter to the same services.
75	- `sshactivity` owns private durable per-profile usage and test observations. Usage records actual local dev-mediated SSH process starts; network/full tests never update usage. Observations retain source fingerprints and cannot authorize mutations or imply present connectivity.
76	- `tuiissue` owns typed problem guidance and reviewed native dependency installation recipes. UI actions use finite IDs and exact guarded service callbacks, never executable error text.
77	- `selfupdate` selects exact release platform assets and stages native Go source builds when an asset is absent, preferring the checksummed compact source archive over legacy Go module source. CLI owns confirmation and executable replacement; download/checksum failures never authorize a source fallback, and failed builds retain the installed binary.
78	- `platformfs` owns the native Android Termux home anchor, inherited app-data SELinux/encryption metadata recognition and no-replace publication. It also recognizes macOS kernel-managed provenance: observe it for same-file stale detection, but never restore or require it on a replacement. Verify the exact system/app prefix and all user-controlled descendants; never trust arbitrary UID-1000 directories, relabel files, chmod Android system paths or substitute an overwriting rename.
79	- `sshremote` owns strict bounded v1 SSH capability/inventory/resolve/key/connect protocols and private disposable source/route caches. Only explicit capability may initialize remote dev identity. Static inventory never evaluates SSH or agents; source profiles are scoped by observed UUID, user, root and alias. Local imports preserve native controller trust/authentication context, while remote connect reselects remote-local keys and never retries a started session.
80	- `sshcredential` owns per-context operation secrets, guarded ask/never metadata and exact provider references. System stores and explicitly selected Bitwarden contain saved passwords; the TOML ledger never does. Source-bound authentication evidence authorizes an optional save prompt, not arbitrary askpass, MFA or host-key text. Unknown provider writes stay unknown and are not retried automatically.
81	- `sshvault` owns explicit new vault-key creation, service-bound single-attempt plans, exact public receipts, and native account/profile execution context. It never imports existing private keys or writes new private material to files. Experimental Bitwarden memory creation and delegation to a native profile need separate approvals; freeze the actual environment/cwd and revalidate session/profile/tool identity without exposing session values or hashes. A session or base URL is not endpoint identity: native-context consistency and endpoint-unverified status remain separate from creation and agent visibility. Native no-interaction must prevent private JSON stdin from becoming a credential response; ambiguous writes retain receipts and never auto-retry/delete. Live vault/hardware checks remain separately consented.
82	
83	- `fleetnav` owns contextual host/repository navigation ordering, explicit Herdr profile/session selection and partial results. Repository checks precede profile changes; preparation uses a distinct versioned helper and session-scoped runtime with no focus or attach. Inside Herdr, navigation reports a native sidebar target; outside it attaches to the explicit session. Failures never implicitly switch to SSH.
84	- `fleet` merges the user-authored primary `remotes.toml` with strict dev-owned `remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` registrations. Remote `dev` state remains host-local. `remote_os` selects target semantics: POSIX uses the shell launcher, while Windows uses an encoded PowerShell launcher that accepts only hidden fleet helpers, preserves sync stdin, and never applies controller path rules to remote paths.
85	
86	The principal task start flow spans `internal/cli/start.go`, `start_flow.go`, `gitx`/`wt`, `runtime`, and `task`: resolve the canonical repository and explicit base, create or select the checkout, provision/open it, then persist and annotate the task. Task-backed park/resume/completion/retirement and exact unmanaged Adopt/Remove policy belong in `taskflow`; CLI commands, the dashboard, `sweep`, and `flowtui` are adapters. Preserve report-before-apply and no-data-loss ordering, including the isolated compatibility paths that have not migrated to taskflow.
87	
88	State is split intentionally:
89	
90	- Git remotes/branches are durable code truth.
91	- Worktrees are disposable local checkouts.
92	- Runtime sessions are per-host and re-derivable.
93	- Task TOML and catalog assets hold only intent/identity that Git cannot answer.
94	- Repository quick-note Markdown is durable sidecar data; `notes.db` is only its disposable search index.
95	- `stats.db` is durable observation data; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/*` is disposable.
96	- SSH source/route caches are disposable; remote dev UUIDs, local canonical machine UUIDs and fleet trust pins are separate identities. Credential policy/reference TOML is durable intent; its provider-owned secret is not a cache. Removing a reference does not erase a vault item or revoke a remote password.
97	- The user's OpenSSH configuration is durable connection truth. Ordinary setup/remove own only the exact top-level `Include ~/.ssh/dev.d/*.conf` and structurally valid fragments in `~/.ssh/dev.d`; key bootstrap sends public material only and has no private-key transfer or remote-key revocation lifecycle.
98	- Fleet intent is the merged primary `remotes.toml` plus generated sibling `remotes.d` fragments. A generated fragment exists only after explicit `dev ssh setup --fleet` / `--to fleet|both` or `dev ssh manage --action register --to fleet|both`, and a fresh ordinary alias login; controller caches and each remote machine's paths/tasks/runtime remain re-derivable or host-local.
99	- `paths.state_dir/machines/registry.db` is durable controller-local identity and binding intent; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/ssh-discovery/` contains disposable dated Tailscale/LAN observations. Plain `dev ssh list` stays static; `--tailscale` explicitly queries the optional local CLI and `--lan` reads cached observations. Neither list nor dashboard refresh scans the LAN. The active SSH dashboard may refresh local Tailscale status when `[tui.ssh].background_refresh` is enabled; native discovery returns typed observations independently of cache writes. Candidate setup preserves source/scope provenance and per-stage retained effects.
100	
101	## Behavioral contracts
102	
103	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
104	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
105	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
106	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
107	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
108	- Submodule initialization uses committed gitlinks, never implicitly advances to `main`. Whole child-clone disposal requires explicit recursive approval and fresh recovery proof for its private refs/objects; outer and shared canonical repositories are retained. Local graph refresh never performs remote proof. Child task/runtime/artifact claims block parent disposal.
109	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
110	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
111	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
112	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
113	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
114	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
115	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
116	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output, including `dev hygiene report --json` (`hygiene_summary` schema 1). Stored summaries are historical observations, not proof of current source bytes.
117	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
118	- Explicit SSH format/organize and fleet profile rename/remove are plan-first exceptions for user-selected files; retain comments, Include order, original metadata and private recovery. Never activate dormant files with a new broad Include. Herdr machine add may prepare/start a remote server; leave native approvals native, and remove/disable never stops remote sessions.
119	- SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. Full bootstrap requires an explicit existing key or explicit generation, registers fleet only when explicitly selected, and reports interrupted remote installation as unknown rather than pretending to roll it back.
120	- SSH wizard permission preflight may separately review and apply metadata-only tightening on exact current-user-owned canonical/selected paths. It never recursively chmods, changes ownership, guesses ACLs, or widens permissions; completed repairs survive later cancellation. Listing and dry-run never repair permissions. Local key listing evaluates OpenSSH only behind explicit `--alias`; selected key material remains service-bound and is revalidated before configuration changes and bootstrap.
121	- `dev ssh key doctor` exposes the same permission Plan/Apply with bounded metadata-only key discovery; `--key` restricts the reviewed scope, and `--fix` requires a complete safe plan plus confirmation. Default doctor never mutates, reads private contents, or queries agents/remotes. Batch repairs revalidate the whole reviewed union and retain successful tightening on partial failure.
122	- Source-aware SSH setup can use `--auth existing` without installing a key, and registers only explicitly selected `--to fleet|herdr|both` destinations. Tailscale SSH advertisement is advisory; its port-22 endpoint is not an authorized_keys bootstrap target. Preserve the key-authentication guard and never treat Tailscale policy login as proof that a selected public key worked. Names, ports and cached observations never authorize machine merges; binding/source changes invalidate reviewed plans.
123	- Fleet-source SSH discovery selects explicit hosts without recursive fleet traversal. Local ProxyJump imports never copy remote identity/agent/trust paths; cached route data cannot authorize apply. `connect --on` is one interactive fixed-helper session with no agent forwarding or arbitrary command payload. Normal SSH errors retain child exit status.
124	- Controller password brokerage uses a private per-operation Unix socket or protected Windows pipe, never password argv/environment/files. Exact host/user/port/route contexts gate replies and save evidence. Remote source-to-target credentials remain outside this feature; native key/passphrase interaction is separate.
125	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
126	
127	## Versioning and changelog
128	
129	The current published baseline is `v0.2.39` (2026-09-17). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
130	
131	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
132	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
133	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
134	
135	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
136	
137	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
138	
139	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
140	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
141	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
142	
143	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
144	
145	For a release:
146	
147	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
148	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
149	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
150	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
151	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and publish the matching Homebrew formula. The repository secret `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` must be a fine-grained token with Contents write access to `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap`; a tap publication failure fails the release job so it can be retried instead of leaving Homebrew users stale.
152	
153	If the Homebrew step needs a retry or an older stable release needs a one-time backfill, run `gh workflow run publish-homebrew.yml -f version=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. The manual workflow verifies that the release exists and republishes only the formula; it does not create or move a tag or GitHub release.
154	
155	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
156	
157	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
158	
159	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
160	
161	| Change | Required synchronization |
162	|---|---|
163	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
164	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
165	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
166	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
167	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
168	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
169	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
170	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
171	
172	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
173	
174	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
175	
176	## Hygiene and skill batch operations
177	
178	`internal/hygiene` owns per-repository setup plans and batch ledgers. REPOS and
179	`hygiene manage` are adapters; JSON batch management previews only. Keep legacy
180	artifact finalizers until their independent lifecycle is replaced. Cached machine
181	privacy imports use only bounded local cache readers and revalidate their source.
182	`internal/agentskill` owns selected-removal policy: exact native names/agent scopes
183	or bundled manifests, source/ownership/dependency proof and postconditions under
184	the provider lease. Never infer complete Windows validation from an advisory
185	step's success conclusion; inspect logs and require the dedicated native gates.
186	
187	## Agent history policy
188	
189	`dev help ai-artifacts` separates source retention, archive location, protection
190	and distribution. New configuration is opt-in. Sources are SpecStory Markdown or
191	explicit files; provider IDs name the originating agent. Do not infer writer exit
192	from byte stability or close agents to finalize evidence. Archive mode verifies
193	ignored bytes before cleanup; existing tracked intents retain their original lane.
194	`git-filter-repo` only operates on new verified copies. Ordinary migration never
195	rewrites source refs or published tags, and raw backups are not secret audits.
196	
197	`artifact` owns native intent revisions, exact transcript selection and writer
198	Guard/CAS checks. Product-first remains the default (committed products, empty
199	index). Explicit co-commit binds a feature-only index to a separately installed
200	canonical v2 helper and authentic wrapper launched without `--allow-commit`.
201	Native code never launches/closes the agent or invents queue acknowledgement,
202	SessionEnd or export evidence. Queue success, including queued-but-not-bound,
203	requires reporting finalization queued and exiting without more repository work.
204	External finalization uses canonical prepare-only, fresh native guards and exact
205	helper revision before one commit-capable call; uncertain outcomes reconcile
206	only. Commit proof includes parent, tree, full normalized message and unique
207	request identity, not trailers alone. Status/readiness keep native intent and
208	helper observations separate and never mutate or reconcile. Helper/tool identity
209	drift, unsupported versions and native Windows fail closed; no automatic install
210	or v1-journal upgrade. Per-finding noncredential review releases only the exact
211	sanitized run's rotation gate, never restores secrets or bypasses hooks; actual
212	credentials still require rotation and unknown findings remain blocked.

343	Copies the gitignored files, applies the dependency strategy and runs the

405	func newWtPlanCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
406		var (
407			repoRef string
408			write   bool
409		)
410		cmd := &cobra.Command{
411			Use:   "plan",
412			Short: "Show what a new worktree of this repo would be provisioned with",
413			Long: `Report the project types detected in this repository and exactly what
414	provisioning a new worktree would do — which gitignored files get copied,
415	which dependency directories are copied or shared, and which install commands
416	run.
417	
418	A worktree that comes up broken is the commonest reason people abandon
419	worktrees, and the config alone cannot answer "what will this actually do":
420	that depends on which lockfiles exist, which tools are installed here, and
421	which files are genuinely gitignored. This computes all of it and changes
422	nothing.
423	
424	With --write, seed .dev-cli/config.toml from what was detected, so the repository can
425	commit its own setup and every machine gets the same one.`,
426			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
427			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
428				ctx := ctxOf()

431					return err
432				}
433				set := wt.SettingsFor(app.Cfg, repoPath)
434				plan := wt.BuildPlan(ctx, set, repoPath)
435	
436				if write {
437					return writeRepoTemplate(app, repoPath, plan, set)
438				}
439				renderPlan(app, plan, repoPath)
440				return nil
441			},
442		}
443		f := cmd.Flags()
444		f.StringVarP(&repoRef, "repo", "r", "", "repository (default: the current one)")
445		f.BoolVar(&write, "write", false, "seed .dev-cli/config.toml in the repository from what was detected")
446		registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "repo", completeRepoFlag(app))
447		return cmd
448	}

450	// renderPlan prints a provisioning plan as a table plus its warnings.
451	func renderPlan(app *App, plan wt.Plan, repoPath string) {
452		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s\n\n", config.Contract(repoPath))
453	
454		if len(plan.Ecosystems) == 0 {
455			gitInit := false
456			for _, step := range plan.Steps {
457				if step.Kind == wt.StepInitSubmodules {
458					gitInit = true
459				}
460			}
461			if gitInit {
462				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Submodule Git acquisition and configured files; no dependency manager detected.")
463			} else {
464				fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "No project type detected — only gitignored files will be carried over.")
465			}
466		} else {
467			t := app.newTable("PROJECT", "MANAGER", "FROM", "DEPENDENCIES", "TOOL")
468			style := app.outStyle()
469			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
470				deps := "—"
471				if len(e.DepDirs) > 0 {
472					deps = strings.Join(e.DepDirs, ", ")
473				} else {
474					deps = "global cache"
475				}
476				tool := "installed"
477				if !e.ToolInstalled() {
478					tool = style.danger("MISSING: " + e.Tool)
479				} else {
480					tool = style.success(tool)
481				}
482				t.Add(e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, deps, tool)
483			}
484			t.Render(app.Out)
485		}
486	
487		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
488		if len(plan.Steps) == 0 {
489			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Nothing to provision.")
490		} else {
491			st := app.newTable("", "ACTION", "WHAT", "WHY")
492			style := app.outStyle()
493			for _, s := range plan.Steps {
494				mark := "✓"
495				if s.Skipped {
496					mark = style.dim("·")
497				} else {
498					mark = style.success(mark)
499				}
500				st.Add(mark, string(s.Kind), truncate(s.What, 34), s.Why)
501			}
502			st.Render(app.Out)
503		}
504	
505		for _, w := range plan.Warnings {
506			fmt.Fprintf(app.Err, "\n%s %s\n", app.errStyle().warning("warning:"), w)
507		}
508		if plan.Empty() {
509			fmt.Fprintln(app.Err, "\nNothing would run. If a new worktree comes up broken, add what it needs to "+
510				"worktree.post_create, or commit .dev-cli/config.toml with `dev wt plan --write`.")
511		}
512	}
513	
514	// writeRepoTemplate seeds .dev-cli/config.toml from the detected plan.
515	//
516	// Committing it is what makes a project's worktree setup reproducible: the
517	// next machine, and the next person, get the same one without having to
518	// rediscover it.
519	func writeRepoTemplate(app *App, repoPath string, plan wt.Plan, set wt.Settings) error {
520		path, err := projectconfig.ConfigPath(repoPath)
521		if err != nil {
522			return err
523		}
524		if _, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil {
525			return fmt.Errorf("%s already exists — edit it directly", config.Contract(path))
526		}
527		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
528			return err
529		}
530	
531		var b strings.Builder
532		b.WriteString("# dev project configuration (versioned with this repository).\n")
533		b.WriteString("version = 1\n\n")
534		b.WriteString("#\n")
535		b.WriteString("# Committed on purpose: a worktree is a clean checkout, so without this a\n")
536		b.WriteString("# new one comes up with no dependencies and none of the gitignored files the\n")
537		b.WriteString("# project needs. Seeded by `dev wt plan --write`; edit freely.\n\n")
538		b.WriteString("[worktree]\n")
539	
540		b.WriteString("# Gitignored files to carry into a new worktree. Only files that are BOTH\n")
541		b.WriteString("# listed here AND gitignored are copied — a tracked file is already in the\n")
542		b.WriteString("# checkout on the correct branch.\n")
543		b.WriteString("include = [")
544		for i, inc := range set.Include {
545			if i > 0 {
546				b.WriteString(", ")
547			}
548			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%q", inc)
549		}
550		b.WriteString("]\n\n")
551	
552		if len(plan.Ecosystems) > 0 {
553			b.WriteString("# Detected in this repository:\n")
554			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
555				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "#   %-8s %-8s (%s) → %s\n", e.Name, e.Manager, e.Marker, e.Install)
556			}
557			b.WriteString("#\n")
558			b.WriteString("# \"auto\" runs those install commands. Replace with an explicit list if this\n")
559			b.WriteString("# project needs something else:  post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
560			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n\n")
561	
562			b.WriteString("# How each project type gets its dependencies:\n")
563			b.WriteString("#   reinstall  run the install command (correct, the default)\n")
564			b.WriteString("#   copy       duplicate the directory from the source checkout (fast)\n")
565			b.WriteString("#   link       share one directory between checkouts (fastest, risky)\n")
566			b.WriteString("#   skip       leave the worktree without dependencies\n")
567			b.WriteString("[worktree.strategies]\n")
568			for _, e := range plan.Ecosystems {
569				switch {
570				case len(e.DepDirs) == 0:
571					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# %-8s = \"reinstall\"  # %s uses a global cache; nothing to copy\n",
572						e.Name, e.Manager)
573				case e.CopySafe:
574					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # \"copy\" is sound here and much faster\n", e.Name)
575				default:
576					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%-10s = \"reinstall\"  # copy/link unsupported: %s\n", e.Name, e.Hazard)
577				}
578			}
579		} else {
580			b.WriteString("# No project type detected. Add the commands a fresh checkout needs:\n")
581			b.WriteString("# post_create = [\"make bootstrap\"]\n")
582			b.WriteString("post_create = \"auto\"\n")
583		}
584	
585		for _, step := range plan.Steps {
586			if step.Kind == wt.StepInitSubmodules {
587				mode := set.Submodules.Init
588				if mode == "" {
589					mode = "recursive"
590				}
591				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n[submodules]\ninit = %q\ndevelop = [", mode)
592				for i, member := range set.Submodules.Develop {
593					if i > 0 {
594						b.WriteString(", ")
595					}
596					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%q", member)
597				}
598				b.WriteString("]\n")
599				break
600			}
601		}
602		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
603			return err
604		}
605		fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "wrote %s\n", config.Contract(path))
606		fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "Commit it so every machine provisions worktrees the same way.")
607		return nil
608	}

66	
67	## Source categories and upstream sync
68	
69	- `skills/local/` — canonical skills authored in this repository.
70	- `skills/owned/` — first-party skills maintained in another repository owned by the maintainer. Edit the source project, then sync its distribution copy here.
71	- `skills/vendor/` — third-party upstream skills; preserve upstream content.
72	
73	`vendor.yaml` remains the shared sync manifest. `collection: owned` selects
74	`skills/owned/`; an omitted collection defaults to `vendor`. Both support `series`,
75	`license_path`, `frozen`, and upstream commit tracking. Add published owned sources
76	with `scripts/add-vendor.sh --owned <owner/repo/path>`. A cross-repository symlink
77	cannot serve as a distributable copy.
78	
79	An unpublished owned skill may use `pending_upstream: true`. Its bootstrap mirror
80	contains real files but claims no remote SHA; routine sync/check preserves it.
81	After publishing the canonical source, run `scripts/sync-vendor.sh --activate <name>`.
82	Only a successful sync clears pending. See [owned workflow](docs/workflows/adding-owned-skills.md).
83	
84	## Vendor System (also used for owned sources)
85	
86	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; optional `license_path:` copies a repo-level license into the vendored directory as `LICENSE.txt`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
87	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
88	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
89	
90	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA. When `license_path` is present it also tracks the license blob SHA, so a license-only upstream change is visible to `make sync-check`.
91	
92	`.github/workflows/vendor-sync.yml` runs `make sync` weekly (Mon 03:00 UTC,
93	plus `workflow_dispatch` with an optional single-skill filter) and opens/updates
94	a PR on the fixed branch `chore/vendor-sync` — never a direct commit to `main`,
95	because vendored content ships to downstream agents via `npx skills update` and
96	a broken frontmatter is silently skipped rather than erroring. PRs created with
97	`GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger `validate.yml`, so the sync job runs the publish
98	gates itself. A red sync job usually means an upstream rename/removal — handle
99	it with `renamed_from:` or `frozen:` as below.
100	
101	Active series in this repo:
102	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
103	
104	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
105	
106	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
107	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
108	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
109	
110	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
111	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
112	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
113	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
114	  `skills@1.5.24` writes `skills-lock.json`, but a renamed skill is still a
115	  different install ID; review the lock and explicitly reinstall the new name.
116	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
117	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
118	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
119	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
120	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
121	
122	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
123	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
124	
125	## Marketplace Catalog
126	
127	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
128	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
129	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
130	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
131	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
132	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
133	for the full mechanism.
134	
135	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
136	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
137	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
138	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
139	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>`, `./owned/<name>`, or
140	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
141	
142	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
143	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
144	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
145	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
146	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
147	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
148	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
149	within-group caveat in
150	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
151	
152	## SKILL.md Format
153	
154	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
155	
156	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
157	
158	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
159	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
160	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
161	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
162	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
163	
164	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
165	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
166	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
167	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
168	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
169	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
170	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
171	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
172	
173	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
174	
175	```bash
176	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
177	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
178	
179	# …or remove them afterward
180	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
181	```
182	
183	## Project Memory Workflow
184	
185	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
186	
187	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
188	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
189	
190	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
191	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
192	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
193	
194	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
195	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
196	
197	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
198	
199	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
200	
201	   ```bash
202	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
203	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
204	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
205	   ```
206	
207	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
208	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
209	
210	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
211	
212	   ```bash
213	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
214	   ```
215	
216	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
217	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
218	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
219	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
220	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
221	
222	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
223	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
224	   afterwards to catch drift.
225	
226	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
227	
228	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
229	
230	```bash
231	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
232	```
233	
234	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
235	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
236	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
237	
238	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
239	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
240	
241	### External skill / MCP / domain / curiosity catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
242	
243	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
244	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
245	own conventions). It has four subareas:
246	
247	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
248	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
249	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
250	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
251	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
252	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
253	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
254	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
255	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
256	- `docs/catalog/curiosities.md` — docs-only shelf for interesting,
257	  provocative, or highly personal skills that are deliberately excluded
258	  from `vendor.yaml`, marketplace grouping, and routine skill discovery.
259	  Entries use `skipped` with the reason they remain docs-only.
260	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
261	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
262	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
263	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
264	  status / license / last_verified`).
265	
266	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
267	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
268	
269	| Status | Meaning |
270	|---|---|
271	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
272	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
273	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
274	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
275	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
276	
277	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
278	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
279	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
280	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
281	
282	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
283	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
284	
285	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
286	
287	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
288	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
289	
290	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
291	2. The root cause
292	3. The workaround
293	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
294	
295	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
296	the explanation they do not know yet.
297
```

# dev-cli

Git owns durable code; worktrees are local checkouts; runtimes are host-local
sessions; dev records task intent.

## Discover what you need

Use `dev <command> --help` for current syntax and flags, and `dev help <topic>`
for workflow explanations. `dev --help` lists commands; `dev help` lists topics.
Prefer supported `--json` output for automation. Read the relevant command before
mutation: some actions execute immediately, while others require preview/apply.
Do not preload manuals, repeat `dev --skill`, or run routine diagnostics.

## Preserve these boundaries

- Opening a repository needs no task. Choose direct, branch, or worktree
  deliberately; pass an explicit `--base` for branch/worktree creation. Keep
  managed worktrees outside repositories.
- `dev start` normally prepares a checkout/runtime. Agent launch is explicit.
  Parallel writers need coordinated ownership and verified launch targets.
- Completion, artifact finalization, retirement and branch deletion are separate.
  Finalize after writer exit; retire externally. Use `retire --base` when a fork
  point cannot prove integration. Runtime `done` is not cleanup-ready.
- Unknown or cached observations, merged PRs, and command refusals do not grant
  cleanup authority. Resolve the reported conditions; do not improvise force
  removal or bypass trust checks.

## Read a reference for advanced operations

- Worktree provisioning or cross-host lifecycle: [ownership](references/worktree-ownership.md), [lifecycle](references/task-lifecycle.md).
- Parallel agent launches or prompt transports: [agents](references/parallel-agents.md), [handoffs](references/prompt-handoffs.md).
- History retention: [artifacts](references/ai-artifacts.md).
- Agent completion or cleanup batches: [retirement](references/agent-retirement.md), [triage](references/local-triage.md).
- Repository hygiene batches, `report --json` summaries, scans or redaction: [hygiene](references/hygiene.md).
- Repository hooks, publication, or physical organization: [setup](references/repository-bootstrap.md), [bootstrap](references/bootstrap.md).
- SSH dashboard, diagnosis, discovery, tests/activity, keys, credentials and registration: [SSH](references/ssh-hosts.md).
- Dotfile setup, native chezmoi operations, or FLEET host actions: [dotfiles](references/dotfiles.md).
- Skill/MCP/instruction transfers, updates or removal: [transfers](references/agent-interop.md), [maintenance](references/skills-management.md).
- Recursive Git children: [submodules](references/submodules.md).

Use command help and its workflow topic for everyday operations.

## Unexpected dev failures

Read [feedback and repair](references/feedback-and-repair.md). Preserve the
original task; extra investigation, repair, subagents and publication need
explicit consent covering scope and cost.

5	// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
6	// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
7	// re-derivable.

42		WorkspaceIdentityObserved bool
43		WorkspaceCheckout         string

46		// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single

49		// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:

51		AgentStatus string
52		// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
53		AgentSessions []string

61	func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
62		for _, d := range s.Dirs {

64			// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
65			// $HOME active.

92	// Load reads configuration and prepares the shared stores.
93	func (a *App) Load() error {
94		cfg, err := config.Load(a.configPath)
95		if err != nil {
96			return err
97		}
98		a.Cfg = cfg
99		if a.In == nil {
100			a.In = os.Stdin
101		}
102		if a.Out == nil {
103			a.Out = os.Stdout
104		}
105		if a.Err == nil {
106			a.Err = os.Stderr
107		}
108		a.Tasks = task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
109		a.Catalog = catalog.NewStore(cfg.AssetsDir(), catalog.WithDiagnosticSink(func(diagnostic catalog.Diagnostic) {
110			fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "%s %s\n", a.errStyle().warning("dev: warning:"), diagnostic.Error())
111		}))
112		a.Registry = catalog.NewRegistry(a.Catalog)
113		noteStore := note.NewStore(cfg.NotesDir(), note.WithDiagnosticSink(func(path string, err error) {
114			fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: warning: skipping note %s: %v\n", filepath.Base(path), err)
115		}))
116		a.Notes = note.NewService(noteStore, cfg.NotesIndexFile())
117		a.Notes.IndexDiagnostic = func(err error) {
118			fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "dev: warning: note search index: %v\n", err)
119		}
120		if a.Sizes == nil {
121			cache := diskusage.NewCache(filepath.Join(config.CacheHome(), "dev", "sizes-v1.json"), 10*time.Minute)
122			a.Sizes = diskusage.NewManager(cache, 2)
123		}
124		return nil
125	}

134	// Runtime resolves the multiplexer backend for this invocation, honouring

136	func (a *App) Runtime() runtime.Runtime {
137		if a.runtimeInstance != nil {
138			return a.runtimeInstance
139		}
140		if a.noRuntime {
141			return runtime.None{}
142		}
143		backend := a.Cfg.Runtime.Backend
144		if a.runtimeOverride != "" {
145			backend = a.runtimeOverride
146		}
147		return a.runtimeNamed(backend)
148	}

150	// runtimeNamed resolves the backend that owns a persisted opaque handle. It
151	// deliberately bypasses the current backend override: feeding a Herdr handle to
152	// tmux after a config change is never valid.
153	func (a *App) runtimeNamed(name string) runtime.Runtime {
154		if rt := a.runtimesByName[name]; rt != nil {
155			return rt
156		}
157		if a.runtimeInstance != nil && (name == "" || a.runtimeInstance.Name() == name) {
158			return a.runtimeInstance
159		}
160		rt := runtime.Select(name)
161		if h, ok := rt.(*runtime.Herdr); ok {
162			return h.WithMetadataSource(a.Cfg.Runtime.MetadataSource)
163		}
164		return rt
165	}

170	}

173	func (a *App) warnf(format string, args ...any) {
174		message := fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)
175		fmt.Fprintf(a.Err, "%s %s\n", a.errStyle().warning("dev:"), message)

178	// cdDirective asks the shell wrapper to move its parent process. The wrapper
179	// gives dev a child-only file descriptor so normal output stays connected to
180	// the terminal and an inherited environment variable can never name a file to
181	// overwrite. NUL terminates the path because filesystem paths may contain
182	// newlines. Without the wrapper, retain the printable directive used by older
183	// integrations.
184	func (a *App) cdDirective(dir string) error {
185		if a.workflowHandoff != nil {
186			copy := *a
187			copy.workflowHandoff = nil
188			return a.workflowHandoff(func() error { return copy.cdDirective(dir) })
189		}
190		// Windows shells do not inherit an extra descriptor the way the POSIX
191		// wrapper's `3>file` redirection does, so the PowerShell wrapper names a
192		// temp file instead and reads it back after dev exits.
193		if path := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE"); path != "" {
194			return os.WriteFile(path, append([]byte(dir), 0), 0o600)
195		}
196		if rawFD := os.Getenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD"); rawFD != "" {
197			fd, err := strconv.Atoi(rawFD)
198			if err != nil || fd < 3 {
199				return fmt.Errorf("invalid DEV_SHELL_CD_FD %q", rawFD)
200			}
201			file := os.NewFile(uintptr(fd), "dev-shell-cd")
202			if file == nil {
203				return fmt.Errorf("invalid shell directory descriptor %d", fd)
204			}
205			if _, err := file.Write(append([]byte(dir), 0)); err != nil {
206				return fmt.Errorf("write shell directory directive: %w", err)
207			}
208			if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
209				return fmt.Errorf("close shell directory directive: %w", err)
210			}
211			return nil
212		}
213		_, err := fmt.Fprintf(a.Out, "cd %s\n", shellQuote(dir))
214		return err

18	}

20	// New initialises a repository with one commit on branch "main".

22		t.Helper()
23		// Windows hands back an 8.3 short path (C:\Users\RUNNER~1\...) that git then
24		// reports in its long form, so canonicalize once up front.

27			tempDir = resolved
28		}

30		if err := os.MkdirAll(root, 0o755); err != nil {
31			t.Fatal(err)
32		}
33		r := &Repo{T: t, Root: root}

35		// Identity and signing are configured locally so the test never depends on
36		// (or is broken by) the developer's global git config.
37		r.Git("config", "user.email", "dev@example.test")
38		r.Git("config", "user.name", "dev test")
39		r.Git("config", "commit.gpgsign", "false")
40		// Keep line endings and symlinks byte-for-byte on every platform; the
41		// Windows CI runner defaults core.autocrlf to true.

43		r.Git("config", "core.symlinks", "true")

47		return r
48	}

```text
1	# Worktree ownership
2	
3	Submodule initialization is core Git acquisition, before provisioning/runtime, and defaults to recursive pinned checkouts. `--no-provision` does not skip it; `--submodules=none` does. Gitlink children are independent submodule clones, not nested managed linked worktrees. Read `submodules.md` for selection and explicit disposal rules.
4	
5	Read this before creating a worktree, sharing a checkout between agents, or when
6	a new checkout lacks dependencies, env files, or launcher backend state.
7	
8	## The rule
9	
10	| Change boundary | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
11	|---|---|---|---|
12	| Durable feature/fix/experiment/handoff | **`dev`** | `paths.worktree_path` | until external `dev retire` |
13	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation | Claude Code | `.claude/worktrees/` | managed by that harness; do not assume artifact relocation |
14	| Runtime workspace/panes | Herdr | per-host runtime | until explicitly closed |
15	| Rendered agent history | SpecStory | process launch checkout | until committed/removed with that checkout |
16	
17	Use a `dev` worktree for independent approaches or any change stream whose code,
18	history, or plan must remain reviewable. Agents with explicitly disjoint file
19	ownership may share one checkout, but `--allow-shared-checkout` is a deliberate
20	coordination override—not a default.
21	
22	`EnterWorktree` changes an agent's working location; it does not prove an
23	existing SpecStory wrapper/watcher rebound its source/output paths. Start the
24	new process from the target worktree root.
25	
26	## Why dev creates the checkout
27	
28	`dev` runs `git worktree add`, then asks Herdr to run
29	`worktree open --path <path> --no-focus`. Path policy therefore remains stable
30	on machines without Herdr, while Herdr still displays repo/branch provenance.
31	A fallback plain workspace is reported as such and is not an exact agent launch
32	target.
33	
34	Never nest a durable worktree inside another checkout. Every watcher, language
35	server, backup tool and search then sees a second copy of the repository.
36	
37	Herdr's native **New worktree** action is still valid for an external,
38	unmanaged checkout. When the canonical repository is under a configured scan
39	root, Git registration lets dev discover the checkout without scanning
40	`~/.herdr/worktrees`; dev does not auto-adopt, relocate, or provision it. Run
41	`dev wt provision <path>` if it needs the project environment and `dev adopt`
42	followed by `dev adopt --apply` only when it should enter the durable task
43	lifecycle. For one exact checkout, `dev flow [repo]` offers plan-first
44	metadata-only Adopt and clean branch-preserving Remove Checkout. It never removes
45	the canonical checkout or a harness/conflicting/locked/prunable/task-claimed row,
46	and it does not prune repository-wide stale registrations.
47	
48	## Paths
49	
50	Default:
51	
52	```text
53	~/Worktrees/<repo>/<branch-slug>
54	```
55	
56	Configurable through `paths.worktree_root` and `paths.worktree_path`, with
57	`worktree_root`, `repo`, `repo_path`, `branch`, `category`, `host`, and `date`
58	variables plus `slug`, `lower`, and `base` filters.
59	
60	Always pass `--base` for unattended creation so the intended starting point is
61	explicit. `dev start` and `dev wt create` otherwise resolve the repository's
62	default branch; they do not use whichever feature happens to be checked out.
63	
64	## Provisioning
65	
66	A worktree is a clean checkout. `dev wt create` and `dev start` build and apply
67	an inspectable plan:
68	
69	```bash
70	dev wt plan
71	dev wt plan --write
72	dev wt provision --dry-run
73	```
74	
75	Effective settings come from global config or committed repo
76	`.dev-cli/config.toml` (legacy `.dev.toml` remains readable):
77	
78	```toml
79	[worktree]
80	include = [".env", ".env.local"]
81	link = []
82	post_create = "auto"
83	strategy = "reinstall"
84	```
85	
86	An executable `post_create` from `.dev-cli/config.toml` requires approval of its
87	exact content hash with `dev config trust <repo> --yes`. Legacy `.dev.toml`
88	retains its compatibility behavior.
89	
90	Only paths that are both explicitly included and genuinely gitignored are
91	copied. Tracked files already have the branch-correct version. Included files
92	must remain the same regular file from validation through open; source swaps and
93	symlinked destination parents are refused. Existing destinations are reported
94	as skipped, never falsely as copied, and file contents are never logged.
95	
96	This is local provisioning only. Off-machine `dev fleet files` deliberately uses
97	a separate `[local_files].include` allowlist plus explicit `--to`; never infer
98	export permission from `[worktree].include`.
99	
100	### Project-local Claude backend state
101	
102	`.claude/settings.local.json` stays gitignored and is **not** a universal default
103	include. The verified `claude-copilot-once` wrapper preserves an existing
104	Copilot pin and creates/removes only its own pin when one was absent;
105	`codex-copilot-once` injects its backend via CLI. Neither needs a copied project
106	file. Claude's Copilot proxy must already be running; the Codex path may
107	self-start its proxy flow.
108	
109	An explicitly selected sticky/plain-Claude profile may opt in exactly:
110	
111	```toml
112	[worktree]
113	include = [".env", ".env.local", ".claude/settings.local.json"]
114	```
115	
116	Verify the file arrived before launch. If absent, stop instead of allowing the
117	launcher to fall back silently to another backend. `dev` logs the relative path
118	only, never its contents.
119	
120	## Dependency strategies
121	
122	- `reinstall`: safe default; run lockfile-derived installer.
123	- `copy`: duplicate path-independent dependency trees.
124	- `link`: explicit and usually unsafe for mutable dependencies.
125	- `skip`: for external/container-managed environments.
126	
127	`dev` refuses unsound choices, such as copied/linked Python virtualenvs, and
128	reports missing tools or failed setup without deleting the usable checkout.
129	
130	## Cleanup
131	
132	- `dev wt rm <branch>` removes only the checkout after external runtime safety checks; branch survives.

1	# dev and Herdr
2	
3	Read this on a Herdr machine, when task state should appear in the sidebar, or
4	when a `dev start --json` result will be used to launch an agent.
5	
6	## Division of responsibility
7	
8	```
9	Herdr       per-host workspace, pane, process and live-agent state
10	dev         durable task, branch and checkout lifecycle
11	SpecStory   history writer rooted at the launched process checkout
12	Git         durable commits, transcript and plan
13	```
14	
15	Herdr is not synced between machines. `dev` persists an advisory runtime handle
16	with its owning backend name, revalidates the handle against live checkout
17	coverage before close/resume, and reopens stale handles. This prevents a Herdr
18	handle being sent to Tmux/none after config changes. Legacy nameless handles are
19	used only after exact current-backend validation. Root-pane data stays transient.
20	
21	## What dev asks Herdr to do
22	
23	| dev operation | Herdr command |
24	|---|---|
25	| list live sessions | `workspace list` + `pane list` |
26	| list pane-level agent activity | `agent list` |
27	| inspect exact foreground programs | `pane process-info --pane <id>` |
28	| open a checkout | `workspace create --cwd <dir> --no-focus --label <name>` |
29	| open a worktree | `worktree open --cwd <parent-root> --path <path> --no-focus --label <repo/branch>` |
30	| activate an opened checkout | `workspace focus <id>`; outside Herdr, attach the default client |
31	| dispatch an explicit start command | `pane run <exact-root-pane-id> <command>` |
32	| close a session | `workspace close <id>` |
33	| show task state | `workspace report-metadata <id> --source dev --token …` |
34	
35	`dev` creates worktrees with Git and only asks Herdr to open them. It derives
36	the canonical parent checkout from Git and passes it with `--cwd`, so grouping
37	does not depend on whichever Herdr pane invoked `dev`. First-class `worktree
38	open` gives the child native repository/worktree grouping plus branch/ahead-
39	behind data. Worktree-mode `dev start` uses the same `repo/branch`
40	label as `dev wt create`; no special origin labels or metadata are needed.
41	
42	A plain-workspace fallback reports `surface=workspace` honestly. A root pane is
43	automatically launchable only when the same successful `worktree open` response
44	proves a newly created layout. Reuse, fallback, missing/malformed responses,
45	Tmux, and the `none` runtime never supply a launchable pane. `--no-focus`
46	preserves the caller's context; never substitute the focused/current pane.
47	
48	`dev start --run '<shell command>'` consumes that proof directly, dispatches
49	opaque shell text without persisting or echoing it, and returns after Herdr
50	accepts the command. It does not wait for completion or report the command's
51	exit status. `--focus` remains independent and runs only after successful
52	dispatch. `--json` stays a separate pure creation contract.
53	
54	Read `parallel-agents.md` for exact machine validation, pane verification,
55	SpecStory profiles and permission-mode rules.
56	
57	## Collision preflight
58	
59	On Herdr, `dev` compares recognized agent cwd values by canonical Git worktree
60	root before writer-claiming direct/branch starts and resume. It resolves
61	`herdr pane current --current` before excluding the caller, because inherited
62	`HERDR_PANE_ID` may be stale after a pane move. Every recognized state—including
63	`idle`, `done`, and `unknown`—is occupied; malformed/missing activity data fails
64	closed.
65	
66	Pure local repo/worktree open and TUI Enter reuse the live owner's workspace and
67	do not claim a second writer. Inside Herdr they request runtime focus;
68	outside Herdr the TUI first restores the terminal and then attaches, matching
69	`hhere`. The root `--allow-shared-checkout` escape hatch is
70	only for coordinated writer ownership. A default worktree start remains
71	separate and needs no override.
72	
73	For artifact operations, only an exact agent session ID (`agent_session` kind
74	`id`, not a title) can prove the caller differs from a stopped transcript's
75	valid UUID in the actual SpecStory-generated anchored preamble. Other live
76	agents always block. Unknown caller identity or artifact ownership needs explicit
77	`--allow-shared-checkout`; an identified caller-owned live transcript remains
78	forbidden. This does not prove recorder exit. See the
79	[artifact writer guard](hygiene.md#artifact-writer-guard).
80	
81	`dev status` shows recognized activities for the current worktree.
82	
83	## Sidebar metadata
84	
85	Task annotations use `$stage` and `$next`. Tokens render only if the local Herdr
86	row layout names them; reporting an unused token succeeds silently.
87	
88	```toml
89	[ui.sidebar.spaces]
90	rows = [
91	  ["state_icon", "workspace", "$stage"],
92	  ["branch", "git_status"],
93	  ["$next"],
94	]
95	```
96	
97	## Cleanup semantics
98	
99	Recursive submodule retirement retains the version-2 coordinator's exact caller,
100	foreground-program consent, and task/Git/artifact preview checks. Child graph,
101	workspace intent and artifact ownership are bound to that same preview; changed
102	child refs or state require a new preview before runtime closure or removal.
103	
104	Herdr agent `done` means the latest turn settled. It does not establish that
105	history is synced, review is complete, code is committed, or cleanup is safe.
106	Never auto-close based on agent state.
107	
108	- `dev park` records WARM; inside its own workspace it leaves runtime alive for normal agent exit.
109	- `dev park --cold --push` closes/removes only from an external safe caller.
110	- `dev done --ff` integrates and keeps worktree/branch; selected task pane closures are explicit and reported.
111	- `dev done --pr` leaves task/runtime/worktree for review.
112	- `dev retire` externally closes, waits, revalidates and removes.
113	- `dev sweep` reports first and routes DONE cleanup through retire.
114	
115	`workspace close` itself touches no branch or checkout, but it can kill the
116	caller before later cleanup runs. Retirement therefore refuses caller
117	workspace/pane containment, mixed workspaces, and working/blocked/waiting
118	agents. Unknown status needs external `--close-unknown`; close failure or timeout
119	stops worktree removal. `--cold --keep-session` remains rejected.
120	
121	The independent `dev flow [repo]` preview treats local refresh as local-only and
122	does not expose `--close-unknown`, `--assume-no-runtime`, shared-writer, or
123	takeover overrides. `runtime=none` means session/agent occupancy is unobserved,
124	not known closed; otherwise complete Git/task snapshots may still be fresh.
125	Resume handoff activates a runtime or changes directory only after the alternate
126	screen exits.
127	
128	## Agent-session handoff
129	
130	Herdr exposes live agent session IDs and `Task.AgentSession` exists in the task
131	schema. `dev prepare` captures one exact `provider:uuid` from its flag, the task,
132	or a unique covering runtime session and persists it for artifact finalization.
133	Resume still reopens/rebuilds checkout and runtime only; launching/resuming an
134	agent conversation remains an explicit wrapper operation.
135	
136	## Without Herdr
137	
138	Runtime selection is Herdr → Tmux → Zellij → none unless pinned. Tmux follows
139	sesh semantics: switch the current client inside tmux, attach outside. Zellij
140	attaches outside and uses `action switch-session` inside on Zellij 0.44+;
141	older releases report the missing switch capability instead of nesting a
142	second client. Tmux and Zellij can report session creation/reuse but no pane.
143	Zellij keeps exited sessions resurrectable in its listing; `dev` recognizes the
144	exact `(EXITED - attach to resurrect)` marker and treats those sessions as closed
145	(they cover no checkout and are never killed). A live name merely containing
146	`EXITED` remains live. A name an exited session still owns fails `dev start`
147	closed, and a session that exits during layout inspection asks for a retry,
148	rather than resurrecting its old layout — reclaim it with
149	`zellij delete-session <name>`.
150	`none` emits a shell `cd` directive in human mode;
151	`dev start --json` suppresses that directive and stays pure JSON.
152	
153	On Windows there is no tmux, Zellij or Herdr, so the backend is always `none`
154	regardless of configuration. `dev shell-init powershell` still consumes the `cd`
155	directive (via a `DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE` temp file rather than file descriptor 3).
156	
157	The trusted `dev shell-init` output installs a shell wrapper. Navigation uses a
158	private side channel containing one NUL-terminated path; the wrapper calls
159	`builtin cd` or `Set-Location` without evaluating command output. The standalone
160	binary's printable legacy directive cannot change its parent shell's directory.
161	
162	## Completion and process consent
163	
164	Parent/canonical and other-checkout workspaces are preserved, including when
165	their panes cd into a task worktree. Missing first-class Herdr workspace
166	ownership blocks retirement. Only task-worktree idle/done panes can be selected
167	for closure under final taskflow Apply. General programs need separate FF
168	file-change consent and `CLOSE <workspace-id>` for interactive retirement.
169	Process evidence includes tab/terminal incarnation, shell/group PID and a
170	redacted executable/argv digest. Supported probe failures block; background jobs
171	are unobserved. Version-2 coordinator handoffs bind this evidence and permit
172	only the exact dev caller returning to its original foreground shell. See
173	`agent-retirement.md` for the full scope and cancellation rules.
174	
175	Dashboard start wizards offer open/stay, defaulting to open. Runtime and external retirement handoffs execute only after the dashboard exits. See [dashboard actions](dashboard-actions.md).
176	
177	## Saved SSH machines
178	
179	`dev ssh manage` integrates Herdr 0.9.0's native machine CLI. It keeps SSH target,
180	label, opaque profile ID and explicit session separate. Native add can prepare
181	and start the remote server; native approvals remain required. Disabling or

185

193	These catalog actions refresh only local metadata. Herdr 0.9.0 connects enabled

195	The menu keeps native installation approvals. --no-runtime skips Herdr reads. SSH remains a

198	
199	FLEET Enter and `dev fleet open` share contextual navigation. `HERDR_ENV=1`

236	        if probe_docs not in normalized or normalized.intersection({"docs", "docs/_snippets"}):

242	            f"({details}). Run: bash .agents/skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/"
243	            "migrate-i18n-llmstxt.sh --target-dir . --apply --verify --json",

248	def configured_locales(i18n: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str | None, list[str]]:
249	    languages = i18n.get("languages", [])
250	    if not isinstance(languages, list):
251	        raise BuildFailure("Plugin `i18n.languages` must be a list.", 2)
252	
253	    locales: list[str] = []
254	    defaults: list[str] = []
255	    for language in languages:
256	        if not isinstance(language, dict) or not isinstance(language.get("locale"), str):
257	            raise BuildFailure("Every `i18n.languages` entry needs a string `locale`.", 2)
258	        locale = language["locale"]
259	        locales.append(locale)
260	        if language.get("default") is True:
261	            defaults.append(locale)
262	    if len(set(locales)) != len(locales):
263	        raise BuildFailure("Plugin `i18n.languages` contains duplicate locales.", 2)
264	    if len(locales) > 1 and len(defaults) != 1:
265	        raise BuildFailure(
266	            "A multilingual build needs exactly one `i18n.languages` entry with "
267	            "`default: true`.",
268	            2,
269	        )
270	    if len(locales) > 1 and i18n.get("docs_structure", "suffix") != "suffix":
271	        raise BuildFailure(
272	            "This managed helper supports only `i18n.docs_structure: suffix`.", 2
273	        )
274	    default = defaults[0] if defaults else (locales[0] if locales else None)
275	    return default, locales

278	def assert_safe_tree(source: Path, target: Path, site_dir: Path) -> None:
279	    if not source.exists() or not source.is_dir():
280	        raise BuildFailure(f"Docs directory not found: {source}", 2)
281	    if source.is_symlink():
282	        raise BuildFailure(f"Refusing symlinked docs directory: {source}", 2)
283	    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(source, followlinks=False):
284	        root_path = Path(root)
285	        for name in [*dirs, *files]:
286	            candidate = root_path / name
287	            if candidate.is_symlink():
288	                raise BuildFailure(
289	                    f"Refusing symlink inside docs tree: {candidate.relative_to(source)}", 2
290	                )
291	
292	    if not is_relative_to(source, target):
293	        raise BuildFailure(
294	            f"Docs directory must stay inside --target-dir: {source} (target: {target}).",
295	            2,
296	        )
297	    if not is_relative_to(site_dir, target) or site_dir == target:
298	        raise BuildFailure(
299	            f"Site directory must be a child of --target-dir, not {site_dir}.", 2
300	        )
301	    if (
302	        site_dir == source
303	        or is_relative_to(source, site_dir)
304	        or is_relative_to(site_dir, source)
305	    ):
306	        raise BuildFailure("site_dir and docs_dir may not contain one another.", 2)
307	    if site_dir.is_symlink():
308	        raise BuildFailure(f"Refusing symlinked site directory: {site_dir}", 2)
309	    if site_dir.exists() and not site_dir.is_dir():
310	        raise BuildFailure(f"site_dir exists but is not a directory: {site_dir}", 2)

313	def is_translated_source(path: Path, nondefault_locales: Iterable[str]) -> bool:
314	    name = path.name.casefold()
315	    return any(
316	        name.endswith(f".{locale.casefold()}{extension}")
317	        for locale in nondefault_locales

322	def copy_docs_tree(
323	    source: Path,
324	    destination: Path,
325	    *,
326	    nondefault_locales: Iterable[str] = (),
327	) -> None:
328	    blocked = tuple(nondefault_locales)
329	
330	    def ignore(directory: str, names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
331	        base = Path(directory)
332	        return [name for name in names if is_translated_source(base / name, blocked)]
333	
334	    shutil.copytree(source, destination, ignore=ignore if blocked else None)
