389	def llmstxt_expected_pages(config: dict[str, Any], docs_dir: Path) -> set[str]:
390	    present, llms = plugin_definition(config, "llmstxt")
391	    if not present:
392	        return set()
393	    sections = llms.get("sections", {})
394	    if not isinstance(sections, dict):
395	        raise BuildFailure("Plugin `llmstxt.sections` must be a mapping.", 2)
396	    source_uris = [
397	        path.relative_to(docs_dir).as_posix()
398	        for path in docs_dir.rglob("*")
399	        if path.is_file()
400	    ]
401	    expected: set[str] = set()
402	    for inputs in sections.values():
403	        if not isinstance(inputs, list):
404	            raise BuildFailure("Every `llmstxt.sections` value must be a list.", 2)
405	        for item in inputs:
406	            value = next(iter(item)) if isinstance(item, dict) and item else item
407	            if not isinstance(value, str):
408	                raise BuildFailure("llmstxt section entries must be paths or path mappings.", 2)
409	            if "*" in value:
410	                expected.update(fnmatch.filter(source_uris, value))
411	            else:
412	                expected.add(value)
413	    return expected

416	def safe_output_path(value: Any, label: str) -> Path | None:
417	    if value is None:
418	        return None
419	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
420	        raise BuildFailure(f"Plugin `llmstxt.{label}` must be a non-empty path.", 2)
421	    path = Path(value)
422	    if path.is_absolute() or ".." in path.parts:
423	        raise BuildFailure(f"Plugin `llmstxt.{label}` must stay inside site_dir: {value}", 2)
424	    return path

427	def generated_sidecars(site_dir: Path) -> list[Path]:
428	    return sorted(path for path in site_dir.rglob("*.md") if path.is_file())

431	def local_markdown_links(llms_file: Path, site_url: str) -> list[Path]:
432	    parsed_site = urlparse(site_url)
433	    base_path = parsed_site.path.rstrip("/") + "/"
434	    links: list[Path] = []
435	    destinations: list[str] = []
436	    for line in llms_file.read_text("utf-8").splitlines():
437	        match = re.match(r"^\s*-\s+\[[^]]*\]\((.+?)\)(?::.*)?\s*$", line)
438	        if match:
439	            destinations.append(match.group(1))
440	    for destination in destinations:
441	        parsed = urlparse(destination.strip("<>"))
442	        if parsed.scheme or parsed.netloc:
443	            if (parsed.scheme, parsed.netloc) != (parsed_site.scheme, parsed_site.netloc):
444	                continue
445	            path = parsed.path
446	        elif parsed.path.startswith("/"):
447	            path = parsed.path
448	        else:
449	            path = base_path + parsed.path
450	        if not path.startswith(base_path):
451	            raise BuildFailure(
452	                f"Generated llms.txt contains a local URL outside site_url: {destination}"
453	            )
454	        relative = unquote(path[len(base_path) :]).lstrip("/")
455	        candidate = Path(relative)
456	        if candidate.suffix == ".md":
457	            if candidate.is_absolute() or ".." in candidate.parts:
458	                raise BuildFailure(f"Unsafe generated Markdown URL: {destination}")
459	            links.append(candidate)
460	    return links
461

463	def has_locale_path(path: Path, nondefault_locales: Iterable[str]) -> bool:
464	    folded_parts = {part.casefold() for part in path.parts}
465	    name = path.name.casefold()
466	    return any(
467	        locale.casefold() in folded_parts
468	        or name.endswith(f".{locale.casefold()}.md")
469	        for locale in nondefault_locales
470	    )

473	def verify_llms_output(
474	    *,
475	    site_dir: Path,
476	    config: dict[str, Any],
477	    docs_dir: Path,
478	    site_url: str,
479	    full_output: Path | None,
480	    nondefault_locales: list[str],
481	) -> tuple[list[Path], list[Path]]:
482	    llms_file = site_dir / "llms.txt"
483	    if not llms_file.is_file() or not llms_file.read_text("utf-8").strip():
484	        raise BuildFailure("llmstxt pass did not produce a non-empty llms.txt.")
485	    if full_output is not None:
486	        full_file = site_dir / full_output
487	        if not full_file.is_file() or not full_file.read_text("utf-8").strip():
488	            raise BuildFailure(f"llmstxt pass did not produce a non-empty {full_output}.")
489	
490	    sidecars = generated_sidecars(site_dir)
491	    expected = llmstxt_expected_pages(config, docs_dir)
492	    if len(sidecars) < len(expected):
493	        raise BuildFailure(
494	            f"llmstxt generated {len(sidecars)} Markdown sidecars for "
495	            f"{len(expected)} configured pages."
496	        )
497	    links = local_markdown_links(llms_file, site_url)
498	    if len(set(links)) < len(expected):
499	        raise BuildFailure(
500	            f"llms.txt links to {len(set(links))} Markdown pages but "
501	            f"{len(expected)} are configured."
502	        )
503	    for relative in [*sidecars, *(site_dir / link for link in links)]:
504	        checked = relative.relative_to(site_dir)
505	        if has_locale_path(checked, nondefault_locales):
506	            raise BuildFailure(
507	                f"Default-language LLM output unexpectedly contains locale path: {checked}"
508	            )
509	        if not relative.is_file():
510	            raise BuildFailure(f"Generated llms.txt points to missing local file: {checked}")
511	    return sidecars, links

514	def copy_artifacts(
515	    source_site: Path,
516	    destination: Path,
517	    *,
518	    full_output: Path | None,
519	    include_sidecars: bool,
520	) -> int:
521	    artifacts = [Path("llms.txt")]
522	    if full_output is not None:
523	        artifacts.append(full_output)
524	    if include_sidecars:
525	        artifacts.extend(path.relative_to(source_site) for path in generated_sidecars(source_site))
526	    copied = 0
527	    for relative in artifacts:
528	        source = source_site / relative
529	        if not source.is_file():
530	            raise BuildFailure(f"Required generated artifact is missing: {source}")
531	        target = destination / relative
532	        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
533	        shutil.copy2(source, target)
534	        copied += int(relative.suffix == ".md")
535	    return copied

547	def atomic_replace_tree(staged: Path, destination: Path) -> None:
548	    destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
549	    backup = destination.parent / f".{destination.name}.backup-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
550	    had_destination = destination.exists()
551	    if had_destination:
552	        os.replace(destination, backup)
553	    try:
554	        os.replace(staged, destination)
555	    except BaseException:
556	        if had_destination and backup.exists():
557	            os.replace(backup, destination)
558	        raise
559	    if backup.exists():
560	        try:
561	            shutil.rmtree(backup)
562	        except OSError as error:
563	            log(f"warning: could not remove previous site backup {backup}: {error}")

566	def build(argv: list[str]) -> int:
567	    args = parse_args(argv)
568	    target = Path(args.target_dir).expanduser().resolve(strict=False)
569	    if not target.is_dir():
570	        raise BuildFailure(f"Target directory not found: {target}", 2)
571	    config_candidate = unresolved_under(target, args.config_file)
572	    if config_candidate.is_symlink():
573	        raise BuildFailure(f"Refusing symlinked MkDocs config: {config_candidate}", 2)
574	    config_file = config_candidate.resolve(strict=False)
575	    if not config_file.is_file():
576	        raise BuildFailure(f"MkDocs config not found: {config_file}", 2)
577	    config = load_raw_config(config_file)
578	    validate_env_contract(config_file, config)
579	
580	    docs_value = config.get("docs_dir", "docs")
581	    if not isinstance(docs_value, (str, os.PathLike)):
582	        raise BuildFailure("mkdocs.yml `docs_dir` must be a path.", 2)
583	    docs_candidate = unresolved_under(config_file.parent, docs_value)
584	    if docs_candidate.is_symlink():
585	        raise BuildFailure(f"Refusing symlinked docs directory: {docs_candidate}", 2)
586	    docs_dir = docs_candidate.resolve(strict=False)
587	    if args.site_dir:
588	        site_candidate = unresolved_under(target, args.site_dir)
589	    else:
590	        site_value = config.get("site_dir", "site")
591	        if not isinstance(site_value, (str, os.PathLike)):
592	            raise BuildFailure("mkdocs.yml `site_dir` must be a path.", 2)
593	        site_candidate = unresolved_under(config_file.parent, site_value)
594	    if site_candidate.is_symlink():
595	        raise BuildFailure(f"Refusing symlinked site directory: {site_candidate}", 2)
596	    site_dir = site_candidate.resolve(strict=False)
597	    assert_safe_tree(docs_dir, target, site_dir)
598	
599	    has_i18n, i18n_config = plugin_definition(config, "i18n")
600	    has_llmstxt, llmstxt_config = plugin_definition(config, "llmstxt")
601	    default_locale, locales = configured_locales(i18n_config if has_i18n else {})
602	    nondefault_locales = [locale for locale in locales if locale != default_locale]
603	    multilingual = has_i18n and bool(nondefault_locales)
604	    full_output = (
605	        safe_output_path(llmstxt_config.get("full_output"), "full_output")
606	        if has_llmstxt
607	        else None
608	    )
609	    site_url = config.get("site_url")
610	    if has_llmstxt and (not isinstance(site_url, str) or not site_url):
611	        raise BuildFailure("mkdocs.yml `site_url` is required when llmstxt is configured.", 2)
612	
613	    two_pass = multilingual and has_llmstxt
614	    mode = (
615	        "multilingual-two-pass"
616	        if two_pass
617	        else ("multilingual" if multilingual else "monolingual")
618	    )
619	    passes = 2 if two_pass else 1
620	    base_payload: dict[str, Any] = {
621	        "config_file": str(config_file),
622	        "default_locale": default_locale,
623	        "docs_dir": str(docs_dir),
624	        "locales": locales,
625	        "mode": mode,
626	        "passes": passes,
627	        "site_dir": str(site_dir),
628	        "target": str(target),
629	    }
630	    if args.dry_run:
631	        emit({**base_payload, "status": "dry-run"})
632	        return 0
633	
634	    site_dir.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
635	    temp_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=".mkdocs-site-bootstrap-", dir=site_dir.parent))
636	    result_payload = base_payload
637	    try:
638	        full_docs = temp_dir / "full-docs"
639	        copy_docs_tree(docs_dir, full_docs)
640	
641	        if two_pass:
642	            default_docs = temp_dir / "default-docs"
643	            default_site = temp_dir / "default-site"
644	            main_site = temp_dir / "main-site"
645	            copy_docs_tree(
646	                docs_dir,
647	                default_docs,
648	                nondefault_locales=nondefault_locales,
649	            )
650	            run_mkdocs(
651	                target=target,
652	                config_file=config_file,
653	                docs_dir=default_docs,
654	                site_dir=default_site,
655	                i18n=False,
656	                llmstxt=True,
657	                copy_to_llm=False,
658	                social=False,
659	                label="default-language llmstxt pass",
660	            )
661	            sidecars, _ = verify_llms_output(
662	                site_dir=default_site,
663	                config=config,
664	                docs_dir=default_docs,
665	                site_url=site_url,
666	                full_output=full_output,
667	                nondefault_locales=nondefault_locales,
668	            )
669	            copy_artifacts(
670	                default_site,
671	                full_docs,
672	                full_output=full_output,
673	                include_sidecars=False,
674	            )
675	            run_mkdocs(
676	                target=target,
677	                config_file=config_file,
678	                docs_dir=full_docs,
679	                site_dir=main_site,
680	                i18n=True,
681	                llmstxt=False,
682	                copy_to_llm=True,
683	                social=True,
684	                label="multilingual HTML pass",
685	            )
686	            verify_multilingual_html(main_site, nondefault_locales)
687	            copied = copy_artifacts(
688	                default_site,
689	                main_site,
690	                full_output=full_output,
691	                include_sidecars=True,
692	            )
693	            verify_llms_output(
694	                site_dir=main_site,
695	                config=config,
696	                docs_dir=default_docs,
697	                site_url=site_url,
698	                full_output=full_output,
699	                nondefault_locales=nondefault_locales,
700	            )
701	            if copied != len(sidecars):
702	                raise BuildFailure("Not all generated Markdown sidecars were merged.")
703	            staged_site = main_site
704	            sidecar_count = copied
705	        else:
706	            staged_site = temp_dir / "main-site"
707	            run_mkdocs(
708	                target=target,
709	                config_file=config_file,
710	                docs_dir=full_docs,
711	                site_dir=staged_site,
712	                i18n=has_i18n,
713	                llmstxt=has_llmstxt,
714	                copy_to_llm=True,
715	                social=True,
716	                label="strict site pass",
717	            )
718	            if multilingual:
719	                verify_multilingual_html(staged_site, nondefault_locales)
720	            if has_llmstxt:
721	                sidecars, _ = verify_llms_output(
722	                    site_dir=staged_site,
723	                    config=config,
724	                    docs_dir=full_docs,
725	                    site_url=site_url,
726	                    full_output=full_output,
727	                    nondefault_locales=nondefault_locales,
728	                )
729	                sidecar_count = len(sidecars)
730	            else:
731	                sidecar_count = 0
732	
733	        atomic_replace_tree(staged_site, site_dir)
734	        result_payload = {
735	            **base_payload,
736	            "artifacts": {
737	                "full_output": str(full_output) if full_output is not None else None,
738	                "llms": "llms.txt" if has_llmstxt else None,
739	                "markdown_sidecars": sidecar_count,
740	            },
741	            "status": "ok",
742	        }
743	        if args.keep_temp:
744	            result_payload["temp_dir"] = str(temp_dir)
745	        emit(result_payload)
746	        return 0
747	    finally:
748	        if args.keep_temp:

750	        else:
751	            shutil.rmtree(temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)

754	def main() -> int:

757	    except BuildFailure as error:

766	        log(f"error: unexpected build failure: {error}")
767	        emit({"error": str(error), "status": "error"})
768	        return 4

```text
1	# Worktrees
2	
3	Submodule workspaces initialize recursively at committed gitlinks by default.
4	Use `--submodules=none` to skip, or `start --submodule PATH` to select children
5	for task branches. `dev submodule status/init/develop/recover` inspects, prepares
6	and restores child checkouts. Explicit `--recursive` cleanup verifies initialized
7	child clones' remote recovery before removing them and the outer linked worktree;
8	canonical repositories and the outer branch are retained.
9	
10	A worktree is a second working directory for the same repository: its own
11	files, its own checked-out branch, sharing one history and one remote.
12	
13	## What they are actually for
14	
15	**Preventing two writers from editing the same files at once.** Not feature
16	management — that is what branches are for.
17	
18	So the question is never "how many agents am I running?" It is:
19	
20	> Could these two writers touch the same file?
21	
22	- Different files, one goal → one checkout is fine. Several agents, several
23	  panes, one branch.
24	- Different *approaches* to the same problem → one worktree each, so they can
25	  be compared and the loser discarded.
26	- Anything where the file ranges are unknown → worktrees.
27	
28	## Who owns which worktree
29	
30	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
31	|---|---|---|---|
32	| Feature, fix, experiment, handoff | `dev` | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until external retirement |
33	| Harness-owned turn-scoped isolation | Claude Code | `.claude/worktrees/` | owned by that harness; no transcript-relocation guarantee |
34	
35	**Might you review or return to the code/history/plan later → `dev`.**
36	
37	Never put a long-lived worktree inside the repository. Every file watcher,
38	language server, indexer and `rg` run in the outer repo then sees a second copy
39	of the whole tree.
40	
41	## Commands
42	
43	```bash
44	dev wt create feat/auth --base main   # create at the configured path
45	dev wt list                           # every worktree of this repo
46	dev wt open feat/auth                 # open an existing one
47	dev wt rm feat/auth                   # remove the checkout; branch survives
48	dev wt provision                      # re-run setup on an existing checkout
49	```
50	
51	## Always pass a base
52	
53	```bash
54	dev wt create fix/orderbook --base main
55	```
56	
57	Without `--base`, dev uses the repository's default branch. Passing it
58	explicitly is still preferred for scripts and agent-driven creation because
59	the intended committed starting point stays reviewable in the command.
60	
61	## Worktrees created directly in Herdr
62	
63	Herdr's **New worktree** action is allowed. Git registers that checkout with
64	the canonical repository, so dev can display it as an external worktree as
65	long as the canonical repo is discoverable through `paths.scan_roots` or
66	`paths.repo_paths`—even
67	when the checkout lives under `~/.herdr/worktrees` and that directory is not a
68	scan root.
69	
70	It remains deliberately unmanaged: dev does not silently create a task, move
71	the checkout, or run provisioning. If the work becomes durable, opt in:
72	
73	```bash
74	dev wt provision /path/to/worktree  # optional: env files + dependencies
75	dev adopt                           # report candidates; changes nothing
76	dev adopt --apply                   # record the selected candidates as tasks
77	```
78	
79	Until adoption, `dev park`, `dev resume`, and `dev done` have no task lifecycle
80	to operate on. Use `dev start` when that lifecycle is wanted from the outset.
81	
82	`dev flow [repo]` also shows every registered checkout. An eligible unmanaged
83	linked row offers plan-first **Adopt** (task metadata only; bytes stay untouched)
84	and **Remove Checkout** (clean, non-force, branch always preserved). Canonical,
85	harness, locked/prunable, task-claimed, or ambiguous rows have no destructive
86	path. Flow does not prune repository-wide stale registrations; inspect and repair
87	those explicitly.
88	
89	## A worktree starts empty of everything untracked
90	
91	No `node_modules`, no `.venv`, no `.env`. `dev` fixes this on create:
92	
93	- copies the gitignored files listed in `worktree.include`;
94	- symlinks anything in `worktree.link` (opt-in);
95	- runs `post_create`, detected from lockfiles when set to `"auto"`.
96	
97	Only files that are **both listed and gitignored** are copied. A tracked file
98	is already in the checkout on the correct branch — copying the other branch's
99	version over it would be wrong.
100	
101	## Removing one
102	
103	```bash
104	dev wt rm feat/auth
105	```
106	
107	Never deletes the branch. A dirty checkout needs an explicit `--force`, and
108	that refusal is the feature, not an obstacle.
109	
110	Gitlinks still need `--recursive`, even if never initialized. For linked-worktree
111	removal only, an absent or truly empty child path with no retained Git store may
112	be proved empty locally; no initialization, download, remote proof or push is
113	needed merely for removal. Retained/deinitialized data, orphan stores, local or
114	ignored files, unexpected `.git`, symlinks/reparse points, external claims and
115	incomplete observations block. Path-based task/artifact claims protect empty
116	children without inheriting parent Git identity; any non-discarded matching
117	artifact intent blocks, and discarded records still bind the reviewed authority.
118	
119	Physical emptiness alone is not removal permission. Manually deleting a tracked
120	gitlink directory makes the parent dirty, blocking ordinary non-force removal
121	before admin pruning. Cleanup never silently creates or restores placeholders to
122	bypass this guard. A never-initialized, Git-created empty directory can pass;
123	an absent child alone does not prove the parent safe to remove.
124	
125	Only exact reviewed empty modules admin scaffolding may be pruned under locks,
126	revalidating directory identity and emptiness immediately before native
127	directory-only removal. Empty checkout directories stay for normal non-force Git
128	removal. Real child stores retain full recovery proofs and journals/rollback;
129	partial pruning failure is not retirement success. Layout changes, new child
130	initialization or claims require a new plan. General removal guards and
131	initialization/publication policy are unchanged; no recursive file-deletion
132	workaround is used. See `dev help retirement` and `dev help ai-artifacts`.
133	
134	If a directory was deleted behind Git's back, the registration is a recovery
135	case. Inspect repository-wide `git worktree prune` scope before applying it;
136	`dev flow` reports the drift and does not prune implicitly.
137
```

1	---
2	description: Choose the owner and location of each worktree, then provision ignored files and dependencies safely.
3	authority: project
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-08-29
6	---
7	
8	# Worktrees and provisioning
9	
10	Submodule Git initialization precedes environment provisioning and defaults to recursive pinned checkouts. `--no-provision` does not disable it; use `--submodules=none`. Initialization failure retains the worktree without opening its runtime. See [Submodule workspaces](submodule-workspaces.md).
11	
12	A Git worktree begins as a clean checkout. `dev` owns durable change-stream worktrees and builds an inspectable plan for the ignored files and dependencies needed to make them usable.
13	
14	## Choose one lifecycle owner
15	
16	| Worktree kind | Owner | Typical location | Lifetime |
17	|---|---|---|---|
18	| feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | `dev` | configured `paths.worktree_path` | `dev done` records MERGED only; a later `dev retire`, explicit `dev wt rm`, or approved sweep removes it |
19	| harness-scoped isolation | Claude Code or another harness | harness-owned directory such as `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` | governed by that harness's retention and safe-cleanup rules; Flow never adopts or removes it |
20	| externally created linked worktree | external until adopted | tool-specific | visible to `dev`/`dev flow`; unmanaged until explicit adoption |
21	
22	Use `dev` when code, history, or plans must remain reviewable or a human may return later. Do not nest a long-lived `dev` worktree inside a repository; file watchers, language servers, backup tools, and searches in the outer checkout would see a second copy of the tree.
23	
24	`dev` creates the checkout with Git at its configured path. Herdr only opens that existing path, so worktree placement remains identical on machines without Herdr.
25	
26	`dev flow [repo]` uses Git's authoritative worktree records to show canonical,
27	managed, unmanaged, and strict `.claude/worktrees/` harness rows, plus task-only
28	rows that have no checkout. It never guesses ownership from a `worktree-*`
29	branch prefix; ambiguous path/task binding is labelled CONFLICT and stops
30	lifecycle mutation. See [Repository lifecycle flow](repository-flow.md).
31	
32	## Inspect before creating
33	
34	```bash
35	dev wt plan
36	dev wt plan --write          # seed repository-owned .dev-cli/config.toml
37	dev wt create feat/auth --base main
38	dev wt list
39	```
40	
41	`dev wt plan` reads lockfiles, tool availability, configured include/link rules, and Git ignore state without changing the checkout. The resulting plan shows every runnable or skipped step and any safety downgrade.
42	
43	## Carry ignored files by allowlist
44	
45	```toml
46	[worktree]
47	include = [".env", ".env.local", "config/local.json"]
48	link = []
49	post_create = "auto"
50	strategy = "reinstall"
51	```
52	
53	Only paths that are both listed and confirmed by Git as ignored are copied. A tracked file already arrives through the branch; copying a different checkout's version over it would violate branch isolation.
54	
55	Included files are copied as files, not logged. Current provisioning also rechecks the source and destination path shape while opening/copying so source swaps and symlinked destination parents are refused.
56	
57	Do not add `.claude/settings.local.json` globally. Include that exact file only for a deliberately chosen launcher whose behavior depends on it, and verify the copy in the plan.
58	
59	## Select dependency strategy by correctness
60	
61	| Strategy | Effect | Guidance |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| `reinstall` | run the lockfile-derived install command | safe default |
64	| `copy` | duplicate an installed dependency directory | use only where paths are portable |
65	| `link` | share one dependency directory | fastest and usually unsafe for concurrent writers |
66	| `skip` | leave dependencies absent | container- or CI-driven development |
67	
68	Per-ecosystem overrides live in the project or global config:
69	
70	```toml
71	[worktree.strategies]
72	node = "copy"
73	```
74	
75	New project-owned overrides belong in `.dev-cli/config.toml`; legacy
76	`.dev.toml` remains readable under its compatibility behavior. A `post_create`
77	command from `.dev-cli/config.toml` does not run until its exact
78	executable-config hash is approved with `dev config trust . --yes`. Changing
79	the command invalidates that approval.
80	
81	Important built-in decisions:
82	
83	- Python virtual environments cannot be copied or linked because they embed absolute paths; `uv sync` can reuse its global cache.
84	- Node `node_modules` may be copied, but sharing is refused because either checkout can mutate it.
85	- Go uses a global content-addressed module cache, so there is no checkout-local dependency tree to copy.
86	- Cargo `target/` may be copied, but sharing concurrent build output is refused.
87	
88	An invalid or unsound request narrows to `reinstall` with a warning instead of silently creating a broken environment.
89	
90	## Auto-detected setup
91	
92	`post_create = "auto"` recognizes one manager per ecosystem, in priority order:
93	
94	| Marker | Command |
95	|---|---|
96	| `uv.lock` | `uv sync` |
97	| `poetry.lock` | `poetry install` |
98	| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` |
99	| `package-lock.json` | `npm ci` |
100	| `yarn.lock` | `yarn install --immutable` |
101	| `go.mod` | `go mod download` |
102	| `Cargo.toml` | `cargo fetch` |
103	| `Gemfile.lock` | `bundle install` |
104	
105	A missing tool is reported and skipped. A failed setup command leaves the worktree in place so the branch and checkout can be repaired rather than discarded.
106	
107	## Reprovision or remove
108	
109	```bash
110	dev wt provision /path/to/worktree --dry-run
111	dev wt provision /path/to/worktree
112	dev wt rm feat/auth
113	```
114	
115	Removing a worktree and deleting a branch are separate decisions. `dev wt rm` preserves the branch and refuses a dirty checkout without explicit force. If the directory disappeared outside Git, it prunes the stale administrative entry.
116

123	- [Claude Code worktrees](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees)
124
```

8	
9	# Worktree 與環境佈建
10	
11	Submodule Git 初始化先於環境 provisioning，預設遞迴建立固定在 gitlink 的 checkout。`--no-provision` 不略過它，需使用 `--submodules=none`。初始化失敗保留 worktree，但不開 runtime。見 [Submodule 工作區](submodule-workspaces.md)。

16	Git worktree 一開始是乾淨 checkout。`dev` 擁有持久變更流 (change stream) 的 worktree，並建立可檢查的 provisioning plan，說明要加入哪些 ignored files 與 dependencies。
17	
18	## 只選一個 lifecycle owner
19	
20	| Worktree 類型 | Owner | 常見位置 | Lifetime |
21	|---|---|---|---|
22	| feature、fix、experiment、跨機器 handoff | `dev` | 設定的 `paths.worktree_path` | `dev done` 只記錄 MERGED；直到後續 `dev retire`、明確 `dev wt rm` 或核准的 sweep 才移除 |
23	| harness-scoped isolation | Claude Code 或其他 harness | harness-owned path，例如 `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` | 由該 harness 的 retention 與 safe-cleanup 規則管理；Flow 不會 Adopt/Remove |
24	| 外部建立的 linked worktree | adoption 前由外部管理 | tool-specific | `dev`/`dev flow` 可看見；只有明確 Adopt 後才有 managed lifecycle |
25	
26	Code、history 或 plans 需要保持可 review，或人之後可能回來時，使用 `dev`。不要把長期 `dev` worktree 巢狀放在 repository 內；外層 checkout 的 file watcher、language server、backup tool 與搜尋會看到第二份 tree。
27	
28	`dev` 使用 Git 在設定路徑建立 checkout；Herdr 只開啟現有 path，因此沒有 Herdr 的機器仍維持相同 placement policy。
29	
30	`dev flow [repo]` 以 Git 的 authoritative worktree records 顯示 canonical、managed、unmanaged 與 strict `.claude/worktrees/` harness rows，另加入沒有 checkout 的 task-only rows。它不以 `worktree-*` branch prefix 猜 ownership；path/task binding 有歧義時標示 CONFLICT 並停止 lifecycle mutation。詳見 [Repository Flow 預覽](repository-flow.zh-TW.md)。
31	
32	## 建立前先檢查
33	
34	```bash
35	dev wt plan
36	dev wt plan --write          # 建立 repository-owned .dev-cli/config.toml
37	dev wt create feat/auth --base main
38	dev wt list
39	```
40	
41	`dev wt plan` 會讀取 lockfile、tool availability、include/link 規則與 Git ignore state，但不修改 checkout。Plan 列出每個可執行或 skipped step，以及任何 safety downgrade。
42	
43	## 用 allowlist 攜帶 ignored files
44	
45	```toml
46	[worktree]
47	include = [".env", ".env.local", "config/local.json"]
48	link = []
49	post_create = "auto"
50	strategy = "reinstall"
51	```
52	
53	只有明確列出、且 Git 確認為 ignored 的 path 才會被複製。Tracked file 已透過 branch 進入 checkout；用另一個 checkout 的版本覆蓋它會破壞 branch isolation。
54	
55	Included files 以檔案方式複製，內容不寫入 log。現行 provisioning 在 open/copy 過程也會再次檢查 source 與 destination path shape，拒絕 source swap 與 symlinked destination parent。
56	
57	不要全域加入 `.claude/settings.local.json`。只有刻意選擇且確實依賴它的 launcher 才加入該精確 path，並在 plan 中驗證。
58	
59	## 依 correctness 選 dependency strategy
60	
61	| Strategy | 效果 | 建議 |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| `reinstall` | 執行 lockfile 推導出的 install command | 安全預設 |
64	| `copy` | 複製 installed dependency directory | 只用於 path 可攜的情況 |
65	| `link` | 共用同一個 dependency directory | 最快，但通常不適合 concurrent writers |
66	| `skip` | 不安裝 dependencies | container 或 CI-driven development |
67	
68	每個 ecosystem 的 override 可放在 project 或 global config：
69	
70	```toml
71	[worktree.strategies]
72	node = "copy"
73	```
74	
75	新的 project-owned overrides 應放在 `.dev-cli/config.toml`；legacy `.dev.toml`
76	仍以 compatibility behavior 讀取。來自 `.dev-cli/config.toml` 的 `post_create`
77	command 必須先用 `dev config trust . --yes` 核准其 exact executable-config hash
78	才會執行；command 變更後原核准立即失效。
79	
80	重要內建判斷：
81	
82	- Python virtual environment 內嵌 absolute path，不能 copy 或 link；`uv sync` 可重用 global cache。
83	- Node `node_modules` 可以 copy，但拒絕共享，因為任何 checkout 都可能修改它。
84	- Go 使用 global content-addressed module cache，沒有需要複製的 checkout-local dependency tree。
85	- Cargo `target/` 可以 copy，但拒絕讓 concurrent build 共用 output。
86	
87	無效或不安全的設定會附 warning 縮限到 `reinstall`，不會偷偷建立壞環境。
88	
89	## 自動偵測 setup
90	
91	`post_create = "auto"` 依 priority 為每個 ecosystem 選一個 manager：
92	
93	| Marker | Command |
94	|---|---|
95	| `uv.lock` | `uv sync` |
96	| `poetry.lock` | `poetry install` |
97	| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` |
98	| `package-lock.json` | `npm ci` |
99	| `yarn.lock` | `yarn install --immutable` |
100	| `go.mod` | `go mod download` |
101	| `Cargo.toml` | `cargo fetch` |
102	| `Gemfile.lock` | `bundle install` |
103	
104	缺少 tool 時會回報並 skip。Setup command 失敗時 worktree 仍保留，讓 branch 與 checkout 能被修復，而不是直接丟棄。
105	
106	## 重新 provision 或移除
107	
108	```bash
109	dev wt provision /path/to/worktree --dry-run
110	dev wt provision /path/to/worktree
111	dev wt rm feat/auth
112	```

114	移除 worktree 與刪除 branch 是兩個決定。`dev wt rm` 會保留 branch，且沒有 explicit force 時拒絕 dirty checkout。Directory 若在 Git 之外消失，它會 prune stale administrative entry。
115	
116	在 `dev flow` 中，UNMANAGED row 的 Remove Checkout 只對 exact、clean、unlocked、non-prunable、non-harness linked checkout 出現，並在移除前後 revalidate task claims、Git/agent/runtime/artifact facts；branch 與其 OID 必須保留。Flow 不提供 force/dirty-discard/unknown-runtime override。Managed DONE row 不是 Remove Checkout，而是最後才 reap task record 的 Retire plan；可選 branch deletion 是另一個 typed confirmation。Raw `git worktree remove --force` 會繞過這些 guarantees。

```text
1	---
2	description: Coordinate several coding agents around change-stream ownership, explicit mutation boundaries, and replaceable runtimes.
3	authority: project-policy
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-09-02
6	---
7	
8	# Parallel agents and runtimes
9	
10	A submodule task uses one complete outer worktree with independent child checkouts. Only explicitly selected children receive task branches; initialization failure prevents runtime/agent handoff. Child task, artifact and runtime claims participate in recursive retirement. See [Submodule workspaces](submodule-workspaces.md).
11	
12	> **Worktree per change stream. Pane per cooperating agent.**
13	
14	Do not create one worktree merely because another agent exists. Create one when another independent writer can mutate overlapping or unknown state.
15	
16	## Decide whether agents can share
17	
18	| Parallel work | Same checkout? | Condition |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| researcher plus implementer | yes | researcher is read-only |
21	| frontend plus backend | usually | ownership of shared schemas/manifests is explicit |
22	| tests plus implementation | usually | one integration owner resolves interface changes |
23	| two known disjoint directories | yes | no shared codegen/formatter output |
24	| both edit one manifest/API | risky | serialize or split streams |
25	| competing implementations | no | separate branch/worktree per approach |
26	| large refactors or unknown ranges | no | overlap cannot be bounded |
27	| any worker switches/reset/rebases `HEAD` | no | Git state mutation affects the checkout |
28	
29	Worktrees isolate files/index/HEAD. They do not isolate ports, databases, caches, hooks, credentials, queues, generated artifacts, or deployment targets; assign those resources separately.
30	
31	## Topology for one feature
32	
33	```text
34	one change stream / branch / dev worktree
35	                    │
36	             one runtime workspace
37	          ┌─────────┼─────────┐
38	        pane A     pane B     pane C
39	        agent      agent      tests/review
40	```
41	
42	This topology keeps one integration history and avoids merging execution artifacts. Give each writer a path/symbol contract and name the person or agent responsible for the final combined test.
43	
44	Inside a `dev` worktree, launch agents in the existing checkout. Do not automatically ask Claude Code to create another nested worktree; the outer worktree already provides the mutation boundary.
45	
46	## Topology for competing or independent work
47	
48	```bash
49	dev wt create exp/jwt --base main
50	dev wt create exp/session --base main
51	dev wt create exp/oauth --base main
52	```
53	
54	Each approach gets its own branch and worktree. Compare results, integrate one deliberately, and remove the others only after their useful commits or notes are recoverable.
55	
56	## Runtime selection
57	
58	`runtime.Select("auto")` chooses:
59	
60	1. **Herdr** when its binary and server are available. It can present linked worktrees as first-class grouped workspaces and report agent activity/session IDs.
61	2. **tmux** when installed. It opens a named session rooted at the checkout and stores display metadata in user options.
62	3. **Zellij** when a compatible installation is available. It opens or focuses a session rooted at the checkout.
63	4. **none** everywhere else. Core Git/task/worktree behavior remains available, while shell integration changes directories.
64	
65	A runtime opens and displays a checkout; `dev`, not Herdr or tmux, owns branch/worktree lifecycle. Closing a runtime never deletes the task or checkout.
66	
67	Zellij keeps exited sessions available for resurrection. `dev` recognizes only
68	the exact `(EXITED - attach to resurrect)` marker, omits those sessions from live
69	coverage, and refuses to create over their names. A live name merely containing
70	the word `EXITED` remains live. If a session exits between listing and layout
71	inspection, open fails closed and asks for a retry rather than resurrecting the
72	old layout at an unrelated checkout.
73	
74	For one reviewed shell command in a new independent worktree, Herdr supports a
75	direct one-liner:
76	
77	```bash
78	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main --run 'codex' --focus
79	```
80	
81	`--run` accepts only the exact root pane returned while creating a first-class
82	Herdr worktree. Reuse, fallback, missing pane identity, another runtime, and
83	direct/branch-only modes fail closed. The task and usable worktree remain if
84	dispatch fails. `--focus` independently switches after a successful dispatch;
85	dev does not wait for the command's exit status.
86	
87	`dev prompt open <recipe>` is a different contract: it starts one configured
88	foreground process in the terminal that invoked it and never creates, focuses,
89	reuses, or injects into a runtime pane. Inside Herdr it stays in the current
90	pane. To hold the conversation in a separate pane, create/focus that pane
91	manually, enter the exact checkout, and run `prompt open` there. It does not
92	weaken the fresh-worktree/exact-root-pane proof of `start --run`; see
93	[Prompt handoffs](prompt-handoffs.md).
94	
95	## Coordination contract
96	
97	Before launching parallel writers, record:
98	
99	- the shared goal and acceptance test;
100	- each worker's files/symbols and forbidden shared surfaces;
101	- dependencies and when blocked work may start;
102	- whether a worker may run Git operations that change `HEAD`;
103	- merge/integration order;
104	- the integration owner and full verification command;
105	- cleanup ownership for worktrees, runtimes, ports, containers, and temporary data.
106	
107	Use a read-only researcher or reviewer when independent context is useful but another writer would add merge cost.
108	
109	## Safe finish
110	
111	1. Stop new mutation and collect each worker's summary/tests.
112	2. Inspect every diff and preserve useful commits.
113	3. Integrate in dependency order.
114	4. Run formatting/codegen once under one owner.
115	5. Run the complete relevant suite in the integrated checkout.
116	6. Park or close runtime sessions.
117	7. Remove only clean, recoverable worktrees; keep branches until merge status is verified.
118	
119	For Claude-specific primitive selection, continue with the [parallel work decision guide](../claude/parallel-work-chooser.md).
120	
121	## Sources
122	
123	- [`internal/help/topics/agents.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/help/topics/agents.md)
124	- [`internal/runtime/runtime.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/runtime/runtime.go)
125	- [`internal/runtime/herdr.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/runtime/herdr.go)
126	- [`internal/cli/prompt_command.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/prompt_command.go)
127	- [Claude Code: run agents in parallel](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents)
128
```

1	---
2	description: 以變更流 ownership、明確 mutation boundary 與可替換 runtime 協調多個 coding agents。
3	authority: project-policy
4	status: stable
5	verified_on: 2026-09-02
6	lang: zh-TW
7	---
8	
9	# 平行 Agent 與 Runtime
10	
11	Submodule task 使用一個完整外層 worktree 與獨立子 checkout；只有明確選中的子 repo 建立 task branch。初始化失敗不進行 runtime／agent handoff，內層 task、artifact 與 runtime claim 都會影響遞迴回收。見 [Submodule 工作區](submodule-workspaces.md)。
12	
13	!!! note "術語規則"
14	    有公認中文譯名且本文使用中文時，首次以「中文 (English original)」呈現。產品名稱與 Git／CLI／agent domain terms 可直接保留英文；沒有公認譯名不得自創。程式碼、API／tool 名稱、CLI flag、套件名與路徑一律不翻譯。
15	
16	> **每條變更流 (change stream) 一個 worktree；每個協作 agent 一個 pane。**
17	
18	不要只因為多了一個 agent 就增加 worktree。只有另一位獨立 writer 可能修改重疊或未知 state 時，才需要新的 mutation boundary。
19	
20	## 判斷 agents 能否共用
21	
22	| 平行工作 | 同一 checkout？ | 條件 |
23	|---|---|---|
24	| researcher 加 implementer | 可以 | researcher 是 read-only |
25	| frontend 加 backend | 通常可以 | shared schema/manifest 的 owner 明確 |
26	| tests 加 implementation | 通常可以 | 一位 integration owner 處理 interface change |
27	| 兩個已知互斥 directories | 可以 | 沒有共用 codegen/formatter output |
28	| 都修改同一 manifest/API | 有風險 | serialize 或拆分 streams |
29	| 互斥實作方案 | 不行 | 每方案獨立 branch/worktree |
30	| 大型 refactor 或未知範圍 | 不行 | 無法限制 overlap |
31	| 任一 worker 會 switch/reset/rebase `HEAD` | 不行 | Git state mutation 會影響 checkout |
32	
33	Worktree 隔離 files/index/HEAD，不隔離 port、database、cache、hook、credential、queue、generated artifact 或 deployment target；這些資源要另外分配。
34	
35	## 同一 feature 的 topology
36	
37	```text
38	一條 change stream / branch / dev worktree
39	                    │
40	             一個 runtime workspace
41	          ┌─────────┼─────────┐
42	        pane A     pane B     pane C
43	        agent      agent      tests/review
44	```
45	
46	這個 topology 保留單一 integration history，也避免合併 execution artifacts。每位 writer 都要有 path/symbol contract，並指定最後負責 combined test 的人或 agent。
47	
48	在 `dev` worktree 內，直接於現有 checkout 啟動 agents。不要自動要求 Claude Code 再建立巢狀 worktree；外層已經提供 mutation boundary。
49	
50	## 互斥或獨立工作的 topology
51	
52	```bash
53	dev wt create exp/jwt --base main
54	dev wt create exp/session --base main
55	dev wt create exp/oauth --base main
56	```
57	
58	每個方案使用自己的 branch 與 worktree。比較結果後刻意整合一個；其餘 worktree 只有在有價值的 commits 或 notes 可復原後才移除。
59	
60	## Runtime 選擇
61	
62	`runtime.Select("auto")` 依序選擇：
63	
64	1. **Herdr：**binary 與 server 都可用時使用。它能把 linked worktree 呈現為 grouped workspace，並回報 agent activity/session ID。
65	2. **tmux：**已安裝時使用。它建立以 checkout 為 root 的 named session，並在 user option 保存 display metadata。
66	3. **Zellij：**有相容安裝時使用。它會開啟或 focus 以 checkout 為 root 的 session。
67	4. **none：**其他情況都可用。核心 Git/task/worktree 行為不受影響，shell integration 負責切換 directory。
68	
69	Runtime 只開啟與顯示 checkout；branch/worktree lifecycle 由 `dev` 管理，不由 Herdr 或 tmux 管理。關閉 runtime 不會刪除 task 或 checkout。
70	
71	Zellij 會保留可 resurrect 的 exited session。`dev` 只辨識 exact
72	`(EXITED - attach to resurrect)` marker，從 live coverage 省略這些 session，並拒絕用
73	同一 name 建立新 session；name 只是含有 `EXITED` 的 live session 仍視為 live。若 session
74	在 listing 與 layout inspection 之間退出，open 會 fail closed 並要求 retry，不會在無關
75	checkout resurrect 舊 layout。
76	
77	若要在新建的獨立 worktree 執行一個已 review 的 shell command，Herdr 支援直接
78	one-liner：
79	
80	```bash
81	dev start api --task "token refresh" --base main --run 'codex' --focus
82	```
83	
84	`--run` 只接受建立 first-class Herdr worktree 時回傳的 exact root pane。Reuse、
85	fallback、缺少 pane identity、其他 runtime，以及 direct/branch-only modes 都會
86	fail closed。Dispatch 失敗時 task 與可用 worktree 仍會保留。`--focus` 只在成功
87	dispatch 後獨立控制轉跳；dev 不等待 command exit status。
88	
89	`dev prompt open <recipe>` 是不同 contract：它在呼叫 terminal 中啟動一個 configured
90	foreground process，絕不建立、focus、reuse 或 inject runtime pane。在 Herdr 裡會留在
91	current pane。若要在 separate pane 對話，請手動建立/focus 該 pane、進入 exact
92	checkout，再從那裡執行 `prompt open`。它不會放寬 `start --run` 的
93	fresh-worktree/exact-root-pane proof；詳見
94	[Prompt handoff](prompt-handoffs.zh-TW.md)。
95	
96	## 協調 contract
97	
98	啟動 parallel writers 前先記錄：
99	
100	- shared goal 與 acceptance test；
101	- 每位 worker 的 files/symbols，以及不可碰的 shared surfaces；
102	- dependencies 與 blocked work 的開始條件；
103	- worker 是否能執行改變 `HEAD` 的 Git 操作；
104	- merge/integration order；
105	- integration owner 與完整 verification command；
106	- worktree、runtime、port、container 與 temporary data 的 cleanup owner。
107	
108	需要獨立 context，但增加 writer 只會增加 merge cost 時，使用 read-only researcher 或 reviewer。
109	
110	## 安全完成
111	
112	1. 停止新的 mutation，收集每位 worker 的 summary/tests。
113	2. 檢查每個 diff 並保留有價值的 commits。
114	3. 依 dependency order 整合。
115	4. 由一位 owner 執行一次 formatting/codegen。
116	5. 在 integrated checkout 跑完整相關 suite。
117	6. Park 或關閉 runtime sessions。
118	7. 只移除 clean 且可復原的 worktree；merge status 未確認前保留 branch。
119	
120	Claude-specific primitive 的選擇請接著看[平行工作決策指南](../claude/parallel-work-chooser.md)。
121	
122	## 來源
123

125	- [`internal/runtime/runtime.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/runtime/runtime.go)
126	- [`internal/runtime/herdr.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/runtime/herdr.go)
127	- [`internal/cli/prompt_command.go`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/blob/main/internal/cli/prompt_command.go)
128	- [Claude Code：平行執行 agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agents)
129
```

1296	`dev status` and the TUI detail pane also show the unique changed-path total
1297	and type breakdown (added / modified / deleted / renamed). A path staged and
1298	then modified again is one changed path, while correctly appearing in both the

1300	`dev status` also renders independent local `checkout`, `task`, and `worktree`

1303	
1304	## Worktree ownership
1305	
1306	Three mechanisms create git worktrees. `dev` takes one position so nobody has
1307	to improvise:
1308	
1309	| Kind | Owner | Where | Lifetime |
1310	|---|---|---|---|
1311	| Feature, fix, experiment, cross-machine handoff | **`dev`** | `~/Worktrees/<repo>/<slug>` | until external `dev retire` |
1312	| Harness-owned turn-scoped subagent isolation | **Claude Code** | `.claude/worktrees/` (gitignored) | owned by that harness; no history-relocation guarantee |
1313	| `herdr worktree create` | **not used** — `dev` runs `git worktree add`, then `herdr worktree open --path …` | — | — |
1314	
1315	**If code, history, or plans must remain reviewable—or you may return tomorrow—
1316	use `dev`.**
1317	
1318	Claude Workflow cleanup is an explicit, stricter exception to the normal
1319	harness-owned lifetime. From the canonical non-bare checkout, first review:
1320	
1321	```bash
1322	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --stale-days 14
1323	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --json        # schema version 1; report only
1324	```
1325	
1326	The V1 adapter reads only bounded fixed-depth structure under
1327	`~/.claude/projects`; it reports normalized IDs/states/times and never emits
1328	prompts, scripts, logs, result bodies, or transcript content. A candidate needs
1329	one exact provider mapping, a `completed` or `killed` workflow, matching `done`
1330	agent plus journal `started` and `result`, no same-ID resumed transcript, and
1331	provider inactivity older than the threshold. Killed/no-result, progress, or
1332	resumed evidence remains `unknown` with no attestation bypass.
1333	
1334	There is one additional non-replay requirement: provider metadata must bind the
1335	run to the live branch, HEAD, common-dir, and an opaque registration generation
1336	that cannot be reused with the path. Claude Code 2.1.259 records none of that Git
1337	identity. Its current claims therefore show `provider-git-identity: unknown` and
1338	remain report-only; even `--apply` will not prompt for or remove them. This is
1339	intentional—stale terminal metadata must not authorize deleting a later checkout
1340	that reused the same path. Do not infer identity from the path, branch naming, or
1341	GitDir pathname.
1342	
1343	Eligibility also requires a present registered unlocked non-prunable named
1344	linked worktree with matching common-dir/branch/HEAD, no staged, unstaged,
1345	conflicted, untracked, ignored, or recursive-submodule content, no Git operation,
1346	no task or unsafe artifact intent, a caller outside the target, and known empty
1347	runtime coverage. Missing, prunable, unregistered, and orphan paths are report
1348	only. Apply is interactive and confirms each item, then reacquires every proof
1349	under a common-dir cleanup lock and compares a stable fingerprint before plain
1350	non-force removal:
1351	
1352	```bash
1353	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply
1354	# Optional only when separately approved and proved safe:
1355	dev sweep --ephemeral-worktrees --apply --delete-branches --base main
1356	```
1357	
1358	A clean worktree may have commits unique to its branch because the branch is
1359	retained by default. Branch deletion separately requires unchanged branch/base
1360	tips, containment, zero unique commits, and `git branch -d`. This flow never
1361	prunes registrations, closes runtimes, deletes Claude metadata, or rescues,
1362	stashes, commits, or force-removes dirty work.
```

38	## [0.2.39] - 2026-09-17
39	
40	### Added
41	
42	- `dev hygiene report` summarizes the newest stored scan for the current
43	  checkout without scanning again (so the pre-commit hook's staged scan is
44	  readable right after a blocked commit), or `--report ID` / `--rescan`.
45	  Findings are grouped by severity, rule, file and category, ordered by
46	  disposition then occurrences, with `--top`, `--disposition`, `--rule`,
47	  `--category`, `--path` filters and a `--findings` drill-down. `--json` emits
48	  the new `hygiene_summary` schema-v1 document. `--values` shows masked
49	  distinct values per rule; raw values and their context go only to a private
50	  review file whose location `dev hygiene review-path <report-id>` prints.
51	  Scan findings gain additive keyed `value_id` and `file_id` fields, keeping
52	  private filenames distinct even when their displayed labels match. Stored
53	  summaries show the scan date without claiming current source freshness;
54	  legacy file counts are explicitly marked as lower bounds. Value capture is
55	  byte-bounded and skipped samples are visible; a failed values sidecar retains
56	  a partial scan receipt. Invalid path globs fail before scanning, and filter
57	  metadata is policy-masked.
58	- `dev retire --base <ref>` overrides the containment target used to prove a
59	  DONE task or linked worktree is integrated: a local branch, a remote-tracking
60	  branch such as `origin/main`, or a commit. `dev sweep --base` forwards the
61	  same override to DONE tasks, and `--merged-worktrees` proves managed tasks
62	  against the base it already verified. After `dev done --merged --base-ref`,
63	  cleanup hints and the cleanup wizard carry that ref forward.
64	
65	### Fixed
66	
67	- Artifact readiness no longer lets unrelated repositories' intent records
68	  block a detached checkout. Repository identity is filtered before branch
69	  identity is required for moved intents; relevant pending, ambiguous or
70	  unreadable records still block cleanup. Windows non-directory store errors
71	  are no longer mistaken for an absent store. Submodule artifact observation
72	  errors retain their specific cause instead of only reporting unfinished artifacts.
73	- Recursive worktree cleanup can locally prove never-initialized submodules
74	  empty without downloading or publishing children. Exact empty module
75	  administration is revalidated and pruned with directory-only operations before
76	  ordinary no-force Git removal. Retained child stores, orphan data, ignored
77	  files, links and ownership claims remain blockers. Mixed initialized/empty
78	  graphs retain recovery proofs and rollback for real child repositories, and
79	  interrupted empty-directory pruning reports partial effects. Native path
80	  spellings share bookkeeping keys on Windows without relaxing physical identity
81	  checks. `--recursive` remains required; alternates and squash-ancestry
82	  protections are unchanged.
83	- Guarded file replacements on macOS no longer fail with a metadata round-trip

92	  batch in one pass. A reviewed retirement or removal plan is bound only to the
93	  worktrees that share its branch or path, so removing an unrelated sibling
94	  earlier in the batch no longer turns every remaining plan stale. A new

100	  exist". Bases resolve as a local branch, then a remote-tracking branch, then a
101	  commit, and apply re-resolves the same input. A recorded fork-point commit is
102	  never replaced by the default branch: when it cannot prove integration, the
103	  plan stays blocked and names `--base <branch>`.
104	- An agent can now repair or redact another session's stopped SpecStory
105	  transcript from its own pane. The artifact writer guard previously blocked

107	  Other live agents still always block. The caller is exempt only when Herdr's

111	  An identified caller-owned live transcript is refused even with the override;

```text
1	# Parallel background agents
2	
3	Submodule workspaces retain a complete outer directory tree. Only selected children get task branches. Initialization must succeed before launching; child claims and recovery proofs also gate cleanup. See `submodules.md`.
4	
5	Read this when starting independent agent work while another agent remains live,
6	or when launching an agent into a worktree created by `dev start --json`.
7	
8	## Boundary and owners
9	
10	> **Worktree per change stream; one SpecStory root per worktree; exact pane per
11	> agent; exact transcript/plan finalization.**
12	
13	- `dev` owns the durable task, branch and checkout.
14	- Herdr owns workspace/pane layout and live process detection.
15	- Fleet navigation prepares workspaces without focus in an explicit remote
16	  session. Select the reported machine/workspace in Herdr's native sidebar;
17	  it never uses session-wide focus to navigate one client. See `runtime-herdr.md`.
18	- SpecStory owns rendered history rooted at the process launch checkout.
19	- Git owns the code, transcript and plan that survive cleanup.
20	
21	By default, `dev start` does not start an agent. An explicit
22	`dev start --run '<shell command>'` can dispatch to the exact root pane of a
23	newly created first-class Herdr worktree, with optional independent `--focus`.
24	It does not choose or validate the launcher profile, permission mode, agent
25	name, or wait policy. The JSON workflow below remains the composable path when
26	those steps need separate inspection or automation.
27	
28	## Preflight
29	
30	- [ ] `test "${HERDR_ENV:-}" = 1`
31	- [ ] `dev doctor`
32	- [ ] `command -v specstory`
33	- [ ] Explicit task name and committed base ref are known.
34	- [ ] New work does not depend on another checkout's uncommitted state.
35	- [ ] Launch profile and permission mode are explicit.
36	
37	If the new task needs dirty state, wait for the owning agent to make a checkpoint
38	commit and use that exact commit/ref as `--base`. Do not stash, reset, switch, or
39	copy another agent's checkout.
40	
41	## Create and validate the target
42	
43	Use Herdr's native repository/worktree tree as provenance. Worktree-mode
44	`dev start` passes the same `repo/branch` label as `dev wt create`; do not invent
45	special origin labels or metadata.
46	
47	For a human one-liner with an already reviewed command:
48	
49	```bash
50	dev start <repo> --task '<task>' --base '<committed-ref>' \
51	  --run '<launch-command>' --focus
52	```
53	
54	This fails closed before creation for non-Herdr/non-worktree combinations and,
55	after creation, refuses reuse, fallback, or missing exact root-pane data. A
56	dispatch failure leaves the recorded task and usable worktree in place.
57	
58	```bash
59	result="$(dev start <repo> --task '<task>' --base '<committed-ref>' --json)" || {
60	  # Side effects may exist even though no success JSON was emitted. Stop and
61	  # reconcile the reported task/worktree manually; do not retry blindly.
62	  exit 1
63	}
64	```
65	
66	Accept the result only when all of these are true:
67	
68	```text
69	mode == "worktree"
70	repo_path, worktree_path and checkout are absolute
71	checkout == worktree_path
72	runtime.name == "herdr"
73	runtime.surface == "worktree"
74	runtime.opened == true
75	runtime.created == true
```
</details></tool-use>

package cli

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/runtime"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/task"
)

// Retain the activityRuntime dispatch/annotation spies while recording the exact
// checkout and distinguishing worktree opening from generic runtime opening.
type wtOpenRuntime struct {
	*activityRuntime
	openPaths     []string
	worktreePaths []string
	beforeActive  func()
}

func (r *wtOpenRuntime) Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (runtime.OpenResult, error) {
	r.openPaths = append(r.openPaths, dir)
	return r.activityRuntime.Open(ctx, dir, label)
}

func (r *wtOpenRuntime) OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (runtime.OpenResult, error) {
	r.worktreePaths = append(r.worktreePaths, dir)
	return r.activityRuntime.OpenWorktree(ctx, dir, label)
}

func (r *wtOpenRuntime) Activate(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
	if r.beforeActive != nil {
		r.beforeActive()
	}
	return r.activityRuntime.Activate(ctx, handle)
}

type wtOpenFixture struct {
	t      *testing.T
	repo   *gittest.Repo
	path   string
	app    *App
	stdout bytes.Buffer
	stderr bytes.Buffer
}

func newWtOpenFixture(t *testing.T, rt runtime.Runtime) *wtOpenFixture {
	t.Helper()
	t.Setenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE", "")
	t.Setenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD", "")
	r := gittest.New(t)
	// This checkout was created externally, not by dev's worktree manager.
	path := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(r.Root), "external checkout")
	r.Git("worktree", "add", "-b", "feat/visible", path, "main")
	linked := &gittest.Repo{T: t, Root: path}
	linked.Write("README.md", "staged change\n")
	linked.Git("add", "README.md")
	linked.Write("README.md", "staged plus unstaged change\n")
	linked.Write("untracked.txt", "untracked bytes\n")
	r.Write("README.md", "canonical dirty bytes\n")

	cfg := config.Default()
	cfg.Paths.StateDir = t.TempDir()
	store := task.NewStore(cfg.TasksDir())
	if err := store.Save(&task.Task{
		Name: "existing task", Repo: "repo", RepoPath: r.Root, Branch: "main", Base: "main",
		Mode: task.ModeDirect, State: task.Warm, Next: "keep existing intent",
		RuntimeName: "herdr", RuntimeHandle: "w-existing",
	}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f := &wtOpenFixture{t: t, repo: r, path: path}
	f.app = &App{Cfg: cfg, Tasks: store, Out: &f.stdout, Err: &f.stderr, runtimeInstance: rt, colorMode: "never"}
	return f
}

func (f *wtOpenFixture) run(args ...string) error {
	f.t.Helper()
	cmd := newWtOpenCmd(f.app)
	cmd.SilenceErrors, cmd.SilenceUsage = true, true
	cmd.SetArgs(append([]string{"feat/visible", "--repo", f.repo.Root}, args...))
	return cmd.Execute()
}

// Compare bytes as well as Git observations: status alone would miss an index
// rewrite or a task metadata update that happened to preserve its meaning.
func (f *wtOpenFixture) snapshot() map[string]string {
	f.t.Helper()
	got := map[string]string{
		"refs":      f.repo.Git("show-ref"),
		"worktrees": f.repo.Git("worktree", "list", "--porcelain"),
	}
	for i, dir := range []string{f.repo.Root, f.path} {
		prefix := fmt.Sprintf("checkout-%d/", i)
		got[prefix+"HEAD"] = f.repo.GitIn(dir, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
		got[prefix+"branch"] = f.repo.GitIn(dir, "symbolic-ref", "HEAD")
		got[prefix+"status"] = f.repo.GitIn(dir, "--no-optional-locks", "status", "--porcelain=v1", "-z")
		index := f.repo.GitIn(dir, "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-path", "index")
		data, err := os.ReadFile(index)
		if err != nil {
			f.t.Fatal(err)
		}
		got[prefix+"index"] = string(data)
	}
	for i, root := range []string{f.repo.Root, f.path, f.app.Cfg.Paths.StateDir} {
		err := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, entry fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			if entry.IsDir() {
				if entry.Name() == ".git" {
					return filepath.SkipDir
				}
				return nil
			}
			data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			rel, err := filepath.Rel(root, path)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			got[fmt.Sprintf("files-%d/%s", i, rel)] = string(data)
			return nil
		})
		if err != nil {
			f.t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	return got
}

func (f *wtOpenFixture) assertUnchanged(before map[string]string) {
	f.t.Helper()
	if after := f.snapshot(); !reflect.DeepEqual(after, before) {
		f.t.Fatalf("opening changed checkout, refs, index, worktree registration or private task state\nbefore: %v\nafter: %v", before, after)
	}
}

func TestWtOpenDefaultActivates(t *testing.T) {
	for _, args := range [][]string{nil, {"--no-focus=false"}} {
		t.Run(fmt.Sprint(args), func(t *testing.T) {
			rt := &wtOpenRuntime{activityRuntime: &activityRuntime{openResult: runtime.OpenResult{
				Handle: "w-visible", Surface: "worktree", Opened: true, Created: true,
			}}}
			f := newWtOpenFixture(t, rt)
			wantOutput := fmt.Sprintf("feat/visible  %s  (herdr w-visible)\n", config.Contract(f.path))
			rt.beforeActive = func() {
				if got := f.stdout.String(); got != wantOutput {
					t.Fatalf("output before activation = %q, want %q", got, wantOutput)
				}
			}
			before := f.snapshot()
			if err := f.run(args...); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(rt.activateCalls, []string{"w-visible"}) {
				t.Fatalf("activation calls = %v", rt.activateCalls)
			}
			f.assertUnchanged(before)
		})
	}
}

func TestWtOpenNoFocus(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name    string
		result  runtime.OpenResult
		generic bool
		want    string
	}{
		{"created", runtime.OpenResult{Handle: "w-new", Surface: "worktree", Opened: true, Created: true, RootPaneID: "w-new:p1"}, false, "runtime opened (surface=\"worktree\")"},
		{"reused", runtime.OpenResult{Handle: "w-existing", Surface: "worktree", Opened: true}, false, "runtime reused (surface=\"worktree\")"},
		{"fallback", runtime.OpenResult{Handle: "w-fallback", Surface: "workspace", Opened: true, Created: true}, false, "runtime opened (surface=\"workspace\")"},
		{"generic-session", runtime.OpenResult{Handle: "session-visible", Surface: "session", Opened: true}, true, "runtime reused (surface=\"session\")"},
		{"not-opened", runtime.OpenResult{Handle: "hint-only"}, false, "runtime not opened (surface=\"\")"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			rt := &wtOpenRuntime{activityRuntime: &activityRuntime{openResult: tc.result}}
			var backend runtime.Runtime = rt
			if tc.generic {
				rt.name = "tmux"
				// Hide WorktreeOpener to exercise openCheckout's generic path.
				backend = struct{ runtime.Runtime }{rt}
			}
			f := newWtOpenFixture(t, backend)
			before := f.snapshot()
			if err := f.run("--no-focus"); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			paths, otherPaths := rt.worktreePaths, rt.openPaths
			if tc.generic {
				paths, otherPaths = rt.openPaths, rt.worktreePaths
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(paths, []string{f.path}) || len(otherPaths) != 0 || rt.openCalls != 1 ||
				!reflect.DeepEqual(rt.openLabels, []string{"repo/feat/visible"}) {
				t.Fatalf("open target: paths=%v other=%v calls=%d labels=%v", paths, otherPaths, rt.openCalls, rt.openLabels)
			}
			if len(rt.activateCalls) != 0 || len(rt.runCalls) != 0 || len(rt.annotations) != 0 ||
				len(rt.closeCalls) != 0 || len(rt.closePaneCalls) != 0 || rt.activityCalls != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("visibility-only open requested extra runtime effects: %+v", rt.activityRuntime)
			}
			want := fmt.Sprintf("feat/visible  %s  (%s %s)\n   %s; focus not requested\n",
				config.Contract(f.path), rt.Name(), tc.result.Handle, tc.want)
			if got := f.stdout.String(); got != want || f.stderr.Len() != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("stdout=%q stderr=%q, want %q", got, f.stderr.String(), want)
			}
			f.assertUnchanged(before)
		})
	}
}

func TestWtOpenNoFocusNone(t *testing.T) {
	for _, channel := range []string{"printable", "file", "descriptor", "dashboard"} {
		t.Run(channel, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := newWtOpenFixture(t, runtime.None{})
			file := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "shell-cd")
			const sentinel = "leave shell handoff untouched"
			if err := os.WriteFile(file, []byte(sentinel), 0o600); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			switch channel {
			case "file":
				t.Setenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FILE", file)
			case "descriptor":
				// Fails on every OS if cdDirective is reached; no native FD needed.
				t.Setenv("DEV_SHELL_CD_FD", "invalid")
			case "dashboard":
				f.app.workflowHandoff = func(func() error) error {
					t.Fatal("no-focus must not queue a shell handoff")
					return nil
				}
			}
			before := f.snapshot()
			if err := f.run("--no-focus"); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			want := fmt.Sprintf("feat/visible  %s\n   no runtime opened; no shell directory change requested\n", config.Contract(f.path))
			if got := f.stdout.String(); got != want {
				t.Fatalf("stdout = %q, want %q", got, want)
			}
			if data, err := os.ReadFile(file); err != nil || string(data) != sentinel {
				t.Fatalf("shell handoff modified: %q, %v", data, err)
			}
			f.assertUnchanged(before)
		})
	}
}

	}
	f.assertUnchanged(before)
}

func TestWtOpenNoFocusMissingWorktree(t *testing.T) {
	rt := &wtOpenRuntime{activityRuntime: &activityRuntime{}}
	f := newWtOpenFixture(t, rt)
	before := f.snapshot()
	cmd := newWtOpenCmd(f.app)
	cmd.SilenceErrors, cmd.SilenceUsage = true, true
	cmd.SetArgs([]string{"missing", "--repo", f.repo.Root, "--no-focus"})
	if err := cmd.Execute(); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), `no worktree for branch "missing"`) {
		t.Fatalf("missing worktree error = %v", err)
	}
	if rt.openCalls != 0 || f.stdout.Len() != 0 {
		t.Fatal("missing worktree opened runtime or reported success")
	}
	f.assertUnchanged(before)
}

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Build the real Git source archive, checking its packaging boundary.
3	
4	Run after committing the packaging change: python3 scripts/check-source-archive.py
5	The checkout, index, refs and attributes are never modified. Go caches may grow.
6	"""
7	
8	import argparse
9	import json
10	import os
11	from pathlib import Path
12	import subprocess
13	import tarfile
14	import tempfile
15	
16	
17	def main():
18	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
19	    parser.add_argument("--ref", default="HEAD")
20	    parser.add_argument("--version", default="archive-check")
21	    args = parser.parse_args()
22	    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
23	    oid = subprocess.check_output(
24	        ["git", "rev-parse", "--verify", "--end-of-options", args.ref + "^{commit}"],
25	        cwd=root, text=True,
26	    ).strip()
27	    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="dev-source-archive-") as temporary:
28	        directory = Path(temporary)
29	        archive = directory / "source.tar.gz"
30	        with archive.open("wb") as output:
31	            subprocess.run(
32	                ["git", "archive", "--format=tar.gz", oid], cwd=root,
33	                stdout=output, check=True,
34	            )
35	        source = directory / "source"
36	        source.mkdir()
37	        with tarfile.open(archive) as bundle:
38	            members = bundle.getmembers()
39	            names = {member.name for member in members}
40	            if any(name == ".specstory" or name.startswith(".specstory/") for name in names):
41	                raise SystemExit("source archive contains SpecStory data")
42	            required = {"go.mod", "go.sum", "cmd/dev/main.go", "internal/skill/dev-cli/SKILL.md"}
43	            if not required <= names:
44	                raise SystemExit("source archive is missing required build inputs")
45	            bundle.extractall(source, filter="data")
46	        binary = directory / ("dev.exe" if os.name == "nt" else "dev")
47	        subprocess.run([
48	            "go", "build", "-ldflags",
49	            "-X github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/cli.Version=" + args.version,
50	            "-o", str(binary), "./cmd/dev",
51	        ], cwd=source, check=True)
52	        version = subprocess.check_output([str(binary), "--version"], text=True).strip()
53	        if version != "dev version " + args.version:
54	            raise SystemExit("archive binary version mismatch")
55	        print(json.dumps({"commit": oid, "archive_bytes": archive.stat().st_size,
56	                          "files": sum(member.isfile() for member in members),
57	                          "specstory_excluded": True, "build": "passed"}))
58	
59	
60	if __name__ == "__main__":
61	    main()
62

8	# that real parsers reject. This script closes that gap.

13	#                                                ^ YAML reads a nested mapping

21	#   2. Frontmatter parses as YAML (yq / PyYAML / js-yaml, whichever is found)
22	#   3. Root is a mapping; `name` and `description` present as plain strings
23	#   4. (warn) unquoted plain scalar containing " #" — YAML treats the rest of
24	#      the line as a comment and silently truncates the value

27	# on PATH it degrades to the pattern heuristic and says so.

29	set -uo pipefail

31	usage() {
32	  cat <<'EOF'
33	Usage: lint-frontmatter.sh [OPTIONS] [PATH...]
34	
35	Validate the YAML frontmatter of every SKILL.md under PATH (default: ".").
36	PATH may be a SKILL.md file or a directory to search recursively.
37	
38	Options:
39	  --parser NAME      Force a parser: auto (default), yq, python3 (PyYAML),
40	                     node (the js "yaml" package — what `npx skills` uses).
41	  --quiet            Only print failures and the summary line.
42	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
43	
44	Examples:
45	  bash lint-frontmatter.sh                    # lint every SKILL.md under cwd
46	  bash lint-frontmatter.sh skills             # lint a collection directory
47	  bash lint-frontmatter.sh skills/local/my-skill/SKILL.md
48	
49	Exit codes:
50	  0  every SKILL.md parses and has string name + description
51	  1  at least one file failed
52	  2  invalid arguments / path not found / forced parser unavailable
53	EOF
54	}

56	QUIET=0
57	FORCED_PARSER="auto"
58	PATHS=()

63	               FORCED_PARSER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
64	    --parser=*) FORCED_PARSER="${1#--parser=}"; shift ;;
65	    --quiet)   QUIET=1; shift ;;
66	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
67	    -*)        printf 'error: unknown flag: %s (try --help)\n' "$1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
68	    *)         PATHS+=("$1"); shift ;;

104	    {

111	      print out s

115	probe_yq() {
116	  local tmp="$1" err root name desc
117	  if ! err=$(yq e '.' "$tmp" 2>&1 >/dev/null); then

124	  printf 'OK|%s|%s|%s\n' \

126	}
127	
128	normalize_tag() {
129	  case "$1" in
130	    '!!map') printf 'map' ;;
131	    '!!str') printf 'str' ;;
132	    '!!null'|'') printf 'null' ;;
133	    *) printf 'other' ;;
134	  esac
135	}
136	
137	probe_python3() {
138	  python3 - "$1" <<'PY'
139	import sys, yaml
140	def t(v):
141	    if v is None: return "null"
142	    if isinstance(v, str): return "str"
143	    if isinstance(v, dict): return "map"
144	    return "other"
145	try:
146	    with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as fh:
147	        doc = yaml.safe_load(fh)
148	except Exception as exc:
149	    print("FAIL|" + str(exc).replace("\n", " ")[:200])
150	    sys.exit(0)
151	if isinstance(doc, dict):
152	    print("OK|map|%s|%s" % (t(doc.get("name")), t(doc.get("description"))))
153	else:
154	    print("OK|%s|null|null" % t(doc))
155	PY
156	}
157	
158	probe_node() {
159	  node -e '
160	    const YAML = require("yaml"), fs = require("fs");
161	    const t = v => v === null || v === undefined ? "null"
162	      : typeof v === "string" ? "str"
163	      : (typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v)) ? "map" : "other";
164	    let doc;
165	    try { doc = YAML.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8")); }
166	    catch (e) { console.log("FAIL|" + String(e.message).split("\n")[0].slice(0, 200)); process.exit(0); }
167	    if (t(doc) === "map") console.log(`OK|map|${t(doc.name)}|${t(doc.description)}`);
168	    else console.log(`OK|${t(doc)}|null|null`);
169	  ' "$1"
170	}
171	
172	probe() {
173	  local raw
174	  case "$PARSER" in
175	    yq)      raw=$(probe_yq "$1") ;;
176	    python3) raw=$(probe_python3 "$1") ;;
177	    node)    raw=$(probe_node "$1") ;;
178	    *)       raw='SKIP|no YAML parser on PATH' ;;

189	risky_scalars() {

193	      val = $0; sub(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:[ \t]*/, "", val)

195	      first = substr(val, 1, 1)
196	      # Quoted or block scalars are already safe.
197	      if (first == "\"" || first == "'\''" || first == ">" || first == "|" \
198	          || first == "[" || first == "{") next
199	      if (val ~ /: / || val ~ /:$/)
200	        printf "  line %d: %s value contains \": \" — YAML reads it as a nested mapping; wrap the value in single quotes\n", NR + 1, key
201	      else if (val ~ / #/)

203	      else if (index("-?,[]{}#&*!|>%@`", first) > 0)
204	        printf "  line %d: %s value starts with the reserved YAML character %s — wrap the value in single quotes\n", NR + 1, key, first
205	    }
206	  ' "$1"
