# Skill Author

Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
once a draft exists).

## When to use this vs `skill-creator`

| Task | Use |
|---|---|
| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |

If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.

## Workflow

### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)

Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:

1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)

Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.

### 2. Scaffold

Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
```

Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):

| Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
|---|---|---|
| **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
| **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
| **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |

The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.

> **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
> but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
> available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this
> project (`--project`)?" before running the script. The script is
> non-interactive — once you've picked a scope, files land and symlinks fan
> out without further prompting.

After running, the script emits a single JSON object on stdout with
`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}` so you can chain
follow-up actions deterministically.

### 3. Author the SKILL.md

Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
that matter most:

- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
  this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
  501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
  loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
  escape hatches.

Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
happens"), not just that it exists.

### 4. Design any scripts

Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
requirements:

- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations

For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
have to set up an environment first.

### 5. Lint

Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
```

It checks three things:

1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; name is
   hyphen-case and <=64 chars; description has a "use when" trigger phrase,
   respects the 1024-char hard limit, and SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
   script).
3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).

Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.

### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator

Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
skill runs test cases and benchmarks."

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold the canonical skill dir
  (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/) and add discovery symlinks for
  non-universal agents. Auto-detects scope (LOCAL / PROJECT / GLOBAL); see
  table in step 2.
  - Scope flags (mutually exclusive): `--local` (force this repo's
    `skills/local/`), `--project` (force `<repo>/.agents/skills/`),
    `--global` (force `~/.agents/skills/`).
  - Other flags: `--vendor` (LOCAL only — `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead of
    `skills/local/`; rare, vendored skills normally come via `vendor.yaml`);
    `--root DIR` (override walk-up); `--no-symlinks` (skip the fan-out);
    `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite existing canonical dir + replace
    symlinks).
- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).
- **`scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh [PATH...]`** — YAML-parse the frontmatter of
  every `SKILL.md` under PATH (default `.`) with a real parser, and check that
  the root is a mapping with string `name` + `description`. Catches the
  breakage class `lint-skill.sh`'s awk extractor cannot see — an unquoted
  `description:` containing `": "` makes `npx skills` (and Claude Code /
  Cursor) **silently skip the skill**. `lint-skill.sh` calls this for the
  single-skill case; run it directly to sweep a whole collection.
  - Flags: `--parser auto|yq|python3|node` (`node` = the js `yaml` package,
    exactly what `npx skills` uses); `--quiet`.

## Bundled assets

Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:

- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.

## Reference files

- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.

## Gotchas

- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
  symlink with a real file.
- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
- **`description` is always-on context and has agent-specific hard limits.**
  Put concrete trigger phrases in frontmatter, but keep local skills in the
  120-500 char preferred range when possible. Treat >1024 chars as invalid:
  Codex and Cursor/spec-aligned validators can skip the skill entirely.
- **Quote any `description` containing `:`, `#`, or leading punctuation.** An
  unquoted YAML plain scalar cannot contain `": "` — `npx skills` fails with
  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings" and drops the skill
  from the picker without a non-zero exit. ` #` is worse: it parses, but YAML
  treats the rest as a comment and silently truncates your trigger string.
  Single quotes need no escaping except `'` itself. Run
  `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` to catch both; see
  `pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md` in this repo.
- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
  investing in authoring.
- **Scope auto-detect can surprise you.** `new-skill.sh` walks up looking for
  a publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
  `skills/.claude-plugin/`) *first*, then a `.git`. If you ran it from inside
  a clone of this repo while meaning to add a skill to your *other* project,
  it'll silently land in `skills/local/`. Pass `--project` or `--global`
  explicitly when intent isn't obvious, and prefer asking the user
  system-wide-vs-project-wide before running.
- **Discovery symlinks must be `../../`-relative**, not repo-root-relative —
  POSIX resolves symlink targets relative to the link's own directory. The
  script enforces this and verifies each link with `test -e <link>/SKILL.md`;
  if you ever hand-create one, see
  [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md).

## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)

Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
quantitative validation.

21	## Spending context wisely
22	
23	Every token in `SKILL.md` competes with the conversation history, the system
24	prompt, and every other active skill. Spend tokens on what the agent **wouldn't
25	know without you**:
26	
27	- Project-specific conventions (table names, repo layout, internal jargon)
28	- Domain-specific procedures with non-obvious steps
29	- Edge cases the agent will misjudge by default
30	- Specific tools/APIs to prefer (with the *why*, briefly)
31	
32	Don't spend tokens on:
33	
34	- Explaining what well-known things are (PDF, HTTP, REST, JSON)
35	- Generic "best practices" the agent already applies (handle errors, write tests)
36	- Comprehensive option enumerations — give a default and one escape hatch
37	
38	**Test:** for each paragraph, ask "would the agent get this wrong without it?"
39	If no, cut it.
40	
41	### Progressive disclosure
42	
43	Three loading levels:
44	
45	| Level | Loaded | Budget |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| Frontmatter (`name`, `description`) | always | 120-500 chars preferred, 1024 max |
48	| `SKILL.md` body | when skill triggers | <500 lines, <5000 tokens |
49	| `references/*.md`, `assets/*`, `scripts/*` | on demand | unlimited |
50	
51	If `SKILL.md` is creeping past 500 lines, move sections to `references/<topic>.md`
52	and reference them with **load conditions** ("Read X if Y happens"), not just
53	"see X for details". Conditions let the agent load on demand; bare pointers tend
54	to either get ignored or get pre-loaded out of caution.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility
59	
60	Use this as the portable baseline for coding agents that consume Agent Skills:
61	
62	- `name`: required, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens only, no leading/trailing
63	  hyphen, no `--`, <=64 characters.
64	- `description`: required, non-empty string, <=1024 characters. Include both
65	  what the skill does and concrete trigger contexts. Keep the first 60
66	  characters meaningful because `npx skills` truncates picker hints there.
67	- **Quoting**: a YAML plain (unquoted) scalar may not contain `": "`, and ` #`
68	  starts a comment. Long English descriptions hit both constantly
69	  (`"…debug a FastAPI app: choosing def vs async def"`). Wrap such values in
70	  single quotes — the whole skill is otherwise skipped at install time with
71	  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings", or installs with a
72	  silently truncated description. `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` gates this.
73	- Keep `name` and `description` as the only required frontmatter fields for
74	  portability. Agent-specific fields are allowed when needed, but isolate them
75	  intentionally: Cursor uses `disable-model-invocation`, Codex can read
76	  `agents/openai.yaml`, and some vendored skills carry upstream-only metadata.
77	
78	Description budget tiers:
79	
80	| Tier | Length | Meaning |
81	|---|---:|---|
82	| Green | 120-500 chars | Preferred for local skills: enough trigger surface without context bloat |
83	| Yellow | 501-900 chars | Valid, but context-heavy; move details to `SKILL.md` body |
84	| Orange | 901-1024 chars | Valid, but close to hard loader limits |
85	| Red | >1024 chars | Invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned validators |
86	
87	Agent notes:
88	
89	- **Codex** skips invalid `SKILL.md` files; OpenAI's validator enforces the
90	  64-char name and 1024-char description limits.
91	- **Cursor** managed `create-skill` guidance matches the same 64/1024 limits
92	  and supports `disable-model-invocation` for explicit-only skills.
93	- **Claude Code** uses descriptions for discovery and tolerates additional
94	  frontmatter in practice, but long descriptions still consume always-on
95	  context and are poor picker hints.
96	- **OpenCode** follows the Agent Skills convention and uses descriptions for
97	  invocation; stay within the portable baseline unless a target agent's docs
98	  say otherwise.
99	- **Claude.ai upload** may impose stricter UI limits. Treat that as a separate
100	  packaging target, not the default coding-agent baseline for this repo.
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Calibrating control
105	
106	Match instruction specificity to **task fragility**, not to "we should be thorough".
107	
108	### Be prescriptive when:
109	
110	- The operation is destructive or has side effects
111	- A specific sequence of steps must hold (migration, release, deploy)
112	- An external system requires exact format (API contract, parser input)
113	
114	```markdown
115	## Database migration
116	
117	Run exactly this sequence:
118	
119	    python scripts/migrate.py --verify --backup
120	
121	Do not modify the command or add flags. The `--verify` step seeds an
122	integrity check that later phases depend on.
123	```
124	
125	The trailing sentence is the trick — even when prescriptive, **explain why**.
126	Agents that understand the reason follow it more reliably than agents that just
127	see "DO NOT" in caps.
128	
129	### Give the agent freedom when:
130	
131	- Multiple valid approaches exist
132	- The output is judgment-driven (code review, refactor proposal)
133	- You'd be hand-coding policy if you wrote it all out
134	
135	```markdown
136	## Code review process
137	
138	1. Check database queries for SQL injection (use parameterized queries)
139	2. Verify auth checks on every endpoint
140	3. Look for race conditions in concurrent code paths

122	- Source-aware SSH setup can use `--auth existing` without installing a key, and registers only explicitly selected `--to fleet|herdr|both` destinations. Tailscale SSH advertisement is advisory; its port-22 endpoint is not an authorized_keys bootstrap target. Preserve the key-authentication guard and never treat Tailscale policy login as proof that a selected public key worked. Names, ports and cached observations never authorize machine merges; binding/source changes invalidate reviewed plans.
123	- Fleet-source SSH discovery selects explicit hosts without recursive fleet traversal. Local ProxyJump imports never copy remote identity/agent/trust paths; cached route data cannot authorize apply. `connect --on` is one interactive fixed-helper session with no agent forwarding or arbitrary command payload. Normal SSH errors retain child exit status.
124	- Controller password brokerage uses a private per-operation Unix socket or protected Windows pipe, never password argv/environment/files. Exact host/user/port/route contexts gate replies and save evidence. Remote source-to-target credentials remain outside this feature; native key/passphrase interaction is separate.
125	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
126	
127	## Versioning and changelog
128	
129	The current published baseline is `v0.2.39` (2026-09-17). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
130	
131	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
132	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
133	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
134	
135	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
136	
137	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
138	
139	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
140	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
141	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
142	
143	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.

125	The manifest for each release is also attached to the GitHub release as

127	
128	### Go or source
129	
130	```bash
131	go install github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/cmd/dev@latest
132	# Pin @v0.2.39 instead when you need a reproducible install.
133	# Or from a checkout: make install  # also installs the bundled agent skill
134	```
135	
136	Source checkouts include `mise.toml`, pinning the repository toolchain to Go
137	1.26.4. With mise installed, `mise install` selects the same compiler used by
138	the module and CI instead of relying on a possibly mismatched global GOROOT.
139	
140	Every release also publishes `darwin/arm64`, `darwin/amd64`, `linux/amd64`,
141	`linux/arm64` (`.tar.gz`) and `windows/amd64`, `windows/arm64` (`.zip`) archives
142	with a `SHA256SUMS` file, so a binary can be verified without a Go toolchain.
143	
144	To find out whether the binary you have is current, and to update it:
145	
146	```bash
147	dev version           # what this build is, and whether it is a published release
148	dev version --check    # also ask GitHub for the newest release (cached for a day)
149	dev doctor            # reports the running version, install owner/path, and PATH collisions
150	dev upgrade --check    # report whether a newer release exists
151	dev upgrade            # delegate to its owner, or verify and replace a standalone binary
152	```
153	
154	For a standalone install, `dev upgrade` checks the release's actual asset list.
155	If this platform has an archive, it downloads and verifies `SHA256SUMS`. If the
156	platform is absent (including Android/Termux today), it offers to build the exact
157	release tag with native Go. New releases include a compact
158	`dev-cli_<tag>_source.tar.gz`, verified against `SHA256SUMS` and excluding
159	conversation history. Older releases without this asset use Go's configured
160	module verification and may download a much larger archive. Both paths use
161	two build workers and the installed toolchain; they may take several minutes
162	on the first run. The candidate must build and report the expected version before
163	replacing the old executable. Download or checksum failures stop the upgrade.
164	
165	On Termux, prepare the native tools with `pkg install golang clang git`.
166	Android builds use `GOOS=android`, CGO and Clang; Linux archives are not Android
167	substitutes. Go must satisfy that release's `go.mod`; automatic toolchain downloads
168	are disabled for source upgrades. To recover an older `dev` whose upgrade command
169	only attempts the missing Android archive, build the published version separately:
170	
171	```bash
172	pkg update && pkg upgrade -y && pkg install golang clang git curl
173	stage="$(mktemp -d "$HOME/.local/bin/.dev-build.XXXXXX")" && (
174	  trap 'rm -rf "$stage"' EXIT
175	  set -e
176	  version=v0.2.39
177	  asset="dev-cli_${version}_source.tar.gz"
178	  base="https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/releases/download/$version"
179	  cd "$stage"
180	  curl -fL "$base/$asset" -o "$asset"
181	  curl -fL "$base/SHA256SUMS" -o SHA256SUMS
182	  awk -v asset="$asset" '$2 == asset { print }' SHA256SUMS > source.sha256
183	  test -s source.sha256
184	  sha256sum -c source.sha256
185	  mkdir source
186	  tar -xzf "$asset" -C source

+## Visibility without navigation
+
+Use `dev start <repo> --task '<task>' --base '<committed-ref>'` for new managed
+work. For an existing external registered checkout, use
+`dev wt open <branch> --repo <repo> --runtime herdr --no-focus` when only runtime
+visibility is needed. It reports branch, actual path, backend/handle and the
+actual opened/reused runtime surface immediately without focusing or attaching.
+It does not adopt/annotate a task, provision, launch an agent, or modify Git/index/
+dirty files. A reused or fallback surface is not a new exact agent launch target.
+Runtime `none` reports no runtime and emits no shell `cd` handoff. Without the
+flag, normal navigation is unchanged; opening failures remain errors. Report the
+repository, branch, actual path and runtime handle/result when handing work back.
+See [Worktrees and provisioning](worktrees-provisioning.md).
+
 For one reviewed shell command in a new independent worktree, Herdr supports a
 direct one-liner:

+++ b/docs/guides/worktrees-provisioning.md
@@ -29,6 +29,33 @@ rows that have no checkout. It never guesses ownership from a `worktree-*`
 branch prefix; ambiguous path/task binding is labelled CONFLICT and stops
 lifecycle mutation. See [Repository lifecycle flow](repository-flow.md).
 
+## New managed work versus existing checkout visibility
+
+Prefer `dev start` with an explicit committed base for new managed work:
+
+```bash
+dev start api --task "auth fix" --branch fix/auth --base main
+```
+
+For an existing registered external worktree that only needs runtime visibility:
+
+```bash
+dev wt open fix/auth --repo api --runtime herdr --no-focus
+```
+
+The open command reports branch, actual path and backend/handle immediately, then
+the actual runtime opened/reused surface. It does not switch focus or attach,
+create another Git worktree, adopt a task, provision, launch an agent, or change
+Git refs, the index or dirty files. A fallback workspace is reported as a workspace,
+not a new Git checkout or an agent launch target. With runtime `none`, it opens no
+runtime and emits no shell `cd` handoff. Without the flag, activation/shell
+navigation is unchanged; runtime errors still fail the command.
+
+Report repository, branch, actual checkout path and runtime handle/result when
+handing work back. Adoption is separate task intent, not a visibility switch;
+harness-owned temporary isolation remains distinct from durable implementation
+work. See [Parallel agents and runtimes](parallel-agents-runtimes.md).
+

+dev wt open <branch> --repo <repo> --runtime herdr --no-focus
+```
+
+This opens or reuses the exact checkout without switching/attaching, launching an
+agent, provisioning, or adopting a task. Dirty files and the index stay untouched.
+It reports branch, actual path and backend/handle immediately, followed by the
+observed runtime opened/reused surface; this is not Git worktree creation. With
+runtime `none`, no runtime opens and no shell `cd` handoff is emitted. Without
+`--no-focus`, normal activation or shell navigation is unchanged. Runtime errors
+remain errors; do not turn a failed open into a success report.
+
+When handing work back, report the repository, branch, actual checkout path and
+runtime handle/result immediately. Adoption is a separate lifecycle decision,
+not a visibility switch. See `runtime-herdr.md` for reuse/fallback boundaries.
+
 ## Why dev creates the checkout
 
 `dev` runs `git worktree add`, then asks Herdr to run

431					Symlink: real != abs, CommonDir: g.GitCommonDir, HasGit: true, Bare: g.Bare,
432				}, nil, nil

Base directory for this skill: /Users/zhouhanru/Documents/David/Program/dev-cli/.claude/skills/skill-author

# Skill Author

Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
once a draft exists).

## When to use this vs `skill-creator`

| Task | Use |
|---|---|
| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |

If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.

## Workflow

### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)

Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:

1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)

Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.

### 2. Scaffold

Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
```

Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):

| Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
|---|---|---|
| **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
| **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
| **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |

The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.

> **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
> but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
> available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this
> project (`--project`)?" before running the script. The script is
> non-interactive — once you've picked a scope, files land and symlinks fan
> out without further prompting.

After running, the script emits a single JSON object on stdout with
`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}` so you can chain
follow-up actions deterministically.

### 3. Author the SKILL.md

Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
that matter most:

- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
  this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
  501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
  loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
  escape hatches.

Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
happens"), not just that it exists.

### 4. Design any scripts

Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
requirements:

- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations

For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
have to set up an environment first.

### 5. Lint

Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
```

It checks three things:

1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; name is
   hyphen-case and <=64 chars; description has a "use when" trigger phrase,
   respects the 1024-char hard limit, and SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
   script).
3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).

Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.

### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator

Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
skill runs test cases and benchmarks."

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold the canonical skill dir
  (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/) and add discovery symlinks for
  non-universal agents. Auto-detects scope (LOCAL / PROJECT / GLOBAL); see
  table in step 2.
  - Scope flags (mutually exclusive): `--local` (force this repo's
    `skills/local/`), `--project` (force `<repo>/.agents/skills/`),
    `--global` (force `~/.agents/skills/`).
  - Other flags: `--vendor` (LOCAL only — `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead of
    `skills/local/`; rare, vendored skills normally come via `vendor.yaml`);
    `--root DIR` (override walk-up); `--no-symlinks` (skip the fan-out);
    `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite existing canonical dir + replace
    symlinks).
- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).
- **`scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh [PATH...]`** — YAML-parse the frontmatter of
  every `SKILL.md` under PATH (default `.`) with a real parser, and check that
  the root is a mapping with string `name` + `description`. Catches the
  breakage class `lint-skill.sh`'s awk extractor cannot see — an unquoted
  `description:` containing `": "` makes `npx skills` (and Claude Code /
  Cursor) **silently skip the skill**. `lint-skill.sh` calls this for the
  single-skill case; run it directly to sweep a whole collection.
  - Flags: `--parser auto|yq|python3|node` (`node` = the js `yaml` package,
    exactly what `npx skills` uses); `--quiet`.

## Bundled assets

Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:

- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.

## Reference files

- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.

## Gotchas

- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
  symlink with a real file.
- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
- **`description` is always-on context and has agent-specific hard limits.**
  Put concrete trigger phrases in frontmatter, but keep local skills in the
  120-500 char preferred range when possible. Treat >1024 chars as invalid:
  Codex and Cursor/spec-aligned validators can skip the skill entirely.
- **Quote any `description` containing `:`, `#`, or leading punctuation.** An
  unquoted YAML plain scalar cannot contain `": "` — `npx skills` fails with
  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings" and drops the skill
  from the picker without a non-zero exit. ` #` is worse: it parses, but YAML
  treats the rest as a comment and silently truncates your trigger string.
  Single quotes need no escaping except `'` itself. Run
  `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` to catch both; see
  `pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md` in this repo.
- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
  investing in authoring.
- **Scope auto-detect can surprise you.** `new-skill.sh` walks up looking for
  a publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
  `skills/.claude-plugin/`) *first*, then a `.git`. If you ran it from inside
  a clone of this repo while meaning to add a skill to your *other* project,
  it'll silently land in `skills/local/`. Pass `--project` or `--global`
  explicitly when intent isn't obvious, and prefer asking the user
  system-wide-vs-project-wide before running.
- **Discovery symlinks must be `../../`-relative**, not repo-root-relative —
  POSIX resolves symlink targets relative to the link's own directory. The
  script enforces this and verifies each link with `test -e <link>/SKILL.md`;
  if you ever hand-create one, see
  [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md).

## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)

Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
quantitative validation.


ARGUMENTS: Targeted release-label synchronization only in existing internal/skill/dev-cli/references Markdown. Do not edit SKILL.md, generate files, install tools, or run tests.

132	`prepare --specstory-path PATH` pins one provider/UUID/capture-path selection;

153	request proof and receipt reachability still precede integration or retirement;
154	queued or runtime-done is not READY. Native Windows co-commit remains unsupported.

156	## Choose the containment base
157	
158	`dev retire --base <ref>` overrides the containment target for a DONE task or
159	linked worktree without changing recorded task intent. Resolution checks a local
160	branch (`refs/heads/X`), then a remote-tracking branch (`refs/remotes/X`, such as
161	`origin/main`), then a commit. Fully qualified branch refs keep their named kind.
162	Apply re-resolves the same input and requires the same kind, ref and commit OID;
163	a moved base or a newly created same-name branch makes the reviewed plan stale.
164	Remote-tracking refs are local observations, not an implicit fetch.
165	
166	Without an override, task retirement keeps its recorded base. A recorded
167	fork-point commit is never silently replaced by the default branch: if it cannot
168	prove integration, retirement stays blocked with `pass --base <branch>` guidance.
169	After `dev done --merged --base-ref X`, cleanup hints, the cleanup wizard and the

124	## Parking
125	
126	```bash
127	dev park --next "reproduce the token refresh race, then add a regression test"
128	```
129	
130	This is the move the whole design exists to make safe. It records what to do
131	next and leaves the checkout boundary exactly where it is. An external caller
132	may close an eligible runtime; when park is invoked from inside its own runtime,
133	it records WARM but deliberately leaves that runtime alive so the agent can exit
134	normally. In direct mode the boundary is the current branch; in worktree mode it
135	is the branch and linked checkout.
136	
137	`--next` is the important part. Without it, resuming means re-deriving where
138	you were from a diff, which is most of the cost of a context switch. Always
139	supply one.
140	
141	Before finishing agent work, default `dev prepare` requires committed product
142	changes and an empty index. Select the exact session UUID, optionally pin its
143	`--specstory-path` (Unreleased), then exit normally. The post-writer finalizer—not
144	the still-running agent—preserves the exact transcript in its recorded lane.
145	The explicit Unreleased `--closeout co-commit` alternative queues a reviewed
146	feature-only index through an authentic v2 wrapper launched without automatic
147	commit approval; read [AI artifacts](ai-artifacts.md) before using it. After
148	queueing (even `queued_but_not_bound`), report "finalization queued" and exit with
149	no more repository operations. Only an external guarded finalizer may authorize
150	its commit; unknown outcomes are reconcile-only. Read-only helper observations
151	never update native intent. A settled Herdr `done` state is not evidence that
152	history, review or commits are complete.
153	
154	Useful variations:
155	
156	```bash
157	dev park --wip                    # checkpoint uncommitted work first
158	dev park --cold --push            # close session, push, remove worktree
159	dev park --keep-session           # warm only: record state, keep session
160	```
161	
162	`--cold --keep-session` is rejected because a runtime must not remain pointed at
163	a checkout that cold parking removes. A verified runtime-close failure likewise
164	stops cold cleanup before deleting the checkout; warm park reports the close
165	failure and keeps the recorded handle for reconciliation.
166	
167	## Checkpoint commits, not stashes
```
</details></tool-use>

989	可選 `--specstory-path PATH` 保存 capture 範圍內精確 provider／UUID 匯出檔的
990	選取。Source-commit 與 archive finalizer 重新檢查選取、live writer guards 與
991	native intent revisions；`--revision HASH` 可綁定精確審閱紀錄。
992	
993	`prepare --closeout co-commit --session claude:UUID --specstory-path PATH
994	--message-file PATH` 則要求一個 `--plan PATH` 或明確 `--no-plan`，且 index 只有
995	審閱後的 product changes。可選 `--closeout-helper` 指定已安裝 canonical v2 的
996	scripts directory；`--allow-large` 同意新增大於 2 MiB 的 untracked transcript。
997	真實 wrapper 必須不帶 `--allow-commit` 啟動。Queue 不會啟動／關閉 agent：保留
998	真實 ACK，回報 finalization queued 後退出，不再操作 repository。`--run-id` 只
999	修復已排入之精確 run 的 binding，不新增 queue／ACK。
1000	
1001	外部 `artifact finalize --intent ID --allow-commit [--revision HASH]` 對
1002	canonical prepare-only 及一次可 commit 的呼叫執行 guards；結果未知只 reconcile。
1003	`--preview-review --json` 為唯讀，不可搭配 `--allow-commit`、`--review-file` 或
1004	`--rotation-confirmed`。套用精確 private review 需 absolute `--review-file`；
1005	`--rotation-confirmed` 代表實際憑證輪替，不是 fixture review。審閱規則、helper
1006	安裝邊界及平台限制見 [AI 產物](../guides/ai-artifacts.zh-TW.md)。
1007	
1008	Product-first 的 `prepare --json` 與 `artifact finalize --json` 使用 schema 1、
1009	kind `artifact_preparation`／`artifact_finalization`。Co-commit 使用 schema 1、
1010	kind `co_commit_handoff`，保留 partial status、request ID、native revision／intent、
1011	helper 觀測，並在 queue 成功時保留 canonical v2 `queue_ack`。Human queue output
1012	也以一行完整緊湊 JSON 保留 ACK，供 recorder 記錄。`artifact list --json` 使用
1013	schema 1、kind `artifact_handoffs`；`handoffs` 每個 row 的已保存 Intent 欄位與
1014	`co_commit_observation` 或 `observation_error` 分開。List／status／readiness 不
1015	修改或 reconcile 紀錄。
1016	
1017	### 保存設定
1018	
1019	`dev artifact setup` 與 `dev repo setup --artifacts` 共用審閱 plan。
1020	`.dev-cli/artifacts.toml` 保存 project ID、track/archive/unmanaged 模式、
1021	specstory/files 來源、capture 策略、literal 路徑與 export 規則。本機 archive／
1022	protection binding 與有簽章的 receipts 留在 `paths.state_dir/agent-history/`，
1023	屬於 private 持久資料，不是 cache。
1024	
1025	Capture/provider identity、source retention、off/check/redact 副本保護與
1026	發行排除是獨立選擇。支援限制、preview/apply 命令與歷史遷移詳見
1027	[AI 產物](../guides/ai-artifacts.md)。
1028

751	## Native artifact closeout (Unreleased)
752	
753	Product-first remains the default: commit products and leave an empty index.
754	Optional `prepare --specstory-path` pins the exact provider/UUID/capture-path
755	selection, including archive handoffs, without weakening ambiguity, traversal or
756	symlink refusal. Finalizers recheck live writer/source guards and locked native
757	intent revisions; `--writer-stopped` never overrides a recognized live writer.
758	
759	Explicit co-commit currently requires `claude:UUID`, in-checkout SpecStory capture,
760	a feature-only index and a separately installed canonical v2 helper. The authentic
761	wrapper must start without `--allow-commit`; dev never launches/closes an agent.
762	The helper is maintained separately and unreleased, not bundled or automatically
763	installed/upgraded with dev. Missing capabilities, changed helper/tool identities
764	and v1 journals fail closed; native Windows co-commit is unsupported pending a
765	verified native backend. The external-archive lane is not a co-commit destination.
766	
767	Queue success—including `queued_but_not_bound`—requires the agent to report
768	finalization queued and exit, preserving the real recorder's `queue_ack` evidence.
769	`--run-id` only repairs an exact existing binding, not queue or lifecycle proof.
770	External finalization delegates prepare-only, rechecks native Guard/CAS and helper
771	journal revision, then permits one commit-capable call. Uncertain outcomes are
772	reconcile-only. Commit proof includes exact parent/tree/full normalized message
773	and unique request identity. Status/readiness never reconcile native records;
774	schema-1 `artifact_handoffs` keeps persisted Intent fields separate from
775	`co_commit_observation`/`observation_error`.
776	
777	V2 uses no-cloud through run/sync/export and requires exact export digest plus
778	request/session linkage, not idle or mtime alone. Durable private beforeimages
779	and receipts bind all finding occurrences and source/index/tool/policy identities.
780	Eligible staged products are scanned read-only; only selected artifacts are
781	sanitized. Read-only review cannot authorize apply. `reviewed_noncredential`
782	releases only that already-sanitized run's rotation gate, never restores secrets,
783	creates blanket exceptions or bypasses hooks. Actual credentials still require
784	rotation; unknown findings stay blocked. See [AI artifacts](../guides/ai-artifacts.md).
785	
786	## Agent history archives
787	
788	History policy is opt-in through `artifact setup` or `repo setup --artifacts`.
789	Only SpecStory Markdown and explicitly selected files are capture sources.
790	Archive copies require post-writer proof; off stores unscanned input, while
791	check/redact use enabled source hygiene rules. Native session databases, cloud
792	resume, automatic knowledge mining, encrypted/LFS archive filters and original
793	remote history replacement are outside this integration.
794	
795	Current file snapshots cap at 128 MiB, inventories at 10,000 files and plans at
796	256 selected files. Split migration requires git-filter-repo (native CI pins
797	2.47.0) and complete locally recoverable refs. Backup coverage and partial results
```

## Summary

Prepare **v0.2.40** with guarded artifact closeout and small dashboard/worktree usability improvements.

- Add exact SpecStory-path selection, source/writer checks and revision-bound artifact transitions without changing the default product-first or archive lanes.
- Add an explicit canonical v2 co-commit adapter: authentic queue acknowledgement, preparation-only boundary, fresh native guards, exact commit proof and reconciliation-only uncertain outcomes. - Exclude tracked agent-plan directories as well as SpecStory history from compact release source archives, without untracking Git evidence.
- Add a required native Windows gate for the portable selector/CAS/filter/worktree contracts. Native Windows co-commit helper execution remains explicitly unsupported.

Remove a worktree's checkout.

198	// Executables are observed, never replaced. Unlike configuration transactions,
199	// this permits root-owned system tools and standard package-manager ancestors.
200	// The held-path read and persistent inode/content identity still reject drift.
201	func coCommitExecutableToken(ctx context.Context, path string) (string, error) {
202		before, err := os.Lstat(path)
203		if err != nil || !before.Mode().IsRegular() || before.Mode().Perm()&0o111 == 0 || before.Mode().Perm()&0o022 != 0 {
204			return "", errors.New("unverified executable")
205		}
206		metadata := reflect.Indirect(reflect.ValueOf(before.Sys()))
207		if metadata.Kind() != reflect.Struct {
208			return "", errors.New("unsupported executable identity")
209		}
210		dev, ino, uid, gid := metadata.FieldByName("Dev"), metadata.FieldByName("Ino"), metadata.FieldByName("Uid"), metadata.FieldByName("Gid")
211		if !dev.IsValid() || !ino.IsValid() || !uid.IsValid() || !gid.IsValid() || !uid.CanUint() || (uid.Uint() != 0 && uid.Uint() != uint64(os.Getuid())) {
212			return "", errors.New("unsupported executable ownership")
213		}
214		data, err := safefile.ReadStablePath(ctx, path, 128<<20)
215		if err != nil {
216			return "", err
217		}
218		after, err := os.Lstat(path)
219		if err != nil || !os.SameFile(before, after) || before.Mode() != after.Mode() || before.Size() != after.Size() || !before.ModTime().Equal(after.ModTime()) {
220			return "", errors.New("executable changed during observation")
221		}
222		hash := sha256.New()
223		fmt.Fprintf(hash, "%s\x00%v:%v:%v:%v:%d:%d:%d\x00", path, dev.Interface(), ino.Interface(), uid.Interface(), gid.Interface(), before.Size(), before.ModTime().UnixNano(), before.Mode())
224		_, _ = hash.Write(data)
225		return hex.EncodeToString(hash.Sum(nil)), nil
226	}

26						path = "/private" + path
27					}
28				}
29			}
30		}
31		anchor, err := platformfs.Resolve(path)
32		if err != nil {
33			return nil, err
34		}
35		base := anchor.Path
36		parts := strings.Split(strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimPrefix(path, base), string(filepath.Separator)), string(filepath.Separator))
37		if len(parts) == 0 || len(parts) > 128 {
38			return nil, ErrUnsafeType
39		}
40		root, info, err := OpenRoot(base)
41		if err != nil {
42			return nil, err
43		}
44		defer root.Close()
45		type edge struct {
46			parent *os.Root
47			name   string
48			info   fs.FileInfo
49		}
50		var edges []edge
51		current := root
52		for _, part := range parts[:len(parts)-1] {
53			next, id, e := OpenChildRoot(current, part)
54			if e != nil {
55				return nil, e
56			}
57			defer next.Close()
58			edges = append(edges, edge{current, part, id})
59			current = next
60		}
61		data, _, err := ReadStableRegular(ctx, current, parts[len(parts)-1], nil, limit)

63			return nil, err

71			return nil, err
72		}

**Verified root cause: the installed-tool test assumes that any Python on `PATH` satisfies the executable trust policy. Both CI interpreters are writable by group/others, so the production guard correctly rejects them.**

### Exact failure
Both jobs fail at:
- `TestCoCommitInstalledToolIdentityIsReadOnly/python3`
- `co_commit_test.go:685`
- Sanitized error: `ordinary installed executable was rejected: co-commit unverified_tool; next: inspect_native_helper_dependencies`

The failing workflow command is `go test ./internal/agenthistory ./internal/artifact`, not the scanner regression.

### Concrete evidence
- **Ubuntu:** logged runner image `ubuntu24/20260907.300`; setup-python selects cached Python **3.12.14**. The [pinned image initialization](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/blob/ubuntu24/20260907.300/images/ubuntu/scripts/build/configure-system.sh#L12-L15) recursively sets `/opt`—including its Python toolcache—to **0777**.
- **macOS:** setup-python selects **3.12.10**. I inspected the [exact released package](https://github.com/actions/python-versions/releases/download/3.12.10-14343898437/python-3.12.10-darwin-arm64.tar.gz) entirely in memory. Its `bin/python3.12` is a regular executable, **0775**, UID **0**, size **152096** bytes. Its installer links the toolcache to that framework.

Both hit `before.Mode().Perm() & 0o022 != 0` in [co_commit_helper.go:203](/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui/internal/artifact/co_commit_helper.go#L203), **before ownership, stable-read, or size validation**.

Local Python is **0755**; the focused test passes locally. The other protocol tests use private **0700** wrappers, explaining why this isolated installed-tool check fails.

### Minimal fix and coverage
Preserve the production guard and runner permissions. Correct the unconditional success expectation in [co_commit_test.go:674–691](/Users/zhouhanru/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui/internal/artifact/co_commit_test.go#L674):
- Assert typed `unverified_tool` rejection for group/other-writable installed executables.
- Add deterministic fixtures proving **0700/0755 acceptance**, **0775/0777 rejection**, and **no content/metadata mutation**.
- Retain success coverage for trusted installed binaries; do not blanket-skip CI Python failures.

Focused reproduction in the existing setup-python environment:
```bash
go test ./internal/artifact -run '^TestCoCommitInstalledToolIdentityIsReadOnly/python3$' -count=1 -v
```

Supporting writable Python installations in production would require a separately reviewed trust-policy change—not removing this guard to satisfy CI.

**No checkout edits, permission changes, workflow reruns, or persisted downloads/logs.**

751	## Native artifact closeout (v0.2.40)
752	
753	Product-first remains the default: commit products and leave an empty index.
754	Optional `prepare --specstory-path` pins the exact provider/UUID/capture-path
755	selection, including archive handoffs, without weakening ambiguity, traversal or
756	symlink refusal. Finalizers recheck live writer/source guards and locked native
757	intent revisions; `--writer-stopped` never overrides a recognized live writer.
758	
759	Explicit co-commit currently requires `claude:UUID`, in-checkout SpecStory capture,
760	a feature-only index and a separately installed canonical v2 helper. The authentic
761	wrapper must start without `--allow-commit`; dev never launches/closes an agent.
762	Canonical v2 source is maintained separately in `agent-skills`; the helper is not
763	bundled or automatically installed/upgraded with dev. An installed helper with
764	compatible v2 capabilities is required. Missing capabilities, changed helper/tool
765	identities and v1 journals fail closed; native Windows co-commit is unsupported
766	pending a verified native backend. The external-archive lane is not a co-commit
767	destination.
768	
769	Queue success—including `queued_but_not_bound`—requires the agent to report
770	finalization queued and exit, preserving the real recorder's `queue_ack` evidence.
771	`--run-id` only repairs an exact existing binding, not queue or lifecycle proof.
772	External finalization delegates prepare-only, rechecks native Guard/CAS and helper
773	journal revision, then permits one commit-capable call. Uncertain outcomes are
774	reconcile-only. Commit proof includes exact parent/tree/full normalized message
775	and unique request identity. Status/readiness never reconcile native records;
776	schema-1 `artifact_handoffs` keeps persisted Intent fields separate from
777	`co_commit_observation`/`observation_error`.
778	
779	V2 uses no-cloud through run/sync/export and requires exact export digest plus
780	request/session linkage, not idle or mtime alone. Durable private beforeimages
781	and receipts bind all finding occurrences and source/index/tool/policy identities.
782	Eligible staged products are scanned read-only; only selected artifacts are
783	sanitized. Read-only review cannot authorize apply. `reviewed_noncredential`
784	releases only that already-sanitized run's rotation gate, never restores secrets,
785	creates blanket exceptions or bypasses hooks. Actual credentials still require
786	rotation; unknown findings stay blocked. See [AI artifacts](../guides/ai-artifacts.md).
787	
788	## Agent history archives
789	
790	History policy is opt-in through `artifact setup` or `repo setup --artifacts`.
```

# 2. Key Technical Concepts and Constraints

## Toolchain and architecture

- Go 1.26.4 in the repository’s `go.mod`.
- Cobra CLI.
- Bubble Tea dashboard.
- Python 3.11+ for canonical post-session helper; uv/Python docs environments.
- Git common-directory identity for canonical and linked checkouts.
- Herdr runtime integration; current observed client/server version 0.9.1.
- Git owns code truth, worktrees are disposable checkouts, runtimes are host-local, task records hold intent.
- `artifact` owns native handoffs and bindings; `agenthistory` owns source retention/archive policy.
- Canonical helper remains the sole co-commit staging/sanitation/commit/reconciliation authority.
- Native dev is a guarded adapter, not a second commit engine.
- `taskflow` remains lifecycle/readiness authority.
- `hygiene` owns policy, scans, signed review/change plans.

Core implementation:

```go
func newWtOpenCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
    var repoRef string
    var noFocus bool
    cmd := &cobra.Command{
        Use:   "open <branch>",
        Short: "Open an existing worktree in the runtime",
        Args:  cobra.ExactArgs(1),
        RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
            ctx := ctxOf()
            repoPath, repoName, err := repoContext(app, repoRef)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            w, ok, err := gitx.WorktreeFor(ctx, repoPath, args[0])
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            if !ok {
                return fmt.Errorf(
                    "no worktree for branch %q — create one with `dev wt create %s`",
                    args[0], args[0],
                )
            }
            rt := app.Runtime()
            opened, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, w.Path, repoName+"/"+w.Branch)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            style := app.outStyle()
            fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s  %s", style.success(w.Branch), config.Contract(w.Path))
            if rt.Name() != "none" {
                fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  %s",
                    style.dim(fmt.Sprintf("(%s %s)", rt.Name(), opened.Handle)))
            }
            fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
            if noFocus {
                if rt.Name() == "none" {
                    fmt.Fprintln(app.Out, "   no runtime opened; no shell directory change requested")
                } else {
                    status := "not opened"
                    if opened.Opened {
                        status = "reused"
                        if opened.Created {
                            status = "opened"
                        }
                    }
                    fmt.Fprintf(app.Out,
                        "   runtime %s (surface=%q); focus not requested\n",
                        status, opened.Surface)
                }
                return nil
            }
            if rt.Name() == "none" {
                return app.cdDirective(w.Path)
            }
            return activateRuntime(ctx, rt, opened.Handle)
        },
    }
    cmd.Flags().StringVarP(&repoRef, "repo", "r", "",
        "repository (default: the current one)")
    cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&noFocus, "no-focus", false,
        "open or reuse the runtime without switching, attaching, or changing shell directory")
    registerFlagCompletion(cmd, "repo", completeRepoFlag(app))
    cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeWorktrees(app, true)
    return cmd
}
```

Important:
- Default behavior unchanged.
- No-focus returns before both activation and `none` shell handoff.
- No task adoption/provisioning/agent launch/annotation/Git mutation.
- No new JSON mode.
- Uses exact existing checkout and existing first-class Herdr opening.
- Real manual verification reused `w11`:

```text
fix/closeout-review-tui  ~/Worktrees/dev-cli/fix-closeout-review-tui  (herdr w11)
   runtime reused (surface="worktree"); focus not requested
```

Guidance updated to:

- Use `dev wt open ... --no-focus` to surface existing external worktrees.
- Report branch/path/runtime handle promptly.
- Do not treat reading `--skill` as side-effectful.

`CoCommitBinding` retains:

JSON identity keys deliberately use:
```text
helper_identity
python_identity
bash_identity
artifact_policy_identity
```
not `_token`, because real Gitleaks classified synthetic noncredential `_token` fingerprints as API keys. Go field names remain `HelperToken`, etc.; no detector exemptions were added.

inspect_v2
authentic_context_v2
queue_idempotent_v2
sanitation_receipt_v2
review_v2
exact_export_v2
no_cloud_v2
prepare_only_v2
revision_guard_v2
reconcile_only_v2
```

Native helper invocation:
```text
<bound python> -I -B <scripts>/_post_session.py capabilities --json
<bound python> -I -B <scripts>/_post_session.py inspect --context --json
<bound python> -I -B <scripts>/_post_session.py inspect --request ABS --json
<bound python> -I -B <scripts>/_post_session.py queue --script-dir S ...
<bound python> -I -B <scripts>/_post_session.py finalize --script-dir S ...
```

The direct Python command invokes canonical `cmd_queue` / `cmd_finalize`; native dev does not duplicate shell parsing or commit execution.

Queue requires:
- Real authenticated wrapper context.
- `automatic_commit == false` so the outer parent cannot auto-commit around native Guard/policy checks.
- Explicit exact session/transcript/one-plan-or-no-plan/message.
- Feature-only staged index.
- No active Git operation, archive-policy incompatibility, unsafe paths, or unsupported helper.
- No manufactured run ID or journal.
- `--run-id` only repairs a binding of an existing exact queued request.
- `queued_but_not_bound` is retained partial state; no requeue.
- Native deterministic intent ID is `co-<run UUID>`.

Typed queue ACK:

```go
type CoCommitQueueAck struct {
    Kind            string `json:"kind"`
    SchemaVersion   int    `json:"schema_version"`
    RequestID       string `json:"request_id"`
    RequestPath     string `json:"request_path"`
    RequestRevision string `json:"request_revision"`
    HelperRevision  string `json:"helper_revision"`
}
```

Exact wire format:

```json
{
  "kind": "agent_history_queue_ack",
  "schema_version": 2,
  "request_id": "RUN_UUID",
  "request_path": "ABSOLUTE_REQUEST_PATH",
  "request_revision": "64_HEX",
  "helper_revision": "64_HEX"
}
```

- Public JSON nests this under `queue_ack`.
- Human output emits the actual canonical ACK as one compact JSON line so the recorder can retain typed evidence.
- ACK is never invented during old-run binding repair.
- Invalid/proven mismatched ACKs are not emitted.
- Valid ACK survives post-queue inspection/native-store failure.
- It proves retained queue fact, not binding success or commit approval.

Finalization:
1. Explicit fresh `--allow-commit`.
2. Native expected-record revision check.
3. Canonical request/tool/policy/current Git validation.
4. Genuine child exit/group/sync/freshness proof.
5. Native Guard.
6. Canonical `--prepare-only --expected-revision <journal revision>`.
7. Reinspect retained prepared evidence.
8. Recheck native revision/current state and fresh Guard.
9. One canonical commit-capable call with exact expected journal revision.
10. Independent Git object proof and CAS result persistence.

For `committing`, only canonical `--reconcile-only` is allowed. No automatic retry.

Commit proof:
- Bounded raw `git --no-replace-objects cat-file commit`.
- Maximum accepted commit object 512 KiB.
- Recompute SHA-1/SHA-256 over Git’s `commit <len>\0<bytes>` framing.
- Exact one parent equals intent HEAD.
- Exact tree equals prepared tree.
- Exactly one matching `Agent-History-Request` trailer.
- Full message normalized with native `git stripspace`, hashed against helper proof.
- Not just trailer presence.
- Historical completed receipt can remain valid after normal descendant work; reachability is checked separately.

Transport/security:
- Native Windows co-commit is explicitly unsupported.
- Helper scripts/assets source fingerprint rechecked around execution.
- Python/Bash canonical executable identity includes inode/device/UID/GID/mode/size/mtime/content.
- Reject alternate Git index/worktree/object/config injection.
- Strip Python/Bash startup injection environments.
- Darwin Bash is explicitly `/bin/bash`.
- Output bounded; errors use finite code/remediation mapping, never reflect arbitrary helper labels.
- Invalid inspection returns zero DTO.
- Review is typed/allowlisted, not arbitrary JSON proxy.
- Masked values must be exactly `[REDACTED]`; complete finding IDs/occurrence/path/receipt binding required.
- `artifact list --json` separates stored intent from `co_commit_observation` and errors.

### Production executable trust guard — unchanged by latest CI fix

File:
`internal/artifact/co_commit_helper.go`

Important implementation:

```go
func coCommitTool(ctx context.Context, name string) (string, string, error) {
    if name == "bash" && runtime.GOOS == "darwin" {
        name = "/bin/bash"
    }
    path, err := exec.LookPath(name)
    if err != nil {
        return "", "", coCommitFailure(
            "dependency_missing", "install_native_helper_dependencies")
    }
    path, err = filepath.EvalSymlinks(path)
    if err != nil || !filepath.IsAbs(path) {
        return "", "", coCommitFailure(
            "unsafe_tool", "inspect_native_helper_dependencies")
    }
    token, err := coCommitExecutableToken(ctx, path)
    if err != nil {
        return "", "", coCommitFailure(
            "unverified_tool", "inspect_native_helper_dependencies")
    }
    return path, token, nil
}
```

`coCommitExecutableToken` rejects:

```go
if err != nil ||
    !before.Mode().IsRegular() ||
    before.Mode().Perm()&0o111 == 0 ||
    before.Mode().Perm()&0o022 != 0 {
    return "", errors.New("unverified executable")
}
```

It then requires root/current-user ownership, reads through `safefile.ReadStablePath`, verifies same file/mode/size/mtime, and computes the identity digest. It does not chmod/replace tools.

### Latest CI test correction

File:
`internal/artifact/co_commit_test.go`

The old test unconditionally expected every installed `python3`/`bash` to pass. New test:
- Resolves the actual tool, including stock Darwin `/bin/bash`.
- Reads pre-observation stat/content.
- If installed mode has group/other write, requires typed `unverified_tool`, empty returned path/token.
- Otherwise requires valid exact identity.
- Verifies bytes, inode identity, mode, size and mtime unchanged.

Deterministic new test:

```go
func TestCoCommitExecutablePermissionContract(t *testing.T) {
    if runtime.GOOS == "windows" {
        t.Skip("POSIX tool contract")
    }
    for _, tc := range []struct {
        name    string
        mode    os.FileMode
        trusted bool
    }{
        {"owner-only", 0o700, true},
        {"readable-executable", 0o755, true},
        {"group-writable", 0o775, false},
        {"world-writable", 0o777, false},
    } {
        // Create/chmod only this test-owned fixture.
        // Call coCommitTool on exact absolute path.
        // Assert acceptance or typed refusal.
        // assertCoCommitToolUnchanged verifies identity/content/metadata.
    }
}
```

The only chmod is on newly created test fixtures, never runner-installed Python.

## E. Latest CI failure and correction — current publication blocker being revalidated

Original PR head `808135e`:
- Main CI matrix, Docs, scan, native Windows hygiene passed.
- Repository hygiene native Ubuntu/macOS failed:
  `TestCoCommitInstalledToolIdentityIsReadOnly/python3`.

Exact cause:
- Production rejects executable mode `& 0o022 != 0`.
- Ubuntu runner image `ubuntu24/20260907.300` applies recursive `chmod -R 777 /opt`, including toolcache Python 3.12.14.
- macOS setup-python package Python 3.12.10 contains `Versions/3.12/bin/python3.12` mode **0775**, UID 0, size 152096.
- Both correctly fail before ownership/stable-read/size checks.
- Local Python is 0755, explaining local pass.

Correction in `cfe3e39`:
- Preserve production guard.
- Assert writable installed tools are rejected rather than assuming PATH implies trust.
- Deterministic 0700/0755 acceptance and 0775/0777 rejection.
- Verify no executable mutation.
- Clarify policy in paired compatibility docs and regenerated LLM docs.
- No CI skip or chmod of installed tools.

Local validation passed:
- Focused permission/lookup race tests.
- Full affected `agenthistory`/`artifact` race suites.
- Vet/whitespace.
- Strict bilingual docs.

New CI at `cfe3e39`:
- Previously failing native Ubuntu/macOS hygiene jobs now pass.
- Other jobs are still pending as of last observation.

45	      # .zip with dev.exe; every other platform a .tar.gz with dev.
46	      - name: Build release archives

54	              go build -ldflags "$ldflags" -o "dist/$bin" ./cmd/dev
55	            if [ "$os" = windows ]; then
56	              ( cd dist && zip -q "dev-cli_${VERSION}_${os}_${arch}.zip" "$bin" )
57	            else

59	            fi

22	    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

31	            subprocess.run(

```text
Remove a worktree's checkout.

The branch is never deleted: removing a checkout and abandoning a change
stream are different decisions, and conflating them is how work gets lost.
A checkout with uncommitted changes needs an explicit --force.

Usage:
  dev wt rm <branch> [flags]

Aliases:
  rm, remove

Flags:
      --assume-no-runtime   continue when runtime enumeration fails
      --close-unknown       allow external closure of unknown runtime status
  -f, --force               remove even with uncommitted changes (never bypasses caller/runtime safety)
  -h, --help                help for rm
      --recursive           verify and dispose workspace-owned submodule clones from the inside out
  -r, --repo string         repository (default: the current one)
      --timeout duration    maximum time to wait for runtime closure (default 5s)

Global Flags:
      --allow-shared-checkout   allow a writer claim in a checkout occupied by another live agent
      --color string            colorize human output: auto, always or never (default "auto")
      --config string           path to config.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/config.toml)
      --no-runtime              do not touch any terminal multiplexer
      --remotes string          path to remotes.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/remotes.toml)
      --runtime string          override runtime backend: herdr, tmux, zellij or none
      --scaffolds string        path to scaffolds.toml (default: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dev/scaffolds.toml)
